item.title: Numerology
item.description:
Numerology is an early-to-mid Metaphysics upgrade under the Science -> Metaphysics tab that ties your village’s production to the calendar’s celestial cycle.

Cost & Prerequisites

  • Tab: Science $\to$ Metaphysics
  • Cost: 16 Paragon
  • Prerequisites: Unlocked after researching Megamania.
  • Tree Position: Serves as the gateway requirement for downstream temporal metaphysics upgrades: Numeromancy (50 Paragon) and Carnivals / Pawgan calendar enhancements.

What It Does: Celestial Cycle Modifiers

The game’s calendar progresses through 10 celestial cycles, each lasting 5 calendar years (a full cycle loop takes 50 game years).
item.content:encoded:
Numerology is an early-to-mid Metaphysics upgrade under the Science -> Metaphysics tab that ties your village’s production to the calendar’s celestial cycle.

Cost & Prerequisites

  • Tab: Science $\to$ Metaphysics
  • Cost: 16 Paragon
  • Prerequisites: Unlocked after researching Megamania.
  • Tree Position: Serves as the gateway requirement for downstream temporal metaphysics upgrades: Numeromancy (50 Paragon) and Carnivals / Pawgan calendar enhancements.

What It Does: Celestial Cycle Modifiers

The game’s calendar progresses through 10 celestial cycles, each lasting 5 calendar years (a full cycle loop takes 50 game years).

Without Numerology, these cycle signs are purely cosmetic. Once Numerology is purchased, each celestial sign grants a specific $+35%$ production bonus to a designated resource, paired with minor penalties to others:

Celestial Sign Primary Boost (+35%) Secondary Modifiers
Charon Catnip Winter penalties slightly harsher
Umber Coal Minor boost to fossil fuels
Kharon Iron Slight reduction to mineral gathering
Yarn Culture Boosts parchment/manuscript generation
Zeus Minerals Boosts baseline ground extraction
Hermes Trade Ratio Improves caravan transaction returns
Ares Catpower / Hunting Higher Fur and Ivory yields
Helios Solar & Faith Boosts Solar Farms and base Faith accumulation
Tithonus Wood Improves logging and beam production
Ananke Oil Speeds up oil wells and fuel conversion

Why It Matters

  1. Cycle Awareness: During early and mid-game runs, aligning your big build phases with beneficial signs (e.g., waiting for Kharon to mass-forge Steel or Ares for major hunt batches) provides free efficiency boosts.
  2. Gateway to Numeromancy: Its primary long-term importance is unlocking Numeromancy (50 Paragon), which applies similar cycling percentage multipliers to Space missions, deep-space projects, and festival durations.
  3. Synergy with Time Shattering: In the late game, when combusting Time Crystals via Resource Retrieval, you skip through years instantly. The cycle modifiers cycle rapidly, evening out into a solid, passive net boost across all resources.

When to Buy It

Buy it around Runs 3–5, after you have secured your baseline 150–200 banked Paragon floor and picked up the first two price-ratio discounts (Golden Ratio and Divine Proportion).

At only 16 Paragon, it is a cheap pickup that paves the way toward late-game temporal metaphysics.

item.title: Event Horizon
item.description:
Event Horizon is a Cryptotheology upgrade under the Religion tab that fundamentally expands your late-game resource limits.

Unlike standard bonfire or space buildings, Cryptotheology structures are bought using Relics and persist permanently across resets.

Cost & Requirements

  • Tab: Religion to Cryptotheology
  • Unlock Requirement: Requires building a Black Pyramid (via Ziggurat sacrifices) to access the Cryptotheology panel.
  • Cost: Scales exponentially in Relics and Void:
    • Relic Cost: approx 100 times 1.25^N
    • Void Cost: Scales alongside relics per purchase rank.

What It Does
item.content:encoded:
Event Horizon is a Cryptotheology upgrade under the Religion tab that fundamentally expands your late-game resource limits.

Unlike standard bonfire or space buildings, Cryptotheology structures are bought using Relics and persist permanently across resets.

Cost & Requirements

  • Tab: Religion to Cryptotheology
  • Unlock Requirement: Requires building a Black Pyramid (via Ziggurat sacrifices) to access the Cryptotheology panel.
  • Cost: Scales exponentially in Relics and Void:
    • Relic Cost: approx 100 times 1.25^N
    • Void Cost: Scales alongside relics per purchase rank.

What It Does

  • Compounding Global Storage Bonus: Each purchase of Event Horizon increases maximum storage capacity across all standard resources (Catnip, Wood, Minerals, Iron, Coal, Titanium, Oil, Unobtainium, Uranium, etc.).

  • The Math:

    Storage Multiplier = (1 + 0.10)^N = 1.10^N

    Every level grants a +10% compounding bonus to overall storage caps.

  • Stacking with Void Rifts: While Void Rifts (in the Space tab) also give compounding storage bonuses, Void Rifts reset when you reset your game. Event Horizon provides a permanent baseline that makes every subsequent run start with larger storage caps out of the gate.

Why It Is Critical in Late Game

  1. Unlocking Late-Game Price Thresholds: Late-game science techs, high-tier Chronospheres, AI Cores, and deep space missions have astronomical resource costs that standard Barns, Warehouses, and Harbors cannot hold. Event Horizon pushes those ceilings higher.
  2. Fueling the Shatter Loop: Higher Unobtainium caps mean you can hold more Unobtainium per time-shattered year via Resource Retrieval, allowing for larger bulk trades with Leviathans without overflowing and wasting materials.
  3. Reset Cushion: Because Event Horizon never resets, future runs reach high-capacity storage rapidly, letting you build advanced housing and factories much earlier.

Spending Recommendation

With a solid Relic reserve (such as 100k–200k+ Relics), aim for 15–25 levels of Event Horizon. Balancing Event Horizon with Black Nexus (which boosts Relic/TC yields from Leviathan trades) ensures your resource caps grow alongside your trade volume.

item.title: Late Game
item.description:
The late game begins once standard resets are effortless and you transition into deep temporal manipulation, relic economies, and cryptotheology. Instead of measuring progress in kittens or ground resources, your civilization runs on Time Crystals (TC), Void, Antimatter, and Relics, powered by thousands of years skipped per session.

System Primary Resources Key Structures / Mechanics Main Objective
Chronoforge Time Crystals, Void Resource Retrieval, Chrono Heat Sinks, Blazars High-yield, continuous Time Crystal shattering
Cryptotheology Relics Black Nexus, Event Horizon, Black Obelisk Permanent, reset-proof global scaling
Deep Space Void, Antimatter Void Rifts, Sunlifters, Cryostations Astronomical storage caps to break late-game building costs
Elders (Leviathans) Unobtainium, Necrocorns Black Pyramids, Markers, Feed Elders Infinite TC and Relic generation via trade caravans

The Core Late-Game Engines

  1. The Resource Retrieval (RR) Shatter Loop

Combusting Time Crystals advances the calendar instantly. At base, time skips yield zero production, but Resource Retrieval extracts a percentage of full annual production per shattered TC ($1% \text{ per level}$ ):

Cryptotheology Relics Black Nexus, Event Horizon, Black Obelisk Permanent, reset-proof global scaling
Deep Space Void, Antimatter Void Rifts, Sunlifters, Cryostations Astronomical storage caps to break late-game building costs
Elders (Leviathans) Unobtainium, Necrocorns Black Pyramids, Markers, Feed Elders Infinite TC and Relic generation via trade caravans

The Core Late-Game Engines

  1. The Resource Retrieval (RR) Shatter Loop

Combusting Time Crystals advances the calendar instantly. At base, time skips yield zero production, but Resource Retrieval extracts a percentage of full annual production per shattered TC ($1% \text{ per level}$ ):

  • Break-Even Point: Around RR Level 20–30, shattering a single TC produces enough Unobtainium to trade with Leviathans for more than 1 replacement TC.
  • Hyper-Scaling: At RR 100+, every click dumps multiple years of gross civilization output straight into your stockpiles, instantly maxing out Unobtainium, Alloy, Faith, and Oil.
  1. Heat Management & Blazars

Shattering TCs builds up Heat in the Chronoforge:

  • Chrono Heat Sinks: Increase maximum heat capacity and cooling rates so you can combust hundreds of crystals in rapid bursts.
  • Blazars: Accelerate resource yields per year skipped and improve heat dissipation, keeping the combustion engine sustainable.
  1. Cryptotheology (Reset-Proof Compounding)

Relics purchased through Leviathan trades or generated passively via Black Pyramids are invested into Cryptotheology under the Religion tab. Unlike standard bonfire structures, these upgrades persist forever across resets:

  • Black Nexus: Multiplies Relic and TC yields from Leviathan trade fleets.
  • Event Horizon: Exponentially scales global storage caps.
  • Black Obelisk: Elevates the maximum ceiling of your Solar Revolution multiplier.
  • Black Core & Black Library: Massively expand Science capacity, eliminating compendium grinding.
  1. The Void & Antimatter Economy
  • Void Rifts: Consumes Void and Antimatter in Space to grant compounding percentage bonuses to global storage caps, enabling multi-million Unobtainium requirements.
  • Sunlifters & Containment: Harvest Antimatter during year-skips to fund Void Rifts, Dark Novas, and AI Core management.

The Late-Game Reset Routine: Chronospheres & Cryochambers

Late-game runs often last for tens of thousands of calendar years, but when you do reset:

  • Chronospheres: Carry forward fixed percentages of your current resource stockpiles into the new run.
  • Cryochambers (Stasis): Preserve kitten ranks and leaders, letting you start Run $N+1$ with hundreds of seasoned kittens instantly rather than breeding them from zero.
  • Apocrypha Bank: Massive cumulative faith earned during thousands of skipped years is sacrificed into Apocrypha, compounding your Solar Revolution multiplier into six- and seven-figure percentages.

item.title: Mid Game
item.description:
n Kittens Game, the mid-game spans the transition from initial industrialization to your first Moon landing and early Paragon farming—roughly between Navigation / Chemistry and Rocketry / Unobtainium. During this phase, progress shifts from manually gathering base resources to establishing production loops, balancing the power grid, and mitigating bottlenecks like Titanium, Coal, and Oil.

Mid-Game Milestones & Arc

Phase Core Techs Key Buildings & Unlocks Primary Bottleneck
Early Mid-Game Navigation, Architecture, Physics Trade Ships, Tradeposts, Warehouses Titanium, Coal, Catpower
Industrial Core Chemistry, Industrialization, Mechanization Magnetos, Steamworks, Calciners, Factories Steel, Oil, Energy
Modern Era Electricity, Electronics, Ecology Broadcast Towers, Hydro Plants, Oil Wells Culture caps, Energy deficits
Late Mid-Game Nuclear Fission, Rocketry, Particle Physics Reactors, Satellites, Moon Mission, Accelerators Unobtainium, Alloy

The Three Critical Mid-Game Engines

  1. The Magneto + Steamworks Synergy This is your civilization’s primary production engine:
  • Base Mechanic: Each Magneto grants a +2% global production bonus.
  • The Synergy: Each active Steamworks boosts the bonus of all Magnetos by +15%.
  • Formula: Bonus = Magnetos * 0.02 * (1 + Steamworks * 0.15).
  • A setup of 10 Magnetos and 10 Steamworks multiplies every resource in your settlement by +50%, scaling Catnip, Minerals, Wood, Coal, and Iron simultaneously.
  1. The Trade Fleet (Zebra Titanium Automation)
  • Manual Titanium mining is far too slow to sustain mid-game construction.
  • Build hundreds of Trade Ships using Starcharts and Scaffolds.
  • Trade with the Zebras using Catpower and Gold. A high Trade Ship count guarantees large shipments of Titanium and Iron per trade caravan, easily funding Calciners, Magnetos, and Warehouses.
  1. Power Grid & Clean Energy
  • Turning on Magnetos (-5 W each) and Calciners (-1 W each) without enough energy triggers brownouts, slashing efficiency across the village.
  • Prioritize Hydro Plants (upgrades Aqueducts) and Solar Farms to establish at least +20 to +30 W of clean baseline power before adding heavy consumers.

Essential Mid-Game Workshop Upgrades

  • Pneumatic Bellows / Blast Furnace: Automatically converts raw Coal and Iron into Steel via Calciners and Smelters.
  • Offset Press: Upgrades Steamworks to automatically generate Manuscripts each spring, cutting the Culture bottleneck on Compendiums.
  • Pumpjack & Oil Processing: Boosts Oil Well production and storage caps to prepare rocket fuel reserves. Concrete Huts / Concrete Barns: Uses Concrete (Slabs + Steel) to break ground-level housing and storage caps.

The Mid-Game Reset Target

If you are on your first 1–3 runs, the mid-game is your reset staging ground:

item.title: Order of the Void
item.description:
Order of the Void is an end-game Workshop upgrade that links your Religion workforce to Void generation, allowing priests to produce Void during temporal anomalies.

Core Mechanics & Stats

  • Tab: Workshop
  • Cost:
    • 100,000 Science
    • 50,000 Faith
    • 50 Void
  • Prerequisites: Unlocked after researching the Exophysics technology.

How It Works

  • The Trigger: Normally, Priests only produce Faith, and Void only drops passively from Chronosphere temporal paradoxes.
  • The Synergistic Payout: With Order of the Void, whenever a Temporal Paradox (Day of the Void) triggers, your assigned Priests harvest extra Void directly into your stockpile.
  • Scaling Factors: The amount of Void harvested per paradox scales based on:
    1. The total number of assigned Priests.
    2. Your civilization’s net Faith production (boosted by Sol-tier buildings like Temples, Chapels, and Sunspires).
    3. Your accumulated Solar Revolution bonus.

Internal Faith Weight (F_weight)

The engine first calculates the effective daily faith output per priest: {F_weight} = {Priests} * {Base Faith per Priest} * (1 + ({Solar Revolution Bonus %} /100))
item.content:encoded:
Order of the Void is an end-game Workshop upgrade that links your Religion workforce to Void generation, allowing priests to produce Void during temporal anomalies.

Core Mechanics & Stats

  • Tab: Workshop
  • Cost:
    • 100,000 Science
    • 50,000 Faith
    • 50 Void
  • Prerequisites: Unlocked after researching the Exophysics technology.

How It Works

  • The Trigger: Normally, Priests only produce Faith, and Void only drops passively from Chronosphere temporal paradoxes.
  • The Synergistic Payout: With Order of the Void, whenever a Temporal Paradox (Day of the Void) triggers, your assigned Priests harvest extra Void directly into your stockpile.
  • Scaling Factors: The amount of Void harvested per paradox scales based on:
    1. The total number of assigned Priests.
    2. Your civilization’s net Faith production (boosted by Sol-tier buildings like Temples, Chapels, and Sunspires).
    3. Your accumulated Solar Revolution bonus.

Internal Faith Weight (F_weight)

The engine first calculates the effective daily faith output per priest: {F_weight} = {Priests} * {Base Faith per Priest} * (1 + ({Solar Revolution Bonus %} /100))

The Priest Void Yield (V_priest)

The bonus Void is evaluated using a fractional square root scaling over the accumulated faith weight, capped by diminishing returns:

V_priest = sqrt(F_weight * {Days of the Void}/100,000) * (1 + 0.10 * {Void Resonators})

  • Days of the Void: The duration of the triggered paradox (typically between 2 and 10 game days depending on Chronosphere count and temporal upgrades).
  • Void Resonators: Each Void Resonator on the Chronoforge applies an additive +10% multiplier to temporal yield mechanics.
  • Rounding: If V_priest < 1, the fractional value acts as an independent probabilistic check to award 1 Void; once V_priest > 1, the integer part is guaranteed and the fractional remainder rolls as a probability.

Grand Total Payout

Total Void per Paradox = {Base Void} + V_priest

Practical Implications

  1. Why 0 Priests Yield Low Void: Without Priests, you are receiving purely {Base Void}, which caps out at just a handful of units per event even with a dozen Chronospheres.

  2. Why Solar Revolution Matters: Because F_weight is directly multiplied by (1 + {Solar Rev %}/100), pushing Solar Revolution to +1,000% to +5,000% (via Black Obelisks) magnifies the inner value of the square root by orders of magnitude.

  3. Diminishing Returns: The square root prevents Void from scaling linearly into millions per click, maintaining Void as a tightly controlled gating resource even when burning thousands of Time Crystals.

Strategic Impact in the Late Game

  1. Breaks the Paradox Rate Limit: Relying solely on Chronosphere base drops yields very slow Void income. Order of the Void turns each Day of the Void into a substantial drop, dramatically reducing real-time waiting.
  2. Fuels the Time Shatter Engine: When you combust Time Crystals (TCs) with Resource Retrieval (RR) active, every skipped year rolls for paradoxes. Order of the Void ensures that mass-shattering centuries in a few seconds completely floods your storage with Void.
  3. Funds Expensive Chronoforge Upgrades: Provides the massive Void reserves needed to continually level:
  • Resource Retrieval (scales resource yields per shattered TC)
  • Void Resonators (projects your Solar Revolution multiplier across skipped years)
  • Void Rifts (compounds deep space storage caps using Void and Antimatter)
  • Cryochambers (preserves kittens across resets)

item.title: How to Accumulate Paragon
item.description:
Accumulating 2,000 Paragon in Kittens Game is a massive milestone that requires a deliberate, multi-reset farming strategy (often called “paragon farming” or “speed runs”). Because Paragon is earned primarily by resetting your game with high kitten populations, you cannot achieve this in a single long run.

Here is the step-by-step roadmap to efficiently farm your way to 2,000 Paragon:

1. Understand How Paragon is Calculated

  • The Formula: You earn 1 Paragon for every kitten over 70 that you have in your village when you reset.

  • If you reset with 130 kittens, you get $130 - 70 = 60$ Paragon.

  • If you reset with 200 kittens, you get $200 - 70 = 130$ Paragon.

  • Diminishing Returns: The higher your kitten count goes, the harder it is to house, feed, and keep them happy. Pushing past 180–200 kittens takes exponentially more time than hitting 150. Therefore, fast, repeated medium-length resets are much faster than one massive multi-week run.
item.content:encoded:
Accumulating 2,000 Paragon in Kittens Game is a massive milestone that requires a deliberate, multi-reset farming strategy (often called “paragon farming” or “speed runs”). Because Paragon is earned primarily by resetting your game with high kitten populations, you cannot achieve this in a single long run.

Here is the step-by-step roadmap to efficiently farm your way to 2,000 Paragon:

1. Understand How Paragon is Calculated

  • The Formula: You earn 1 Paragon for every kitten over 70 that you have in your village when you reset.

  • If you reset with 130 kittens, you get $130 - 70 = 60$ Paragon.

  • If you reset with 200 kittens, you get $200 - 70 = 130$ Paragon.

  • Diminishing Returns: The higher your kitten count goes, the harder it is to house, feed, and keep them happy. Pushing past 180–200 kittens takes exponentially more time than hitting 150. Therefore, fast, repeated medium-length resets are much faster than one massive multi-week run.

2. The Fast-Reset Strategy (The Speedrun Loop)

To grind 2,000 Paragon efficiently, you want to set up a cycle:

  1. Aim for the “Sweet Spot” Population: Don’t try to crawl up to 250+ kittens every time. Push your village to around 150 to 180 kittens. This gives you a solid 80 to 110 Paragon per reset without hitting the brutal late-game wall where housing and catnip management slow you down to a crawl.
  2. Hit the Tech Milestones: Run the game until you unlock Chronospheres and enough Space infrastructure to comfortably bootstrap your next run.
  3. Execute the Reset: Bank your Paragon, then start a fresh reset.
  4. Repeat: At ~90–100 Paragon per run, you only need about 20 total resets to hit your 2,000-paragon goal. With a streamlined setup, a single quick run can be pushed to the target population in just a few days or even hours of active/idle play.

3. Key Upgrades & Unlocks to Speed Up the Grind

To make each farming run lightning-fast, make sure you invest in these key areas:

  • Chronospheres (Space Tab): The most critical tool for fast resetting. When you reset, Chronospheres allow a percentage of your raw resources (like titanium, uranium, and unobtainium) and Time Crystals to carry over into the next run. The more Chronospheres you build, the less time you will spend grinding early-game resource walls on your subsequent runs.
  • Burned Paragon: Once you pass a comfortable safety buffer of unburned paragon (usually around 150–200 for the production/storage multipliers), burn the rest of your paragon. Burned Paragon gives a massive, compounding production bonus (up to a cap of around 200% bonus), which makes every subsequent farming run significantly faster.
  • Temporal Flux & Chronosurge: Use your active temporal acceleration during your farming runs to skip past the tedious mid-game resource-gathering phases.

Summary Plan:

Don’t wait for one giant run. Run a few targeted civilization cycles, push your village to ~160 kittens, bank ~90 Paragon each time while burning your excess for production speed, and let your Chronosphere carryovers turn your next run into an even faster sprint!

item.title: How to create Antimatter Storage
item.description:
To successfully push your antimatter storage cap to 5,000 (the crucial threshold required to maximize your Relic Station output), you cannot rely on antimatter production buildings alone. You have to combine specific space structures, workshop multipliers, and your global player stats.

The optimal combination to hit and surpass a 5,000 antimatter cap relies on these core pillars:

1. The Core Building: Containment Chambers

  • What they do: Containment Chambers are your primary space building for storing antimatter. Each base chamber provides +100 antimatter storage.
  • The Math: Without any modifiers, you would need 50 Containment Chambers to hit 5,000. However, because building costs scale exponentially, you want modifiers to lower how many raw chambers you actually have to build and power.

2. The Stat Multiplier: Paragon

  • The Secret Weapon: Every single point of Paragon you own gives a +0.1% storage bonus to your empire (meaning every 1,000 Paragon adds a +100% capacity multiplier to your infrastructure).
  • Why it matters: If you have 2,000 Paragon, your storage capacity across the board is doubled. This drastically reduces the number of expensive Containment Chambers you need to purchase. If your paragon count is low, grinding out a few resets for more paragon is often faster than trying to raw-resource your way through late-stage building cost scaling.

3. The Workshop Upgrade: Heatsinks

  • The Upgrade: Once you have access to advanced workshop technologies, make sure to pick up Heatsinks .
  • What it does: It increases the storage capacity of each Containment Chamber by +2% (at the cost of a slight 1% increase in energy consumption per chamber). Stacking this across all your chambers cuts down the total building count significantly.

4. Managing the Power Crunch

  • The Bottleneck: Containment Chambers consume a massive amount of energy. To support running dozens of them alongside your Sunlifters, Space Beacons, and Entangling Stations, you will need to heavily scale your power grid.
  • The Solution: Max out your Sunlifters and build Tectonics (from the Centaurus system) to shore up your energy grid, and selectively deactivate non-essential deep-space buildings (like extra Space Stations) if your power drops into the negative during winter.

Summary Checklist for 5,000 Antimatter Storage:

  1. Accumulate Paragon: Aim for a healthy Paragon pool (ideally 1,000 to 2,000+) to passively multiplier-boost your storage ceiling.
  2. Unlock & Buy Heatsinks: Research the workshop upgrade to squeeze an extra 2% storage per chamber.
  3. Scale Containment Chambers: Build out as many Containment Chambers as your energy grid and unobtainium supplies allow, letting your Paragon and Heatsinks bridge the gap to 5,000.

item.title: Paragon Farming
item.description:
When you are speed-farming Paragon, your primary goal is to bypass the early-game crawl as fast as possible so you can scale your kitten population to ~160 and reset. Because your Chronospheres carry over raw resources and Time Crystals, you won’t be starting from absolute zero, but your tech tree path still needs to be laser-focused on housing, population scaling, and space access.

Here is the most efficient sequence of technologies to research after a fresh paragon-farming reset:
item.content:encoded:
When you are speed-farming Paragon, your primary goal is to bypass the early-game crawl as fast as possible so you can scale your kitten population to ~160 and reset. Because your Chronospheres carry over raw resources and Time Crystals, you won’t be starting from absolute zero, but your tech tree path still needs to be laser-focused on housing, population scaling, and space access.

Here is the most efficient sequence of technologies to research after a fresh paragon-farming reset:

Phase 1: Securing the Basics & Resource Generation

  • Agriculture & Animal Husbandry: Mandatory first steps to unlock catnip fields, pastures, and basic food stability so your initial few kittens don’t starve.
  • Mining & Metalworking: Essential for getting your iron and titanium production online so you can start constructing basic buildings and workshops.
  • Writing: Unlocks Temples and manuscripts. (If you picked Tradition earlier, this is where your manuscript costs drop).

Phase 2: Unlocking Population & Building Expansion

  • Construction & Architecture: Unlocks concrete, warehouses, and better housing options to expand your storage caps so your Chronosphere carryovers don’t instantly overflow and get wasted.
  • Philosophy: Unlocks Temples further (for Apocrypha/Solar Revolution faith boosts) and your core government policies (like getting your happiness and production modifiers locked in).
  • Civil Service: Crucial for farming. This unlocks your Embassies and foreign trade routes. Trade is your lifeline for bypassing tedious manual resource gathering—specifically trading with the Zebras for Titanium.

Phase 3: Scaling Industry & Energy

  • Machinery & Electronics: Unlocks steamworks, factories, and the energy grid. You need electricity to power advanced housing (Mansions) and space facilities.
  • Industrialization: Accelerates your raw resource conversion rates.

Phase 4: Reaching Space & the Finish Line

  • Rocketry & Satellites: Your gateway to the Space tab. Once you unlock space, you can immediately start building:

  • Lunar Outposts and Space Elevators to flood your economy with Unobtainium and Titanium.

  • Chronospheres (if you have the Unobtainium from your carryover/shatters), which ensure your next farming run starts with even more resources.

  • Biology / Chemistry / Physics: Grab these as needed to support your space program and unlock high-tier workshop upgrades, but don’t waste precious science early on researching deep, non-essential tech trees that don’t help you push your kitten population.

Pro-Tips for Speed-Farming Tech Progression

  1. Rely on Your Carryovers: Thanks to your Chronospheres, don’t waste time manually gathering early-game wood and minerals if your carryover cache already paid out. Drop your wood burners, mines, and libraries immediately.
  2. Skip the Fluff: When speed-farming, ignore deep scientific techs that don’t feed directly into housing, space, or resource multipliers. You don’t need every single late-game tech if your only goal is hitting 160 kittens and resetting.
  3. Keep Festival Active: Run festivals back-to-back as soon as you have the culture and catnip to spare. It supercharges your production and kitten arrival rate, cutting hours off your farm loop.

  • Maximum Kittens: +2
  • Science Bonus: +50%
  • Energy Consumption: 10 Watts (Wt)

3. Critical Mechanics: Deficit vs. Manual Disabling

Because Space Stations house active citizens, managing their power profile requires careful attention to avoid catastrophic happiness drops:

  • The Energy Deficit Safety Net: If your global energy grid slips into a deficit (negative net energy), your Space Stations will experience a penalty to their Science production bonus. However, the game protects your population—the stations’ non-productive aspects remain fully functional, meaning they will continue to safely house and support your 2 kittens even if you have 0 power.
  • The Danger of Manual Disabling: If you manually toggle off or disable a Space Station to free up 10 Wt of electricity, you will instantly lose its housing capacity. This forces your population over the limit, triggering a massive unhappiness penalty of -2% happiness per homeless kitten. This severe dip can cripple your global production multipliers.

4. Planetary Cycle Modifiers (With Numerology)

If you have researched Numerology, the active planetary cycle will directly scale the efficiency of your Space Stations’ scientific capabilities:

  • Cath Cycle (⌾): Temporarily boosts the Space Station science bonus by +50%.
  • Kairo Cycle (℣): Temporarily penalises the Space Station science bonus by -25%.

item.title: Moonbase
item.description:
A Moon Base is a highly valuable, mid-to-late game Space structure located on Redmoon. Its primary function is to act as a massive storage locker, letting you scale your resource caps to bypass the harsh limits of Cath-based buildings.

1. Unlocking & Mission Requirements

To unlock the Moon Base, you must first complete the Moon Mission under your Space tab, which costs:

  • 500 Starcharts
  • 5,000 Titanium
  • 125,000 Science
  • 45,000 Oil

Completing this mission permanently unlocks both the Lunar Outpost (for gathering Unobtainium) and the Moon Base under the Redmoon celestial section.

A Moon Base is a highly valuable, mid-to-late game Space structure located on Redmoon. Its primary function is to act as a massive storage locker, letting you scale your resource caps to bypass the harsh limits of Cath-based buildings.

1. Unlocking & Mission Requirements

To unlock the Moon Base, you must first complete the Moon Mission under your Space tab, which costs:

  • 500 Starcharts
  • 5,000 Titanium
  • 125,000 Science
  • 45,000 Oil

Completing this mission permanently unlocks both the Lunar Outpost (for gathering Unobtainium) and the Moon Base under the Redmoon celestial section.

2. Construction Costs & Price Ratio

Constructing your first Moon Base requires a steep entry investment of mid-game materials:

  • 700 Starcharts
  • 9,500 Titanium
  • 250 Concrete
  • 100,000 Science
  • 50 Unobtainium
  • 70,000 Oil
  • Price Ratio: 1.12 (and 1.05 for Oil). Because it is a Space structure, it does not benefit from Bonfire metaphysics price-reduction upgrades like Golden Ratio or Renaissance.

3. Core Storage Effects

Each Moon Base provides a flat, massive upgrade to your maximum caps across almost all major resources:

  • Maximum Catnip: +45,000
  • Maximum Wood: +25,000
  • Maximum Minerals: +30,000
  • Maximum Coal: +3,500
  • Maximum Iron: +9,000
  • Maximum Titanium: +1,250
  • Maximum Oil: +3,500
  • Maximum Unobtainium: +150

4. Energy Consumption & Deficit Behavior

  • Base Power Draw: Each Moon Base consumes 10 Watts (Wt) of active power.
  • The Deficit Penalty: If your global energy grid slips into a deficit (negative energy), your active Moon Bases will still function, but if you manually disable them to save power, you will instantly lose their entire storage capacity, potentially capping your resources and causing excess stockpiles to evaporate.

5. Key Late-Game Synergies & Upgrades

Because Moon Bases are one of only two structures in the entire game that expand your base Unobtainium capacity (the other being Cryostations), scaling them is critical to executing the late-game Chronosphere loop. You can exponentially boost their effectiveness using these key upgrades:

  • Antimatter Bases (Workshop Upgrade): Costs 15 Eludium and 250 Antimatter. This permanently slashes the energy consumption of your Moon Bases by 50%, bringing their power draw down to 5 Wt each.
  • AI Bases (Workshop Upgrade): Unlocked after Antimatter Bases. This links your Moon Bases to your quantum computing grid, causing every active AI Core to increase the storage capacity of your Moon Bases by +10% (which rises to +11% if you have the Transkittenism policy active).
  • Spaceports: Upgrading your Warehouses into Spaceports provides a passive +0.85% bonus to all Moon Base storage capacities per Spaceport built.
  • Global Multipliers: In the endgame, the flat storage additions of your Moon Bases are multiplied heavily by your Paragon reserves (+0.1% per point), Event Horizons (+10% global storage per level), and Void Rifts (+2% global storage per level).

  • Science: 100k
  • Oil: 55k
  • Price Ratio: 1.12 (and 1.05 for Oil). Like all Space structures, Lunar Outposts do not benefit from Bonfire tab price reductions (such as Golden Ratio or Renaissance).

2. Core Effects & Consumption

Each active Lunar Outpost operates with the following rates:

A Lunar Outpost is an orbital structure located on Redmoon (accessible after completing the Moon Mission). It serves as your primary gateway to the late-game economy, acting as the baseline source for gathering Unobtainium.

1. Construction Costs & Price Ratio

  • Starcharts: 650
  • Uranium: 500
  • Alloy: 750
  • Concrete: 150
  • Science: 100k
  • Oil: 55k
  • Price Ratio: 1.12 (and 1.05 for Oil). Like all Space structures, Lunar Outposts do not benefit from Bonfire tab price reductions (such as Golden Ratio or Renaissance).

2. Core Effects & Consumption

Each active Lunar Outpost operates with the following rates:

  • Unobtainium Production: +0.035 / second
  • Uranium Consumption: -1.75 / second
  • Energy Consumption: 5 Watts (Wt) of power

If you do not have enough active Uranium to support the outpost, it will still run slowly (at a rate bottlenecked by your incoming Uranium) rather than shutting down entirely.

3. Scaling and Production Boosts

You can dramatically increase your Unobtainium yield per outpost through several synergistic mechanisms:

  • Microwarp Reactors (Workshop Upgrade): Costs 50 Eludium. Once researched, it boosts the Unobtainium production of all Lunar Outposts by +75%.
  • Space Manufacturing (Workshop Upgrade): Allows your Factories to amplify the effects of your Space Elevators (+1% space structure bonus each) and Orbital Arrays (+2% bonus each). This compounding space production multiplier is the main way to skyrocket your overall Unobtainium yield.
  • Cycle Modifiers (with Numerology):
    • Charon Cycle (⍙): Temporarily reduces Unobtainium production by -10%.
    • Redmoon Cycle (⍜): Temporarily boosts Unobtainium production by +20%.
    • Strategic Tip: If you have both Numerology and Numeromancy researched and run a Festival during the Redmoon Cycle, your Unobtainium production receives a massive ~2.5x global multiplier. Many players use the Chronoforge to skip seasons and stay inside the Redmoon cycle indefinitely to farm Unobtainium.

4. Overcoming the Uranium Deficit

The primary bottleneck when starting up Lunar Outposts is their heavy Uranium consumption. Because one outpost consumes Uranium 140 times faster than a single standard Accelerator can produce it (+0.0125/sec), you will quickly deplete your reserves. To counteract this:

  1. Trade with Dragons: Continually trade your Titanium with Dragons to purchase massive amounts of Uranium to feed your outposts.
  2. Planet Crackers: Build Planet Crackers on Dune (which produce +1.5/sec Uranium) to actively balance out the drain.
  3. Redshift (Offline progression): If offline progression is enabled in your settings, the game prevents your resources from dropping to zero during offline calculation. Consequently, your Lunar Outposts will run as if they have infinite Uranium, allowing you to generate Unobtainium at maximum speed while offline.

1. Unlocking & Costs

A Research Vessel is an advanced, orbital structure constructed on the aquatic planet Piscine. It serves as a major scientific booster and is the premier mid-to-late game structure for passive starchart generation.

Here is a full breakdown of its costs, effects, upgrades, and cycle modifiers:

1. Unlocking & Costs

To construct a Research Vessel, you must first reach its home planet by launching the Piscine Mission under your Space tab. Once unlocked, each Research Vessel has the following base costs:

  • 100 Starcharts
  • 2,500 Alloy
  • 12,500 Titanium
  • 250 Kerosene
  • Price Ratio: 1.15. Like all other space structures, Research Vessels do not benefit from Bonfire-tab price ratio reductions (such as Golden Ratio or Renaissance), meaning each subsequent build strictly costs 15% more.

2. Core Effects

Each active Research Vessel provides:

  • Max Science +10,000: This significant boost helps you dramatically expand your overall science capacity to unlock late-game exometallurgy and exophysics milestones.
  • Starchart Production (+0.05/sec): It serves as an incredibly efficient, automated source of starcharts, which is key for funding further space exploration.

3. Upgrades & Synergies

You can drastically amplify the Max Science capacity of your vessels by purchasing specialized antimatter and void-themed Workshop upgrades:

  • Antimatter Reactors: Boosts maximum Science from Research Vessels and Space Beacons by +95%.
  • Advanced AM Reactors: Upgrades this bonus to +150%.
  • Void Reactors: Upgrades the bonus to a massive +400%.

4. Cycle Multipliers (With Numerology)

If you have researched the Numerology metaphysics upgrade, the active planetary cycle will directly scale the starchart generation of your vessels:

  • Piscine Cycle (): Provides a +50% boost to Research Vessel starchart production.
  • Yarn Cycle (⍧): Imposes a -50% penalty to Research Vessel starchart production.

5. Black Sky Challenge Interaction

During the Black Sky challenge, Research Vessels do not produce any starcharts. This design prevents you from easily bypassing the challenge’s primary bottleneck, forcing you to find alternative methods for accumulating starcharts.

🛰️ I can break down the requirements and costs of the next planetary mission, Terminus, and its Cryostation structures to help you plan your next step into deep space.

item.title: Containment Chamber
item.description:
In Kittens Game, the Containment Chamber is an essential mid-to-late game Space structure located under the Helios mission tab. It is the primary means of scaling your maximum capacity for Antimatter.

Costs and Scaling

  • Base Cost: 500,000 Science and 2,500 Kerosene.
  • Price Ratio: 1.125.
  • The Space Penalty: Because it is a Space structure, Containment Chambers do not benefit from Bonfire metaphysics price-reduction upgrades (such as Golden Ratio or Renaissance).

Core Effects & The Power Problem

  • Antimatter Storage: Each built chamber increases your maximum antimatter capacity by +100.
  • Energy Consumption: Each active chamber consumes a massive 50 Watts (Wt) of power.

Because of this steep energy requirement, Containment Chambers quickly become a massive strain on your active power grid. If your power grid falls into a deficit (negative energy), your Sunlifters will completely stop generating antimatter. Managing your energy surplus with clean power sources like Sunlifters (generating 30 Wt each) or Centaurus Tectonics (generating 25 Wt each) is crucial to keeping these chambers running.

Because of this steep energy requirement, Containment Chambers quickly become a massive strain on your active power grid. If your power grid falls into a deficit (negative energy), your Sunlifters will completely stop generating antimatter. Managing your energy surplus with clean power sources like Sunlifters (generating 30 Wt each) or Centaurus Tectonics (generating 25 Wt each) is crucial to keeping these chambers running.

Synergy with Heatsinks

Building Heatsinks (also under Helios) directly enhances your existing chambers:

  • Each Heatsink increases the antimatter storage capacity of your Containment Chambers by +2%.
  • However, each Heatsink also increases their energy consumption by +1%.

Strategic Value: Reaching the 5,000 Antimatter Cap

The ultimate goal of building Containment Chambers is to raise your maximum antimatter capacity to 5,000. This threshold is critical for the automated endgame Relic Engine:

  1. Unlocking Relic Stations: You must have a maximum capacity of at least 5,000 antimatter to buy the Relic Station upgrade in your Workshop.
  2. Avoiding the Relic Penalty: If your maximum storage capacity is below 5,000, your relic station production is penalized by -0.02% for every single unit of capacity you are short of that threshold.

To efficiently hit this 5,000 cap, you must balance the Science cost of your chambers against the Thorium and Relic costs of Heatsinks. The most common and recommended configuration is to build 29 Containment Chambers and 34 Heatsinks (which requires 13.5M Science and 526k Thorium). While your science cap may seem like a barrier to building this many chambers, it can be easily expanded by compiling massive stacks of Compendiums.

🧩 Since Kerosene and Science are the key gating resources for building your chambers, we can calculate the best configurations for your Libraries, Data Centers, and Bio Labs to help you expand your Science cap comfortably.

2. Effects & Mechanics

Heatsinks do not store antimatter on their own; instead, they enhance your existing Containment Chambers:
item.content:encoded:
In Kittens Game, a Heatsink is an advanced Space structure located in the Helios section of your Space tab. It is officially unlocked once you complete the Helios Mission, which costs 3,000 Starcharts, 15,000 Titanium, 250,000 Science, and 1,250 Kerosene.

1. Construction Costs & Scaling

  • Base Cost: 125,000 Science, 12,500 Thorium, 1 Relic, and 5,000 Kerosene.
  • Price Ratio: 1.12. Like other Space structures, it does not benefit from Bonfire metaphysics price reductions, meaning every subsequent Heatsink will strictly cost 12% more than the last.

2. Effects & Mechanics

Heatsinks do not store antimatter on their own; instead, they enhance your existing Containment Chambers:

  • Antimatter Storage Capacity (+2% per Heatsink): This percentage boost is applied to your Containment Chambers’ base storage (each base chamber holds 100 antimatter).
  • Containment Chamber Energy Consumption (+1% per Heatsink): Each level increases the power consumption of your active Containment Chambers, which normally require a hefty 50 Watts (Wt) of power each.

Additionally, Heatsinks are highly useful in the late-game for increasing your Chronoforge heat cooldown, allowing you to dissipate heat faster when performing mass time-skips.

3. Strategic Importance: Smashing the 5,000 Antimatter Wall

The primary purpose of mass-producing Heatsinks in the late game is to help expand your maximum Antimatter capacity to 5,000. This threshold is crucial for two reasons:

  1. Unlocking Relic Stations: You must have a maximum capacity of at least 5,000 antimatter to purchase the Relic Station upgrade in your Workshop (which officially kicks off your automated endgame Relic engine).
  2. Avoiding the Relic Penalty: If your maximum antimatter storage cap is below 5,000, your relic station production is penalized by -0.02% for every single unit of capacity you are short of that threshold.

Optimal Setup Configurations

To reach the 5,000 antimatter storage limit, players must balance the high Science cost of Containment Chambers (CCs) against the high Thorium and Relic cost of Heatsinks. For example, in an Iron Will endless run, two common efficient configurations to reach the 5k cap are:

  • 34 Heatsinks (costing roughly 526,000 Thorium in total) and 29 Containment Chambers (costing 13.5M Science).
  • 37 Heatsinks and 28 Containment Chambers, though the Thorium costs for this alternative path are often considered too prohibitive.

4. The Energy Conundrum

Because Heatsinks increase the power draw of your Containment Chambers, expanding your storage cap this way will put an immense strain on your active energy grid. You must ensure you have highly built-up energy sources—such as Sunlifters on Helios (which generate 30 Wt) or Tectonic structures on Centaurus—to keep your grid positive. If your active power grid slips into a deficit, your Sunlifters will not produce any antimatter.

3. The Relic Station Upgrade (Type 1 Relic Engine)

The primary goal of building Space Beacons in the late game is to host Relic Stations (a Workshop upgrade costing 100 Eludium and 5,000 Antimatter). Once researched, your Space Beacons will automatically reverse engineer and generate 0.01 Relics per day.

This passive relic generation can be scaled exponentially through several synergistic mechanics:

  • Black Nexus Synergy: Each level of Black Nexus boosts your Space Beacon relic production by +10% per active Black Pyramid.
  • Hashes/Hashrate Synergy: By running Entanglement Stations, you generate Hashes to gain hashrate levels. Each level grants a multiplicative +25% bonus to Space Beacon relic production.
  • The Antimatter Storage Requirement: Relic production scales dynamically with your maximum antimatter capacity. If your maximum antimatter storage cap is below 5,000, your relic production is penalized by -0.02% for every single unit you are short of that threshold.

4. Science Cap Multipliers

You can dramatically boost the +25k Science storage bonus of your Space Beacons by purchasing specialized Workshop upgrades:

  • Antimatter Reactors: Boosts maximum Science from Research Vessels and Space Beacons by +95%.
  • Advanced AM Reactors: Upgrades this bonus to +150%.
  • Void Reactors: Upgrades this bonus to a massive +400%.

5. Black Sky Challenge

Space Beacons are also the focal point of the Black Sky challenge (where astronomical events are entirely disabled). To successfully complete this challenge, your ultimate goal is to build at least one Space Beacon (with the requirement increasing by +1 beacon for each subsequent completion of the challenge).

item.title: Hydroponics

To build Hydroponics, you must first complete the Yarn Mission and research the corresponding technology on your Science tree:

  • Hydroponics Technology: Costs 1M Science and 25 Relics (unlocked by Terraformation).
  • Structure Construction Cost: Each Hydroponics building costs 1 Unobtainium and 500 Kerosene.
  • Price Ratio: 1.15. Because it is a space structure, it does not benefit from Bonfire metaphysics price reductions.

2. Core Effects & Mechanics

Each Hydroponics station provides three distinct multipliers:
item.content:encoded:
Building on our look at Yarn’s space housing, Hydroponics is an advanced, late-game space structure constructed on the planet Yarn. It acts as a massive scaling mechanism for both your food supply and population capacity in the late game.

1. Unlocking & Construction Costs

To build Hydroponics, you must first complete the Yarn Mission and research the corresponding technology on your Science tree:

  • Hydroponics Technology: Costs 1M Science and 25 Relics (unlocked by Terraformation).
  • Structure Construction Cost: Each Hydroponics building costs 1 Unobtainium and 500 Kerosene.
  • Price Ratio: 1.15. Because it is a space structure, it does not benefit from Bonfire metaphysics price reductions.

2. Core Effects & Mechanics

Each Hydroponics station provides three distinct multipliers:

  • Catnip Production (+2.5% per building): Grants a global multiplier to your catnip generation.
  • Catnip Storage Capacity (+10% per building): Expands your maximum catnip cap. This bonus stacks additively with the Refrigeration workshop upgrade (+75% max catnip). For example, if you have researched Refrigeration and own 50 Hydroponics, your global catnip storage capacity is boosted by +575%.
  • Terraforming Station Synergy (+1.0% per building): Permanently increases the kitten housing bonus of your Terraforming Stations by +1.0% per structure.

3. Strategic Late-Game Value

Taming the Happiness Consumption Spike

As your civilization matures, keeping your kittens happy is vital to scaling your global output. However, keeping happiness high (e.g., above 100%) dramatically increases catnip consumption. A community sitting at 420% happiness suffers a massive 320% increase in kitten catnip consumption.

By mass-producing Hydroponics, you can compound your passive food production so heavily that you can easily sustain hundreds of hyper-productive, highly happy kittens without risking sudden winter starvations.

The Yarn & Piscine Cycle Factors

If you have researched Numerology, your active planetary cycle will directly scale the efficiency of your hydroponic farms:

  • Yarn Cycle (⍧): Temporarily boosts Hydroponics catnip production by +100%.
  • Piscine Cycle (): Temporarily penalises Hydroponics catnip production by -50%.

Orbital Population Scaling

By pairing your Hydroponics with Terraforming Stations, you can squeeze maximum housing out of orbit. Compounding this loop is one of the premier ways to push your overall kitten population well past standard limits. This populates your priestly ranks in the late game, enabling you to farm massive amounts of Faith and Paragon during resets.

item.title: Terraforming Station
item.description:
Terraforming Stations are highly advanced, late-game space structures located on the planet Yarn. They act as a specialized way to expand your maximum population limit from orbit.

Here is a complete breakdown of how to unlock, fund, and optimize these structures:

Before you can build Terraforming Stations, you must travel to their home planet and research the necessary technology:

  • Prerequisite Tech: Research the Terraformation technology, which costs 750,000 Science and 5 Relics.
  • Base Cost:
    • 25 Antimatter
    • 5,000 Uranium
    • 5,000 Kerosene
  • Price Ratio: 1.25. Because it is a Space structure, Terraforming Stations do not benefit from Metaphysics price ratio reductions (such as Golden Ratio or Renaissance). Each subsequent station will strictly cost 25% more than the last.

2. Core Effect & Lore

  • Max Kittens +1: Every station you build permanently increases your maximum kitten capacity by 1.
  • Lore Description: “Explode a charge of antimatter to melt yarn ice and throw oxygen into the atmosphere.”

3. Endgame Synergies

While a flat +1 kitten cap per station is modest given the high resource costs, you can amplify their housing capacity using late-game upgrades:

  • Price Ratio: 1.25. Because it is a Space structure, Terraforming Stations do not benefit from Metaphysics price ratio reductions (such as Golden Ratio or Renaissance). Each subsequent station will strictly cost 25% more than the last.

2. Core Effect & Lore

  • Max Kittens +1: Every station you build permanently increases your maximum kitten capacity by 1.
  • Lore Description: “Explode a charge of antimatter to melt yarn ice and throw oxygen into the atmosphere.”

3. Endgame Synergies

While a flat +1 kitten cap per station is modest given the high resource costs, you can amplify their housing capacity using late-game upgrades:

  • Hydroponics Boost (+1.0% per structure): Building Hydroponics on Yarn (which costs 1 Unobtainium and 500 Kerosene) permanently increases the kitten housing bonus of your Terraforming Stations by +1.0% per Hydroponics structure. Compounding these two structures is one of the premier ways to squeeze extra population out of your space empire.
  • Post Apocalypse Policy Reward (+0.1% bonus): Completing the Post Apocalypse challenge unlocks a special late-game policy that awards a permanent +0.1% housing bonus specifically to your Terraforming Stations.

item.title: Entanglement Station
item.description:
Building on our recent discussion about the AI Core balancing act, the Entanglement Station is a highly specialized late-game space structure located in the Charon planetary system.

Its primary function is to generate entangled particles (qbits) to drive your quantum computing systems, enabling you to “perform a cryptographical attack on the elders’ encryption algorithms”.

1. Unlocking and Costs

To construct Entanglement Stations, you must first research the Quantum Cryptography technology (which costs 1.25M Science and 1,024 Relics).
item.content:encoded:
Building on our recent discussion about the AI Core balancing act, the Entanglement Station is a highly specialized late-game space structure located in the Charon planetary system.

Its primary function is to generate entangled particles (qbits) to drive your quantum computing systems, enabling you to “perform a cryptographical attack on the elders’ encryption algorithms”.

1. Unlocking and Costs

To construct Entanglement Stations, you must first research the Quantum Cryptography technology (which costs 1.25M Science and 1,024 Relics).

Once unlocked, each station is highly resource-intensive to build:

  • Base Cost: 1,250 Relics, 5,250 Antimatter, and 5,000 Eludium.
  • Price Ratio: 1.15. (As a space structure, it does not benefit from Metaphysics price reductions).

2. Core Operations & Stats

  • Energy Consumption: Consumes 25 Watts (Wt) of active power.
  • Gigaflop Consumption: Consumes 0.1 Gigaflops per tick.
  • Hash Production: Generates 0.1 Hashes per tick.

3. Strategic Value: The Hashrate Relic Multiplier

Hashes produced by the Entanglement Station are used to reverse engineer relics. This process establishes Hashrate Levels. Each Hashrate Level provides a multiplicative +25% bonus to your automated relic production from Space Beacons upgraded with Relic Stations.

This makes Entanglement Stations a vital tool for exponentially scaling your Type 1 Relic Engine in the late game.

4. Cycle Multipliers (With Numerology)

If you have researched Numerology, the active planetary cycle will directly modify how much processing power your stations consume:

  • Charon Cycle (⍙): Gigaflop consumption is increased by +100% (consuming 0.2 Gflops/tick).
  • Redmoon Cycle (⍜): Gigaflop consumption is reduced by -50% (consuming only 0.05 Gflops/tick).

5. The Gigaflop Balancing Act

Because a single AI Core produces +0.02 Gigaflops per tick and a standard Entanglement Station consumes 0.1 Gigaflops per tick, maintaining a ratio of 5 AI Cores to 1 Entanglement Station keeps your Gigaflop accumulation flat. If you lack the Transkittenism policy, failing to balance this ratio will cause Gigaflops to pile up, increasing your AI level and eventually triggering the AI Apocalypse at AI Level 15.

item.title: Tectonic
item.description:
Tectonic is an advanced, power-generating Space structure located in the Centaurus System. It allows your feline civilization to tap into massive amounts of geothermal energy by literally ripping open the planet near the star Centaurus.

1. Cost and Scaling

Constructing a Tectonic structure represents a major milestone due to its high, premium resource requirements:

  • Base Cost: 600,000 Science, 500 Antimatter, and 75,000 Thorium.
  • Prerequisite: You must first research the Terraformation technology to unlock it.
  • Price Ratio: 1.25.
  • The Space Penalty: Like all Space structures, Tectonics do not benefit from Metaphysics price ratio reductions (such as Golden Ratio or Renaissance). Each subsequent level will strictly cost 25% more than the last.

2. Effects and Synergies

  • High-Yield Power Generation: Each active Tectonic structure produces a flat +25 Watts (Wt) of energy to help power your grid.
  • Molten Core Synergy: As we recently discussed, every level of Molten Core you purchase in the Centaurus System permanently improves the energy output of your Tectonic structures by +5%.
  • Energy Challenge Requirement: Building at least one Tectonic structure is a mandatory milestone to successfully complete the Energy Challenge.

3. Strategic Value and the Late-Game Transition

In the mid-to-late game, Tectonics are highly sought after because they represent one of the most concentrated, reliable power sources available. However, their relative value shifts as you transition into the deep endgame:

item.title: Molten Core
item.description:
What is Molten Core?

Molten Core is an advanced Space structure located in the Centaurus System (unlocked via the Centaurus Mission). It serves as a power-amplification mechanism for your interstellar energy grid.

  • Prerequisite Technology: Exophysics (which costs 25M Science and 500 Relics to research).
  • The Effect: Every level of Molten Core purchased permanently improves the energy production of your Centaurus Tectonic structures by +5%. Since a base Tectonic structure generates 25 Wt of energy, Molten Cores help you squeeze massive amounts of additional power out of your existing setup.

Cost and Scaling

  • Base Cost (Level 1): 25M Science and 5M Uranium.
  • Price Ratio: 1.25.
  • The Space Structure Penalty: Unlike your Bonfire tab buildings, Space structures do not benefit from Metaphysics price ratio reductions (such as Golden Ratio or Renaissance). The price ratio remains a flat, unforgiving 1.25 multiplier for every single level you buy.
  • The Scaling Problem: Because of this aggressive scaling, the Science and Uranium costs quickly balloon. For example, by the time you want to purchase Level 11, the cost will have soared to over 230M Science, along with a massive Uranium requirement.

How to Overcome the Science and Uranium Bottlenecks

Many players hit a massive wall when trying to purchase multiple levels of Molten Core. To reach the extreme science and uranium caps needed, you must stack several multiplicative systems:
item.content:encoded:
What is Molten Core?

Molten Core is an advanced Space structure located in the Centaurus System (unlocked via the Centaurus Mission). It serves as a power-amplification mechanism for your interstellar energy grid.

  • Prerequisite Technology: Exophysics (which costs 25M Science and 500 Relics to research).
  • The Effect: Every level of Molten Core purchased permanently improves the energy production of your Centaurus Tectonic structures by +5%. Since a base Tectonic structure generates 25 Wt of energy, Molten Cores help you squeeze massive amounts of additional power out of your existing setup.

Cost and Scaling

  • Base Cost (Level 1): 25M Science and 5M Uranium.
  • Price Ratio: 1.25.
  • The Space Structure Penalty: Unlike your Bonfire tab buildings, Space structures do not benefit from Metaphysics price ratio reductions (such as Golden Ratio or Renaissance). The price ratio remains a flat, unforgiving 1.25 multiplier for every single level you buy.
  • The Scaling Problem: Because of this aggressive scaling, the Science and Uranium costs quickly balloon. For example, by the time you want to purchase Level 11, the cost will have soared to over 230M Science, along with a massive Uranium requirement.

How to Overcome the Science and Uranium Bottlenecks

Many players hit a massive wall when trying to purchase multiple levels of Molten Core. To reach the extreme science and uranium caps needed, you must stack several multiplicative systems:

1. Smashing the Uranium Cap (The True Bottleneck)

Uranium is generally considered the hardest limit to expand for Molten Core. You can expand your maximum Uranium storage using these strategies:

  • Expand Base Storage: Max out Reactors (+250 max Uranium each) and Cryostations on T-Minus (+5,000 max Uranium each).
  • Compile Paragon: Paragon provides a passive +0.1% storage bonus per unit (and Burned Paragon is twice as effective after you reach the Dark Future).
  • Stack Storage Modifiers:
    • Build Sunforges in Helios (+1% metal and Uranium storage per level).
    • Buy Event Horizons (+10% global storage ratio per level) and Void Rifts (+2% global storage ratio per level).
  • Time skip to the T-Minus Cycle: The T-Minus planetary cycle provides a temporary +20% storage boost specifically to Cryostations.

2. Scaling your Science Cap

Unlocking a 250M+ Science cap is highly achievable if you focus on your library and computer networks:

  • Craft Compendiums: Every Compendium you hold in stock adds a flat +10 to your maximum Science cap (up to 100% of your building-based storage). Buy Codex Levi and Black Libraries t your Libraries:** Convert Libraries into Data Centers and purchase the Uplink upgrade (+1% max science per Bio Lab) and Machine Learning upgrade (+10% effectiveness per AI Core).
  • Max out Observatories: Upgrading them with Astrolabe (+50% storage), plus Titanium, Unobtainium, and Eludium Reflectors, will add +2% Library/Data Center effectiveness per Observatory.
  • Boost Space Science Structures: Construct Research Vessels (+10k base Science) and Space Beacons (+25k base Science). Maximize them using Antimatter Reactors (+95% science), Advanced AM Reactors (+150%), and Void Reactors (+400% science).

Is Molten Core Worth It?

While Molten Core is highly beneficial for boosting Tectonic energy, it is generally considered a late-endgame luxury. By the time you can comfortably afford high levels of Molten Core, you will likely have established a high-level Shatter Engine. In the very late game, skipping thousands of years will make your Hawking Radiation (HR) Harvesters on Umbra (which scale based on the Dark Future years) produce far more energy than Centaurus Tectonics, reducing your dependency on Molten Cores.

⚡ I can help you check your current power consumers and calculate your energy grid’s balance to see if it’s time to transition to Hawking Radiation Harvesters.

item.title: Void Resonator
item.description:
Continuing our journey through late-game temporal structures, the Void Resonator is an advanced, game-changing building located under the Void Space section of your Time tab. It is unlocked after researching the Paradox Theory technology (which costs 1,000,000 Science, 40 Time Crystals, and 250 Void).

Its primary function is to transform how you generate religious prestige in the late game by creating a powerful bridge between time-skipping and faith.

The Order of the Void Synergy

The Void Resonator works hand-in-hand with the Order of the Void metaphysics upgrade. Normally, Order of the Void passively converts 10% of your faith production directly into Worship.
item.content:encoded:
Continuing our journey through late-game temporal structures, the Void Resonator is an advanced, game-changing building located under the Void Space section of your Time tab. It is unlocked after researching the Paradox Theory technology (which costs 1,000,000 Science, 40 Time Crystals, and 250 Void).

Its primary function is to transform how you generate religious prestige in the late game by creating a powerful bridge between time-skipping and faith.

The Order of the Void Synergy

The Void Resonator works hand-in-hand with the Order of the Void metaphysics upgrade. Normally, Order of the Void passively converts 10% of your faith production directly into Worship.

When you build Void Resonators, they multiply this effect. The game calculates the conversion using the following formula: {Worship Generated} = {Faith Production} * 0.1 * (1 + ({Void Resonators} * 0.1))

In other words, each Void Resonator you construct adds a flat +10% bonus to your passive Order of the Void conversion rate.

The Game-Changer: Time-Skip Integration

Crucially, Void Resonators allow the Order of the Void conversion to trigger every time you combust a Time Crystal to skip a year.

Normally, time-skipping bypasses passive production ticks. But with Void Resonators active:

  1. Every time you shatter a Time Crystal, you advance the calendar by one year.
  2. The game calculates your massive yearly faith production.
  3. The Void Resonators instantly inject a huge portion of that faith directly into your Worship pool.

Strategic Late-Game Value

When you establish a high-level Shatter Engine (Resource Retrieval + Chrono Furnaces), you will be skipping thousands of years in rapid succession. Void Resonators turn these time-skips into a passive faith-farming machine.

Instead of waiting on manual praises, simply skipping years will passively flood your pool with billions of units of Worship. This makes pushing your civilization up to Transcendence Tier 20 and beyond incredibly fast and effortless, permanently compounding your global production multipliers via the Solar Revolution bonus.

item.title: Void Rift
item.description:
A Void Rift is an advanced, late-game structure found in the Void Space section of your Time tab. Building on our recent look at Void Hoovers, these rifts are vital for scaling your global storage capacities and power output to break through deep late-game bottlenecks.

Unlocking & Costs

To construct a Void Rift, you must first research the Void Space technology and purchase the Void Aspiration workshop upgrade (which costs 15 Time Crystals and 2,000 Antimatter).
item.content:encoded:
A Void Rift is an advanced, late-game structure found in the Void Space section of your Time tab. Building on our recent look at Void Hoovers, these rifts are vital for scaling your global storage capacities and power output to break through deep late-game bottlenecks.

Unlocking & Costs

To construct a Void Rift, you must first research the Void Space technology and purchase the Void Aspiration workshop upgrade (which costs 15 Time Crystals and 2,000 Antimatter).

Once unlocked, your first Void Rift costs:

  • 75 Void
  • Price Ratio: 1.3 — Like other void space structures, the cost scales aggressively with each subsequent build.

Core Effects

Each built Void Rift provides two highly valuable, passive multipliers:

  1. Global Resource Storage Ratio (+2% per Rift): This increases your maximum capacity for every single resource in the game. Crucially, this bonus stacks additively with Event Horizons (which grant a massive +10% storage ratio per level) and multiplicatively with all other storage bonuses, such as your Paragon multipliers.
  2. HR Harvester Energy Boost (+10% per Rift): It permanently boosts the energy production of your Hawking Radiation (HR) Harvesters (located on Umbra) by +10% per rift. Because HR Harvesters automatically generate more energy the further you skip into the “Dark Future,” Void Rifts make them highly competitive late-game power generators.

Strategic Endgame Value

Though a 2% storage multiplier may seem modest initially, Void Rifts become indispensable in the deep endgame for two main reasons:

  • Shattering the Unobtainium Capacity Wall: To execute “positive resets” (where the resources carried over exceed the cost of constructing your next set of Chronospheres), you need to amass billions of units of Unobtainium. Since Moon Bases and Cryostations are the only buildings that grant base Unobtainium storage, Void Rifts and Event Horizons are the primary tools used to compound and scale your storage caps high enough to support 70+ Chronospheres.
  • Balancing Your Power Grid: As you scale your Gigaflop-producing AI Cores and Entanglement Stations, your active energy consumption will skyrocket. Investing in Void Rifts allows you to rely on HR Harvesters to generate massive amounts of power, keeping your grid positive even while running heavy quantum computing pipelines.

  • Once Void Aspiration is purchased, the Void Hoover (along with Void Rifts) is permanently unlocked for construction.

2. Costs & Price Ratio

Constructing a Void Hoover requires premium late-game resources:

  • Price Ratio: 1.25 — Like many time-based structures, every subsequent Void Hoover you construct will cost 25% more than the previous level.

3. The Effect & Strategic Value

  • The Effect: Every level of Void Hoover permanently increases the maximum amount of Void you might gain on a Temporal Paradox day by +1.

Active Chronospheres occasionally trigger a Temporal Paradox event. Because Void is a strictly capped and slow-to-generate resource in the mid-to-late game, Void Hoovers are essential for amplifying your Void income during these paradox windows. This accelerated Void generation feeds directly into other powerful endgame systems, allowing you to stockpile the massive amounts of Void needed to buy Void Rifts (which expand global storage capacity) and execute the Cryo Engine strategy (which requires 500 Void per repaired Cryochamber).

item.title: Resource Retrieval
item.description:
Resource Retrieval is an advanced, late-game Time upgrade that serves as the foundation for the self-sustaining endgame economy.

Here is a complete breakdown of its mechanics, costs, and strategic value:

1. How to Unlock It

To unlock Resource Retrieval, you must advance deep into the temporal science and tech trees:

  • First, research Void Space (requires Tachyon Theory).
  • Then research Paradox Theory (costs 1,000,000 Science, 40 Time Crystals, and 250 Void).
  • This allows you to research Paradoxal Knowledge science (requires 250 Void), which officially unlocks Resource Retrieval under the Time tab.

2. Costs and Scaling

  • Base Cost: 1,000 Time Crystals (TCs).
  • Price Ratio: 1.3. Because of this steep price ratio, subsequent levels become progressively more expensive very quickly (e.g., level 2 costs 1,300 TCs, level 3 costs 1,690 TCs).

3. Core Effects and Calculations

Each level of Resource Retrieval lets you retrieve 1% of your yearly resource production every single time you shatter/combust a Time Crystal.
item.content:encoded:
Resource Retrieval is an advanced, late-game Time upgrade that serves as the foundation for the self-sustaining endgame economy.

Here is a complete breakdown of its mechanics, costs, and strategic value:

1. How to Unlock It

To unlock Resource Retrieval, you must advance deep into the temporal science and tech trees:

  • First, research Void Space (requires Tachyon Theory).
  • Then research Paradox Theory (costs 1,000,000 Science, 40 Time Crystals, and 250 Void).
  • This allows you to research Paradoxal Knowledge science (requires 250 Void), which officially unlocks Resource Retrieval under the Time tab.

2. Costs and Scaling

  • Base Cost: 1,000 Time Crystals (TCs).
  • Price Ratio: 1.3. Because of this steep price ratio, subsequent levels become progressively more expensive very quickly (e.g., level 2 costs 1,300 TCs, level 3 costs 1,690 TCs).

3. Core Effects and Calculations

Each level of Resource Retrieval lets you retrieve 1% of your yearly resource production every single time you shatter/combust a Time Crystal.

  • The “Yearly” Formula: The game calculates your “yearly” production of resources (such as Unobtainium or Alicorns) based on your active net production per second. Normally, this is your per-second rate divided by 800.
  • Chronosurge Boost: If you have purchased the Chronosurge workshop upgrade, your yearly resource calculations are improved—they are calculated as your per-second rate divided by 533, resulting in a much larger payout per skip.
  • Blazar Synergy: If you reach Transcendence-tier 15, you can purchase Blazars (costing 50,000 Relics). Blazars permanently and multiplicatively boost the resource yield from each level of your Resource Retrieval.

4. Strategic Value: The “Shatter Engine”

The ultimate goal of purchasing Resource Retrieval is to build an infinite Shatter Engine, transitioning your civilization away from waiting on slow, passive resource generation:

  • The Infinite Loop: When you shatter a Time Crystal to skip a year, you instantly receive a massive dump of resources (especially Unobtainium and Alicorns). With enough levels of Resource Retrieval, the Unobtainium you retrieve can be traded to the Leviathans (Elders) and the Alicorns sacrificed to yield more than 1 Time Crystal in return.
  • The Sweet Spot: Players generally aim to reach level 6 or 7 of Resource Retrieval (requiring roughly 12,000 TCs in total) to cleanly break even and execute this loop indefinitely. If your base Unobtainium production is exceptionally high (over 100/sec), you can sometimes initiate the loop as early as level 3 to 5.
  • Chronoforge Automation: Once your Shatter Engine is profitable, you can scale your Chrono Furnaces to quickly dissipate heat, allowing you to skip thousands of years in rapid succession to generate massive, overcapped stockpiles of resources.

⏳ We can calculate the exact Time Crystal costs required to reach your target level of Resource Retrieval, or look at how to optimize your Unobtainium capacity to prepare for the transition.

item.title: Controlled Delay
item.description:
What is Controlled Delay?

In Kittens Game, Controlled Delay is an advanced upgrade located in the Chronoforge section of your Time tab. It is designed to help you pace out automated time-skips in the late-to-end game.

Prerequisites & Unlocking

Because Controlled Delay is a Chronoforge upgrade, it is hidden until you unlock its parent section:

  1. Tachyon Theory: You must first research the Tachyon Theory technology on your Science tree (which requires researching Chronophysics beforehand).
  2. Chronoforge Workshop Upgrade: Once Tachyon Theory is researched, you must purchase the Chronoforge upgrade in your Workshop. This costs 500,000 Science, 5 Relics, and 10 Time Crystals and officially unlocks the Chronoforge sub-section on your Time tab.

Once the Chronoforge section is unlocked, Controlled Delay will be visible and available for purchase.

What is Controlled Delay?

In Kittens Game, Controlled Delay is an advanced upgrade located in the Chronoforge section of your Time tab. It is designed to help you pace out automated time-skips in the late-to-end game.

Once the Chronoforge section is unlocked, Controlled Delay will be visible and available for purchase.

Cost & Price Ratio

  • Time Crystals: 1
  • Gears: 10
  • Price Ratio: 1.0 — Crucially, because the price ratio is a flat 1.0, the cost of this upgrade never increases as you purchase subsequent levels.

Effects & Strategic Value

  • Paced Automation: Each purchased level of Controlled Delay forces your Chrono Furnace automation to wait 0.2 seconds between using 500% fuel to trigger a time-skip.
  • Active Gameplay Window: This upgrade was explicitly created to allow you to perform meaningful in-game actions (such as praising, adoring, or trading) during Chrono Furnace automation. Without a Controlled Delay, a massive backlog of accumulated chrono furnace fuel would fire instantly, skipping time too quickly for you to safely interact with the game.
  • Limitations: Toggling the automation button on the Controlled Delay itself has no gameplay effect, and it has no impact on batch uses of the manual “Use Temporal Energy” button.

item.content:encoded:
Chronocontrol (or Chrono Control) is an advanced, late-game Time structure under the Void Space section of your Time tab. It plays a crucial role in managing time skips, temporal flux, and anomalies.

Here is a comprehensive breakdown of its prerequisites, costs, effects, and late-game synergies:

1. Prerequisites & Costs

To unlock Chronocontrol, you must first research the Paradox Theory technology, which costs 1,000,000 Science, 40 Time Crystals, and 250 Void.

Once unlocked, constructing your first Chronocontrol costs:

  • 30 Time Crystals
  • 500 Void
  • 3,000 Temporal Flux
  • Price Ratio: 1.25 (meaning subsequent structures cost 25% more)
  • Energy Consumption: Consumes 15 Watts (Wt) of active power

2. Core Effects & Synergies

  • Temporal Paradox Extension: Chronocontrol directly increases the duration (in days) of a Temporal Paradox, an event occasionally triggered by active Chronospheres.
  • Distortion Synergy: Once you purchase the Distortion workshop upgrade (unlocked by Paradox Theory), each level of Chronocontrol adds an extra +3 days to your Temporal Paradoxes.
  • Unlocking Chronosurge: Building at least one Chronocontrol is a hard requirement to unlock the Chronosurge upgrade in your Workshop.

3. Strategic Importance: The Active Flux Loop

Unlocking and building Chronocontrol is the vital gateway to transitioning your temporal flux generation from passive to active.

By building Chronocontrol and purchasing Chronosurge (which costs 25 Time Crystals, 100k Unobtainium, 750 Void, and 6,500 Temporal Flux), your Chronospheres will automatically gather 1 temporal flux per year. Since shattering (combusting) a Time Crystal immediately advances the calendar by one year, every single time skip you perform will instantly generate flux. This is absolutely essential for the late-game “Cryo Engine” strategy, allowing you to instantly generate the massive amounts of flux (3,000 per chamber) required to repair used Cryochambers and carry over hundreds of kittens across resets to farm millions of Paragon.

item.title: Chronosurge
item.description:
To unlock the Chronosurge workshop upgrade and transition from offline-only temporal flux generation to active farming, you need to navigate a specific branch of the late-game Science and Time trees.

Here is the exact progression path, costs, and requirements to unlock and fund this upgrade:

Step 1: The Technology Foundation

You must progress through the temporal science tree to unlock the necessary mechanics:

  1. Chronophysics: Costs 250k Science and 5 Time Crystals. This unlocks the Chronosphere building.
  2. Tachyon Theory: Costs 750k Science, 25 Time Crystals, and 1 Relic. This unlocks the Chronoforge workshop upgrade (which itself costs 500k Science, 5 Relics, and 10 Time Crystals to buy).
  3. Void Space: Costs 800k Science, 30 Time Crystals, and 100 Void.
  4. Paradox Theory: Costs 1M Science, 40 Time Crystals, and 250 Void. Researching this is what officially unlocks the Chronocontrol time structure and enables the Chronosurge upgrade to be researched.

Step 2: Build a Chronocontrol Station

Before you can purchase the Chronosurge upgrade in your Workshop, you must construct at least one Chronocontrol structure:
