item.title: Hubble_Space_Telescope
item.description:
The Hubble Space Telescope is a powerful mid-to-late game Workshop upgrade that significantly boosts your space-based resource generation. It is specifically designed to solve the “starchart bottleneck” that often occurs once you begin exploring the solar system.

Key Effects

The primary function of the Hubble upgrade is to increase the efficiency of your space infrastructure:

  • Starchart Production: It provides a +30% bonus to starchart production from Satellites, Research Vessels, and Space Beacons.
  • Astrophysicists: If you have researched Astrophysicists (which allows Kitten Scientists to produce starcharts), the Hubble upgrade also increases their production by 30%.
  • Science Storage: While its main draw is starcharts, the increased effectiveness of your orbital buildings indirectly helps manage your Science cap, which is vital for late-game tech like Antimatter.

Requirements to Unlock

Since you’ve already been working with Enriched Uranium and Distortion, you likely meet most of the prerequisites, but here is the breakdown:

Rocketry Technology Required to enter the Space Tab

Science Resource 125,000 Science

Strategic Value

By the time you reach the Dark Future (which we discussed regarding Distortion), starcharts usually stop being a primary concern because your production is so high. However, the Hubble upgrade is essential for:

  1. Mass Satellite Deployment: If you are using Solar Satellites for energy, the Hubble bonus makes the side-product of starcharts much more meaningful.
  2. Leviathan Trading: In the very late game, starcharts are used to trade with Leviathans for Time Crystals and Relics. The 30% boost from Hubble helps sustain these trades without stalling your other space missions.
  3. Path to the Farther Ring: Reaching distant planets like Charon or Centaurus System requires hundreds of thousands of starcharts. Hubble is the engine that gets you there faster.

Note: If you are currently in a Black Sky Challenge, note that Research Vessels do not produce starcharts, making the Hubble-boosted Satellites your most reliable source of income.

item.title: High_Pressure_Engine
item.description:
The High Pressure Engine is a Workshop upgrade available in Kittens Game.

To see this upgrade in your Workshop, you must first meet the technical prerequisites:

  • Prerequisite Tech: You must research Chemistry.

Key Benefits

item.content:encoded:
The High Pressure Engine is a Workshop upgrade available in Kittens Game.

How to Unlock and Craft

To see this upgrade in your Workshop, you must first meet the technical prerequisites:

  • Prerequisite Tech: You must research Chemistry.
  • Prerequisite Building: You need to have at least one Steamworks built.
  • Cost: * 25,000 Gear
    • 20,000 Steel
    • 5,000 Blueprint

Key Benefits

The High Pressure Engine is a “quality of life” upgrade that fundamentally changes how your Steamworks function:

  • Steamworks Efficiency: It increases the effectiveness of your Steamworks’ automated tasks.
  • Coal Consumption: Most importantly, it reduces the coal consumption of your Steamworks by 20%. This is vital for maintaining a positive coal balance as you scale up your steel production.
  • Logistics: It provides a +20% bonus to the effectiveness of your Magnetos when Steamworks are active. Since Magnetos provide a global production boost, this upgrade effectively raises your entire civilization’s resource output.

Strategic Impact

By the time you are looking at Enriched Uranium and dealing with Temporal Distortion, the High Pressure Engine should be a core part of your infrastructure.

  1. Steel Production: Because it lowers coal costs, you can run more Steamworks, which in turn automates more Steel production via the “Advanced Automation” upgrade.
  2. Power Synergy: When combined with Magnetos, this upgrade is one of the most efficient ways to boost production without needing extra kittens.
  3. Late Game Utility: Even in the “Dark Future,” the efficiency gained here helps keep your basic resource floor high while you focus your kittens on specialized jobs like Engineers or Scientists.

item.title: Gold Ore
item.description:
Gold Ore is a crucial Workshop upgrade that enables your civilization to generate gold, which is a mandatory step before you can begin trading with other civilizations.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Prerequisite: You must first unlock the Currency science technology.
  • Cost: Purchasing the upgrade requires 1,000 Science, 800 Minerals, and 100 Iron.

Core Effects

Once researched, Gold Ore allows your Smelters to passively create gold alongside their normal iron production. Specifically, each active Smelter will produce 0.001 gold per tick (which equates to 0.005 gold per second). Because gold generation is essential for trade and upgrading certain buildings, obtaining this upgrade is a significant milestone for mid-game economic progression.

Once researched, every hunt has a 25% chance of yielding gold, with the exact amount determined by random integers that scale with your total hunting bonus.

item.title: GM Catnip
item.description:
In Kittens Game, GM (Game Master) Catnip is an incredibly rare, “cheat-tier” resource that functions differently than standard catnip. It is not part of the normal progression and is typically only encountered through specific developer-related events, game-testing modes, or save-file manipulation.

What is GM Catnip?

Unlike regular catnip, which is the foundational food and wood source for your civilization, GM Catnip represents an infinite or hyper-efficient version of the resource.
item.content:encoded:
In Kittens Game, GM (Game Master) Catnip is an incredibly rare, “cheat-tier” resource that functions differently than standard catnip. It is not part of the normal progression and is typically only encountered through specific developer-related events, game-testing modes, or save-file manipulation.

What is GM Catnip?

Unlike regular catnip, which is the foundational food and wood source for your civilization, GM Catnip represents an infinite or hyper-efficient version of the resource.

  • Production: It cannot be produced by Farmers or Catnip Fields in a standard game.
  • Purpose: It is primarily used by the developer (Bloodrizer) or testers to bypass early-game bottlenecks when debugging new late-game mechanics.
  • Storage: It usually does not respect standard storage limits, allowing for “impossible” amounts of resources.

How it Relates to Your Progress

Since you are currently managing advanced mechanics like Enriched Uranium and Distortion, GM Catnip likely has two points of relevance for you:

  1. Testing/Debug Mode: If you have enabled “Cheat Mode” or used the console to test building ratios, GM Catnip is the fuel used to keep kittens alive without needing thousands of Farmers.
  2. Resource Conversions: In some very specific (often older or modded) versions of the game, GM Catnip was a placeholder for “perfect” efficiency.

Standard Catnip in the Late Game

At your stage of the game (likely Year 40,000+ or deep into Chronospheres), standard catnip should be a non-issue.

  • BioLabs and Hydroponics should be providing more than enough catnip to support your population.
  • If you are actually running low on catnip while focusing on Enriched Uranium, ensure your Reactors aren’t consuming too much energy, as a power deficit can sometimes stall your automated production buildings.

Note: If you found “GM Catnip” in your save data or a guide, it’s a sign of a modified game state. In a “clean” run, you will never need it to reach the end-game.

item.title: Enriched_Uranium
item.description:
In Kittens Game, Enriched Uranium is a specialized resource required for advanced late-game structures and space travel. It represents a refined version of standard Uranium, used primarily for high-energy applications.

How to Obtain Enriched Uranium

You cannot mine Enriched Uranium directly. It must be crafted in the Workshop once you have unlocked the necessary technology.

  • Prerequisite Tech: You must research Nuclear Fission.
  • Crafting Recipe: $1$ Enriched Uranium costs 500 Uranium.
  • Automation: Once you unlock the Centrifuge (an upgrade for Reactors), your Reactors will begin converting standard Uranium into Enriched Uranium automatically over time, though at a very slow rate.

Primary Uses

Enriched Uranium is a “bottleneck” resource for the mid-to-late game, used for:
item.content:encoded:
In Kittens Game, Enriched Uranium is a specialized resource required for advanced late-game structures and space travel. It represents a refined version of standard Uranium, used primarily for high-energy applications.

How to Obtain Enriched Uranium

You cannot mine Enriched Uranium directly. It must be crafted in the Workshop once you have unlocked the necessary technology.

  • Prerequisite Tech: You must research Nuclear Fission.
  • Crafting Recipe: $1$ Enriched Uranium costs 500 Uranium.
  • Automation: Once you unlock the Centrifuge (an upgrade for Reactors), your Reactors will begin converting standard Uranium into Enriched Uranium automatically over time, though at a very slow rate.

Primary Uses

Enriched Uranium is a “bottleneck” resource for the mid-to-late game, used for:

  • Elevators: Used to build and upgrade Space Elevators, which significantly reduce the oil cost of launching missions into space.
  • Satellites: Required for launching certain orbital modules that improve map visibility and energy production.
  • Lunar Outposts: Essential for maintaining bases on the Moon, which are your primary source of Unobtainium.
  • Fission Reactors: Used to upgrade your power grid to produce significantly more energy than standard coal or steam power.

Strategic Tip

The 500:1 conversion ratio is quite steep. To manage this, focus on increasing your Uranium production via Accelerators and Lunar Outposts. Once you have a steady flow of Unobtainium, you can trade with the Griffins or Leviathans (if available) to bolster your Uranium stocks for mass crafting.

item.title: Enriched Thorium
item.description:
Enriched Thorium is a late-game Workshop upgrade that improves the efficiency of your Reactors when they are running on thorium fuel.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Prerequisite Technology: You must first research Thorium Reactors.
  • Upgrade Costs:
    • Science: 500,000
    • Thorium: 12,500

Core Effects and Mechanics

The primary function of this upgrade is to reduce the resource burden of the thorium energy cycle:

  • Consumption Reduction: It reduces the amount of Thorium consumed by Reactors by 25%.
  • Specific Yield: Depending on the base consumption rate (which varies in sources), this reduction amounts to either 0.0125 or 0.0625 per tick per reactor.

Strategic Context: The Thorium Cycle

Enriched Thorium is the second of two major upgrades that allow Reactors to use Thorium (a resource crafted from Uranium) to boost energy production:
item.content:encoded:
Enriched Thorium is a late-game Workshop upgrade that improves the efficiency of your Reactors when they are running on thorium fuel.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Prerequisite Technology: You must first research Thorium Reactors.
  • Upgrade Costs:
    • Science: 500,000
    • Thorium: 12,500

Core Effects and Mechanics

The primary function of this upgrade is to reduce the resource burden of the thorium energy cycle:

  • Consumption Reduction: It reduces the amount of Thorium consumed by Reactors by 25%.
  • Specific Yield: Depending on the base consumption rate (which varies in sources), this reduction amounts to either 0.0125 or 0.0625 per tick per reactor.

Strategic Context: The Thorium Cycle

Enriched Thorium is the second of two major upgrades that allow Reactors to use Thorium (a resource crafted from Uranium) to boost energy production:

  1. Thorium Reactors: This initial upgrade allows Reactors to consume Thorium in exchange for a +25% boost to energy production.
  2. Enriched Thorium: Once the first upgrade is active, Enriched Thorium makes the process more sustainable by cutting the fuel cost.

Optimization Tips

  • Crafting Thorium: Thorium is produced in the Workshop by converting Uranium.
  • Kitten Synergy: Kittens with the Chemist trait provide a +0.075 bonus to the craft ratio when producing Thorium, making it significantly cheaper to mass-produce the fuel needed for your reactor network.
  • Power Management: Thorium-fueled reactors are particularly useful in the very late game when performing “time skips” to generate Antimatter, as they provide the high energy output necessary for containment structures.

item.title: Distortion
item.description:
In Kittens Game, Distortion (often referred to as Temporal Distortion) is a late-game mechanic tied specifically to Chronospheres and the management of your resource “memory” during resets.

It represents the instability of time as you attempt to carry resources across different timelines.

How Distortion Works

Distortion is primarily a byproduct of Temporal Paradoxes. When you have Chronospheres, you can carry resources through a reset. However, if you have Void Resonators and certain Paradox upgrades, your game generates “Temporal Paradoxes” (indicated by a purple notification).
item.content:encoded:
In Kittens Game, Distortion (often referred to as Temporal Distortion) is a late-game mechanic tied specifically to Chronospheres and the management of your resource “memory” during resets.

It represents the instability of time as you attempt to carry resources across different timelines.

How Distortion Works

Distortion is primarily a byproduct of Temporal Paradoxes. When you have Chronospheres, you can carry resources through a reset. However, if you have Void Resonators and certain Paradox upgrades, your game generates “Temporal Paradoxes” (indicated by a purple notification).

  • The Resource Penalty: High levels of Distortion/Paradoxes can cause your resource production to fluctuate or stall.
  • The Paradox Reset: Every time a paradox occurs, you gain a small amount of Void, but you also increase your Distortion level.

Key Upgrades Related to Distortion

As you progress into the “Dark Future” (Year 40,000+), managing Distortion becomes a full-time job for your kittens:

  • [Temporal Accelerators]: These increase the rate at which time passes but also increase the likelihood of paradoxes.
  • [Rectilinear Pitcher]: This upgrade helps mitigate the negative effects of Distortion, allowing your timeline to remain more stable even when carrying massive amounts of resources.
  • [Void]: Paradoxes are the primary way to generate Void in the mid-game. You actually want some level of Distortion/Paradoxes to occur so you can harvest Void for Chronotheology upgrades.

Strategic Impact

  1. Void Farming: Early on, you trigger paradoxes (and thus Distortion) intentionally to get enough Void for your first Obelisks or Nexus.
  2. Stability: In very long runs, Distortion can become a nuisance. You eventually build Mausoleums and other structures to stabilize the timeline.
  3. Flux: Distortion interacts with Temporal Flux. If your Distortion is too high, your ability to “Shatter Crystals” to skip years becomes less efficient.

Summary Table: Managing Time Stability

Feature Impact on Distortion Purpose
Chronospheres Increases via resets Carry resources to New Game+
Void Resonators Increases via Paradoxes Generates Void
Temporal Battery Reduces effect Stores Flux for later use

item.title: Dark Revolution
item.description:
Dark Revolution is a religion-tier upgrade in Kittens Game that acts as a pivot point for your late-game faith and resource strategy. It essentially converts your religious progression into a tool for efficiency and speed, particularly regarding the “Dark Future” mechanics.

Key Benefits & Effects

  • Solar Revolution Cap: Its most significant effect is providing a way to increase the Solar Revolution production bonus cap. In later stages of the game, your faith bonus can become so massive it hits a ceiling; Dark Revolution helps push through that.
  • Kitten Sacrifice Efficiency: It increases the yield of Tears when sacrificing kittens (via the Ziggurat). This is crucial for building up your Cryptotheology structures (like Black Obelisks and Event Horizons).
  • Blackcoin Interaction: While it doesn’t directly change the market price of Blackcoin, the increased faith and relic generation it supports allow you to engage in much larger Blackcoin speculation cycles.
  • Zebra Synergy: It makes Zebra Outposts 10x more effective at increasing your Catpower production limit, which is vital for late-game hunting and trading.

How to Unlock It

To see Dark Revolution in your Religion tab, you typically need to meet several high-level requirements:
item.content:encoded:
Dark Revolution is a religion-tier upgrade in Kittens Game that acts as a pivot point for your late-game faith and resource strategy. It essentially converts your religious progression into a tool for efficiency and speed, particularly regarding the “Dark Future” mechanics.

Key Benefits & Effects

  • Solar Revolution Cap: Its most significant effect is providing a way to increase the Solar Revolution production bonus cap. In later stages of the game, your faith bonus can become so massive it hits a ceiling; Dark Revolution helps push through that.
  • Kitten Sacrifice Efficiency: It increases the yield of Tears when sacrificing kittens (via the Ziggurat). This is crucial for building up your Cryptotheology structures (like Black Obelisks and Event Horizons).
  • Blackcoin Interaction: While it doesn’t directly change the market price of Blackcoin, the increased faith and relic generation it supports allow you to engage in much larger Blackcoin speculation cycles.
  • Zebra Synergy: It makes Zebra Outposts 10x more effective at increasing your Catpower production limit, which is vital for late-game hunting and trading.

How to Unlock It

To see Dark Revolution in your Religion tab, you typically need to meet several high-level requirements:

  1. Transcendence Tier: You generally need to be at least Transcendence Tier 5-10.
  2. Zebra Workshop: You must have unlocked the Zebra Workshop (which requires hunting with at least 10 Zebras and gathering Bloodstones).
  3. Cryptotheology: Having at least one Black Pyramid or Marker is often a prerequisite to unlock the “darker” side of the religion tree.

Strategic Use

You should prioritize Dark Revolution when your runs start lasting long enough to hit the Dark Future (Year 40,000+). It helps offset the production penalties that occur in the deep future and scales your resource generation to the levels needed for Chronospheres and massive paragon grinding.

Pro Tip: Combine Dark Revolution with Black Obelisks. The Obelisks increase the effectiveness of your Solar Revolution bonus, and Dark Revolution ensures you have the raw power to reach those higher caps.

item.title: Relic Station
item.description:
The Relic Station is a highly important mid-to-late game workshop upgrade that forms the foundation of your passive Relic economy by upgrading your Space Beacons.

Here are the details on how to acquire and optimize Relic Stations:

Acquisition and Costs

  • Prerequisites: To unlock the Relic Station upgrade, you must first research the Cryptotheology science, which costs 5 Relics.
  • Cost: Purchasing the Relic Station upgrade requires a massive investment of 100 Eludium and 5,000 Antimatter.
  • Antimatter Preparation: Gathering 5,000 Antimatter is a major bottleneck. You will need to build Sunlifters to generate Antimatter, and heavily expand your Antimatter storage capacity by constructing Containment Chambers and Heatsinks.

Core Effects and Scaling

  • Passive Relic Generation: Once purchased, every Space Beacon you have built will begin passively generating 0.01 Relics per game-day (which equates to roughly 432 Relics per real-life day per beacon).
  • Antimatter Storage Penalty: Your Relic Station’s efficiency is directly tied to your Antimatter storage limit. If your maximum Antimatter storage drops below 5,000, your Relic production will decrease by 0.02% for every missing unit of storage.

How to Boost Relic Station Production

While the base production of 432 Relics a day per beacon is somewhat slow, it can be drastically multiplied through late-game synergies:

item.title: Unicorn Selection
item.description:
Based on the sources, Unicorn Selection is a Workshop upgrade designed to significantly boost your unicorn generation.

Here are the specific details regarding its costs and effects:

Acquisition and Costs

  • Prerequisite: To unlock the ability to purchase Unicorn Selection, you must first research the Genetics science.

Core Effects

  • Production Boost: The upgrade improves the overall effectiveness of your Unicorn Pastures, granting a +25% multiplier to your unicorn production.
  • Scaling: This 25% boost acts as a true multiplier that scales alongside your other production effects, making it an essential upgrade for establishing a strong unicorn economy and generating tears and alicorns faster.

  • Cost: 175,000 Science, 1,500 Titanium, and 1,000,000 Catnip.
  • Effect: This upgrade creates genetically modified catnip that improves your Bio Labs’ oil yield by 60%. To benefit from this, you must already have the Biofuel Processing upgrade active (which automatically converts catnip into oil). Importantly, GM Catnip provides this massive 60% boost to oil production without increasing the amount of catnip your Bio Labs actually consume.

item.title: Black Liquid Sorrow
item.description:
Black Liquid Sorrow (frequently referred to as BLS or simply Sorrow) is a rare, uncommon resource used heavily in the late game to interact with the Leviathans and permanently boost your civilization’s production.

Here is a breakdown of how to acquire and manage this resource:

How to Acquire Sorrow

  • Refining Tears: The most consistent way to get BLS is by refining Unicorn Tears at a rate of 10,000 Tears to 1 Sorrow. To unlock this ability, you must first purchase the Megalomania metaphysics upgrade.
  • Trading: Once the Leviathans arrive, every trade you make with them (costing 5,000 Unobtainium) has a 15% chance to yield 1 Black Liquid Sorrow.
  • Events: You can occasionally acquire it through a random weather event called “Black Rain”.

Primary Uses

  • Black Pyramids: The most important use for your first few Sorrows is building Black Pyramids, which cost 5 Sorrow each (alongside Megaliths, Spice, and Unobtainium). You must construct at least one Black Pyramid to make the Leviathans appear for trading.
  • The Necrocracy Policy: After you make your first trade with the Leviathans, you can unlock a powerful late-game government policy called Necrocracy. This policy grants a global production bonus of 0.1% for every percent of Black Liquid Sorrow you possess.

Storage Limits

  • Base Cap: Your civilization starts with a very strict maximum storage limit of 16 BLS.
  • Expanding Storage: You can eventually increase this cap by purchasing Black Cores, an advanced Cryptotheology upgrade (unlocked at Transcendence Tier 5) that increases your sorrow limit by 1% per level.
  • Refining Warning: If you attempt to refine Unicorn Tears into Sorrow while you are already at your maximum storage capacity, the game will prevent it; nothing will happen, but thankfully your Tears will not be consumed.

Resetting the Game

One of the most important aspects of Black Liquid Sorrow is that it is a permanent resource. Your entire stockpile of BLS will automatically carry over in full whenever you reset your game. Because it survives resets, it is highly recommended to refine any leftover Unicorn Tears you have into Sorrow right before you hit the reset button to ensure you don’t lose that value.

item.title: Oil
item.description:
Oil is an essential common resource in Kittens Game that acts as the primary fuel for your mid-to-late game industrial revolution and space exploration.

Production and Acquisition

  • Oil Wells: The earliest and primary way to generate oil is by constructing Oil Wells. Their output can be drastically multiplied through a series of workshop upgrades: Pumpjack (+45% output, but costs 1 Watt of energy), Oil Refinery (+35%), and Oil Distillation (+75%).
  • Bio Labs: By researching the Biofuel Processing upgrade, your Bio Labs will automatically convert 5 catnip per second into 0.10 oil. You can boost this conversion yield by an additional 60% with the GM Catnip genetics upgrade.
  • Hydraulic Fracturers: In the space phase, you can build these on the planet Dune to generate a massive 2.5 oil per second. Their production is boosted by Space Elevators and receives a +50% bonus during the Dune cycle.
  • Trading: You can acquire oil by trading Scaffolds to Spiders.

Primary Uses

  • Powering Industry: Oil is a constant upkeep requirement for key industrial buildings; Magnetos consume 0.05 oil per tick, and Calciners consume 0.024 oil per tick.
  • Space Missions: Reaching and expanding in space requires huge, lump-sum investments of oil. For example, the Orbital Launch requires 15,000 oil, the Moon Mission requires 45,000, and building a Moon Base costs 70,000. Building Space Elevators will help reduce the oil requirements for space missions by 5% each.
  • Kerosene: Oil must be refined into Kerosene, a highly advanced rocket fuel used for deep space exploration. The Factory Processing upgrade makes this conversion more efficient.

Oil Storage

Your civilization starts with a very restrictive base storage limit of 1,500 oil. Because space technologies require tens of thousands of units at once, aggressively expanding your storage is mandatory. You can increase your oil cap by:

item.title: What is the fastest way to farm Time Crystals?
item.description:
The absolute fastest way to farm Time Crystals in the late game is through mass trading Unobtainium with the Leviathans, which is roughly 30 times faster than waiting for Alicorns to sacrifice.

To achieve this, you need to maximize your Unobtainium production and your trade efficiency, eventually creating a self-sustaining “Shatter Engine”. Here is the step-by-step strategy:

1. Maximize Unobtainium Production Since each trade with the Leviathans costs 5,000 Unobtainium, your base production must be astronomically high:
item.content:encoded:
The absolute fastest way to farm Time Crystals in the late game is through mass trading Unobtainium with the Leviathans, which is roughly 30 times faster than waiting for Alicorns to sacrifice.

To achieve this, you need to maximize your Unobtainium production and your trade efficiency, eventually creating a self-sustaining “Shatter Engine”. Here is the step-by-step strategy:

1. Maximize Unobtainium Production Since each trade with the Leviathans costs 5,000 Unobtainium, your base production must be astronomically high:

  • Space Structures: Max out Lunar Outposts, Space Elevators, Orbital Arrays, and Factories.
  • Upgrades and Policies: Research the Factory Logistics workshop upgrade, and enact the Full Industrialization, Cosmological Libertarianism, and Necrocracy policies.
  • Festivals: Maximize Breweries and ensure festivals are running non-stop.
  • The Redmoon Cycle : With the Numerology and Numeromancy metaphysics upgrades, the Redmoon cycle grants a massive multiplier to Unobtainium production. Use Time Crystals to skip right to the Redmoon cycle and spend the majority of your time there.

2. Maximize Time Crystals per Trade You want to ensure that every 5,000 Unobtainium traded yields as many Time Crystals as possible:

  • Leviathan Energy: Feed Necrocorns to the Leviathans (Elders) whenever possible. Each point of energy increases the resources they give you by 2%.
  • Tradeposts: Max out your Tradeposts, as each one adds a +1.5% bonus to your trades.
  • Leader: Assign a Merchant leader, which significantly boosts trade efficiency, especially if you have a lot of burned paragon.

3. Build a “Shatter Engine” Once your base Unobtainium production reaches hundreds per second, you can transition to a Shatter Engine:

  • Purchase levels of Resource Retrieval (1,000 TCs each). Each level instantly grants you 1% of your yearly resource production every time you shatter a Time Crystal to skip a year.
  • Combine this with Chronofurnaces (to manage the heat generated from shattering time) and Blazars (to improve Resource Retrieval effectiveness).
  • The Infinite Loop: With roughly 7 levels of Resource Retrieval and high base Unobtainium production, shattering a single Time Crystal will instantly yield enough Unobtainium to trade back to the Leviathans for multiple Time Crystals.

Once this break-even point is reached, you can rapidly shatter crystals, trade the retrieved Unobtainium, and farm millions of Time Crystals without ever running out.

item.title: Tempus Fugit
item.description:
Tempus Fugit is a powerful toggleable time-manipulation ability that accelerates calendar time and increases your overall production tick rate by 50%.

Here are the core mechanics and strategies regarding its use:

  • Activation and Upkeep: Turning on the ability costs 1 Temporal Flux, and it aggressively consumes 5 Temporal Flux for every real-time second it is active.
  • Production Multiplier: The 50% boost applies globally to your resource generation, acting as a massive multiplier for late-game resources like Unobtainium.
  • Endgame Paragon Farming: Tempus Fugit is highly valued in the deep endgame for rapid Paragon grinding. Players will activate it alongside thousands of Breweries and stacked Festivals to make kittens arrive incredibly fast, allowing them to rapidly cap their population and reset the game for Paragon.
  • Strategic Limitations: Importantly, Tempus Fugit does not affect the amount of resources you receive from Resource Retrieval when shattering Time Crystals. Additionally, if you are playing actively without automation (especially in Iron Will mode), accelerating calendar time gives you less real-world time to manually click on fleeting astronomical events.
  • Sustainment Challenges: Because it drains flux so quickly, maintaining 100% uptime on Tempus Fugit is difficult and often impractical. While you can purchase Temporal Batteries to stockpile a larger reserve of flux while offline, trying to permanently sustain Tempus Fugit using the Chronosurge upgrade is often considered uneconomical due to the massive amounts of Void required to unlock and power it.

item.title: Temporal Battery
item.description:
The Temporal Battery is a time-manipulation upgrade located in the game’s Time tab.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Base Cost: Purchasing your first Temporal Battery requires an investment of 5 Time Crystals.
  • Price Ratio: The cost of each subsequent battery scales with a 1.25 price ratio.

Core Effect The sole function of the Temporal Battery is to improve your temporal flux capacity by 25% per level purchased.

Strategic Value and Mechanics To understand the value of the Temporal Battery, it helps to understand how temporal flux operates within the game. Temporal flux is a special resource used for time-related experiments. You passively earn 5 units of temporal flux per minute whenever the game is paused or closed (offline). Additionally, if you have the Chronosurge upgrade, your Chronospheres will automatically generate a small amount of flux every in-game year.

The Temporal Battery is a time-manipulation upgrade located in the game’s Time tab.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Price Ratio: The cost of each subsequent battery scales with a 1.25 price ratio.

Core Effect The sole function of the Temporal Battery is to improve your temporal flux capacity by 25% per level purchased.

Strategic Value and Mechanics To understand the value of the Temporal Battery, it helps to understand how temporal flux operates within the game. Temporal flux is a special resource used for time-related experiments. You passively earn 5 units of temporal flux per minute whenever the game is paused or closed (offline). Additionally, if you have the Chronosurge upgrade, your Chronospheres will automatically generate a small amount of flux every in-game year.

This hoarded flux is primarily spent to activate Tempus Fugit, a powerful toggleable ability that accelerates calendar time and increases your overall production tick rate by 50%. Because Tempus Fugit aggressively consumes 5 temporal flux every second it is active, purchasing Temporal Batteries allows you to stockpile a much larger reserve of flux while away from the game. This ultimately lets you sustain the massive 50% production boost from Tempus Fugit for significantly longer periods when you return to active play.

item.title: Void Rift
item.description:
The Void Rift is an advanced time-manipulation building that provides powerful, permanent boosts to both your storage capacity and energy production in the late game.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Prerequisite: To unlock the Void Rift, you must first acquire the Void Aspiration upgrade.
  • Cost: The first Void Rift requires an investment of 75 Void.
  • Price Ratio: The cost scales with a 1.3 price ratio for each subsequent purchase.

Core Effects

  • Global Storage Boost: Each Void Rift permanently increases all of your global resource storage capacity by 2%. This specific storage bonus stacks additively with the 10% storage bonus provided by Event Horizons, and scales multiplicatively alongside other storage bonuses like those from Paragon.
  • Energy Production: Each Void Rift also increases the energy production of your HR Harvesters by 10%. Because HR Harvesters scale infinitely with Dark Future years, accumulating Void Rifts is an excellent way to drastically multiply your late-game power output.

Endgame Strategy

In the deep endgame, acquiring dozens of Void Rifts becomes a primary objective to accelerate your resource velocity. A common strategic milestone is to amass around 200 million Void to purchase 50 Void Rifts.

item.title: Iron
item.description:
Iron is a fundamental common resource in Kittens Game that bridges the gap between your early-game village and your mid-to-late game industrial economy. It is primarily used to craft essential advanced components and construct critical infrastructure.

Production

You cannot gather iron directly; it must be refined or acquired through trade.

  • Smelters: The earliest way to generate iron is by constructing Smelters, which continuously refine wood and minerals into iron. You can double their efficiency by researching the Electrolytic Smelting workshop upgrade, which adds +95% to both iron and coal production.
  • Calciners: As you advance into chemistry, you can build Calciners, which refine oil and minerals into both iron and titanium. Their iron output can be drastically enhanced through a series of workshop upgrades: Oxidation (+95%), Rotary Kiln (+75%), and Fluidized Reactors (+100%).

Trade and Strategic Arbitrage

Because standard production facilities like Smelters often struggle to scale efficiently enough to meet mid-game demands, iron frequently becomes a major bottleneck. To overcome this, players utilize trade arbitrage, converting high-volume resources into iron:
item.content:encoded:
Iron is a fundamental common resource in Kittens Game that bridges the gap between your early-game village and your mid-to-late game industrial economy. It is primarily used to craft essential advanced components and construct critical infrastructure.

Production

You cannot gather iron directly; it must be refined or acquired through trade.

  • Smelters: The earliest way to generate iron is by constructing Smelters, which continuously refine wood and minerals into iron. You can double their efficiency by researching the Electrolytic Smelting workshop upgrade, which adds +95% to both iron and coal production.
  • Calciners: As you advance into chemistry, you can build Calciners, which refine oil and minerals into both iron and titanium. Their iron output can be drastically enhanced through a series of workshop upgrades: Oxidation (+95%), Rotary Kiln (+75%), and Fluidized Reactors (+100%).

Trade and Strategic Arbitrage

Because standard production facilities like Smelters often struggle to scale efficiently enough to meet mid-game demands, iron frequently becomes a major bottleneck. To overcome this, players utilize trade arbitrage, converting high-volume resources into iron:

  • Griffins: Griffins will sell you iron in exchange for Wood. This is an incredibly powerful strategy early on, effectively allowing you to bypass the slow smelting process. Griffins yield the most iron during Autumn (+35%), but suffer penalties during Spring (-25%) and Winter (-20%).
  • Zebras: Zebras will sell you iron, plates, and titanium in exchange for Slabs. Zebras yield the most iron during Summer (+15%), but suffer penalties in Autumn (-10%) and Winter (-20%).

Primary Uses and Crafting

Iron is the critical raw material required to craft two major mid-game resources in the Workshop:

  • Metal Plates: Costs 125 Iron. Plates are heavily used for construction, particularly for Harbours.
  • Steel: Costs 100 Iron and 100 Coal. Steel is a durable metal mandatory for crafting gears, complex machinery, and advanced buildings. To optimize your steel production later in the game, the Steel Plants upgrade allows Calciners to automatically reserve 10% of their iron output and craft it into steel.

Storage Capacity

Your initial civilization can only hold 50 iron by default. Because advanced technologies and buildings require massive amounts of iron, constantly expanding your storage limits is mandatory:

  • Early/Mid Game: Iron storage is expanded by building Barns (+50), Warehouses (+25), and Harbours (+150). You can multiply these base values by purchasing workshop storage upgrades such as Expanded, Reinforced, Titanium, Alloy, and Concrete Barns and Warehouses.
  • Late Game & Space: As you progress, massive iron storage vaults become available. Accelerators (once upgraded with Energy Rifts) add +7,500 to your iron cap. In space, Moon Bases provide +9,000 iron storage, and Cryostations grant a staggering +50,000 iron storage.

item.title: Divine Proportion
item.description:
Divine Proportion is a highly recommended Metaphysics upgrade that directly improves your civilization’s economy by lowering the escalating costs of buildings. It serves as the third major upgrade in the crucial price ratio reduction chain, bridging the gap between Golden Ratio and Vitruvian Feline.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Prerequisite: You must first purchase the Golden Ratio metaphysics upgrade to unlock Divine Proportion.
  • Cost: Purchasing the upgrade requires an investment of 100 Paragon.

Core Effects

  • Price Ratio Reduction: Divine Proportion reduces all building price ratios by ~1.77% (exactly 16/9%). This means subsequent buildings will escalate in cost much slower, allowing you to construct significantly more structures before hitting your resource storage caps.
  • Progression: Acquiring Divine Proportion directly unlocks Vitruvian Feline, the next tier of price ratio reduction.

Strategy and Timing

  • Prioritization: It is highly advised that you prioritize buying all of the price ratio reduction upgrades (Enlightenment, Golden Ratio, Divine Proportion, Vitruvian Feline, and Renaissance) as early as possible in your playthroughs, as making everything in your village cheaper is vital for rapid expansion.
  • When to Buy: A common community strategy is to aim for purchasing Divine Proportion around your third reset. Players typically try to acquire it when they reach a population of about 200 kittens, and then continue pushing their population to 220+ kittens before resetting again. This ensures you generate enough Paragon (around 150) to comfortably afford your next set of upgrades in the following run.

item.title: Renaissance
item.description:
Renaissance is the final and most powerful Metaphysics upgrade in the building price ratio reduction chain (following Enlightenment, Golden Ratio, Divine Proportion, and Vitruvian Feline).

Core Effects and Cost

  • Effect: Renaissance provides a massive 2.25% reduction to all building price ratios. This makes buildings significantly cheaper to construct, allowing you to build many more structures to boost your population and production before hitting your resource storage caps. It is widely considered one of the most powerful (“OP”) metaphysics upgrades in the game because once you acquire it, you will rarely have issues generating enough paragon for anything else.
  • Cost: Purchasing the upgrade requires a substantial investment of 750 Paragon.

Strategy and Timing

  • Progression: It is highly recommended that you prioritise acquiring all price ratio reduction upgrades, culminating in Renaissance, before making serious investments into other late-game mechanics like end-game unicorn ziggurats.
  • When to Buy: Players typically aim to purchase Renaissance around their fifth to seventh reset. A common strategy is to keep resetting at Unobtainium Huts until you have generated enough paragon to comfortably afford it.
  • Challenges: If you plan on taking on the game’s difficult challenge modes, such as the Anarchy challenge, it is highly advised to secure Renaissance beforehand to ensure your economy can withstand the harsh penalties.

item.title: Vitruvian Feline
item.description:
Vitruvian Feline is a highly valuable Metaphysics upgrade that directly improves your civilization’s economy by lowering the escalating costs of buildings.

Acquisition and Prerequisites

  • Prerequisite: You must first purchase the Divine Proportion metaphysics upgrade to unlock Vitruvian Feline.
  • Cost: Purchasing the upgrade requires a substantial investment of 250 Paragon.

Core Effects and Strategy

  • Price Ratio Reduction: Vitruvian Feline reduces all building price ratios by 2%. This means buildings will become cheaper to construct, allowing you to buy significantly more structures before you hit your resource storage caps.
  • Progression: Acquiring Vitruvian Feline unlocks Renaissance, which is the final price ratio reduction upgrade.
  • Strategic Importance: It is highly recommended that you prioritize buying all of the price ratio reduction upgrades (including Vitruvian Feline) early in your playthroughs, as they make everything in your village cheaper and allow for rapid expansion. A common community strategy is to aim for Vitruvian Feline around your fourth reset, which typically requires reaching a population of about 320 kittens in a single run to generate enough Paragon to afford it.

item.title: Burned Paragon
item.description:
Burned Paragon provides several crucial bonuses to your civilization’s production, storage capacity, and leader traits. It operates similarly to regular Paragon and stacks with it, but with different scaling rules:

  • Production Bonus: Burned paragon provides a global production boost, but it generally has half the effectiveness of regular paragon. It stacks directly with your normal paragon bonuses. For example, having 400 regular paragon and 400 burned paragon yields a combined 285% production increase. It is highly recommended to acquire around 200 to 400 burned paragon to significantly boost your production capabilities.
  • Storage Capacity Bonus: By default, each burned paragon grants a 0.05% bonus to your storage capacity, which is half the value of regular paragon. However, this bonus undergoes a massive change when you enter the Dark Future phase. During the Dark Future, the storage bonus from burned paragon is multiplied by four, increasing to 0.2% per burned paragon. This makes it twice as effective as regular paragon for expanding storage in the deep endgame. These bonuses stack additively with your standard paragon storage bonuses.
  • Leader Trait Boost: Burned paragon also slightly increases the effectiveness of your assigned Leader’s specific trait. For instance, if you have a Merchant leader, possessing burned paragon will directly improve the formula that dictates how many Time Crystals you receive per trade with the Leviathans.

item.title: Dark Future
item.description:
The Dark Future is a late-game phase that officially begins when your in-game calendar reaches year 40,000. Advancing into this era introduces a mix of temporal penalties and significant boosts to your civilization’s capabilities.

Trigger Condition

  • Requirement: You enter the Dark Future automatically when the game year reaches 40,000.
  • Time Skips: This includes years gained artificially by shattering Time Crystals using the Chronoforge. You do not need to wait 40,000 real-time years; advanced players reach this state by skipping thousands of years instantly.

The Temporal Penalty The primary negative effect of the Dark Future is that the cost to advance time (using Time Crystals) will progressively increase the further you venture into the timeline. To mitigate this, you can purchase the Time Impedance upgrade, which suppresses the Dark Future penalty by 1,000 years per level. You can further enhance this suppression by building Temporal Accelerators. Fortunately, the rising cost penalty is considered relatively minimal by the community and shouldn’t require excessive worrying or over-investment.
item.content:encoded:
The Dark Future is a late-game phase that officially begins when your in-game calendar reaches year 40,000. Advancing into this era introduces a mix of temporal penalties and significant boosts to your civilization’s capabilities.

Trigger Condition

  • Requirement: You enter the Dark Future automatically when the game year reaches 40,000.
  • Time Skips: This includes years gained artificially by shattering Time Crystals using the Chronoforge. You do not need to wait 40,000 real-time years; advanced players reach this state by skipping thousands of years instantly.

The Temporal Penalty The primary negative effect of the Dark Future is that the cost to advance time (using Time Crystals) will progressively increase the further you venture into the timeline. To mitigate this, you can purchase the Time Impedance upgrade, which suppresses the Dark Future penalty by 1,000 years per level. You can further enhance this suppression by building Temporal Accelerators. Fortunately, the rising cost penalty is considered relatively minimal by the community and shouldn’t require excessive worrying or over-investment.

The Benefits This is the primary strategic reason players aim for the Dark Future.

  • Storage Boost: Before the Dark Future, Burned Paragon provides a relatively small storage bonus (0.05% per point). Once Dark Future activates, this bonus quadruples to 0.2% per point.

  • Endgame Scaling: This massive boost to global storage capacity allows you to hold significantly more Unobtainium, which is required to build the 70–100 Chronospheres needed for infinite resource loops.

  • HR Harvesters: The energy production of your HR Harvesters receives a continuous, infinitely scaling boost for every year that passes after 40,000. Importantly, this includes the thousands of years you actively skip by shattering Time Crystals.

Strategic Summary

Reaching the Dark Future is a goal for “deep endgame” runs. Players purposefully shatter Time Crystals to reach year 40,000 to activate the Burned Paragon bonus, which provides the storage necessary to buy more Chronospheres and Event Horizons. They then manage the rising costs by purchasing Time Impedance.

item.title: Time Impedance
item.description:
Time Impedance is a late-game time manipulation upgrade designed to counteract the negative penalties associated with the Dark Future.

Core Mechanics and Visibility

  • Effect: Each level of Time Impedance suppresses the Dark Future temporal penalty by 1,000 years. Without this upgrade, the Dark Future causes the cost of Time Crystals to progressively increase as you advance further into the timeline.
  • Visibility Requirement: The upgrade is hidden for the vast majority of a playthrough; it will only become visible on your menu once your in-game calendar year reaches at least 40,000.

Costs and Scaling

  • Base Cost: Purchasing the upgrade requires 100 Time Crystals and 250 Relics.
  • Price Ratio: The cost of subsequent levels scales relatively slowly, with a price ratio of just 1.05.

Synergies and Boosts

The base 1,000-year suppression effect of Time Impedance can be enhanced by other time-related upgrades:

Synergies and Boosts

The base 1,000-year suppression effect of Time Impedance can be enhanced by other time-related upgrades:

  • Temporal Accelerator: Each accelerator provides a 5% improvement to the effectiveness of your Time Impedance.
  • Blazars: Each level of this advanced Cryptotheology upgrade improves your Time Impedance by an additional 10%.

Strategic Value

Once you cross the 40k year threshold, you will notice your Time Crystal costs beginning to rise due to the Dark Future. While purchasing a few levels of Time Impedance and Temporal Accelerators is recommended to help ward off these increasing costs, the penalty is relatively minimal, so it doesn’t require excessive worrying or over-investment.

item.title: Resource Retrieval
item.description:
Resource Retrieval is a late-game upgrade found in the Time tab that forms the backbone of advanced time-manipulation strategies.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Prerequisite: You must first unlock the Paradox Theory science.
  • Base Cost: 1,000 Time Crystals.
  • Price Ratio: The cost of subsequent levels scales with a 1.3 price ratio.

Core Effects

  • Whenever you shatter a Time Crystal (using the Chronoforge to skip a year), Resource Retrieval instantly gives you 1% of your yearly resource production per level purchased.
  • Activating Tempus Fugit does not affect the amount of resources you retrieve.

Synergies
item.content:encoded:
Resource Retrieval is a late-game upgrade found in the Time tab that forms the backbone of advanced time-manipulation strategies.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Prerequisite: You must first unlock the Paradox Theory science.
  • Base Cost: 1,000 Time Crystals.
  • Price Ratio: The cost of subsequent levels scales with a 1.3 price ratio.

Core Effects

  • Whenever you shatter a Time Crystal (using the Chronoforge to skip a year), Resource Retrieval instantly gives you 1% of your yearly resource production per level purchased.
  • Activating Tempus Fugit does not affect the amount of resources you retrieve.

Synergies

  • Blazars: This advanced Cryptotheology upgrade improves the effectiveness of your Resource Retrieval by +2% per level.
  • Chronoengineers: If you have this workshop upgrade, your assigned Engineer kittens will automatically perform crafting cycles based on your Resource Retrieval amounts whenever you combust Time Crystals.

Strategic Importance: The “Shatter Engine” In the deep late-game, Resource Retrieval is essential for creating what the community calls a “Shatter Engine” (or a Type 2 Relic Engine).

The primary goal is to purchase enough levels of Resource Retrieval so that every time you shatter a Time Crystal, you generate a massive dump of resources—specifically unobtainium and alicorns. If your yields from a single shatter are high enough, you can immediately trade that retrieved unobtainium to the Leviathans (or sacrifice the retrieved alicorns) to earn more Time Crystals than you just spent.

Reaching this self-sustaining “infinite loop” typically requires roughly 7 levels of Resource Retrieval, which demands an investment of around 12,000 Time Crystals. Once this engine is established, you can rapidly and repeatedly shatter time crystals (or automate your Chrono Furnaces) to farm massive amounts of resources, relics, and Time Crystals without ever running out.

item.title: Temporal Accelerator
item.description:
The Temporal Accelerator is an advanced upgrade found in the Time tab that enhances various time manipulation mechanics and improves the performance of automated time skips.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Cost: Purchasing your first Temporal Accelerator requires 10 Time Crystals and 1,000 Relics.
  • Price Ratio: The cost of each subsequent accelerator scales with a 1.25 price ratio.

Core Effects and Mechanics

  • Time-Related Bonus: It provides a 5% bonus to time-related effects. Specifically, this translates to a 1.25% improvement to both your Chronomancy and Unicornmancy upgrades, and a 5% improvement to your Time Impedance.
  • Redshift Boost: It increases the production of temporal flux you earn from “redshift” (the game’s offline progression mechanic) by 5%.
  • Lag Reduction: For late-game players utilizing “Shatter Engines,” this upgrade offers a massive quality-of-life improvement. When you have time automation activated (such as with the Chrono Furnace), the Temporal Accelerator directly reduces the lag caused by rapidly smashing time crystals.

item.title: Time Boiler
item.description:
The Time Boiler is an advanced time-manipulation upgrade that directly improves the functionality of the Chrono Furnace by expanding its maximum heat capacity. This upgrade is essential for late-game “mass shattering” strategies, allowing you to skip thousands of years and farm resources or paragon without hitting your heat limit as quickly.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Base Cost: Your first Time Boiler requires a massive investment of 25,000 Time Crystals.
  • Price Ratio: The cost scales with a price ratio of 1.25 for each subsequent purchase.

Core Effects and Unique Scaling

Unlike most upgrades, Time Boilers operate with unique, exponential scaling mechanics for both their benefits and their energy requirements:
item.content:encoded:
The Time Boiler is an advanced time-manipulation upgrade that directly improves the functionality of the Chrono Furnace by expanding its maximum heat capacity. This upgrade is essential for late-game “mass shattering” strategies, allowing you to skip thousands of years and farm resources or paragon without hitting your heat limit as quickly.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Base Cost: Your first Time Boiler requires a massive investment of 25,000 Time Crystals.
  • Price Ratio: The cost scales with a price ratio of 1.25 for each subsequent purchase.

Core Effects and Unique Scaling

Unlike most upgrades, Time Boilers operate with unique, exponential scaling mechanics for both their benefits and their energy requirements:

  • Base Effect: The very first Time Boiler you purchase grants a maximum heat expansion of 10 and consumes 1 Watt of energy.
  • Scaling Increases: For every Time Boiler you already own, the heat expansion granted by the next one increases by 20, and its energy cost increases by an additional 2 Watts.
  • Net Result: This compounding effect means that your total energy cost will equal the square of your Time Boilers, calculated as (Time Boilers)², while your total heat expansion will equal 10 * (Time Boilers)².

item.title: Chrono Furnace
item.description:
The Chrono Furnace is a powerful late-game upgrade found in the Time tab that heavily enhances your ability to perform time skips (shattering Time Crystals).

Acquisition and Costs

Before you can build a Chrono Furnace, you must first purchase the Chronoforge upgrade. Each Chrono Furnace has a base cost of 25 Time Crystals and 5 Relics, and scales with a 1.25 price ratio.

Core Mechanics and Effects

The Chrono Furnace serves several crucial functions for managing the “chronoheat” generated when you shatter Time Crystals:
item.content:encoded:
The Chrono Furnace is a powerful late-game upgrade found in the Time tab that heavily enhances your ability to perform time skips (shattering Time Crystals).

Acquisition and Costs

Before you can build a Chrono Furnace, you must first purchase the Chronoforge upgrade. Each Chrono Furnace has a base cost of 25 Time Crystals and 5 Relics, and scales with a 1.25 price ratio.

Core Mechanics and Effects

The Chrono Furnace serves several crucial functions for managing the “chronoheat” generated when you shatter Time Crystals:

  • Heat Capacity and Cooling: Each furnace increases your maximum chronoheat limit by 100 and passively dissipates heat at a rate of -0.02 chronoheat per tick.
  • Cooldown Reduction: It drastically reduces the cooldown time required between time skips. The cooldown is calculated as 50 seconds / (Number of Chrono Furnaces + 1). For example, owning 24 Chrono Furnaces allows you to shatter Time Crystals every 2 seconds.
  • Fuel and Automation: Chrono Furnaces automatically convert your accumulated chronoheat into chrono furnace fuel. If you toggle automation “on,” the furnace will automatically spend 500% of its stored fuel each tick to trigger a free time skip. You also have the option to toggle automation off, allowing you to hoard fuel and delay your time skips for a later burst.

Synergies and Related Upgrades

  • Time Boilers: An upgrade that expands the heat capacity of your Chrono Furnaces.
  • Controlled Delay: Because massive amounts of stored fuel can cause the furnace to fire too rapidly for you to click anything else, the Controlled Delay upgrade forces the automated Chrono Furnace to wait 0.2 seconds between firing, allowing you to perform meaningful actions during the skips.
  • 1000 Years Challenge: Completing this challenge increases the efficiency of converting chronoheat into Chrono Furnace fuel by 10% per completion, and makes each shatter directly add a bit of heat to the furnace to offset lost heat generation.

Strategic Importance

In the deep endgame, Chrono Furnaces are a mandatory component of “Shatter Engines”. By building dozens of Chrono Furnaces alongside Resource Retrieval, you can rapidly and automatically skip thousands of years into the future, harvesting massive amounts of resources (like antimatter and unobtainium) in fractions of the real-world time it would normally take.

item.title: Scholar
item.description:
+0.175 science per second

Scholars are a specialized job for your kittens that becomes available after you construct your first Library (which requires 25 Wood). Their primary function is to generate Science, which is essential for purchasing new technologies and unlocking Workshop upgrades.

Core Production

Each kitten actively assigned as a Scholar generates a base output of +0.035 Science per tick.

Upgrades and Late-Game Utility

While their main purpose is Science generation, Scholars gain a massive secondary utility in the late game through the Astrophysicists workshop upgrade.

Scholars are a specialized job for your kittens that becomes available after you construct your first Library (which requires 25 Wood). Their primary function is to generate Science, which is essential for purchasing new technologies and unlocking Workshop upgrades.

Core Production

Upgrades and Late-Game Utility

While their main purpose is Science generation, Scholars gain a massive secondary utility in the late game through the Astrophysicists workshop upgrade.

  • Astrophysicists: Costing 250,000 Science and 350 Unobtainium, this upgrade enables each of your Scholar kittens to passively produce +0.0005 starcharts per second.

Because starcharts can become a major bottleneck for space exploration and ship building, reallocating extra kittens to the Scholar job is an effective late-game strategy to boost your starchart generation without relying solely on manual astronomical events.

item.title: Priest
item.description:
+0.0075 faith per second

[Priests] ( /job/priest/) are a specialized job for your kittens that becomes available after you research the Theology science technology. Their primary role is to generate Faith, which is the fundamental resource used in the game’s Religion tab.

Core Production

  • Base Output: A kitten assigned as a Priest natively produces 0.0015 faith per tick.

Strategic Importance: The Late Game

While [Priests] ( /job/priest/) are introduced in the mid-game, they become arguably the most important job assignment in the deep late game. As you progress into the Relic and Unicorn eras, most conventional resources matter less, and your primary goal shifts to maximizing your global production via the Solar Revolution religion upgrade.
item.content:encoded:
+0.0075 faith per second

[Priests] ( /job/priest/) are a specialized job for your kittens that becomes available after you research the Theology science technology. Their primary role is to generate Faith, which is the fundamental resource used in the game’s Religion tab.

Core Production

  • Base Output: A kitten assigned as a Priest natively produces 0.0015 faith per tick.

Strategic Importance: The Late Game

While [Priests] ( /job/priest/) are introduced in the mid-game, they become arguably the most important job assignment in the deep late game. As you progress into the Relic and Unicorn eras, most conventional resources matter less, and your primary goal shifts to maximizing your global production via the Solar Revolution religion upgrade.

To fuel this, you will eventually assign almost all of your kittens as [Priests] ( /job/priest/). The massive amounts of faith they generate are continually converted into Worship (by using the “Praise the Sun” action), which can exponentially boost your entire civilization’s production by up to +1000%.

Upgrades and Boosts

You can improve the effectiveness of your [Priests] ( /job/priest/) through specific upgrades:

  • Solar Chant: This religion upgrade increases your total faith production by +10%. You can purchase additional levels of Solar Chant after you unlock Transcendence, with each level granting another +10% boost.
  • Order of the Void: This Metaphysics upgrade (which costs 75 Paragon) fundamentally changes how [Priests] ( /job/priest/) work. Once purchased, all of your [Priests] ( /job/priest/) (and any other faith-producing structures) will automatically generate an additional 10% of their faith output directly as Worship. This acts as a powerful passive engine for building your Solar Revolution bonus.

item.title: Miner
item.description:
adds +0.25 mineral per second

Quote: “I don’t really understand how can I hold a pick with my paws”

Miners are a specialized job you can assign to your kittens, serving as your civilization’s primary workforce for generating Minerals.

Acquisition and Prerequisites

To employ Miners, you must first research the Mining science technology, which grants you the ability to construct a Mine. Building your first Mine officially unlocks the Miner job, while also providing a permanent +20% boost to your overall mineral production.

Miners are a specialized job you can assign to your kittens, serving as your civilization’s primary workforce for generating Minerals.

Acquisition and Prerequisites

To employ Miners, you must first research the Mining science technology, which grants you the ability to construct a Mine. Building your first Mine officially unlocks the Miner job, while also providing a permanent +20% boost to your overall mineral production.

Core Production

Each kitten actively assigned as a Miner natively generates 0.05 minerals per tick.

Strategic Importance

Minerals are a fundamental resource necessary for purchasing and crafting a wide variety of advanced buildings and expansions for your village. When balancing your workforce during the early stages of the game, a highly recommended strategy is to employ about half as many Miners as you have Woodcutters. Because wood is required to build the Mines that boost your mineral output, maintaining this specific ratio typically results in a stable and equal production rate of both wood and minerals.

item.title: Geologist
item.description:
adds +0.075 coal per second (may be upgraded)

Geologists are a specialized job you can assign to your kittens that primarily provides a steady source of coal, and later, gold.

Acquisition and Prerequisites

  • Unlock: The Geologist job becomes available once you research the Geology science technology.
  • Cost: Reaching Geology requires progressing past the Navigation technology and saving up 65,000 Science and 65 Compendiums. Because of the high science capacity required, it is generally considered a mid-game job.

Core Production

  • Base Output: A Geologist natively produces +0.015 coal per tick.
  • Strategic Use: Early in the mid-game, coal can be a major bottleneck (especially since active Steamworks consume it heavily), making Geologists an excellent way to increase coal income without relying solely on Smelters or Mines. If you lack coal for vital mid-game structures like Oil Wells, assigning more Geologists is a standard strategy.

Upgrades and Boosts

Geologists can be significantly improved through specific Workshop upgrades, effectively turning them into the backbone of your late-game trade economy:
item.content:encoded:
adds +0.075 coal per second (may be upgraded)

Geologists are a specialized job you can assign to your kittens that primarily provides a steady source of coal, and later, gold.

Acquisition and Prerequisites

  • Unlock: The Geologist job becomes available once you research the Geology science technology.
  • Cost: Reaching Geology requires progressing past the Navigation technology and saving up 65,000 Science and 65 Compendiums. Because of the high science capacity required, it is generally considered a mid-game job.

Core Production

  • Base Output: A Geologist natively produces +0.015 coal per tick.
  • Strategic Use: Early in the mid-game, coal can be a major bottleneck (especially since active Steamworks consume it heavily), making Geologists an excellent way to increase coal income without relying solely on Smelters or Mines. If you lack coal for vital mid-game structures like Oil Wells, assigning more Geologists is a standard strategy.

Upgrades and Boosts

Geologists can be significantly improved through specific Workshop upgrades, effectively turning them into the backbone of your late-game trade economy:

  • Geodesy: Arguably the most important upgrade for this job. Costing 90,000 Science, 250 Titanium, and 500 Starcharts, Geodesy increases coal output by +0.0075 per tick and allows Geologists to passively generate gold at a rate of +0.0008 per tick (or +0.004 per second). Once you reach the Space phase, you will likely assign the vast majority of your kittens as Geologists, using their gold production to fuel massive trades with Zebras for titanium and iron.
  • Mining Drill: Costs 100k Science, 1,750 Titanium, and 750 Steel. It increases Geologist coal production by +0.01 per tick, and gold production by +0.0005 per tick (provided you have already researched Geodesy).
  • Unobtainium Drill: Costs 250k Science, 250 Unobtainium, and 1,250 Alloy. It adds another +0.015 coal per tick and +0.0005 gold per tick.

item.title: Exophysics
item.description:
Exophysics is a highly advanced late-game Science technology.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Prerequisite: You must first research the Hydroponics technology.
  • Cost: Researching Exophysics requires a massive investment of 25 Million Science and 500 Relics.

Unlocked Content

Researching Exophysics unlocks the Molten Core space upgrade.

The Molten Core upgrade costs 25 Million Science and 5 Million Uranium. It is used to directly improve the energy output of your Tectonic space structures (which are built in the Centaurus System). Every level of Molten Core you purchase will increase Tectonic energy production by +5%.

item.title: Hunter
item.description:
produces +0.3 catpower per second

We’re so cute we purr at our prey until it dies

Hunters are a specialized job for your kittens that becomes available after you research the Archery technology. Their primary function is to slowly generate Catpower, which they produce at a base rate of 0.06 per tick.

The Hunting Mechanic

Whenever you accumulate 100 Catpower, you can initiate a hunt. Interestingly, you do not actually need to have any kittens actively assigned to the Hunter job to perform a hunt; you only need to have the required 100 Catpower saved up.

Hunters are a specialized job for your kittens that becomes available after you research the Archery technology. Their primary function is to slowly generate Catpower, which they produce at a base rate of 0.06 per tick.

The Hunting Mechanic

Whenever you accumulate 100 Catpower, you can initiate a hunt. Interestingly, you do not actually need to have any kittens actively assigned to the Hunter job to perform a hunt; you only need to have the required 100 Catpower saved up.

Hunting is essential for progressing through the game because it yields several rare and valuable resources:

  • Furs and Ivory: These are the most common drops you will receive. Simply possessing these luxury items grants a +10% boost to your kittens’ happiness for each resource type. However, Furs and Ivory will gradually degrade over time, so it is best to use them (such as crafting Furs into Parchment) rather than hoarding them.
  • Unicorns: Every hunt has a 5% chance to yield a Unicorn, which eventually allows you to build Unicorn Pastures.
  • Gold (Iron Will Mode): If you are playing the kitten-less Iron Will mode and have the Gold Ore upgrade, each hunt has a 25% chance to yield gold.
  • Bloodstones (Iron Will Mode): In Iron Will mode, if you have at least 10 Zebras, every hunt has a 0.05% chance to drop a bloodstone (this chance increases to 5% if you currently possess zero bloodstones).

Note: Hunting is completely disabled if you are attempting the Pacifism challenge.

Upgrades and Boosts

You can improve your Hunters and the hunting mechanic through two distinct upgrade paths in the Workshop:

  • Catpower Production Boosts: Upgrades such as the Composite Bow (+50%), Crossbow (+25%), and Railgun (+25%) directly increase the amount of Catpower your assigned Hunters generate per tick.
  • Hunting Yield Boosts: Upgrades such as Bolas, Hunting Armour, Steel Armour, Alloy Armour, and Nanosuits increase your civilization’s overall “Hunting bonus”. This bonus stacks additively and directly multiplies the amount of Furs, Ivory, and other random resources you receive every time you spend 100 Catpower to execute a hunt.

item.title: Iron Axe
item.description:
The Iron Axe is an early-game Workshop upgrade that significantly boosts your wood production.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Cost: Purchasing the upgrade requires 100 Science and 50 Iron.

Core Effects and Mechanics

  • Boost: It makes your Woodcutter kittens 50% more effective, directly increasing the amount of wood they generate per tick.
  • The Axe Chain: The Iron Axe is part of the “axe” chain of workshop upgrades, which progresses from the Mineral Axe up through Steel, Titanium, Alloy, and Unobtainium axes.
  • Synergy: Importantly, the production bonuses from the axe chain of upgrades stack multiplicatively with the bonuses provided by Lumber Mills, making them incredibly valuable for scaling your wood economy as you progress.

item.title: Invisible_Black_Hand
item.description:
The Invisible Black Hand is a late-game upgrade that gives you greater control over the game’s cryptocurrency economy.

Here are the details:

  • Core Effect: It adds an option that allows you to force a blackcoin market crash in exchange for time crystals. The in-game description states that it leads the blackcoin market “usually smoothly, but it can punch the market in the face if angry” (and notes that it is not related to the Invisible Pink Unicorn).
  • Prerequisite: You must first unlock Blackchain.
  • Cost: Purchasing the Invisible Black Hand requires 128 Time Crystals, 64 Blackcoin, 32 Void, and 4,096 Temporal Flux.

item.title: Farmer
item.description:
produces +5 catnip per second

Farmers are one of the earliest specialized jobs you can assign to your kittens. Unlocked by researching Agriculture, they serve as your civilization’s primary defense against starvation during the early game.

Core Production and Mechanics

  • Base Output: A Farmer produces 1 catnip per tick (which equates to 5 catnip per second).
  • Net Gain: Because every working kitten natively consumes 0.85 catnip per tick, assigning a kitten as a Farmer yields a net gain of 0.15 catnip per tick.

Strategic Importance: Surviving Winter

The most critical attribute of Farmers is that their production is completely immune to seasonal and weather penalties. While your Catnip Fields will suffer a devastating production drop of up to -75% (or -90% in a Cold Winter), Farmers will continue producing at their full, regular rate. In the early stages of the game, a standard and vital strategy is to reallocate all or most of your kittens to the Farmer job just before Winter arrives to ensure your village does not starve.

Farmers are one of the earliest specialized jobs you can assign to your kittens. Unlocked by researching Agriculture, they serve as your civilization’s primary defense against starvation during the early game.

Core Production and Mechanics

  • Base Output: A Farmer produces 1 catnip per tick (which equates to 5 catnip per second).
  • Net Gain: Because every working kitten natively consumes 0.85 catnip per tick, assigning a kitten as a Farmer yields a net gain of 0.15 catnip per tick.

Strategic Importance: Surviving Winter

The most critical attribute of Farmers is that their production is completely immune to seasonal and weather penalties. While your Catnip Fields will suffer a devastating production drop of up to -75% (or -90% in a Cold Winter), Farmers will continue producing at their full, regular rate. In the early stages of the game, a standard and vital strategy is to reallocate all or most of your kittens to the Farmer job just before Winter arrives to ensure your village does not starve.

As you construct more Catnip Fields, Pastures, and Aqueducts to bolster your passive catnip generation, you can gradually reduce your reliance on Farmers. Eventually, you may only need to keep a single kitten employed as a Farmer to maintain a positive food balance.

Upgrades and Boosts

You can increase the efficiency of your Farmers through several Workshop upgrades and buildings:

  • Mineral Hoes: Increases Farmer production by +50%.
  • Iron Hoes: Increases Farmer production by an additional +30%.
  • Note on Stacking: These two hoe upgrades stack additively with each other.
  • Aqueducts: Building an Aqueduct provides a +3% boost to your total catnip production, which directly scales the catnip generated by your Farmers.
  • Leadership: If you assign a Farmer as your Leader, their rank will provide a multiplier to your farming output, meaning you will need far fewer kittens working as Farmers to feed your population.

item.title: Eludium Reflectors
item.description:
Eludium Reflectors is an advanced Workshop upgrade that significantly scales your maximum science capacity in the late game.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Prerequisite: It is unlocked by researching the Advanced Exogeology (also known as Exometallurgy) science technology.
  • Cost: Purchasing the upgrade requires 250,000 Science and 15 Eludium.

Core Effects

  • The upgrade installs improved telescope reflectors, which causes every Observatory you own to grant an additional +2% maximum science bonus to the effectiveness of your Libraries and Data Centers.
  • This means your Libraries’ and Data Centers’ max science bonus increases by a percentage equal to 2 multiplied by your total number of Observatories.

Synergy

This upgrade serves as the third and final tier of reflector upgrades. It stacks directly with the earlier Titanium Reflectors and Unobtainium Reflectors, which each also provide a +2% bonus per Observatory. When combined, these upgrades allow a large array of Observatories to exponentially multiply your base science storage limits.
