item.title: Fix Cryochambers
item.description:
The Fix Cryochambers action allows you to repair a Used Cryochamber, making it as good as new after it breaks from carrying a kitten through a game reset.

Costs and Requirements

  • Repair Cost: Fixing a single cryochamber costs a flat rate of 100 Time Crystals, 500 Void, and 3,000 Temporal Flux.
  • Prerequisites: The repair button will only appear on your menu if you currently possess a Used Cryochamber and have already purchased the Chronoforge upgrade.

Strategic Mechanics
item.content:encoded:
The Fix Cryochambers action allows you to repair a Used Cryochamber, making it as good as new after it breaks from carrying a kitten through a game reset.

Costs and Requirements

  • Repair Cost: Fixing a single cryochamber costs a flat rate of 100 Time Crystals, 500 Void, and 3,000 Temporal Flux.
  • Prerequisites: The repair button will only appear on your menu if you currently possess a Used Cryochamber and have already purchased the Chronoforge upgrade.

Strategic Mechanics

  • Bypassing Build Limits: By fixing broken chambers rather than just building new ones, you can actually accumulate more Cryochambers than your active number of Chronospheres. However, you should note that the maximum number of kittens you can bring back with you on your next reset is still strictly limited by your number of active Chronospheres.
  • Challenge Complications: If you use cryochambers to bring kittens into certain restrictive challenges (such as Atheism or Pacifism), you will not be able to reclaim your reserve resources to help pay for their repairs. This means you will be forced to generate all of the necessary Time Crystals, Void, and Temporal Flux entirely from scratch during that challenge run, or risk losing those kittens on your next reset.

item.title: Cryochamber
item.description:
Cryochambers are late-game Void Space structures that allow you to carry kittens over into your next game reset. Each Cryochamber houses one kitten, and upon resetting, the game will prioritise saving the kittens with the highest experience levels.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Prerequisite: You must research the Void Space technology to unlock them.
  • Standard Cost: Building one costs 2 Time Crystals, 100 Void, and 1 Karma.
  • Cost Reduction: The Karma cost can be reduced by your burned paragon, with diminishing returns eventually capping at a 100% reduction.

Limits and Capacity

Normally, you cannot build more Cryochambers than your current number of active Chronospheres. However, completing the Post Apocalypse challenge increases the amount of operational Cryochambers you can support, effectively capping them at your number of Chronospheres plus your total Post Apocalypse challenge completions.
item.content:encoded:
Cryochambers are late-game Void Space structures that allow you to carry kittens over into your next game reset. Each Cryochamber houses one kitten, and upon resetting, the game will prioritise saving the kittens with the highest experience levels.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Prerequisite: You must research the Void Space technology to unlock them.
  • Standard Cost: Building one costs 2 Time Crystals, 100 Void, and 1 Karma.
  • Cost Reduction: The Karma cost can be reduced by your burned paragon, with diminishing returns eventually capping at a 100% reduction.

Limits and Capacity

Normally, you cannot build more Cryochambers than your current number of active Chronospheres. However, completing the Post Apocalypse challenge increases the amount of operational Cryochambers you can support, effectively capping them at your number of Chronospheres plus your total Post Apocalypse challenge completions.

Used Cryochambers and Repairs

After you reset the game and successfully carry your kittens over, your Cryochambers will break and become Used Cryochambers. In this state, they do absolutely nothing, but they can be repaired using the Fix Cryochambers action.

  • Repair Cost: Fixing a Used Cryochamber costs a flat rate of 100 Time Crystals, 500 Void, and 3,000 Temporal Flux.
  • Prerequisite for Repair: You must have the Chronoforge upgrade for the repair button to appear on your menu.
  • Strategy Note: You can fix used chambers to theoretically own more Cryochambers than Chronospheres, but the number of kittens you can actually bring into the next run will always remain strictly limited by your active Chronosphere limit.

Role in Challenges

  • Atheism: The primary victory condition for the Atheism challenge is to reach space and reset the game with at least one active Cryochamber.
  • Post Apocalypse: In this highly polluted challenge timeline, having a high number of broken Cryochambers makes the game significantly harder by causing Catnip Fields to cost unobtainium. If you successfully bring kittens into this challenge via Cryochambers, you will also bring over a proportional store of catnip to help your newly transferred population survive.

item.title: Temporal Flux
item.description:
Temporal Flux is an uncommon endgame resource used for various time-related experiments and technologies.

How to Acquire Temporal Flux:

  • Offline Generation: It is passively earned at a rate of 5 units per minute while the game is not active (i.e., when it is closed or paused).
  • Chronosurge Upgrade: Once you purchase the Chronosurge upgrade, each of your Chronospheres will automatically generate 1 temporal flux every game year.

Key Uses:

  • Tempus Fugit: You can spend temporal flux to activate Tempus Fugit, a state which accelerates the game’s tick rate and calendar time speed by 50%, significantly boosting your resource gain. This consumes 5 temporal flux per second while activated.
  • Fixing Cryochambers: Repairing a Used Cryochamber to bring kittens into your next run costs 3,000 temporal flux, alongside 100 Time Crystals and 500 Void.
  • Time Upgrades: It is a required currency to purchase advanced time-manipulation upgrades, including Chronocontrol (costs 3,000 flux) and Chronosurge (costs 6,500 flux).

Game Resets: Conveniently, any accumulated temporal flux you have is automatically saved and carries over when you reset the game.

Temporal Flux is an uncommon endgame resource used for various time-related experiments and technologies.

How to Acquire Temporal Flux:

  • Offline Generation: It is passively earned at a rate of 5 units per minute while the game is not active (i.e., when it is closed or paused).
  • Chronosurge Upgrade: Once you purchase the Chronosurge upgrade, each of your Chronospheres will automatically generate 1 temporal flux every game year.

Key Uses:

  • Tempus Fugit: You can spend temporal flux to activate Tempus Fugit, a state which accelerates the game’s tick rate and calendar time speed by 50%, significantly boosting your resource gain. This consumes 5 temporal flux per second while activated.
  • Fixing Cryochambers: Repairing a Used Cryochamber to bring kittens into your next run costs 3,000 temporal flux, alongside 100 Time Crystals and 500 Void.
  • Time Upgrades: It is a required currency to purchase advanced time-manipulation upgrades, including Chronocontrol (costs 3,000 flux) and Chronosurge (costs 6,500 flux).

Game Resets: Conveniently, any accumulated temporal flux you have is automatically saved and carries over when you reset the game.

Storage

In Kittens Game, the maximum capacity for Temporal Flux is determined by a specific time-related upgrade.

The Primary Method: Temporal Battery

To increase your maximum temporal flux capacity, you must purchase the Temporal Battery upgrade:

  • Where to find it: It is located under the Time tab, which is unlocked after researching Calendar.
  • The Cost: Constructing your first Temporal Battery costs 5 Time Crystals.
  • The Price Ratio: It has a price ratio of 1.25, meaning each subsequent level will cost 25% more Time Crystals than the last.
  • The Effect: Every level of Temporal Battery you purchase permanently increases your maximum temporal flux capacity by +25%.

Optimising Your Temporal Flux Generation

While you are building up your capacity, you can also improve how quickly you accumulate and gather temporal flux:

  1. Offline Accumulation (Base Rate): Temporal flux is earned passively at a rate of 5 units per minute while the game is either paused or completely closed.
  2. Temporal Accelerators: This Time tab upgrade (costing 10 Time Crystals and 1,000 Relics) increases the production of temporal flux generated via redshift (offline progression) by 5%.
  3. Chronosurge (Active Gathering): Once you can afford this Workshop upgrade (which requires 1 Chronocontrol, 25 Time Crystals, 100k Unobtainium, 750 Void, and 6,500 Temporal Flux), your Chronospheres will begin actively generating 1 temporal flux per year on the calendar, acting similarly to Sunlifters.

Why Is High Capacity Important?

Maximising your temporal flux capacity is crucial for two major late-game systems:

  • Tempus Fugit: Activating this accelerates the game’s tick rate and calendar speed by 50%. However, it consumes a heavy 5 temporal flux per second while active, meaning a low cap will quickly drain your reserve.
  • Fixing Cryochambers: If you are using Cryochambers to carry over kittens across resets, repairing a used chamber back to operating condition requires a massive flat cost of 3,000 temporal flux (along with 100 Time Crystals and 500 Void). Having a high maximum capacity is mandatory to store enough flux to repair multiple chambers at once.

🔄 We can explore how to set up the endgame “Cryo Engine” to utilise this temporal flux and farm millions of Paragon per day through rapid resets.

item.title: Used Cryochamber
item.description:
A Used Cryochamber is an “Unsealed Cryochamber” that is currently “Not in operating condition”. In this broken state, the structure does absolutely nothing, but it can be repaired.

Cryochambers become “used” after you perform a game reset and successfully utilize them to carry your kittens over into your new run.

To restore a Used Cryochamber and make it as good as new, you must use the Fix Cryochambers action, which costs a flat rate of 100 Time Crystals, 500 Void, and 3,000 Temporal Flux. Keep in mind that the option to repair them will only appear on your menu if you have already purchased the Chronoforge upgrade.

item.title: What buildings increase max science
item.description:
Several buildings and structures increase your maximum science capacity, ranging from early-game terrestrial buildings to late-game space structures.

Standard Terrestrial Buildings

  • Libraries: The first science building, providing +250 Max Science.
  • Academies: Provides +500 Max Science.
  • Observatories: Provides +1,000 Max Science.
  • Bio Labs: Provides +1,500 Max Science.
  • Data Centers: An upgraded version of the Library that provides +750 Max Science.

Buildings Requiring Specific Upgrades

  • Temples: Initially provide no science, but after purchasing the Scholasticism religion upgrade, each Temple provides +500 Max Science. Each additional level of Scholasticism purchased via Transcendence increases this by an extra +100.
  • Accelerators: Normally used for uranium, but once the LHC (Large Hadron Collider) workshop upgrade is researched, each Accelerator provides +2,500 Max Science.

Space Structures

  • Research Vessels: Found on the Piscine mission, each provides +10,000 Max Science.
  • Space Beacons: Found on the Kairo mission, each provides a massive +25,000 Max Science.

Craftable Resources

  • Compendiums: While not a building, crafting this resource is vital for science storage. Each Compendium adds +10 to your Max Science. This bonus is capped at 100% of your maximum science from buildings (or 1000% if playing in Iron Will mode).

Important Scaling Upgrades

Your base maximum science can be multiplied and scaled through several Workshop and Space upgrades:

  • Reflectors (Titanium, Unobtainium, Eludium): These upgrades allow your Observatories to boost the effectiveness of your Libraries and Data Centers.
  • Uplink & Starlink: These upgrades create a synergy where your Bio Labs and Data Centers provide percentage-based max science boosts to each other.
  • Antimatter & Void Reactors: These endgame upgrades massively multiply the science capacity of your Space Beacons and Research Vessels by up to +400%.

item.title: Eludium Huts
item.description:
Eludium Huts is a high-tier Workshop upgrade that provides the final available reduction to the price ratio of Hut buildings. It is a key component for maximizing your kitten population before a reset to increase prestige rewards.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Science Cost: 275,000.
  • Resource Cost: 125 Eludium.
  • Prerequisite Technology: You must first research Exometallurgy (which was formerly known as Advanced Exogeology).

Core Effects and Mechanics

The primary function of this upgrade is to reduce the Hut price ratio by 10%.
item.content:encoded:
Eludium Huts is a high-tier Workshop upgrade that provides the final available reduction to the price ratio of Hut buildings. It is a key component for maximizing your kitten population before a reset to increase prestige rewards.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Science Cost: 275,000.
  • Resource Cost: 125 Eludium.
  • Prerequisite Technology: You must first research Exometallurgy (which was formerly known as Advanced Exogeology).

Core Effects and Mechanics

The primary function of this upgrade is to reduce the Hut price ratio by 10%.

  • Ratio Reduction: When stacked with earlier upgrades—Ironwood (-50%), Concrete (-30%), and Unobtainium (-25%)—this brings the Hut price ratio down to approximately 1.289.
  • Population Scaling: This reduction allows you to build approximately 23% more Huts than was possible with Unobtainium Huts alone. For instance, a player who previously capped at 50 Huts could reach 61 Huts after this upgrade, adding 22 extra kittens to their village.

Strategic Importance

  • The Eludium Era: Purchasing this upgrade typically occurs as you transition into the mid-to-late game, often coinciding with the beginning of the Unicorn Era and the stabilization of unobtainium production at approximately 1 per second.
  • Paragon Farming: Because reset rewards (Paragon and Karma) are calculated based on population, Eludium Huts are essential for “deep runs” where you aim to maximize your total kitten count.
  • Efficiency Considerations: While valuable for long runs, some optimization guides suggest that Eludium Huts may be ignored during short paragon-grinding runs. This is because the additional kittens only improve paragon-per-hour efficiency by about 1% (for example, increasing efficiency from 86% to 86.6%), which may not justify the 125 eludium cost in a fast-reset scenario.
  • Science Cap Synergy: During this era, your science cap must be sufficiently high (around 275k) to purchase the upgrade, which usually requires a significant network of Observatories, Data Centers, and Bio Labs.

item.title: Electrolytic Smelting
item.description:
Electrolytic Smelting is a powerful mid-to-late-game Workshop upgrade that significantly boosts the output of your terrestrial Smelters.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Prerequisite Technology: You must first research the Metallurgy science.
  • Resource Requirements:
    • Science: 100,000
    • Titanium: 2,000.

Core Effects

This upgrade makes Smelters “twice as effective” by providing a massive boost to their primary outputs:

  • Iron Production: Increases iron yield from Smelters by +95%.
  • Coal Production: Increases coal yield from Smelters (assuming you have the Coal Furnace upgrade) by +95%.

Strategic Importance

  • Doubling Output: Electrolytic Smelting effectively doubles your Smelter production rate for two critical industrial resources.
  • Resource Bottlenecks: This upgrade is essential for scaling your industrial base. Iron is constantly needed for building components and Observatories, while Coal is the primary ingredient for Steel, which becomes a major bottleneck as you approach the Space era.
  • Synergy: It works alongside other Smelter upgrades like Gold Ore (+0.001 gold/tick) and Nuclear Smelters (+0.0015 titanium/tick), transforming simple early-game buildings into advanced multi-resource refineries.

This upgrade makes Smelters “twice as effective” by providing a massive boost to their primary outputs:

  • Iron Production: Increases iron yield from Smelters by +95%.
  • Coal Production: Increases coal yield from Smelters (assuming you have the Coal Furnace upgrade) by +95%.

Strategic Importance

  • Doubling Output: Electrolytic Smelting effectively doubles your Smelter production rate for two critical industrial resources.
  • Resource Bottlenecks: This upgrade is essential for scaling your industrial base. Iron is constantly needed for building components and Observatories, while Coal is the primary ingredient for Steel, which becomes a major bottleneck as you approach the Space era.
  • Synergy: It works alongside other Smelter upgrades like Gold Ore (+0.001 gold/tick) and Nuclear Smelters (+0.0015 titanium/tick), transforming simple early-game buildings into advanced multi-resource refineries.

item.title: Pollution
item.description:
In Kittens Game, pollution (represented as atmospheric CO2) is a late-game mechanic that negatively impacts your civilization’s productivity and growth as you industrialize. While its effects are generally negligible up to approximately 1,000 ppm, higher levels progressively harm your village in several ways.

Sources of Pollution

Pollution is primarily generated by industrial buildings and certain environmental policies:

  • Industrial Buildings: Mines, Smelters, Steamworks, Calciners, Quarries, Magnetos, Oil Wells, Bio Labs, and Factories all contribute to pollution.
  • Policies: Choosing production-heavy policies like Strip Mining, Clear Cutting, Full Industrialization, or Open Woodlands each adds a +5% increase to global pollution.
  • Challenges: In the Post Apocalypse challenge, you start in a broken timeline where pollution begins at a staggering 10 million ppm.

Negative Effects

As pollution levels rise, they trigger a series of cascading penalties:
item.content:encoded:
In Kittens Game, pollution (represented as atmospheric CO2) is a late-game mechanic that negatively impacts your civilization’s productivity and growth as you industrialize. While its effects are generally negligible up to approximately 1,000 ppm, higher levels progressively harm your village in several ways.

Sources of Pollution

Pollution is primarily generated by industrial buildings and certain environmental policies:

  • Industrial Buildings: Mines, Smelters, Steamworks, Calciners, Quarries, Magnetos, Oil Wells, Bio Labs, and Factories all contribute to pollution.
  • Policies: Choosing production-heavy policies like Strip Mining, Clear Cutting, Full Industrialization, or Open Woodlands each adds a +5% increase to global pollution.
  • Challenges: In the Post Apocalypse challenge, you start in a broken timeline where pollution begins at a staggering 10 million ppm.

Negative Effects

As pollution levels rise, they trigger a series of cascading penalties:

  • Production Hits: High levels of pollution directly reduce catnip production. Eventually, it also reduces the Solar Revolution bonus for certain resources.
  • Societal Impact: Pollution decreases kitten happiness and slows down the kitten arrival speed.
  • Economic Costs: In extreme cases (like the Post Apocalypse challenge), trade costs for gold and catpower increase, and Catnip Fields may even begin to cost Unobtainium.

Mitigation and Management

While some pollution is considered inevitable, it can be managed through the following methods:

  • Environmental Policies:
    • Environmentalism, Sustainability, and Conservation each provide a -5% reduction to global pollution.
    • Lizard Relations: Ecologists can be enacted to further reduce pollution by 5%.
  • Carbon Sequestration: This high-tier Workshop upgrade (unlocked via Ecology) allows your Factories to capture pollution instead of producing it. When enabled, each Factory consumes 4 Watts of energy but reduces pollution by 2 points per tick.
  • Clean Energy: Utilizing environmentally friendly energy sources helps mitigate the need for polluting structures.
  • Operational Control: You can simply turn off polluting buildings to halt their contribution to CO2 levels.

For players who want to see the specific impact, typing game.detailedPollutionInfo=true into the browser console will display more detailed pollution numbers on the Science tab.

Building Impact on Pollution

Pollution per Tick for

  • Calciner: 1
  • Mine: 0.08
  • Magneto: 5
  • Factory: -2 if automation is enabled
  • OilWell : 1 if automation is enabled, else 0
  • Quarry : 0.25
  • Smelter: 0.15
  • Steamworks: 1

item.title: Robotic Assistance
item.description:
Robotic Assistance is a mid-to-late-game Workshop upgrade that improves the efficiency of your workforce by reducing their food requirements.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Prerequisite Technology: You must first research the Robotics science, which costs 140,000 Science and 80 Blueprints.
  • Upgrade Resource Requirements:
    • Science: 100,000
    • Steel: 10,000
    • Gears: 250.

Core Effect

The primary benefit of Robotic Assistance is that it reduces the catnip consumption of all working kittens by 25%. By building robots to assist with labor, your “workers do less effort” and therefore require less food to maintain their productivity.
item.content:encoded:
Robotic Assistance is a mid-to-late-game Workshop upgrade that improves the efficiency of your workforce by reducing their food requirements.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Prerequisite Technology: You must first research the Robotics science, which costs 140,000 Science and 80 Blueprints.
  • Upgrade Resource Requirements:
    • Science: 100,000
    • Steel: 10,000
    • Gears: 250.

Core Effect

The primary benefit of Robotic Assistance is that it reduces the catnip consumption of all working kittens by 25%. By building robots to assist with labor, your “workers do less effort” and therefore require less food to maintain their productivity.

Strategic Importance

  • Managing the Food Burden: Each kitten in your village normally consumes 4.25 catnip per second (0.85 per tick). As your population grows, this consumption becomes a significant constraint on your expansion. Robotic Assistance provides a powerful global reduction to this burden, specifically for those kittens assigned to jobs.
  • Mitigating Happiness Penalties: When kitten happiness exceeds 100%, their catnip consumption increases significantly (for example, at 420% happiness, consumption increases by 320%). Researching Robotic Assistance is a vital step in balancing this “happiness liability,” allowing you to maintain high production bonuses from a happy population without triggering catastrophic food shortages.
  • Synergy with Automation: It is typically researched alongside other automation-focused upgrades like Factory Robotics and Steel Plants, which together transition your village from manual labor to a more industrialized and efficient economy.

item.title: Railgun
item.description:
The Railgun is a high-tier Workshop upgrade that provides a permanent boost to your civilization’s catpower generation.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Prerequisite Technology: You must first research the Particle Physics science (which requires 185,000 Science and 135 Blueprints).
  • Resource Requirements:
    • Science: 150,000
    • Titanium: 5,000
    • Blueprints: 25.

Core Effects

The Railgun is categorized as a weapon technology for the Hunter job.

  • Catpower Production: It provides a +25% boost to catpower production.
  • Hunter Efficiency: This bonus specifically increases the rate at which Hunter kittens (or Zebras in Iron Will mode) generate catpower.

Strategic Utility

  • Hunting and Trading: By increasing the rate of catpower accumulation, the Railgun allows you to send out more frequent hunting expeditions (for furs, ivory, and unicorns) and perform more trades with other civilizations.
  • Iron Will Mode: It is considered a vital late-game upgrade for Iron Will runs. Since players in this mode cannot use kittens, they rely entirely on Zebras to generate catpower; the Railgun helps overcome the scarcity of this resource for high-level tasks like launching orbital missions.
  • Late-Game Scaling: It is one of the final upgrades in the weapon chain, which includes the Composite Bow (+50% catpower) and Crossbow (+25% catpower).

Challenge Modifier: Pacifism

In the Pacifism challenge (where hunting is disabled), the effectiveness of weapon technologies like the Railgun is significantly penalized. For each completion of the challenge, the effectiveness of the Railgun is reduced by -10% (additive), up to a maximum penalty of -100%.

item.title: Offset_Press
item.description:
The Offset Press is a mid-to-late-game Workshop upgrade for the Steamworks building that significantly enhances automated manuscript production.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Unlocked By: You must first research the Combustion technology.
  • Resource Requirements:
    • Science: 100,000
    • Gears: 250
    • Oil: 15,000

Core Effects

The Offset Press serves as a direct multiplier to the Printing Press upgrade:

  • Production Boost: It makes the Printing Press four times as effective.
  • Manuscript Rate: It increases the passive manuscript generation of active Steamworks from 0.0025 per second to 0.01 manuscripts/sec.
  • Prerequisite: Purchasing this upgrade is required to eventually unlock Photolithography, which further quadruples production to 0.04 manuscripts/sec.

Strategic Importance

  • Overcoming Bottlenecks: Throughout the mid-game, Manuscripts are a major “speedbump” required for critical research like Theology and Astronomy.
  • Automation: By increasing the effectiveness of Steamworks, the Offset Press allows you to generate manuscripts passively while idling or away from the computer, reducing the need to manually “craft all” after hunting for furs.
  • Synergy: While Steamworks consume coal, maintaining them is vital for this automated production chain, and the Offset Press ensures that the coal-to-manuscript conversion is as efficient as possible.

item.title: Logistics
item.description:
In Kittens Game, logistics primarily refers to two distinct Workshop upgrades that improve workforce efficiency and industrial scaling, as well as broader systems for managing resource distribution.

1. The “Logistics” Workshop Upgrade

This is a mid-game upgrade focused on the productivity of your kittens.

  • Acquisition: Unlocked after researching the Industrialization technology.
  • Cost: 100,000 Science, 100 Gears, and 1,000 Scaffolds.
  • Effect: Increases the production bonus derived from kitten skills by 15%.
  • Synergy: This bonus multiplies with the base skill bonus and stacks additively with the later Augmentations upgrade (+100% skill effectiveness). It ensures that “Master” level kittens provide significantly more resources than “Adequate” ones.

2. The “Factory Logistics” Workshop Upgrade

This is a high-tier industrial upgrade that is critical for transitioning into the endgame “Shatter Engine.”
item.content:encoded:
In Kittens Game, logistics primarily refers to two distinct Workshop upgrades that improve workforce efficiency and industrial scaling, as well as broader systems for managing resource distribution.

1. The “Logistics” Workshop Upgrade

This is a mid-game upgrade focused on the productivity of your kittens.

  • Acquisition: Unlocked after researching the Industrialization technology.
  • Cost: 100,000 Science, 100 Gears, and 1,000 Scaffolds.
  • Effect: Increases the production bonus derived from kitten skills by 15%.
  • Synergy: This bonus multiplies with the base skill bonus and stacks additively with the later Augmentations upgrade (+100% skill effectiveness). It ensures that “Master” level kittens provide significantly more resources than “Adequate” ones.

2. The “Factory Logistics” Workshop Upgrade

This is a high-tier industrial upgrade that is critical for transitioning into the endgame “Shatter Engine.”

  • Acquisition: Unlocked after researching the Electronics technology.
  • Cost: 100,000 Science, 250 Gears, and 2,000 Titanium.
  • Effect on Crafting: Increases the global crafting bonus provided by each Factory by +1%. (This typically moves the base Factory bonus from 5% to 6% per building).
  • Effect on Space Production: It serves as a multiplier for space-based structures. Once the Space Manufacturing upgrade is active, Factory Logistics increases the “Space Bonus” provided by Factories to Space Elevators and Orbital Arrays from 3.75% to 4.5% per Factory.
  • Strategic Importance: This upgrade is essential for maximizing Unobtainium production, as it allows your terrestrial factory network to significantly scale the output of Lunar Outposts.

3. Broader Logistic Systems

The term is also applied to automated management systems within the game:

  • AI Logistics (AI Bases): A Workshop upgrade where each AI Core increases the storage effectiveness of Moon Bases by 10%. This helps manage the massive Unobtainium caps required for building Chronospheres.
  • Trade Logistics (Caravanserai): While not named “logistics,” this upgrade allows Tradeposts to improve your standing with other races, effectively managing the “hostility” of partners like Zebras to ensure successful resource acquisition.
  • Job Management (Register): This Workshop upgrade allows your Leader to manage kitten deployments more efficiently, automatically prioritizing kittens with higher experience levels for job assignments.

item.title: Fluidized Reactors
item.description:
In Kittens Game, Fluidized Reactors (often referred to as Fluidised Reactors) is a high-tier Workshop upgrade that significantly enhances the industrial output of your Calciners.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Prerequisite Technology: You must first research Nanotechnology (which costs 200k Science and 150 Blueprints).
  • Upgrade Cost:
    • Science: 175,000 (175k)
    • Alloy: 200

Core Effects

The primary function of this upgrade is to make Calciners substantially more productive:

  • Production Boost: It increases Calciner Iron production by +100% and Titanium production by +300%.
  • Efficiency: The upgrade is described as making Calciners “twice as effective,” as it provides a flat doubling of the iron output and a massive quadrupling boost to the titanium yield.

Strategic Importance

Fluidized Reactors represent the final major tier in the progression of Calciner-specific production upgrades, following Oxidation (+95% iron, +285% titanium) and Rotary Kiln (+75% iron, +225% titanium).

  • Titanium Bottlenecks: In the late-to-endgame, titanium is required in massive quantities for space structures and advanced materials like Alloy and Eludium. While trading with Zebras remains a primary source, Fluidized Reactors make Calciners a far more viable automated source for maintaining your titanium supply.
  • Automation: When combined with upgrades like Steel Plants (which automatically convert some Calciner iron into Steel), these reactors help create a self-sustaining industrial loop that requires less manual intervention from the player.

item.title: Factory Robotics
item.description:
Factory Robotics is a mid-to-late-game Workshop upgrade that improves the efficiency of your automation by increasing the “know-how” (crafting effectiveness) of your Engineer kittens.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Prerequisite Technology: You must first research the Robotics science (which requires 140,000 Science and 80 Blueprints).
  • Resource Requirements:
    • Science: 75,000
    • Gears: 250
    • Titanium: 1,250.

Core Effects: Engineer Know-How

The upgrade specifically boosts the crafting effectiveness of the first three classes of Engineers. “Know-how” determines how many “Engineer points” each kitten contributes to the Workshop’s automated crafting pool.
item.content:encoded:
Factory Robotics is a mid-to-late-game Workshop upgrade that improves the efficiency of your automation by increasing the “know-how” (crafting effectiveness) of your Engineer kittens.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Prerequisite Technology: You must first research the Robotics science (which requires 140,000 Science and 80 Blueprints).
  • Resource Requirements:
    • Science: 75,000
    • Gears: 250
    • Titanium: 1,250.

Core Effects: Engineer Know-How

The upgrade specifically boosts the crafting effectiveness of the first three classes of Engineers. “Know-how” determines how many “Engineer points” each kitten contributes to the Workshop’s automated crafting pool.

  • Class 1 Engineer: Know-how is set to 10.
  • Class 2 Engineer: Know-how increases to 5.
  • Class 3 Engineer: Know-how is added at 2.

Strategic Importance

Factory Robotics is a direct successor to the Factory Optimization upgrade (which only covers Classes 1 and 2). By expanding and increasing these values, it allows your technical workforce to handle significantly higher resource throughput.

This is particularly vital as your industrial base grows and storage caps for resources like Oil, Iron, and Coal become harder to manage manually. Maximizing Engineer efficiency through this and subsequent upgrades (like Space Engineers or AI Engineers) ensures that your village continues to produce materials like Kerosene or Steel at high speeds while idling.

item.title: Factory Optimization
item.description:
Factory Optimization is a mid-to-late-game Workshop upgrade that enhances the effectiveness of the Engineer kitten job, facilitating better automation of the crafting process.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Prerequisite Technology: Researching Electronics is required to unlock the upgrade.
  • Resource Requirements:
    • Science: 75,000
    • Gears: 250
    • Titanium: 1,250.

Effects on Engineer Know-How

The primary function of this upgrade is to increase the “know-how” (efficiency) of Engineers based on their class:

  • Class 1 Engineer: Know-how increases to 10.
  • Class 2 Engineer: Know-how increases to 2.

This improvement allows a smaller number of Engineers to perform a higher volume of automated crafts, which is critical for managing resources like Oil or Iron that would otherwise hit their storage caps while the player is away.

Effects on Engineer Know-How

  • Class 2 Engineer: Know-how increases to 2.

This improvement allows a smaller number of Engineers to perform a higher volume of automated crafts, which is critical for managing resources like Oil or Iron that would otherwise hit their storage caps while the player is away.

Related Industrial Optimizations

While “Factory Optimization” specifically targets Engineer efficiency, several other “Factory” upgrades and mechanics are essential for maximizing industrial output:

  • Factory Logistics: This upgrade increases the global craft bonus provided by each Factory building by 1% (moving the base bonus from 5% to 6%).
  • Factory Processing: This upgrade links your industrial base to your fuel production, providing a +5% bonus to oil refinement effectiveness (Kerosene production) for every Factory built.
  • Space Manufacturing: A game-changing upgrade that allows Factories to provide a bonus to space structures like Space Elevators and Orbital Arrays. This bonus is calculated as 75% of your total factory craft ratio.
  • Full Industrialization (Policy): This policy makes all Factories 5% more powerful (boosting their crafting and space bonuses) at the cost of increased pollution.

Strategic Importance

In the mid-to-late game, optimizing factories is a top priority because their effects are multiplicative and provide global multipliers. High-level players typically focus on maxing out their Factory count to drive massive Unobtainium production through Space Elevators, as this is the primary gateway to Phase 4 (Endgame) content like Time Crystals and Chronospheres.

item.title: Factory Processing
item.description:
Factory Processing is a mid-to-late-game Workshop upgrade that significantly enhances your civilization’s ability to refine oil into Kerosene by leveraging your industrial infrastructure.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Prerequisite Technology: You must first research Oil Processing, which is unlocked after Rocketry.
  • Resource Requirements:
    • Science: 195,000
    • Titanium: 7,500
    • Concrete: 125.

Core Effects and Mechanics

The primary function of Factory Processing is to link your Factory buildings to your Kerosene production:

  • Scaling Bonus: Each Factory built provides a +5% bonus to oil refinement effectiveness (the amount of Kerosene produced from Oil).
  • Multiplicative Stacking: This effectiveness bonus stacks multiplicatively with your global crafting ratio bonuses, allowing for massive Kerosene yields as your industrial base grows.
  • Workshop Interaction: While primarily categorized as a Factory upgrade, it is purchased in the Workshop and listed as improving “Kerosene Crafting”.

Strategic Importance

  • Fuel for Space Exploration: Kerosene is a critical resource for late-game progression, used as fuel for Spaceports and for sending high-tier space missions like Piscine, Helios, and T-Minus.
  • Managing Oil Caps: Oil production is often slow but hits its storage cap frequently. By using Engineers to automate the conversion of Oil to Kerosene, players can prevent Oil production from stalling; Factory Processing ensures this conversion is as efficient as possible.
  • Infrastructure Synergy: This upgrade transforms Factories from simple crafting boosters into vital components of your energy and fuel supply chain, making large factory networks essential for sustained space operations.

item.title: Particle_Physics
item.description:
Particle Physics is a pivotal mid-to-late-game science technology that serves as the gateway to uranium refining and advanced temporal mechanics.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Science Cost: 185,000 Science.
  • Blueprint Cost: 135 Blueprints.
  • Prerequisite: You must first research Nuclear Fission.
  • Strategic Tip: Assigning a Scientist leader can reduce the science cost of this technology by 5%, bringing it down to approximately 175,750 Science.

Unlocked Buildings: The Accelerator

Researching Particle Physics is the mandatory prerequisite for constructing Accelerators.
item.content:encoded:
Particle Physics is a pivotal mid-to-late-game science technology that serves as the gateway to uranium refining and advanced temporal mechanics.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Science Cost: 185,000 Science.
  • Blueprint Cost: 135 Blueprints.
  • Prerequisite: You must first research Nuclear Fission.
  • Strategic Tip: Assigning a Scientist leader can reduce the science cost of this technology by 5%, bringing it down to approximately 175,750 Science.

Unlocked Buildings: The Accelerator

Researching Particle Physics is the mandatory prerequisite for constructing Accelerators.

  • Function: Accelerators provide a steady source of Uranium by refining Titanium (at a rate of -0.015 Titanium and +0.0025 Uranium per tick).
  • Energy Impact: Each active Accelerator consumes 2 Watts of energy.
  • Storage Potential: Once the Energy Rifts upgrade is researched (via Dimensional Physics), Accelerators provide massive storage capacity for various resources, including catnip, wood, minerals, coal, iron, titanium, and gold.

Unlocked Technologies

Particle Physics is required to unlock two high-tier science branches:

  • Chronophysics: The branch dealing with time manipulation, Chronospheres, and reset preservation.
  • Dimensional Physics: The branch that unlocks the LHC (Large Hadron Collider) and Energy Rifts for expanded storage.

Unlocked Workshop Upgrades

  • Enriched Uranium: Reduces the Uranium consumption of Reactors by 25% and provides a +25% Uranium production bonus to Quarries.
  • Railgun: A permanent military upgrade that increases the Catpower production of Hunter kittens by 25%.

Strategic Importance

Particle Physics marks the transition into the “Metaphysics” era. It is essential for generating the initial Unobtainium needed for space exploration; because Lunar Outposts consume uranium to produce unobtainium, players often rely on Accelerators (and trading with Dragons) to maintain their uranium supply until more efficient space-based uranium sources like Planet Crackers are built.

item.title: Fuel Injector
item.description:
The Fuel Injector is a mid-to-late-game Workshop upgrade for the Steamworks building that improves coal management efficiency.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Unlocked By: Researching the Combustion technology.
  • Resource Requirements:
    • Science: 100,000
    • Gears: 250
    • Oil: 20,000.

Core Effects

The primary function of the Fuel Injector is to reduce the coal production penalty (or coal consumption) of active Steamworks by 20%.

Strategic Context

  • Coal Efficiency: Active Steamworks are notorious for consuming large amounts of coal, which can bottleneck the production of Steel. The Fuel Injector, along with the High Pressure Engine (which provides an identical 20% reduction), is essential for maintaining active Steamworks without completely depleting your coal reserves.
  • Synergy: These upgrades allow you to keep Steamworks running to benefit from their automated features—such as manuscript printing via the Printing Press or the production boost to Magnetos—while still gathering enough coal to support industrial crafting.

item.title: Sustainability vs Full Industrialisation
item.description:
In Kittens Game, Sustainability and Full Industrialization are mutually exclusive environmental policies. They are unlocked after researching Industrialization and require you to have previously chosen either the Strip Mining or Clear Cutting policy.

Sustainability

  • Cost: 10,000 Culture.
  • Primary Effects:
    • Removes the happiness penalty (-2%) incurred from choosing Strip Mining or Clear Cutting.
    • Reduces global pollution by 5%.
  • Strategic Use: This policy is generally recommended for the first run. During your initial playthrough, you will likely only build one or two Factories to unlock the policy system, meaning you cannot take significant advantage of industrial boosts. Sustainability allows you to keep the production bonuses of your earlier policy (wood or minerals) while eliminating the morale hit.

Full Industrialization

  • Cost: 10,000 Culture.
  • Primary Effects:
    • Boosts Factory Power: Makes Factories 5% more powerful. This increases their base crafting bonus from 5% to 5.25% (or from 6% to 6.3% if Factory Logistics is researched).
    • Increases Pollution: Adds a +5% penalty to global pollution.
    • Space Production Synergy: Provides a 5% bonus to the “Space Production Bonus” generated by Factories once the Space Manufacturing upgrade is active.
  • Strategic Use: This is considered the superior choice for the mid-to-late game (typically starting from the second run onwards). Once you begin building dozens of Factories, the multiplicative nature of the crafting bonus becomes far more valuable than the small happiness gain from Sustainability.

Comparison Summary

Feature Sustainability Full Industrialization
Focus Happiness & Environment Crafting & Industrial Scaling
Happiness +2% (restores lost happiness) No bonus
Pollution -5% reduction +5% increase
Factories No effect +5% effectiveness boost
Space Bonus No effect +5% space production bonus
Best For First Run / Low Factory Count Mid-to-Late Game / High Factory Count

Strategic Recommendation: Most players choose Clear Cutting early in the run to resolve wood bottlenecks, then pivot to Full Industrialization once they have a robust factory network. In the late game, Full Industrialization is essential for the “Shatter Engine,” as it significantly scales Unobtainium production through Space Elevators and Orbital Arrays.

item.title: Knowledge sharing vs Cultural Exchange
item.description:
In Kittens Game, Knowledge Sharing and Cultural Exchange are mutually exclusive foreign policies unlocked after researching Astronomy and adopting the Diplomacy policy. Because they are in the same policy group, choosing one will permanently lock the other for the remainder of your current run.

Direct Comparison

Policy Cost Primary Effect Strategic Value
Knowledge Sharing 4,000 Culture +5% science income Generally considered suboptimal because science is relatively easy to generate through Scholars and astronomical events.
Cultural Exchange 4,000 Culture +5% culture income Generally preferred because culture is a notorious mid-game bottleneck required for manuscripts and advanced research.

Strategic Considerations

  • The Culture Bottleneck: Throughout the mid-game (the “Theology” era), players often struggle to produce enough culture to craft the manuscripts needed for scientific advancement. Sources explicitly recommend Cultural Exchange over Knowledge Sharing because “culture is slow” while “science is easy”.
  • Science Management: Science income is rarely the primary constraint on progress, as science caps (expanded by Libraries and Academies) are usually more significant hurdles than science production rates. Consequently, a 5% boost to science income often provides negligible benefits.
  • Iron Will Progression: In the specialised Iron Will mode (playing without kittens), where resources are even tighter, some guides suggest the Diplomacy → Cultural Exchange path as a way to bolster early culture production, which is vital for unlocking trade with the Nagas.

In summary, unless you are in a very specific scenario where your science production is lagging significantly behind your ability to store it, Cultural Exchange is the standard choice to help mitigate the game’s cultural bottlenecks.

item.title: Strip Mining vs Clear Cutting vs Environmentalism
item.description:
In Kittens Game, Strip Mining, Clear Cutting, and Environmentalism are mutually exclusive environmental policies unlocked after researching the Engineering technology. You may only choose one of these policies per run.

Direct Comparison of Effects

Policy Cost Primary Effects Pollution Impact
Clear Cutting 2,000 Science +30% wood production, -2% happiness +5%
Strip Mining 2,000 Science +30% mineral production, -2% happiness +5%
Environmentalism 2,000 Culture +3% happiness -5%

Iron Will Bonuses

In Iron Will mode (where you have no kittens), these policies provide unique bonuses to your zebras and celestial events:
item.content:encoded:
In Kittens Game, Strip Mining, Clear Cutting, and Environmentalism are mutually exclusive environmental policies unlocked after researching the Engineering technology. You may only choose one of these policies per run.

Direct Comparison of Effects

Policy Cost Primary Effects Pollution Impact
Clear Cutting 2,000 Science +30% wood production, -2% happiness +5%
Strip Mining 2,000 Science +30% mineral production, -2% happiness +5%
Environmentalism 2,000 Culture +3% happiness -5%

Iron Will Bonuses

In Iron Will mode (where you have no kittens), these policies provide unique bonuses to your zebras and celestial events:

  • Clear Cutting: +10% bonus to catnip refinement (equivalent to one un-upgraded Lumber Mill).
  • Strip Mining: +10% bonus minerals from meteors.
  • Environmentalism: No specific Iron Will bonus is listed for the base policy, but it leads to Open Woodlands, which provides a 4.16% bonus to both refinement and meteor minerals.

Strategic Advice from the Sources

  • The Case for Clear Cutting: This is widely considered the strongest choice for early-to-mid-game runs. Wood is a major bottleneck when transitioning into the “Titanium Era,” as you need massive amounts of it for Observatories, Harbours, and Ships.
  • The Case for Strip Mining: Generally viewed as the least useful of the production-based choices. Minerals are typically easier to accumulate than wood through standard progression, making the 30% boost less impactful than the wood boost from Clear Cutting.
  • The Case for Environmentalism: Sources describe this policy as “pretty weak” because the 3% happiness boost is often outweighed by the raw production benefits of the other two. However, it is the only option that directly reduces pollution, which otherwise reduces catnip production and Solar Revolution bonuses.

Downstream Policy Unlocks

The choice you make here determines which advanced policies you can research later in the run after reaching Industrialization or Ecology:

Following Clear Cutting or Strip Mining:

  • Sustainability (10k Culture): Removes the -2% happiness penalty from your chosen production policy and provides a further -5% pollution reduction.
  • Full Industrialization (10k Culture): Makes Factories 5% more powerful (boosting their crafting bonus), but increases pollution by another +5%.

Following Environmentalism:

  • Conservation (10k Culture): Increases the happiness bonus from Environmentalism to +5% and provides another -5% pollution reduction.
  • Open Woodlands (10k Culture): A compromise policy that provides +12.5% wood and mineral production at the cost of +5% pollution.

item.title: Burn Paragon
item.description:
In Kittens Game, Burning Paragon is a way to squeeze more efficiency out of your prestige bonuses. It converts your “live” Paragon into Burned Paragon, which exists in a separate pool and stacks with your regular Paragon.

Since you are currently struggling with Faith storage for Sunspires, understanding how burning affects your storage is critical.

1. The Immediate Trade-off

When you burn Paragon, the effect on your current run is usually negative unless you are very far into the game:
item.content:encoded:
In Kittens Game, Burning Paragon is a way to squeeze more efficiency out of your prestige bonuses. It converts your “live” Paragon into Burned Paragon, which exists in a separate pool and stacks with your regular Paragon.

Since you are currently struggling with Faith storage for Sunspires, understanding how burning affects your storage is critical.

1. The Immediate Trade-off

When you burn Paragon, the effect on your current run is usually negative unless you are very far into the game:

  • Storage: Regular Paragon gives 0.1% storage per point. Burned Paragon only gives 0.05% (half as much) before Year 40,000.
  • Production: Regular Paragon caps its bonus at 150 points. Burned Paragon caps its bonus at 75 points.

Why do it then? Because they stack. 150 regular Paragon + 75 burned Paragon gives you a higher production bonus than 1,000 regular Paragon alone, because regular Paragon hits diminishing returns very quickly.

2. When to Burn for Your Faith Problem

Burning Paragon is a “reset” for your storage, which might actually make your Sunspire problem worse in the short term. However, it is a powerful long-term strategy:

  • The “75/150” Rule: The most efficient setup for a mid-game player is to have 75 Burned Paragon and 150+ Regular Paragon. This maximizes your production bonus before diminishing returns cripple you.
  • The Best Time to Burn: Always burn right before you reset your game. If you burn in the middle of a run, your storage caps (including Faith) will instantly drop, potentially breaking your production lines.
  • Dark Future (Year 40,000+): If you are doing a very long run, Burned Paragon becomes 4x more powerful for storage than regular Paragon. If you reach Year 40k, burning becomes your primary way to massive storage increases.

3. Other Benefits of Burned Paragon

  • Leader Bonus: Burned Paragon provides a unique boost to your Leader’s traits (e.g., if your leader is a Manager, they get even better at reducing hunting costs).
  • Karma/Cryochambers: It reduces the amount of Karma needed to build Cryochambers, which helps you carry more kittens into the next run. Burned Paragon is a permanent prestige resource in Kittens Game created by “burning” regular Paragon. While burned paragon provides smaller initial production bonuses than regular paragon, it stacks with regular paragon and becomes significantly more powerful during the late-game Dark Future (Year 40,000+).

4. Core Effects

  • Production Bonus: Burned paragon provides a global production boost that is exactly half as effective as regular paragon before reaching Year 40,000. However, because it is tracked as a separate pool, it stacks additively with regular paragon, allowing you to bypass the severe diminishing returns that regular paragon hits at high levels (starting around 150–200).
  • Storage Bonus: Each point of burned paragon increases your resource storage capacity.
    • Pre-Dark Future: +0.05% storage capacity per point.
    • During Dark Future: +0.2% storage capacity per point, making it twice as effective as regular paragon for storage in the deep endgame.
  • Leader Trait Boost: Burned paragon provides a small multiplicative boost to the effectiveness of your Leader’s Trait (e.g., Artisan crafting or Scientist research discounts).
  • Trading Bonus: When using a Merchant leader, burned paragon increases the number of Time Crystals received per trade with the Leviathans.

5. Strategic Utility and Timing

  • Early Mid-Game (400 Threshold): Many players choose to burn their first 400 paragon. This is considered an optimal “sweet spot” because 400 burned paragon provides production bonuses roughly equivalent to the peak efficiency of regular paragon (around 200) before heavy diminishing returns set in.
  • Iron Will Strategy: Burned paragon is vital for Iron Will mode because it provides essential production and storage boosts that cannot be easily acquired through normal buildings.
  • Relic Era Prep: It is recommended to have at least 200 to 400 burned paragon before focusing heavily on Relics and Antimatter to ensure your industrial base is strong enough to handle the costs.
  • Late-Game “Seed”: In the extreme late game, players aim for massive stockpiles (up to 250,000+ burned paragon) to maximize storage for the push toward 100 Chronospheres and “Positive Resets.”

6. The “Dark Future” Interaction

The primary reason to accumulate large amounts of burned paragon is to mitigate the penalties of the Dark Future, which begins at Year 40,000. During this period, regular paragon production bonuses are suppressed, but burned paragon effects are amplified. Its storage bonus quadruples (from 0.05% to 0.2%), which is critical for reaching the multi-billion Unobtainium caps required for endgame progression.

7. How to Burn

  • Burning is done via the Metaphysics tab (unlocked with Unobtainium).
  • Caution: Once paragon is burned, it cannot be turned back into regular paragon. It is generally advised to buy your desired Metaphysics upgrades (like price ratio reductions) before burning your remaining spare paragon.
  • Note: Burned paragon always carries over across resets, even if you are not using Chronospheres.

Summary Recommendation

If you are stuck at 6 Sunspires:

  1. Don’t burn right now if you are in the middle of a run; you will lose the storage you need.
  2. Wait until you are ready to reset. Just before you click “Reset,” go to the Metaphysics tab and click Burn Paragon.
  3. On your next run, you will have the Burned Paragon bonus plus the new Paragon you get from your kittens. This combined total will make reaching that 7th Golden Spire much easier.

item.title: Karma
item.description:
Karma is a permanent prestige resource in Kittens Game that is primarily used to boost kitten happiness and overall production efficiency across game resets.

Earning Karma

  • Threshold: You begin earning karma points when you reset your game with more than 35 kittens.
  • Scaling: The amount of karma gained is based on your total population at the time of reset; more kittens result in a higher karma yield.
  • Challenge Modifier: In the Anarchy challenge, kittens count double toward karma gains when you reset.

Core Effects

  • Happiness Boost: Karma’s primary mechanical benefit is providing a +1% happiness modifier per point.
  • Production Bonus: Since kitten productivity is tied to happiness, karma acts as a global production multiplier for all working kittens.
  • Pre-Space Utility: In early runs, karma is essential for mitigating the “population penalty” to happiness, which otherwise acts as a “production killer” as your village grows.
  • Late-Game Scaling: When combined with the Holy Genocide cryptotheology building, karma can contribute to “karmakittens,” which increases the paragon earned per kitten during resets.

Usage and Costs

  • Cryochambers: Karma is consumed as a resource to build Cryochambers (costing 1 karma each), which allows you to carry individual kittens over into your next run.
  • Diminishing Returns: While regular paragon production bonuses suffer from diminishing returns, the happiness bonus from karma scales linearly.

Persistence

Unlike buildings or standard resources, karma is one of the few items that always carries over when you reset your game, providing a permanent foundation for future growth. Strategic advice often suggests pushing for at least 130 kittens in early runs to ensure a healthy amount of karma and paragon for subsequent progression.

item.title: Paradox Theory
item.description:
Paradox Theory is a high-tier late-game science technology that acts as a fundamental gateway to advanced temporal mechanics and the “Shatter Engine” in Kittens Game.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Science Cost: 1,000,000 (1M)
  • Resource Requirements: 40 Time Crystals and 250 Void
  • Prerequisite: You must first research Void Space

Unlocked Upgrades and Structures

Researching Paradox Theory is required to unlock several critical late-game features:

  • Resource Retrieval (Time Tab): This is perhaps the most vital unlock; it allows you to retrieve 1% of your yearly resources (per level) whenever you shatter a Time Crystal. This is the foundation for infinite Time Crystal loops.
  • Chronocontrol (Void Space Structure): A structure that increases the duration (number of days) of a Temporal Paradox event. It also serves as the prerequisite for unlocking Chronosurge.
  • Distortion (Workshop Upgrade): This upgrade enhances the effectiveness of Chronocontrol, adding +3 days to the Temporal Paradox for every level of Chronocontrol built.
  • Void Resonator: An upgrade that allows the Order of the Void metaphysics bonus to trigger during a time skip. It also improves faith-to-worship production based on the number of resonators owned.

Strategic Importance

  • The Shatter Engine: Paradox Theory is the cornerstone of Phase 4 (Endgame) progression. By unlocking Resource Retrieval, it enables a self-sustaining cycle where shattering a Time Crystal generates enough Unobtainium to buy back more than one crystal through Leviathan trading.
  • Void Accumulation: Because it unlocks structures that extend the duration and effectiveness of Temporal Paradoxes, Paradox Theory is essential for farming the massive quantities of Void required for endgame buildings like Void Rifts.
  • Faith Scaling: Through the Void Resonator, players can continue to build their religious “Apocrypha” bonus while time skipping, ensuring that their production multipliers remain high even when bypassing thousands of years of normal game time.

item.title: Neural Networks
item.description:
In Kittens Game, the Neural Network is a high-tier Workshop upgrade that significantly enhances your village’s automation capabilities by improving the Engineer job.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Prerequisite Technology: You must first research the Artificial Intelligence science (which requires 250,000 Science and 150 Blueprints).
  • Resource Requirements:
    • Science: 200,000
    • Titanium: 7,500

Core Effects

The upgrade provides two primary benefits, one mechanical and one thematic:

  • Doubled Engineer Effectiveness: The primary mechanical benefit is that it doubles the efficiency of all Engineer kittens. Since Engineers are responsible for automating the crafting of resources (such as converting Oil to Kerosene or Iron to Plates), this upgrade effectively doubles your passive crafting rate.
  • Noosphere Learning: Thematically, the upgrade allows kittens to “learn from the noosphere”. This means kittens can learn job skills from other kittens employed in different roles, facilitating faster skill acquisition across your population.

Strategic Importance

The Neural Network is a critical component of the late-game industrial engine. By doubling the effectiveness of your Engineers, it allows your civilization to handle much higher resource throughput without hitting storage caps, which is essential for maintaining the production of advanced materials like Eludium or Kerosene while idling. It is often purchased alongside other AI-related upgrades like Machine Learning and AI Engineers to maximize the utility of your technical workforce.

item.title: Factory Logistics
item.description:
Factory Logistics is a late-game Workshop upgrade that enhances the efficiency of your industrial infrastructure, specifically focusing on boosting the bonuses provided by Factories.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Prerequisite Technology: You must first research Electronics, which is unlocked via Mechanization.
  • Resource Requirements:
    • Science: 100,000
    • Gears: 250
    • Titanium: 2,000

Core Effects and Mechanics

The primary function of Factory Logistics is to increase the global crafting effectiveness bonus provided by each Factory building:

  • Base Factory Bonus: Standard Factories provide a +5% crafting bonus.
  • Upgrade Bonus: Researching Factory Logistics increases this bonus by +1%, bringing the total crafting bonus per Factory to 6%.
  • Multiplicative Impact: Because crafting bonuses stack multiplicatively across different resource tiers (e.g., Wood to Beams to Scaffolds), even a small 1% increase per Factory can lead to massive efficiency gains once dozens of Factories are constructed.

Strategic Synergies

Factory Logistics is a critical component of the late-game “Space Manufacturing” engine:
item.content:encoded:
Factory Logistics is a late-game Workshop upgrade that enhances the efficiency of your industrial infrastructure, specifically focusing on boosting the bonuses provided by Factories.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Prerequisite Technology: You must first research Electronics, which is unlocked via Mechanization.
  • Resource Requirements:
    • Science: 100,000
    • Gears: 250
    • Titanium: 2,000

Core Effects and Mechanics

  • Multiplicative Impact: Because crafting bonuses stack multiplicatively across different resource tiers (e.g., Wood to Beams to Scaffolds), even a small 1% increase per Factory can lead to massive efficiency gains once dozens of Factories are constructed.

Strategic Synergies

Factory Logistics is a critical component of the late-game “Space Manufacturing” engine:

  • Space Manufacturing Synergy: When combined with the Space Manufacturing upgrade, Factories provide a bonus to all space structures based on their crafting ratio.
  • Space Bonus Scaling: Without this upgrade, Factories contribute a 3.75% space production bonus; with Factory Logistics active, this contribution increases to 4.5% per Factory.
  • Unobtainium Production: This upgrade is essential for maximizing Unobtainium output, as it significantly scales the effectiveness of Space Elevators and Orbital Arrays.
  • Late-Game Farming: It is listed as a mandatory requirement for high-efficiency Time Crystal farming and establishing “positive resets” in the deep endgame.

By improving the efficiency of resource conversion and space production, Factory Logistics helps clear the significant resource bottlenecks that define the transition into the Relic and Chronosphere eras.

item.title: Sun Forge
item.description:
The Sunforge is a late-game space structure located on the star Helios that provides a global multiplier to your civilization’s metal storage capacity.

Acquisition and Building Requirements

  • Mission Unlock: You must first complete the Helios Mission, which costs 3,000 starcharts, 15,000 titanium, 250,000 science, and 1,250 kerosene.
  • Construction Costs: Building a Sunforge requires the following resources:
    • Science: 100,000
    • Relic: 1
    • Kerosene: 1,250
    • Antimatter: 250
  • Price Ratio: 1.12.

Core Effects

The Sunforge provides a +1% bonus to the storage capacity of all base metals. This storage boost specifically applies to:
item.content:encoded:
The Sunforge is a late-game space structure located on the star Helios that provides a global multiplier to your civilization’s metal storage capacity.

Acquisition and Building Requirements

  • Mission Unlock: You must first complete the Helios Mission, which costs 3,000 starcharts, 15,000 titanium, 250,000 science, and 1,250 kerosene.
  • Construction Costs: Building a Sunforge requires the following resources:
    • Science: 100,000
    • Relic: 1
    • Kerosene: 1,250
    • Antimatter: 250
  • Price Ratio: 1.12.

Core Effects

The Sunforge provides a +1% bonus to the storage capacity of all base metals. This storage boost specifically applies to:

  • Iron
  • Titanium
  • Gold
  • Uranium
  • Unobtainium

Strategic Importance

  • Late-Game Scaling: While a 1% bonus per building may seem small, Sunforges are critical in the late game for breaking through resource caps that terrestrial buildings (like Barns or Warehouses) can no longer effectively expand.
  • Unobtainium Benchmarks: Sunforges are a key component in reaching the massive 8.14 billion unobtainium capacity required to build 100 Chronospheres. This capacity is necessary to establish a “positive reset” loop, where you start each new run with more resources than you spent on Chronospheres in the previous one.
  • Endgame Estimates: Advanced strategy guides suggest that during a deep endgame run, players should aim for approximately 100 Sunforges to provide a massive cumulative boost to their storage limits.

item.title: Engineering
item.description:
In Kittens Game, Engineering is an early-game science technology that acts as a gateway to both physical infrastructure and societal governance.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Science Cost: 1,500 Science.
  • Prerequisite: You must first research Construction.
  • Leads to: Researching Engineering is the mandatory prerequisite for Writing.

Unlocked Features

Researching Engineering provides two primary unlocks:

  • Aqueducts: A building that costs 75 Minerals (with a 1.12 price ratio) and increases catnip production by 3%. This bonus applies to both Catnip Fields and Farmer kittens. Strategically, Aqueducts are often more cost-effective than building additional Catnip Fields once the fields’ prices have escalated.
  • Policies: Engineering unlocks the Policy system, allowing you to officially sponsor systems of government, foreign relations, philosophy, and environmental management.

Strategic Importance

Engineering marks a transition from simple resource gathering to more complex management:
item.content:encoded:
In Kittens Game, Engineering is an early-game science technology that acts as a gateway to both physical infrastructure and societal governance.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Science Cost: 1,500 Science.
  • Prerequisite: You must first research Construction.
  • Leads to: Researching Engineering is the mandatory prerequisite for Writing.

Unlocked Features

Researching Engineering provides two primary unlocks:

  • Aqueducts: A building that costs 75 Minerals (with a 1.12 price ratio) and increases catnip production by 3%. This bonus applies to both Catnip Fields and Farmer kittens. Strategically, Aqueducts are often more cost-effective than building additional Catnip Fields once the fields’ prices have escalated.
  • Policies: Engineering unlocks the Policy system, allowing you to officially sponsor systems of government, foreign relations, philosophy, and environmental management.

Strategic Importance

Engineering marks a transition from simple resource gathering to more complex management:

  • Food Stability: Along with Agriculture, Engineering is vital for establishing a food surplus that can withstand “Cold Winters”.
  • Societal Direction: The policy system unlocked here allows for early-game optimization. For example, you can choose the Clear Cutting or Strip Mining policies to boost wood or mineral production by 30% at the cost of some happiness and increased pollution.
  • Path to Culture: Because it is required for Writing, Engineering is an essential step toward unlocking Amphitheatres, which generate the Culture needed for advanced mid-game research like Theology.

Naming Note and Potential Confusion

It is important to distinguish the Engineering technology from other similarly named mechanics:

  • Metaphysics: The “Enlightenment” metaphysics upgrade (which reduces all price ratios by 1%) was formerly named Engineering.
  • Engineer (Job): The Engineer kitten profession is not unlocked by this technology; it is unlocked much later via Mechanization.
  • Artisan (Trait): The Artisan kitten trait was also formerly known as the “Engineer” trait before being renamed to avoid confusion with the automation job.

item.title: Flux Condensator
item.description:
The Flux Condensator is a high-tier Workshop upgrade for the Chronosphere mega-structure that enables the preservation of crafted resources during a game reset.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Prerequisite Technology: It is unlocked by researching Chronophysics, which requires 250,000 Science and 5 Time Crystals.
  • Upgrade Cost: Purchasing the upgrade costs 250 Alloy, 5,000 Unobtainium, and 5 Time Crystals.
  • Persistence: The Flux Condensator upgrade does not carry over across resets; it must be repurchased in every run where you intend to use its effects.

Core Effects and Mechanics

While the Chronosphere normally only preserves a percentage of non-crafted resources, the Flux Condensator extends this ability to include complex materials.
item.content:encoded:
The Flux Condensator is a high-tier Workshop upgrade for the Chronosphere mega-structure that enables the preservation of crafted resources during a game reset.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Prerequisite Technology: It is unlocked by researching Chronophysics, which requires 250,000 Science and 5 Time Crystals.
  • Upgrade Cost: Purchasing the upgrade costs 250 Alloy, 5,000 Unobtainium, and 5 Time Crystals.
  • Persistence: The Flux Condensator upgrade does not carry over across resets; it must be repurchased in every run where you intend to use its effects.

Core Effects and Mechanics

While the Chronosphere normally only preserves a percentage of non-crafted resources, the Flux Condensator extends this ability to include complex materials.

  • Preservation Formula: The amount of each crafted resource preserved is determined by the number of Chronospheres built and the amount held at reset: $1.5 {number of Chronospheres} \sqrt{{resource amount}}$**.
  • Resources Affected: This includes critical materials such as Steel, Alloy, Concrete, Eludium, Gear, Scaffold, Ship, Tanker, Kerosene, Parchment, Manuscript, Compendium, Blueprint, Thorium, and Megalith.
  • Diminishing Returns: Because the formula uses a square root function, the efficiency of resource carryover decreases the more of a resource you have.

Strategic Importance

The Flux Condensator is considered a game-changing upgrade for mid-to-late-game progression loops:

  • Science Storage Carryover: Its most significant benefit is the preservation of Compendiums. Since Compendiums increase maximum science storage, bringing thousands into a new run allows players to hit late-game science caps and unlock advanced technologies in the very first years of a new run.
  • Early Industrial Stability: Bringing over Ships and Scaffolds significantly speeds up early titanium collection and harbour construction, eliminating the early-game trading bottlenecks.
  • Endgame “Positive Resets”: In the deep endgame, the Flux Condensator is mandatory for “positive resets,” where the goal is to start each run with a net profit of materials compared to the previous one.
  • Resource Management: Players are advised to stockpile crafted resources before resetting with this upgrade to maximize the square-root-based yield. For example, having a high crafting ratio before reset is more efficient than waiting to craft resources in the next run.

item.title: Engineer
item.description:
In Kittens Game, the Engineer is a specialised kitten job focused on automating the crafting process in the Workshop.

Unlocking and Assignment

  • Prerequisite: To assign kittens as Engineers, you must first research the Mechanization technology (costs 115k Science and 45 Blueprints).
  • Assignment: Once unlocked, kittens can be assigned to the Engineer job in the Village tab.
  • Note on Traits: The Artisan trait was previously named “Engineer” but was changed to avoid confusion with this job role. While the Artisan trait provides a global bonus to crafting efficiency, the Engineer job performs the physical automation of crafts.

Core Functionality: Automation

The primary role of Engineers is to automate the conversion of resources that would otherwise hit their storage caps.
item.content:encoded:
In Kittens Game, the Engineer is a specialised kitten job focused on automating the crafting process in the Workshop.

Unlocking and Assignment

  • Prerequisite: To assign kittens as Engineers, you must first research the Mechanization technology (costs 115k Science and 45 Blueprints).
  • Assignment: Once unlocked, kittens can be assigned to the Engineer job in the Village tab.
  • Note on Traits: The Artisan trait was previously named “Engineer” but was changed to avoid confusion with this job role. While the Artisan trait provides a global bonus to crafting efficiency, the Engineer job performs the physical automation of crafts.

Core Functionality: Automation

The primary role of Engineers is to automate the conversion of resources that would otherwise hit their storage caps.

  • Crafting Points: Each assigned kitten provides “Engineer points” to the Workshop’s automated crafting pool.
  • Resource Management: They are particularly vital for managing resources like Oil, which they can automatically convert into Kerosene to prevent production from halting due to full storage.
  • Late-Game Utility: As the game progresses and manual crafting becomes tedious, players typically shift a larger portion of their population into Engineer and Priest roles to handle massive resource throughput.

Upgrades and Effectiveness

The efficiency of Engineers—often measured in “know-how”—can be significantly enhanced through various Workshop upgrades:

  • Know-How Progression: Multiple upgrades increase the effectiveness of different “classes” of Engineers:
    • Factory Optimization: Increases know-how for Class 1 (10) and Class 2 (2).
    • Space Engineers: Increases know-how for Class 1 (10), Class 2 (5), and adds Class 3 and 4 (2 each).
    • AI Engineers: Further expands know-how across classes 1 through 5.
    • Factory Robotics: Provides another boost to Classes 1, 2, and 3.
  • Neural Network: This critical upgrade doubles Engineer effectiveness and allows kittens to learn skills from the “noosphere”.
  • Antimatter Fission: Specifically makes Engineers 25% more effective at producing Eludium.

Temporal Capabilities

In the late game, Engineers gain the ability to function outside of normal time:

  • Chronoengineers: This upgrade allows Engineers to continue crafting during time skips (combusting Time Crystals).
  • Resource Retrieval Synergy: When working during a time skip, their crafting is based on the Resource Retrieval level, ensuring they can produce materials even as years are bypassed.

item.title: Dark Brew
item.description:
Dark Brew is a specific Zebra Upgrade available in the Workshop tab.

Acquisition and Costs

To purchase this upgrade, you must meet the following requirements:

  • Prerequisite Building: You must have constructed at least one Brewery.
  • Resource Costs:
    • Bloodstone: 1
    • Parchment: 3,000
    • Science: 100

Effects

The primary function of Dark Brew is to link Festivals with your zebra population growth. When this upgrade is active, holding a festival provides a boost to the chance of zebra arrival. Specifically, the “festival arrival rate” (the speed at which new kittens normally arrive during a festival) also functions as a multiplier for the zebra arrival chance.

Strategic Context

This upgrade is part of the late-game zebra progression system, which is particularly relevant in Iron Will mode where zebras serve as your primary labor force. Because Bloodstones are rare resources (obtained from hunting with at least 10 zebras or crafted from Time Crystals and Relics), Dark Brew represents an advanced stage of zebra accumulation. By using the Brewery to run festivals, players can significantly accelerate the rate at which they reach higher zebra counts, which in turn provides more Catpower and better hunting yields.
