item.title: Civil Service
item.description:
Civil Service is an early-game science technology that focuses on village management and kitten specialization. It is essential for transitioning from a basic settlement to a more organized and efficient civilization.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Science Cost: 1,500 Science.
  • Prerequisites: You must first research Animal Husbandry.
  • Unlocks: Researching Civil Service provides the path to Currency and enables the Census feature.

The Census Feature

Unlocking Civil Service enables the Census section within the Village tab, providing detailed information about your population.
item.content:encoded:
Civil Service is an early-game science technology that focuses on village management and kitten specialization. It is essential for transitioning from a basic settlement to a more organized and efficient civilization.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Science Cost: 1,500 Science.
  • Prerequisites: You must first research Animal Husbandry.
  • Unlocks: Researching Civil Service provides the path to Currency and enables the Census feature.

The Census Feature

Unlocking Civil Service enables the Census section within the Village tab, providing detailed information about your population.

  • Kitten Identity: It reveals the names of your individual kittens (e.g., Lily, Oscar, Tails, Shadow).
  • Performance Monitoring: You can view how ably each kitten performs in their respective jobs.
  • Skill Levels: The Census tracks job experience, showing skill tiers such as Dabbling, Novice, Competent, and Master. These tiers provide multiplicative productivity bonuses for that specific job, ranging from 1% at Novice to 18.75% at Master.

Leader System

Civil Service grants the ability to assign a single kitten as the Leader of the village.

  • Assigning a Leader: A kitten can be made Leader by clicking the star icon next to their name in the Census.
  • Leader Traits: Each kitten is born with a random trait (e.g., Scientist, Artisan, Merchant) that provides a specific bonus only when they are assigned as the leader. For example, an Artisan leader increases your global craftRatio by +0.05, while a Scientist reduces the science cost of technologies by 5%.
  • Promotion and Rank: Leaders can be Promoted using gold and accumulated experience (Exp). Higher ranks significantly boost the kitten’s job production, and if you research the Republic policy, the leader’s rank provides a small production bonus to all other kittens in the village.

Strategic Importance

In the early game, Civil Service is primarily used to identify and assign kittens to jobs they are most skilled in, ensuring maximum resource yield. By promoting a leader who is highly skilled in a bottlenecked resource (like Woodcutting), you can effectively gain the equivalent of several extra kittens gathering that resource. Additionally, beelining this technology is required to unlock Currency, which is vital for starting international trade.

item.title: Calendar
item.description:
Calendar is the foundational science technology in Kittens Game, costing 30 Science to research. It is the primary prerequisite for the entire technology tree, unlocking Agriculture and the Time tab.

Functionality

Once researched, the Calendar provides essential information about the passage of time in your village:

  • Yearly Progression: It allows you to see the current day and season.
  • Village Age: It displays the total number of years your civilization has existed.
  • Time Tab: It unlocks the dedicated Time tab, where late-game temporal mechanics (like Redshift and Chronoforges) are managed.

The Time System

The game operates on a tick system, where one “tick” lasts 200 milliseconds. The units of time are defined as follows:
item.content:encoded:
Calendar is the foundational science technology in Kittens Game, costing 30 Science to research. It is the primary prerequisite for the entire technology tree, unlocking Agriculture and the Time tab.

Functionality

Once researched, the Calendar provides essential information about the passage of time in your village:

  • Yearly Progression: It allows you to see the current day and season.
  • Village Age: It displays the total number of years your civilization has existed.
  • Time Tab: It unlocks the dedicated Time tab, where late-game temporal mechanics (like Redshift and Chronoforges) are managed.

The Time System

The game operates on a tick system, where one “tick” lasts 200 milliseconds. The units of time are defined as follows:

  • Day: 10 ticks (2 seconds of real-time).
  • Season: 100 days (3 minutes and 20 seconds).
  • Year: 400 days (13 minutes and 20 seconds).
  • Cycle: 5 years (1 hour, 6 minutes, and 40 seconds).
  • Millennium: 1,000 years (approximately 9 days and 6 hours).

Seasonal and Weather Mechanics

The calendar year is divided into four seasons—Spring, Summer, Autumn, and Winter—which directly affect catnip production.

  • Catnip Production: Fields receive a +50% boost in Spring and a -75% penalty in Winter.
  • Weather Modifiers: Starting at Year 4, seasons have a 35% chance to be “warm” (improving catnip yields) or “cold” (decreasing them further). In a Cold Winter, catnip production can drop by 90%.

Cycles and Late-Game Time

The game features ten five-year cycles named after space destinations: Charon, Umbra, Yarn, Helios, Cath, Redmoon, Dune, Piscine, Terminus (T-minus), and Kairo.

  • Looping: The full sequence of cycles repeats every 50 years.
  • Modifiers: With late-game Metaphysics (Numerology and Numeromancy), these cycles provide various production boosts or penalties to space structures and festivals.
  • Temporal Limits: In the 1000 Years challenge, the calendar stops advancing normally at year 500, requiring players to “shatter” Time Crystals to progress the year counter further.

item.title: Blackchain
item.description:
Blackchain is an extreme late-game science technology that serves as the gateway to the speculative cryptocurrency market within Kittens Game.

Costs and Prerequisites

To unlock Blackchain, you must first research Quantum Cryptography. The technology is exceptionally expensive, requiring:

  • Science: 5,000,000 (5M)
  • Relics: 4,096

Core Functionality

The primary effect of researching Blackchain is that it unlocks Blackcoin, a unique and uncommon resource. Blackcoin functions as a speculative cryptocurrency that is bought and sold from the Leviathans in exchange for relics. Its price fluctuates over time, and these price stats are preserved even when you reset the game.

Blackchain is an extreme late-game science technology that serves as the gateway to the speculative cryptocurrency market within Kittens Game.

Costs and Prerequisites

To unlock Blackchain, you must first research Quantum Cryptography. The technology is exceptionally expensive, requiring:

  • Science: 5,000,000 (5M)
  • Relics: 4,096

Core Functionality

The primary effect of researching Blackchain is that it unlocks Blackcoin, a unique and uncommon resource. Blackcoin functions as a speculative cryptocurrency that is bought and sold from the Leviathans in exchange for relics. Its price fluctuates over time, and these price stats are preserved even when you reset the game.

Associated Upgrades

Researching Blackchain is also a mandatory prerequisite for the Invisible Black Hand Workshop upgrade.

  • Cost: 128 Time Crystals, 64 Blackcoin, 32 Void, and 4,096 Temporal Flux.
  • Effect: This upgrade grants you the ability to force a blackcoin market crash at the cost of time crystals, providing a level of control over the speculative market.

Because of the massive relic requirement, Blackchain is typically one of the final scientific milestones achieved in the “Relic Era” or during high-paragon endgame runs.

item.title: Chemistry
item.description:
Chemistry is a pivotal mid-game science technology that initiates the “Alloy Era”, providing the necessary foundation for advanced industrialisation and early space exploration.

Costs and Prerequisites

To research Chemistry, you must first unlock Physics. The technology itself requires the following resources:

  • Science: 60,000
  • Compendium: 50

Unlocked Buildings and Resources

Chemistry unlocks the ability to produce Alloy, a high-end craftable material made from Steel and Titanium. It also enables the construction of two critical industrial buildings:
item.content:encoded:
Chemistry is a pivotal mid-game science technology that initiates the “Alloy Era”, providing the necessary foundation for advanced industrialisation and early space exploration.

Costs and Prerequisites

To research Chemistry, you must first unlock Physics. The technology itself requires the following resources:

  • Science: 60,000
  • Compendium: 50

Unlocked Buildings and Resources

Chemistry unlocks the ability to produce Alloy, a high-end craftable material made from Steel and Titanium. It also enables the construction of two critical industrial buildings:

  • Oil Well: Your primary source of terrestrial oil production, providing +0.02 oil per tick.
  • Calciner: A complex industrial structure that consumes minerals and oil to produce iron and small amounts of Titanium. While slow, Calciners provide a steady domestic alternative to trading with Zebras for Titanium.

Workshop Upgrades

Researching Chemistry makes several high-impact Alloy-tier upgrades available in the Workshop:

  • Alloy Barns: Increases the storage capacity of Barns, Warehouses, and Harbours for wood, minerals, and iron by 100%.
  • Alloy Warehouses: Boosts the storage of wood, minerals, coal, iron, gold, and titanium in your facilities by 45%.
  • Alloy Axe: Makes Woodcutters 50% more effective.
  • Alloy Armour: Provides a +0.5 hunting bonus, making each hunt yield roughly 40–50% more furs and ivory.

Strategic Importance

  • Breaking Resource Caps: The Alloy-tier storage upgrades are essential for reaching the high science and resource limits required for the Concrete Era and Mechanization.
  • Transition to Space: Chemistry is a mandatory step in the technology tree leading toward Electricity, Biology, and eventually the Rocketry needed for space missions.
  • Titanium Management: Strategic guides recommend building several Calciners immediately after researching Chemistry to begin accumulating the Titanium needed for advanced Workshop upgrades before domestic production becomes more efficient through later Metallurgy upgrades.
  • Village Progression: Players typically aim to acquire all Alloy buildings when they have approximately 90–100 kittens, using the expanded storage to push toward a population of 130+ for an efficient first reset.

item.title: Currency
item.description:
In Kittens Game, “currency” can refer to the Currency technology, the primary economic resource Gold, or the prestige-based currencies used for long-term progression.

The Currency Technology

Currency is a mid-early game science technology that costs 2,200 Science and is unlocked after researching Civil Service. Researching it provides the following:

  • Building Unlock: Enables the construction of Tradeposts, which reduce luxury resource demand and improve trading effectiveness.
  • Workshop Upgrade: Unlocks Gold Ore, which allows your Smelters to produce a small amount of gold (0.001 per tick) while they are active.

Gold (Primary Economic Currency)

Gold is the standard currency used for domestic improvements and international relations.
item.content:encoded:
In Kittens Game, “currency” can refer to the Currency technology, the primary economic resource Gold, or the prestige-based currencies used for long-term progression.

The Currency Technology

Currency is a mid-early game science technology that costs 2,200 Science and is unlocked after researching Civil Service. Researching it provides the following:

  • Building Unlock: Enables the construction of Tradeposts, which reduce luxury resource demand and improve trading effectiveness.
  • Workshop Upgrade: Unlocks Gold Ore, which allows your Smelters to produce a small amount of gold (0.001 per tick) while they are active.

Gold (Primary Economic Currency)

Gold is the standard currency used for domestic improvements and international relations.

  • Production: Initially generated by Smelters with the Gold Ore upgrade. Later, Geologist kittens can produce it once the Geodesy workshop upgrade is purchased. In Iron Will mode, hunting also has a 25% chance of yielding gold.
  • Usage:
    • Trading: Used as a cost for discovering new civilizations and executing trades with certain races.
    • Promotion: Required to Promote kittens, which increases their rank and production bonuses.
    • Construction: A mandatory material for building Temples, Tradeposts, and Mints.
    • Religion: Essential for purchasing high-tier Order of the Sun upgrades and executing faith resets via Apocrypha.

Prestige Currencies (Resets)

These are earned by resetting the game and provide permanent, stacking benefits for future runs.

  • Karma: Earned if you have more than 35 kittens at reset. It primarily increases Kitten Happiness, which provides a global production bonus.
  • Paragon: Earned if you have more than 70 kittens at reset (1 point for every kitten over 70). It provides a global production bonus and increases resource storage caps.
  • Burned Paragon: Regular Paragon can be “burned” to provide a smaller but separate production boost that is highly effective during the Dark Future (Year 40,000+).

Special and Late-Game Currencies

  • Catpower: While technically a resource, it functions as a currency for Sending Explorers (1,000 Catpower) and initiating Hunts (100 Catpower).
  • Blackcoin: A speculative cryptocurrency bought and sold from Leviathans in exchange for relics. Its price fluctuates over time.
  • Time Crystals: A rare currency used to purchase advanced temporal technologies like Chronospheres and to skip years via time shattering.

item.title: Temporal Paradox
item.description:
In Kittens Game, a Temporal Paradox is a random event tied to the late-game Chronosphere mega structure that serves as the primary method for generating Void.

Mechanics and Triggering

  • Source: Temporal paradoxes occur occasionally once you have built one or more Chronospheres.
  • Output: During a paradox, you gain Void, a unique resource required for advanced endgame technologies and structures.
  • Visual Indicator: The paradox is a timed event that lasts for a specific number of game days.

Paradox Trigger Check

On every daily tick (or skipped day during time combustion), the game evaluates whether a paradox occurs: {Paradox Chance per Day} = {Chronospheres}/10,000
item.content:encoded:
In Kittens Game, a Temporal Paradox is a random event tied to the late-game Chronosphere mega structure that serves as the primary method for generating Void.

Mechanics and Triggering

  • Source: Temporal paradoxes occur occasionally once you have built one or more Chronospheres.
  • Output: During a paradox, you gain Void, a unique resource required for advanced endgame technologies and structures.
  • Visual Indicator: The paradox is a timed event that lasts for a specific number of game days.

Paradox Trigger Check

On every daily tick (or skipped day during time combustion), the game evaluates whether a paradox occurs: {Paradox Chance per Day} = {Chronospheres}/10,000

  • Threshold: If {Chronospheres} = 0$, chance is 0.
  • With 10 Chronospheres, the daily chance is $0.1%$ per calendar day.
  • With 50 Chronospheres, the daily chance is $0.5%$ per calendar day.

Base Chronosphere Void Payout

When a paradox triggers, the Chronospheres generate a base quantity of Void:

{Base Void} = 1 + ({Chronospheres} - 1)/2

  • 1 Chronosphere: $1 + \lfloor 0 \rfloor = 1\text{ Void}$
  • 5 Chronospheres: $1 + \lfloor 2 \rfloor = 3\text{ Void}$
  • 10 Chronospheres: $1 + \lfloor 4.5 \rfloor = 5\text{ Void}$
  • 25 Chronospheres: $1 + \lfloor 12 \rfloor = 13\text{ Void}$

See also Order of the Void

Benefits of Paradoxes

  • Happiness Boost: Each unit of Void obtained from these events provides a +10% happiness modifier, which enhances your kittens’ overall production efficiency.
  • Resource Carryover: Void is a non-crafted resource that can be preserved across resets if you have Chronospheres.

Associated Upgrades

Several structures and Workshop upgrades specifically modify the efficiency and duration of a Temporal Paradox:

  • Void Hoover: A structure that increases the maximum amount of Void you can receive during a single paradox day.
  • Chronocontrol: A Time-tab structure that increases the duration (number of days) of the paradox event.
  • Distortion: A late-game Workshop upgrade (unlocked by Paradox Theory) that improves the effectiveness of Chronocontrol, adding +3 days to the Temporal Paradox per level of Chronocontrol built.
  • Void Resonator: Another upgrade unlocked by Paradox Theory that further enhances Void production and interacts with the Order of the Void metaphysics upgrade.

Strategically, players often focus on maximizing the frequency and yield of these paradoxes in Phase 4 (Endgame) to accumulate the millions of Void units required for high-tier upgrades like Void Rifts, which provide permanent global storage bonuses.

item.title: Alloy Warehouses
item.description:
Alloy Warehouses is a mid-to-late-game Workshop upgrade that significantly boosts the storage capacity of your village’s infrastructure.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Prerequisite Science: You must first research Chemistry, which requires Physics and Navigation.
  • Resource Cost:
    • Science: 90,000
    • Titanium: 750
    • Alloy: 50

Core Effects

The upgrade provides a multiplicative storage bonus to several buildings:

  • Storage Increase: It increases the maximum amount of wood, minerals, coal, iron, gold, and titanium stored in Warehouses, Barns, Harbours, and Mints by 45%.
  • Gold Storage: Specifically for Mints, this upgrade is a primary way to scale your maximum gold capacity, which is vital for late-game trading and religion.

Strategic Utility

  • The “Alloy Era”: Acquiring Alloy Warehouses and Alloy Barns is a major milestone often reached when a player has between 90 and 100 kittens.
  • Titanium Management: Because this upgrade requires 750 Titanium, players must prioritize building a large fleet of Trade Ships and Observatories to ensure reliable Titanium yields from trading with Zebras.
  • Progression Bottleneck: Increasing your storage caps with Alloy-tier upgrades is often a mandatory step to afford the science costs of the Concrete era, specifically the 125,000 science limit required for Concrete Huts.
  • Automation Synergy: While Warehouses themselves do not initially store catnip, if you have researched Silos, they gain catnip storage. However, unlike “Barn” upgrades, the Alloy Warehouses upgrade does not contribute to the additional 25% catnip storage bonus.

By expanding resource caps, Alloy Warehouses allow you to accumulate the massive quantities of materials needed for advanced industrial structures like Factories, Reactors, and early space missions.

  • Gold Storage: Specifically for Mints, this upgrade is a primary way to scale your maximum gold capacity, which is vital for late-game trading and religion.

Strategic Utility

  • The “Alloy Era”: Acquiring Alloy Warehouses and Alloy Barns is a major milestone often reached when a player has between 90 and 100 kittens.
  • Titanium Management: Because this upgrade requires 750 Titanium, players must prioritize building a large fleet of Trade Ships and Observatories to ensure reliable Titanium yields from trading with Zebras.
  • Progression Bottleneck: Increasing your storage caps with Alloy-tier upgrades is often a mandatory step to afford the science costs of the Concrete era, specifically the 125,000 science limit required for Concrete Huts.
  • Automation Synergy: While Warehouses themselves do not initially store catnip, if you have researched Silos, they gain catnip storage. However, unlike “Barn” upgrades, the Alloy Warehouses upgrade does not contribute to the additional 25% catnip storage bonus.

By expanding resource caps, Alloy Warehouses allow you to accumulate the massive quantities of materials needed for advanced industrial structures like Factories, Reactors, and early space missions.

item.title: Advanced AM Reactors
item.description:
Advanced Antimatter Reactors (Advanced AM Reactors) is a high-tier Workshop upgrade that significantly expands your civilization’s maximum science capacity by enhancing space-based research structures.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Prerequisite Upgrade: You must first purchase Antimatter Reactors.
  • Resource Costs: 70 Eludium and 1,750 Antimatter.

Core Effects

The primary function of this upgrade is to boost the effectiveness of two specific space structures:

  • Science Cap Increase: It raises the maximum science bonus provided by Research Vessels and Space Beacons to 150%.
  • Relative Efficiency: This represents approximately a 77% increase in effectiveness over the standard Antimatter Reactors upgrade.

Strategic Utility

  • Breaking Science Bottlenecks: This upgrade is a critical component of the late-game “Antimatter Phase”. It is often necessary to reach the massive science caps required for endgame technologies, such as Quantum Cryptography (1.25M Science).
  • Endgame Progression: By maximizing the science storage of Space Beacons, players can better support Relic Station operations and general research velocity.
  • Upgrade Path: Advanced AM Reactors is the penultimate tier of science-boosting reactor upgrades, eventually being succeeded by Void Reactors, which increase the science bonus from these structures to 400%.

item.title: Piscine Cycle
item.description:
The Piscine cycle is the eighth in the sequence of ten five-year cycles in the Kittens Game time system. It is represented by the glyph ⎈ and provides specific modifiers to space production and festivals once late-game Metaphysics are researched.

Cycle Mechanics and Effects

The modifiers for the Piscine cycle are active only after researching specific Metaphysics technologies:

  • Numerology Effects: Researching Numerology activates production modifiers for space-based structures, acting as a “boom” period for starcharts but a “fallow” period for advanced catnip production:
    • Research Vessels: Starchart production is increased by +50%.
    • Hydroponics: Catnip production is reduced by -50%.
  • Numeromancy (Festival) Effects: If a festival is held during this cycle and Numeromancy is researched, the village receives a x2 multiplier (doubled income) for Science.

Relationship to Planet Piscine

The cycle is named after the planet Piscine, described as a gigantic aquatic planet with an acid body and a methane atmosphere.

Relationship to Planet Piscine

The cycle is named after the planet Piscine, described as a gigantic aquatic planet with an acid body and a methane atmosphere.

  • Piscine Mission: Reaching the planet requires 1,500 starcharts, 9,000 titanium, 200,000 science, and 250 kerosene.
  • Research Vessel: Completing the mission unlocks the ability to build Research Vessels. Each vessel provides +10,000 science storage and produces 0.05 starcharts per second.

Strategic Importance

The Piscine cycle and the associated planet are critical for mid-to-late game progression:

  • Solving Starchart Bottlenecks: Research Vessels are considered the earliest “best” way to generate starcharts. Because these vessels receive a 50% production boost during the Piscine cycle, it is the most efficient window to accumulate the starcharts needed for high-tier missions.
  • Science Farming: The 2x festival bonus to science income makes this cycle an ideal time to stockpile science for expensive late-game technologies or for crafting large quantities of Compendiums and Blueprints.
  • Food Warning: Players must be cautious of the -50% penalty to Hydroponics catnip production. While this rarely causes starvation in the late game due to massive terrestrial production bonuses, it can reduce the surplus available for wood refinement.

item.title: Helios Cycle
item.description:
The Helios cycle is the fourth in the sequence of ten five-year cycles within the Kittens Game time system. Represented by the glyph ⌒, it repeats every 50 years, beginning at Year 15 of every millennium (e.g., Years 15–19, 65–69, etc.).

Cycle Mechanics and Effects

The modifiers for the Helios cycle are only activated once specific late-game Metaphysics technologies have been researched:

  • Numerology Effects: Researching Numerology activates modifiers for energy and space storage:
    • Sunlifter: Energy output is increased by +50%.
    • Cryostations: Storage capacity is reduced by -10%.
  • Numeromancy (Festival) Effects: If a festival is active during this cycle and Numeromancy is researched, your village receives significant bonuses to religion-based resources:
    • Faith income x2 (doubled).
    • Unicorn income x1.25.

Space Exploration Context

The cycle is named after the star Helios, a G2V spectral type star at the center of the Cath solar system. Reaching it requires the Helios Mission, which is unlocked after the Dune mission and costs 3,000 starcharts, 15,000 titanium, 250,000 science, and 1,250 kerosene. Completing this mission unlocks several critical late-game structures:

Cycle Mechanics and Effects

The modifiers for the Helios cycle are only activated once specific late-game Metaphysics technologies have been researched:

  • Numerology Effects: Researching Numerology activates modifiers for energy and space storage:
    • Sunlifter: Energy output is increased by +50%.
    • Cryostations: Storage capacity is reduced by -10%.
  • Numeromancy (Festival) Effects: If a festival is active during this cycle and Numeromancy is researched, your village receives significant bonuses to religion-based resources:
    • Faith income x2 (doubled).
    • Unicorn income x1.25.

Space Exploration Context

The cycle is named after the star Helios, a G2V spectral type star at the center of the Cath solar system. Reaching it requires the Helios Mission, which is unlocked after the Dune mission and costs 3,000 starcharts, 15,000 titanium, 250,000 science, and 1,250 kerosene. Completing this mission unlocks several critical late-game structures:

  • Sunlifter: Generates Antimatter (1 per year) and high energy (30 Watts base).
  • Containment Chamber: Increases maximum antimatter storage.
  • Heatsink: Enhances the storage capacity of Containment Chambers by +2% and increases their power consumption.
  • Sunforge: Provides a +1% bonus to the storage capacity of all base metals (iron, titanium, gold, uranium, and unobtainium).

Strategic Importance

  • Energy Maximisation: Because Sunlifters receive a +50% production boost during this cycle, it is one of the best times to run energy-intensive infrastructure, such as high numbers of AI Cores or Entanglement Stations.
  • Religion Farming: The doubled faith income from festivals makes the Helios cycle an ideal window for “Praising the Sun” to maximize the Solar Revolution bonus or for pushing toward higher Transcendence Tiers.
  • Storage Penalties: Players must be cautious of the -10% penalty to Cryostation storage. Since Cryostations are one of only two buildings that provide Unobtainium storage, this cycle can temporarily lower your resource cap, which may cause you to lose surplus unobtainium if you are near your maximum capacity.
  • Antimatter Production: While some early strategy guides consider Helios missions a low priority, acquiring Sunlifters is mandatory for entering the Relic era, as they are the primary source of the antimatter needed for Relic Stations.

item.title: Kairo Cycle
item.description:
The Kairo cycle is the tenth and final five-year cycle in the Kittens Game time system. Represented by the glyph ℣, it repeats every 50 years (Years 45–49, 95–99, etc.).

Cycle Mechanics and Modifiers

The effects of the Kairo cycle are only active if you have researched specific Metaphysics technologies:

  • Numerology Effects: This technology activates several production and science modifiers for space-based structures, primarily acting as a “fallow” period for general production but a massive boom for starcharts:
    • Space Elevators: Their transferred production bonus is reduced by -50%.
    • Satellites: Starchart production and the science bonus provided to Observatories are both reduced by -25%.
    • Space Stations: Their science bonus is reduced by -25%.
    • Space Beacons: In contrast to the penalties above, their starchart production is boosted by +400%.
  • Numeromancy (Festival) Effects: If a festival is held during this cycle and Numeromancy is researched, your village receives a massive x5 multiplier to starchart income.

Relationship to Space Exploration

The cycle is tied to the Kairo Mission, which is required to reach the dwarf planet Kairo at the edge of the solar system.

Cycle Mechanics and Modifiers

The effects of the Kairo cycle are only active if you have researched specific Metaphysics technologies:

  • Numerology Effects: This technology activates several production and science modifiers for space-based structures, primarily acting as a “fallow” period for general production but a massive boom for starcharts:

    • Space Stations: Their science bonus is reduced by -25%.
    • Space Beacons: In contrast to the penalties above, their starchart production is boosted by +400%.
  • Numeromancy (Festival) Effects: If a festival is held during this cycle and Numeromancy is researched, your village receives a massive x5 multiplier to starchart income.

Relationship to Space Exploration

The cycle is tied to the Kairo Mission, which is required to reach the dwarf planet Kairo at the edge of the solar system.

  • Mission Requirements: Reaching Kairo requires 5,000 starcharts, 20,000 titanium, 300,000 science, and 7,500 kerosene.
  • Space Beacon: Once Kairo is reached, you can construct Space Beacons. These structures are the primary beneficiary of the cycle’s modifiers, providing significant starchart generation and expanded science limits.

Strategic Importance

The Kairo cycle is the ultimate window for farming starcharts in the late game. While the penalties to Space Elevators and Satellites can temporarily slow down general resource production and unobtainium gathering, the combination of the +400% Space Beacon boost and the x5 festival bonus allows players to accumulate the massive starchart reserves needed for high-tier missions like Centaurus or for building large fleets of Trade Ships.

Advanced players often use a Chronoforge to skip through less productive cycles to land in Kairo when they need to break a starchart bottleneck.

item.title: Umbra Cycle
item.description:
The Umbra cycle is the second of ten five-year cycles in the Kittens Game time system. Represented by the glyph ⍦, it begins at Year 5 of every millennium and repeats every 50 years (Years 5–9, 55–59, etc.).

Cycle Mechanics and Modifiers

The effects of the Umbra cycle are only active once specific late-game Metaphysics technologies have been researched:

  • Numerology Effects: This technology activates modifiers for space-based structures, primarily those located on the planet Dune and the Umbra black hole:
    • HR Harvester (Umbra): Energy production is increased by +50%.
    • Hydraulic Fracturer (Dune): Oil output is reduced by -25%.
    • Planet Cracker (Dune): Uranium output is reduced by -10%.
  • Numeromancy (Festival) Effects: If a festival is held during this cycle and Numeromancy is researched, your village receives a 1.5x income multiplier for four critical industrial resources: Coal, iron, titanium, and gold.

Relationship to Space Exploration

The cycle is tied to the Umbra Mission, which involves reaching a supermassive black hole at the heart of the Helios system.

The Umbra cycle is the second of ten five-year cycles in the Kittens Game time system. Represented by the glyph ⍦, it begins at Year 5 of every millennium and repeats every 50 years (Years 5–9, 55–59, etc.).

Cycle Mechanics and Modifiers

The effects of the Umbra cycle are only active once specific late-game Metaphysics technologies have been researched:

  • Numerology Effects: This technology activates modifiers for space-based structures, primarily those located on the planet Dune and the Umbra black hole:
    • HR Harvester (Umbra): Energy production is increased by +50%.
    • Hydraulic Fracturer (Dune): Oil output is reduced by -25%.
    • Planet Cracker (Dune): Uranium output is reduced by -10%.
  • Numeromancy (Festival) Effects: If a festival is held during this cycle and Numeromancy is researched, your village receives a 1.5x income multiplier for four critical industrial resources: Coal, iron, titanium, and gold.

Relationship to Space Exploration

The cycle is tied to the Umbra Mission, which involves reaching a supermassive black hole at the heart of the Helios system.

  • Mission Requirements: Reaching Umbra requires 25,000 starcharts, 500,000 science, 25,000 kerosene, and 15,000 thorium.
  • HR Harvester: Once reached, you can build HR Harvesters, which generate energy from black hole evaporation. These structures are significantly more efficient during the Umbra cycle.

Strategic Context

  • Energy Maximisation: In the deep late game, players often rely on HR Harvesters for power. Because these receive a 50% boost during the Umbra cycle, it is the most stable time for energy-heavy operations, such as running high numbers of AI Cores or Entanglement Stations.
  • Fallow Industrial Period: For players farming Unobtainium, the Umbra cycle is generally considered a “fallow” or less profitable period. Advanced players often use a Chronoforge to skip through both the Charon and Umbra cycles to reach the more lucrative Redmoon cycle, which provides massive bonuses to unobtainium production.
  • Metal Stockpiling: Despite being a “skip” year for space minerals, the 1.5x festival bonus to basic metals makes it a useful time for mid-game players to refill their stocks of titanium and gold for terrestrial building projects.

item.title: Terminus Cycle
item.description:
The Terminus cycle (often referred to in tables as the T-minus cycle) is the ninth in the sequence of ten five-year cycles within the Kittens Game time system. Represented by the glyph ⍝, it repeats every 50 years (beginning at Year 40 of a millennium, then Year 90, 140, etc.).

Cycle Mechanics and Effects

The effects of the Terminus cycle are activated only after researching specific Metaphysics technologies:

  • Numerology Effects: Researching Numerology activates production and storage modifiers for space-based structures:
    • Sunlifter: Energy output is reduced by -50%.
    • Cryostations: Storage capacity is increased by +20%.
  • Numeromancy (Festival) Effects: If a festival is held during this cycle and Numeromancy is researched, the village receive a 2x multiplier (doubled income) for Oil.

Space Exploration Context

The cycle is named after the planet Terminus, which is reached through the T-minus Mission.

Space Exploration Context

The cycle is named after the planet Terminus, which is reached through the T-minus Mission.

  • Planet Description: Terminus is described as a supermassive ice giant located at the far end of the Helios solar system.
  • Mission Requirements: Reaching it requires 2,500 starcharts, 12,000 titanium, 225,000 science, and 750 kerosene.
  • Unlocks: Completing the mission unlocks the Kairo Mission, the Cryostation structure, and access to the T-Minus planet.

Strategic Importance

In the late game, the Terminus cycle is highly valued for its bonus to Unobtainium storage capacity:

  • UO Cap Scaling: Because Cryostations are one of only two structures that provide Unobtainium storage, the +20% storage bonus from this cycle is essential for players attempting to reach the 8.14 billion Unobtainium cap needed to build 100 Chronospheres.
  • Oil Management: The 2x festival bonus makes this cycle an ideal time to stockpile oil, especially when preparing to build expensive space structures like Research Vessels.
  • Energy Warning: Players must be cautious of the -50% penalty to Sunlifter energy output during this cycle, which can lead to a sudden energy deficit and global production penalties if their grid is not sufficiently diversified.

item.title: Dune Cycle
item.description:
The Dune cycle is the seventh in the sequence of ten five-year cycles within the Kittens Game time system. Represented by the glyph ⍫, it repeats every 50 years (starting at Year 30 of a millennium, then Year 80, 130, etc.). Its primary function is to significantly boost industrial outputs related to the planet for which it is named.

Cycle Mechanics and Effects

Like other cycles, Dune’s effects are activated only after researching specific late-game Metaphysics technologies:
item.content:encoded:
The Dune cycle is the seventh in the sequence of ten five-year cycles within the Kittens Game time system. Represented by the glyph ⍫, it repeats every 50 years (starting at Year 30 of a millennium, then Year 80, 130, etc.). Its primary function is to significantly boost industrial outputs related to the planet for which it is named.

Cycle Mechanics and Effects

Like other cycles, Dune’s effects are activated only after researching specific late-game Metaphysics technologies:

  • Numerology Effects: This technology activates modifiers for space-based structures located on the planet Dune and the Umbra black hole:
    • Planet Crackers: Uranium output is increased by +10%.
    • Hydraulic Fracturers: Oil output is increased by +50%.
    • HR Harvesters: Energy production is reduced by -25%.
  • Numeromancy (Festival) Effects: If a festival is held while the Dune cycle is active and Numeromancy is researched, your village receives a 2x multiplier (doubled income) for Uranium.

Relationship to Planet Dune

The cycle is tied to the Dune Mission, which is unlocked after the Moon Mission. Reaching Dune requires 1,000 starcharts, 7,000 titanium, 175,000 science, and 75 kerosene. Once reached, you can construct the structures affected by the cycle’s modifiers:

  • Planet Cracker: The primary source of automated Uranium production.
  • Hydraulic Fracturer: Provides a high-pressure stream of Oil.
  • Spice Refinery: Refines sand into Spice, a rare resource that improves happiness.

Strategic Importance

The Dune cycle is a critical window for resource management in the late mid-game and early space eras:

  • Uranium Farming: Uranium is essential for powering Reactors, funding Nuclear Smelters (for titanium), and fueling Lunar Outposts (to produce unobtainium). The 2x festival bonus makes this cycle the most efficient time to stockpile uranium.
  • Oil Stabilization: Because Hydraulic Fracturers receive a 50% production boost during this cycle, it is an ideal time to fill your oil caps to build expensive space structures like Research Vessels or Moon Bases.
  • Energy Management: Players heavily reliant on HR Harvesters for power (common in the deep late game) must be wary of the -25% energy penalty during this cycle, which could lead to an energy deficit and global production penalties.
  • Progression Flow: In the sequence of cycles, Dune acts as a mirrored opposite to the Umbra cycle, which penalizes Dune structure output while boosting Umbra structures. Shattering Time Crystals is often used to skip Umbra and land in cycles like Dune or Redmoon to maximize resource yield.

item.title: Charon Cycle
item.description:
The Charon cycle is the first in the sequence of ten five-year cycles within the Kittens Game time system. Each cycle is associated with a specific glyph and provides production modifiers or festival bonuses once certain late-game Metaphysics technologies are researched.

Cycle Mechanics and Effects

The effects of the Charon cycle are only active after researching specific Metaphysics technologies:

  • Numerology Effects: Researching Numerology activates modifiers for space-based structures during this cycle:
    • Lunar Outposts: Unobtainium output is reduced by 10%.
    • Entanglement Stations: Gigaflops consumption is increased by 100%.
  • Numeromancy (Festival) Effects: If Numeromancy is researched, holding a festival during the Charon cycle provides a 1.5x multiplier to the income of three basic resources: Catnip, wood, and minerals.
  • Visual Indicator: The cycle is represented by the glyph ⍙. The color of this glyph changes annually to indicate progress through the five-year period: red (Year 0), orange-yellow (Year 1), green (Year 2), blue (Year 3), and violet (Year 4).

Relationship to Space Exploration

The cycle is named after the planet Charon, which is the destination of a high-tier late-game space mission.

  • Numerology Effects: Researching Numerology activates modifiers for space-based structures during this cycle:
    • Lunar Outposts: Unobtainium output is reduced by 10%.

Relationship to Space Exploration

The cycle is named after the planet Charon, which is the destination of a high-tier late-game space mission.

  • Charon Mission: Unlocked after the Umbra mission, it requires 75,000 starcharts, 750,000 science, 35,000 kerosene, and 35,000 thorium.
  • Planet Charon: Described as an incredibly dense dwarf planet at the edge of the Helios system, sometimes called “The Gates of Death”.
  • Entanglement Station: Once Charon is reached, you can construct Entanglement Stations, which generate hashes for reverse-engineering relics but consume significant energy and gigaflops. As noted above, their gigaflops consumption is doubled during the Charon cycle.

Strategic Context

In the late game, the Charon cycle is generally considered a “fallow” period for industrial production, particularly because of the penalty to unobtainium output from Lunar Outposts. Advanced strategies for farming unobtainium often involve using a Chronoforge to skip through the Charon and Umbra cycles to reach more profitable years, such as those in the Redmoon cycle. Conversely, if a player is still in the early-to-mid game and needs to build up stocks of wood or minerals, the Numeromancy festival bonus makes Charon a useful time to run festivals.

item.title: Yarn Cycle
item.description:
The Yarn cycle is one of the ten five-year cycles in the Kittens Game time system. Each cycle is associated with a specific glyph and provides various production modifiers and festival bonuses once certain late-game technologies are researched.

Cycle Mechanics and Effects

The effects of the Yarn cycle become active only after researching specific Metaphysics technologies:

  • Numerology Effect: When Numerology is researched, the Yarn cycle provides a +100% boost to catnip production from Hydroponics. Conversely, it imposes a -50% penalty to starchart production from Research Vessels.
  • Numeromancy Effect: If Numeromancy is researched, holding a festival during the Yarn cycle results in doubled culture income (x2).
  • Timing: As the third cycle in the sequence, it begins at Year 10 of a millennium and repeats every 50 years (Years 10–14, 60–64, etc.).

Space Exploration Context

The cycle is named after the planet Yarn, a Class M planet with a moderate climate and oxygen atmosphere.
item.content:encoded:

Cycle Mechanics and Effects

  • Numerology Effect: When Numerology is researched, the Yarn cycle provides a +100% boost to catnip production from Hydroponics. Conversely, it imposes a -50% penalty to starchart production from Research Vessels.

Space Exploration Context

The cycle is named after the planet Yarn, a Class M planet with a moderate climate and oxygen atmosphere.

  • Mission: The Yarn Mission is unlocked after the Helios mission and requires 7,500 starcharts, 35,000 titanium, 350,000 science, and 12,000 kerosene.
  • Planet Structures: Once reached, you can build Terraforming Stations (which increase your maximum kitten population by +1) and Hydroponics systems.
  • Hydroponics: These structures provide a +10% bonus to maximum catnip and a +2.5% boost to catnip production. During the Yarn cycle, this production bonus is significantly enhanced by the Numerology modifier.

Strategic Importance

In the extreme endgame, terraforming Yarn is a key strategy for maximizing kitten population. By building a massive number of Terraforming Stations, players can reach population levels high enough to generate “unreasonable” amounts of Paragon (up to 120,000 per RL-day) during long runs. Additionally, the cycle’s festival bonus makes it an ideal time to grind culture if you are still using it for early-to-mid-game crafts like Manuscripts or Compendiums.

item.title: Gear
item.description:
Gears are a critical mid-to-late-game craftable resource in Kittens Game, functioning as an integral component for buildings and upgrades that increase automation and industrial efficiency.

Production and Acquisition

  • Recipe: One Gear is crafted in the Workshop using 15 Steel.
  • Prerequisites: You must first research the Steel science technology to unlock Gear crafting.
  • Crafting Efficiency: Kittens with the Metallurgist trait provide a specific +0.1 bonus to your craftRatio for Gears when assigned as the village leader.

Primary Building Requirements

Gears are a mandatory material for constructing several industrial and resource-gathering structures:
item.content:encoded:
Gears are a critical mid-to-late-game craftable resource in Kittens Game, functioning as an integral component for buildings and upgrades that increase automation and industrial efficiency.

Production and Acquisition

  • Recipe: One Gear is crafted in the Workshop using 15 Steel.
  • Prerequisites: You must first research the Steel science technology to unlock Gear crafting.
  • Crafting Efficiency: Kittens with the Metallurgist trait provide a specific +0.1 bonus to your craftRatio for Gears when assigned as the village leader.

Primary Building Requirements

Gears are a mandatory material for constructing several industrial and resource-gathering structures:

  • Steamworks: Requires 20 Gears.
  • Magnetos: Requires 5 Gears.
  • Oil Wells: Requires 25 Gears.

Key Workshop Upgrades

Gears are heavily utilized in the Workshop, particularly for upgrades that automate manual tasks or enhance industrial output:

  • Printing & Pressing: Upgrades like the Printing Press (45 Gears), Offset Press (250 Gears), and Photolithography (1,250 Gears) allow Steamworks to automatically generate manuscripts.
  • Industrial Automation: Workshop Automation (25 Gears) and Advanced Automation (75 Gears) enable Steamworks to automatically craft slabs and beams.
  • Production Boosts: Upgrades such as Steel Plants (750 Gears) and Rotary Kiln (500 Gears) improve the efficiency of Calciners.
  • Environmental & Efficiency: Carbon Sequestration (125 Gears) reduces factory pollution, while Robotic Assistance (10,000 Gears) significantly reduces kitten catnip consumption.

Strategic Importance

Gears represent the transition from manual resource management to automated industrial cycles. Because Gears are crafted from Steel (which is itself a refined resource), it is highly recommended to maximize your Workshops and Factories to achieve a high craft ratio. This ensures you produce multiple Gears for the same amount of Steel, which is vital for overcoming the “Theology hurdle” and establishing a robust industrial base.

item.title: Concrete
item.description:
Concrete is a critical mid-to-late-game craftable resource used primarily for advanced infrastructure, storage expansion, and space exploration. Its acquisition marks the beginning of the “Concrete Era,” which is a major milestone in a player’s first run.

Production and Unlocking

  • Prerequisite: You must first research the Mechanization science technology (115K Science, 45 Blueprints) to unlock the ability to craft concrete and assign Engineers to automate its production.
  • Recipe: Crafting one unit of concrete requires 2,500 Slabs and 25 Steel.
  • Trait Bonus: Kittens with the Chemist trait provide a specific bonus to crafting efficiency for concrete when assigned as a leader.

Major Upgrades

Concrete is essential for several Workshop upgrades that significantly boost village capacity:
item.content:encoded:
Concrete is a critical mid-to-late-game craftable resource used primarily for advanced infrastructure, storage expansion, and space exploration. Its acquisition marks the beginning of the “Concrete Era,” which is a major milestone in a player’s first run.

Production and Unlocking

  • Prerequisite: You must first research the Mechanization science technology (115K Science, 45 Blueprints) to unlock the ability to craft concrete and assign Engineers to automate its production.
  • Recipe: Crafting one unit of concrete requires 2,500 Slabs and 25 Steel.
  • Trait Bonus: Kittens with the Chemist trait provide a specific bonus to crafting efficiency for concrete when assigned as a leader.

Major Upgrades

Concrete is essential for several Workshop upgrades that significantly boost village capacity:

  • Concrete Huts: Reduces the price ratio of Huts by 0.3 (30%), allowing for a much larger kitten population.
  • Concrete Pillars: Increases the maximum storage of wood, minerals, and iron in Barns and Warehouses by 5%, and gold/titanium by 5%.
  • Concrete Barns: Increases the storage capacity of Barns by 75%.
  • Concrete Warehouses: Increases the storage capacity of Warehouses by 35%.

Construction Uses

Many advanced buildings and space structures require concrete as a primary material:

  • Industrial/Science: Factories (15), Reactors (50), Accelerators (125), Hydro Plants (100), and Data Centers (10).
  • Space Infrastructure: Lunar Outposts (150), Moon Bases (250), and Cryostations (1,500).

Strategic Importance

The “Concrete Era” is often the target for a player’s first reset. Strategy guides generally recommend pushing until you can afford Concrete Huts and reach at least 130 kittens. This ensures you gain at least 60 Paragon, providing a substantial production and storage boost for your next run. To reach the 125K science cap required for Concrete Huts, players often research Biology to build Bio Labs.

item.title: Catnip Enrichment
item.description:
Catnip Enrichment is an early-game Workshop upgrade that significantly improves the efficiency of your wood production by doubling the effectiveness of catnip refinement.

Costs and Prerequisites

To unlock this upgrade, you must first research the Construction science technology (which costs 1,300 Science). Once researched, the upgrade becomes available in the Workshop for the following resources:

  • Science: 500
  • Catnip: 5,000

Core Effect

The primary function of Catnip Enrichment is to reduce the raw material cost of crafting wood:
item.content:encoded:
Catnip Enrichment is an early-game Workshop upgrade that significantly improves the efficiency of your wood production by doubling the effectiveness of catnip refinement.

Costs and Prerequisites

To unlock this upgrade, you must first research the Construction science technology (which costs 1,300 Science). Once researched, the upgrade becomes available in the Workshop for the following resources:

  • Science: 500
  • Catnip: 5,000

Core Effect

The primary function of Catnip Enrichment is to reduce the raw material cost of crafting wood:

  • Resource Efficiency: It reduces the cost to Refine Catnip into wood by 50%.
  • Refinement Ratio: Without this upgrade, crafting 1 unit of Wood costs 100 Catnip; with Catnip Enrichment, the cost is lowered to 50 Catnip per unit of Wood.

Strategic Utility

In the very early stages of the game, wood is your primary building block for essential structures like Huts, Barns, and Libraries. Since your initial wood income relies heavily on manually refining surplus catnip before you have a large team of Woodcutter kittens, this upgrade effectively doubles your early-game wood production velocity from refinement.

It is particularly useful during the Spring season when catnip production receives a +50% boost, allowing you to convert that massive seasonal surplus into building materials much more efficiently.

item.title: AI Engineers
item.description:
AI Engineers is a specialized late-game Workshop upgrade that provides the final set of specific “know-how” boosts to your Engineer kittens, significantly enhancing their automated crafting capabilities across all five mastery classes.

Acquisition and Costs

To access this upgrade, you must first research the Artificial Intelligence science technology (which requires 250,000 Science and 150 Blueprints). Once the technology is researched, the upgrade can be purchased in the Workshop for:

  • Science: 35,000
  • Eludium: 50
  • Antimatter: 500

Core Effects: Know-how Scaling

The upgrade improves the base “know-how” of your Engineers, which serves as a multiplier for their crafting productivity. It provides the following specific values to each class:
item.content:encoded:
AI Engineers is a specialized late-game Workshop upgrade that provides the final set of specific “know-how” boosts to your Engineer kittens, significantly enhancing their automated crafting capabilities across all five mastery classes.

Acquisition and Costs

To access this upgrade, you must first research the Artificial Intelligence science technology (which requires 250,000 Science and 150 Blueprints). Once the technology is researched, the upgrade can be purchased in the Workshop for:

  • Science: 35,000
  • Eludium: 50
  • Antimatter: 500

Core Effects: Know-how Scaling

The upgrade improves the base “know-how” of your Engineers, which serves as a multiplier for their crafting productivity. It provides the following specific values to each class:

  • Class 1: 10 know-how
  • Class 2: 5 know-how
  • Class 3: 5 know-how
  • Class 4: 2 know-how
  • Class 5: 2 know-how

Strategic Utility

  • Final Know-how Tier: This is the highest tier of specific class-based upgrades, following Factory Optimization, Factory Robotics, and Space Engineers.
  • Endgame Automation: AI Engineers is critical for managing the high resource volumes of the late game. It ensures that your Engineers can convert raw materials into refined goods (like Eludium, Alloy, and Kerosene) fast enough to prevent them from hitting storage caps, especially during time skips.
  • Synergy with Neural Network: Researching AI Engineers is typically done in tandem with the Neural Network workshop upgrade (also unlocked by AI science). While AI Engineers increases base know-how, Neural Network doubles the overall effectiveness of your Engineers, creating a massive multiplicative boost to your village’s automated industrial output.

item.title: Alloy Saw
item.description:
The Alloy Saw is a late-mid-game Workshop upgrade that enhances the passive wood production of your Lumber Mills.

Costs and Prerequisites

To unlock the Alloy Saw, you must first research the Chemistry science technology. Once unlocked, it is available in the Workshop for the following resources:

  • Science: 85,000
  • Alloy: 75
  • Prerequisite Upgrade: You must have already purchased the Titanium Saw.

Core Effect

The primary function of this upgrade is to boost the efficiency of every Lumber Mill in your village:
item.content:encoded:
The Alloy Saw is a late-mid-game Workshop upgrade that enhances the passive wood production of your Lumber Mills.

Costs and Prerequisites

To unlock the Alloy Saw, you must first research the Chemistry science technology. Once unlocked, it is available in the Workshop for the following resources:

  • Science: 85,000
  • Alloy: 75
  • Prerequisite Upgrade: You must have already purchased the Titanium Saw.

Core Effect

The primary function of this upgrade is to boost the efficiency of every Lumber Mill in your village:

  • Production Bonus: It increases the wood production bonus of each Lumber Mill by an additional 15%.
  • Scaling: This bonus is additive with previous saw upgrades (Reinforced, Steel, and Titanium Saws). A base Lumber Mill provides +10% wood production; with the full chain of upgrades including the Alloy Saw, each mill becomes significantly more productive.

Strategic Utility

  • Late-Game Wood Velocity: As the costs for advanced structures like Observatories and Harbours escalate, maintaining a high wood production rate is critical. The Alloy Saw allows you to continue scaling wood income without needing to constantly build more mills, which eventually become prohibitively expensive.
  • Efficiency Benchmark: Mathematically, moving from 40 to 50 Lumber Mills with an Alloy Saw provides approximately a 21.4% relative increase in wood production, compared to only a 20% increase if no saws were researched.
  • Crafting Chain: Because wood is a foundational resource for second-order crafts like Beams and Scaffolds, this upgrade helps speed up the production of materials required for early space exploration and the transition into the Titanium era.

item.title: Alloy Axe
item.description:
The Alloy Axe is a late-mid-game Workshop upgrade that significantly improves the productivity of your Woodcutter kittens.

Costs and Prerequisites

To unlock the Alloy Axe, you must first research the Chemistry science technology, which enables the production of Alloy. Once researched, the upgrade can be purchased in the Workshop for the following resources:

  • Science: 70,000
  • Alloy: 25

Core Effect

  • Production Bonus: Researching the Alloy Axe makes Woodcutters 50% more effective (increasing your total woodRatio).
  • Flavor Description: The game describes these axes with the note: “The more you use them, the sharper they are!”.

Strategic Context

The Alloy Axe is part of a continuous chain of tool upgrades for your Woodcutters. It specifically follows the Titanium Axe (+50%) and is eventually succeeded by the Unobtainium Axe as you progress into deep-space operations.
item.content:encoded:
The Alloy Axe is a late-mid-game Workshop upgrade that significantly improves the productivity of your Woodcutter kittens.

Costs and Prerequisites

To unlock the Alloy Axe, you must first research the Chemistry science technology, which enables the production of Alloy. Once researched, the upgrade can be purchased in the Workshop for the following resources:

  • Science: 70,000
  • Alloy: 25
