  • Flavor Description: The game describes these axes with the note: “The more you use them, the sharper they are!”.

Strategic Context

The Alloy Axe is part of a continuous chain of tool upgrades for your Woodcutters. It specifically follows the Titanium Axe (+50%) and is eventually succeeded by the Unobtainium Axe as you progress into deep-space operations.

Because wood remains a foundational resource even in the late game—required for Scaffolds, Ships, and various buildings—this 50% boost is essential for maintaining the high resource velocity needed to overcome late-game bottlenecks. While it provides the same percentage boost as the previous Titanium Axe, it is necessary to stack these additive bonuses to keep up with the escalating costs of advanced structures.

item.title: Alloy Barns
item.description:
Alloy Barns is a major late-mid-game Workshop upgrade that significantly expands your village’s storage capacity for basic resources. It is considered a key milestone for transitioning out of the early game and preparing for space exploration.

Costs and Prerequisites

To unlock Alloy Barns, you must first research the Chemistry science technology (which requires Physics and Navigation). Once researched, the upgrade is available in the Workshop for:

  • Science: 75,000
  • Alloy: 20
  • Plate: 750

Core Effects

The primary function of Alloy Barns is to double the base storage effectiveness of your primary storage buildings:
item.content:encoded:
Alloy Barns is a major late-mid-game Workshop upgrade that significantly expands your village’s storage capacity for basic resources. It is considered a key milestone for transitioning out of the early game and preparing for space exploration.

Costs and Prerequisites

To unlock Alloy Barns, you must first research the Chemistry science technology (which requires Physics and Navigation). Once researched, the upgrade is available in the Workshop for:

  • Science: 75,000
  • Alloy: 20
  • Plate: 750

Core Effects

The primary function of Alloy Barns is to double the base storage effectiveness of your primary storage buildings:

  • +100% Storage Bonus: It increases the maximum amount of wood, minerals, and iron that can be stored in Barns, Warehouses, and Harbours by 100%.
  • Catnip Storage Synergy: If you have already purchased the Silos workshop upgrade, Alloy Barns will also apply 25% of its effect to your maximum catnip storage.

Strategic Importance

  • Affording Expensive Upgrades: As you progress toward Phase 2 (Space), the science and resource costs for technologies like Mechanization and Electronics escalate rapidly. Alloy Barns is often necessary to raise your resource caps high enough to purchase these advanced techs.
  • Kitten Population Growth: Expanding storage is a prerequisite for building more housing, such as Mansions or additional Log Houses, which in turn allows for a larger kitten population and more industrial output.
  • Titanium Management: Strategic guides note that Alloy-tier buildings and upgrades require substantial amounts of Titanium. Because Titanium is primarily gained through trading with Zebras, you will likely need to build a significant number of Trade Ships and Observatories to fund the Alloy production needed for this upgrade.
  • Progression Milestone: Players typically aim to acquire all Alloy-based storage upgrades (including Alloy Warehouses) when they reach approximately 90–100 kittens. This provides the storage foundation required to reach the Concrete era and eventually produce Concrete Huts for a more efficient reset.

item.title: HR Harvester
item.description:
The HR Harvester (Hawking Radiation Harvester) is an advanced late-game space structure located at the black hole Umbra. It functions as a dynamic energy generator that operates on the energy of black hole evaporation.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Location: Helios system, orbiting Umbra.
  • Science/Mission Prerequisite: Accessing Umbra requires a mission costing 25k Starcharts, 500k Science, 25k Kerosene, and 15k Thorium.
  • Construction Cost: 25 Relics and 1,250 Antimatter.
  • Price Ratio: 1.15.

Energy Production Mechanics

The HR Harvester is unique because its power output is not static; it provides a base of 1 Watt that increases indefinitely based on the age of your civilization and specific late-game upgrades.
item.content:encoded:
The HR Harvester (Hawking Radiation Harvester) is an advanced late-game space structure located at the black hole Umbra. It functions as a dynamic energy generator that operates on the energy of black hole evaporation.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Location: Helios system, orbiting Umbra.
  • Science/Mission Prerequisite: Accessing Umbra requires a mission costing 25k Starcharts, 500k Science, 25k Kerosene, and 15k Thorium.
  • Construction Cost: 25 Relics and 1,250 Antimatter.
  • Price Ratio: 1.15.

Energy Production Mechanics

The HR Harvester is unique because its power output is not static; it provides a base of 1 Watt that increases indefinitely based on the age of your civilization and specific late-game upgrades.

  • Dark Future Scaling: The energy output is primarily driven by a “year bonus” that activates once the calendar passes Year 40,000.
    • The bonus increases based on the number of years passed beyond 40,000, including years gained by shattering Time Crystals.
    • While the rate of increase slows down over time (following a square root formula), there is no upper limit to how high the energy production can go.
  • Void Rift Synergy: Each Void Rift (a structure in the Time tab) increases HR Harvester energy production by 10%.

Environmental and Cycle Modifiers

The effectiveness of the harvester fluctuates based on the current cosmic cycle if Numerology has been researched:

  • Umbra Cycle: Energy production is increased by +50%.
  • Dune Cycle: Energy production is reduced by -25%.

Strategic Importance

  • Energy Challenge: Building at least one HR Harvester is a mandatory requirement for completing the Energy Challenge.
  • Endgame Power Grid: Because its production scales with years, it eventually becomes a vital source of power for energy-intensive endgame structures like AI Cores and Entanglement Stations, especially during “Deep Runs” where the year count reaches into the hundreds of thousands.

item.title: Void
item.description:
Void is a specialized, late-game resource in Kittens Game primarily used to unlock advanced temporal and scientific mechanics. Unlike common resources, it cannot be produced by kittens or buildings; instead, it is randomly generated during “temporal paradoxes” that occur if you have constructed Chronospheres.

Acquisition and Generation

  • Temporal Paradoxes: Void is gained only during these events. The generation rate is notoriously slow, making it a major late-game bottleneck.
  • Scaling Generation: Having more Chronospheres increases the frequency and amount of void generated.
  • Void Hoover: This structure (costing 250 void and 10 time crystals) increases the maximum amount of void you can gain during a single paradox day.
  • Chronocontrol: Researching this increases the duration of temporal paradoxes, providing more opportunities for void to accumulate.
  • Preservation: As a non-luxury, non-crafted resource, 1.5% of your current void is preserved per Chronosphere upon resetting the game.

Technological and Scientific Progression

Void is the mandatory gatekeeper for Phase 3 (“Endgame”) technologies and several high-tier sciences:
item.content:encoded:
Void is a specialized, late-game resource in Kittens Game primarily used to unlock advanced temporal and scientific mechanics. Unlike common resources, it cannot be produced by kittens or buildings; instead, it is randomly generated during “temporal paradoxes” that occur if you have constructed Chronospheres.

Acquisition and Generation

  • Temporal Paradoxes: Void is gained only during these events. The generation rate is notoriously slow, making it a major late-game bottleneck.
  • Scaling Generation: Having more Chronospheres increases the frequency and amount of void generated.
  • Void Hoover: This structure (costing 250 void and 10 time crystals) increases the maximum amount of void you can gain during a single paradox day.
  • Chronocontrol: Researching this increases the duration of temporal paradoxes, providing more opportunities for void to accumulate.
  • Preservation: As a non-luxury, non-crafted resource, 1.5% of your current void is preserved per Chronosphere upon resetting the game.

Technological and Scientific Progression

Void is the mandatory gatekeeper for Phase 3 (“Endgame”) technologies and several high-tier sciences:

  • Void Space (800k Science, 30 Time Crystals, 100 Void): This science is the prerequisite for attempting the Atheism Challenge and for unlocking the ability to build Cryochambers.
  • Paradox Theory (1M Science, 40 Time Crystals, 250 Void): Unlocks the most advanced time-manipulation tools, including Resource Retrieval, Distortion, and Void Resonators.
  • Void Aspiration: A workshop upgrade that unlocks Void Hoovers and Void Rifts.

Key Benefits and Multipliers

  • Happiness: Simply holding any amount of void provides a flat +10% happiness bonus to your kittens.
  • Storage Capacity: Void Rifts (initially costing 75 void) increase your global resource storage ratio by 2%. This effect stacks additively with Event Horizons. In the extreme endgame, building approximately 50 Void Rifts is a common goal for resource scaling.
  • Energy Production: Each Void Rift increases the energy production of HR Harvesters by 10%.
  • Science Scaling: Void is required for the Void Reactors upgrade, which increases the maximum science capacity of Research Vessels and Space Beacons by 400%.

Advanced Infrastructure Costs

Void is required for constructing and maintaining endgame structures:

  • Cryochambers: Building one costs 100 void, and fixing a used cryochamber costs 500 void.
  • Dark Nova: An endgame cryptotheology building costing 7,500 void and 75k relics; it provides a 2% boost to global energy production.
  • Holy Genocide: A high-tier upgrade costing 25,000 void and 100k relics.
  • Chronosurge: Costs 750 void and enables Chronospheres to generate temporal flux yearly.
  • Temporal Press: Used to fine-tune time-crystal shattering, these cost 10 void each.

item.title: Void Space
item.description:
Void Space is a high-tier endgame science technology and a dedicated section in the Time tab that marks the transition into Phase 3 of Kittens Game, focusing on advanced temporal mechanics and the use of the Void resource.

Technological Unlock

  • Cost: 800,000 Science, 30 Time Crystals, and 100 Void.
  • Prerequisite: You must first research Tachyon Theory.
  • Immediate Unlocks: Researching this technology grants access to the Atheism challenge, the Paradox Theory science, and the Cryochambers and Void Aspiration workshop upgrades.

The Atheism Challenge

Void Space is the mandatory requirement to attempt the Atheism Challenge. In this challenge, the Order of the Sun is unavailable, meaning you must play without any faith bonuses. The goal is to reset the game with at least one Cryochamber constructed.
item.content:encoded:
Void Space is a high-tier endgame science technology and a dedicated section in the Time tab that marks the transition into Phase 3 of Kittens Game, focusing on advanced temporal mechanics and the use of the Void resource.

Technological Unlock

  • Cost: 800,000 Science, 30 Time Crystals, and 100 Void.
  • Prerequisite: You must first research Tachyon Theory.
  • Immediate Unlocks: Researching this technology grants access to the Atheism challenge, the Paradox Theory science, and the Cryochambers and Void Aspiration workshop upgrades.

The Atheism Challenge

Void Space is the mandatory requirement to attempt the Atheism Challenge. In this challenge, the Order of the Sun is unavailable, meaning you must play without any faith bonuses. The goal is to reset the game with at least one Cryochamber constructed.

Void Space Structures (Time Tab)

Once the technology is researched, several advanced structures become available in the Void Space section of the Time tab:

  • Cryochambers: Each chamber houses one kitten and allows you to carry that kitten (and its experience) over to your next game. You cannot build more cryochambers than your current number of active Chronospheres.
  • Void Hoover: Unlocked via Void Aspiration; increases the maximum amount of void you can gain during a Temporal Paradox day by 1.
  • Void Rift: Unlocked via Void Aspiration; each rift increases your global resource storage ratio by 2% and boosts HR Harvester energy production by 10%.
  • Chronocontrol: Unlocked via Paradox Theory; increases the number of days a Temporal Paradox lasts.
  • Void Resonator: Unlocked via Paradox Theory; improves faith production and allows Order of the Void to trigger during a time skip.

Strategic Importance

Void Space is a critical gatekeeper for the Endgame Reset Loop. It is the prerequisite for Paradox Theory, which unlocks Resource Retrieval—the mechanic that allows you to gain a percentage of your yearly resources every time you shatter a Time Crystal. Furthermore, building a “Void Seed” through numerous Void Rifts is a primary strategy for reaching the massive Unobtainium caps (over 8 billion) required for self-sustaining positive resets in the late game.

item.title: Dimensional Physics
item.description:
Dimensional Physics is a high-level late-game technology in Kittens Game that focuses on expanding resource storage and scientific capacity through the enhancement of Accelerators. It is part of the progression path toward time manipulation and antimatter technologies.

Costs and Prerequisites

  • Science Cost: 235,000.
  • Prerequisite: You must first research Particle Physics.
  • Technology Path: It is unlocked following Nuclear Fission and Particle Physics.

Unlocked Workshop Upgrades

Researching Dimensional Physics is primarily done to access two powerful upgrades for the Accelerator building:
item.content:encoded:
Dimensional Physics is a high-level late-game technology in Kittens Game that focuses on expanding resource storage and scientific capacity through the enhancement of Accelerators. It is part of the progression path toward time manipulation and antimatter technologies.

Costs and Prerequisites

  • Science Cost: 235,000.
  • Prerequisite: You must first research Particle Physics.
  • Technology Path: It is unlocked following Nuclear Fission and Particle Physics.

Unlocked Workshop Upgrades

Researching Dimensional Physics is primarily done to access two powerful upgrades for the Accelerator building:

  • Energy Rifts:

    • Cost: 200k Science, 7,500 Titanium, and 250 Uranium.
    • Effect: Transforms Accelerators into storage facilities by creating “rifts to pocket dimensions”.
    • Capacity Bonuses: Each Accelerator provides substantial storage for several resources: +30,000 Catnip, +20,000 Wood, +25,000 Minerals, +7,500 Iron, +2,500 Coal, +250 Gold, and +750 Titanium.
    • Strategic Value: This is a major late-game tool for bypassing the storage bottlenecks of standard buildings like Barns and Warehouses.

  • LHC (Large Hadron Collider):

    • Cost: 250k Science, 100 Unobtainium, and 150 Alloy.
    • Effect: Adds a flat bonus to your maximum science capacity for every Accelerator owned.
    • Bonus: +2,500 Max Science per Accelerator.
    • Strategic Value: This helps reach the massive science thresholds required for deep-space and temporal technologies, such as Chronophysics and Antimatter.

Strategic Utility

Dimensional Physics is often described as a turning point for resource management. By investing in Energy Rifts, players can significantly increase their Titanium and Gold caps, which are essential for mass trading with civilisations like the Zebras or Nagas. Furthermore, the LHC provides a scalable way to increase science storage without relying solely on expensive Observatories or Bio Labs.

item.title: Satellites
item.description:
Satellites are essential space structures in Kittens Game that bridge the gap between early-game astronomy and advanced interstellar exploration. They are primarily used to automate starchart production and significantly expand your scientific capacity.

Unlocking and Deployment

  • Prerequisites: You must first research Rocketry to unlock the Satellites technology (costing 190k Science and 125 Blueprints). Once the technology is researched, the “Deploy Satellite” mission becomes available in the Space tab.
  • Deployment Cost: Each satellite costs 325 Starcharts, 2,500 Titanium, 100k Science, and 15k Oil.
    • Note: In the Black Sky challenge, the cost is altered to remove the starchart requirement, making them accessible without prior astronomical observations.

Core Effects

Deploying satellites provides immediate global benefits to your science and resource generation:
item.content:encoded:
Satellites are essential space structures in Kittens Game that bridge the gap between early-game astronomy and advanced interstellar exploration. They are primarily used to automate starchart production and significantly expand your scientific capacity.

Unlocking and Deployment

  • Prerequisites: You must first research Rocketry to unlock the Satellites technology (costing 190k Science and 125 Blueprints). Once the technology is researched, the “Deploy Satellite” mission becomes available in the Space tab.
  • Deployment Cost: Each satellite costs 325 Starcharts, 2,500 Titanium, 100k Science, and 15k Oil.
    • Note: In the Black Sky challenge, the cost is altered to remove the starchart requirement, making them accessible without prior astronomical observations.

Core Effects

Deploying satellites provides immediate global benefits to your science and resource generation:

  • Science Cap: Each satellite improves the Science capacity of Observatories by 5%. This bonus can be further increased by 10% if the Militarize Space policy is enacted.
  • Starchart Production: Satellites generate a base of 0.005 starcharts per second. While slower than Research Vessels, they are often the first automated source of starcharts available to the player.
  • Energy Consumption: By default, each satellite consumes 1 Watt of energy.

Workshop Upgrades and Synergies

The utility of satellites is greatly enhanced through various Workshop upgrades:

  • Hubble Space Telescope: Increases the starchart production of all buildings, including satellites, by 30%.
  • Solar Satellites: Transforms satellites from energy consumers into producers, causing each one to generate 1 Watt instead of consuming it.
  • Satellite Navigation: This is a critical mid-game upgrade where every active satellite reduces the starchart cost of crafting Trade Ships by 1.25% (capped at a 75% discount).
  • Satellite Radio: Every active satellite provides a +0.5% bonus to the maximum culture and culture production of Broadcast Towers.

Cyclical and Environmental Impacts

The effectiveness of your satellite network fluctuates based on the current temporal cycle:

  • Cath Cycle: Provides a +100% bonus to satellite starchart production and the science bonus they provide to observatories.
  • Kairo Cycle: Imposes a -25% penalty to these same bonuses.
  • Challenges: Building at least one satellite is a mandatory goal for completing the Energy challenge. In the Black Sky challenge, their starchart production is reduced based on the number of times you have completed the challenge.

item.title: Cold Fusion
item.description:
Cold Fusion is a Workshop upgrade that significantly improves the power output of your Reactors. It is a critical mid-to-late game upgrade for managing the increasing energy demands of space structures and advanced automation.

Requirements and Costs

To unlock Cold Fusion, you must first research the Superconductors technology.

  • Science Cost: 200,000
  • Eludium Cost: 25
  • Prerequisite Tech: Superconductors

Core Effects

  • Energy Boost: It increases the energy output of all Reactors by 25%.
  • Production Value: Specifically, it raises the base energy production of a Reactor by 2.5 Watts (typically increasing it from 10 to 12.5 Watts).

Strategic Utility

Cold Fusion acts as a major “step up” for your energy infrastructure during the Eludium Era.
item.content:encoded:
Cold Fusion is a Workshop upgrade that significantly improves the power output of your Reactors. It is a critical mid-to-late game upgrade for managing the increasing energy demands of space structures and advanced automation.

Requirements and Costs

To unlock Cold Fusion, you must first research the Superconductors technology.

  • Science Cost: 200,000
  • Eludium Cost: 25
  • Prerequisite Tech: Superconductors

Core Effects

  • Energy Boost: It increases the energy output of all Reactors by 25%.
  • Production Value: Specifically, it raises the base energy production of a Reactor by 2.5 Watts (typically increasing it from 10 to 12.5 Watts).

Strategic Utility

Cold Fusion acts as a major “step up” for your energy infrastructure during the Eludium Era.

  • Powering Space: As you build energy-heavy structures like Containment Chambers (50 Watts) and Entanglement Stations (25 Watts), the passive boost from Cold Fusion helps maintain a positive energy balance without needing to build excessive numbers of Sunlifters immediately.
  • Efficiency: Unlike Thorium Reactors, which require a constant fuel source (Thorium) to provide their bonus, Cold Fusion provides a permanent, passive increase to reactor output with no ongoing resource cost.

item.title: Composite Bow
item.description:
The Composite Bow is an early-game Workshop upgrade that permanently increases the efficiency of your workforce’s hunting capabilities.

Core Effects and Stats

  • Effect: It provides a +50% bonus to Catpower production for all kittens assigned to the Hunter job.
  • Prerequisite: You must research the Construction technology to unlock it.
  • Cost: 500 Science, 100 Iron, and 200 Wood.

Strategic Utility

  • Hunting Frequency: By boosting the rate at which Catpower generates, the Composite Bow allows you to send hunts more frequently. This is critical in the early game for accumulating Furs (for Parchment) and Ivory (for happiness and trade).
  • Weapon Progression: It is the first tier of weapon upgrades, serving as a prerequisite step before you can eventually unlock better versions like the Crossbow (Machinery) and Railgun (Particle Physics).

Relevance to Iron Will

In this mode, Zebras replace kittens and act as your Hunters. Consequently, purchasing the Composite Bow will increase the passive Catpower generation of your Zebra population, allowing for more frequent trading and hunting without a kitten workforce.

  • Cost: 500 Science, 100 Iron, and 200 Wood.

Strategic Utility

  • Hunting Frequency: By boosting the rate at which Catpower generates, the Composite Bow allows you to send hunts more frequently. This is critical in the early game for accumulating Furs (for Parchment) and Ivory (for happiness and trade).
  • Weapon Progression: It is the first tier of weapon upgrades, serving as a prerequisite step before you can eventually unlock better versions like the Crossbow (Machinery) and Railgun (Particle Physics).

Relevance to Iron Will

In this mode, Zebras replace kittens and act as your Hunters. Consequently, purchasing the Composite Bow will increase the passive Catpower generation of your Zebra population, allowing for more frequent trading and hunting without a kitten workforce.

item.title: Concrete Barns
item.description:
Concrete Barns is a Workshop upgrade that significantly increases the storage capacity of your Barns, marking a major step up in resource management during the mid-game “Concrete Era.”

Core Effects

  • Storage Boost: It increases the maximum storage of Wood, Minerals, and Iron provided by Barns by +75%.
  • Catnip Synergy: If you have researched the Silos upgrade, Concrete Barns also increases your Catnip storage (the bonus is 25% of the main effect, contributing to the total barn storage multiplier).

Costs and Requirements

  • Resources: 45 Concrete and 2,000 Titanium.
  • Science Cost: 2,000 Science.
  • Prerequisite: You must first purchase the Concrete Pillars upgrade (which in turn requires the Mechanization technology).

Strategic Context

  • The Concrete Era: This upgrade is part of a suite of “Concrete” improvements (including Concrete Warehouses and Concrete Huts) unlocked via Mechanization and Concrete Pillars. It is essential for breaking through the storage bottlenecks that typically occur after the “Titanium Era”.
  • Scaling: Because it provides a percentage-based boost (+75%), its value scales with the number of Barns you have constructed. This increased capacity is often necessary to stockpile the massive amounts of Minerals and Wood required for late-game housing (Mansions) and space structures.

item.title: Concrete Huts
item.description:
Concrete Huts is a pivotal Workshop upgrade that marks the end of the “early game” and is considered the primary goal for your first run. It drastically reduces the cost scaling of Huts, allowing for a massive population boom.

Core Effects and Costs

  • Effect: Reduces the price ratio of Huts by 30%.
    • Huts have a very steep base price ratio (2.5). This upgrade, combined with the earlier Ironwood Huts (-50%), makes high-level Huts significantly affordable.
  • Cost: 125,000 Science, 45 Concrete, and 3,000 Titanium.
  • Prerequisite: You must research Mechanization (which unlocks Concrete Pillars) and typically need to have purchased Concrete Pillars first.

Strategic Importance: The First Reset

Concrete Huts is the single most important milestone for determining when to perform your first reset.

  • Cost: 125,000 Science, 45 Concrete, and 3,000 Titanium.

Strategic Importance: The First Reset

Concrete Huts is the single most important milestone for determining when to perform your first reset.

  • The 130 Kitten Goal: Without this upgrade, most players cap out around 70–80 kittens. Concrete Huts allows you to push your population to 130–140 kittens.
  • Paragon Farming: Since you earn 1 Paragon for every kitten over 70, reaching 130 kittens guarantees you 60 Paragon upon resetting. This is the recommended amount needed to buy essential Metaphysics upgrades (like Diplomacy and Golden Ratio) for your second run.

Requirements and The “Concrete Era”

Reaching Concrete Huts requires overcoming two main bottlenecks:

  1. Science Cap: The 125,000 Science cost is often higher than your caps allow. You will likely need to build Bio Labs (unlocked by Biology) or craft extensive Compendiums to raise your maximum science limit enough to afford it.
  2. Titanium: The 3,000 Titanium cost requires a robust trade network with the Zebras. You should rely on Trade Ships and Geodesy (if unlocked) to stockpile this Titanium.

Once you purchase Concrete Huts, the strategy is simple: build as many Huts as your storage allows, maximize your population, and then execute the BMF (Backup, Metas, Faith) checklist before resetting.

item.title: Concrete Pillars
item.description:
Concrete Pillars is a Workshop upgrade that serves as the foundation for the “Concrete Era” of storage and housing. It is generally the first concrete-based upgrade players purchase after researching the Mechanization technology.

Costs and Requirements

  • Science Cost: 100,000 Science.
  • Resource Cost: 50 Concrete.
  • Prerequisite: You must research the Mechanization technology.

Core Effects

Unlike the massive +75% boost from Concrete Barns, this upgrade provides a smaller, universal reinforcement to your storage infrastructure:

  • General Storage: It increases the storage capacity of Barns, Warehouses, and Harbors by +5%.
  • Gold Storage: It increases the Max Gold capacity provided by Mints by +5%.
  • Catnip Synergy: If you have the Silos upgrade, the +5% bonus also applies to the Catnip storage of your Barns and Warehouses.

Strategic Context

While a 5% boost may seem small compared to other upgrades, Concrete Pillars is a critical stepping stone:

item.title: Crossbow
item.description:
The Crossbow is a mid-game Workshop upgrade that further improves the efficiency of your hunting workforce. It serves as the second tier of weapon technology, following the Composite Bow.

Core Effects

  • Production Boost: It provides a permanent +25% bonus to Catpower production for all kittens assigned to the Hunter job.
  • Cumulative Effect: This bonus stacks additively with other weapon upgrades (like the Composite Bow’s +50%), contributing to your total hunting multiplier.

Costs and Requirements

  • Science Cost: 12,000 Science.
  • Resource Cost: 1,500 Iron.
  • Prerequisite: You must research the Machinery technology to unlock this upgrade.

Strategic Utility

  • Hunting Frequency: Like the Composite Bow, the primary value of the Crossbow is increasing your Catpower cap fill rate. This allows you to send hunts more frequently to gather Furs (for Parchment/Manuscripts) and Ivory (for happiness and trade).
  • Iron Will Synergy: Since you are interested in Iron Will mode: The Crossbow upgrade applies to Zebras, who act as your Hunters in the absence of kittens. Purchasing this will boost your Zebras’ passive Catpower generation by 25%, which is vital for maintaining trade with races like the Nagas and Zebras.
  • Pacifism Challenge: Note that if you ever attempt the Pacifism challenge, weapon upgrades like the Crossbow suffer a penalty, becoming -10% effective per completion.

item.title: Cryocomputing
item.description:
Cryocomputing is a late-game Workshop upgrade that significantly improves the energy efficiency of your scientific infrastructure, specifically targeting Data Centers.

Core Effects

  • Energy Reduction: It reduces the energy consumption of Data Centers by 50%.
  • Specific Value: This drops the power usage of each Data Center from 2 Watts to 1 Watt.

Requirements and Costs

  • Prerequisite: You must research the Superconductors technology.
  • Science Cost: 125,000 Science.
  • Resource Cost: 15 Eludium.

Strategic Utility

Cryocomputing becomes essential when you transition from Libraries to Data Centers to boost your science cap.

Strategic Utility

Cryocomputing becomes essential when you transition from Libraries to Data Centers to boost your science cap.

  • The Energy Bottleneck: While Data Centers provide vastly superior stats to Libraries (offering +750 Max Science and +250 Max Culture), they come with a steep upkeep cost of 2 Watts per building. Since you typically need hundreds of Data Centers to reach the science caps required for endgame technologies (like Void Space or Paradox Theory), this can drain hundreds of Watts from your grid.
  • Efficiency: By halving this consumption, Cryocomputing essentially refunds massive amounts of power, allowing you to reallocate that energy to other heavy consumers like Containment Chambers, Accelerators, or Space Stations without needing to build as many Sunlifters.

item.title: Chronoforge
item.description:
The Chronoforge is a major Workshop upgrade unlocked in the late game that grants access to the Time tab’s advanced functions. It is the central mechanic for manipulating time, allowing you to skip years instantly to accelerate resource production and unlock the “Shatter Engine” loop.

Unlocking and Costs

To access the Chronoforge, you must first progress through the Particle Physics and Chronophysics technologies to unlock Tachyon Theory.

  • Workshop Upgrade Cost: 500,000 Science, 5 Relics, and 10 Time Crystals.
  • Effect: It unlocks the “Chronoforge” section within the Time tab.
  • Important Note: Unlike Cryptotheology buildings, Chronoforge upgrades do not carry over through resets. You must rebuild your infrastructure in the Time tab every run.

Core Mechanic: Combusting Time Crystals

The primary function of the Chronoforge is the ability to “Combust Time Crystal” (often called “shattering”).
item.content:encoded:
The Chronoforge is a major Workshop upgrade unlocked in the late game that grants access to the Time tab’s advanced functions. It is the central mechanic for manipulating time, allowing you to skip years instantly to accelerate resource production and unlock the “Shatter Engine” loop.

Unlocking and Costs

To access the Chronoforge, you must first progress through the Particle Physics and Chronophysics technologies to unlock Tachyon Theory.

  • Workshop Upgrade Cost: 500,000 Science, 5 Relics, and 10 Time Crystals.
  • Effect: It unlocks the “Chronoforge” section within the Time tab.
  • Important Note: Unlike Cryptotheology buildings, Chronoforge upgrades do not carry over through resets. You must rebuild your infrastructure in the Time tab every run.

Core Mechanic: Combusting Time Crystals

The primary function of the Chronoforge is the ability to “Combust Time Crystal” (often called “shattering”).

  • Effect: Instantly skips the game calendar to the beginning of the next Spring.
  • Cost: 1 Time Crystal (Base).
  • Heat Mechanic: Each shatter generates 10 units of Chronoheat. If your current heat exceeds your maximum heat limit, the Time Crystal cost to shatter increases by +1% for every unit of excess heat.

Key Chronoforge Structures

Once the Chronoforge is unlocked, you can purchase several sub-structures in the Time tab to manage heat and improve efficiency:

Structure Cost Function
Chrono Furnace 25 TCs, 5 Relics Increases max heat capacity by 100. It also automatically converts accumulated heat into “fuel” to trigger free time skips.
Time Boiler 25k TCs Expands the heat capacity of Chrono Furnaces by 10 per boiler.
Temporal Accelerator 10 TCs, 1k Relics Improves time-related effects (like Time Impedance and Unicornmancy) by 5%. It also reduces the “lag” associated with mass-shattering.
Resource Retrieval 1k TCs Crucial for the Endgame. Requires Paradox Theory. It allows you to gain 1% of your yearly resource production per level every time you shatter a Time Crystal.

Strategic Utility: The Shatter Engine

The Chronoforge is the engine of the late-game economy (Phase 3/4).

  1. Antimatter Generation: By building Sunlifters and shattering Time Crystals, you can cycle through years rapidly, generating massive amounts of Antimatter (which is produced annually) without waiting for real-time days to pass.
  2. Void Generation: If you have Chronospheres, skipping years forces “Temporal Paradoxes” (Void spawns) to occur more frequently in real-time.
  3. Redmoon Cycling: Players use the Chronoforge to skip “weak” planetary cycles (like Charon) and land specifically on Redmoon or Dune cycles to maximize Unobtainium production for trading.
  4. Infinite Loop: With enough Resource Retrieval levels, a single shatter yields enough Unobtainium/Alicorns to trade or sacrifice for more than 1 Time Crystal. This creates a self-sustaining loop where you can skip time indefinitely.

item.title: Reset
item.description:
Resetting is the primary mechanic used to exchange current progress for permanent prestige currencies—Karma and Paragon—which provide global multipliers to production and resource storage capacity.

Timing Your Reset

Deciding when to reset depends on your current game phase and prestige goals:

  • The First Reset: It is strategically recommended to reset only after researching Concrete Huts and reaching at least 130 kittens. This ensures you gain roughly 60 Paragon, enough to purchase essential early Metaphysics upgrades like Diplomacy or Golden Ratio.
  • Subsequent Early Runs: Aim for 170+ kittens on your second run to secure 100 Paragon for the Divine Proportion upgrade.
  • Prestige Minimums: You must have more than 35 kittens to gain Karma and more than 70 kittens to receive Paragon (one point per kitten over 70).
  • The “Slow-Down” Rule: Generally, you should reset when progress becomes “too slow” or when building costs exceed your current production and storage limits.

The Pre-Reset Checklist (BMF)

Experienced players use the BMF mnemonic (Backup, Metas, Faith) to ensure no progress is wasted before a reset:
item.content:encoded:
Resetting is the primary mechanic used to exchange current progress for permanent prestige currencies—Karma and Paragon—which provide global multipliers to production and resource storage capacity.

Timing Your Reset

Deciding when to reset depends on your current game phase and prestige goals:

  • The First Reset: It is strategically recommended to reset only after researching Concrete Huts and reaching at least 130 kittens. This ensures you gain roughly 60 Paragon, enough to purchase essential early Metaphysics upgrades like Diplomacy or Golden Ratio.
  • Subsequent Early Runs: Aim for 170+ kittens on your second run to secure 100 Paragon for the Divine Proportion upgrade.
  • Prestige Minimums: You must have more than 35 kittens to gain Karma and more than 70 kittens to receive Paragon (one point per kitten over 70).
  • The “Slow-Down” Rule: Generally, you should reset when progress becomes “too slow” or when building costs exceed your current production and storage limits.

The Pre-Reset Checklist (BMF)

Experienced players use the BMF mnemonic (Backup, Metas, Faith) to ensure no progress is wasted before a reset:

  • Backup: Manually save and export your game data to prevent accidental loss.
  • Metas (Metaphysics): Use your accumulated Paragon to buy permanent upgrades in the Metaphysics tab, particularly price ratio reductions like Enlightenment or Renaissance, which make future buildings cheaper.
  • Faith (The TAP Sequence): To maximize spiritual carry-over, perform the TAP sequence: Transcendence (to increase your tier), then Adore the Galaxy (to convert worship into Epiphany), and finally Praise the Sun.
  • Population Push: Max out all housing, including Huts, Log Houses, and Mansions, to squeeze out every possible Paragon point.
  • Resource Conversion: Sacrifice all unicorns for tears and alicorns for Time Crystals before they are lost.

Carry-over Mechanics

Understanding what survives the reset is vital for planning your next run:

  • Permanent Carry-over: Karma, Paragon, Metaphysics upgrades, Epiphany, Transcendence tiers, Black Liquid Sorrow (BLS), and Cryptotheology buildings are preserved.
  • Resources Lost: You lose all standard buildings, technology, and luxury resources like furs, ivory, and spice.
  • Conditional Carry-over:
    • Chronospheres: Each sphere preserves 1.5% of your non-crafted resources.
    • Flux Condensator: This workshop upgrade is required to carry over crafted resources like steel, plates, and blueprints.
    • Cryochambers: These allow you to carry over one kitten per chamber, retaining their job skills and experience.

Advanced Reset Strategies

  • Iron Will (IW) Mode: In this kittenless mode, the goal is to reset immediately after researching Archery to accumulate Zebras, which provide passive Catpower for future runs.
  • Positive Resets: In the endgame, the goal is to build at least 73 Chronospheres. At this level, the resources carried over exceed the cost of the spheres themselves, allowing for infinite, self-sustaining growth loops.

Checklist

To maximize the benefits of a reset and ensure your next run starts with a massive economic foundation, you should follow a thorough pre-reset preparation sequence. The community often uses the acronym BMF (Backup, Metas, and Faith) to remember the core steps. Here is a comprehensive pre-reset checklist:

  1. Maximize Your Population (Paragon Preparation)

    Before anything else, cap out all of your housing structures (Huts, Log Houses, Mansions, Space Stations). Because Paragon rewards are based directly on your kitten population at the time of reset (granting 1 Paragon for every kitten over 70), you should push your population as high as your storage caps allow.

  2. Backup and Metaphysics (The “B” and “M” in BMF)

    • Backup: Always export and save a backup of your game just in case you forget a step or realize you didn’t have enough resources stockpiled.
    • Metaphysics: If you have enough Paragon, purchase any planned Metaphysics upgrades (such as price ratio reductions). If you plan to burn any Paragon for its unique production and storage bonuses, do so now while you have a small spare amount.

  3. Optimize Your Religion (The “F” in BMF) To ensure your faith bonuses carry over effectively, execute the TAP sequence:

    • Transcend: Spend your accumulated epiphany to buy Transcendence tiers.
    • Adore the Galaxy: Convert all of your worship into epiphany. The game will do this automatically if you forget, but manually clicking the button grants an extra 1% bonus.
    • Praise the Sun: Convert your remaining faith pool into worship.

  4. Refine Luxury Resources:

    Do not leave valuable resources behind, as luxuries do not carry over on reset. Sacrifice all of your accumulated Alicorns to turn them into Time Crystals, ensuring you have the Anachronomancy metaphysics upgrade so the crystals survive the reset. Refine any spare unicorn tears into Black Liquid Sorrow (BLS), which is permanently retained.

  5. Chronosphere and Resource Stockpiling:

    Chronospheres allow you to carry over 1.5% of your standard resources per sphere into the next run to optimize this:

    • Turn off automation: Disable any scripts or autoclickers (like auto-praise or auto-crafting) so they don’t consume your carefully balanced stockpiles right before you reset.
    • Buy Flux Condensator: Purchase this workshop upgrade (costing 5,000 unobtainium and 5 Time Crystals) so your crafted resources, such as blueprints, alloy, and compendiums, will also carry over.
    • Stockpile everything: Cap out your non-crafted resources (like gold, faith, and starcharts). Heavily stockpile crafted resources; carrying over a massive amount of Compendiums is especially critical, as they will vastly increase your science cap at the very start of your next run, allowing you to instantly rebuy key technologies.
    • Liquidate Buildings: Right before buying your Chronospheres, you can sell off expensive buildings like Orbital Arrays and Space Elevators at a 50% refund to squeeze out extra resources for your carryover pool.
    • Buy Chronospheres: Finally, purchase as many Chronospheres as your unobtainium allows.

Once all these steps are complete, you are ready to hit the reset button.

Progression

Paragon progression in Kittens Game follows a compounding curve. Paragon functions as both a raw production and storage multiplier when stockpiled and a currency spent in Metaphysics. The central rule of farming it is: never spend down to zero, because your banked reserve is what makes subsequent runs fast.

How Paragon Is Earned

When you reset via the Time tab:

  • You gain 1 Paragon per kitten over 70 (Kittens - 70).
    • 130 kittens = 60 Paragon
    • 200 kittens = 130 Paragon
    • 250 kittens = 180 Paragon
  • You also earn Karma, which increases kitten happiness and scales with total historical kittens sacrificed across resets.

The Golden Ratio: The 150–200 Banked Floor

  • Production Bonus: Each banked Paragon grants +1% global production, capped at +200% with diminishing returns past 200 (hard cap asymptotic behavior).
  • Storage Bonus: Each banked Paragon grants a flat +0.1% to storage caps, with no diminishing returns.
  • The Spending Rule: When buying Metaphysics upgrades, always maintain at least 150 to 200 unspent Paragon in reserve. Spending all your Paragon to buy an upgrade sets your early-game production back to ground zero.

Step-by-Step Reset Progression Strategy

The Exact Reset Point Rule

The trap in Kittens Game is overextending a run hoping for “just a few more kittens.”

Reset immediately when:

Time to unlock the next 2 kitten housing slots > Time to rebuild to your current kitten count on a fresh run

More specifically, reset when all three conditions are met:

  1. Housing Caps Hard-Stall: You have capped all available Log Cabins, Mansions, and Huts, and the next housing structure requires either days of waiting or a massive tech tree leap (e.g., waiting days to mine enough Unobtainium for another Space Station).
  2. Kitten Count is at its Natural Bracket:
  • Early Game: Reset around 130 kittens.
  • Mid Game (Post-Concrete/Unobtainium Huts): Reset around 180–220 kittens.
  • Post-Renaissance: Reset around 250–270+ kittens.
  1. Pre-Reset Checklist is Done:
  • Burn excess Catpower into Hunts (maximize furs/ivory/parchment).
  • Trade all spare resources for maximum storage fill.
  • Praise the Sun and perform an Apocrypha reset if you have excess faith stored, to permanently increase your Solar Revolution multiplier.
  • Fill every housing slot to capacity before hitting the reset button.

item.title: Compendium
item.description:
A Compendium is a mid-game craftable resource that represents the “sum of all modern knowledge of catkind”. It is primarily used to expand your Science storage capacity, which is essential for unlocking late-game technologies and space missions.

Production and Costs

To craft a Compendium, you must first research the Philosophy technology.

  • Cost: 50 Manuscripts and 10,000 Science.
  • Crafting Efficiency: Like other workshop resources, the number of Compendiums produced per craft is significantly increased by your Workshop and Factory craft bonuses.
  • Metaphysics Bonus: The Codex Logos upgrade (50 Paragon) adds +25% to the craft ratio and provides a x1.1 multiplier to Compendium crafting.

Primary Effects

  • Science Storage: Each Compendium provides a permanent +10 bonus to your maximum Science cap.
  • Storage Cap: By default, the maximum bonus you can receive from Compendiums is capped at 100% of your total science storage from buildings.
    • In Iron Will mode, this cap is significantly higher (1000%).
    • Data Centres increase the “Compendium Cap” by 1,000 each.
    • The Uplink and Starlink workshop upgrades further increase this cap by +1% per Bio Lab.

Strategic Utility

Compendiums act as a bridge between the industrial era and the space era, where technology costs begin to exceed the storage limits of standard buildings.

Primary Effects

  • Storage Cap: By default, the maximum bonus you can receive from Compendiums is capped at 100% of your total science storage from buildings.
    • In Iron Will mode, this cap is significantly higher (1000%).
    • Data Centres increase the “Compendium Cap” by 1,000 each.
    • The Uplink and Starlink workshop upgrades further increase this cap by +1% per Bio Lab.

Strategic Utility

Compendiums act as a bridge between the industrial era and the space era, where technology costs begin to exceed the storage limits of standard buildings.

  • Technological Gatekeeper: Compendiums are a required component for researching critical sciences, including:
    • Architecture (10 Compendiums)
    • Physics (35 Compendiums)
    • Chemistry (50 Compendiums)
    • Acoustics (60 Compendiums)
    • Geology (65 Compendiums)
    • Biology (100 Compendiums)
  • Grinding Blueprints: Compendiums are the raw material for crafting Blueprints (25,000 Science + 25 Compendiums), which are necessary for advanced industrial and space structures.
  • Chronosphere Resets: When resetting with Chronospheres, carrying over a large stockpile of Compendiums is vital. Because they preserve your science cap, you can immediately research expensive technologies in the next run without waiting to rebuild massive amounts of libraries and observatories.

Optimization Tip

To grind Compendiums efficiently, focus on maximizing your Culture and Catpower production first. This allows you to mass-produce Manuscripts, which are the primary bottleneck for Compendium crafting. Once your Science cap is full, use the “Craft All” function in the Workshop to convert those manuscripts into Compendiums.

item.title: Numeromancy
item.description:
Numeromancy is a late-game Metaphysics upgrade that grants your civilisation unique production bonuses during Festivals based on the current active Cycle of the Cath solar system.

Key Statistics and Requirements

  • Cost: 250 Paragon.
  • Prerequisite: Numerology (which costs 50 Paragon and applies cycle-based effects to space production).
  • Unlocks: The Malkuth metaphysics upgrade.

Festival Effects by Cycle

When a Festival is active, Numeromancy applies the following multipliers depending on the current 5-year cycle:

Cycle Resource Bonus (x) Primary Focus
Charon 1.5x Catnip, Wood, Minerals
Umbra 1.5x Coal, Iron, Titanium, Gold
Yarn 2.0x Culture
Helios 2.0x / 1.25x Faith / Unicorns
Cath 2.0x Catpower
Redmoon 2.0x Unobtainium
Dune 2.0x Uranium
Piscine 2.0x Science
Terminus 2.0x Oil
Kairo 5.0x Starcharts

Strategic Synergies

The most powerful application of Numeromancy is during the Redmoon cycle to resolve the Unobtainium bottleneck.

Cycle Resource Bonus (x) Primary Focus

Umbra 1.5x Coal, Iron, Titanium, Gold
Yarn 2.0x Culture
Helios 2.0x / 1.25x Faith / Unicorns
Cath 2.0x Catpower
Redmoon 2.0x Unobtainium
Dune 2.0x Uranium
Piscine 2.0x Science
Terminus 2.0x Oil
Kairo 5.0x Starcharts

Strategic Synergies

The most powerful application of Numeromancy is during the Redmoon cycle to resolve the Unobtainium bottleneck.

  • The Redmoon Engine: By running a festival during the Redmoon cycle, you receive a base 2x boost to Unobtainium income. When combined with other endgame bonuses, this can reach nearly 2.5x total production.
  • Brewery Scaling: Each Brewery you construct increases the “Festival Cycle Bonus” by 1%. For example, having 50 breweries would increase the Redmoon festival bonus from 2.0x to 2.5x.
  • Temporal Arbitrage: Experienced players use a Chronoforge to “shatter” Time Crystals, skipping less profitable years to land precisely on the Redmoon cycle and maximise the Numeromancy festival bonus.

Why It Matters

Numeromancy is essential for the mid-to-late game transition (Phase 3 and 4). It transforms Festivals from simple happiness-boosting events into high-leverage tools for resource generation. This is particularly vital for reaching Transcendence Tier 15, as the faith income bonus in the Helios cycle and the Unobtainium boost in Redmoon accelerate the accumulation of Time Crystals and Relics.

item.title: Arbitrage
item.description:
In Kittens Game, arbitrage refers to the strategic manipulation of resource conversion and trading cycles to generate a net profit or bypass severe production bottlenecks. Rather than relying on linear accumulation, players use arbitrage to transform high-volume, low-value resources into restricted, high-value capital.

Key Arbitrage Strategies

Strategy Mechanism Goal
Trade Arbitrage Refining Catnip into Wood and immediately trading it to Griffins. Resolving the mid-game Iron bottleneck by bypassing slow smelters.
Iron Will (IW) Loop Trading Iron to Sharks for Catnip, refining it to Wood, and trading that back to Griffins for Iron. Generating a net profit of Iron and Wood in resource-constrained IW runs.
Temporal Arbitrage Shattering Time Crystals to skip less productive years and land on the Redmoon cycle. Converting temporal capital into a $2.5\times$ spike in Unobtainium production.
Positive Resets Building enough Chronospheres to carry over more resources than were spent during the run. Establishing a self-sustaining engine of exponential growth.

Detailed Arbitrage Mechanics

1. Mid-Game Trade Arbitrage

The raw production rates of base resources often become the primary bottleneck for industrial expansion. To solve this, players use the Catnip $\to$ Wood $\to$ Iron loop. This system exploits the high volume of catnip to create wood, which is then traded to the Griffins for Iron. This “trade arbitrage” effectively turns food production into high-value industrial metal, which is much faster than waiting for standard Smelters or Calciners to process ore.
