Detailed Arbitrage Mechanics

1. Mid-Game Trade Arbitrage

The raw production rates of base resources often become the primary bottleneck for industrial expansion. To solve this, players use the Catnip $\to$ Wood $\to$ Iron loop. This system exploits the high volume of catnip to create wood, which is then traded to the Griffins for Iron. This “trade arbitrage” effectively turns food production into high-value industrial metal, which is much faster than waiting for standard Smelters or Calciners to process ore.

2. Temporal and Cycle Arbitrage

In the late game, the focus shifts to system arbitrage. Because the Redmoon cycle provides a massive multiplier to Unobtainium production, players use Time Crystals as a currency to “buy” more productive time.

  • By skipping the “fallow” years of other cycles, players ensure their Outposts and Space Elevators are always operating at maximum efficiency.
  • When combined with Numeromancy and active Festivals, this temporal arbitrage generates the massive amounts of Unobtainium required for endgame goals.

3. Positive Chrono-Reset Arbitrage

The ultimate goal of endgame optimization is the positive reset. This occurs when your storage capacity for Unobtainium is high enough (at least 8.14 billion) to build 73 or more Chronospheres.

  • At 73 Chronospheres, the amount of resources carried over into the next game exceeds the cost of building those spheres.
  • This transforms expendable resources into compounding capital, meaning every reset starts the player with an exponentially larger foundation than the previous run.

item.title: Festivals
item.description:
In Kittens Game, Festivals are temporary global events that provide significant growth and production bonuses. They are unlocked via the Drama and Poetry technology, which requires 90,000 Science and 5,000 Parchment.

Base Effects and Duration

A standard festival lasts for one game year (400 days, which is approximately 13 minutes and 20 seconds of real-time).

  • Kitten Growth: The primary benefit of a festival is doubling the rate at which new kittens arrive (from roughly 0.16 to 0.32 kittens per second). This is essential for quickly filling housing to reach population milestones for Paragon.
  • Happiness: Festivals provide a base happiness boost, which improves overall village productivity.

Advanced Mechanics (Numeromancy)

Once you research the Numeromancy Metaphysics upgrade, festivals grant powerful Cycle-specific bonuses. These are often used to resolve specific late-game resource bottlenecks:
item.content:encoded:
In Kittens Game, Festivals are temporary global events that provide significant growth and production bonuses. They are unlocked via the Drama and Poetry technology, which requires 90,000 Science and 5,000 Parchment.

Base Effects and Duration

A standard festival lasts for one game year (400 days, which is approximately 13 minutes and 20 seconds of real-time).

  • Kitten Growth: The primary benefit of a festival is doubling the rate at which new kittens arrive (from roughly 0.16 to 0.32 kittens per second). This is essential for quickly filling housing to reach population milestones for Paragon.
  • Happiness: Festivals provide a base happiness boost, which improves overall village productivity.

Advanced Mechanics (Numeromancy)

Once you research the Numeromancy Metaphysics upgrade, festivals grant powerful Cycle-specific bonuses. These are often used to resolve specific late-game resource bottlenecks:

  • Redmoon: Doubles Unobtainium income (essential for the space race).
  • Cath: Doubles Catpower income (ideal for mass trading or hunting).
  • Piscine: Doubles Science income.
  • Helios: Doubles Faith income and increases Unicorn income by 25%.
  • Kairo: Increases Starchart income by 5x.

Building and Policy Synergies

  • Brewery: This building is specifically designed to enhance festivals. Each Brewery provides +1% to Festival Happiness and the Cycle Bonus, while slightly increasing kitten arrival speed (+0.1%).
  • Carnivals (Metaphysics): This upgrade allows you to stack festivals, adding to their duration so you do not have to manually restart them every year.
  • Carnivale (Policy): Increases the kitten growth rate during festivals by an additional 30%, though it also increases luxury resource consumption.
  • Extravagance (Policy): Makes rare resources provide significantly more happiness during festivals but consumes them twice as fast.

Strategic Utility

  • Early Game: Most guides recommend skipping Drama and Poetry (and thus festivals) on your first few runs because the 5,000 Parchment cost is too high for the marginal early-game benefit.
  • Late Game Paragon Farming: Festivals are mandatory for “short runs” (approx. 30 minutes) where the goal is to max out population as fast as possible to reset for Paragon.
  • Resource Spikes: In the mid-to-late game, players often “shatter” Time Crystals to reach the Redmoon Cycle and then hold a festival to maximize Unobtainium production.

item.title: Redmoon Cycle
item.description:
The Redmoon cycle is the sixth phase in the ten-cycle system of Kittens Game and is widely considered the most strategically important period for late-game resource farming. Its primary purpose is to provide a massive multiplier to Unobtainium production, which is the critical bottleneck for space exploration and time manipulation.

The character used for the Redmoon cycle is the glyph ⍜.

Core Effects

The impact of the Redmoon cycle depends on your researched Metaphysics upgrades:
item.content:encoded:
The Redmoon cycle is the sixth phase in the ten-cycle system of Kittens Game and is widely considered the most strategically important period for late-game resource farming. Its primary purpose is to provide a massive multiplier to Unobtainium production, which is the critical bottleneck for space exploration and time manipulation.

The character used for the Redmoon cycle is the glyph ⍜.

Core Effects

The impact of the Redmoon cycle depends on your researched Metaphysics upgrades:

Upgrade Required Effect during Redmoon
Numerology +20% Unobtainium output from Lunar Outposts.
Numerology -50% Gigaflop consumption for Entanglement Stations.
Numeromancy Holding a festival provides an additional x2 Unobtainium income.

The “Shatter into Redmoon” Strategy

Because the Redmoon cycle is so much more productive than other cycles, endgame players use Time Crystals to skip less profitable years and land exactly on the Redmoon phase.

  • Timing: The first Redmoon cycle begins at Year 25 and lasts for five years (approximately 66.67 minutes of real-time play).
  • The Shatter Engine: By “shattering” (combusting) Time Crystals in the Chronoforge, players can advance the calendar instantly. It takes 45 skips to get from the end of one Redmoon cycle back to the start of the next one.
  • Maximising Returns: Strategic guides recommend staying in Redmoon as much as possible to fuel the “Type 0 Relic Engine”. When combined with Breweries, the festival bonus in Redmoon can reach nearly 2.5x total production.

Why It Matters for Progression

The Redmoon cycle is the foundation of the self-sustaining positive chrono-reset loop.

  • Unobtainium Accumulation: Players need billions of Unobtainium to build the 70+ Chronospheres required to carry over enough resources to make a reset profitable.
  • Arbitrage: By timing their most intensive production and trading (specifically with the Elders/Leviathans) during Redmoon, players can generate the massive amounts of Unobtainium and Time Crystals needed to reach the Endgame.

item.title: Cath Cycle
item.description:
The Cath cycle is the fifth of ten cycles in the Kittens Game temporal system, following the Helios cycle and preceding the Redmoon cycle. Each cycle lasts for five game years (20,000 ticks), which translates to approximately 1 hour, 6 minutes, and 40 seconds of real-time.

Indicators and Identification

  • Glyph: The cycle is identified by the ⌾ symbol appearing to the left of the year in the calendar.
  • Color Coding: The color of the glyph changes to denote the specific year within the five-year Cath cycle: Red (Year 0), Orange-Yellow (Year 1), Green (Year 2), Blue (Year 3), and Violet (Year 4).

Resource Multipliers (Requires Numerology)

If you have researched the Numerology metaphysics upgrade, the Cath cycle provides specific bonuses and penalties to space-based production:
item.content:encoded:
The Cath cycle is the fifth of ten cycles in the Kittens Game temporal system, following the Helios cycle and preceding the Redmoon cycle. Each cycle lasts for five game years (20,000 ticks), which translates to approximately 1 hour, 6 minutes, and 40 seconds of real-time.

Indicators and Identification

  • Glyph: The cycle is identified by the ⌾ symbol appearing to the left of the year in the calendar.
  • Color Coding: The color of the glyph changes to denote the specific year within the five-year Cath cycle: Red (Year 0), Orange-Yellow (Year 1), Green (Year 2), Blue (Year 3), and Violet (Year 4).

Resource Multipliers (Requires Numerology)

If you have researched the Numerology metaphysics upgrade, the Cath cycle provides specific bonuses and penalties to space-based production:

  • Space Elevators: Provides a +100% bonus to the transferred production bonus, specifically for Oil.
  • Satellites: Provides a +100% bonus to starchart production and a +100% bonus to the Satellite observatory science bonus.
  • Space Stations: Provides a +50% bonus to science production.
  • Space Beacons: Imposes a -50% penalty to starchart production.

Festival Effects (Requires Numeromancy)

When the Numeromancy metaphysics upgrade is researched, holding a Festivals during the Cath cycle grants a unique global modifier:

  • Catpower Boost: All Catpower income is doubled (x2) for the duration of the festival. This effect can be further enhanced by building Breweries.

Strategic Utility

In the late game, players often use the Chronoforge to “shatter” Time Crystals, skipping through less desirable cycles to reach those that benefit their current bottleneck. While Redmoon is often the primary target for Unobtainium farming, the Cath cycle is strategically valuable for players needing to maximize Oil transfer via Space Elevators or those looking to quickly cap Science through boosted Satellites and Space Stations. Additionally, the doubled Catpower income from festivals makes Cath an ideal time for mass trading or hunting.

item.title: Spider Relations
item.description:
Spiders are a friendly trade partner in Kittens Game that players typically encounter in the mid-to-late game. They are a valuable source for acquiring Coal and Oil, which can help resolve industrial bottlenecks when production from Smelters or Geologists is insufficient.

Discovery and Unlock Requirements

Because of their steep requirements, Spiders are considered “waayyyy off” for early-game players. You can discover them by Sending Explorers (costing 1,000 catpower) only once you have achieved the following:
item.content:encoded:
Spiders are a friendly trade partner in Kittens Game that players typically encounter in the mid-to-late game. They are a valuable source for acquiring Coal and Oil, which can help resolve industrial bottlenecks when production from Smelters or Geologists is insufficient.

Discovery and Unlock Requirements

Because of their steep requirements, Spiders are considered “waayyyy off” for early-game players. You can discover them by Sending Explorers (costing 1,000 catpower) only once you have achieved the following:

  • 125,000 Max Science capacity.
  • At least 100 Trade Ships.

Trade Mechanics

The Spiders have a Friendly attitude, which grants a baseline +15% bonus to trade rewards. Their primary trade involves purchasing Scaffolds from you.

Action Resource Base Amount Chance Requirement
They Buy Scaffolds 50 100% N/A
They Sell Coal 350 100% N/A
They Sell Oil 100 25% Embassy Level 5

Seasonal Strategy

Like most trade partners, the Spiders’ resource yields are affected by the current season. To maximise your Coal returns, you should focus your trading during Autumn.

  • Spring: +0% (Standard).
  • Summer: +5% bonus.
  • Autumn: +15% bonus (Optimal for trading).
  • Winter: -5% penalty.

Strategic Utility

While trading Scaffolds for Coal is not always realistic in the early game due to the high cost of Scaffolds, it becomes a viable strategy later on. Spiders are particularly useful for:

  • Automated Coal Gains: They provide an alternative to the Geologist job or Smelter upgrades like the Coal Furnace.
  • Oil Acquisition: For players who have reached the Titanium/Space eras, Spiders offer a way to supplement Oil production alongside Oil Wells and Bio Labs.
  • Diplomacy Synergy: If you have the Diplomacy Metaphysics upgrade, you can further improve your standing and trade efficiency with the Spiders, though they are already friendly by default.

item.title: Seasons
item.description:
In Kittens Game, Seasons are a core cyclical mechanic that dictates the efficiency of your resource production, particularly catnip, and influences the success of trade with other civilisations.

The Seasonal Cycle

Each year consists of four seasons: Spring, Summer, Autumn, and Winter.

  • Duration: Each season lasts 100 days, which equates to 1,000 game ticks or approximately 3 minutes and 20 seconds in real-time.
  • Calendar: The progression of seasons is hidden until you research the Calendar technology (30 Science).

Catnip Production and Survival

The primary impact of seasons is on Catnip Fields, which receive a production boost in Spring and a massive penalty in Winter.
item.content:encoded:
In Kittens Game, Seasons are a core cyclical mechanic that dictates the efficiency of your resource production, particularly catnip, and influences the success of trade with other civilisations.

The Seasonal Cycle

Each year consists of four seasons: Spring, Summer, Autumn, and Winter.

  • Duration: Each season lasts 100 days, which equates to 1,000 game ticks or approximately 3 minutes and 20 seconds in real-time.
  • Calendar: The progression of seasons is hidden until you research the Calendar technology (30 Science).

Catnip Production and Survival

The primary impact of seasons is on Catnip Fields, which receive a production boost in Spring and a massive penalty in Winter.

Season Catnip Multiplier (Average Weather) Impact on Strategy
Spring +50% Best time to expand your population and build up stocks.
Summer +0% Standard production; a good time to focus on non-food resources.
Autumn +0% Focus on accumulating large catnip reserves for the coming cold.
Winter -75% Production nosedives; kittens are at high risk of starvation.

Key Exception: Farmers are vital because their catnip production is not affected by seasonal modifiers. Reallocating kittens to the Farmer job during Winter is a standard survival tactic.

Weather Variations

Starting in Year 4, seasons have a 35% chance to be “abnormal”—either Warm or Cold. This adds a further modifier to your catnip fields:

  • Warm Weather: Provides an additional boost (e.g., Spring becomes +65%).
  • Cold Weather: Makes penalties harsher (e.g., Winter drops to -90%).

The Communism policy makes cold winters even more dangerous by setting catnip field production to -100%.

Seasonal Trade Strategy

Different races offer better deals or different resource amounts depending on the time of year.

  • Spring: The best time to trade with Nagas for Minerals (+25%).
  • Summer: Lizards provide a +35% bonus to Wood.
  • Autumn: Griffins are most efficient, providing +35% Iron.
  • Winter: Sharks are the MVP of Winter, providing a +45% bonus to Catnip, which can be refined into Wood to survive the season.

Advanced Seasonal Mechanics

  • Energy Generation: Solar Farms are more efficient in Summer (+2.67 Energy) than in Winter (+1.5 Energy).
  • Space Production: Once Numerology is researched, different years in a 10-year Cycle (like Redmoon or Helios) provide additional multipliers to space resources.
  • “Winter Has Come” Challenge: This challenge forces the game into a permanent, endless Winter, requiring players to rely entirely on Farmers for food.

item.title: Shark_relations
item.description:
In Kittens Game, Shark Relations refers to the trade mechanics and specialized policies associated with the Sharks, a neutral trade race discovered in the early-to-mid game. They are primarily used to acquire Catnip and cultural resources like Parchment and Manuscripts in exchange for Iron.

Trade Mechanics

Sharks are discovered around Year 20 (or Year 1 if you have the Diplomacy metaphysics upgrade). Their attitude is Neutral, meaning they provide no baseline bonus or penalty to trade.
item.content:encoded:
In Kittens Game, Shark Relations refers to the trade mechanics and specialized policies associated with the Sharks, a neutral trade race discovered in the early-to-mid game. They are primarily used to acquire Catnip and cultural resources like Parchment and Manuscripts in exchange for Iron.

Trade Mechanics

Sharks are discovered around Year 20 (or Year 1 if you have the Diplomacy metaphysics upgrade). Their attitude is Neutral, meaning they provide no baseline bonus or penalty to trade.

  • Primary Trade: You give 100 Iron; they give Catnip.
  • Secondary Gains: Successful trades have a chance to yield Parchment (25%), Manuscripts (15%), and Compendiums (10%).
  • Seasonal Bonus: They are most effective in Winter, providing a +45% bonus to catnip rewards.
  • Iron Will Strategy: In a “Black Sky” challenge, Sharks trade iron for Science instead of catnip.

Shark Relations Policies

Once you reach Shark Embassy Level 20 and possess the Diplomacy metaphysics upgrade, you can enact one of three mutually exclusive policies. Choosing one locks out the other two for that run.

Policy Effect Best Use Case
Scribes +25% Parchment chance, +15% Manuscript chance; +50% Iron cost per trade. Accelerating science when you have a massive surplus of Iron.
Merchants +3% Trade Ratio (scales up to +30% based on total trades completed). Long-term scaling of all trade rewards.
Botanists -75% Bio Lab energy, +1% Brewery catpower bonus, +25% Wood crafting bonus. Managing energy deficits or boosting late-game wood production.

Strategic Synergies

The Sharks are a core component of the “Winter Trade Loop,” which players use to bypass resource bottlenecks.

  1. The Loop: In Winter, trade Iron to the Sharks for massive amounts of Catnip. Refine that catnip into Wood, then trade the wood to the Griffins for Iron.
  2. Culture Grind: In challenges like Pacifism, where hunting for furs (to make parchment) is disabled, Sharks are the primary source of early cultural resources. Investing in Shark Embassies speeds up manuscript gains significantly.
  3. Pollution Mitigation: While not a direct trade benefit, the Lizard Relations: Ecologists policy reduces pollution, which helps preserve the high catnip production levels that the Sharks can supplement.

Hostility and Standing

While the Sharks are neutral, other races like the Griffins and Zebras are hostile. Using Tradeposts and the Caravanserai upgrade improves your standing with all races, but the Sharks’ neutral starting point makes them a reliable trade partner even before these upgrades are maxed out.

item.title: Technocracy vs Order of the Stars vs Cosmological Libertarianism
item.description:
Technocracy, Order of the Stars, and Cosmological Libertarianism are mutually exclusive high-tier government Policy/ unlocked in the Science tab once you reach Dune. Each costs 150,000 Culture and forces you to choose between prioritising science capacity, faith production, or the generation of the critical late-game resource, unobtainium.

Comparison of Dune-Tier Policy/

Policy Effect Key Prerequisite Strategic Focus
Cosmological Libertarianism +15% Unobtainium production Reach Dune General progression and overcoming the unobtainium bottleneck.
Order of the Stars +20% Faith production; leaders must be [Priests] ( /job/priest/) Reach Dune + assigned Priest leader Religious-focused runs and grinding Transcendence tiers.
Technocracy +20% Science cap Reach Dune Reaching massive science thresholds for high-tier technologies.

Strategic Deep Dive

1. Cosmological Libertarianism (The “Meta” Choice)

This is widely considered the strongest option for most players.
item.content:encoded:
Technocracy, Order of the Stars, and Cosmological Libertarianism are mutually exclusive high-tier government Policy/ unlocked in the Science tab once you reach Dune. Each costs 150,000 Culture and forces you to choose between prioritising science capacity, faith production, or the generation of the critical late-game resource, unobtainium.

Comparison of Dune-Tier Policy/

Policy Effect Key Prerequisite Strategic Focus
Cosmological Libertarianism +15% Unobtainium production Reach Dune General progression and overcoming the unobtainium bottleneck.
Order of the Stars +20% Faith production; leaders must be [Priests] ( /job/priest/) Reach Dune + assigned Priest leader Religious-focused runs and grinding Transcendence tiers.
Technocracy +20% Science cap Reach Dune Reaching massive science thresholds for high-tier technologies.

Strategic Deep Dive

1. Cosmological Libertarianism (The “Meta” Choice)

This is widely considered the strongest option for most players.

  • Unobtainium is King: Unobtainium is the primary bottleneck for advanced space missions and time manipulation. A 15% boost to its production is significant because few other modifiers affect it directly.
  • Efficiency: Strategic guides recommend this over the others because “you REALLY need more unob” to progress through Phase 4 and establish a positive reset loop.

2. Order of the Stars (The Religious Choice)

This policy shifts your government’s focus to the heavens and the Order of the Sun.

  • Faith Grinding: It is most useful during long runs where your primary goal is increasing your epiphany and religion bonuses.
  • Leader Restriction: Note that while it provides a 20% faith boost, it mandates that only [Priests] ( /job/priest/) can be assigned as leaders. However, the policy bonus itself still functions even if you do not have an active leader assigned.

3. Technocracy (The Niche Choice)

Technocracy provides a flat 20% increase to your Science storage capacity.

  • Redundancy: Strategy guides often label Technocracy as unnecessary because players have numerous other options to expand science storage—such as Compendiums, Observatories, and Data Centers—making a policy slot for science cap a lower priority.
  • Specific Utility: It is only truly beneficial if you are struggling to hit a specific, massive science threshold for a high-tier technology that other storage buildings cannot reach.

Choosing the Right Path

Because these Policy/ are mutually exclusive, selecting one will permanently lock the other two for the remainder of your current run.

  • For most runs: Choose Cosmological Libertarianism to speed up the acquisition of time crystals and eludium.
  • For deep-endgame/40k runs: You might consider Order of the Stars if your unobtainium production is already self-sustaining and you wish to focus purely on religious scaling.

Do you have a specific goal for your current run, such as farming Paragon or pushing for the 40k achievement? This could help determine which of these three would serve you best right now.

item.title: Megalomania
item.description:
Megalomania is a mid-game Metaphysics upgrade that serves as the essential gateway to advanced religious structures and the “Unicorn Era”. It costs 10 Paragon to purchase.

Unlocks and Benefits

By purchasing Megalomania, you gain access to high-tier structures and mechanics that are otherwise hidden:

  • Black Pyramids: These are necessary to attract Leviathans, allowing you to trade Unobtainium for Time Crystals and Relics.
  • Markers: These strange structures initiate the corruption process, which slowly transforms Alicorns into Necrocorns.
  • Black Codex: Unlocks further religious upgrades, such as the Unicorn Graveyard, which boosts your maximum culture based on the number of Ziggurats you possess.

Acquisition Requirements

To unlock Megalomania in the Metaphysics menu, you must meet the following criteria:
item.content:encoded:
Megalomania is a mid-game Metaphysics upgrade that serves as the essential gateway to advanced religious structures and the “Unicorn Era”. It costs 10 Paragon to purchase.

Unlocks and Benefits

By purchasing Megalomania, you gain access to high-tier structures and mechanics that are otherwise hidden:

  • Black Pyramids: These are necessary to attract Leviathans, allowing you to trade Unobtainium for Time Crystals and Relics.
  • Markers: These strange structures initiate the corruption process, which slowly transforms Alicorns into Necrocorns.
  • Black Codex: Unlocks further religious upgrades, such as the Unicorn Graveyard, which boosts your maximum culture based on the number of Ziggurats you possess.

Acquisition Requirements

To unlock Megalomania in the Metaphysics menu, you must meet the following criteria:

  • Science Tech: Research the Metaphysics technology (55k Science and 5 Unobtainium).
  • Metaphysics Prerequisite: You must first purchase Enlightenment (formerly Engineering) for 5 Paragon.

Strategic Timing: When to Buy

While its cost is relatively low, strategic guides offer specific warnings regarding when to invest your Paragon:

  • The “Early Game Trap”: Megalomania is often considered a trap for new players. Because the structures it unlocks (like Black Pyramids) are “really expensive” and belong to the endgame resource line, it is not recommended for your first few runs.
  • Priority Order: You should prioritise all price ratio reduction upgrades—specifically Golden Ratio, Divine Proportion, and Renaissance—before buying Megalomania.
  • The 40k Run Exception: If you are attempting a very long run (such as the 40k years milestone), Megalomania is considered necessary to begin working toward Time Crystals as early as possible.

Role in the Unicorn Era

Megalomania is the catalyst for transitioning from simple unicorn gathering to a full Time Crystal engine. Once purchased, you can refine Unicorn Tears into Black Liquid Sorrow (BLS); five units of BLS allow you to build your first Black Pyramid, which officially begins the process of trading with Leviathans for the temporal resources we discussed previously, such as Anachronomancy and Chronospheres.

item.title: Ivory
item.description:
Ivory is a rare luxury resource in Kittens Game that is primarily used to increase colony happiness and facilitate progression through the religious “Unicorn Era”. Unlike standard building materials, ivory is a consumable resource; as long as you have it in your inventory, it provides a +10% happiness bonus to your kittens, which in turn boosts their overall production efficiency.

How to Obtain Ivory

There are three primary ways to accumulate ivory throughout the different phases of the game:
item.content:encoded:
Ivory is a rare luxury resource in Kittens Game that is primarily used to increase colony happiness and facilitate progression through the religious “Unicorn Era”. Unlike standard building materials, ivory is a consumable resource; as long as you have it in your inventory, it provides a +10% happiness bonus to your kittens, which in turn boosts their overall production efficiency.

How to Obtain Ivory

There are three primary ways to accumulate ivory throughout the different phases of the game:

  • Hunting: Once you research Archery, you can send kittens to hunt using 100 catpower. Each hunt has a (44 + 2* hunting bonus)% chance to yield ivory. Researching workshop upgrades like Bolas, Hunting Armour, and Nanosuits increases the amount of ivory retrieved per hunt.
  • Mints: These industrial buildings provide a way to automate ivory production. When active, a Mint consumes catpower and gold to produce ivory at a rate of 0.0021% of your maximum catpower per tick.
  • Ivory Meteors: In the late game, building Ivory Citadels enables a random astronomical event called an “Ivory Meteor”. These events have a 0.05% chance of occurring per game-day for each citadel and provide a bulk amount of ivory. This is considered an excellent “AFK” source of the resource.

Strategic Uses

Ivory is essential for both trade and advanced religious development:

  • The Unicorn Era: Ivory is a core requirement for almost all advanced unicorn-related buildings in the Religion tab. This includes Ivory Towers (25k), Sky Palaces (125k), and Sunspires (750k), which are necessary to summon alicorns and generate Time Crystals.
  • Trading with Nagas: The Nagas are a neutral trade partner that buys ivory in exchange for minerals, slabs, and concrete. This trade is a critical mechanism for bypassing mineral bottlenecks, especially in Iron Will mode.
  • Happiness Buffs: Since ivory is a rare resource, its presence directly influences kitten morale. This effect can be enhanced by the Epicurianism policy, which increases the happiness bonus to 11%.

Management and Policy/

Because ivory degrades over time and is consumed by your kittens, managing its supply is important to maintain production bonuses.

  • Stoicism: This policy halves the consumption rate of ivory, helping your hoard last longer.
  • Frugality: This policy increases the resource output of your Mints by 10%.
  • Religious Boosts: Buildings like Sky Palace , , Unicorn Utopia , and Sunspire provide percentage-based increases to the amount of ivory you gain from Ivory Meteors.

item.title: Golden Ratio
item.description:
Golden Ratio is an early-to-mid-game Metaphysics upgrade that reduces the price ratio of buildings on the Bonfire tab. By slowing down how quickly construction costs increase, it allows you to build significantly more structures before hitting your resource caps, which directly boosts your production and maximum kitten population.

Acquisition and Prerequisites

  • Paragon Cost: 50 Paragon.
  • Prerequisite: You must first purchase the Enlightenment metaphysics upgrade (5 Paragon).
  • Unlocks: Purchasing Golden Ratio is required to unlock Divine Proportion (100 Paragon).

Core Effects

  • Price Reduction: It reduces all price ratios by approximately 1.618%.
  • Mathematical Basis: The exact percentage reduction is derived from the mathematical golden ratio: $\frac{1+\sqrt{5}}{2}$.
  • Scope: Note that this price ratio reduction only applies to buildings found in the Bonfire tab; it does not affect space structures or other categories.

Strategic Utility

The Golden Ratio is considered a “price reduction meta” and is a cornerstone of efficient progression.

Strategic Utility

The Golden Ratio is considered a “price reduction meta” and is a cornerstone of efficient progression.

  • Optimal Purchase Timing: Strategic guides generally recommend purchasing Golden Ratio during your second run.
  • Kitten Threshold: It is often advised to wait until you have accumulated between 155 and 160 kittens before buying it. This timing allows you to benefit from the production and storage bonuses of your unspent Paragon for the majority of the run before spending the 50 points on the upgrade.
  • Scaling Production: Because it allows for more buildings (such as Huts and Log Houses), it facilitates a higher kitten population, which in turn leads to more Paragon and Karma upon your next reset.
  • Late-Game Path: In long-term or “Endgame” strategies, Golden Ratio is the first major step toward the Renaissance upgrade, which is the final and most powerful price-reduction tier.

Would you like to know more about the next upgrade in this chain, Divine Proportion, or how these ratios interact with your kitten population for a reset?

item.title: Carnivale
item.description: Policy: Carnivale Distinct from the Metaphysics upgrade, the Carnivale policy is an environmental and philosophical choice found in the Science tab. • Cost: 3500 Culture. • Prerequisites: You must have the Epicureanism policy active. Enacting Carnivale will permanently lock you out of the Extravagance policy for that run. • Effects: ◦ +30% Festival Growth Rate: Kittens arrive significantly faster while a festival is active. ◦ +30% Luxury Consumption: Rare resources (furs, ivory, spice) are consumed 30% faster during festivals. Strategic Utility and Synergies • Early Game: Both the upgrade and the policy are generally considered unnecessary for your first few runs. At this stage, the resource cost for festivals is often too high to justify the bonuses. • Mid-to-Late Game: Once your economy can support constant festivals, the Carnivals Metaphysics upgrade becomes very high-value for idling, as you can queue up many years of festivals at once. • Brewery Synergy: The effectiveness of festivals (and thus the value of Carnivals/Carnivale) is increased by building Breweries. These buildings provide bonuses to festival happiness (+1%), cycle bonuses (+1%), and kitten arrival speed (+0.1%). • Kitten Grinding: If your current goal is Paragon farming, the combination of the Carnivale policy and several Breweries can significantly decrease the time it takes to reach your population cap.

item.title: Burn your paragon
item.description:
Burning paragon is a mechanic that converts your standard unspent paragon into “burned” paragon. While burned paragon is less effective than regular paragon for production in the early game, it provides unique stacking bonuses and becomes significantly more powerful during the late-game “Dark Future” period.

Core Effects of Burned Paragon

  • Production Bonus: Burned paragon has approximately half the production effectiveness of regular paragon. However, it stacks with regular paragon, allowing you to bypass the diminishing returns that standard paragon faces after the 150–200 point threshold.
  • Storage Capacity:
    • Before Dark Future (Year 40,000): Each burned paragon provides a 0.05% storage capacity bonus (half of regular paragon’s 0.1%).
    • During Dark Future: Each burned paragon provides a 0.2% storage capacity bonus, making it twice as effective as regular paragon for increasing resource caps.
  • Leader Trait Bonus: Having burned paragon provides a slight boost to the effects of your kitten leader’s traits (such as Scientist, Artisan, or Manager).
  • Persistence: Like regular paragon, burned paragon is a permanent resource that carries over through all resets.

Strategic Timing: When to Burn

Deciding when to burn your stash depends on your current progression:

  • Storage Capacity:

    • During Dark Future: Each burned paragon provides a 0.2% storage capacity bonus, making it twice as effective as regular paragon for increasing resource caps.
  • Leader Trait Bonus: Having burned paragon provides a slight boost to the effects of your kitten leader’s traits (such as Scientist, Artisan, or Manager).
  • Persistence: Like regular paragon, burned paragon is a permanent resource that carries over through all resets.

Strategic Timing: When to Burn

Deciding when to burn your stash depends on your current progression:

  • The 400-Point Threshold: A common strategy is to consider burning paragon once you reach 400 unspent points. At this stage, 400 burned paragon provides roughly the same production boost as 200 regular paragon, but because it stacks, it helps push production higher as standard paragon gains become marginal.
  • Storage Caps: Because burned paragon storage bonuses never diminish, they are essential in the late game for reaching the massive unobtainium caps (e.g., 8.14 billion) required for self-sustaining resets with 100 Chronospheres.
  • Preparation for Iron Will: For players attempting the “Insane” Space Oddity achievement, you must have less than 10 unburned paragon in your bank. Burning your paragon allows you to keep the production and storage benefits of your prestige without disqualifying yourself from the achievement.

Important Considerations

  • Wait for Metaphysics: It is generally recommended to prioritize purchasing price ratio reduction Metaphysics (like Golden Ratio, Divine Proportion, and Renaissance) before burning paragon.
  • Dark Future Milestone: Since the storage bonus quadruples during the Dark Future, burning paragon is a primary strategy for players planning “Endless Runs” or deep-space exploration.
  • Gold Star Space Oddity: Obtaining the Space Oddity gold star reward provides a permanent benefit: it allows you to burn paragon in the future without exiting Iron Will mode.

item.title: Adjustment Bureau
item.description:
The Adjustment Bureau is a low-cost Metaphysics upgrade that serves as the gateway to the Challenges system in Kittens Game. Once purchased, it unlocks a dedicated Challenges tab (separate from the Science tab), where you can activate specific game-altering restrictions in exchange for permanent global rewards.

Costs and Unlocks

  • Cost: 5 Paragon.
  • Unlocks: The Challenges menu and the secret ASCOH upgrade.
  • Prerequisites: You must first research the Metaphysics technology (which requires 55,000 Science and 5 Unobtainium) to access the Metaphysics purchase menu.

How Challenges Work

Challenges impose special handicaps that typically require a game reset to begin. When a challenge is active, Chronospheres will not bring resources into the run (unless it is the Post-Apocalypse challenge); instead, those resources are placed in reserves and can be reclaimed once the challenge is complete.

The Adjustment Bureau is a low-cost Metaphysics upgrade that serves as the gateway to the Challenges system in Kittens Game. Once purchased, it unlocks a dedicated Challenges tab (separate from the Science tab), where you can activate specific game-altering restrictions in exchange for permanent global rewards.

Costs and Unlocks

  • Cost: 5 Paragon.
  • Unlocks: The Challenges menu and the secret ASCOH upgrade.
  • Prerequisites: You must first research the Metaphysics technology (which requires 55,000 Science and 5 Unobtainium) to access the Metaphysics purchase menu.

How Challenges Work

Challenges impose special handicaps that typically require a game reset to begin. When a challenge is active, Chronospheres will not bring resources into the run (unless it is the Post-Apocalypse challenge); instead, those resources are placed in reserves and can be reclaimed once the challenge is complete.

  • Rewards: Completing a challenge for the first time grants both a Base Reward and an Increasing Reward. Multiple challenges can be active simultaneously, and rewards for repeated completions stack.
  • Examples: Common challenges include Winter Has Come (endless winter), Anarchy (lazy kittens), and Atheism (no faith bonus).

Strategic Advice

  • Timing: Strategic guides suggest that you are generally not ready for the Adjustment Bureau and its challenges until you reach Phase 2 (mid-game). It is usually better to prioritise price ratio reduction upgrades (like Golden Ratio or Renaissance) before attempting challenge runs.
  • Iron Will Exception: You do not need to purchase the Adjustment Bureau to play in Iron Will mode. Iron Will is a “hidden” challenge that is triggered simply by resetting and playing without building any kitten housing.

item.title: Carnivals
item.description: a mid-game Metaphysics upgrade that allows festivals to stack in duration, though there is also a similarly named Carnivale policy that modifies festival effects. Metaphysics: Carnivals The Carnivals upgrade is an essential step in the temporal and religious Metaphysics tree. • Cost: 25 Paragon. • Primary Effect: It allows your Festivals to stack in duration. Without this, clicking “Hold a Festival” while one is already active simply wastes resources; with Carnivals, the time is added to the remaining duration. • Progression: It is the direct prerequisite for Numerology. It is also considered a mandatory part of the path to Order of the Void and reaching high Transcendence Tiers in the late game.

item.title: Anachronomancy
item.description:
Anachronomancy is a pivotal mid-game Metaphysics upgrade that allows your civilisation to preserve its most advanced temporal assets across resets.

It is considered a mandatory requirement before a player begins focusing seriously on Time Crystals or deep-space exploration.

Costs and Prerequisites

  • Paragon Cost: 125.
  • Unlock Prerequisite: You must first purchase the Chronomancy metaphysics upgrade.
  • Technology Prerequisite: You must have researched the Metaphysics technology (which requires 5 unobtainium) to access the purchase menu.

Core Effects

item.content:encoded:
Anachronomancy is a pivotal mid-game Metaphysics upgrade that allows your civilisation to preserve its most advanced temporal assets across resets.

It is considered a mandatory requirement before a player begins focusing seriously on Time Crystals or deep-space exploration.

Costs and Prerequisites

  • Paragon Cost: 125.
  • Unlock Prerequisite: You must first purchase the Chronomancy metaphysics upgrade.
  • Technology Prerequisite: You must have researched the Metaphysics technology (which requires 5 unobtainium) to access the purchase menu.

Core Effects

The primary function of Anachronomancy is to change the rules of what carries over when you reset your game:

  • Time Crystal Preservation: Your stockpile of Time Crystals is saved. Without this upgrade, all Time Crystals are lost upon reset.
  • Chronophysics Persistence: The Chronophysics technology is saved across resets. Once you have both Anachronomancy and have researched Chronophysics once, you will start every future run with that technology already researched.

Strategic Importance

Anachronomancy is the gateway to the “Mid-Game” and the Relic/Time Crystal economy.

  1. Enabling Chronospheres: Since Chronophysics is the prerequisite for building Chronospheres, having it available at the start of a run allows you to begin using temporal mechanics much earlier in your progression.
  2. Unicorn Era Progression: It is essential for the “Unicorn Era,” where players sacrifice unicorns and alicorns to generate Time Crystals. Anachronomancy ensures that this effort isn’t wasted when you decide to reset for more Paragon.
  3. Efficiency Milestone: Strategic guides typically suggest purchasing Anachronomancy after you have secured primary price-reduction upgrades like Renaissance. It allows you to “experiment with time crystals” without the risk of losing your investment.

Summary of Carry-Over Mechanics

Resource/Tech Without Anachronomancy With Anachronomancy
Time Crystals Lost Saved
Chronophysics Must be re-researched Saved/Auto-Researched
Temporal Flux Saved Saved
Chronosphere Resources Depends on CS count Depends on CS count

Would you like to know more about how to best use the Time Crystals that Anachronomancy helps you save?

item.title: Unicornmancy
item.description:
Unicornmancy is a mid-to-late-game Metaphysics upgrade that increases the frequency of rare unicorn-related astronomical events. It is a critical component for players entering the “Unicorn Era”, as it accelerates the acquisition of Unicorns and Ivory, which are the foundational resources for generating Time Crystals and Relics.

Acquisition and Cost

To access Unicornmancy, you must first research the Metaphysics technology (requiring 5 Unobtainium) to unlock the Metaphysics purchase menu.

  • Paragon Cost: 125 Paragon.
  • Strategic Timing: Sources recommend purchasing Unicornmancy once you have secured your primary price-reduction upgrades (up to Renaissance) and are ready to begin serious progression into time manipulation.

Primary Effects

The upgrade provides a 10% increase to the daily chance of the following phenomena:
item.content:encoded:
Unicornmancy is a mid-to-late-game Metaphysics upgrade that increases the frequency of rare unicorn-related astronomical events. It is a critical component for players entering the “Unicorn Era”, as it accelerates the acquisition of Unicorns and Ivory, which are the foundational resources for generating Time Crystals and Relics.

Acquisition and Cost

To access Unicornmancy, you must first research the Metaphysics technology (requiring 5 Unobtainium) to unlock the Metaphysics purchase menu.

  • Paragon Cost: 125 Paragon.
  • Strategic Timing: Sources recommend purchasing Unicornmancy once you have secured your primary price-reduction upgrades (up to Renaissance) and are ready to begin serious progression into time manipulation.

Primary Effects

The upgrade provides a 10% increase to the daily chance of the following phenomena:

  • Unicorn Rifts: Random events enabled by Ivory Towers that grant a bulk amount of unicorns.
  • Ivory Meteors: Random events enabled by Ivory Citadels that provide a burst of ivory.

Synergies and Scaling

The benefits of Unicornmancy can be significantly amplified by late-game infrastructure:

  • Blazars: Each level of this Cryptotheology building improves the effectiveness of Unicornmancy by 2.5%.
  • Ivory Infrastructure: Because the frequency of Rifts and Ivory Meteors is fundamentally tied to the number of Ivory Towers and Ivory Citadels you possess, Unicornmancy becomes exponentially more valuable as your religious infrastructure grows.
  • Solar Revolution: While Unicornmancy increases the frequency of events, the Solar Revolution bonus is one of the only multipliers that boosts the actual production of unicorn resources.

Strategic Importance

In the late game, Ivory often becomes a major bottleneck because its production does not benefit from standard paragon or building bonuses. By increasing the frequency of Ivory Meteors, Unicornmancy provides a necessary “AFK” source of ivory. This allows you to build the vast numbers of Ziggurats required to refine Unicorn Tears and eventually trade with Leviathans for the resources needed to reach the “Infinity” stage of the game.

item.title: Astromancy
item.description:
In Kittens Game, Astromancy is an early-to-midgame Metaphysics upgrade that drastically accelerates astronomical events and early-game Starchart generation.

1. Cost and Prerequisites

  • Cost: 50 Paragon.
  • Prerequisite: Chronomancy (25 Paragon).

2. Core Effects

Astromancy doubles both the frequency and the automated success rate of astronomical events:

  • Doubles Astronomical Event Chance: Multiplies your base astronomical event chance and the event chance added by Observatories by 2\times\).
  • Doubles Observatory Effectiveness: Multiplies the automatic event observation chance provided by Observatories by 2\times\) (from +1% per Observatory up to +2% per Observatory).
  • (Note: It affects event chances and auto-observation rates, but does not double the science bonus or science cap of Observatories).

3. Strategic Impact

  • Reaching 100% Auto-Observation Faster: Normally, each Observatory adds +1% chance to automatically observe an event without manual clicking, requiring 100 Observatories to guarantee success. With Astromancy, each Observatory gives +2%, cutting the requirement down to only 50 Observatories before you achieve 100% automated success (prior to unlocking SETI).
  • Breaking the Starchart Bottleneck: In early space runs and resets, Starcharts are one of the most punishing bottlenecks needed to craft Trade Ships, unlock Geodesy, and fund early rocket launches. Pairing Chronomancy (+10% daily chance) with Astromancy 2 times chance) more than doubles your incoming Starcharts early in a run.
  • When to Buy: Community guides typically recommend purchasing Astromancy around your 3rd or 4th run (often alongside or shortly after Golden Ratio and Divine Proportion), right as you are preparing to push through early space missions and build up large Trade Ship fleets.

item.title: Chronomancy
item.description:
Chronomancy is a mid-game Metaphysics upgrade that serves as a vital bridge toward advanced temporal and astronomical technologies. It costs 25 Paragon to purchase and is primarily used to increase the frequency of celestial phenomena.

Core Effects and Unlocks

  • Event Multiplier: It provides a 1.1x multiplier to the daily chance of both meteors and astronomical events. The sources explicitly note that this is a multiplicative bonus to the base chance, not a flat +10% addition.
  • Technological Prerequisites: Purchasing Chronomancy is required to unlock two essential high-tier Metaphysics:
    • Anachronomancy: Allows Time Crystals and Chronophysics to persist across game resets.
    • Astromancy: Further doubles the chance of star events and increases the effectiveness of Observatories.

Strategic Utility

The value of Chronomancy depends on your current stage of progression:

Core Effects and Unlocks

  • Event Multiplier: It provides a 1.1x multiplier to the daily chance of both meteors and astronomical events. The sources explicitly note that this is a multiplicative bonus to the base chance, not a flat +10% addition.

Strategic Utility

The value of Chronomancy depends on your current stage of progression:

  • The Starchart Solution: In early runs where Starchart production is a bottleneck, the combination of Chronomancy and Astromancy is described as “pure magic”. It more than doubles event frequency, allowing you to build a larger fleet of Trade Ships for Titanium acquisition.
  • Late-Game Priority: In very advanced “Endgame” or “Iron Will” runs, some strategies suggest prioritising price-ratio reductions (like Renaissance) first, treating Chronomancy as a “less vital” upgrade to be picked up once your economic foundation is stable.

Advanced Synergies

The effectiveness of the Chronomancy bonus can be further amplified through late-game structures and upgrades:

  • Temporal Accelerators: These items in the Time tab improve Chronomancy’s time-related effects by 1.25%.
  • Blazars: As a Cryptotheology building, each Blazar improves Chronomancy effectiveness by 2.5%.
  • Observatory Integration: Within the Bonfire tab, Chronomancy is listed as an upgrade for the Observatory, specifically increasing the Astronomical Event Chance by the 1.1x multiplier.

item.title: Diplomacy
item.description:
Diplomacy is a low-cost entry-level Metaphysics upgrade that significantly accelerates your early-game trade and exploration by allowing you to discover other civilisations much sooner. It is widely considered one of the essential first purchases when you begin spending Paragon.

Core Effects and Costs

The basic Diplomacy upgrade costs 5 Paragon and provides the following immediate benefits:

  • Earlier Discovery: Civilisations can be discovered starting at Year 1 instead of the default Year 5.
  • Improved Relations: Your starting standing ratio with discovered races is increased by 10, meaning they are less likely to be hostile.
  • Hostility Mitigation: It reduces the number of Tradeposts required to negate Zebra hostility from 85 down to 58.

The Diplomacy Metaphysics Tree

Buying Diplomacy opens a progression path primarily focused on the specialised Iron Will mode and advanced navigation:

  • Improved Relations: Your starting standing ratio with discovered races is increased by 10, meaning they are less likely to be hostile.
  • Hostility Mitigation: It reduces the number of Tradeposts required to negate Zebra hostility from 85 down to 58.

The Diplomacy Metaphysics Tree

Buying Diplomacy opens a progression path primarily focused on the specialised Iron Will mode and advanced navigation:

Upgrade Cost (Paragon) Key Effect
Diplomacy 5 Discover races at Year 1; +10 standing ratio.
Zebra Diplomacy 35 10% of your Zebra cap stays when ending Iron Will mode.
Zebra Covenant 75 50% of your Zebra cap stays when ending Iron Will mode.
Navigation Diplomacy 300 Allows civilisation discovery as soon as you have Trade Ships.

Strategic Advice

  • Priority Purchase: Strategic guides recommend purchasing Diplomacy on your second run, alongside price-reduction upgrades like Golden Ratio.
  • The “Zebra Trap”: While Diplomacy itself is vital, the subsequent upgrades (Zebra Diplomacy and Zebra Covenant) are often described as traps for newer players. Keeping a small number of Zebras when transitioning out of Iron Will mode provides very little benefit for the high Paragon cost.
  • Starchart Synergy: By discovering races earlier and mitigating hostility faster, you can build a larger fleet of Trade Ships more efficiently, which helps overcome the mid-game Titanium bottleneck.

If you are currently on your first or second run, focusing on Diplomacy and the price ratio reduction upgrades (Enlightenment, Golden Ratio) will provide the most significant boost to your village’s growth.

item.title: Enlightenment
item.description:
Enlightenment is an entry-level Metaphysics upgrade that provides a permanent global reduction in building costs on the Bonfire tab., It is considered a foundational purchase because it slows the rate at which building prices increase, allowing you to build more structures before hitting resource caps.

Costs and Unlocks

  • Cost: 5 Paragon.
  • Unlocks: Purchasing Enlightenment is a prerequisite for several critical branches of the Metaphysics tree:
    • Price Reduction: Unlocks Golden Ratio.
    • Religious/Unicorn Mechanics: Unlocks Megalomania.,
    • Crafting: Unlocks Codex Vox.

Core Effects

  • Price Ratio Reduction: It reduces all building price ratios by 1%.
  • Persistent Bonus: Like all Metaphysics upgrades, Enlightenment is permanent and carries over through game resets, though the “Metaphysics” technology itself must be re-researched in each new run to access the menu.,

Strategic Timing

Strategic guides emphasize that Enlightenment is one of the essential first purchases when you begin spending your Paragon:

item.title: Orbital Array
item.description:
An Orbital Array is a high-tier space structure in the Cath solar system that provides a 2% bonus to all space structures. While powerful, it is an energy-intensive building, consuming 20 Watts of power per unit.

Construction Requirements

To build an Orbital Array, you must have unlocked the Piscine mission. The base resource costs are substantial:

  • Science: 250,000
  • Eludium: 100
  • Kerosene: 500
  • Starchart: 2,000
  • Price Ratio: 1.15

Strategic Synergies and Scaling

The primary utility of the Orbital Array is scaling late-game resource production, particularly Unobtainium from Lunar Outposts. Its effectiveness is significantly amplified by the following:

  • Starchart: 2,000
  • Price Ratio: 1.15

Strategic Synergies and Scaling

The primary utility of the Orbital Array is scaling late-game resource production, particularly Unobtainium from Lunar Outposts. Its effectiveness is significantly amplified by the following:

  • Space Manufacturing: Once this workshop upgrade is researched, Factories provide a bonus to the effectiveness of Orbital Arrays. The bonus is calculated as 3.75% per factory (or 4.5% with the Factory Logistics upgrade).
  • Production Formula: The global space production bonus is calculated using the number of Space Elevators and Orbital Arrays, meaning they work together to exponentially increase output from structures like Planet Crackers and Lunar Outposts.

Efficiency and Profitability Analysis

In endgame strategy, players often debate whether Orbital Arrays are worth the high Eludium cost during short runs:

  • Short Runs vs. Long Runs: In runs shorter than 30 to 60 minutes, most strategic guides suggest ignoring Orbital Arrays and Moon Bases, instead prioritizing Space Elevators because they are more cost-effective.
  • The Eludium Bottleneck: Because Eludium is a crafted resource, its cost effectively consumes 1,000 Unobtainium per unit (modified by craft ratio). Consequently, an array is only considered profitable if the remaining time in the run allows it to generate more Unobtainium than was spent on its construction.
  • Break-even Calculation: To determine if an array is “worth it,” players can calculate their OF (Outposts multiplied by Factories) and compare the projected Unobtainium gain against the cost of the next array level.

Role in the “Path to Infinity”

During the final “Phase 4” of development—aimed at achieving a self-sustaining reset loop—Orbital Arrays are essential for maximizing the Unobtainium generation rate. This rate is critical for trading with Leviathans for Time Crystals and Relics, which eventually allow the player to bypass traditional resource mining altogether.

item.title: Unobtainium
item.description:
Unobtainium is a rare, high-tier resource that marks the transition into the late game (Phase 4). It is primarily refined from uranium and is essential for space exploration, time manipulation, and advanced engineering.

Production and Acquisition

Unobtainium is generated using Lunar Outposts on Redmoon, which convert 1.75 uranium into 0.035 unobtainium per second. Production can be significantly enhanced through several methods:

  • Global Multipliers: Productivity is boosted by Space Elevators (+1%), Orbital Arrays (+2%), and the Cosmological Libertarianism policy (+15%).
  • Space Manufacturing: This workshop upgrade allows Factories to improve the effectiveness of Space Elevators and Orbital Arrays, further scaling output.
  • Celestial Cycles: During the Redmoon cycle, unobtainium output increases by 20%. If Numeromancy is researched, holding a festival during this cycle provides a 2x multiplier to unobtainium income. Conversely, the Charon cycle imposes a 10% production penalty.

Storage and Capacity

Managing unobtainium storage is a major bottleneck in late-game progression. The base capacity is 150 units, which must be expanded to reach milestones like the “Eludium Era”.
item.content:encoded:
Unobtainium is a rare, high-tier resource that marks the transition into the late game (Phase 4). It is primarily refined from uranium and is essential for space exploration, time manipulation, and advanced engineering.

Production and Acquisition

Unobtainium is generated using Lunar Outposts on Redmoon, which convert 1.75 uranium into 0.035 unobtainium per second. Production can be significantly enhanced through several methods:

  • Global Multipliers: Productivity is boosted by Space Elevators (+1%), Orbital Arrays (+2%), and the Cosmological Libertarianism policy (+15%).
  • Space Manufacturing: This workshop upgrade allows Factories to improve the effectiveness of Space Elevators and Orbital Arrays, further scaling output.
  • Celestial Cycles: During the Redmoon cycle, unobtainium output increases by 20%. If Numeromancy is researched, holding a festival during this cycle provides a 2x multiplier to unobtainium income. Conversely, the Charon cycle imposes a 10% production penalty.

Storage and Capacity

Managing unobtainium storage is a major bottleneck in late-game progression. The base capacity is 150 units, which must be expanded to reach milestones like the “Eludium Era”.

  • Storage Buildings: Moon Bases provide +150 capacity, while Cryostations (located on Terminus) provide a much larger +750 capacity.
  • Storage Enhancements: Capacity is further boosted by Paragon (0.1% per point), AI Bases (+10% per AI Core), Sunforges (+1% for base metals), Event Horizons (+10%), and Void Rifts (+2%).
  • T-Minus Cycle: This cycle provides a +20% storage bonus specifically for Cryostations.

Strategic Uses

Unobtainium is a prerequisite for the most advanced technologies and upgrades in the game:

  • Metaphysics: Unlocking the Metaphysics technology requires 5 units of unobtainium.
  • Eludium: This advanced alloy is crafted using 1000 unobtainium and 2500 alloy.
  • Trading with Leviathans: Once a Black Pyramid is built, you can trade 5000 units of unobtainium to the Leviathans for Time Crystals and Relics.
  • Infrastructure Upgrades: It is required for Unobtainium Huts (which reduce hut price ratios), Unobtainium Reflectors (increasing science caps), and the construction of Markers.
  • Chronospheres: Building a Chronosphere costs 2500 units. These are vital for resets, as each Chronosphere preserves 1.5% of your unobtainium for the next run.

The “Positive Reset” Goal

For endgame players, the ultimate objective is to establish a self-sustaining reset loop. This is achieved by reaching an unobtainium capacity of at least 8.14 billion units, allowing for the construction of 100 Chronospheres. At this level, the resources carried over during a reset exceed the costs of the Chronospheres built, enabling exponential growth in subsequent runs.

item.title: Cryo Station
item.description:
A Cryostation is a vast, high-tier space storage facility located on the ice giant Terminus. It is a critical structure for mid-to-late-game progression, specifically for overcoming the storage bottlenecks required to enter the Eludium era and establish Chronosphere resets.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Unlocking: To build a Cryostation, you must first successfully complete the T-minus mission (which requires 2,500 starcharts, 12k titanium, 225k science, and 750 kerosene).
  • Construction Cost: Each station costs 200k Science, 25 Eludium, 1,500 Concrete, and 500 Kerosene.
  • Price Ratio: It features a relatively low price ratio of 1.12, making it easier to stack compared to terrestrial storage buildings.

Storage Capabilities

The primary function of a Cryostation is its massive boost to resource caps. Each station provides the following base storage increases:
item.content:encoded:
A Cryostation is a vast, high-tier space storage facility located on the ice giant Terminus. It is a critical structure for mid-to-late-game progression, specifically for overcoming the storage bottlenecks required to enter the Eludium era and establish Chronosphere resets.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Unlocking: To build a Cryostation, you must first successfully complete the T-minus mission (which requires 2,500 starcharts, 12k titanium, 225k science, and 750 kerosene).
  • Construction Cost: Each station costs 200k Science, 25 Eludium, 1,500 Concrete, and 500 Kerosene.
  • Price Ratio: It features a relatively low price ratio of 1.12, making it easier to stack compared to terrestrial storage buildings.

Storage Capabilities

The primary function of a Cryostation is its massive boost to resource caps. Each station provides the following base storage increases:

  • Wood and Minerals: +200,000
  • Titanium: +7,500
  • Oil: +7,500
  • Uranium: +5,000
  • Iron: +50,000
  • Coal: +25,000
  • Unobtainium: +750
  • Note: Unlike Moon Bases, Cryostations do not provide any catnip storage.

Strategic Importance

  • The Titanium Bottleneck: Cryostations are one of the most effective ways to increase titanium storage, which is necessary to reach the 125k cap required to research Space Manufacturing.
  • Unobtainium Era: They are essential for reaching the 1,000 unobtainium storage threshold needed to craft Eludium effectively.
  • Endgame Chronospheres: In the late game, Cryostations (along with Moon Bases) are the only buildings that provide unobtainium capacity. They are vital for reaching the multi-billion unobtainium caps required for massive Chronosphere resets.

Environmental and Scaling Modifiers

The effectiveness of Cryostations is influenced by the following factors:

  • Celestial Cycles: With Numerology researched, the T-minus cycle increases Cryostation storage by +20%, while the Helios cycle reduces it by -10%.
  • Spaceports: Each Spaceport provides a +0.85% boost to the capacity of your Cryostations.
  • Global Modifiers: Storage capacity is further enhanced by your current Paragon (0.1% per point), Event Horizons (+10% each), and Void Rifts (+2% each).
  • Sunforges: These improve the storage of base metals (iron, titanium, uranium) by 1% per building.

Distinction from Cryochambers

It is important not to confuse Cryostations with Cryochambers. While Cryostations are for resource storage, Cryochambers are found in the Time tab and are used to house and carry over individual kittens into your next game reset. Cryochambers require Time Crystals, Void, and Karma to build and are limited by the number of active Chronospheres you possess.

item.title: Space Elevator
item.description:
The Space Elevator is a foundational space structure in the sources, situated on the planet Cath, that serves as a critical bridge between terrestrial industry and orbital expansion. It is unlocked following a successful Orbital Launch and requires the research of both Orbital Engineering and Nanotechnology.

Costs and Core Effects

The structure requires 6,000 Titanium, 75,000 Science, and 50 Unobtainium to construct, featuring a price ratio of 1.15. Its primary benefits include:
item.content:encoded:
The Space Elevator is a foundational space structure in the sources, situated on the planet Cath, that serves as a critical bridge between terrestrial industry and orbital expansion. It is unlocked following a successful Orbital Launch and requires the research of both Orbital Engineering and Nanotechnology.

Costs and Core Effects

The structure requires 6,000 Titanium, 75,000 Science, and 50 Unobtainium to construct, featuring a price ratio of 1.15. Its primary benefits include:

  • Oil Efficiency: It reduces the oil requirements for space missions and buildings by 5% per level. This effect is subject to diminishing returns and is capped at a 75% reduction.
  • Space Structure Bonus: It provides a flat 1% bonus to the effectiveness of all other space structures.
  • Production Transfer: It transfers 0.1% of your global production specifically to Hydraulic Fracturers and Spice Refineries on Dune.

Strategic Synergies and Scaling

The true utility of Space Elevators depends heavily on late-game technological integration. The sources emphasize that Space Elevators are not particularly worth their cost until the Space Manufacturing workshop upgrade is researched.

  • Space Manufacturing Interaction: Once unlocked, each Factory provides a bonus to space production (3.75% per factory, or 4.5% with Factory Logistics) that amplifies the base bonus provided by Space Elevators.
  • Cycle Modifiers: If Numerology is researched, the Cath cycle doubles the transferred production bonus for oil, while the Kairo cycle reduces the overall transferred production bonus by 50%.

Endgame Utility and Management

In the late game, Space Elevators become a primary driver for Unobtainium and Time Crystal farming.

  • Unobtainium Production: They are essential for boosting the output of Lunar Outposts. Strategic advice suggests prioritizing the purchase of Space Elevators over Moon Bases and Orbital Arrays during short runs.
  • Profitability Calculations: Advanced players use a “break-even” formula to determine if building another elevator is worth it based on the remaining time in a run. For example, if the calculated gain in unobtainium is greater than half the construction cost, it is profitable to build and later sell the structure.
  • Reset Procedure: Because Space Elevators do not carry over during a reset, the sources recommend selling them all immediately before resetting to reclaim 50% of the invested resources.

item.title: Spice refinery
item.description:
A Spice Refinery is a space-based industrial structure located on the planet Dune. It is designed to refine the planet’s sand into Spice, a rare and psychoactive luxury resource.

Acquisition and Costs

The Spice Refinery becomes available once you have successfully completed the Dune Mission.

  • Resource Requirements: 500 Starcharts, 500 Alloy, 75,000 Science, and 125 Kerosene.
  • Price Ratio: 1.15.

Production and Synergies

  • Base Output: Each refinery produces 0.125 Spice per second.
  • Space Elevator Synergy: Space Elevators provide a specialized bonus to Spice Refineries, granting them 0.1% of your global production.
  • Automation: While not directly listed as having specific “upgrades” like the Planet Cracker, its production can be amplified by general space production modifiers such as Orbital Arrays (+2%) and Space Manufacturing (bonus based on factory craft ratio).

The Utility of Spice

Spice is a “Rare Resource” that plays a critical role in colony happiness and late-game utility:

The Spice Refinery becomes available once you have successfully completed the Dune Mission.

  • Resource Requirements: 500 Starcharts, 500 Alloy, 75,000 Science, and 125 Kerosene.
  • Price Ratio: 1.15.

Production and Synergies

  • Automation: While not directly listed as having specific “upgrades” like the Planet Cracker, its production can be amplified by general space production modifiers such as Orbital Arrays (+2%) and Space Manufacturing (bonus based on factory craft ratio).

The Utility of Spice

Spice is a “Rare Resource” that plays a critical role in colony happiness and late-game utility:

  • Happiness Bonus: Each unit of spice provides a +10% happiness boost.
  • Consumption: Like other rare resources (furs and ivory), spice is gradually consumed over time. Consumption rates can be managed through Policy/:
    • Stoicism: Reduces spice consumption by 50%.
    • Epicureanism/Extravagance: Increases the happiness benefit of spice (up to 5 happiness points) but causes it to be consumed much faster (up to 200% rate).
  • Brewery Interaction: Spice is a required input for Breweries, which consume 0.1 spice per tick to provide bonuses to festivals, such as increased happiness and kitten arrival speed.

Strategic Importance

In the mid-to-late game, the Spice Refinery is the primary method for automating spice acquisition. Prior to reaching Dune, spice is only obtainable as a rare, random drop from trading with other civilizations. By building refineries, you ensure a stable supply to maintain high kitten happiness and power your Breweries without relying on the RNG of trade.

item.title: Hyrdaulic Fracturer
item.description:
A Hydraulic Fracturer is a high-tier space structure situated on the planet Dune that produces a high-pressure stream of oil. It is a critical component of late-game resource management, specifically for sustaining the heavy oil requirements of the Eludium Era.

Acquisition and Costs

To access this building, you must first reach the Space tab by researching Rocketry and successfully complete the Dune Mission.

  • Mission Requirements: 1,000 Starcharts, 7,000 Titanium, 175k Science, and 75 Kerosene.
  • Building Cost: Each Hydraulic Fracturer costs 750 Starcharts, 1,025 Alloy, 150k Science, and 100 Kerosene.
  • Price Ratio: The building has a price ratio of 1.18.

Production and Scaling

The base effect of a Hydraulic Fracturer is the production of 2.5 oil per second. While powerful, its true utility comes from several late-game scaling mechanisms:
item.content:encoded:
A Hydraulic Fracturer is a high-tier space structure situated on the planet Dune that produces a high-pressure stream of oil. It is a critical component of late-game resource management, specifically for sustaining the heavy oil requirements of the Eludium Era.

Acquisition and Costs

To access this building, you must first reach the Space tab by researching Rocketry and successfully complete the Dune Mission.

  • Mission Requirements: 1,000 Starcharts, 7,000 Titanium, 175k Science, and 75 Kerosene.
  • Building Cost: Each Hydraulic Fracturer costs 750 Starcharts, 1,025 Alloy, 150k Science, and 100 Kerosene.
  • Price Ratio: The building has a price ratio of 1.18.

Production and Scaling

The base effect of a Hydraulic Fracturer is the production of 2.5 oil per second. While powerful, its true utility comes from several late-game scaling mechanisms:

  • Space Manufacturing: Sources indicate that Hydraulic Fracturers are “not particularly effective” until the Space Manufacturing workshop upgrade is researched. Once active, Factories provide a bonus to space production (equivalent to 75% of the factory craft ratio), which significantly amplifies the output of these structures.
  • Space Elevators: These terrestrial structures provide a unique synergy, granting 0.1% of your global production specifically to Hydraulic Fracturers and Spice Refineries.
  • Orbital Arrays: These provide a flat 2% bonus to all space structures, including the Fracturer.

Environmental and Cyclical Modifiers

If you have researched Numerology, the current celestial cycle will drastically alter the efficiency of your oil production on Dune:

  • Dune Cycle: Provides a massive +50% boost to oil output.
  • Umbra Cycle: Imposes a -25% penalty to production.
  • Festivals: Under the Numeromancy upgrade, holding a festival during the T-minus cycle provides a 2x multiplier to oil income, which further synergises with your Fracturer infrastructure.

Strategic Utility

As you transition into the late game, oil becomes a significant bottleneck for producing Kerosene and maintaining Research Vessels. While early-game oil management relies on Oil Wells and Bio Labs, the Hydraulic Fracturer is the primary method for scaling oil production to the levels required for deep-space exploration and Antimatter generation. Strategic advice suggests that if your oil is constantly hitting its cap, you should consider using Engineers to automate the conversion of oil into Kerosene to ensure your Fracturers never halt production.

item.title: Planet Cracker
item.description:
A Planet Cracker (specifically the USS Mining Vessel Hissmeowra) is a massive space-based mining structure used to extract large quantities of Uranium from the planet Dune. It is a critical component for transitioning into the Eludium Era, as it provides the steady Uranium supply required for Lunar Outposts to refine into Unobtainium.

Acquisition and Costs

The structure is found in the Space tab once the player has successfully landed on Dune.

  • Prerequisite: You must complete the Dune Mission (which costs 1,000 Starcharts, 7,000 Titanium, 175k Science, and 75 Kerosene).
  • Cost: Each Planet Cracker costs 2,500 Starcharts, 1,750 Alloy, 125,000 Science, and 50 Kerosene.
  • Price Ratio: 1.18.

Core Effects

  • Uranium Production: Generates 1.5 Uranium per second.
  • Uranium Storage: Increases your maximum Uranium capacity by 1,750.
  • Capacity Boost: Upgrading a Warehouse to a Spaceport increases the capacity of Planet Crackers by 0.85%.

Upgrades and Scaling

The effectiveness of a Planet Cracker can be significantly enhanced through various technological and industrial milestones:
item.content:encoded:
