It is a critical component for transitioning into the Eludium Era, as it provides the steady Uranium supply required for Lunar Outposts to refine into Unobtainium.

Acquisition and Costs

The structure is found in the Space tab once the player has successfully landed on Dune.

  • Prerequisite: You must complete the Dune Mission (which costs 1,000 Starcharts, 7,000 Titanium, 175k Science, and 75 Kerosene).
  • Cost: Each Planet Cracker costs 2,500 Starcharts, 1,750 Alloy, 125,000 Science, and 50 Kerosene.
  • Price Ratio: 1.18.

Core Effects

  • Uranium Production: Generates 1.5 Uranium per second.
  • Uranium Storage: Increases your maximum Uranium capacity by 1,750.
  • Capacity Boost: Upgrading a Warehouse to a Spaceport increases the capacity of Planet Crackers by 0.85%.

Upgrades and Scaling

The effectiveness of a Planet Cracker can be significantly enhanced through various technological and industrial milestones:

  • Planet Busters: This upgrade, available via the Exometallurgy (Advanced Exogeology) technology, increases the Uranium output of Planet Crackers by 100% (effectively doubling it).
  • Space Manufacturing: Once researched, Factories provide a bonus to Planet Crackers (and other space structures) based on your factory craft ratio.
  • Space Production Bonus: Output is also boosted by the combined bonuses from Space Elevators and Orbital Arrays.

Cycle and Environmental Modifiers

If the player has researched Numerology, the current celestial cycle impacts the vessel’s efficiency:

  • Dune Cycle: Uranium output is increased by 10%.
  • Umbra Cycle: Uranium output is reduced by 10%.
  • Pollution: High levels of CO2 and pollution in the atmosphere can harm resource production and may reduce the effectiveness of the production bonuses applied to these structures.

Strategic Importance

The Planet Cracker is the most efficient method for generating the massive amounts of Uranium needed in the late game. For context, a Lunar Outpost consumes Uranium at a rate of 1.75 per second, meaning a single un-upgraded Planet Cracker (producing 1.5/sec) almost entirely offsets the cost of one outpost. Without this stable supply, players must rely on Accelerators or trading with Dragons, which are significantly slower and less reliable for sustaining large-scale Unobtainium production.

item.title: Sunlifter
item.description:
A Sunlifter is a high-tier space structure built in the center of the Helios solar system, serving as the primary engine for antimatter production and late-game energy generation. It is a critical component for transitioning into the Relic era and completing high-level challenges.

Acquisition and Costs

To construct a Sunlifter, you must first complete the Helios Mission (3,000 starcharts, 15k titanium, 250k science, and 1,250 kerosene).

  • Structure Cost: 500k Science, 225 Eludium, and 2,500 Kerosene.
  • Price Ratio: 1.15.
  • Challenge Requirement: Building at least one Sunlifter is a mandatory goal for completing the Energy Challenge.

Core Functions

The Sunlifter provides two essential resources simultaneously:
item.content:encoded:
A Sunlifter is a high-tier space structure built in the center of the Helios solar system, serving as the primary engine for antimatter production and late-game energy generation. It is a critical component for transitioning into the Relic era and completing high-level challenges.

Acquisition and Costs

To construct a Sunlifter, you must first complete the Helios Mission (3,000 starcharts, 15k titanium, 250k science, and 1,250 kerosene).

  • Structure Cost: 500k Science, 225 Eludium, and 2,500 Kerosene.
  • Price Ratio: 1.15.
  • Challenge Requirement: Building at least one Sunlifter is a mandatory goal for completing the Energy Challenge.

Core Functions

The Sunlifter provides two essential resources simultaneously:

  1. Energy Production: It generates 30 Watts of energy. Alongside Hydro Plants, Sunlifters are the main focus for power generation in the late game.
  2. Antimatter Generation: It produces 1 antimatter per year. Antimatter is only generated at the change of the calendar year and only if your global energy production is positive.

Celestial Cycle Interactions

The effectiveness of Sunlifters is heavily influenced by the ten-cycle system if you have researched Numerology:

  • Helios Cycle: Provides a +50% bonus to Sunlifter energy output.
  • T-minus Cycle: Imposes a -50% penalty to Sunlifter energy output.

Strategic Utility

  • The Relic Era: Sunlifters are vital for reaching the 5,000 antimatter cap required for Relic Stations. To achieve this cap, you will typically need to power a vast array of Heatsinks and Containment Chambers, which require massive energy surpluses provided by Sunlifters.
  • Time Skipping: Because antimatter is granted only once per year, players often use Time Crystals to “shatter” or skip years. This triggers the year-change logic repeatedly, allowing you to harvest antimatter from your Sunlifters much faster than waiting in real-time.
  • Late-Game Power: While Reactors provide significant power, they consume Thorium; Sunlifters provide a stable, “clean” alternative that is essential for maintaining the energy required for Heatsinks and Containment Chambers.

item.title: IronWill
item.description:
Iron Will (IW) is a specialised gameplay mode in Kittens Game where the colony operates without any kitten housing or population. Entering this mode requires resetting the game with zero Chronospheres and avoiding the construction of Huts, Log Houses, or Mansions; building any housing immediately exits the mode.

The Zebra Accumulation Loop

The primary engine of an Iron Will run is the Zebra, which replaces kittens as hunters and provides Catpower.
item.content:encoded:
Iron Will (IW) is a specialised gameplay mode in Kittens Game where the colony operates without any kitten housing or population. Entering this mode requires resetting the game with zero Chronospheres and avoiding the construction of Huts, Log Houses, or Mansions; building any housing immediately exits the mode.

The Zebra Accumulation Loop

The primary engine of an Iron Will run is the Zebra, which replaces kittens as hunters and provides Catpower.

  • Initial Discovery: Zebras begin to appear only after researching Archery.
  • Zebra Farming Strategy: To build a viable foundation, players should research Archery and then immediately reset. Each reset performed after reaching Archery in IW increases the maximum Zebra limit for the next run by one.
  • The 50–60 Zebra Target: Strategic guides recommend repeating this “Archery reset” loop 6 to 10 times to accumulate 50–60 Zebras. This provides a permanent, efficient Catpower source that bypasses the need for food management, significantly accelerating mid-game economic stability.

Early Infrastructure and Science

Without kittens to assign as Scholars or Farmers, resource acquisition and research are fundamentally altered:

  • Science Generation: Initial science is gained exclusively through astronomical events, which are unlocked by building Libraries. Since manual observation is required early on, the automatic success chance is set to a flat 25% in IW mode.
  • Mineral Acquisition: Minerals are obtained via meteors, with the yield increasing for every Mine built.
  • Scientific Prioritisation: Research Mathematics early to unlock Celestial Mechanics, which provides a 60% boost to science gained from events and meteors in IW. Avoid job-specific upgrades like Mineral Hoes or Iron Axes, as they have no effect without workers.

Mid-Game Progression and Bottlenecks

The transition to space and high-tier industry is gated by specific IW constraints:

  • The Culture Cap: To progress, you must discover the Nagas to trade for minerals. This requires a 1,500 culture cap, which is achieved by building Amphitheatres, Academies, and crafting Manuscripts.
  • Gold and Ivory: Gold is obtained solely through hunting until Geodesy is researched. Ivory is also sourced from hunting and is essential for building the “Unicorn Tree”.
  • Trade Arbitrage: Use the Shark and Griffin loop to bypass early production limits. Trade iron to Sharks for Catnip, refine it into Wood, and trade Wood to Griffins for more Iron.
  • Policy Selection: In IW, Clear Cutting (+10% catnip refinement) and Strip Mining (+10% meteor minerals) provide specialised benefits.

Prestige and Endgame IW Goals

Significant milestones like the “Space Oddity” (reaching space in IW) or the “Cathammer 40k” (staying in IW for 40,000 years) require substantial preparation:

  • Paragon and Metaphysics: It is highly recommended to have 400+ burnt paragon and all Metaphysics price reduction upgrades (Golden Ratio, etc.) before a serious long-term IW run. Burnt paragon is particularly valuable as it provides a production and storage boost that works within IW.
  • Oil Cap Management: Reaching the high oil storage required for space missions is a major hurdle. Strategies suggest grinding steel for Oil Wells rather than relying on expensive Tankers.
  • Religious Utility: Pursuing Unicorn Religion is beneficial as Ivory Meteors (unlocked via Ivory Citadels) provide an automated source of ivory, reducing the reliance on active hunting for trades. Reaching Transcendence Tier 15 for Blazars is a common endgame goal to stabilise Time Crystal production.

item.title: Agriculture
item.description:
Agriculture is a foundational early-game scientific technology in Kittens Game that is essential for stabilising your colony’s food supply and expanding resource storage limits. It is unlocked after researching Calendar and costs 100 Science.

Unlocks and Features

Researching Agriculture provides two critical components for the survival of your kittens:

  • The Farmer Job: You can now assign kittens to the Farmer profession. Each Farmer produces 1 catnip per tick (5 per second), resulting in a net gain of 0.15 catnip per tick after their personal consumption is deducted.
  • Barns: This is the first major storage building available. Each Barn increases the maximum capacity for several resources: Catnip (+5,000), Wood (+200), Minerals (+250), Iron (+50), Coal (+60), Gold (+10), and Titanium (+2).

Strategic Importance

The primary utility of Agriculture is ensuring Winter survival.
item.content:encoded:
Agriculture is a foundational early-game scientific technology in Kittens Game that is essential for stabilising your colony’s food supply and expanding resource storage limits. It is unlocked after researching Calendar and costs 100 Science.

Unlocks and Features

Researching Agriculture provides two critical components for the survival of your kittens:

  • The Farmer Job: You can now assign kittens to the Farmer profession. Each Farmer produces 1 catnip per tick (5 per second), resulting in a net gain of 0.15 catnip per tick after their personal consumption is deducted.
  • Barns: This is the first major storage building available. Each Barn increases the maximum capacity for several resources: Catnip (+5,000), Wood (+200), Minerals (+250), Iron (+50), Coal (+60), Gold (+10), and Titanium (+2).

Strategic Importance

The primary utility of Agriculture is ensuring Winter survival.

  • Season-Proof Production: While Catnip Fields suffer a massive production penalty during Winter (typically -75% or up to -90% in cold winters), the catnip generated by Farmers is not affected by seasons or weather.
  • Winter Reallocation: Strategic guides recommend reallocating most of your kittens to the Farmer job temporarily when Autumn ends to ensure your food production remains positive throughout the Winter months.
  • Storage Caps: Without Barns, your wood and mineral caps will be too low to purchase higher-tier buildings or research advanced technologies.

Technology Path and Progression

Agriculture serves as a mandatory gate for several essential branches of the technology tree:

  • Immediate Path: Agriculture is the direct prerequisite for Mining (which unlocks the Workshop) and Archery (which unlocks the Hunter job).
  • Build Order: Efficient progression usually involves researching Calendar → Agriculture → Mining → Archery in rapid succession.
  • Enhancements: Farmer productivity can be further improved through Workshop upgrades like Mineral Hoes (+50% boost) and Iron Hoes (+30% boost).

Transition to Late Game

While Agriculture is vital early on, its relative importance shifts as you progress. In the mid-to-late game, players often replace Aqueducts with Hydro Plants and Pastures with Solar Farms to prioritise energy production over raw catnip bonuses. Eventually, once you have accumulated enough Paragon and Karma, your base production bonuses may become high enough that you only need a single Farmer to sustain a large population.

item.title: Animal Husbandry
item.description:
Animal Husbandry is an early-game scientific technology that is essential for transitioning from basic survival to infrastructure development and more advanced resource management. It is unlocked after researching Archery and costs 500 Science.

Core Buildings and Effects

Researching Animal Husbandry unlocks two primary structures focused on managing the colony’s food economy and rare resources:

  • Pastures: These buildings cost 100 Catnip and 10 Wood. Each Pasture provides a -0.5% reduction in catnip demand per kitten.
  • Unicorn Pastures: These structures cost 2 Unicorns and provide a smaller -0.15% reduction in catnip demand. Additionally, they automatically generate 0.001 unicorns per tick.

The demand reduction from both building types is vital for surviving Winter, as it decreases the constant food burden imposed by the kitten population. However, this reduction is subject to strict diminishing returns and is hard-capped at 50%.

Animal Husbandry is an early-game scientific technology that is essential for transitioning from basic survival to infrastructure development and more advanced resource management. It is unlocked after researching Archery and costs 500 Science.

Core Buildings and Effects

Researching Animal Husbandry unlocks two primary structures focused on managing the colony’s food economy and rare resources:

  • Pastures: These buildings cost 100 Catnip and 10 Wood. Each Pasture provides a -0.5% reduction in catnip demand per kitten.
  • Unicorn Pastures: These structures cost 2 Unicorns and provide a smaller -0.15% reduction in catnip demand. Additionally, they automatically generate 0.001 unicorns per tick.

The demand reduction from both building types is vital for surviving Winter, as it decreases the constant food burden imposed by the kitten population. However, this reduction is subject to strict diminishing returns and is hard-capped at 50%.

Scientific and Industrial Gateway

Animal Husbandry serves as a critical technological pivot point, acting as the mandatory prerequisite for three major scientific branches:

  • Construction: This allows for the building of Log Houses, Warehouses, Lumber Mills, and Ziggurats, as well as the enabling of crafting.
  • Mathematics: This unlocks Academies and the Celestial Mechanics upgrade to boost science gains from meteors.
  • Civil Service: This enables the Census system and the ability to assign a Leader to the colony.

Because it leads directly to Construction, Animal Husbandry is an indirect prerequisite for Engineering, which unlocks the game’s powerful policy system.

Late-Game Transitions

As the colony advances into the industrial and space eras, the role of Animal Husbandry shifts:

  • Energy Pivot: Once Ecology is researched, players can replace Pastures with Solar Farms to generate energy. This is considered a safe transition in the late game because the catnip demand reduction from Pastures is marginal by that point.
  • Unicorn Tree: Animal Husbandry remains relevant to religious progression through the Unicorn Tree. Workshop upgrades like Unicorn Selection (unlocked via Genetics) further improve the effectiveness of Unicorn Pastures by 25%.

item.title: Antimatter
item.description:
In Kittens Game, Antimatter is a late-game science technology that introduces powerful upgrades and leads into the endgame Terraformation phase.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Prerequisite Technology: You must first research Superconductors.
  • Resource Requirements:
    • Science: 500,000.
    • Relic: 1.

Unlocked Content

Researching Antimatter unlocks the subsequent Terraformation science, as well as several high-impact Workshop upgrades:

  • Antimatter Bases: Reduces the energy consumption of your Moon Bases by 50% (from 10 Watts down to 5 Watts).
  • Antimatter Reactors: Makes your Research Vessels and Space Beacons 95% more effective, significantly boosting your maximum science cap.
  • Antimatter Fission: Increases your Engineer kittens’ effectiveness at crafting eludium by 25%.
  • Antimatter Drive: A powerful rocket engine upgrade that drastically speeds up space travel, dividing travel time by 25.

The Antimatter Resource

Alongside the technology, the Antimatter resource itself becomes a critical bottleneck in the late game.

The Antimatter Resource

Alongside the technology, the Antimatter resource itself becomes a critical bottleneck in the late game.

  • Production: It is generated by Sunlifters once every game year, provided you have a positive energy balance.
  • Storage: Its storage capacity is extremely limited and must be expanded using Containment Chambers and Heatsinks.
  • Strategic Use: Amassing 5,000 Antimatter is a major endgame milestone required to build the Relic Station upgrade, which allows your Space Beacons to passively generate Relics.

item.title: Data Center
item.description:
A Data Centre is a high-tier scientific building that serves as the direct upgrade to the Library. It provides significantly enhanced storage for science and culture, and it is a critical component for reaching the massive science caps required for late-game progression.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Unlocking: You must research Electronics (135k Science, 70 Blueprints) to enable the option to upgrade Libraries into Data Centres.
  • Cost: Each Data Centre costs 10 Concrete and 100 Steel.
  • Energy Requirement: Unlike Libraries, which are energy-neutral, each Data Centre consumes 2 Watts of energy.

Primary Effects and Benefits

Once a Library is upgraded, the resulting Data Centre provides the following bonuses:
item.content:encoded:
A Data Centre is a high-tier scientific building that serves as the direct upgrade to the Library. It provides significantly enhanced storage for science and culture, and it is a critical component for reaching the massive science caps required for late-game progression.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Unlocking: You must research Electronics (135k Science, 70 Blueprints) to enable the option to upgrade Libraries into Data Centres.
  • Cost: Each Data Centre costs 10 Concrete and 100 Steel.
  • Energy Requirement: Unlike Libraries, which are energy-neutral, each Data Centre consumes 2 Watts of energy.

Primary Effects and Benefits

Once a Library is upgraded, the resulting Data Centre provides the following bonuses:

  • Science Production: Grants a +10% bonus to overall science production.
  • Science Storage: Increases the maximum science cap by 750.
  • Culture Storage: Increases the maximum culture cap by 250.
  • Compendium Efficiency: Provides a +1,000 increase to the Compendium Cap, allowing you to store more science via crafted compendiums.

Workshop Upgrades and Synergies

Data Centres can be made exponentially more powerful through specific Workshop research:

  • Cryocomputing: This upgrade (from Superconductors) reduces energy consumption by 50%, bringing the drain down from 2 Watts to 1 Watt per building.
  • Uplink: Creates a synergy with Bio Labs, increasing the science and culture caps of Data Centres by +1% per Bio Lab owned.
  • Reflectors (Titanium, Unobtainium, and Eludium): These upgrades allow your Observatories to boost the effectiveness of Data Centres. Each built Observatory provides an additive +2% bonus to the Data Centre’s science capacity.
  • Machine Learning: This Artificial Intelligence upgrade increases the effectiveness of Data Centres by +10% for every AI Core built.
  • Starlink: Further enhances the Uplink synergy by providing additional bonuses to science caps.

Strategic Utility

  • Efficiency Scaling: One Data Centre provides the same maximum science as three Libraries. This makes them highly space-efficient for players struggling to hit the science requirements for advanced technologies like Chronophysics.
  • The “Dead Stop” Warning: You should never upgrade your last Library if you do not have the materials (Concrete and Steel) to immediately build a Data Centre. If you have zero Libraries and zero Data Centres, astronomical events will cease to occur, halting your supply of starcharts.
  • Blueprint Crafting: Be aware that switching to Data Centres may initially decrease your bonus for crafting blueprints if you end up with fewer total buildings than you had as Libraries. This can be mitigated through the CAD System upgrade, which applies a +1% craft ratio per scientific building.
  • Energy Management: Because they consume energy, mass-upgrading Libraries into Data Centres can quickly crash your power grid. It is often wise to wait until your energy production (via Magnetos or Reactors) is stable before performing a bulk upgrade.

item.title: Tanker
item.description:
A Tanker is a high-tier craftable resource in Kittens Game primarily used to expand your colony’s maximum Oil storage capacity. Each Tanker built provides a flat increase of +500 to the oil cap.

Acquisition and Cost

Tankers are unlocked by researching Robotics. Because they require a significant amount of materials, they are considered a relatively expensive method of increasing storage. The crafting cost for a single Tanker is:

  • 200 Trade Ships
  • 1250 Alloy
  • 5 Blueprints

Strategic Utility and Advice

While Tankers provide a reliable way to boost your oil limit, strategic guides offer specific warnings regarding their efficiency:
item.content:encoded:
A Tanker is a high-tier craftable resource in Kittens Game primarily used to expand your colony’s maximum Oil storage capacity. Each Tanker built provides a flat increase of +500 to the oil cap.

Acquisition and Cost

Tankers are unlocked by researching Robotics. Because they require a significant amount of materials, they are considered a relatively expensive method of increasing storage. The crafting cost for a single Tanker is:

  • 200 Trade Ships
  • 1250 Alloy
  • 5 Blueprints

Strategic Utility and Advice

While Tankers provide a reliable way to boost your oil limit, strategic guides offer specific warnings regarding their efficiency:

  • The Oil Well Alternative: In some stages of the game (specifically during the Iron Will 40k run), relying on Tankers to reach oil caps is often deemed suboptimal. It is generally recommended to focus on grinding out the Steel necessary to build more Oil Wells instead, as they are often more resource-effective for reaching cap requirements.
  • Automation: Once you have Engineers, you can assign them to automatically craft Tankers (as well as Kerosene) to prevent your oil from capping and production from halting while you are away from the game.

Preservation and Resets

As a crafted resource, Tankers are normally lost upon resetting the game. However, they can be preserved across runs if the player has:

  1. Chronospheres: At least one active Chronosphere.
  2. Flux Condensator: This workshop upgrade allows Chronospheres to carry over a portion of crafted resources, including Tankers.

The amount preserved is calculated as a fraction based on the number of Chronospheres and the square root of the quantity of Tankers possessed prior to the reset. This makes them vital for “Positive Resets” in the late game, where players aim to start a new run with high storage capacities already intact.

item.title: Fur
item.description:
Fur is a rare luxury resource in Kittens Game that serves two primary functions: providing a happiness boost to your workforce and acting as the foundational material for crafting parchment.

Acquisition and Production

There are two main methods to obtain fur:

  • Hunting: Once you research Archery, you can send your kittens on hunts. Each hunt costs 100 Catpower and is guaranteed to yield some amount of fur. The amount returned is dictated by your Hunting Bonus, which is increased by workshop upgrades such as Bolas, Hunting Armour, Steel Armour, Alloy Armour, and Nanosuits.
  • Mints: In the mid-game, Mints (unlocked via Architecture) can be activated to automatically generate furs. The production rate of a Mint is tied to your maximum Catpower capacity (0.00875% of max catpower per tick). Using Mints is highly recommended during idle periods to stockpile fur without manual clicking.

Key Uses and Mechanics

  • Happiness and Efficiency: As a “rare resource”, fur provides a +10% bonus to kitten happiness. Because happy kittens are more productive, maintaining a supply of fur is a global production modifier. However, furs are gradually consumed over time, meaning you must constantly replenish them to maintain the bonus.
  • Crafting Parchment: Fur is the exclusive ingredient for Parchment (requiring 175 fur per craft). Parchment is an essential bottleneck resource used to create Manuscripts, which are required for nearly all mid-game scientific advancements and religious structures like Temples.
  • Loss on Reset: Like all luxury resources, accumulated furs are lost upon resetting the game.

Strategic Management and Policy/

The consumption and effectiveness of fur can be altered through various Policy/:

Key Uses and Mechanics

Because happy kittens are more productive, maintaining a supply of fur is a global production modifier. However, furs are gradually consumed over time, meaning you must constantly replenish them to maintain the bonus.
  • Crafting Parchment: Fur is the exclusive ingredient for Parchment (requiring 175 fur per craft). Parchment is an essential bottleneck resource used to create Manuscripts, which are required for nearly all mid-game scientific advancements and religious structures like Temples.
  • Loss on Reset: Like all luxury resources, accumulated furs are lost upon resetting the game.

Strategic Management and Policy/

The consumption and effectiveness of fur can be altered through various Policy/:

  • Stoicism: Reduces the consumption rate of luxury resources like fur by 50%.
  • Epicureanism: Increases the happiness bonus provided by fur from 10% to 11%.
  • Extravagance: Increases the happiness from consumable luxuries to 5 points but triples the consumption rate.
  • Tradition: While it doesn’t affect fur directly, it reduces the amount of parchment needed for manuscripts, thereby making your fur-to-culture conversion more efficient.

Note: “Fur” is also one of the possible last names randomly assigned to your kittens upon their arrival in the village.

Analogy: Think of Fur as fuel for a fire on a cold night. While it’s burning, it provides warmth (Happiness) that makes everyone work better, but if you don’t keep adding logs (Hunting or Mints), the fire will eventually go out as the wood is consumed. If you have enough wood, you can also stop using it for heat and carve it into furniture (Parchment) to build more permanent structures for your home.

item.title: Levels
item.description:
Transcendence is a late-game religious mechanic that allows you to spend Epiphany (also known as the Apocrypha bonus) to permanently increase your Transcendence Tier. These tiers carry over through resets and provide powerful scaling for your faith production, religious upgrades, and endgame buildings.

Unlocking Transcendence

To access this system, you must first research Theology and then purchase the Transcendence upgrade in the Religion tab.

  • Cost: 7,500 Faith and 7,500 Gold.
  • Requirement: A maximum Faith capacity of at least 125,000.
  • Function: Unlocking this provides the Transcend button, which is used to level up your tier by sacrificing a portion of your accumulated Epiphany.

Core Benefits and Effects

Transcending is essential for transitioning into the mid-to-late game “Relic Era” due to the following effects:
item.content:encoded:
Transcendence is a late-game religious mechanic that allows you to spend Epiphany (also known as the Apocrypha bonus) to permanently increase your Transcendence Tier. These tiers carry over through resets and provide powerful scaling for your faith production, religious upgrades, and endgame buildings.

Unlocking Transcendence

To access this system, you must first research Theology and then purchase the Transcendence upgrade in the Religion tab.

  • Cost: 7,500 Faith and 7,500 Gold.
  • Requirement: A maximum Faith capacity of at least 125,000.
  • Function: Unlocking this provides the Transcend button, which is used to level up your tier by sacrificing a portion of your accumulated Epiphany.

Core Benefits and Effects

Transcending is essential for transitioning into the mid-to-late game “Relic Era” due to the following effects:

  • Adoration Multiplier: Each tier significantly increases the conversion multiplier when you Adore the Galaxy, allowing you to rebuild your Praise bonus much faster after a reset.
  • Multi-level Upgrades: It allows you to purchase several religious upgrades (such as Scholasticism, Golden Spire, and Sun Altar) multiple times, though each additional level costs 2.5x more than the last.
  • Cryptotheology Gateway: Advanced endgame structures are gated by specific Transcendence Tiers. For example, Black Obelisks require Tier 1, while the powerful Blazars require Tier 15.
  • Atheism Challenge Synergy: If you complete the Atheism challenge, your Solar Revolution cap increases by 100 percentage points for every Transcendence Tier you have attained.

Strategic Advice: The “TAP” Method

Experienced players use a specific sequence called TAP to manage their faith bonuses effectively without destroying their current production.

  1. Transcend: Level up your tier when you have roughly 1.5x the required Epiphany for that level to avoid losing too much of your bonus.
  2. Adore: Immediately “Adore the Galaxy” to convert your remaining Worship into a now-stronger Epiphany bonus.
  3. Praise: Praise the sun with a full store of faith to quickly regain your Solar Revolution production boost.

Transcendence Tier Requirements

The cost in Epiphany scales exponentially with each tier:

Tier Minimum Epiphany Needed Key Unlock / Benefit
1 ~1.97% Black Obelisk
3 ~17.38% Black Nexus
9 ~151.34K% Black Library
15 ~3.04M% Blazar (Vital for Relic production)
20 ~451.14M% Dark Nova
25 ~66.96G% Holy Genocide (Post Apocalypse challenge)

Because the Epiphany requirement for Tier 15 is over 3 million percent, it is considered a major long-term goal for the late-game Relic and Time Crystal engine.

Transcendence Tiers carry over permanently through resets,. They are part of a select group of endgame achievements and prestige markers that are not lost when you restart your timeline.

Carry-over Mechanics

  • Permanent Progression: Once you reach a certain Transcendence Tier, it remains active in all subsequent runs,.
  • Cryptotheology Visibility: While the tiers themselves are saved, you must re-research the Cryptotheology technology in each new run to view your tier level or purchase/interact with the associated buildings.
  • Epiphany and Adoration: Your tiers increase the conversion multiplier when you “Adore the Galaxy”, making your future faith resets more powerful.

Key Benefits of Retaining Tiers

Maintaining your tiers across resets provides several compounding advantages:

  • Religious Scaling: Tiers allow you to purchase certain religious upgrades multiple times (like Solar Chant or Golden Spire) at an escalating cost.
  • Solar Revolution Cap: If you have completed the Atheism challenge, your Solar Revolution production bonus cap is increased by 100% for every Transcendence Tier you have attained,.
  • Cryptotheology Unlocks: Higher tiers are required to unlock advanced permanent buildings, such as Black Obelisks (Tier 1) or Blazars (Tier 15),.

item.title: Long Range Spaceships
item.description:
Unlocks Space Shuttle (space Building). Need to be staffed with a crew of two kittens.

The sources do not describe a specific entity named a “long range spaceship”, though the Research Vessel is explicitly defined as a “mobile research space vessel”. The Research Vessel is unlocked after completing the Piscine mission. To construct one vessel, you must invest 100 Starcharts, 2,500 Alloy, 12,500 Titanium, and 250 Kerosene. Each vessel provides a significant boost to your infrastructure by increasing the maximum science capacity by 10,000 and generating 0.05 Starcharts per second. These vessels can be further enhanced through several workshop upgrades, including Antimatter Reactors (+95% max science), Advanced AM Reactors (+150% max science), and Void Reactors (+400% max science). In the late game, the utility of these vessels for starchart production is complemented by Space Beacons, which provide higher starchart generation (0.125/sec) and a larger science cap boost (25,000).
item.content:encoded:
Unlocks Space Shuttle (space Building). Need to be staffed with a crew of two kittens.

The sources do not describe a specific entity named a “long range spaceship”, though the Research Vessel is explicitly defined as a “mobile research space vessel”. The Research Vessel is unlocked after completing the Piscine mission. To construct one vessel, you must invest 100 Starcharts, 2,500 Alloy, 12,500 Titanium, and 250 Kerosene. Each vessel provides a significant boost to your infrastructure by increasing the maximum science capacity by 10,000 and generating 0.05 Starcharts per second. These vessels can be further enhanced through several workshop upgrades, including Antimatter Reactors (+95% max science), Advanced AM Reactors (+150% max science), and Void Reactors (+400% max science). In the late game, the utility of these vessels for starchart production is complemented by Space Beacons, which provide higher starchart generation (0.125/sec) and a larger science cap boost (25,000).

True long-range interstellar travel is represented by the Centaurus System and Furthest Ring missions. The Centaurus System mission requires a massive investment of 100,000 Starcharts, 40,000 Titanium, 400,000 Science, 50,000 Kerosene, and 50,000 Thorium. The Furthest Ring is described as the “end of the universe” and carries the highest mission costs in the game, requiring 500,000 Starcharts, 1.25 million Science, 75,000 Kerosene, and 75,000 Thorium. Standard travel time to the Furthest Ring is approximately 725,200,000 game-days, which is over 16,000 real-world days, though this can be drastically reduced by researching advanced propulsion systems. The Thorium Drive divides travel time by 50, while the Antimatter Drive divides it by 25; researching both reduces travel times by a factor of 75.

Managing fuel for these long-range operations is a critical bottleneck, as missions to the outer reaches of the solar system and beyond require high quantities of Kerosene and Thorium. To sustain these operations, the sources recommend focusing on maximising unobtainium production via Lunar Outposts to craft the Eludium needed for high-tier space structures. Additionally, the USS Mining Vessel Hissmeowra, known as the Planet Cracker, acts as a heavy industrial vessel used to produce Uranium from Dune. Successful long-range progression relies on balancing these mobile assets with terrestrial storage and science capacity.

item.title: Dragons
item.description:
Dragons are a neutral trading civilization in Kittens Game that are crucial for acquiring Uranium and Thorium, essential resources for progressing into the space and atomic phases of the game.

Here is a detailed breakdown of the Dragons and their strategic importance:

Prerequisites and Attitude

  • Attitude: Dragons are a Neutral civilization, starting with a 0% attitude towards your kittens.
  • Unlocking: Dragons are unlocked once you have researched the Nuclear Fission technology.
  • Trade Requirements: To trade with Dragons, you must buy Uranium or Thorium by offering Titanium. The minimum cost they require is 250 Titanium.

Resources Traded

Dragons specialize in selling advanced radioactive resources:
item.content:encoded:
Dragons are a neutral trading civilization in Kittens Game that are crucial for acquiring Uranium and Thorium, essential resources for progressing into the space and atomic phases of the game.

Here is a detailed breakdown of the Dragons and their strategic importance:

Prerequisites and Attitude

  • Attitude: Dragons are a Neutral civilization, starting with a 0% attitude towards your kittens.
  • Unlocking: Dragons are unlocked once you have researched the Nuclear Fission technology.
  • Trade Requirements: To trade with Dragons, you must buy Uranium or Thorium by offering Titanium. The minimum cost they require is 250 Titanium.

Resources Traded

Dragons specialize in selling advanced radioactive resources:

Resource Sold Minimum Amount Chance to Receive Strategic Note
Uranium 1 95% Uranium is a Common Resource.
Thorium 1 50% Thorium is sold once you reach Embassy Level 5.

Dragon trades do not have any seasonal adjustments that affect the amount of resources received.

Strategic Role and Uranium Acquisition

The primary function of trading with Dragons is to gain Uranium, which is necessary for creating Unobtainium (UO) and for powering Reactors.

  1. Unobtainium Production: The Lunar Outpost converts Uranium into Unobtainium. Since the Lunar Outpost consumes Uranium at a rate 140 times faster than a single Accelerator can produce it internally, trading Titanium for Uranium with Dragons provides a vital alternative source for this bottleneck resource.
  2. Thorium Acquisition: Dragons are a source for Thorium, a highly radioactive and unstable fuel. Thorium is used for the Thorium Reactors upgrade and the Thorium Drive space engine upgrade.
  3. Embassy Bonus: If you build Embassies with the Dragons, the chance to receive Uranium increases, reaching a guaranteed 100% chance at Embassy Level 6.

In the progression towards Metaphysics, where you need Unobtainium, you will need to research Nuclear Fission to unlock Dragons. Trading with Dragons to acquire Uranium, which then converts to Unobtainium via the Lunar Outpost, is a standard path forward.

The reliance on Dragons for Uranium highlights the constant trade-offs in resource management: you exchange your hard-won Titanium (acquired mainly through trading with the hostile Zebras) for the prerequisite resource Uranium needed for the next technological jump to Unobtainium.

item.title: Lizards
item.description:
The Lizards are the first trade partner you encounter in Kittens Game, and they are crucial for unlocking the Trade tab and establishing early access to resources you may struggle to produce initially.

Here is a detailed breakdown of the Lizards:

Unlocking and Attitude

  • Discovery: A Lizard arrives at your Village after 20 years of game play, offering to trade Wood for Minerals, which immediately unlocks the Trade tab.
  • Prerequisite Reduction: This initial unlock time of Year 20 can be reduced to Year 5 if you have more than 0 Karma, and can be further reduced to Year 1 with the Diplomacy Metaphysics upgrade.
  • Attitude: Lizards are categorized as a Friendly civilization, starting with a high attitude bonus of +25%. As a Friendly civilization, they have a chance of giving you 15–25% extra resources during a successful trade.
  • Currency Requirement: Before you can trade with the Lizards, you must first develop the Gold Ore upgrade in the Workshop, enabling you to create Gold.

Trade Details

The Lizards’ primary trade early in the game involves wood and minerals, helping to balance your foundational resource production:

Trade Details

The Lizards’ primary trade early in the game involves wood and minerals, helping to balance your foundational resource production:

Action Resource Minimum Amount Cost/Gain Strategic Note
Buy Minerals 1000 Cost Lizards buy Minerals.
Sell Wood 500 Gain Lizards sell Wood.

Secondary Resources Unlocked via Embassies: Building embassies with the Lizards allows access to advanced materials:

  • Beam (10 units, 15% chance) at Embassy Level 5.
  • Scaffold (1 unit, 10% chance) at Embassy Level 10.

Seasonal Optimization: Lizard trades for Wood are subject to seasonal adjustments, making it most efficient to trade during Summer:

  • Summer: +35% Amount Modifier for Wood.
  • Autumn: +15% Amount Modifier for Wood.
  • Winter: +5% Amount Modifier for Wood.
  • Spring: -5% Amount Modifier for Wood.

Strategic Importance

  • Exploration: Trading with the Lizards unlocks the Trade tab, which allows you to Send Explorers to find additional civilizations.
  • Rare Resources: Any successful trade, including those with Lizards, has a fixed 10% chance of receiving one Blueprint and a 35% chance of receiving Spice as extra resources.

Advanced Relations Policy/

Once you reach Lizard Embassy Level 20 and research the Diplomacy Metaphysics upgrade, you unlock specialized foreign Policy/ related to the Lizard civilization:

  1. Lizard Relations: Ecologists: Reduces pollution by 5%.
  2. Lizard Relations: [Priests] ( /job/priest/ ): Causes Manuscripts to grant maximum faith equal to the maximum culture they grant (though this reduces maximum culture by 25%).
  3. Lizard Relations: Diplomats: Increases the standing ratio by +0.1% per Embassy built with neutral races, which can help those neutral races become Friendly.

item.title: Naga
item.description:
The Nagas are a neutral trading partner (0% attitude) in Kittens Game, specializing in Minerals and mineral-based materials. They are crucial for accelerating your supply of building materials and advanced resources.

Here is a comprehensive overview of Nagas:

Unlocking and Prerequisites

  • Prerequisite: Nagas are unlocked once you achieve a 1500 Culture maximum. Achieving this culture maximum often requires a substantial culture grind.
  • Trade Currency: Before you can trade with Nagas (or any other civilization), you must first develop the Gold Ore upgrade in the Workshop, enabling you to create Gold, which is required for trade costs.

Trade Details

The Nagas primarily trade minerals in exchange for Ivory:
item.content:encoded:
The Nagas are a neutral trading partner (0% attitude) in Kittens Game, specializing in Minerals and mineral-based materials. They are crucial for accelerating your supply of building materials and advanced resources.

Here is a comprehensive overview of Nagas:

Unlocking and Prerequisites

  • Prerequisite: Nagas are unlocked once you achieve a 1500 Culture maximum. Achieving this culture maximum often requires a substantial culture grind.
  • Trade Currency: Before you can trade with Nagas (or any other civilization), you must first develop the Gold Ore upgrade in the Workshop, enabling you to create Gold, which is required for trade costs.

Trade Details

The Nagas primarily trade minerals in exchange for Ivory:

Action Resource Minimum Amount Buy/Sell Strategic Note
Buy Ivory 500 Buy Ivory is gained via Hunting.
Sell Minerals 1000 Sell Naga trade is a huge step forward with respect to mineral production.

Secondary Resources: Nagas also sell higher-tier crafted materials once you build embassies:

  • Slab (5 units, 75% chance) at Embassy Level 5.
  • Concrete (5 units, 25% chance) at Embassy Level 10.
  • Megalith (1 unit, 10% chance) at Embassy Level 15.

Strategic Trading

  1. Seasonal Optimization: The trade for Minerals is optimally performed during the Spring season, which provides a +25% Amount Modifier. It is specifically suggested to trade with the Nagas only in spring.
  2. Trade Loop: The minerals acquired from Nagas in exchange for Ivory can be immediately reinvested. These minerals can be put back into your Smelters to produce more Gold, which is required to cover trade costs and build other structures.
  3. Blueprint Acquisition: Like all trades, a successful trade with Nagas has a 10% chance of including one Blueprint as an extra resource. This is a fixed rate unaffected by general trade bonuses.

Related Policy/ and Upgrades (Naga Relations)

The Naga Relations foreign Policy/ become available after reaching Embassy Level 20 and researching the Diplomacy metaphysics upgrade.

  • Naga Relations: Architects: This policy increases the chance to get blueprints from Nagas by 0.25% per embassy, capping at 10% at 40 embassies. Once the maximum bonus is reached, additional embassies improve the blueprint crafting ratio by +2% instead.
  • Naga Relations: Masons: This policy grants a +2.5% Quarry slab crafting bonus.
  • Naga Relations: Cultists: This policy causes Ziggurat to gain 10% of the bonuses that the Order of the Sun grants to temples.
  • Isolationism Path: The policy choice Isolationism over Diplomacy may be preferred for the additional naga exchanges.

item.title: Sharks
item.description:
The Sharks are a pivotal trading civilization in Kittens Game, primarily valued for their large supply of Catnip in exchange for Iron, often playing a role in crucial resource trade loops.

Trading Profile and Unlocking

  • Attitude: Sharks are a Neutral (0%) civilization.
  • Discovery: They can be discovered after 20 years of game play, though this is reduced to Year 5 if you have Karma, or Year 1 with the Diplomacy Metaphysics upgrade.
  • Trade Currency: Like all civilizations, trading requires you to first develop the Gold Ore upgrade in the Workshop.

Primary Trade and Seasonal Optimization

Sharks specialize in the exchange of Iron for Catnip:
item.content:encoded:
The Sharks are a pivotal trading civilization in Kittens Game, primarily valued for their large supply of Catnip in exchange for Iron, often playing a role in crucial resource trade loops.

Trading Profile and Unlocking

  • Attitude: Sharks are a Neutral (0%) civilization.
  • Discovery: They can be discovered after 20 years of game play, though this is reduced to Year 5 if you have Karma, or Year 1 with the Diplomacy Metaphysics upgrade.
  • Trade Currency: Like all civilizations, trading requires you to first develop the Gold Ore upgrade in the Workshop.

Primary Trade and Seasonal Optimization

Sharks specialize in the exchange of Iron for Catnip:

  • Sharks Buy: Iron (minimum 100 units).
  • Sharks Sell: Catnip (minimum 35,000 units).
    • This catnip can be refined into Wood for construction purposes.
  • Trading for Catnip is optimally performed during Winter, which provides a +45% Amount Modifier. They also offer a good bonus in Spring (+20%) and Autumn (+15%), but the trade is worst in Summer (-5%).

Secondary and Rare Resources

As you build Embassies with the Sharks, they unlock more sophisticated trade items:

  • Crafted Paper: At Embassy Level 5, they may sell Parchment (5 units, 25% chance); at Level 10, Manuscript (3 units, 15% chance); and at Level 15, Compendium (1 unit, 10% chance).
  • Any successful trade with Sharks has a fixed 10% chance of yielding one Blueprint and a 35% chance of yielding Spice as an extra resource.

Strategic Role (The Trade Loop)

Sharks are essential in a powerful industrial trade loop, often paired with the hostile Griffins:

  1. The cycle begins in Autumn by trading Wood to Griffins to gather Iron.
  2. In Winter, this acquired Iron is traded to Sharks for Catnip.
  3. The Catnip is then refined into Wood (costing 50 catnip per wood after the Catnip Enrichment upgrade) to prepare for the next Autumn trade with Griffins.

This trading loop is a “great way to start collecting wood, steel, gears, and blueprints for Steamworks”.

Advanced Policy/

If you reach Embassy Level 20 and have the Diplomacy Metaphysics upgrade, you unlock specific Shark Relations Policy/ that further enhance resource production and trade efficiency:

  • Increases Parchment and Manuscript trade chance, but raises the Iron cost per trade by 50%.
  • Boosts trade ratio, starting at +3% and scaling multiplicatively up to +30% based on the total trades completed.
  • Provides a (catnip refinement).

Role in Challenges

In the difficult Iron Will challenge, especially when combined with the Black Sky Challenge, the Sharks’ role shifts dramatically:

  • Trade Change: Sharks trade iron for science.
  • Trade Cost: The trade initially requires only iron, then shifts to require catpower after the first Zebra joins, and finally requires gold once Currency and Gold Ore are researched.
  • Seasonal Inversion: The seasonal adjustments are inverted while Sharks are science traders.

item.title: Zebra
item.description:
The Zebras are a crucial civilization in Kittens Game, primarily known as who provide essential industrial resources during the mid-game, particularly in the Titanium era.

Here is a comprehensive breakdown of the Zebras, their role in trade, and their unique function in the Iron Will challenge:

Trading and Strategic Importance

Zebras are primarily sought after for their critical resource exports:

  • Acquisition and Attitude: Zebras are a Hostile civilization with an initial attitude of -30%. They are unlocked once you have 1 Trade Ship. Since they are hostile, they have a chance of giving you no resources at all during a trade.
  • Trade Mitigation: The penalty from Zebra hostility can be negated by building a sufficient number of Tradeposts (85 posts, or 58 with the Diplomacy Metaphysics upgrade).
  • Resources Traded: Zebras buy Slab (50 minimum). In return, they sell three critical resources:
    • Iron (300 minimum amount).
    • Plate (2 minimum, with a 65% chance).
    • Titanium (amount is calculated based on the number of Trade Ships you possess: (0.03 * Trade Ships) + 1.5).
    • They also offer Alloy (0.25 minimum, 5% chance) once you reach Embassy Level 5.
  • Titanium Trade Mechanic: Unlike most resources gained through trade, the amount of Titanium received from the Zebras (such as the bonus received from Tradeposts).
  • Seasonal Optimization: Trades are best conducted during Summer for Iron (+15% amount modifier) and Winter for Plate (+25% amount modifier).
  • Strategic Goal: In the Titanium era, the focus often becomes trading with Zebras non stop to acquire Titanium and Iron. This trade is crucial for unlocking titanium-heavy technologies and buildings.

Policy/ and Upgrades

Zebras are associated with several Policy/ and specialized upgrades:
item.content:encoded:
The Zebras are a crucial civilization in Kittens Game, primarily known as who provide essential industrial resources during the mid-game, particularly in the Titanium era.

Here is a comprehensive breakdown of the Zebras, their role in trade, and their unique function in the Iron Will challenge:

Trading and Strategic Importance

Zebras are primarily sought after for their critical resource exports:

  • Acquisition and Attitude: Zebras are a Hostile civilization with an initial attitude of -30%. They are unlocked once you have 1 Trade Ship. Since they are hostile, they have a chance of giving you no resources at all during a trade.
  • Trade Mitigation: The penalty from Zebra hostility can be negated by building a sufficient number of Tradeposts (85 posts, or 58 with the Diplomacy Metaphysics upgrade).
  • Resources Traded: Zebras buy Slab (50 minimum). In return, they sell three critical resources:
    • Iron (300 minimum amount).
    • Plate (2 minimum, with a 65% chance).
    • Titanium (amount is calculated based on the number of Trade Ships you possess: (0.03 * Trade Ships) + 1.5).
    • They also offer Alloy (0.25 minimum, 5% chance) once you reach Embassy Level 5.
  • Titanium Trade Mechanic: Unlike most resources gained through trade, the amount of Titanium received from the Zebras (such as the bonus received from Tradeposts).
  • Seasonal Optimization: Trades are best conducted during Summer for Iron (+15% amount modifier) and Winter for Plate (+25% amount modifier).
  • Strategic Goal: In the Titanium era, the focus often becomes trading with Zebras non stop to acquire Titanium and Iron. This trade is crucial for unlocking titanium-heavy technologies and buildings.

Policy/ and Upgrades

Zebras are associated with several Policy/ and specialized upgrades:

  • After meeting the Zebras, you must choose between two foreign Policy/: * Zebra Relations: Appeasement (5000 Culture): This policy is generally preferred because it improves relations (equivalent to 15 extra tradeposts) and provides a multiplicative boost to the titanium trade ratio (equivalent to 15 tradeposts). It is highly recommended because players are often desperate for titanium. * Zebra Relations: Bellicosity (5000 Culture): This policy worsens relations with Zebras but slightly improves relations with other races.
  • There are several buildings associated with this race, including the Zebra Outpost, Zebra Workshop, and Zebra Forge. Additionally, the workshop upgrade Mineralogy Department is a Zebra upgrade for Academies.

Role in Iron Will (IW) Mode

In the specialized Iron Will challenge (a mode played without kittens or housing), Zebras adopt a unique and critical function:

  • Job Replacement: In IW mode, Zebras are categorized as a Special Resource that acts as hunters to replace the absent kitten population, generating Catpower. Catpower is essential for hunting, which yields Gold (due to the Gold Ore upgrade effect in IW mode) and Ivory.
  • Acquisition: You gain one zebra after researching Archery. Players often perform short reset runs (6 to 10 runs) solely to rush Archery and accumulate .
  • Zebra Limit: The maximum zebra limit can be increased by 1 every time you research Archery and reset (up to 10 or 11 initially). The limit also increases based on the amount of science spent in the previous run.
  • While a higher zebra count is desired to speed up hunting and catpower generation, diminishing returns on catpower production start to set in .
  • Bloodstone: If you have at least in IW mode, hunting gains a 0.05% chance of yielding Bloodstone.
  • IW Carryover: The Zebra counter carries over when you reset the game. The Zebra Diplomacy and Zebra Covenant Metaphysics upgrades allow a portion of your Zebras (10% and 50% of cap, respectively) to remain if you choose to end Iron Will mode by building housing.

Analogy: Zebras act as an offshore supplier for heavy manufacturing materials. They are a hostile, high-risk trade partner, but they are the only reliable source for large quantities of Titanium—the resource needed to build your space program and advanced factories. In the unique constraints of Iron Will, however, they become a primary workforce, serving as essential substitute hunters to generate the gold and ivory required for civilization building.

item.title: Acoustics
item.description:
Acoustics is a crucial mid-game technology research that advances your religious and cultural infrastructure by enabling the construction of the Chapel building.

1. Unlocking and Cost

  • Prerequisite: Acoustics is unlocked after successfully researching Architecture.
  • Cost: Researching Acoustics requires 60,000 Science and 60 Compendiums.
  • Progression: This technology is part of the progression pathway following Navigation and Architecture. Acoustics subsequently unlocks Drama and Poetry research.

2. Key Building Unlocked: Chapel

The primary function of Acoustics is to unlock the Chapel building, which significantly improves the rate of faith accumulation.
item.content:encoded:
Acoustics is a crucial mid-game technology research that advances your religious and cultural infrastructure by enabling the construction of the Chapel building.

1. Unlocking and Cost

  • Prerequisite: Acoustics is unlocked after successfully researching Architecture.
  • Cost: Researching Acoustics requires 60,000 Science and 60 Compendiums.
  • Progression: This technology is part of the progression pathway following Navigation and Architecture. Acoustics subsequently unlocks Drama and Poetry research.

2. Key Building Unlocked: Chapel

The primary function of Acoustics is to unlock the Chapel building, which significantly improves the rate of faith accumulation.

Building Cost Effects
Chapel 2000 Minerals, 250 Culture, 250 Parchment Generates +0.005 Faith per Tick (a higher rate than the 0.0015 faith per tick generated by Temples). Also generates +0.05 Culture per Tick and increases Max Culture by +200.

3. Strategic Importance

Acoustics is strategically important because it addresses two major resource bottlenecks in the mid-game:

  • Faith and Culture: Acoustics improves faith and culture production, which are resources that accumulate slowly. Chapels provide a substantial increase to faith generation compared to the prior Temple building.
  • Mid-Game Choices: When facing the choice between advanced sciences unlocked after Navigation (Chemistry, Acoustics, Geology, Electricity), experts generally recommend pursuing Acoustics to boost the crucial, slower-generating faith and culture resources. This is key for advancing through technologies like Theology and later, the Religion tab upgrades.

item.title: Cryptotheology
item.description:
The query is about Cryptotheology, which is both a specific high-tier technology and the name of the system it unlocks in Kittens Game, defining the Phase 3 or Late Game progression.

Here is a comprehensive overview of Cryptotheology, its purpose, and its related elements based on the sources:

1. Cryptotheology as a Technology

  • Unlock Requirement: The technology Cryptotheology is unlocked after researching Theology and costs 650K Science and 5 Relics .
  • Effect: Researching this technology grants access to the Cryptotheology system and unlocks the Relic Station upgrade.
  • Persistence: The technology itself does not carry over when you reset the game, even though the buildings purchased within the Cryptotheology system do persist across resets.

2. The Cryptotheology System (Phase 3)

Cryptotheology is described as the system that provides “Insights into the mysteries of time and space” and focuses on the Time, Relics, and Void mechanics of the game. It is the defining feature of the Phase 3 (End Game) of Kittens Game .
item.content:encoded:
The query is about Cryptotheology, which is both a specific high-tier technology and the name of the system it unlocks in Kittens Game, defining the Phase 3 or Late Game progression.

Here is a comprehensive overview of Cryptotheology, its purpose, and its related elements based on the sources:

1. Cryptotheology as a Technology

  • Unlock Requirement: The technology Cryptotheology is unlocked after researching Theology and costs 650K Science and 5 Relics .
  • Effect: Researching this technology grants access to the Cryptotheology system and unlocks the Relic Station upgrade.
  • Persistence: The technology itself does not carry over when you reset the game, even though the buildings purchased within the Cryptotheology system do persist across resets.

2. The Cryptotheology System (Phase 3)

Cryptotheology is described as the system that provides “Insights into the mysteries of time and space” and focuses on the Time, Relics, and Void mechanics of the game. It is the defining feature of the Phase 3 (End Game) of Kittens Game .

The core purpose of the system is to purchase permanent, powerful structures using Relics and Void, which often scale with the player’s Transcendence Tiers (TT).

3. Buildings and Upgrades

Cryptotheology buildings purchased persist across resets and are unlocked sequentially based on your Transcendence Tier (TT), which is bought with Epiphany.

Building/Upgrade Primary Cost Transcendence Prerequisite Primary Effect
Black Obelisk 100 Relics TT 1 Improves your Solar Revolution bonus cap by +5% per Transcendence Tier.
Black Nexus 5,000 Relics TT 3 Improves relic production from two sources: Refining Time Crystals (1 + (Black Nexus * Black Pyramid) relics) and Relic Station upgraded Space Beacons.
Black Core 10,000 Relics TT 5 Increases the Sorrow (Black Liquid Sorrow or BLS) limit by +1% .
Event Horizon 25,000 Relics TT 7 Increases global resource storage ratio by +10%. This stacks additively with Void Rifts and multiplicatively with other storage bonuses [6, 8].
Black Library 30,000 Relics TT 9 Improves Codex Leviathanianus scaling by +2% per library, further boosted by Unicorn Graveyards .
Black Radiance 37,500 Relics TT 12 Increases the alicorn corruption rate based on the amount of Sorrow (BLS) and the number of Black Radiances.
Blazar 50,000 Relics TT 15 Improves Chronomancy and Unicornmancy by 2.5%, Time Impedance by 10%, and Resource Retrieval effectiveness by 2% [9]. Blazars are vital to a Time Crystal engine .
Dark Nova 75,000 Relics, 7,500 Void TT 20 Provides a +2% global energy production bonus.
Mausoleum 50,000 Relics, 12,500 Void, 10 Necrocorn TT 23 Unlocks the ability to purchase Pacts.
Holy Genocide 100,000 Relics, 25,000 Void TT 25 Unlocks the Post Apocalypse challenge upon reset .

4. Strategic Role and Goals

  • Relic Conversion: Cryptotheology provides direct use for Relics, which are primarily created by refining Time Crystals (25 TCs = 1 Relic).
  • Late-Game Gate: Once a player can build Eludium Huts easily, they are ready for the unicorn/time crystal phase. The next major goal is to maximize the Solar Revolution bonus (capped at 1000% before Cryptotheology upgrades) and reach Transcendence Tier15 . Reaching TT 15 is necessary to purchase the Blazar, which is considered vital to a Time Crystal engine [10, 15].
  • Boosting Persistence: Cryptotheology buildings are key to late-game scaling. For example, Black Obelisks boost the cap of the Solar Revolution bonus.
  • Challenges: The ultimate building, the Holy Genocide, is required to unlock the Post Apocalypse challenge.

item.title: Fascism
item.description:
The policy Fascism is an advanced Government policy in Kittens Game, primarily focused on aggressively boosting population by reducing housing costs and eliminating population-related happiness penalties.

Here is a comprehensive breakdown of the Fascism policy:

Policy Details and Effects

Category Detail
Cost 15,000 Culture.
Description The policy’s description is “Lebensraum!”.
Prerequisites You must Build a factory and have previously chosen Autocracy or Monarchy.
Locks Choosing Fascism locks out both the Communism and Liberalism Policy/.
Key Effects Log cabins are 50% cheaper. Log Houses are the housing structure that follows Huts.
Eliminates population penalties to happiness.

Strategic Evaluation

Fascism is one of three major government policy choices (Liberalism, Fascism, or Communism) available after meeting the Factory prerequisite.
item.content:encoded:
The policy Fascism is an advanced Government policy in Kittens Game, primarily focused on aggressively boosting population by reducing housing costs and eliminating population-related happiness penalties.

Here is a comprehensive breakdown of the Fascism policy:

Policy Details and Effects

Category Detail
Cost 15,000 Culture.
Description The policy’s description is “Lebensraum!”.
Prerequisites You must Build a factory and have previously chosen Autocracy or Monarchy.
Locks Choosing Fascism locks out both the Communism and Liberalism Policy/.
Key Effects Log cabins are 50% cheaper. Log Houses are the housing structure that follows Huts.
Eliminates population penalties to happiness.

Strategic Evaluation

Fascism is one of three major government policy choices (Liberalism, Fascism, or Communism) available after meeting the Factory prerequisite.

  • First Run Population Push: This policy is strategically useful on the first run. The main goal of the initial run is often to accumulate sufficient population to gain Paragon upon reset. You might select Fascism for a couple of extra log houses to help reach 130+ kittens before the first reset.
  • Population Boost: The policy gives a nice population boost because the reduced cost of log cabins makes expanding housing capacity easier.
  • Happiness Management: By eliminating population penalties to happiness, it allows players to grow their workforce faster without suffering the associated production drop caused by unhappiness.
  • Policy Alternatives: In later runs, Policy/ that offer long-term industrial boosts or trade relations are often prioritized:
    • Liberalism may be preferred if you are struggling with zebra hostility (which impacts titanium acquisition).
    • Communism may be preferred if zebra hostility has been negated, as it provides a strong boost to industry (+25% iron, coal, and titanium production). Communism is also suggested to give better time crystal results in self-imposed restriction runs.
  • Paragon Scaling: As your Paragon grows, the Fascism policy can be unlocked to aid in population growth.

item.title: Rationing vs Frugality
item.description:
Rationing and Frugality are mutually exclusive Philosophical Policy/ in Kittens Game, both requiring the precursor policy Stoicism and costing 3,500 Culture. The choice between them depends on whether you prioritise managing food consumption penalties or boosting automated rare resource production.

Here is a breakdown of their effects:

Policy Prerequisite Cost Key Effects
Rationing Stoicism 3500 Culture Reduces Catnip Consumption: Decreases the catnip consumption increase caused by high happiness by $-10%$. Boosts Hunting: Provides a permanent $+0.1$ Hunting bonus.
Frugality Stoicism 3500 Culture Boosts Mints: Increases the resource output of Mints by $+10%$.

Strategic Context

The decision between Rationing and Frugality often arises when a player is attempting to manage late-game resource consumption, particularly luxury resources (Furs, Ivory, Spice) and Catnip demand, which is heavily increased by high Happiness levels (e.g., $420%$ happiness increases catnip consumption by $320%$).

The choice between them depends on whether you prioritise managing food consumption penalties or boosting automated rare resource production.

Here is a breakdown of their effects:

Policy Prerequisite Cost Key Effects
Rationing Stoicism 3500 Culture Reduces Catnip Consumption: Decreases the catnip consumption increase caused by high happiness by $-10%$. Boosts Hunting: Provides a permanent $+0.1$ Hunting bonus.
Frugality Stoicism 3500 Culture Boosts Mints: Increases the resource output of Mints by $+10%$.

Strategic Context

The decision between Rationing and Frugality often arises when a player is attempting to manage late-game resource consumption, particularly luxury resources (Furs, Ivory, Spice) and Catnip demand, which is heavily increased by high Happiness levels (e.g., $420%$ happiness increases catnip consumption by $320%$).

  • Rationing is useful if you are struggling with keeping up with food demands, as it mitigates the negative effect that increased Happiness has on catnip consumption. The bonus to Hunting also provides a slight general boost to acquiring Furs, Ivory, and Unicorns.
  • Frugality is specifically designed to make the automated production of resources from Mints more effective, resulting in $10%$ more output from them. Mints are important for generating Furs and Ivory later in the game.

General strategic advice suggests that by the time you reach this choice, if you are still running out of luxury resources despite already having Stoicism (which halves luxury resource consumption) and many Tradeposts (which slow consumption), either Rationing or Frugality might help, but they are often viewed as providing relatively minor gains compared to major production multipliers available elsewhere.

item.title: Alloy
item.description:
Alloy is a crucial craftable resource in Kittens Game, marking a mid-to-late game phase of infrastructure development.

Resource Details

Alloy is a composite material refined from other metals and is categorised as a craftable resource.

Detail Specification
Prerequisite Technology Chemistry, which itself requires Physics.
Crafting Cost 75 Steel and 10 Titanium.
Unlocks The crafting of Alloy is unlocked by the Chemistry technology.

Uses and Strategic Importance

Alloy is necessary for constructing advanced buildings, structures, and various Workshop upgrades:
item.content:encoded:
Alloy is a crucial craftable resource in Kittens Game, marking a mid-to-late game phase of infrastructure development.

Resource Details

Alloy is a composite material refined from other metals and is categorised as a craftable resource.

Detail Specification
Prerequisite Technology Chemistry, which itself requires Physics.
Crafting Cost 75 Steel and 10 Titanium.
Unlocks The crafting of Alloy is unlocked by the Chemistry technology.

Uses and Strategic Importance

Alloy is necessary for constructing advanced buildings, structures, and various Workshop upgrades:

  1. Buildings:
    • Bio Lab: Requires 25 Alloy and 100 Slab to build, significantly boosting Science production and storage.
    • Magneto: Requires 10 Alloy, 5 Gear, and 1 Blueprint to construct, providing a crucial +2% Global Production boost and generating 5 Energy.
  2. Workshop Upgrades: Alloy is the prerequisite material for several high-tier upgrades:
    • Alloy Saw: Requires Alloy and improves Lumber Mill efficiency by $+15%$.
    • Alloy Axe: Requires Alloy and makes Woodcutters $50%$ more effective.
    • Alloy Barns/Warehouses: Required for various storage upgrades.
    • Alloy Armour/Nanosuits: Required for advanced Hunting bonuses.

Progression in the “Alloy Era”

The point where Alloy becomes readily available signals a major checkpoint in the game’s progression.

  • Technology Path: Getting to the Alloy era requires a specific scientific path: Navigation $\to$ Physics $\to$ Chemistry.
  • Resource Bottlenecks: Alloy requires substantial amounts of Titanium, which must be acquired primarily through trading slabs with Zebras. This titanium requirement mandates ongoing construction of Trade Ships and Observatories (to acquire Starcharts).
  • Strategic Focus: Once Alloy is unlocked, strategic focus shifts to purchasing Alloy buildings and the associated upgrades to boost storage and production. The next major goal after the Alloy era is typically achieving Concrete Huts.
  • Trait Bonus: Kittens with the Metallurgist trait, when assigned as a leader, provide a specific bonus to metal crafting efficiency, increasing the craft ratio for resources including Alloy by $+0.1$.

Finally, Alloy is also a component, alongside Unobtainium, in crafting the late-game resource Eludium.

item.title: Bloodstone
item.description:
Bloodstone is classified as an uncommon resource in Kittens Game that plays a role in late-game crafting and unlocks specific buildings associated with the Zebras,. It is poetically described as a strange jewelry claimed to be made of time and a blood of elder gods.

Acquisition Methods

Bloodstone can be acquired through hunting and crafted using advanced resources:

  1. Hunting: Bloodstone has a chance to be found when engaging in hunting, provided you have at least 10 Zebras,. In the Iron Will challenge mode, the chance to yield a bloodstone during a hunt is 0.05% if you already have it. However, this chance increases significantly to 5% if you do not already have bloodstone.

  2. Crafting: Bloodstone is a craftable item unlocked by the Zebra Forge. The crafting cost is high, requiring temporal and elder resources: 5,000 Time Crystal and 10,000 Relic.

  2. Crafting: Bloodstone is a craftable item unlocked by the Zebra Forge. The crafting cost is high, requiring temporal and elder resources: 5,000 Time Crystal and 10,000 Relic.

Uses and Buildings

Bloodstone is a prerequisite resource for several Zebra structures and other craftable materials:

  • Zebra Outpost: Requires 1 Bloodstone.
  • Zebra Workshop: Requires 5 Bloodstone.
  • Zebra Forge: Requires 50 Bloodstone. The Zebra Forge itself unlocks the ability to craft Bloodstone, as well as T-Mythril.
  • T-Mythril: Bloodstone is a component in crafting T-Mythril,.

Persistence

As a craftable resource, Bloodstone is retained across game resets, but only conditionally. It is carried over if the player has Chronospheres built and the Flux Condensator workshop upgrade researched. The amount carried over is subject to diminishing returns.

item.title: T Mythril
item.description:
T-Mythril is a late-game craftable resource in Kittens Game, specifically associated with the Zebra civilisation structures and resource conversion.

Acquisition and Crafting

T-Mythril crafting is unlocked by constructing the Zebra Forge building.

The resource cost to craft T-Mythril is high, involving advanced resources, unicorn resources, and titanium:

  • 5 Bloodstone
  • 1,000 Ivory
  • 500 Titanium

The Zebra Forge itself is a major structure, costing 50 Bloodstone, and is necessary to unlock the ability to craft both T-Mythril and Bloodstone.
item.content:encoded:
T-Mythril is a late-game craftable resource in Kittens Game, specifically associated with the Zebra civilisation structures and resource conversion.

Acquisition and Crafting

T-Mythril crafting is unlocked by constructing the Zebra Forge building.

The resource cost to craft T-Mythril is high, involving advanced resources, unicorn resources, and titanium:

  • 5 Bloodstone
  • 1,000 Ivory
  • 500 Titanium

The Zebra Forge itself is a major structure, costing 50 Bloodstone, and is necessary to unlock the ability to craft both T-Mythril and Bloodstone.

Uses in Infrastructure

T-Mythril is primarily used to build the Ivory Temple:

  • Ivory Temple Cost: 1 T-Mythril and 100 Ivory.
  • Effect: The Ivory Temple serves as a resource converter, continuously consuming 100 Ivory per tick and producing 1 Mineral per tick.
  • Automation: The Ivory Temple structure also has an automation upgrade (Whispers) that doubles both ivory consumption and mineral production, while also generating a minuscule amount of T-Mythril (0.00005 per tick).

item.title: Quarry
item.description:
The Quarry is a bonfire building unlocked by the Geology technology. It is a mid-to-late-game structure primarily used to enhance mineral output and automate the production of coal and uranium.

Construction and Base Effects

  • Cost: Initial construction requires 50 Scaffolds, 125 Steel, and 1,000 Slabs.
  • Price Ratio: 1.15.
  • Mineral Bonus: Each Quarry provides a flat +35% bonus to mineral production.
  • Coal Production: It generates +0.015 coal per tick (0.075 per second). This makes it a significant source of passive coal alongside Smelters and Mines.

Environmental Impact

Quarries are listed as industrial structures that contribute to pollution. High levels of pollution can eventually reduce catnip production, kitten happiness, and arrival speeds.

Construction and Base Effects

  • Price Ratio: 1.15.
