Environmental Impact

Quarries are listed as industrial structures that contribute to pollution. High levels of pollution can eventually reduce catnip production, kitten happiness, and arrival speeds.

Workshop Upgrades and Uranium

Quarries are essential for the transition into the space era through two specific workshop upgrades:

  • Orbital Geodesy: Unlocked by Satellites, this upgrade allows Quarries to produce uranium at a base rate of 0.0005 per tick. This is a critical alternative for gathering uranium without trading titanium to Dragons.
  • Enriched Uranium: This upgrade provides a +25% bonus specifically to the uranium production rate of Quarries.

Policy Interactions

The effectiveness of Quarries can be modified by foreign relations Policy/:

  • Naga Relations: Masons: This policy provides a +2.5% bonus to slab crafting when using Quarries. This is unlocked by reaching Naga Embassy level 20 and owning the Diplomacy metaphysics upgrade.

Strategic Utility

Quarries are considered a “supplemental production building” necessary to push past resource bottlenecks. They are particularly useful for automating materials needed for Steel, Gears, and Nuclear Reactors. In the deep endgame, maintaining high production from Quarries supports the uranium supply required for Lunar Outposts and Planet Crackers.

item.title: Black Pyramid
item.description:
The Black Pyramid is a significant religious megastructure in the late-game Unicorn/Time Crystal progression path, serving as a gateway to interacting with the powerful Leviathan race.

1. Requirements and Acquisition

The Black Pyramid is a high-cost structure unlocked via the Megalomania metaphysics upgrade.

  • Cost: Building one Black Pyramid requires 5 Sorrow (also known as Black Liquid Sorrow or BLS), 2500 Megalith, 150,000 Spice, and 5000 Unobtainium.
  • Unlock Path: To obtain the necessary resource, the player must first build a Ziggurat, sacrifice 2500 Unicorns for Unicorn Tears, and then refine 10,000 Tears into 1 Sorrow. After collecting 5 Sorrow, the Black Pyramid can be constructed.

2. Effects and Strategic Importance

The construction of the Black Pyramid dramatically shifts the endgame progression by introducing the Leviathans and enhancing subsequent late-game resource mechanisms.
item.content:encoded:
The Black Pyramid is a significant religious megastructure in the late-game Unicorn/Time Crystal progression path, serving as a gateway to interacting with the powerful Leviathan race.

1. Requirements and Acquisition

The Black Pyramid is a high-cost structure unlocked via the Megalomania metaphysics upgrade.

  • Cost: Building one Black Pyramid requires 5 Sorrow (also known as Black Liquid Sorrow or BLS), 2500 Megalith, 150,000 Spice, and 5000 Unobtainium.
  • Unlock Path: To obtain the necessary resource, the player must first build a Ziggurat, sacrifice 2500 Unicorns for Unicorn Tears, and then refine 10,000 Tears into 1 Sorrow. After collecting 5 Sorrow, the Black Pyramid can be constructed.

2. Effects and Strategic Importance

The construction of the Black Pyramid dramatically shifts the endgame progression by introducing the Leviathans and enhancing subsequent late-game resource mechanisms.

  • Leviathan Trading: The primary effect of building a Black Pyramid is that it unlocks trade with the Leviathans. Leviathans are crucial because they allow the player to trade 5000 Unobtainium for scarce resources like Time Crystals (with a 98% chance), Relics (with a 5% chance), and Black Liquid Sorrow (with a 15% chance).
  • Leviathan Appearance: More Black Pyramids mean the Leviathans show up more often.
  • Black Nexus and Relic Production: The Black Pyramid provides a multiplicative bonus to relic generation mechanisms.
    • The Black Nexus upgrade, unlocked at Transcendence Tier 3, produces relics based on the formula: $1 + ({Black Nexus}* Black Pyramid)$ relics.
    • Similarly, Space Beacons upgraded with Relic Station produce relics, and this rate is boosted by $+10%$ relic production per Black Pyramid per Black Nexus.
    • The Pact of Cleansing and Pact of Destruction benefits, which respectively increase global resource limits and global production, scale with the number of Black Pyramids.
  • Challenge Reward: Completing the Black Sky Challenge provides the Base Reward of having Elders arrive early, which acts as a free, invisible Black Pyramid. This invisible structure functions just like a real Black Pyramid, improving the effects of the Black Nexus and other related structures.

The Black Pyramid is described as “A dark relic of unspeakable horrors”. Its acquisition is a key turning point, marking the start of the Unicorn/Time crystal Era and providing access to Time Crystals, which are essential for unlocking Chronospheres and performing prestige resets.

item.title: Unicorn_Utopia
item.description:
Unicorn Utopia is a late-game religious upgrade in Kittens Game that dramatically increases the rate of Unicorn production.

Building and Effects

The Unicorn Utopia is an upgrade for the Unicorn Pasture structure. It is part of the extensive unicorn religious path that culminates in the acquisition of Time Crystals.

Detail Specification Citation
Prerequisite Must complete at least one Sky Palace building.
Cost Requires 5,000 Tears, 1 Million Ivory, and 500 Gold.
Effect Improves unicorn generation by +250%.
Additional Effects Increases alicorn summon chance by $+0.015%$ per game-day.
Production Produces $0.000025$ alicorns per tick ($0.1$ per year).
Time Crystal Bonus Improves the Time Crystal refine ratio by $+5%$ (this bonus applies when turning alicorns into Time Crystals).

The Sunspire is the next upgrade in this line, further boosting unicorn generation by $500%$ and increasing the Time Crystal refine ratio by 10%.

Strategic Importance

The Unicorn Utopia is a key step in the Unicorn/Time Crystal Era of the game. Increasing unicorn and alicorn production is vital because:

  1. Time Crystal Acquisition: Alicorns (which are produced by Sky Palaces, Unicorn Utopias, and Sunspires) must be sacrificed (25 alicorns per Time Crystal) to generate Time Crystals, which are necessary for Chronospheres and endgame progression. The +5% Time Crystal refine ratio boost from the Utopia also makes this conversion more efficient.
  2. Resource Cycling: Strategic guides suggest optimizing for Ivory returns early in the unicorn path by building Ivory Citadels, but later players should transition to Utopias and Sunspires to prepare for the subsequent alicorn mode when working towards Time Crystals and Paragon accumulation.

item.title: Photovoltaic Cells
item.description:
Photovoltaic Cells is a workshop upgrade that significantly increases the power output of your Solar Farms. The upgrade requires the Nanotechnology technology to be researched before it becomes available in the workshop menu. To purchase this enhancement, you must invest 75,000 Science and 5,000 Titanium.

Once purchased, it provides a +50% bonus to the energy production of all constructed Solar Farms. This efficiency modifier is uniquely powerful because it multiplies with other effects affecting Solar Farm output. Solar Farms are a mid-to-late-game structure that replaces Pastures, and their base energy production fluctuates according to the seasons, with peak output occurring during Summer.
item.content:encoded:
Photovoltaic Cells is a workshop upgrade that significantly increases the power output of your Solar Farms. The upgrade requires the Nanotechnology technology to be researched before it becomes available in the workshop menu. To purchase this enhancement, you must invest 75,000 Science and 5,000 Titanium.

Once purchased, it provides a +50% bonus to the energy production of all constructed Solar Farms. This efficiency modifier is uniquely powerful because it multiplies with other effects affecting Solar Farm output. Solar Farms are a mid-to-late-game structure that replaces Pastures, and their base energy production fluctuates according to the seasons, with peak output occurring during Summer.

The bonus from Photovoltaic Cells functions alongside other specialised solar upgrades, such as Thin Film Cells, which provides a +15% boost during winter, and Quantum Dot Cells, which adds further percentage bonuses across the entire year. Stabilising energy production through this upgrade is a critical step in powering high-consumption industrial buildings and advanced space missions.

item.title: Starlink
item.description:
Starlink is a late-game workshop upgrade that enhances the scientific synergy between Bio Labs and Data Centres. It is unlocked after researching the Orbital Engineering technology and requires 175,000 Science, 5,000 Alloy, and 25,000 Oil to purchase.

Mechanical Effects and Synergy

The primary function of Starlink is to increase the maximum science capacity of your colony by linking building counts:

  • Capacity Bonus: Every active Data Centre provides an additional 1% bonus to the maximum science capacity provided by each Bio Lab.
  • Stacking with Uplink: Starlink acts as a follow-up to the Uplink upgrade. While Uplink provides an initial 1% bonus to Bio Lab science per Data Centre (and improves Data Centre caps per Bio Lab), Starlink adds a second 1% modifier, effectively doubling the contribution Bio Labs receive from your Data Centre infrastructure.

Strategic Utility

Scaling the maximum science cap is a critical requirement for late-game progression, as advanced technologies and space missions have resource requirements that eventually exceed base storage limits. Because this bonus is percentage-based and scales with the number of buildings, it allows players to reach the high science thresholds necessary for Exometallurgy (325,000 Science), Tachyon Theory (750,000 Science), and even higher-tier endgame goals.

Because this bonus is percentage-based and scales with the number of buildings, it allows players to reach the high science thresholds necessary for Exometallurgy (325,000 Science), Tachyon Theory (750,000 Science), and even higher-tier endgame goals.

By investing in Starlink, you maximise the return on your terrestrial science buildings, reducing the need to rely solely on Observatories or high-cost Research Vessels to expand your knowledge capacity. This is particularly useful when preparing for Antimatter production or the Unicorn/Time Crystal Era, where science caps must be sufficiently high to craft complex components like Blueprints and Compendiums in mass quantities.

item.title: Oil Refinery
item.description:
Oil Refinery is a mid-game workshop upgrade that increases the resource output of your Oil Wells. It is unlocked by researching the Combustion technology and serves as a key efficiency modifier during the transition from terrestrial industry to space exploration.

Costs and Requirements

To purchase the Oil Refinery upgrade, you must invest the following resources:

  • 125,000 Science
  • 1,250 Titanium
  • 500 Gears

The prerequisite technology, Combustion, requires 115,000 Science and 45 Blueprints.

Mechanical Effects

The primary function of the Oil Refinery is to provide a flat +35% production bonus to all active Oil Wells. This bonus is additive with other terrestrial oil production upgrades:
item.content:encoded:
Oil Refinery is a mid-game workshop upgrade that increases the resource output of your Oil Wells. It is unlocked by researching the Combustion technology and serves as a key efficiency modifier during the transition from terrestrial industry to space exploration.

Costs and Requirements

To purchase the Oil Refinery upgrade, you must invest the following resources:

  • 125,000 Science
  • 1,250 Titanium
  • 500 Gears

The prerequisite technology, Combustion, requires 115,000 Science and 45 Blueprints.

Mechanical Effects

The primary function of the Oil Refinery is to provide a flat +35% production bonus to all active Oil Wells. This bonus is additive with other terrestrial oil production upgrades:

  • Pumpjack: Provides a +45% production boost but adds a 1-Watt energy cost to each Oil Well.
  • Oil Distillation: Provides a +75% production boost.
  • Factory Processing: Increases oil refinement effectiveness by 5% for every active Factory.

Strategic Utility

The Oil Refinery is a critical component for overcoming the oil bottleneck that often occurs before the establishment of high-output space structures.

  1. Scaling for Space Missions: Early space milestones have high oil requirements that far exceed base storage and production rates. For example, an Orbital Launch requires 15,000 oil, a Moon Mission requires 45,000, and a Moon Base requires 70,000. The 35% boost from refineries helps fill these high caps in a reasonable timeframe.
  2. Mitigating Production Slumps: Oil production is inherently slow compared to wood or minerals. By stacking the refinery bonus with Pumpjacks and Oil Distillation, players can achieve a terrestrial production rate capable of sustaining the creation of Kerosene for rocket fuel.
  3. Industrial Independence: Increasing Oil Well efficiency reduces the need to rely on Bio Labs and Biofuel Processing for oil production, allowing those buildings to focus on expanding the science cap.

Strategic advice recommends purchasing the Oil Refinery as soon as Titanium production is stabilised through trade with Zebras, as the increased oil flow is necessary to power Calciners and Magnetos while still saving enough for space mission fuel.

item.title: Pneumatic Press
item.description:
Pneumatic Press is a workshop upgrade that enhances the automation capabilities of Steamworks. It is unlocked by researching the Physics technology and requires 20,000 Science, 30 Gears, and 5 Blueprints to purchase.

Mechanical Effects

The upgrade functions as an extension of the Workshop Automation system. Once enacted, it provides the following benefits:

  • Plate Automation: Steamworks will automatically convert a portion of your iron into plates whenever iron reaches 98% of its maximum storage capacity.
  • Conversion Rate: The amount of iron converted into plates is determined by the number of active Steamworks, following the formula: (2 + 2 * [Number of Steamworks])% of the total resource.
  • Operational Requirements: This automation only triggers when Steamworks are active and powered.

Prerequisites and Context

To access the Pneumatic Press, you must first navigate the mid-game technology tree:
item.content:encoded:
Pneumatic Press is a workshop upgrade that enhances the automation capabilities of Steamworks. It is unlocked by researching the Physics technology and requires 20,000 Science, 30 Gears, and 5 Blueprints to purchase.

Mechanical Effects

The upgrade functions as an extension of the Workshop Automation system. Once enacted, it provides the following benefits:

  • Plate Automation: Steamworks will automatically convert a portion of your iron into plates whenever iron reaches 98% of its maximum storage capacity.
  • Conversion Rate: The amount of iron converted into plates is determined by the number of active Steamworks, following the formula: (2 + 2 * [Number of Steamworks])% of the total resource.
  • Operational Requirements: This automation only triggers when Steamworks are active and powered.

Prerequisites and Context

To access the Pneumatic Press, you must first navigate the mid-game technology tree:

  1. Machinery: Required to build Steamworks and unlock the initial Workshop Automation upgrade.
  2. Physics: The direct prerequisite technology for the Pneumatic Press.
  3. Workshop Automation: The Pneumatic Press is a secondary upgrade in this chain; the base upgrade must be purchased first to enable the conversion of wood to beams and minerals to slabs.

Strategic Utility

The Pneumatic Press is designed to mitigate resource wastage during long idle periods or when iron production exceeds its relatively low terrestrial storage caps. By automatically converting excess iron into plates, the upgrade ensures that production does not halt at the cap and provides a passive income of a critical craftable resource used extensively for Harbours, Factories, and Reactors. This is particularly valuable before reaching the Space Era, where iron becomes a primary trade resource for obtaining titanium.

item.title: Refrigeration
item.description:
Refrigeration is a mid-to-late-game workshop upgrade that significantly enhances your colony’s ability to stockpile food by increasing the global catnip storage capacity by 75%. This upgrade is unlocked by researching the Electronics technology.

Cost and Requirements

To purchase Refrigeration, you must invest the following resources:

  • 125,000 Science
  • 2,500 Titanium
  • 15 Blueprints

Mechanical Effects and Scaling

The primary function of Refrigeration is to apply a percentage-based multiplier to your total catnip capacity provided by all storage structures, such as Barns, Warehouses, and Harbours.
item.content:encoded:
Refrigeration is a mid-to-late-game workshop upgrade that significantly enhances your colony’s ability to stockpile food by increasing the global catnip storage capacity by 75%. This upgrade is unlocked by researching the Electronics technology.

Cost and Requirements

To purchase Refrigeration, you must invest the following resources:

  • 125,000 Science
  • 2,500 Titanium
  • 15 Blueprints

Mechanical Effects and Scaling

The primary function of Refrigeration is to apply a percentage-based multiplier to your total catnip capacity provided by all storage structures, such as Barns, Warehouses, and Harbours.

  • Additive Synergy: This bonus is additive with the bonuses provided by Hydroponics. For example, if you have researched Refrigeration (+75%) and constructed 50 Hydroponics (+10% each for a total of +500%), your total global catnip storage bonus would be +575%.
  • Storage Formula: The final capacity for catnip is calculated by taking the base storage of your buildings and multiplying it by several factors, including building upgrades (like Expanded Barns), the global catnip storage bonus (Refrigeration and Hydroponics), and global storage multipliers from Paragon or Void Rifts.

Strategic Utility

While early-game survival depends on managing production through Farmers and Aqueducts to survive “Cold” winters, Refrigeration becomes available during the Industrial and Space eras. At this stage of development, increasing the catnip “cap” is less about immediate survival and more about resource efficiency.

  • Preventing Waste: Initially, any catnip produced beyond the 5,000-unit starting limit is lost. Expanding this cap allows for a larger buffer during long idle periods or when shifting the workforce entirely into non-food roles like Scholars or Geologists.
  • Refinement Efficiency: Increasing the cap allows players to hold more catnip for mass-conversion into Wood via the “Refine catnip” button, which becomes more efficient after the Catnip Enrichment upgrade.

Think of Refrigeration like upgrading your colony from a standard esky to a professional walk-in freezer; it doesn’t make the catnip grow faster, but it ensures that when your fields are overflowing, you have the room to keep every last leaf fresh for when the winter nosedive hits.

item.title: Register
item.description:
Register is a workshop upgrade that improves kitten workforce efficiency by allowing a leader to manage job assignments based on experience. It is unlocked once you have researched the Writing technology and requires 500 Science and 10 Gold to purchase.

Mechanical Effects

The upgrade automates the optimisation of kitten skills during the assignment process:

  • Skill Prioritisation: When adding kittens to a job, the system automatically selects kittens with the highest relevant experience levels first.
  • Retention of Expertise: Conversely, when unassigning kittens from a job, those with the least experience are removed first, ensuring your most proficient workers remain in their roles.
  • Leader Requirement: This functionality only active if a Leader has been appointed via the Census (unlocked by Civil Service).

Strategic Utility

Kittens gain experience over time as they perform specific tasks, progressing through seven skill tiers from Dabbling (0% bonus) to Master (18.75% bonus). Because these bonuses stack multiplicatively with other productivity modifiers, ensuring the right kittens are in the right jobs is vital for maximising resource output.

Mechanical Effects

The upgrade automates the optimisation of kitten skills during the assignment process:

  • Skill Prioritisation: When adding kittens to a job, the system automatically selects kittens with the highest relevant experience levels first.
  • Retention of Expertise: Conversely, when unassigning kittens from a job, those with the least experience are removed first, ensuring your most proficient workers remain in their roles.
  • Leader Requirement: This functionality only active if a Leader has been appointed via the Census (unlocked by Civil Service).

Strategic Utility

Kittens gain experience over time as they perform specific tasks, progressing through seven skill tiers from Dabbling (0% bonus) to Master (18.75% bonus). Because these bonuses stack multiplicatively with other productivity modifiers, ensuring the right kittens are in the right jobs is vital for maximising resource output.

Register eliminates the need for manual micro-management of individual kittens within the Census tab. It is particularly useful when players frequently reallocate their workforce to resolve bottlenecks—such as moving all kittens to the Farmer job to survive a “Cold” winter or shifting them to Scholars to quickly push through a new technology. Without this upgrade, mass-assigning kittens can inadvertently replace a “Master” worker with a “Dabbling” one, resulting in a significant loss of production efficiency.

item.title: Rotary_Kiln
item.description:
Rotary Kiln is a mid-to-late-game workshop upgrade that significantly enhances the resource output of Calciners,. It is a critical component for automating the production of metals required for advanced industrial and space-based infrastructure,.

Unlocking and Costs

To access the Rotary Kiln upgrade, you must first research the Robotics technology,. The upgrade requires the following resources:

  • 145,000 Science
  • 5,000 Titanium
  • 500 Gears

Mechanical Effects

Once purchased, Rotary Kiln applies a percentage-based bonus to the base production rates of every active Calciner:

  • 500 Gears

Mechanical Effects

Once purchased, Rotary Kiln applies a percentage-based bonus to the base production rates of every active Calciner:

  • Iron Production: Increased by +75%,.
  • Titanium Production: Increased by +225% (effectively making Calciners three times more effective at generating titanium),.

Strategic Utility and Context

In the progression of Kittens Game, Calciners serve as an essential industrial engine that consumes minerals and oil to passively generate iron and titanium,. Rotary Kiln is the second major efficiency upgrade in the Calciner chain, positioned between Oxidation (+95% iron, +285% titanium) and Fluidized Reactors (+100% iron, +300% titanium).

The massive +225% boost to titanium is particularly vital during the “Titanium Era” and early “Space Era”. During these phases, titanium is a primary bottleneck for building Ships, Observatories, and Moon Missions,,. While trading with Zebras is the initial method for acquiring titanium, upgrades like Rotary Kiln allow Calciners to provide a reliable, automated income of the metal, reducing the reliance on manual trading and catpower expenditure,,.

Furthermore, because Calciners also produce iron, this upgrade supports the production of Steel through the Steel Plants upgrade, which automatically converts a portion of a Calciner’s iron output into steel,. This creates a synergistic loop where Rotary Kiln improves iron throughput, which in turn increases the passive generation of steel for advanced components like Gears and Alloy,,.

This upgrade is part of a progression pathway for improving Solar Farm efficiency, following the Photovoltaic Cells upgrade (which gives +50% energy production), and Thin Film Cells (which also boosts winter energy production by +15%). The prerequisite, Thorium science, is a mid-to-late game technology that costs 375,000 Science and 375 Blueprints. Solar Farms are themselves the upgraded replacement for Pastures, unlocked via Ecology science, and they provide energy,,.q

item.title: Steel Plants
item.description:
Steel Plants is a mid-to-late-game workshop upgrade that automates the production of Steel through Calciners., This upgrade is essential for scaling infrastructure without relying solely on manual crafting or the trade loop with Griffins.,,

Unlocking and Costs

To access Steel Plants, you must first research the Robotics technology, which itself requires Electronics., The upgrade costs the following resources:

  • 140,000 Science
  • 3,500 Titanium
  • 750 Gears

Mechanical Effects

Once purchased, Steel Plants modify the output of every active Calciner., The upgrade reserves 10% of the iron produced by Calciners and automatically converts it into Steel at a 100:1 ratio., It also results in a reduction of Coal production equivalent to 10% of the iron output. This provides a consistent, passive income of Steel that functions independently of your kitten workforce.,
item.content:encoded:
Steel Plants is a mid-to-late-game workshop upgrade that automates the production of Steel through Calciners., This upgrade is essential for scaling infrastructure without relying solely on manual crafting or the trade loop with Griffins.,,

Unlocking and Costs

  • 140,000 Science
  • 3,500 Titanium
  • 750 Gears

Once purchased, Steel Plants modify the output of every active Calciner., The upgrade reserves 10% of the iron produced by Calciners and automatically converts it into Steel at a 100:1 ratio., It also results in a reduction of Coal production equivalent to 10% of the iron output. This provides a consistent, passive income of Steel that functions independently of your kitten workforce.,

Synergistic Enhancements

The effectiveness of Steel Plants can be significantly improved through subsequent workshop upgrades and policy choices:

  • Automated Plants: This follow-up upgrade increases the amount of Steel produced by 25% of your general craft ratio without increasing iron or coal consumption.,
  • Nuclear Plants: Unlocked after Automated Plants, this upgrade further boosts Steel production by 2% for every active Reactor you have built.,
  • Griffin Relations (Metallurgists): Choosing this policy provides a flat 15% bonus to the Steel production of Calciners.,

Strategic Utility

Steel is a critical craftable resource required for high-tier buildings like Oil Wells, Steamworks, and Data Centres, as well as advanced alloys like Eludium.,,, In the “Concrete Era” and beyond, the demand for Steel grows exponentially., While early-game Steel is typically managed through manual crafting or Coal Furnaces in Smelters, Steel Plants allow Calciners to become your primary industrial engine, especially when paired with Oxidation to boost iron throughput.,, This automation is particularly valuable during long idles or when Coal production is slow.,

item.title: Uplink
item.description:
Uplink is a mid-to-late-game workshop upgrade that establishes a symbiotic relationship between your terrestrial science buildings. It is unlocked after researching the Satellites technology and requires 75,000 Science and 1,750 Alloy to purchase.

Mechanical Effects

The upgrade provides percentage-based bonuses to the storage and production capacities of Bio Labs and Data Centres based on the number of each building currently constructed:

  • For Data Centres: Each Bio Lab provides a +1% bonus to maximum science, +1% to maximum culture, and +1% to the compendium cap.
  • For Bio Labs: Each Data Centre provides a +1% bonus to maximum science.

Strategic Utility

Uplink is a critical tool for scaling your science and culture caps without solely relying on the construction of new buildings, which become increasingly expensive due to price ratios.
item.content:encoded:
Uplink is a mid-to-late-game workshop upgrade that establishes a symbiotic relationship between your terrestrial science buildings. It is unlocked after researching the Satellites technology and requires 75,000 Science and 1,750 Alloy to purchase.

Mechanical Effects

The upgrade provides percentage-based bonuses to the storage and production capacities of Bio Labs and Data Centres based on the number of each building currently constructed:

  • For Data Centres: Each Bio Lab provides a +1% bonus to maximum science, +1% to maximum culture, and +1% to the compendium cap.
  • For Bio Labs: Each Data Centre provides a +1% bonus to maximum science.

Strategic Utility

Uplink is a critical tool for scaling your science and culture caps without solely relying on the construction of new buildings, which become increasingly expensive due to price ratios.

  1. Science Cap Expansion: By linking Data Centres (upgraded Libraries) and Bio Labs, the upgrade allows players to reach the high science thresholds required for advanced technologies like Particle Physics (185k Science) or Chronophysics (250k Science).
  2. Compendium Efficiency: The +1% bonus to the compendium cap per Bio Lab is particularly valuable. Because compendiums increase science storage by a flat amount (+10), expanding the cap through Uplink allows these crafted resources to provide a significantly higher total storage limit.
  3. Synergy with Starlink: The benefits of Uplink can be further enhanced by the Starlink workshop upgrade, which provides an additional +1% science bonus to Bio Labs for every Data Centre.

This upgrade is essential for transitioning into the Space and Chronophysics eras, where terrestrial buildings alone often fail to provide the storage capacity necessary to progress.

item.title: Void Aspiration
item.description:
Void Aspiration is a late-game workshop upgrade that becomes available after researching the Void Space technology. Enacting this upgrade requires a specific investment of 15 Time Crystals and 2,000 Antimatter.

The primary function of Void Aspiration is to serve as a prerequisite for two advanced structures: Void Hoovers and Void Rifts. Once this upgrade is secured, the following structures can be developed to enhance resource management during the endgame:

  • Void Hoover: These structures increase the maximum amount of void that may be gained during a Temporal Paradox day by 1 unit.
  • Void Rift: Each rift increases the global resource storage ratio by 2%. Additionally, they provide a 10% boost to the energy production of HR Harvesters, which operate on Hawking Radiation from black holes.

Void Aspiration is a critical step in the Chrono-Optimization phase of development. By unlocking Void Rifts, players can stack storage bonuses additively with Event Horizons, allowing them to overcome the terrestrial storage caps that otherwise bottleneck late-game progression. Accessing these structures is necessary for players aiming to establish self-sustaining resource loops through high-count Chronosphere resets.

item.title: Void Reactors
item.description:
Void Reactors is a late-game workshop upgrade that significantly scales your scientific capacity by improving the effectiveness of specific space structures. It requires a substantial investment of 250 Void and 2,500 Antimatter to purchase. To unlock this upgrade, you must first research the Advanced AM Reactors workshop upgrade.

Mechanical Effects and Bonuses

The primary function of Void Reactors is to expand your maximum science cap through the following structures:

  • Research Vessels: Equipping these vessels with Void Reactors increases their contribution to your maximum science by 400%.
  • Space Beacons: Similar to research vessels, this upgrade increases the science storage provided by each Space Beacon by 400%.

Strategic Utility

In the late-game “Relic Era”, increasing your science cap becomes a critical bottleneck for unlocking endgame technologies like Paradox Theory (1M Science) and Exophysics (25M Science). Void Reactors are considered essential for reaching these storage thresholds without needing to build an excessive number of terrestrial buildings like Libraries or Academies. Because the upgrade scales based on structures that are already established for Starchart or Relic production, it provides a high return on investment for players moving toward the “Chrono-Optimization” phase of the game.

The 400% boost from Void Reactors represents the highest tier of science storage efficiency available for these structures, surpassing the bonuses provided by standard Antimatter Reactors (95%) and Advanced AM Reactors (150%). Accessing this level of storage is necessary for performing the “Positive Resets” required to establish a self-sustaining resource loop.

item.title: Storage Bunkers
item.description:
Storage Bunkers is a late-game workshop upgrade that significantly expands your terrestrial storage capacity. It requires an investment of 25,000 Science, 500 Unobtainium, and 1,250 Concrete. To access this upgrade, you must first research the Exogeology technology.

Mechanical Effects and Resource Scaling

The primary function of Storage Bunkers is to increase the maximum storage capacity of specific buildings by 20%. This percentage-based bonus applies to the following structures:

  • Barns
  • Warehouses
  • Harbours
  • Mints (specifically for gold storage)

The resources that receive this 20% capacity boost include wood, minerals, coal, iron, gold, and titanium. Because the bonus is multiplicative with the base storage of these buildings, it scales effectively as you construct more infrastructure.

Strategic Utility

Storage Bunkers are considered a vital upgrade for transitioning into the Eludium and Space eras. Progression often halts when the cost of new buildings or space missions exceeds your maximum storage limits; this upgrade helps push through those “caps” without requiring the construction of a prohibitive number of new buildings.

Strategic advice suggests purchasing Storage Bunkers as soon as you reach the 500 Unobtainium threshold. Expanding storage for metals like Titanium is particularly important for reaching the 125,000 cap needed for Space Manufacturing, which allows your factories to boost the production of space-based structures. Additionally, the increase to gold storage helps in the construction of Temples and the advancement of religious upgrades.

item.title: Unobtainium Saw
item.description:
While the provided sources do not list an upgrade specifically named the Unobtainium Saw, the saw upgrade chain for Lumber Mills concludes with the Alloy Saw. This terminal saw upgrade requires 85,000 Science and 75 Alloy and improves Lumber Mill efficiency by 15%.

Although a saw of this tier is absent, the Woodcutter job features a late-game tool upgrade called the Unobtainium Axe to boost raw wood production. Similarly, the Geologist job can be enhanced with the Unobtainium Drill workshop upgrade, which is unlocked after researching Exogeology. The Unobtainium Drill costs 250,000 Science, 250 Unobtainium, and 1,250 Alloy, providing geologists with +0.015 coal per tick and a potential gold bonus if Geodesy is active.
item.content:encoded:
While the provided sources do not list an upgrade specifically named the Unobtainium Saw, the saw upgrade chain for Lumber Mills concludes with the Alloy Saw. This terminal saw upgrade requires 85,000 Science and 75 Alloy and improves Lumber Mill efficiency by 15%.

Although a saw of this tier is absent, the Woodcutter job features a late-game tool upgrade called the Unobtainium Axe to boost raw wood production. Similarly, the Geologist job can be enhanced with the Unobtainium Drill workshop upgrade, which is unlocked after researching Exogeology. The Unobtainium Drill costs 250,000 Science, 250 Unobtainium, and 1,250 Alloy, providing geologists with +0.015 coal per tick and a potential gold bonus if Geodesy is active.

Unobtainium is used for several other high-tier efficiency and storage upgrades:

  • Unobtainium Huts: Reduces the price ratio of Huts by 25%, allowing for significantly higher population caps.
  • Unobtainium Reflectors: Increases the maximum science capacity provided by each Observatory by 2%.
  • Storage Bunkers: Uses unobtainium and concrete to increase the storage capacity of Warehouses, Barns, Harbours, and Mints by 20%.
  • Eludium: Unobtainium is a required material for crafting Eludium, a composite of 1,000 Unobtainium and 2,500 Alloy used for endgame space structures.

The primary method for acquiring unobtainium is refining Uranium at a Lunar Outpost on Redmoon, a process that consumes 1.75 Uranium per second to produce 0.035 Unobtainium per second.

item.title: Void Energy
item.description:
Void Energy is a mid-to-late game workshop upgrade designed to significantly expand the resource storage capacity provided by Accelerators. This upgrade is a critical component of the “Energy Rift” storage chain, which allows industrial buildings to compete with terrestrial storage like Barns and Warehouses.

Costs and Prerequisites

To purchase Void Energy, you must first research the Stasis Chambers workshop upgrade. The upgrade requires the following resources:

  • 275,000 Science
  • 250 Alloy
  • 2,500 Uranium
  • 2 Time Crystals

The inclusion of Time Crystals in the cost indicates that Void Energy is a gateway upgrade into the Chronophysics era, where temporal resources begin to influence standard terrestrial infrastructure.
item.content:encoded:
Void Energy is a mid-to-late game workshop upgrade designed to significantly expand the resource storage capacity provided by Accelerators. This upgrade is a critical component of the “Energy Rift” storage chain, which allows industrial buildings to compete with terrestrial storage like Barns and Warehouses.

Costs and Prerequisites

To purchase Void Energy, you must first research the Stasis Chambers workshop upgrade. The upgrade requires the following resources:

  • 275,000 Science
  • 250 Alloy
  • 2,500 Uranium
  • 2 Time Crystals

The inclusion of Time Crystals in the cost indicates that Void Energy is a gateway upgrade into the Chronophysics era, where temporal resources begin to influence standard terrestrial infrastructure.

Mechanical Effects on Storage

The primary function of Void Energy is to make Energy Rifts (the initial storage-enabling upgrade for Accelerators) “even more effective”.

  • Storage Bonus: It provides a flat +75% increase to the resource storage ratio for Accelerators.
  • Affected Resources: This bonus applies to the maximum capacity of catnip, wood, minerals, coal, iron, titanium, and gold.
  • Additive Scaling: The +75% bonus stacks additively with other Accelerator storage upgrades. In a fully optimized late-game setup, Void Energy contributes to a total maximum Accelerator storage bonus of +920% when combined with Stasis Chambers (+95%), Dark Energy (+250%), and Tachyon Accelerators (+500%).

Strategic Utility

Void Energy is essential for overcoming the resource storage “caps” that act as a primary bottleneck for late-game progression. Once buildings like Mansions or advanced Space Missions cost more than your maximum storage allows, progress halts until those caps are raised.

Because Accelerators primarily produce Uranium and consume Titanium, the Energy Rift chain (including Void Energy) allows players to repurpose their industrial power into a massive storage solution. This is particularly useful for reaching the high Titanium and Science caps required for the Eludium and Relic eras, as terrestrial buildings eventually become prohibitively expensive due to steep price ratios. Proper investment in these upgrades allows Accelerators to provide a substantial percentage of a colony’s total storage, often surpassing the utility of Harbours in the very late game.

item.title: Advanced Automation
item.description:
The term Advanced Automation refers to a crucial Workshop upgrade in Kittens Game that enhances the efficiency of your industrial production system.

Here are the specific details regarding this upgrade:

  • Prerequisite Technology: Advanced Automation is unlocked by researching the Industrialization technology.
  • Building Association: This upgrade is associated with the Steamworks building.
  • Cost: The upgrade requires 100,000 Science, 75 Gears, and 25 Blueprints.
  • Effect: The Advanced Automation upgrade causes the core Workshop Automation function to be activated twice per year.
  • Timing: The source notes the upgrade specifically triggers “Steamworks Production: Fall”. Since the original Workshop Automation occurs in Spring, Advanced Automation allows this useful conversion process to run during a second season.

Context of Workshop Automation: The Workshop Automation function itself (unlocked by the Machinery technology) converts small quantities of resources (Wood into Beams and Minerals into Slabs) when those resources are near 98% of their storage limit, typically occurring annually in Spring. Advanced Automation doubles the frequency of this passive resource management, making it more effective at preventing resource bottlenecks and generating necessary materials automatically.

item.title: Coal Furnace
item.description:
The Coal Furnace is a vital Workshop upgrade in Kittens Game used to establish an early supply of Coal.

Here is a comprehensive breakdown of the upgrade:

Prerequisites and Cost

  • Prerequisite Technology: The Coal Furnace upgrade is unlocked once you research the Steel technology.
  • Cost: Acquiring the Coal Furnace requires 5,000 Science, 5,000 Minerals, 2,000 Iron, and 35 Beam.

Function and Strategic Importance

The Coal Furnace upgrade affects your Smelters, which are industrial buildings primarily used to create Iron and Gold.
item.content:encoded:
The Coal Furnace is a vital Workshop upgrade in Kittens Game used to establish an early supply of Coal.

Here is a comprehensive breakdown of the upgrade:

Prerequisites and Cost

  • Prerequisite Technology: The Coal Furnace upgrade is unlocked once you research the Steel technology.
  • Cost: Acquiring the Coal Furnace requires 5,000 Science, 5,000 Minerals, 2,000 Iron, and 35 Beam.

Function and Strategic Importance

The Coal Furnace upgrade affects your Smelters, which are industrial buildings primarily used to create Iron and Gold.

  • Effect: It allows your Smelters to produce Coal while simultaneously burning wood.
  • Production Rate: The Smelters generate Coal at a rate of 0.005 coal per tick (which is 0.025 per second).

The Coal Furnace is one of two key upgrades (the other being Deep Mining) introduced when you research Steel that enable you to accumulate Coal. Coal is essential later in the game because it is consumed to power advanced buildings, such as the Steamworks.

Strategically, players are advised to prioritize researching Steel first (over Philosophy or Machinery) to immediately access upgrades like the Coal Furnace, which helps strengthen the foundational economy. However, once you research Steel and the related coal upgrades, the general advice is to acquire the necessary workshop upgrades, then allow Coal to max out, as Coal is used to produce Iron which is highly valuable for building Lumber Mills and Observatories.

item.title: Deep Mining
item.description:
The term Deep Mining refers to a crucial Workshop upgrade in Kittens Game that helps establish coal production during the mid-game phase.

Here are the specific details regarding the Deep Mining upgrade:

  • Prerequisite Technology: Deep Mining is unlocked when you research the Steel technology.
  • Building Affected: This upgrade specifically enhances the performance of Mines.
  • Cost: To acquire the Deep Mining upgrade, you must spend 5,000 Science, 1,200 Iron, and 50 Beam.
  • Effect: Deep Mining allows your Mines to produce Coal.
    • The production rate is 0.003 Coal per tick, which equates to 0.015 per second.

Deep Mining is introduced at the same time as the Coal Furnace upgrade (which allows Smelters to produce Coal). Both upgrades are important early steps for accumulating Coal, a resource necessary for later industrial buildings like the Steamworks and for crafting Steel and Gears.

item.title: Expanded_Barns
item.description:
The Expanded Barns upgrade is a storage improvement available in the Workshop tab of Kittens Game, specifically designed to increase your capacity for core resources.

Here is a detailed explanation based on the sources:

Function and Effects

The primary effect of Expanded Barns is to increase the maximum resource limits of your essential storage buildings:

  • Storage Increase: The upgrade increases the maximum storage for wood, minerals, and iron provided by Barns, Warehouses, and Harbors by 75%.
  • Catnip Bonus (Conditional): If the Silos upgrade is purchased, Expanded Barns, along with all other storage upgrades containing the word “barns” in their name, will apply 25% of their effect to maximum Catnip storage as well.

This upgrade is crucial because resource storage limits are a major bottleneck that can greatly slow progress in the game.
item.content:encoded:
The Expanded Barns upgrade is a storage improvement available in the Workshop tab of Kittens Game, specifically designed to increase your capacity for core resources.

Here is a detailed explanation based on the sources:

Function and Effects

The primary effect of Expanded Barns is to increase the maximum resource limits of your essential storage buildings:

  • Storage Increase: The upgrade increases the maximum storage for wood, minerals, and iron provided by Barns, Warehouses, and Harbors by 75%.
  • Catnip Bonus (Conditional): If the Silos upgrade is purchased, Expanded Barns, along with all other storage upgrades containing the word “barns” in their name, will apply 25% of their effect to maximum Catnip storage as well.

This upgrade is crucial because resource storage limits are a major bottleneck that can greatly slow progress in the game.

Cost and Prerequisites

Expanded Barns is an early-game upgrade, available before more advanced storage solutions are developed:

  • Cost: The upgrade costs 500 Science, 1,000 Wood, 750 Minerals, and 50 Iron.
  • Prerequisite: There is no specific prerequisite listed for this upgrade in the source material (indicated by a dash in the prerequisite column of the storage table). The foundational building it upgrades, the Barn, is unlocked after researching Agriculture.

Context within Storage Progression

Expanded Barns is part of a series of storage upgrades designed to continuously increase the capacity provided by Barns and related structures:

Upgrade Effect on Max Storage (Wood, Minerals, Iron)
Expanded Barns +75% increase
Reinforced Barns +80% increase
Titanium Barns +100% increase (twice as many resources)
Alloy Barns +100% increase (twice as many resources)
Concrete Barns +75% increase

Building Barns is advised early on, as they are essential for increasing the capacity for Catnip and Wood, which helps in surviving the challenges of Winter.

Analogy: If your civilization’s maximum resource storage is a set of buckets, the Expanded Barns upgrade acts like slightly increasing the size of those initial buckets (Barns, Warehouses, Harbors). This allows you to accumulate a larger reserve of core building materials (wood, minerals, iron) before hitting the resource cap, similar to how adding a larger fuel tank allows a car to travel further between refueling stops.

item.title: Reinforced_Saw
item.description:
The Reinforced Saw is an upgrade available in the Workshop tab of Kittens Game, specifically designed to improve wood production.

Here is a breakdown of the upgrade:

Function and Effect

The Reinforced Saw improves the efficiency of your Lumber Mills:

  • Effect: It increases the efficiency of each Lumber Mill by an additional +20% (lumberMillRatio).
  • Context: Improving wood output is strategically important because wood accumulates slowly, especially in the early game, until you invest in Lumber Mills.

Requirements and Cost

To purchase the Reinforced Saw, you must have researched the necessary technology and accumulated the required resources:
item.content:encoded:
The Reinforced Saw is an upgrade available in the Workshop tab of Kittens Game, specifically designed to improve wood production.

Here is a breakdown of the upgrade:

Function and Effect

The Reinforced Saw improves the efficiency of your Lumber Mills:

  • Effect: It increases the efficiency of each Lumber Mill by an additional +20% (lumberMillRatio).
  • Context: Improving wood output is strategically important because wood accumulates slowly, especially in the early game, until you invest in Lumber Mills.

Requirements and Cost

To purchase the Reinforced Saw, you must have researched the necessary technology and accumulated the required resources:

  • Prerequisite: The technology Construction must be researched to unlock this upgrade.
  • Cost: The upgrade costs 2,500 Science and 1,000 Iron.

Progression

The Reinforced Saw is part of a progression of workshop upgrades aimed at boosting Lumber Mill efficiency:

  1. Reinforced Saw: +20% efficiency per Lumber Mill (requires Construction).
  2. Steel Saw: +20% efficiency per Lumber Mill (requires Physics and Steel Saw).
  3. Titanium Saw: +15% efficiency per Lumber Mill (requires Titanium Saw).
  4. Alloy Saw: +15% efficiency per Lumber Mill (requires Titanium Saw).

Construction, the prerequisite technology, is unlocked after researching Animal Husbandry. Lumber Mills themselves are structures unlocked by Construction. Lumber Mills are often necessary because Wood accumulates “reeeaallyyyy slowlyyyy” until they are built, which requires Iron.

item.title: Astrolabe
item.description:
The Astrolabe is a crucial Workshop upgrade in Kittens Game that enhances the effectiveness of the Observatory building, primarily by boosting your capacity for science storage.

Details of Astrolabe

Category Specification Citation

Prerequisite Unlocked after researching the Navigation technology ,
Cost 25,000 Science, 5 Titanium, and 75 Starchart
Effect Improves Observatory effectiveness by 50%, specifically increasing the Observatory’s Max Science storage by +50% ,

The standard Observatory building already increases maximum Science storage by 1,000. With the Astrolabe upgrade, this capacity is further boosted by 50%.

The standard Observatory building already increases maximum Science storage by 1,000. With the Astrolabe upgrade, this capacity is further boosted by 50%.

item.title: Expanded_Cargo
item.description:
Expanded Cargo is a significant mid-game upgrade focused on augmenting the storage capacity provided by Harbours, which are structures essential for managing resources acquired through trading.

Details and Effects

Detail Specification Citation
Type Workshop Upgrade
Prerequisite Unlocked after researching the Navigation technology
Cost 55,000 Science and 15 Blueprints
Effect Each Trade Ship provides a +1% bonus to Harbour capacity ,,

Storage Expansion Specifics

The bonus provided by Expanded Cargo applies to all resources stored by Harbours, including Catnip.
item.content:encoded:
Expanded Cargo is a significant mid-game upgrade focused on augmenting the storage capacity provided by Harbours, which are structures essential for managing resources acquired through trading.

Details and Effects

Detail Specification Citation
Type Workshop Upgrade
Prerequisite Unlocked after researching the Navigation technology
Cost 55,000 Science and 15 Blueprints
Effect Each Trade Ship provides a +1% bonus to Harbour capacity ,,

Storage Expansion Specifics

The bonus provided by Expanded Cargo applies to all resources stored by Harbours, including Catnip.

  • The increased storage scales with the number of Trade Ships you possess.
  • The bonus is subject to diminishing returns starting past 168.75%, with a maximum limit of 225%,,.
  • This maximum capacity limit can be further increased by subsequent research: the Reactor Vessel upgrade adds a +5% increase to the Harbour capacity limit per Reactor.

Expanded Cargo is important because, as you acquire more Trade Ships to accelerate titanium and iron gathering via trading with Zebras,, it concurrently boosts the capacity of your Harbours, helping to manage the large volumes of resources generated through trade.

item.title: Geodesy
item.description:
In Kittens Game, Geodesy refers to two specific Workshop upgrades that are essential for automating the production of gold and uranium.

Geodesy (Workshop Upgrade)

  • Requirements: Unlocked via the Geology technology. It costs 90,000 Science, 250 Titanium, and 500 Starcharts.
  • Mechanics: This upgrade enables kittens assigned to the Geologist job to produce gold (+0.0008 per tick) and increases their coal production (+0.0075 per tick).
  • Strategic Importance: It is a critical mid-game upgrade used to resolve gold bottlenecks. Gold is required for trading with other civilisations, building Temples, and purchasing Tradeposts. Once Geodesy is active, players often move most kittens to the Geologist job to power a high-volume trade engine, which becomes the primary source of iron and titanium in the mid-to-late game.

Orbital Geodesy (Workshop Upgrade)

  • Requirements: Unlocked via the Satellites technology. It costs 150,000 Science, 1,000 Alloy, and 35,000 Oil.
  • Mechanics: This upgrade allows Quarries to passively produce uranium at a rate of 0.0005 per tick.
  • Strategic Importance: Orbital Geodesy is foundational for the transition into the space era. It allows for the accumulation of uranium without the need to trade titanium to Dragons, which is vital for maintaining the uranium supply required to run Lunar Outposts. It is considered highly beneficial when pushing toward Unobtainium Huts, as it simplifies the management of the resources needed for Moon Bases.

Comparison of Geodesy Upgrades

Feature Geodesy Orbital Geodesy
Prerequisite Tech Geology Satellites
Primary Resource Gold Uranium
Affected Unit Geologist (Kitten Job) Quarry (Building)
Science Cost 90,000 150,000
Primary Utility Scaling trade and religion Passive fuel for space missions

While Geodesy focuses on kitten-based labour to drive the economy through trade and cultural expansion, Orbital Geodesy focuses on industrial automation to provide the radioactive materials necessary for advanced space travel and unobtainium production.

item.title: Oil_Distillation
item.description:
Oil Distillation refers to a specific Workshop upgrade in Kittens Game.

Here is a breakdown of the relevant information regarding this upgrade:

  • Prerequisite: The Oil Distillation upgrade is unlocked after researching the Rocketry technology. Rocketry itself is unlocked by Electronics.
  • Cost: The upgrade requires 175,000 Science and 5,000 Titanium.
  • Effect: Oil Distillation provides a significant boost to your oil production, as it improves Oil Well output by 75%. The Oil Well building description explicitly notes this upgrade’s effect: “+75%”.
  • Mechanics: This 75% bonus to Oil Well output is additive with other oil output boosters, such as the bonuses received from the Oil Refinery and Pumpjack upgrades.

The Oil Processing technology, which enables the creation of Kerosene, is associated with the Oil Distillation upgrade.

Context and Strategic Importance

The Oxidation upgrade provides a massive boost to titanium production ($+285%$) from Calciners, making it a critical step during the “Titanium era” and subsequent resource phases where titanium is a necessary component for advanced buildings, research, and crafting,. Calciners are complex buildings that already refine iron and titanium from minerals and oil,. Oxidation dramatically increases the efficiency of this conversion process, helping to alleviate titanium bottlenecks,.

Oxidation is one of several upgrades within the Calciner upgrade path, alongside others like Rotary Kiln and Fluidized Reactors, which further enhance iron and titanium output,.

Photolithography represents the final stage of automated manuscript production, following the initial Printing Press upgrade (unlocked by Machinery) and the intermediate Offset Press (unlocked by Combustion),,.

Automated manuscript production ensures that the flow of this vital cultural resource keeps pace with the increasing demands of high-level technology,.

item.title: Printing_Press
item.description:
The Printing Press is a vital Workshop upgrade in Kittens Game that automates the production of Manuscripts, helping the player overcome a significant mid-game resource bottleneck.

Unlocking and Functionality

  1. Prerequisite: The Printing Press upgrade is tied to the Machinery technology. Machinery is unlocked after researching Writing, and costs 15,000 Science.
  2. Building Integration: The Printing Press is specifically used in conjunction with the Steamworks building. Steamworks, which consume Coal and provide Energy, can automatically print Manuscripts after this upgrade is acquired.
  3. Production Rate: The Steamworks start producing Manuscripts at a rate of 0.0025 manuscripts/sec with the Printing Press upgrade.

Strategic Importance

The Printing Press is a crucial step in resolving the mid-game Manuscript bottleneck, which gates progression to advanced technologies like Theology and Astronomy.
item.content:encoded:
The Printing Press is a vital Workshop upgrade in Kittens Game that automates the production of Manuscripts, helping the player overcome a significant mid-game resource bottleneck.

Unlocking and Functionality

  1. Prerequisite: The Printing Press upgrade is tied to the Machinery technology. Machinery is unlocked after researching Writing, and costs 15,000 Science.
  2. Building Integration: The Printing Press is specifically used in conjunction with the Steamworks building. Steamworks, which consume Coal and provide Energy, can automatically print Manuscripts after this upgrade is acquired.
  3. Production Rate: The Steamworks start producing Manuscripts at a rate of 0.0025 manuscripts/sec with the Printing Press upgrade.

Strategic Importance

The Printing Press is a crucial step in resolving the mid-game Manuscript bottleneck, which gates progression to advanced technologies like Theology and Astronomy.

  • Manuscript Generation: Prior to automation, Manuscripts must be manually crafted using scarce resources (Parchment from Furs, acquired through Hunting, and Culture from Amphitheatres/Temples). The Printing Press provides an automated source of Manuscripts, converting the high-cost materials (Coal, Iron, Blueprints) required for Steamworks into sustained cultural output.
  • Technological Progression: While acquiring the necessary materials—including Blueprints and Gears (which require Steel)—to build Steamworks can present its own hurdle, establishing automated Manuscript production allows the player to bypass the tedious and slow process of manual crafting.
  • Challenge Mode: The Printing Press is particularly critical in the Pacifism Challenge, where Hunting is unavailable. Since Hunting is the primary source of Furs (needed to craft Parchment), and therefore Manuscripts, the Pacifism Challenge dictates that the player must rely on Mints (to generate Furs/Ivory) and the Printing Press to get the required Manuscripts for progression.

Further Upgrades

The effectiveness of the Printing Press can be significantly improved by later technologies:

  • Offset Press: This upgrade (unlocked by Combustion) is four times as effective, raising Steamworks output to 0.01 manuscripts/sec.
  • Photolithography: This further upgrade (unlocked by Satellites) increases the printing effectiveness again, raising the rate to 0.04 manuscripts/sec.

item.title: Pumpjack
item.description:
The Pumpjack is a crucial mid-game Workshop upgrade in Kittens Game that enhances the efficiency of Oil Wells while introducing a modest energy requirement.

Key Details and Effects

Category Specification Citation
Type Workshop Upgrade for Oil Wells ,
Prerequisite Technology Mechanization ,
Cost 100,000 Science, 250 Titanium, and 125 Gear
Effect Improves Oil Well effectiveness by +45% (additive with other effects like Oil Refinery and Oil Distillation) ,
Energy Oil Wells will now consume 1 Watt (Wt) Energy each ,

Strategic Context

The Pumpjack is essential for accelerating oil production, which is a key bottleneck resource for several subsequent upgrades and buildings, including Kerosene production (rocket fuel),, and space missions such as the Moon Mission.

Strategic Context

The Pumpjack is essential for accelerating oil production, which is a key bottleneck resource for several subsequent upgrades and buildings, including Kerosene production (rocket fuel),, and space missions such as the Moon Mission.

  • Production Boost: The $+45%$ boost to oil output significantly increases your supply, especially when combined with other oil production upgrades like Oil Refinery and Oil Distillation.
  • Energy Management: While it boosts production, the upgrade introduces a base energy cost (1 Wt) to Oil Wells. This reinforces the need for stable energy infrastructure, achieved through buildings like Steamworks and Magnetos or renewable upgrades like Solar Farms and Hydro Plants.

To achieve the necessary technological prerequisite, Pumpjack requires researching Mechanization,, which itself is unlocked via the Industrialization technology path,.

You can think of the Pumpjack as standardising and improving the oil extraction process: it makes your Oil Wells yield significantly more resource, but requires electricity to run the machinery.

item.title: Silos
item.description:
The query refers to Silos, which is a highly important Workshop upgrade in Kittens Game focused on expanding resource storage, particularly for Catnip.

1. Unlocking and Cost

  • Prerequisite Technology: Silos is unlocked after researching Ironwood Huts.
  • Cost: Researching the Silos upgrade requires 50,000 Science, 125 Steel, and 5 Blueprints.

2. Key Effects and Functionality

Silos fundamentally changes how resource storage buildings (Barns, Warehouses, and Harbours) function by enabling the storage of Catnip in structures beyond just Barns, and by enhancing the effectiveness of all general storage upgrades.
item.content:encoded:
The query refers to Silos, which is a highly important Workshop upgrade in Kittens Game focused on expanding resource storage, particularly for Catnip.

1. Unlocking and Cost

  • Prerequisite Technology: Silos is unlocked after researching Ironwood Huts.
  • Cost: Researching the Silos upgrade requires 50,000 Science, 125 Steel, and 5 Blueprints.

2. Key Effects and Functionality

Silos fundamentally changes how resource storage buildings (Barns, Warehouses, and Harbours) function by enabling the storage of Catnip in structures beyond just Barns, and by enhancing the effectiveness of all general storage upgrades.

  • Warehouse Catnip Storage: After Silos is researched, each Warehouse begins to increase maximum Catnip capacity by +750. Warehouses are initially unlocked by researching Construction.
  • Barn Upgrade Bonus Application: Silos causes all storage upgrades that contain the word “barns” in their name (e.g., Expanded Barns, Reinforced Barns, Titanium Barns, Alloy Barns, Concrete Barns, and Concrete Pillars) to apply 25% of their effect to the maximum Catnip capacity as well. This dramatically boosts Catnip storage capacity. For example, the maximum total bonus applied to Catnip storage via this mechanic from all relevant upgrades is $+108.75%$.
  • Warehouse and Harbour Storage Bonus: This same bonus calculation also applies to the Catnip capacity provided by Warehouses and Harbours.

3. Strategic Importance

This upgrade is vital in the mid-game, as managing the Catnip surplus and deficit is a core mechanic of the game.

  • Catnip Stability: While the base Catnip storage capacity starts at 5,000, each Kitten consumes 4.25 Catnip per second. Expanding storage capacity is crucial for surviving harsh Winters, where Catnip production from Catnip Fields can drop by 75% or more. Silos allows the player to overcome storage limits and build up massive stockpiles needed for long-term food security and efficient wood refinement.
  • Technological Progression: The ability to craft this upgrade requires a decent industrial base to produce Steel and acquire Blueprints.

Think of Silos as converting your general storage buildings into food warehouses. Before Silos, only specialised agricultural structures (Barns) could hold your food supply, limiting your stockpile size. With Silos, every Warehouse and Harbour you build can now help keep your community fed, turning industrial storage into emergency reserves.

item.title: Marker
item.description:
Acquisition and Costs

  • Prerequisite: To unlock the ability to build a Marker, you must first purchase the Megalomania metaphysics upgrade.
  • Base Cost: Building your first Marker requires a substantial investment of 5,000 Tears, 750 Megaliths, 50,000 Spice, and 2,500 Unobtainium.
  • Price Ratio: The cost scales with a 1.15 price ratio for each subsequent Marker you build.

Core Effects

  • Alicorn Corruption (Necrocorns): Building a Marker starts a ticking corruption countdown that slowly converts your accumulated Alicorns into Necrocorns. Having multiple Markers will reduce the amount of time it takes to produce a Necrocorn.
  • Leviathan Energy Cap: Each Marker increases the maximum energy capacity of the Leviathans (Elders) by 5. This allows you to feed them more Necrocorns, which permanently improves your trade yields with them.
  • Summoning Leviathans: Markers multiply the probability of Leviathans arriving to trade with your civilization. However, it is crucial to note that you must have at least one Black Pyramid constructed; having Markers alone will never cause the Leviathans to appear.

Challenges and Upgrades

  • Black Sky Challenge: Completing the Black Sky challenge directly enhances your Markers. For each run completed, the Marker’s corruption factor and its Leviathan energy cap increase are both improved by 10% (this is capped at 200% with diminishing returns setting in at 150%).

item.title: Steel
item.description:
Steel is a mid-game technology and a critical craftable resource in Kittens Game, marking a major step toward industrialization and advanced building construction.

Here is a comprehensive overview of Steel based on the sources:

Steel Technology

The technology named Steel has the following characteristics:

  • Prerequisite: It is unlocked after researching Writing.
  • Cost: Researching Steel requires 12,000 Science.
  • Strategic Timing: Steel is one of the three “specialist Techs” available after Writing (alongside Philosophy and Machinery). Strategic advice suggests researching Steel first among these three options to acquire useful upgrades that strengthen your economy.

Steel Resource (Crafting and Composition)

Steel is a Craftable Resource.
item.content:encoded:
Steel is a mid-game technology and a critical craftable resource in Kittens Game, marking a major step toward industrialization and advanced building construction.

Here is a comprehensive overview of Steel based on the sources:

Steel Technology

The technology named Steel has the following characteristics:

  • Prerequisite: It is unlocked after researching Writing.
  • Cost: Researching Steel requires 12,000 Science.
  • Strategic Timing: Steel is one of the three “specialist Techs” available after Writing (alongside Philosophy and Machinery). Strategic advice suggests researching Steel first among these three options to acquire useful upgrades that strengthen your economy.

Steel Resource (Crafting and Composition)

Steel is a Craftable Resource.

  • Composition: Steel is made by combining 100 Iron and 100 Coal.
  • Acquisition: The research of the Steel technology enables the resource Steel.
  • Trading: Steel can also be acquired through trade, notably from Griffins, who sell 25 Steel per trade once you reach Embassy Level 5. Griffins buy Wood.

Key Unlocks and Upgrades

Researching Steel unlocks critical Workshop Upgrades, many of which focus on resource efficiency and early Coal production:

Upgrade Name Cost Components (Examples) Primary Effect
Coal Furnace Science, Minerals, Iron, Beam Allows Smelters to produce 0.005 Coal per tick while burning wood.
Deep Mining Science, Iron, Beam Allows Mines to produce 0.003 Coal per tick.
Steel Axe Science, Steel Makes Woodcutters 50% more effective.
Reinforced Warehouses Science, Plate, Steel, Scaffold Increases resource storage in Warehouses, Barns, Harbours, and Mints by 25%.
Steel Armour Science, Steel Provides a +0.5 Hunting bonus.
Steel Saw Science, Steel Improves Lumber Mill efficiency by 20%.
High Pressure Engine Science, Gear, Blueprint Reduces Steamworks coal consumption by 20%.

Usage in Buildings and Crafting

Steel is crucial for moving beyond basic construction into industrial and specialized buildings:

  • Advanced Materials: Steel is required for crafting Gears.
  • Industrial Buildings:
    • The Steamworks building requires 65 Steel (along with 20 Gear and 1 Blueprint).
    • The Quarry building requires 125 Steel.
    • The Calciner building requires 100 Steel.
  • Housing: It is required for the mid-game Mansion building (75 Steel).
  • Crafting: Steel is a component of Concrete, which is crafted from 25 Steel and 2500 Slab.

Strategic Notes

  • Early Coal: Steel is essential because it unlocks the upgrades (Coal Furnace and Deep Mining) necessary to begin accumulating Coal. Coal is required to craft Steel itself, and to power industrial structures like the Steamworks.
  • Iron Priority: Once Steel is researched and the coal-producing upgrades are acquired, players are often advised to let Coal production max out. This is because the Iron used to produce Coal is highly valuable and better prioritized for building Lumber Mills and Observatories.
  • Trade Importance: Trading with Zebras yields Iron, which can then be converted into Steel. This trade route helps maintain a supply of Steel, especially once it becomes a bottleneck for future buildings.

item.title: Trade_Ship
item.description:
Trade Ships are a craftable resource in Kittens Game essential for enabling trade with other civilisations, particularly for acquiring late-game bottleneck resources like titanium.

Unlocking and Crafting

  • Prerequisite: Trade Ships are unlocked after researching Navigation science, which itself requires Astronomy (28K Science, 65 Manuscripts) and 100 Manuscripts to research.
  • Crafting Cost: Crafting a single Trade Ship requires:
    • 100 Scaffold
    • 150 Plate
    • 25 Starchart
  • Cost Reduction: The starchart requirement to craft Trade Ships can be reduced by the Satellite Navigation upgrade, offering a 1.25% discount per active Satellite, up to a maximum discount of 75%. At 45 Satellites, the cost reaches 10.9375 Starcharts, where diminishing returns begin.

Functionality and Strategic Importance

Trade Ships serve several critical roles in resource acquisition and infrastructure:
item.content:encoded:
Trade Ships are a craftable resource in Kittens Game essential for enabling trade with other civilisations, particularly for acquiring late-game bottleneck resources like titanium.

Unlocking and Crafting

  • Prerequisite: Trade Ships are unlocked after researching Navigation science, which itself requires Astronomy (28K Science, 65 Manuscripts) and 100 Manuscripts to research.
  • Crafting Cost: Crafting a single Trade Ship requires:
    • 100 Scaffold
    • 150 Plate
    • 25 Starchart
  • Cost Reduction: The starchart requirement to craft Trade Ships can be reduced by the Satellite Navigation upgrade, offering a 1.25% discount per active Satellite, up to a maximum discount of 75%. At 45 Satellites, the cost reaches 10.9375 Starcharts, where diminishing returns begin.

Functionality and Strategic Importance

Trade Ships serve several critical roles in resource acquisition and infrastructure:

  1. Enabling Exploration and Trade: Owning at least one Trade Ship is the prerequisite for discovering and trading with the Zebras.
  2. Acquisition of Titanium: Trade Ships are critical for solving the titanium bottleneck. Zebras sell Titanium in amounts determined by the number of Trade Ships you possess, via the formula (0.03 * Trade Ships) + 1.5. Importantly, this amount of titanium acquired is not affected by normal trading bonuses like those from Tradeposts.
  3. Storage Enhancement: Trade Ships enhance the storage capacity of Harbours through the Expanded Cargo Workshop upgrade. Each Trade Ship provides a +1% bonus to Harbour capacity, subject to diminishing returns past 168.75% and a maximum limit of 225%. This limit can be further increased by +5% per active Reactor if the Reactor Vessel upgrade is researched.
  4. Mid-Game Progression: Accumulating Trade Ships accelerates the titanium and iron acquisition necessary for constructing advanced buildings, such as Observatories. Due to the high iron requirement of Observatories, gaining titanium from Zebras allows you to stock up on resources needed to progress to the next technological tier.

Strategic Notes

  • Trade Ships are listed as a craftable resource that increases oil limit when crafted into a Tanker.
  • Starcharts are a significant bottleneck for this stage of the game, making the acquisition of Observatories—which increase the chance of astronomical events and subsequent starchart production—a high priority to sustain Trade Ship construction.
  • In the endgame, Trade Ships are sometimes ignored in favor of mints for Blueprint generation, but later become the fastest possible reset method when trading is used to acquire the blueprints needed for Chronospheres.

item.title: Oil Storage
item.description:
The storage limit for Oil starts at a base capacity and can be increased through the construction of specific buildings and the crafting of specialized items.

Here is a breakdown of how to increase your Oil storage capacity:

Base Oil Storage

The initial, default storage capacity for Oil is 1,500.

Increasing Oil Storage Capacity

You can increase the maximum limit of Oil through the following methods:

  1. Oil Wells: The building used to produce oil, the Oil Well, also increases your maximum oil storage. Each Oil Well provides +1500 Max Oil.

  2. Tankers (Crafted Ships): Oil storage can be significantly increased by crafting and building Tankers.

    • A Tanker is a crafted item that increases the maximum oil capacity by 500 [3, 4].
    • Tankers are crafted in the Workshop, requiring 200 Ships, 1,250 Alloy, and 5 Blueprints [4].
    • The ability to craft Tankers is unlocked by researching Robotics science [4, 5].

  3. Space Structures: Late-game structures contribute to storage, particularly when combined with specific Metaphysics upgrades:

    • Cryostation: This structure’s storage capacity is affected by the T-minus cycle, which can provide a +20% boost to its storage [6, 7].
    • Cryostations are a highly useful method for increasing resource capacity, providing +750 Titanium storage per unit, among other resources [7].

The storage limit for Oil starts at a base capacity and can be increased through the construction of specific buildings and the crafting of specialized items.

Here is a breakdown of how to increase your Oil storage capacity:

Base Oil Storage

The initial, default storage capacity for Oil is 1,500.

Increasing Oil Storage Capacity

You can increase the maximum limit of Oil through the following methods:

  1. Oil Wells: The building used to produce oil, the Oil Well, also increases your maximum oil storage. Each Oil Well provides +1500 Max Oil.

  2. Tankers (Crafted Ships): Oil storage can be significantly increased by crafting and building Tankers.

    • A Tanker is a crafted item that increases the maximum oil capacity by 500 [3, 4].
    • Tankers are crafted in the Workshop, requiring 200 Ships, 1,250 Alloy, and 5 Blueprints [4].
    • The ability to craft Tankers is unlocked by researching Robotics science [4, 5].

  3. Space Structures: Late-game structures contribute to storage, particularly when combined with specific Metaphysics upgrades:

    • Cryostation: This structure’s storage capacity is affected by the T-minus cycle, which can provide a +20% boost to its storage [6, 7].
    • Cryostations are a highly useful method for increasing resource capacity, providing +750 Titanium storage per unit, among other resources [7].

Strategic Considerations for Oil Storage

In the latter stages of the game, particularly during the push toward Metaphysics and space missions, acquiring sufficient Oil capacity is a significant bottleneck [8]:

  • The Lunar Outpost mission requires 55K oil storage [9].
  • The Orbital Launch requires 15K oil, the Moon Mission requires 45K oil, and the subsequent Moon Base requires 70K oil [8, 10].
  • The general strategy suggested is to build Oil Wells quickly and let them “fill up,” then buy space structures as soon as possible so the wells have time to refill [8, 11].
  • The upgrade Oil Distillation, unlocked by Rocketry, boosts oil production by 75%, which helps in replenishing the stock, but does not increase the maximum capacity [8, 12].

As you progress, the primary focus shifts to crafting and building Tankers and later utilizing advanced structures like Cryostations to meet the large oil capacity requirements [7, 13, 14].

item.title: Energy
item.description:
Power generation, referred to in the game as Energy, is produced by specific advanced buildings and structures, typically unlocked starting in the mid-game, and becomes increasingly important as pollution and energy consumption penalties become factors [1-3].

Here is a breakdown of the buildings that produce Energy:

Buildings Producing Energy

Building/Upgrade Technology Prerequisite Energy Produced (Base) Notes Source
Steamworks Machinery +1 Wt This building consumes coal, and the High Pressure Engine and Fuel Injector upgrades reduce its coal consumption [4-7]. [4]
Magneto Electricity +5 Wt This building consumes oil at a rate of $0.05$ per tick [4, 8]. [4]
Solar Farm (Upgrade of Pasture) Ecology +2 Wt Solar Farms are safer to upgrade to than Hydro Plants. They produce +1.5 Wt in Winter and +2.67 Wt in Summer [9-11]. [9]
Hydro Plant (Upgrade of Aqueduct) Robotics +5 Wt Upgrading Aqueducts to Hydro Plants should be approached cautiously as it can lead to starvation if catnip production is insufficient [9, 11, 12]. [9]
Reactor Nuclear Fission +10 Wt Reactors consume uranium at a rate of $0.001$ per tick [4, 13]. [4]
Satellite Satellites +1 Wt Satellites initially consume 1 Wt, but with the Solar Satellites upgrade (unlocked by Orbital Engineering), they produce +1 Wt instead of consuming it [7]. [7, 9, 14]
Sunlifter N/A (Space Structure) N/A (Antimatter) Sunlifters produce Antimatter when the year changes, provided energy is positive [15]. [15]
Advanced Energy Challenge Buildings N/A N/A The Energy challenge requires unlocking and building at least one of every energy production building and space structure, which includes Steamworks, Magneto, Solar Farms, Hydro Plant, Reactor, Satellite, Sunlifter, Tectonic, and HR Harvester [3]. [3]

Energy Boosts and Management

Energy production and consumption can be managed through various upgrades and cycles:
