Hydro Plant (Upgrade of Aqueduct) Robotics +5 Wt Upgrading Aqueducts to Hydro Plants should be approached cautiously as it can lead to starvation if catnip production is insufficient [9, 11, 12]. [9]
Reactor Nuclear Fission +10 Wt Reactors consume uranium at a rate of $0.001$ per tick [4, 13]. [4]

Energy Boosts and Management

Energy production and consumption can be managed through various upgrades and cycles:

  • Reactor Upgrades: The Cold Fusion upgrade increases Reactor energy output by 2.5 Wt (+25%) [16]. The Thorium Reactors upgrade also increases Reactor energy output by $0.25$ Wt (+25%) [16].
  • Solar Farm Upgrades: Photovoltaic Cells increase Solar Farm energy production by +50% [7]. Thin Film Cells and Quantum Dot Cells provide further percentage increases, especially in specific seasons [7].
  • Oil Wells: The Pumpjack upgrade for Oil Wells increases oil output by 45% and causes Oil Wells to consume 1 Wt of energy [16].
  • Cycles: The Helios cycle increases Sunlifter energy output by +50% [17]. Conversely, the T-minus cycle decreases Sunlifter energy output by -50% [17].
  • Policy/: The Dark Nova cryptotheology upgrade provides a +2% global energy production bonus [18].

Maintaining positive energy is vital, as a negative energy balance will result in production penalties [3, 19]. Pollution is partially mitigated by using environmentally friendly energy sources [2].

item.title: Cath
item.description:
Cath (${⌾}$) refers to two distinct concepts within Kittens Game: the name of the solar system where the game takes place, and a specific five-year astrological cycle.

1. The Cath Solar System

Cath is the name of the solar system in which the star Helios resides, which is a G2V spectral type star at the system’s centre. The core resources of the game, such as unobtainium, are produced on planets or satellites within the Cath solar system.
item.content:encoded:
Cath (${⌾}$) refers to two distinct concepts within Kittens Game: the name of the solar system where the game takes place, and a specific five-year astrological cycle.

1. The Cath Solar System

Cath is the name of the solar system in which the star Helios resides, which is a G2V spectral type star at the system’s centre. The core resources of the game, such as unobtainium, are produced on planets or satellites within the Cath solar system.

2. The Cath Astrological Cycle

Cath is one of the ten planetary cycles in the time system, with each cycle lasting five years. It is identified by the glyph ${⌾}$. The effects of this cycle are only triggered once the Numerology upgrade has been researched.

Category Detail
Duration 5 years
Glyph ${⌾}$

Effects with Numerology:

When the Cath cycle is active, it provides several bonuses and a specific penalty related to space structures:

  • Space Elevator transfer production bonus (for oil only): Increased by $+100%$. The Space Elevator structure also has its conversion production (resources produced by Smelters, Calciners, and Accelerators) on Cath boosted by a bonus of $0.4%$ per leader rank per uncapped population buildings.
  • Satellite starchart production: Increased by $+100%$.
  • Satellite observatory’s science bonus: Increased by $+100%$.
  • Space Station science bonus: Increased by $+50%$.
  • Space Beacon starchart production: Decreased by $-50%$.

Festival Effect with Numeromancy:

If the advanced Numeromancy upgrade is researched, holding a festival during the Cath cycle grants a significant $\times 2$ multiplier to Catpower income.

item.title: Charon
item.description:
Charon refers to a late-game deep space mission destination and is also one of the ten astronomical cycles in the Kittens Game time system.

1. Charon Space Mission

The Charon Mission targets a small, dense, and distant dwarf planet located on the far edge of the Helios system, sometimes grimly referred to as ‘The Gates of Death’.

Detail Specification
Prerequisite Unlocked after completing the Umbra Mission.
Cost 75,000 Starchart, 750,000 Science, 35,000 Kerosene, and 35,000 Thorium.
Travel Time 25,000 game-days, which equals 13 hours, 53 minutes, and 20 seconds in real-time. Travel time can be significantly reduced by researching drive upgrades such as the Antimatter Drive and Thorium Drive.
Unlocks Successful completion unlocks the Charon Planet.

2. Charon Astrological Cycle

Charon (${⍙}$) is one of the ten planetary cycles, each lasting five years. Its effects are triggered upon researching advanced Metaphysics upgrades:

1. Charon Space Mission

The Charon Mission targets a small, dense, and distant dwarf planet located on the far edge of the Helios system, sometimes grimly referred to as ‘The Gates of Death’.

Detail Specification
Prerequisite Unlocked after completing the Umbra Mission.
Cost 75,000 Starchart, 750,000 Science, 35,000 Kerosene, and 35,000 Thorium.
Travel Time 25,000 game-days, which equals 13 hours, 53 minutes, and 20 seconds in real-time. Travel time can be significantly reduced by researching drive upgrades such as the Antimatter Drive and Thorium Drive.
Unlocks Successful completion unlocks the Charon Planet.

2. Charon Astrological Cycle

Charon (${⍙}$) is one of the ten planetary cycles, each lasting five years. Its effects are triggered upon researching advanced Metaphysics upgrades:

  • With Numerology: The cycle negatively impacts specific structures related to Unobtainium (UO) and gigaflops:
    • Lunar Outpost unobtainium output is decreased by $-10%$.
    • Entanglement Station gigaflops consumption is increased by $+100%$.
  • Festival Effect (With Numeromancy): If a festival is held during the Charon cycle, it provides a $\times 1.5$ multiplier to Catnip, Wood, and Mineral income.

The severe penalty to Lunar Outpost production during the Charon cycle is notable, especially when compared to the highly advantageous Redmoon cycle, which boosts UO production by $+20%$. Due to this, strategies often revolve around skipping non-profitable cycles, like Charon, using time manipulation.

item.title: Dune
item.description:
Dune (${⍫}$) is a pivotal mid-to-late-game space destination, a planet in the Cath solar system, which unlocks new industrial structures and is tied to a specific astrological cycle that boosts uranium production.

1. Dune Space Mission Details

Dune is described as a large, lifeless planet covered by sand and volcanic rock. The Dune Mission is unlocked after successfully completing the Moon Mission.

Detail Specification
Prerequisite Moon Mission
Cost 1000 Starchart, 7000 Titanium, 175k Science, and 75 Kerosene
Travel Time 356 game-days (11 minutes, 52 seconds in real-time)
Unlocks Helios mission

2. Key Structures and Policy/ Unlocked

Successful completion of the mission unlocks the Dune Planet and critical infrastructure:
item.content:encoded:
Dune (${⍫}$) is a pivotal mid-to-late-game space destination, a planet in the Cath solar system, which unlocks new industrial structures and is tied to a specific astrological cycle that boosts uranium production.

1. Dune Space Mission Details

Dune is described as a large, lifeless planet covered by sand and volcanic rock. The Dune Mission is unlocked after successfully completing the Moon Mission.

Detail Specification
Prerequisite Moon Mission
Cost 1000 Starchart, 7000 Titanium, 175k Science, and 75 Kerosene
Travel Time 356 game-days (11 minutes, 52 seconds in real-time)
Unlocks Helios mission

2. Key Structures and Policy/ Unlocked

Successful completion of the mission unlocks the Dune Planet and critical infrastructure:

  • Planet Cracker: A vessel that generates Uranium (1.5/sec). Building this structure requires a significant investment in Starcharts: 1000 Starchart to reach Dune, and 2500 Starchart to build the cracker itself.
  • Hydraulic Fracturer: A structure that produces Oil (2.5/sec). Hydraulic Fracturers are generally not particularly effective until the Space Manufacturing upgrade is secured.
  • Spice Refinery: Refines Dune sand into ‘Spice’ at a rate of 0.125/sec.

Reaching Dune is also a prerequisite for unlocking several high-level Government Policy/, including Technocracy, Cosmological Libertarianism, and Order of the Stars.

3. Dune Astrological Cycle

Dune (${⍫}$) is one of the ten cycles in the game’s time system, with each cycle lasting five years. The effects of this cycle are leveraged by researching Metaphysics upgrades like Numerology and Numeromancy:

  • With Numerology: The cycle provides significant production bonuses for resources generated on Dune: it increases Planet Cracker uranium output by +10% and Hydraulic Fracturer oil output by +50%. Conversely, it imposes a penalty on HR Harvester Energy Production (-25%).
  • With Numeromancy (Festival Bonus): Holding a festival during the Dune cycle grants a $\times 2$ multiplier to Uranium income.

item.title: Furthest Ring
item.description:
The Furthest Ring is a late-game deep space mission destination, metaphorically described as “The end of the universe”.

Mission Details and Cost

The Furthest Ring mission requires extremely high quantities of resources:

  • Cost: 500,000 Starchart, 1.25 million Science, 75,000 Kerosene, and 75,000 Thorium.
  • Base Travel Time: The base travel time for the mission is massive, calculated at 725,200,000 game-days.

Travel Time Reduction

This extensive travel time can be significantly reduced through drive upgrades:
item.content:encoded:
The Furthest Ring is a late-game deep space mission destination, metaphorically described as “The end of the universe”.

Mission Details and Cost

The Furthest Ring mission requires extremely high quantities of resources:

  • Cost: 500,000 Starchart, 1.25 million Science, 75,000 Kerosene, and 75,000 Thorium.
  • Base Travel Time: The base travel time for the mission is massive, calculated at 725,200,000 game-days.

Travel Time Reduction

This extensive travel time can be significantly reduced through drive upgrades:

  • If you have researched both the Antimatter Drive and the Thorium Drive, the mission travel time is divided by 75.
  • With both drive upgrades, the travel time is reduced to approximately 223 days, 19 hours, 51 minutes, and 7 seconds in real-time.

Status

Currently, the mission’s unlock is listed as “(TBD)”. As of one source’s reported version (1.4.6.2.b), no structures can be built in the Furthest Ring. However, as of a later version (1.4.8.5), players who are logged in will see a text-based interface when they reach the Furthest Ring.

item.title: Helios
item.description:
Helios refers to a pivotal deep space mission destination—a G2V spectral type star in the centre of the Cath solar system—and a recurring astrological cycle. It is also the designated goal for one of the game’s major challenges.

Here is a detailed breakdown of Helios:

1. Helios Space Mission

The Helios mission is a significant undertaking that occurs in the mid-to-late game, following the Dune Mission.

Detail Specification
Prerequisite Unlocked after the Dune Mission (also unlocked by the T-minus Mission).
Cost 3,000 Starchart, 15,000 Titanium, 250k Science, and 1,250 Kerosene.
Travel Time 1,200 game-days, which is 40 minutes in real-time.
Structures Unlocked Successful completion unlocks high-tier structures needed for antimatter and storage capacity: Sunlifter, Containment Chamber, Heatsink, and Sunforge.
Next Mission The Helios Mission unlocks the Yarn Mission.

2. Helios Astrological Cycle

Helios is one of the ten cycles in the time system, identified by the glyph ⌒. Each cycle lasts for five years.

Kairo (${℣}$) refers to a deep space destination reachable via a mission and a recurring astrological cycle that significantly impacts late-game production, particularly starcharts.

Space Beacon Building

Successfully completing the Kairo Mission unlocks the Space Beacon structure.

item.title: Lunar Outpost
item.description:
A Lunar Outpost is a space structure essential for late-game progression, specifically for refining uranium into unobtainium.

Here is a comprehensive overview of the Lunar Outpost based on the sources:

Primary Function and Resources

The Lunar Outpost serves a single, critical purpose:

  • It refines uranium into unobtainium. Unobtainium is a special resource required to unlock Metaphysics and to purchase high-tier buildings and upgrades, including Unobtainium Huts.
  • Consumption Rate: The Lunar Outpost consumes uranium at a rate of 1.75 per second.
  • Production Rate: It produces unobtainium at a rate of 0.035 per second. This means, at full speed, it can produce 5 unobtainium in 142.8 seconds (about 2.3 minutes).

Acquisition and Prerequisites

The Lunar Outpost is unlocked and built through the Space tab:
item.content:encoded:
A Lunar Outpost is a space structure essential for late-game progression, specifically for refining uranium into unobtainium.

Here is a comprehensive overview of the Lunar Outpost based on the sources:

Primary Function and Resources

The Lunar Outpost serves a single, critical purpose:

  • It refines uranium into unobtainium. Unobtainium is a special resource required to unlock Metaphysics and to purchase high-tier buildings and upgrades, including Unobtainium Huts.
  • Consumption Rate: The Lunar Outpost consumes uranium at a rate of 1.75 per second.
  • Production Rate: It produces unobtainium at a rate of 0.035 per second. This means, at full speed, it can produce 5 unobtainium in 142.8 seconds (about 2.3 minutes).

Acquisition and Prerequisites

The Lunar Outpost is unlocked and built through the Space tab:

  • Prerequisite: You must first research the Rocketry science to enable the Space tab and space missions [5, 6].
  • Mission Requirement: The Lunar Outpost itself is unlocked by completing the Moon Mission.
  • Starchart Cost: To complete the Lunar Outpost mission, you need 650 Starcharts [7]. The total starcharts needed to reach the Lunar Outpost, starting from the Orbital Launch (250) and Moon Mission (500), is 1,400 Starcharts [7].
  • Other Costs: The Moon Mission itself also requires 45K oil [8].

Production Efficiency and Optimization

The Lunar Outpost’s production of unobtainium is noted for its inefficiency relative to its resource consumption, which heavily bottlenecks early unobtainium production:

  • Production Slowdown: If your main source of uranium is a single Accelerator (which produces $0.0125$ uranium per second), the Lunar Outpost will run 140 times slower than its maximum speed [9]. This means it could take 5.3 hours to produce 5 unobtainium, rather than 2.3 minutes [4, 9].
  • Trade Solution: Production can be sped up by trading with Dragons for uranium [9].
  • Redshift Advantage (Offline): The source notes that the “Redshift” mechanic, which prevents resources from being deliberately reduced during offline progression, effectively allows Lunar Outposts to run as if you have infinite uranium while offline. This significantly speeds up unobtainium gain during offline progress because the outpost runs at full speed [10].
  • Upgrades: The Microwarp Reactors Workshop upgrade, unlocked by Exometallurgy, makes unobtainium production 75% more effective [11].

Related Space Structures

The Lunar Outpost is key to later resource storage and production:

  • Moon Base: Once you produce 50 unobtainium using the Lunar Outpost, you can build a Moon Base [12]. The Moon Base then increases your overall Unobtainium storage capacity [12, 13].
  • Uranium Consumption: Lunar Outposts initially consume 10 Wt of Energy, although this consumption is reduced by Antimatter Bases [14].

In short, the Lunar Outpost is the specialized factory on the moon that converts titanium-derived uranium into the scarce, late-game resource unobtainium, paving the way for further progression into space and metaphysics [1, 4].

item.title: Piscine
item.description:
Piscine (${⎈}$) refers to a significant destination in the late mid-game space race, resulting in infrastructure critical for advancing scientific research and generating Starcharts. It is also one of the astronomical cycles in the game’s time system.

1. Piscine Space Mission

The Piscine mission targets a gigantic aquatic planet characterised by an acid body and a methane atmosphere.

Detail Specification
Prerequisite Unlocked after successfully completing the Moon Mission.
Cost Requires 1500 Starchart, 9000 Titanium, 200k Science, and 250 Kerosene.
Travel Time 256 game-days (8 minutes, 32 seconds in real-time).
Unlocks Unlocks the Piscine Planet, the Research Vessel building, and the T-minus Mission.

The Pisces Mission is a major investment point, requiring 1500 Starcharts to bypass the starchart bottleneck needed for continued space progression.
item.content:encoded:
Piscine (${⎈}$) refers to a significant destination in the late mid-game space race, resulting in infrastructure critical for advancing scientific research and generating Starcharts. It is also one of the astronomical cycles in the game’s time system.

1. Piscine Space Mission

The Piscine mission targets a gigantic aquatic planet characterised by an acid body and a methane atmosphere.

Detail Specification
Prerequisite Unlocked after successfully completing the Moon Mission.
Cost Requires 1500 Starchart, 9000 Titanium, 200k Science, and 250 Kerosene.
Travel Time 256 game-days (8 minutes, 32 seconds in real-time).
Unlocks Unlocks the Piscine Planet, the Research Vessel building, and the T-minus Mission.

The Pisces Mission is a major investment point, requiring 1500 Starcharts to bypass the starchart bottleneck needed for continued space progression.

2. Research Vessel Building

The successful mission unlocks the Research Vessel building, which is crucial for maximizing scientific progress:

  • Science Storage: Each Research Vessel provides a substantial increase of +10,000 maximum Science.
  • Starchart Production: They are highly efficient, generating 0.05 Starchart per second. Research Vessels are considered the most efficient way to acquire Starcharts.

3. Piscine Astrological Cycle

Piscine (${⎈}$) is one of the ten planetary cycles in the time system, each lasting five years.

  • Numerology Effect: With the Numerology upgrade, the Piscine cycle offers contrasting effects on space production:
    • Research Vessel starchart production is boosted by +50%.
    • Hydroponics Catnip Production is decreased by -50%.
  • Festival Effect (Numeromancy): If the Numeromancy upgrade is researched, holding a festival during the Piscine cycle grants a powerful $\times 2$ multiplier to Science income.

The Piscine Mission unlocks Research Vessels, which are essential for boosting science maximums and generating Starcharts efficiently, setting the stage for the next deep space ventures like the T-minus Mission. This allows you to convert high-cost materials into a sustained, high-volume flow of Starcharts needed for future space exploration.

item.title: Redmoon
item.description:
Redmoon (${⍜}$) is both a key destination in the space exploration phase and a recurring astronomical cycle in Kittens Game, offering significant advantages for late-game production, particularly of Unobtainium (UO).

1. Redmoon as a Planetary Mission

Redmoon is a planet satellite targeted during the mid-to-late game space race:

  • Mission Unlock: The Moon Mission is unlocked after the Orbital Launch and requires 500 Starchart, 5000 Titanium, 125,000 Science, and 45,000 Oil to launch.
  • Travel Time: The journey to Redmoon takes 30 game-days, equivalent to 1 minute in real-time.
  • Unlocks: A successful mission unlocks the Lunar Outpost and the Moon Base structures, as well as the subsequent Dune Mission and Piscine Mission.

2. Buildings on Redmoon

The mission allows for the establishment of two critical structures on Redmoon:
item.content:encoded:
Redmoon (${⍜}$) is both a key destination in the space exploration phase and a recurring astronomical cycle in Kittens Game, offering significant advantages for late-game production, particularly of Unobtainium (UO).

1. Redmoon as a Planetary Mission

Redmoon is a planet satellite targeted during the mid-to-late game space race:

  • Mission Unlock: The Moon Mission is unlocked after the Orbital Launch and requires 500 Starchart, 5000 Titanium, 125,000 Science, and 45,000 Oil to launch.
  • Travel Time: The journey to Redmoon takes 30 game-days, equivalent to 1 minute in real-time.
  • Unlocks: A successful mission unlocks the Lunar Outpost and the Moon Base structures, as well as the subsequent Dune Mission and Piscine Mission.

2. Buildings on Redmoon

The mission allows for the establishment of two critical structures on Redmoon:

  • Lunar Outpost: This nuclear-powered mining outpost is crucial for the Unobtainium economy. It consumes Uranium (at a rate of 1.75/sec) and produces Unobtainium (at 0.035/sec).
  • Moon Base: This base provides large storage increases for core resources, notably providing +45,000 maximum Catnip and +150 maximum Unobtainium storage.

3. Redmoon Astrological Cycle

Redmoon (${⍜}$) is one of the ten astronomical cycles in the game’s time system, with each cycle lasting five years. Its effects are highly advantageous for players who have researched advanced Metaphysics:

  • With Numerology: When the Numerology upgrade is researched, the Redmoon cycle affects specific space production:
    • Lunar Outpost unobtainium output is increased by +20%.
    • Entanglement Station gigaflops consumption is decreased by -50%.
  • Festival Effect (With Numeromancy): If the Numeromancy upgrade is researched, holding a festival during the Redmoon cycle grants a potent $\times 2$ multiplier to Unobtainium income.

Strategic Importance in Endgame

The Redmoon cycle is strategically crucial in the endgame, particularly for advancing the Unobtainium (UO) economy:

  • UO Production: Since Unobtainium is a critical bottleneck resource refined from Uranium by the Lunar Outpost, the Redmoon cycle’s +20% boost to Lunar Outpost output (with Numerology) is highly leveraged.
  • Chrono-Optimization: The Redmoon cycle is part of the Chrono Engine strategy. Using the Chronoforge to shatter Time Crystals (TCs) allows players to skip less profitable periods and arrive at the highly advantageous Redmoon cycle, which provides an instantaneous $2.5\times$ boost to UO production when combined with active Festivals and the Numeromancy upgrade. This strategy converts stored temporal capital (TCs) into a leveraged spike in high-value resource production.
  • Unobtainium Production Formula: If you are always in the Redmoon cycle, the formula for UO production gains an extra factor of $2.4* (1 + 0.01* # Breweries)$ when Numeromancy is researched. Therefore, spending time inside a Redmoon cycle is key for maximising unobtainium production.

item.title: T Minus
item.description:
T-minus (⍝) refers to both a significant deep space mission destination and a recurring astronomical cycle in Kittens Game.

1. T-Minus Space Mission and Structures

The T-minus Mission targets Terminus, a supermassive ice giant at the far end of the Helios solar system.

Detail Specification
Prerequisite The T-minus Mission is unlocked after the Piscine Mission.
Cost 2,500 Starchart, 12,000 Titanium, 225,000 Science, and 750 Kerosene.
Travel Time 2,500 game-days (1 hour, 23 minutes, 20 seconds in real-time).
Unlocks Successful completion unlocks the T-Minus Planet, the Helios Mission, the Kairo Mission, and the Cryostation building.

Cryostation Building: The Cryostation, unlocked by this mission, is a vast storage facility complex that provides significant capacity increases for wood, minerals, iron, coal, uranium, titanium, oil, and unobtainium. Critically, each Cryostation provides $+750$ maximum Unobtainium (UO) storage. UO capacity, specifically from Cryostations and Moon Bases, defines the deep endgame progression toward positive chrono-resets.

item.title: Umbra
item.description:

Umbra is one of the ten cycles featured in the game’s time system, identified by the glyph ${⍦}$. Each cycle lasts for five years.

When the appropriate technologies are researched, the Umbra cycle provides specific bonuses and penalties:

2. Umbra Mission and HR Harvester

Umbra is a destination in deep space, described as a supermassive black hole at the heart of the Helios system.

Here is a detailed overview of the Yarn Mission, its costs, and the resulting infrastructure:

Yarn Space Mission

The Yarn Mission targets a Class M planet described as having a high moderate climate, seas, and an oxygen atmosphere.
item.content:encoded:
Yarn is a key deep space destination in Kittens Game, leading to new structures that boost population, catnip production, and scientific progression. It is identified by the symbol ${⍧}$ in the game’s astrological time system.

Here is a detailed overview of the Yarn Mission, its costs, and the resulting infrastructure:

Yarn Space Mission

The Yarn Mission targets a Class M planet described as having a high moderate climate, seas, and an oxygen atmosphere.

Detail Specification
Prerequisite The Yarn Mission is unlocked after the Helios Mission.
Cost 7,500 Starchart, 35,000 Titanium, 350,000 Science, and 12,000 Kerosene.
Travel Time 3,800 game-days (2 hours, 6 minutes, 40 seconds in real-time).
Unlocks Successful completion unlocks the Yarn Planet and the next step in deep space exploration, the Umbra Mission.

Infrastructure Unlocked on Yarn Planet

Completing the mission allows for the construction of two crucial buildings, provided the necessary technologies have been researched:

  1. Terraforming Station: This structure requires the Terraformation research.

    • Cost: 25 Antimatter, 5,000 Uranium, and 5,000 Kerosene.
    • Effect: Increases maximum kitten population by +1.
    • Terraforming Yarn is noted as a necessary action for maximizing housing during deep endgame paragon farming runs.

  2. Hydroponics: This highly efficient agricultural structure requires the Hydroponics technology.

    • Cost: 1 Unobtainium and 500 Kerosene.
    • Effects: Hydroponics provides a +2.5% increase to Catnip Production and increases maximum Catnip Storage capacity by +10%. It also boosts the kitten bonus from the Terraforming Station by $+1.0%$.

Yarn Astrological Cycle

Yarn (${⍧}$) is one of the ten astronomical cycles in the game, each lasting five years. The cycle has specific effects depending on advanced research:

  • With Numerology: The cycle significantly boosts Hydroponics Catnip Production by +100%. However, it imposes a penalty on Research Vessel starchart production, decreasing it by $-50%$.
  • With Numeromancy: If a festival is held during the Yarn cycle, it provides a powerful $\times 2$ multiplier to Culture income.

item.title: Science
item.description:
Science is a critical resource in Kittens Game, essential for technological advancement, unlocking new capabilities, and progressing to later stages of the game.

Here is an explanation of how Science is acquired, its uses, and how its capacity is managed:

Acquisition and Production

Science is categorized as a Special Resource. Its accumulation is boosted by global factors, including Paragon and Religion production boosts.

  1. Kitten Jobs: Science is primarily generated by the Scholar profession. You should employ Scholars to ensure continuous accumulation, as Techs are crucial for progression.
  2. Buildings: Science production is generated by several buildings:
    • Library (unlocked at 25 Wood): Provides +10% Science per tick.
    • Academy (unlocked by Mathematics): Provides +20% Science per tick.
    • Observatory (unlocked by Astronomy): Provides +25% Science per tick.
    • Bio Lab (unlocked by Biology): Provides +35% Science per tick.
    • Data Center: An upgrade to the Library, it also provides +10% Science per tick.
  3. Events: You can gain Science by observing astronomical events. After building your first Library, these events have a chance to occur daily. Meteors also grant minerals and science. The Celestial Mechanics upgrade grants an additional 20% bonus to science generated by celestial events and meteors (60% bonus in Iron Will mode).
  4. Policy/: Policy/ such as Rationality (+5% science production) and Knowledge Sharing (+5% science income) can increase accumulation rates.

Usage and Role in Progression

Science is essential for expanding your civilization by unlocking new content.

Science is a critical resource in Kittens Game, essential for technological advancement, unlocking new capabilities, and progressing to later stages of the game.

Here is an explanation of how Science is acquired, its uses, and how its capacity is managed:

Acquisition and Production

Science is categorized as a Special Resource. Its accumulation is boosted by global factors, including Paragon and Religion production boosts.

  1. Kitten Jobs: Science is primarily generated by the Scholar profession. You should employ Scholars to ensure continuous accumulation, as Techs are crucial for progression.
  2. Buildings: Science production is generated by several buildings:
    • Library (unlocked at 25 Wood): Provides +10% Science per tick.
    • Academy (unlocked by Mathematics): Provides +20% Science per tick.
    • Observatory (unlocked by Astronomy): Provides +25% Science per tick.
    • Bio Lab (unlocked by Biology): Provides +35% Science per tick.
    • Data Center: An upgrade to the Library, it also provides +10% Science per tick.
  3. Events: You can gain Science by observing astronomical events. After building your first Library, these events have a chance to occur daily. Meteors also grant minerals and science. The Celestial Mechanics upgrade grants an additional 20% bonus to science generated by celestial events and meteors (60% bonus in Iron Will mode).
  4. Policy/: Policy/ such as Rationality (+5% science production) and Knowledge Sharing (+5% science income) can increase accumulation rates.

Usage and Role in Progression

Science is essential for expanding your civilization by unlocking new content.

  1. Purchasing Technologies (Techs): Science is spent to purchase Techs, which grant new information and abilities. Techs must generally be unlocked in sequence, and they are crucial for game progression. However, the cost of sciences escalates very quickly, and players should avoid prioritizing new sciences too aggressively before securing production and caps.
  2. Crafting Advanced Resources: Science is required in the Workshop tab for converting intermediate resources into higher-tier resources:
    • Compendium: Crafted from 50 Manuscripts and 10,000 Science. Compendiums improve the maximum science limit.
    • Blueprint: Crafted from 25 Compendiums and 25,000 Science. Blueprints are required for late-game technologies and automated industry buildings like the Steamworks.
  3. Workshop Upgrades: Science is a resource used to buy various permanent upgrades in the Workshop tab.

Science Capacity and Storage

All resources, including Science, have a maximum storage limit (cap). Reaching this limit can greatly slow progress. Science has a default maximum capacity of 250.

The maximum Science storage (cap) can be increased by various structures and upgrades:

  • Libraries, Academies, and Labs:
    • Library: +250 Max Science.
    • Academy: +500 Max Science.
    • Observatory: +1000 Max Science.
    • Bio Lab: +1500 Max Science.
    • Data Center (upgraded Library): +750 Max Science.
  • Upgrades and Policy/:
    • LHC (unlocked by Dimensional Physics): Grants +2,500 Max Science per Accelerator.
    • Technocracy policy (Government tree): Increases science cap by +20%.
    • Titanium Reflectors, Unobtainium Reflectors, Eludium Reflectors: These upgrades, linked to Observatories, increase the maximum science bonus of Libraries/Data Centers by 2% per Observatory.
    • Uplink/Starlink: These upgrades cause Data Centers and Bio Labs to provide bonuses to each other’s maximum science capacity.

item.title: Manuscript
item.description:
The Manuscript is a critical mid-game crafted resource that serves as a bottleneck for advancing the main scientific and religious technology trees in Kittens Game.

Here is a detailed overview of Manuscripts, their production, cost, and vital strategic role:

1. Acquisition and Crafting

Manuscripts are produced in the Workshop by converting the precursor resource, Parchment, using the resource Culture.

Input Resource Base Cost per Manuscript Cost with Tradition Policy
Parchment (Crafted from Furs) 25 units 20 units
Culture (Generated by Amphitheatres/Temples) 400 units 300 units

Manuscripts are required to continue the technology line after Philosophy.
item.content:encoded:
The Manuscript is a critical mid-game crafted resource that serves as a bottleneck for advancing the main scientific and religious technology trees in Kittens Game.

Here is a detailed overview of Manuscripts, their production, cost, and vital strategic role:

1. Acquisition and Crafting

Manuscripts are produced in the Workshop by converting the precursor resource, Parchment, using the resource Culture.

Input Resource Base Cost per Manuscript Cost with Tradition Policy
Parchment (Crafted from Furs) 25 units 20 units
Culture (Generated by Amphitheatres/Temples) 400 units 300 units

Manuscripts are required to continue the technology line after Philosophy.

Production Sources and Boosts

  • Parchment Generation: Parchment must be crafted from Furs. Furs are acquired through Hunting using Catpower. Players are advised to Begin Crafting Parchment as Often as You Can well before they are required, as a significant amount will be needed.
  • Culture Generation: Culture is generated by Amphitheatres and Temples. Culture accumulation is slow initially.
  • Automation (Steamworks): The Steamworks building (unlocked by Machinery) can automatically print manuscripts. The Printing Press upgrade allows Steamworks to produce 0.0025 manuscripts/sec. This can be multiplied by subsequent upgrades like Offset Press and Photolithography.
  • Trade: Manuscripts can sometimes be obtained by trading with Sharks. Sharks offer 3 Manuscripts with a 15% chance if you have an Embassy Level of 10.
  • Policy Bonus: The Tradition policy reduces the manuscript cost by 100 culture and 5 parchment, and it doubles the manuscript maximum culture effect. Choosing Tradition is generally recommended to accelerate the manuscript grind.

2. Strategic Importance and Uses

Manuscripts represent the primary bottleneck in the early-to-mid game, transitioning resource focus from Wood/Minerals toward cultural and faith production.

  • Technology Advancement: Manuscripts are necessary inputs for critical mid-game sciences:
    • Theology: Requires 35 Manuscripts.
    • Astronomy: Requires 65 Manuscripts.
    • Navigation: Requires 100 Manuscripts.
  • Next Tier Crafting: Manuscripts are refined in the Workshop, along with Science, to produce Compendiums. Compendiums are prerequisites for technologies like Architecture, Physics, and Geology.
  • Blueprint Production: Eventually, Compendiums are crafted into Blueprints, making manuscripts foundational to the late-game crafting resource chain.
  • Temple Building: Manuscripts are required to construct Temples. A single Temple costs 10 Manuscripts.
  • Culture Capacity: Manuscripts grant a minor bonus to the maximum capacity of Culture, though this effect is subject to diminishing returns.
  • Lizard Relations: The Lizard Relations: [Priests] ( /job/priest/) policy allows manuscripts to grant maximum Faith equal to the maximum culture they grant, while reducing the maximum culture they provide by 25%.

3. Overcoming the Manuscript Grind

The necessary manuscript volume creates a “fair bump” in progression. To efficiently grind manuscripts:

  1. Maximize Capacity: Max out your kitten population using Huts and Log Houses to increase Catpower limits and production rate (for hunting furs).
  2. Increase Culture: Build as many Amphitheatres and Temples as reasonably possible, and buy all available culture and catpower bonuses from the Religion tab. Culture generating buildings like Amphitheatres, Academies, and Libraries also boost the culture storage cap, which is often constrained.
  3. Boost Crafting: Maximizing your Workshops is essential, as this provides a multiplicative bonus to all crafting operations, including manuscript creation.
  4. Kitten Allocation: A suggested method for grinding is to temporarily move all kittens to Hunters to generate a massive stockpile of Parchment (since Parchment creation should initially outpace culture consumption), then craft manuscripts whenever your Culture storage maxes out.

Persistence on Reset

Manuscripts are classified as Craftable Resources. They are generally lost upon reset, but they can be conditionally carried over if the player has Chronospheres and the Flux Condensator upgrade. Each Chronosphere preserves $1.5%* 100* \sqrt{X}$ of the resource, where $X$ is the amount before reset, meaning they carry over with diminishing returns.

In the accelerated, late-game reset loop, stocking up on crafted resources like manuscripts is essential for quickly getting back up to speed. For example, stocking 19.6k manuscripts is recommended for maximizing resource carryover using one Chronosphere.

item.title: Compendium
item.description:
Compendiums are an essential craftable resource in the mid-game of Kittens Game, acting as a required input for advanced technological research and increasing your maximum science storage capacity.

Crafting and Unlocking

  • Prerequisite: Compendiums are enabled for crafting after researching Philosophy (9,500 Science).
  • Cost to Craft: Creating one Compendium requires 50 Manuscripts and 10,000 Science.

Strategic Importance and Usage

Compendiums serve two primary, critical functions:

  1. Technological Advancement: They are mandatory prerequisites for several high-cost, mid-game technologies that unlock major industrial and scientific pathways, including:

    • Architecture (Cost: 10 Compendiums)
    • Physics (Cost: 35 Compendiums)
    • Chemistry (Cost: 50 Compendiums)
    • Geology (Cost: 65 Compendiums)
    • Electricity (Cost: 85 Compendiums)

  2. Science Storage Expansion: Each Compendium crafted provides a permanent +10 increase to your maximum Science storage. This bonus is crucial for overcoming the quickly escalating costs of the technology tree, although this increase is capped by default at 100% of your science storage provided by buildings.

Compendiums are an essential craftable resource in the mid-game of Kittens Game, acting as a required input for advanced technological research and increasing your maximum science storage capacity.

Crafting and Unlocking

  • Prerequisite: Compendiums are enabled for crafting after researching Philosophy (9,500 Science).
  • Cost to Craft: Creating one Compendium requires 50 Manuscripts and 10,000 Science.

Strategic Importance and Usage

Compendiums serve two primary, critical functions:

  1. Technological Advancement: They are mandatory prerequisites for several high-cost, mid-game technologies that unlock major industrial and scientific pathways, including:

    • Architecture (Cost: 10 Compendiums)
    • Physics (Cost: 35 Compendiums)
    • Chemistry (Cost: 50 Compendiums)
    • Geology (Cost: 65 Compendiums)
    • Electricity (Cost: 85 Compendiums)

  2. Science Storage Expansion: Each Compendium crafted provides a permanent +10 increase to your maximum Science storage. This bonus is crucial for overcoming the quickly escalating costs of the technology tree, although this increase is capped by default at 100% of your science storage provided by buildings.

Progression and Efficiency

Compendiums are a necessary input for expanding scientific throughput. To efficiently craft them, you must first secure a strong cultural base to produce the precursor resource, Manuscripts.

  • Compendium Crafting Rate: Achieving efficient Compendium production requires maximising your Workshops, as their collective effect provides a multiplicative boost to all crafting operations. For instance, if your crafting bonus is $5\times$, Compendium production would be boosted by a factor of 125 ($5* 5* 5$) compared to having no Workshops.
  • Next Tier Resource: Once Physics is researched, Compendiums become the resource used to craft Blueprints.

Metaphysics Upgrades (Codexes)

The importance of Compendium crafting is recognised in the permanent Metaphysics upgrade system:

  • Codex Logos: Costs 50 Paragon and specifically adds +25% to your craft ratio when crafting Compendia. It also multiplies all Compendium crafting by $\times 1.05$.
  • Codex Agrum: Costs 75 Paragon and further increases the Compendium craft multiplier to $\times 1.1$.
  • Codex Leviathanianus: Costs 75 Paragon and increases the Compendium cut-off limit by $5%$ per Transcendence tier.

While these Codex upgrades boost crafting efficiency, they are often considered low priority for newer players due to their high cost and small returns compared to the critical price ratio reduction upgrades.

For players executing quick runs designed to accumulate Paragon quickly, stockpiling a certain amount of Compendiums (e.g., 16.1k Compendia) before resetting with a Chronosphere and the Flux Condensator upgrade is recommended, as this crafted resource can be carried over to accelerate the next run. This allows players to skip the time-consuming process of crafting them immediately in the new run.

item.title: Faith
item.description:
Faith is a special expendable resource in Kittens Game that is used almost exclusively within the Religion tab.

Unlocking and Production

Faith becomes available after you research the Theology science, which also unlocks the ability to build Temples and assign kittens to the Priest profession.

Faith is generated through several means:

  • Temples: Once Theology is researched, Temples generate 0.0015 faith per tick.
  • [Priests] ( /job/priest/): Kittens assigned as [Priests] ( /job/priest/) (unlocked by Theology) initially produce 0.0015 faith per tick. In the late game, players often assign almost all kittens as [Priests] ( /job/priest/) because faith production is slow.
  • Chapels: These buildings, available after researching Acoustics, generate 0.005 faith per tick.
  • Upgrades: The religious upgrade Solar Chant increases your faith generation rate by 10%, with subsequent levels purchased via Transcendence increasing this bonus by an additional +10%.

Faith production is generally affected by the Paragon and Religion production boosts.

Faith is a special expendable resource in Kittens Game that is used almost exclusively within the Religion tab.

Unlocking and Production

Faith becomes available after you research the Theology science, which also unlocks the ability to build Temples and assign kittens to the Priest profession.

Faith is generated through several means:

  • Temples: Once Theology is researched, Temples generate 0.0015 faith per tick.
  • [Priests] ( /job/priest/): Kittens assigned as [Priests] ( /job/priest/) (unlocked by Theology) initially produce 0.0015 faith per tick. In the late game, players often assign almost all kittens as [Priests] ( /job/priest/) because faith production is slow.
  • Chapels: These buildings, available after researching Acoustics, generate 0.005 faith per tick.
  • Upgrades: The religious upgrade Solar Chant increases your faith generation rate by 10%, with subsequent levels purchased via Transcendence increasing this bonus by an additional +10%.

Faith production is generally affected by the Paragon and Religion production boosts.

Uses and Religious Progression

Faith is used to purchase religious upgrades and to convert into Worship.

  1. Praising the Sun: x You can convert accumulated Faith into Worship by selecting the “Praise the sun!” option. praise the sun
  2. Upgrades: Once unlocked by accumulating sufficient Worship, various religious upgrades can be purchased using Faith. These upgrades, which are part of the Order of the Sun, often affect other aspects of your civilisation:
    • Solar Revolution (Worship 1000 required, costs 750 Faith and 500 Gold) grants a global production bonus based on your accumulated Worship.
    • Scholasticism (Worship 300 required) allows Temples to contribute to Science.
    • Sun Altar (Worship 750 required) contributes to overall Happiness.

Storage Capacity

Faith is a capped resource. The initial storage capacity is 100. Your maximum Faith capacity is increased primarily through buildings and religious upgrades, as noted in our conversation history:

  • Temples are the main source, increasing Faith storage by 100 each.
  • The Sun Altar upgrade increases Temple maximum faith storage by +50, with an additional +50 for each extra level purchased using Transcendence.
  • The Golden Spire upgrade increases Temple maximum faith storage by 50%. This is a multiplier applied after other effects are calculated, and this percentage increases by an additional +10% for each additional level purchased via Transcendence.

End-Game Importance (Apocrypha and Transcendence)

Faith is crucial for accessing the deeper mechanics of the Religion tab:

  • To access Apocrypha (the ability to convert Worship to Epiphany), you must reach a maximum Faith limit of 100K and spend 5000 Faith and 5000 Gold.
  • Apocrypha unlocks the ability to “Adore the galaxy,” which converts all accumulated Worship into Epiphany. Epiphany provides a bonus that makes future Praising more effective.
  • Reaching this high capacity for Apocrypha is also essential for working toward Transcendence, which requires a Worship cap of 125K, and costs 7500 Faith and 7500 Gold. Transcendence levels increase the conversion multiplier when Adoring the Galaxy, helping players quickly max out their Solar Revolution production bonus after a reset.

item.title: Blueprint
item.description:
Blueprints are a crucial Craftable Resource required for technological advancement and the construction of advanced industrial buildings in Kittens Game.

Here is a comprehensive overview of Blueprints:

Acquisition

Blueprints can be acquired through crafting or trade:

  1. Crafting:

    • Blueprints are crafted from 25 Compendium and 25,000 Science.
    • The capacity to craft Blueprints is unlocked after researching the Physics technology.
    • Crafting blueprints is considered to have an “incredibly steep production cost”, and the process is the same as crafting Manuscripts.
    • The process often requires mass conversion: first converting Furs into Parchment, then Parchment into Manuscripts, and finally Manuscripts into Compendiums before crafting the Blueprint.
    • The Metaphysics upgrade Codex Agrum reduces the cost growth ratio by adding +25% to your blueprint craft ratio and multiplying the blueprint craft multiplier by x1.05.

  2. Trading:

    • Any successful trade with other civilizations has a 10% chance of including one blueprint as an extra resource. This is a fixed rate that cannot be increased by other trade bonuses.
    • Trading is often the preferred initial method, as players are advised to “keep Trading with other civilizations until you luck out and get a Blueprints for free” due to their steep production cost.
    • Trading with Nagas can specifically boost Blueprint acquisition: Building Naga embassies increases the chance to get blueprints from Nagas by 0.25%, capping at 10% at 40 embassies. Once the maximum bonus is achieved, embassies over 40 improve the blueprint crafting ratio instead.

    • The Metaphysics upgrade Codex Agrum reduces the cost growth ratio by adding +25% to your blueprint craft ratio and multiplying the blueprint craft multiplier by x1.05.

  2. Trading:

    • Any successful trade with other civilizations has a 10% chance of including one blueprint as an extra resource. This is a fixed rate that cannot be increased by other trade bonuses.
    • Trading is often the preferred initial method, as players are advised to “keep Trading with other civilizations until you luck out and get a Blueprints for free” due to their steep production cost.
    • Trading with Nagas can specifically boost Blueprint acquisition: Building Naga embassies increases the chance to get blueprints from Nagas by 0.25%, capping at 10% at 40 embassies. Once the maximum bonus is achieved, embassies over 40 improve the blueprint crafting ratio instead.

Uses and Costs

Blueprints are necessary for mid-to-late-game progression, being required for both technologies and buildings:

  1. Buildings:

    • Blueprints are integral to constructing key advanced structures.
    • The Steamworks building requires 1 Blueprint, 65 Steel, and 20 Gears.
    • The Magneto building requires 1 Blueprint, 10 Alloy, and 5 Gears.
    • Other important structures like the Calciner and Ziggurat also require 1 Blueprint.
    • Mega Structures, such as the Reactor, require 25 Blueprints.
    • The final upgrade to the Warehouse, the Spaceport, requires 500 Blueprints.

  2. Technologies (Techs):

    • Blueprints become required resources for researching technologies starting with Industrialization (25 Blueprints).
    • Later, more advanced technologies require increasing quantities of Blueprints, such as Orbital Engineering (250 Blueprints), and Exometallurgy (350 Blueprints).

  3. Workshop Upgrades:

    • Many efficiency upgrades require blueprints, especially those associated with Steamworks and automation. Examples include the Advanced Automation (25 Blueprints) and High Pressure Engine (5 Blueprints) upgrades.
    • Upgrades for oil production, such as the Tanker which increases maximum oil capacity, require 5 Blueprints.

Strategic Notes

  • In the Titanium era, Blueprints often become necessary for learning later sciences, and you can stock up on them by trading while also acquiring needed titanium and steel.
  • When crafting blueprints, you can make your leader a scientist to obtain a science discount on the crafting cost.
  • In the end-game, blueprints can become a bottleneck. Strategies for acquiring them quickly involve using Mints to generate Furs (for Parchment) or relying heavily on trade, with trade being the fastest method for resets once you have a massive Catpower stockpile.

item.title: Apocrypha
item.description:
Apocrypha is a high-level religious technology and system in Kittens Game that is crucial for converting accumulated Worship into a permanent prestige resource called Epiphany, which is retained across game resets.

1. Unlocking and Cost

  • Prerequisites: Apocrypha is a religious upgrade that requires reaching a total of 100,000 Worship to unlock.
  • Cost: Once unlocked, purchasing Apocrypha requires 5,000 Faith and 5,000 Gold.

2. Core Functionality: Converting Prestige Currency

Apocrypha unlocks the ability to “Adore the Galaxy”. This action converts all accumulated Worship into Epiphany (a hidden resource formerly known as the “Apocrypha bonus”).
item.content:encoded:
Apocrypha is a high-level religious technology and system in Kittens Game that is crucial for converting accumulated Worship into a permanent prestige resource called Epiphany, which is retained across game resets.

1. Unlocking and Cost

  • Prerequisites: Apocrypha is a religious upgrade that requires reaching a total of 100,000 Worship to unlock.
  • Cost: Once unlocked, purchasing Apocrypha requires 5,000 Faith and 5,000 Gold.

2. Core Functionality: Converting Prestige Currency

Apocrypha unlocks the ability to “Adore the Galaxy”. This action converts all accumulated Worship into Epiphany (a hidden resource formerly known as the “Apocrypha bonus”).

  • Epiphany Effect: Epiphany drives a bonus that makes future Praising (converting Faith to Worship) significantly stronger. This bonus is displayed on the “Praise the Sun!” button.
  • Reset Carry-over: Epiphany is a critical resource because it carries over upon game reset.
  • Worship Loss: Although Apocrypha allows Worship to convert into Epiphany (with a slight penalty) upon a hard game reset, players are advised that it is better to manually Adore the Galaxy before resetting to maximise the benefit. If you forget to manually convert, you won’t lose much of the Worship.

3. Relationship with Transcendence

Apocrypha is integral to the Transcendence system, which is essential for maximizing permanent gains:

  • Transcendence Requirement: Apocrypha is required to unlock Transcendence (which requires 125,000 Worship, 7,500 Faith, and 7,500 Gold).
  • Staging the Reset: To maximize the gain derived from Faith investment before a game reset, players must always execute Transcendence (spending Epiphany to increase Transcendence tiers) before performing Apocrypha (Adoring the Galaxy). This ensures that the Epiphany gain is maximized, as Transcendence tiers increase the conversion multiplier when Adoring the Galaxy.
  • Boosting Solar Revolution: The accumulation of a high Apocrypha bonus (Epiphany) is essential because it allows the player to quickly achieve a high Solar Revolution production bonus in subsequent runs. The Apocrypha bonus is often referred to as the “Adore percentage” when determining if performing Transcendence is worth the temporary sacrifice.

4. Strategic Importance

Apocrypha is a major step in Phase 3 of the game (Religious and Energy Transition Epoch), as it defines how players convert ephemeral religious production into permanent prestige capital.

  • Long-Term Farming: Strategically, you will want to get your Faith and Gold caps high enough to start ‘storing’ it with Apocrypha. In late-game runs, achieving high Apocrypha bonuses (over 3 million percent is needed for Transcendence Tier 15) is necessary to unlock high-tier religious abilities that boost late-game production, such as Blazar.
  • Iron Will Mode: In the resource-constrained Iron Will mode, getting the Apocrypha bonus high prior to entering the mode is suggested, as the resulting high Solar Revolution bonus (which uses Worship/Faith) is highly useful in Iron Will.

item.title: Basilica
item.description:
The Basilica is a late-game upgrade available for the Temple building, focusing on significantly increasing your cultural resources.

Here are the details regarding the Basilica upgrade:

Unlocking and Cost

Detail Specification
Building Type Upgrade for Temple.
Prerequisite Requires 10,000 Worship.
Cost 1250 Faith and 750 Gold.
Price Ratio 2.5.

Effects on Temples

The Basilica primarily boosts the cultural output and storage capacity provided by your Temples:

  • Culture Production: Increases Temple Culture per Tick by $+0.2$.
  • Culture Storage: Increases Temple Max Culture by $+125$.

Transcendence Scaling

The Basilica is one of the religious abilities that can be purchased multiple times using Transcendence tiers, which are acquired by spending Epiphany.

item.title: Epiphany
item.description:
Epiphany is a core prestige resource in Kittens Game, converted from your accumulated Worship and retained across game resets to accelerate progress in subsequent runs.

Function and Conversion

  1. Conversion: Epiphany is converted from Worship by performing the action “Adore the Galaxy”. This ability is unlocked after purchasing the Apocrypha religious upgrade, which requires 100,000 Worship, 5,000 Faith, and 5,000 Gold.
  2. Primary Effect: Epiphany drives a bonus that makes future Praising (converting Faith to Worship) significantly stronger. This bonus helps players quickly build up the Solar Revolution production bonus after a reset.
  3. Persistence: Epiphany is a special resource that carries over upon game reset, providing permanent acceleration for future runs. If you do not manually convert your Worship to Epiphany before resetting, the Worship will convert automatically with a slight penalty.

Role in Transcendence

Epiphany is the currency used to gain Transcendence Tiers (TT), which are permanent religious upgrades.
item.content:encoded:
Epiphany is a core prestige resource in Kittens Game, converted from your accumulated Worship and retained across game resets to accelerate progress in subsequent runs.

Function and Conversion

  1. Conversion: Epiphany is converted from Worship by performing the action “Adore the Galaxy”. This ability is unlocked after purchasing the Apocrypha religious upgrade, which requires 100,000 Worship, 5,000 Faith, and 5,000 Gold.
  2. Primary Effect: Epiphany drives a bonus that makes future Praising (converting Faith to Worship) significantly stronger. This bonus helps players quickly build up the Solar Revolution production bonus after a reset.
  3. Persistence: Epiphany is a special resource that carries over upon game reset, providing permanent acceleration for future runs. If you do not manually convert your Worship to Epiphany before resetting, the Worship will convert automatically with a slight penalty.

Role in Transcendence

Epiphany is the currency used to gain Transcendence Tiers (TT), which are permanent religious upgrades.

  • Spending Epiphany: The Transcend mechanism allows you to spend Epiphany to increase your Transcendence Tier.
  • Multiplier: Increasing the Transcendence Tier, in turn, increases the conversion multiplier when performing “Adore the Galaxy”.
  • Strategic Reset: To maximise the Epiphany bonus before resetting the game, the player should always execute Transcendence BEFORE Apocrypha (Adoring the Galaxy).

For reference, the minimum Epiphany needed to reach Transcendence Tier 15 is approximately 3.04 million per cent. A high Epiphany bonus is necessary to rapidly reach high Solar Revolution bonuses and is particularly useful in challenge modes like Iron Will.

Historical Naming

For historic reasons, Epiphany may sometimes be referred to in the sources or gameplay community as Apocrypha bonus or Adoration.

item.title: Praise the sun
item.description:
“Praise the sun!” is a core action within the Religion tab of Kittens Game, defining the process of converting the special resource Faith into the resource Worship.

Function and Resource Conversion

The action is available once you have any amount of accumulated Faith. When you select the “Praise the sun!” option:

  • It converts all accumulated Faith into Worship.
  • The system operates under the Order of the Sun, which is unlocked once you build a Temple (unlocked after researching Philosophy and subsequently Theology).

Worship is the name given to what was previously referred to as “praised faith”.
item.content:encoded:
“Praise the sun!” is a core action within the Religion tab of Kittens Game, defining the process of converting the special resource Faith into the resource Worship.

Function and Resource Conversion

The action is available once you have any amount of accumulated Faith. When you select the “Praise the sun!” option:

  • It converts all accumulated Faith into Worship.
  • The system operates under the Order of the Sun, which is unlocked once you build a Temple (unlocked after researching Philosophy and subsequently Theology).

Worship is the name given to what was previously referred to as “praised faith”.

Uses of Worship

The primary purpose of performing “Praise the sun!” is to accumulate Worship, which serves two main goals:

  1. Unlocking Religious Upgrades: Various religious upgrades can be purchased using Faith, but only once sufficient Worship has been accumulated to unlock them. Examples include:

    • Solar Chant (requires 150 Worship).
    • Scholasticism (requires 300 Worship).
    • Sun Altar and Stained Glass (require 750 Worship).

  2. Solar Revolution Production Bonus: Once you reach 1000 Worship, you can purchase the Solar Revolution upgrade (costs 750 Faith and 500 Gold). This grants a global production bonus based on the amount of accumulated Worship. This bonus is initially capped at 1000%, with diminishing returns starting at 750%.

Long-Term Progression (Epiphany)

Later in the game, the effectiveness of praising the sun is tied to the Epiphany mechanic:

  • After researching Apocrypha (which requires 100K Worship and 5000 Faith/5000 Gold), you unlock the ability to “Adore the galaxy”.
  • Adoring the galaxy sacrifices all accumulated Worship and converts it into the hidden resource Epiphany (formerly called the “Apocrypha bonus”).
  • Epiphany drives a bonus that makes future Praising (i.e., converting Faith into Worship) stronger. This bonus is displayed on the “Praise” button.
  • A major strategy in later runs involves pushing the Apocrypha/Epiphany bonus high so that after a reset, you can quickly achieve the maximum Solar Revolution production bonus by converting stored Faith into Worship via Praising the Sun.

item.title: Stained Glass
item.description:
The Stained Glass upgrade is a religious upgrade within Kittens Game, part of the Order of the Sun.

Here is a detailed explanation of its function, costs, and requirements:

Function and Effects

The primary function of Stained Glass is to enhance the cultural output of your Temples.

  • Culture Production Increase: Stained Glass increases the amount of culture per tick generated by Temples by +0.05.
  • Scaling: This bonus is increased by an additional +0.05 for each subsequent level of Stained Glass purchased using Transcendence.

Requirements and Cost

Stained Glass becomes available for purchase relatively early in the religious progression:
item.content:encoded:
The Stained Glass upgrade is a religious upgrade within Kittens Game, part of the Order of the Sun.

Here is a detailed explanation of its function, costs, and requirements:

Function and Effects

The primary function of Stained Glass is to enhance the cultural output of your Temples.

  • Culture Production Increase: Stained Glass increases the amount of culture per tick generated by Temples by +0.05.
  • Scaling: This bonus is increased by an additional +0.05 for each subsequent level of Stained Glass purchased using Transcendence.

Requirements and Cost

Stained Glass becomes available for purchase relatively early in the religious progression:

  • Prerequisite: You must have accumulated 750 Worship. Worship is the resource converted from Faith using the “Praise the sun!” action.
  • Cost: The upgrade requires 500 Faith and 250 Gold.

Context

Stained Glass is unlocked at the same Worship threshold (750) as the Sun Altar upgrade. Both of these upgrades enhance the functionality of Temples.

Since Temples are one of the buildings that generate Culture (along with Amphitheatres and Chapels), Stained Glass helps advance your culture production. Culture is a vital special resource used to craft Manuscripts from Parchment, which are required for researching advanced technologies like Theology and Astronomy.

item.title: Ivory Citadel
item.description:
The Ivory Citadel is an advanced building within the Unicorn religious progression, critical for scaling late-game luxury resource production.

Building Details and Effects

The Ivory Citadel is unlocked after constructing at least one Ivory Tower.

  • Cost: Building an Ivory Citadel requires 50 Tears and 50,000 Ivory.
  • Effect on Unicorns: It significantly improves unicorn generation by +25%.
  • Ivory Generation: The Ivory Citadel enables a random event called Ivory Meteors, which generate ivory. The frequency of this event increases by 0.05% per game-day for each Ivory Citadel.

Strategic Context

The Ivory Citadel sits on the path toward the most powerful religious buildings, playing a key role in setting up the Unicorn/Time Crystal Era:
item.content:encoded:
The Ivory Citadel is an advanced building within the Unicorn religious progression, critical for scaling late-game luxury resource production.

Building Details and Effects

The Ivory Citadel is unlocked after constructing at least one Ivory Tower.

  • Cost: Building an Ivory Citadel requires 50 Tears and 50,000 Ivory.
  • Effect on Unicorns: It significantly improves unicorn generation by +25%.
  • Ivory Generation: The Ivory Citadel enables a random event called Ivory Meteors, which generate ivory. The frequency of this event increases by 0.05% per game-day for each Ivory Citadel.

Strategic Context

The Ivory Citadel sits on the path toward the most powerful religious buildings, playing a key role in setting up the Unicorn/Time Crystal Era:

  1. Religious Progression: The Ivory Citadel is a prerequisite for constructing the Sky Palace.
  2. Unicorn Economy: In the late game, the overall religious path relies on generating Unicorns, which are then sacrificed to produce Tears [2, 3]. Tears are then refined into Black Liquid Sorrow (BLS) to produce Black Pyramids, which unlock Leviathan trade [4-6].
  3. Ivory Source: Strategically, Ivory Citadels are built primarily because they provide a valuable, passive, AFK source of ivory via the Ivory Meteor event [1, 7]. Ivory is a necessary resource for trading with the Nagas for minerals [8, 9] and is also needed to construct further unicorn production buildings [10]. In runs focused on maximizing ivory returns early, the strategy recommends building as many Ivory Citadels as possible before moving on to higher-tier buildings like Sky Palaces, Unicorn Utopias, and Sunspires [7].

item.title: Ivory_tower
item.description:
The Ivory Tower is an advanced religious building within the Unicorn progression pathway that helps establish the production of unicorns and associated resources needed for late-game advancement.

Here is a detailed summary of the Ivory Tower:

Building Details and Effects

Category Detail
Cost 25 Tears and 25,000 Ivory.
Prerequisite You must complete at least one Unicorn Tomb before you can build an Ivory Tower.
Unicorn Generation It improves unicorn generation by 10%.
Alicorn/Time Crystal Progression The Ivory Tower unlocks the Unicorn Rifts random event, which generates unicorns. Each Ivory Tower increases the frequency of this event by 0.05% per game-day (or 1% per day per 20 towers). It also provides a boost to your unicorn rift amount equal to 10% of your unicorn ziggurat bonus to unicorn production.

Strategic Context

The Ivory Tower is a key step in the religious pathway focused on Unicorns and Time Crystals (Phase 2 progression) [1, 2]:

The Ivory Tower is an advanced religious building within the Unicorn progression pathway that helps establish the production of unicorns and associated resources needed for late-game advancement.

Here is a detailed summary of the Ivory Tower:

Building Details and Effects

Category Detail
Cost 25 Tears and 25,000 Ivory.
Prerequisite You must complete at least one Unicorn Tomb before you can build an Ivory Tower.
Unicorn Generation It improves unicorn generation by 10%.
Alicorn/Time Crystal Progression The Ivory Tower unlocks the Unicorn Rifts random event, which generates unicorns. Each Ivory Tower increases the frequency of this event by 0.05% per game-day (or 1% per day per 20 towers). It also provides a boost to your unicorn rift amount equal to 10% of your unicorn ziggurat bonus to unicorn production.

Strategic Context

The Ivory Tower is a key step in the religious pathway focused on Unicorns and Time Crystals (Phase 2 progression) [1, 2]:

  1. Religious Hierarchy: The Ivory Tower is the prerequisite structure that leads to the construction of the Ivory Citadel [3].
  2. Unicorn Resource Chain: The primary religious path involves obtaining Unicorns (often initially through Hunting) [4, 5] and then sacrificing them in a Ziggurat to produce Tears [1, 6, 7]. These Tears are then used along with Ivory to construct the Ivory Tower. This process is crucial because it ultimately leads to the production of Alicorns, which are refined into Time Crystals [6, 8].
  3. Efficiency in Specialized Runs: In long runs, such as the Iron Will 40K challenge, players focus on building the unicorn production chain for resources like Ivory, which is then traded for minerals with the Nagas [9, 10]. The unicorn resources produced by Ivory Towers (Unicorns via Rifts) and the subsequent Ivory Citadels (Ivory via Meteors) are often prioritized as a passive, AFK source of these luxury goods [11].

item.title: Sky_palace
item.description:
The Sky Palace is an advanced religious building that plays a crucial role in the late Phase 2 (the Unicorn/Time Crystal Era) progression by generating the unique resource, Alicorns.

Functionality and Effects

  • Prerequisite: The Sky Palace is unlocked after building at least one Ivory Citadel (a preceding unicorn religious upgrade).
  • Cost: It requires a substantial investment of 500 Tears, 125,000 Ivory, and 5 Megalith.
  • Unicorn Production: It provides a significant boost to unicorn generation by +50%.
  • Alicorn Generation: The Sky Palace enables a random event that grants one alicorn. The frequency of this event increases by 0.01% per game-day for each Sky Palace, meaning it takes 100 Palaces to increase the chance by 1% per day. Additionally, each Sky Palace produces a very slow passive rate of 0.00002 alicorns per tick (or 0.08 per year).
  • Other Bonuses: It also improves gold storage by +1% and increases ivory gained from Ivory Meteors by 5%.

Strategic Context

The Sky Palace is strategically important because it is a prerequisite for subsequent powerful religious upgrades and resources:
item.content:encoded:
The Sky Palace is an advanced religious building that plays a crucial role in the late Phase 2 (the Unicorn/Time Crystal Era) progression by generating the unique resource, Alicorns.

Functionality and Effects

  • Prerequisite: The Sky Palace is unlocked after building at least one Ivory Citadel (a preceding unicorn religious upgrade).
  • Cost: It requires a substantial investment of 500 Tears, 125,000 Ivory, and 5 Megalith.
  • Unicorn Production: It provides a significant boost to unicorn generation by +50%.
  • Alicorn Generation: The Sky Palace enables a random event that grants one alicorn. The frequency of this event increases by 0.01% per game-day for each Sky Palace, meaning it takes 100 Palaces to increase the chance by 1% per day. Additionally, each Sky Palace produces a very slow passive rate of 0.00002 alicorns per tick (or 0.08 per year).
  • Other Bonuses: It also improves gold storage by +1% and increases ivory gained from Ivory Meteors by 5%.

Strategic Context

The Sky Palace is strategically important because it is a prerequisite for subsequent powerful religious upgrades and resources:

  • Progression Path: Building a Sky Palace is necessary to unlock the Unicorn Utopia upgrade.
  • Time Crystal Economy: The alicorns generated by the Sky Palace are essential because sacrificing 25 alicorns yields one Time Crystal [3, 4]. Alicorns are therefore a key input for the temporal economy [5].
  • Ivory Acquisition: The Sky Palace is part of a series of unicorn buildings (including Ivory Tower and Ivory Citadel) [1, 6] that are targeted early in the Unicorn Era to provide a passive, AFK source of ivory (via Ivory Meteors) [1, 5, 7], which is needed to trade for minerals with the Nagas [8].

In general late-game strategy, obtaining the Sky Palace and continuing the unicorn pathway (Unicorn Utopia, Sunspire) is advised to maximize the alicorn summon chance and conversion efficiency for generating Time Crystals [2, 9].

item.title: Unicorn Tomb
item.description:
The Unicorn Tomb is an early building within the Unicorn religious progression chain, serving as a direct upgrade to the Unicorn Pasture.

This structure is vital for establishing the infrastructure necessary to scale luxury and temporal resources like Tears and Time Crystals in the mid-to-late game.

Details and Effects

Category Detail
Prerequisite The Unicorn Tomb is an upgrade available after successfully building a Unicorn Pasture [1, 2].
Cost Building a Unicorn Tomb requires 5 Tears and 500 Ivory [1, 3].
Effect It provides a 5% improvement to unicorn generation (Unicorns per Tick +5%) [1, 3].
Progression Completing at least one Unicorn Tomb is the direct prerequisite for unlocking the Ivory Tower.

Context in Religious Progression

The Unicorn Tomb is placed early in the sequence of unicorn buildings that scale unicorn production and eventually lead to the coveted Time Crystal economy:
