Cost 1000 Science,.
Prerequisite Unlocked by Animal Husbandry,.
Unlocks Academy (building),; Celestial Mechanics (workshop upgrade),.

The Academy Building

The Academy is the key building unlocked by this research, offering significant bonuses to science and culture accumulation:

  • Cost: 50 Wood, 70 Minerals, and 100 Science.
  • Primary Effects:
    • Science Boost: Provides a +20% Science bonus.
    • Science Storage: Increases maximum Science storage by +500,.
    • Culture Storage: Increases maximum Culture capacity by +25.
    • Kitten Experience: Provides a +5% Kitten Exp bonus.

Strategic Role

Mathematics is considered “especially useful” because of the Academy’s ability to boost science accumulation and support the cultural infrastructure.

  1. Accelerating Science: Academies directly increase science output and significantly boost maximum science capacity,. Along with Libraries, Academies are key buildings for increasing the culture cap, which is necessary for crafting Manuscripts.
  2. Trade Prerequisite: Academies contribute to increasing your culture cap, which is a requirement for unlocking the Nagas trade partner (requiring 1500 culture cap),,.
  3. Iron Will Mode: In the resource-constrained Iron Will mode, Mathematics is a crucial early research. It unlocks the Celestial Mechanics upgrade (costing 250 Science), which increases the science gained from celestial events and meteors by 60%,. Since astronomical events and meteors are the only initial sources of Science and Minerals, respectively, in Iron Will mode, this boost is essential for early progression,,.

item.title: Mechanization
item.description:
Mechanization is a key technology research in the mid-to-late game of Kittens Game, leading directly to the advanced “Concrete era” of infrastructure development.

Here is a detailed breakdown of its prerequisites, costs, and effects:

Prerequisites and Cost

  • Prerequisite Technology: Mechanization is unlocked after researching Industrialization. It is the final step in a major scientific progression path: Physics $\to$ Electricity $\to$ Industrialization $\to$ Mechanization.
  • Cost: Researching Mechanization is expensive, requiring 115,000 Science and 45 Blueprints.

Key Unlocks and Effects

Researching Mechanization provides crucial industrial capabilities and new construction materials:
item.content:encoded:
Mechanization is a key technology research in the mid-to-late game of Kittens Game, leading directly to the advanced “Concrete era” of infrastructure development.

Here is a detailed breakdown of its prerequisites, costs, and effects:

Prerequisites and Cost

  • Prerequisite Technology: Mechanization is unlocked after researching Industrialization. It is the final step in a major scientific progression path: Physics $\to$ Electricity $\to$ Industrialization $\to$ Mechanization.
  • Cost: Researching Mechanization is expensive, requiring 115,000 Science and 45 Blueprints.

Key Unlocks and Effects

Researching Mechanization provides crucial industrial capabilities and new construction materials:

  1. Resource Unlocked (Concrete): Mechanization enables the production of concrete. Concrete is a highly important crafted material necessary for advancing housing and storage infrastructure.
  2. Building Unlocked (Factory): This technology unlocks the Factory building. Factories are essential for late-game industrial scaling and boosting crafting efficiency.
  3. Kitten Job Unlocked (Engineer): Mechanization enables the Engineer job, allowing kittens to automate crafting processes in the Workshop.
  4. Workshop Upgrades: Mechanization unlocks critical efficiency upgrades in the Workshop:
    • Concrete Pillars: A storage upgrade that increases the maximum capacity of several resources (wood, minerals, iron, coal, gold, and titanium) from Barns, Warehouses, Harbours, and Mints by $+5%$.
    • Pumpjack: This upgrade improves the effectiveness of Oil Wells by $45%$ and enables their automation, although Oil Wells will then consume 1 Watt of energy each.

Strategic Significance

Mechanization is a major checkpoint on the path to high-tier buildings and population management:

  • Concrete Era: This research is necessary for achieving Concrete Huts. Concrete Huts require a tremendous amount of titanium and grant a major reduction in the price ratio of Huts, making population expansion cheaper.
  • Technological Progression: Mechanization directly unlocks the next tier of science, Electronics.
  • Endgame Focus: While the costs for Mechanization are high, players are advised to pre-emptively grind for the huge amount of titanium required for the subsequent Concrete upgrades, as this process will often provide most of the blueprints needed to research Mechanization itself through trade bonuses.

item.title: Metal_Working
item.description:
Metal Working is an important early technology in Kittens Game, serving as a prerequisite for smelting mineral resources into processed materials like iron and gold.

Here is a detailed breakdown of Metal Working:

1. Unlocking and Cost

  • Prerequisite Technology: Metal Working is unlocked after researching Mining.
  • Cost: Researching Metal Working costs 900 Science.

2. Buildings and Resources Unlocked

Researching this technology unlocks the basic structure necessary for converting raw minerals into metal resources:
item.content:encoded:
Metal Working is an important early technology in Kittens Game, serving as a prerequisite for smelting mineral resources into processed materials like iron and gold.

Here is a detailed breakdown of Metal Working:

1. Unlocking and Cost

  • Prerequisite Technology: Metal Working is unlocked after researching Mining.
  • Cost: Researching Metal Working costs 900 Science.

2. Buildings and Resources Unlocked

Researching this technology unlocks the basic structure necessary for converting raw minerals into metal resources:

  • Building Unlocked: Metal Working unlocks the Smelter building.
    • The Smelter converts raw resources, consuming 0.05 Wood per Tick and 0.1 Minerals per Tick to produce 0.02 Iron per Tick.
    • Smelters can be further upgraded with Gold Ore to produce 0.001 Gold per Tick. This means that a small percentage of ore will be smelted into gold.
  • Workshop Upgrade: Metal Working unlocks the Hunting Armour Workshop upgrade. Hunting Armour provides a +2.0 Hunting bonus, making hunters three times as effective (an increase of about 165-200% of the basic fur and ivory hunting amounts).

3. Strategic Role

Metal Working is a critical early-game step for expanding resource production and moving toward industrialisation:

  • Iron Production: This technology is essential because Minerals become increasingly important for advanced buildings. Metal Working allows you to put your minerals to work by building Smelters to create Iron.
  • Production Trade-off: While beneficial for accessing Iron and Gold, building Smelters requires converting minerals and wood, so players must bear in mind that creating Iron will reduce your Wood and Mineral stores.
  • Lumber Mill Prerequisite: The subsequent technology that boosts wood production, the Lumber Mill, requires Iron for construction, meaning Metal Working must be researched first.
  • Iron Will Mode: In Iron Will mode, after Gold Ore is researched, Hunting produces Gold, which is important since kittens cannot be employed as Geologists for gold production in this mode.

Metal Working is a mandatory step in the “Basic Resource Rotation” necessary for establishing a strong economic foundation by processing basic resources into advanced components.

item.title: Metallurgy
item.description:
Metallurgy is a mid-game technology research that is unlocked by Industrialization and provides valuable workshop upgrades focused on boosting the efficiency and output of metal production and refinement processes.

Here is a detailed breakdown of the Metallurgy technology:

Unlocking and Cost

  • Prerequisite: Metallurgy is unlocked after researching Industrialization.
  • Cost: Researching Metallurgy requires 125,000 Science and 60 Blueprints.

Key Workshop Upgrades

Metallurgy is primarily important for the upgrades it provides to metal processing buildings like Smelters and Calciners. These upgrades help manage the mid-game requirement for processed metals and alloys:
item.content:encoded:
Metallurgy is a mid-game technology research that is unlocked by Industrialization and provides valuable workshop upgrades focused on boosting the efficiency and output of metal production and refinement processes.

Here is a detailed breakdown of the Metallurgy technology:

Unlocking and Cost

  • Prerequisite: Metallurgy is unlocked after researching Industrialization.
  • Cost: Researching Metallurgy requires 125,000 Science and 60 Blueprints.

Key Workshop Upgrades

Metallurgy is primarily important for the upgrades it provides to metal processing buildings like Smelters and Calciners. These upgrades help manage the mid-game requirement for processed metals and alloys:

  1. Electrolytic Smelting: This upgrade effectively doubles the production rate of Smelters, making them produce +95% more iron and coal.
  2. Oxidation: This significantly boosts the output of Calciners. Calciners produce +95% more iron and a substantial +285% more titanium.
  3. Mining Drill: This upgrade improves the effectiveness of Geologists. Geologists, if the prerequisite Geodesy upgrade has been researched, gain an additional +0.01 coal/tick and +0.0005 gold/tick. This upgrade costs 100,000 Science, 1750 Titanium, and 750 Steel.

Strategic Context

  • Industrial Path: Metallurgy is part of the industrial expansion pathway, which follows Electricity and Industrialization. This pathway eventually leads to the Mechanization and Electronics branches.
  • Titanium Production: The Oxidation upgrade is crucial in the mid-game for significantly accelerating titanium production from Calciners, helping the player acquire the necessary volume of titanium for advanced structures.
  • Kitten Trait: In addition to the research, kittens can have the Metallurgist trait. When assigned as a leader, this trait increases metal crafting efficiency by adding a +0.1 craft ratio for plate, steel, gear, and alloy.

item.title: Metaphysics
item.description:
Metaphysics is a core technology research and an associated system of permanent, prestige-based upgrades unlocked in the late mid-game of Kittens Game. These upgrades are crucial because, once purchased using Paragon, they carry over across game resets, enabling significantly faster progress in subsequent runs.

1. Unlocking and Requirements

  • Prerequisite Technology: Metaphysics is unlocked by researching Physics.
  • Cost: Researching the technology costs 55,000 Science and 5 Unobtainium.
  • Activation: The technology itself enables the Metaphysics system, but upgrades within the system must be purchased using the prestige currency Paragon.

2. Strategic Role and Benefits

Metaphysics upgrades are the primary tool for achieving geometric scaling in subsequent runs, as they provide permanent bonuses that do not disappear upon reset.
item.content:encoded:
Metaphysics is a core technology research and an associated system of permanent, prestige-based upgrades unlocked in the late mid-game of Kittens Game. These upgrades are crucial because, once purchased using Paragon, they carry over across game resets, enabling significantly faster progress in subsequent runs.

1. Unlocking and Requirements

  • Prerequisite Technology: Metaphysics is unlocked by researching Physics.
  • Cost: Researching the technology costs 55,000 Science and 5 Unobtainium.
  • Activation: The technology itself enables the Metaphysics system, but upgrades within the system must be purchased using the prestige currency Paragon.

2. Strategic Role and Benefits

Metaphysics upgrades are the primary tool for achieving geometric scaling in subsequent runs, as they provide permanent bonuses that do not disappear upon reset.

The most effective upgrades generally fall into three categories:

A. Price Ratio Reduction (Economic Scaling)

These upgrades decrease the price ratio of structures in the Bonfire tab, meaning the cost of buying subsequent buildings grows much slower. This is one of the most significant benefits, allowing players to build many more structures (and gain more production/population) before hitting storage caps.

The recommended sequence for these early upgrades is:

  1. Enlightenment (5 Paragon): Reduces all price ratios by 1%.
  2. Golden Ratio (50 Paragon): Reduces price ratios by approximately 1.618%.
  3. Divine Proportion (100 Paragon): Reduces price ratios by approximately 1.777%.
  4. Vitruvian Feline (250 Paragon): Reduces price ratios by 2%.
  5. Renaissance (750 Paragon): Reduces price ratios by 2.25%.

B. Progression and Quality of Life (QoL) Upgrades

These upgrades accelerate key production bottlenecks and progression hurdles:

  • Diplomacy (5 Paragon): Causes races to be discovered earlier (unlock year reduced from 5 to 1) and with better standing. This is recommended to get early in the game.
  • Chronomancy (25 Paragon) and Astromancy (50 Paragon): These are useful early QoL upgrades. Chronomancy multiplies the daily chance of meteors and astronomical events by 1.1x, while Astromancy doubles the astronomical event chance and observatory effectiveness (for event chances and auto success rates). This helps mitigate the early starchart bottleneck.
  • Venus of Willenfluff (150 Paragon) and Pawgan Rituals (400 Paragon): These significantly boost the speed at which kittens arrive (75% faster and an additional 150% faster, respectively), which is vital for quick paragon farming runs.
  • Anachronomancy (125 Paragon): Crucially, this upgrade ensures that Time Crystals and the Chronophysics technology are saved across resets. This is mandatory before seriously engaging in Time Crystal acquisition.

C. Endgame Systems and Prestige

These upgrades enable or significantly boost endgame systems related to time, religion, and unicorns:

  • Megalomania (10 Paragon): Unlocks Markers and Black Pyramids, which are key to starting the Unicorn/Time crystal Era and engaging the Leviathan trade partner. Megalomania is necessary for refining Unicorn Tears into Black Liquid Sorrow (BLS).
  • Numerology (50 Paragon) and Numeromancy (250 Paragon): These enable Cycles to affect space production (Numerology) and grant bonuses during festivals based on the current cycle (Numeromancy). The Redmoon cycle, when combined with Numeromancy, provides a significant boost to Unobtainium production.
  • Order of the Void (75 Paragon): Causes all faith production to also produce 10% of that amount in Worship.
  • Codex Upgrades (Vox, Logos, Agrum): These increase the crafting ratio for manuscripts, compendiums, and blueprints, respectively. Although they are costly, they are not recommended for newer players as their bonuses are minimal compared to the price ratio reductions.

3. Progression Strategy

Metaphysics dictates the early Paragon Grind phase (Phase 1/Early Game). A player’s goal in the first few runs is to accumulate enough Paragon (by resetting with over 70 kittens) to buy the most impactful Metaphysics upgrades.

A suggested goal is to aim for 60 Paragon on the first reset to buy Diplomacy, Enlightenment, and Golden Ratio, and then 100 Paragon on the second run to buy Divine Proportion. Once price ratio reductions are secured, you can focus on later QoL upgrades like Chronomancy and Astromancy, and eventually, the endgame technologies like Anachronomancy and Megalomania.

item.title: Mining
item.description:
Mining is a crucial early-game technology research in Kittens Game, foundational to developing your industrial economy by unlocking the Miner profession and the Mine building, which produce Minerals.

Unlocking and Costs

  • Prerequisite: Mining is unlocked after researching Agriculture (100 Science).
  • Cost: Researching Mining requires 500 Science.

Effects and Functionality

Mining enables kittens to produce minerals and unlocks critical early buildings and effects:

  • Job Unlocked: It unlocks the Miner job, allowing kittens to accumulate Minerals at a base rate of +0.05 Minerals per Tick.
  • Building Unlocked: It unlocks the Mine building.
    • Mines cost 100 Wood to build and have a price ratio of 1.15.
    • Each Mine provides a +20% Minerals bonus.
  • Resource Source: Mining enables Meteors, which are events that grant a small, automatic boost to your Minerals.
  • Workshop Upgrade: It unlocks the Bolas Workshop upgrade, which improves hunting effectiveness.

Strategic Significance (Early Game)

Mining is essential for transitioning from a simple catnip and wood economy to one capable of producing processed materials:
item.content:encoded:
Mining is a crucial early-game technology research in Kittens Game, foundational to developing your industrial economy by unlocking the Miner profession and the Mine building, which produce Minerals.

Unlocking and Costs

  • Prerequisite: Mining is unlocked after researching Agriculture (100 Science).
  • Cost: Researching Mining requires 500 Science.

Effects and Functionality

Mining enables kittens to produce minerals and unlocks critical early buildings and effects:

  • Job Unlocked: It unlocks the Miner job, allowing kittens to accumulate Minerals at a base rate of +0.05 Minerals per Tick.
  • Building Unlocked: It unlocks the Mine building.
    • Mines cost 100 Wood to build and have a price ratio of 1.15.
    • Each Mine provides a +20% Minerals bonus.
  • Resource Source: Mining enables Meteors, which are events that grant a small, automatic boost to your Minerals.
  • Workshop Upgrade: It unlocks the Bolas Workshop upgrade, which improves hunting effectiveness.

Strategic Significance (Early Game)

Mining is essential for transitioning from a simple catnip and wood economy to one capable of producing processed materials:

  • Mineral Access: Minerals become increasingly important for advanced buildings. Mining allows you to secure a consistent supply of Minerals early on.
  • Progression Path: Mining is typically researched after Agriculture, along with Archery. While Hunting (unlocked by Archery) starts weak, Mining immediately yields a useful amount of Minerals, even with a single Miner.
  • Next Technology: Mining unlocks Metal Working, which is necessary to build Smelters for converting Minerals into Iron.
  • Policy Conflict: Mining also unlocks the Strip Mining environmental policy (costing 2000 Science), which increases mineral production by 30% but adds 5% pollution and incurs a -2% happiness penalty.

Interactions in Iron Will Mode

In the self-imposed restriction mode, Iron Will (where housing cannot be built), Mining is essential for gaining minerals:

  • Mineral Source: In Iron Will mode, meteors that appear after researching Mining are one of the only initial ways to gain Minerals. Building more Mines increases the Mineral bonus received from these meteors.
  • Policy Effect: The Strip Mining policy is highly recommended in Iron Will mode because it grants a +10% bonus minerals from meteors.
  • Coal Production: The Deep Mining upgrade (unlocked by Steel) allows Mines to produce 0.003 Coal per Tick.

item.title: Physics
item.description:
Physics is a crucial mid-game technology research that opens up highly advanced industrial and temporal mechanics, setting the stage for the transition into the titanium and space eras.

Here is a detailed breakdown of the Physics technology:

Unlocking and Cost

  • Prerequisite: Physics is unlocked after researching Navigation.
  • Cost: Researching Physics requires 50,000 Science and 35 Compendiums.

Strategic Importance and Subsequent Research

Physics is a key stepping stone in the scientific progression, particularly because it enables the construction of high-tier industrial buildings and unlocks critical next-tier science branches.
item.content:encoded:
Physics is a crucial mid-game technology research that opens up highly advanced industrial and temporal mechanics, setting the stage for the transition into the titanium and space eras.

Here is a detailed breakdown of the Physics technology:

Unlocking and Cost

  • Prerequisite: Physics is unlocked after researching Navigation.
  • Cost: Researching Physics requires 50,000 Science and 35 Compendiums.

Strategic Importance and Subsequent Research

Physics is a key stepping stone in the scientific progression, particularly because it enables the construction of high-tier industrial buildings and unlocks critical next-tier science branches.

  • Technology Unlocks: Physics immediately unlocks three advanced sciences:
    1. Chemistry
    2. Electricity
    3. Metaphysics
  • Industrial Path: Physics is the first step in the crucial path toward the Concrete era. This path continues through Electricity $\to$ Industrialization $\to$ Mechanization, which ultimately unlocks the Factory building and the ability to craft Concrete.
  • Space Transition: Physics is a prerequisite on the path to Rocketry, which is necessary to access the Space tab.

Upgrades and Resources Unlocked

  • Craftable Resource: Researching Physics enables the ability to craft Blueprints. Blueprints are essential for constructing advanced industrial and utility buildings like Steamworks and Reactors.
  • Workshop Upgrades: Physics unlocks several valuable Workshop upgrades:
    • Steel Saw: Improves Lumber Mill efficiency by an additional +20%.
    • Pyrolysis: Boosts Coal output by +20% (multiplies with other effects, though Smelters are unaffected).
    • Pneumatic Press: Expands Steamworks automation to include converting iron to plates when resources cap out.

Context in the Progression Loop

The decision to research Physics is part of the move past the Theology and Astronomy hurdle. Once unlocked, Physics leads into a phase where the player focuses on generating the titanium needed for construction and acquiring Blueprints (which are convertible from Compendiums after Physics is researched) for technology advancements. Players focused on paragon farming often prioritize this research path to accelerate technological development.

item.title: Policy for Early Game Cycle
item.description:
The Policy/ available early in Kittens Game are crucial for optimizing resource accumulation, accelerating the cultural and scientific development required to reach later phases, and preparing for the first major reset (Phase 1/2: Village, Order of the Sun, chasing Paragon).

The overall strategy in the early game is to maximize global production through kittens and happiness, while overcoming specific resource bottlenecks like wood and manuscripts.

Here are the recommended policy choices during early game cycles, generally unlocked after researching Engineering:
item.content:encoded:
The Policy/ available early in Kittens Game are crucial for optimizing resource accumulation, accelerating the cultural and scientific development required to reach later phases, and preparing for the first major reset (Phase 1/2: Village, Order of the Sun, chasing Paragon).

The overall strategy in the early game is to maximize global production through kittens and happiness, while overcoming specific resource bottlenecks like wood and manuscripts.

Here are the recommended policy choices during early game cycles, generally unlocked after researching Engineering:

1. Environment Policy/

Policy Choice Rationale & Effect
Clear Cutting Clear Cutting is highly recommended over its alternatives.
It provides a substantial +30% wood production bonus.
This boost is critical because wood becomes a “huge help” for constructing major mid-game buildings, such as observatories, harbours, and ships (required after researching Navigation).
Note: Although it introduces a small penalty of -2% happiness and +5% pollution, the resource gain outweighs these drawbacks during this developmental phase. The alternative, Environmentalism, is considered “pretty weak and doesn’t do much for you”.

2. Government Policy/ (Tier 1: Unlocked by Writing)

Policy Choice Rationale & Effect
Tradition Tradition is generally preferred.
This policy accelerates the essential manuscript grind required to advance the science tree (especially toward Theology and Astronomy).
It reduces the manuscript cost ($-100$ culture and $-5$ parchment) and doubles the manuscript maximum culture effect.
Note: While Liberty increases the production effect of happiness, experts favour Tradition for accelerating the major cultural bottleneck. For early runs where unhappiness is a major factor, some players might consider Liberty to offset the production hit, but typically suggest switching to Tradition later.

3. Government Policy/ (Tier 2: Unlocked by Writing + Prior Policy)

Policy Choice Rationale & Effect
Monarchy Monarchy is considered an “AMAZING” choice due to its flexibility and scaling potential.
It makes the leader’s trait twice as powerful. For example, a Leader with the Artisan trait will gain a +10% craft ratio instead of +5% (ignoring other bonuses).
This is powerful because a highly promoted leader can provide a massive boost to whatever resource is currently bottlenecking production, such as wood, science, or crafting efficiency.
Contrast: Alternatives like Republic and Autocracy offer small bonuses that are generally dwarfed by Monarchy’s multiplicative leader effect.

4. Philosophy Policy/ (Unlocked by Philosophy)

Policy Choice Rationale & Effect
Epicureanism Epicureanism is often preferred because it focuses on boosting overall production.
Luxury resources (Furs, Ivory, Spice) will provide 11% happiness instead of the base 10%. Higher happiness is critical for increasing kitten productivity across all jobs.
By the time this policy is reached, trade and hunting systems should be robust enough to manage luxury consumption, making Stoicism (which halves consumption) less necessary.

5. Foreign Policy/ (Unlocked by Currency)

Policy Choice Rationale & Effect
Diplomacy Diplomacy is a standard early pick in the Foreign tree.
Each trade costs 5 less Catpower. Catpower is a foundational resource needed for hunting, exploration, and trade.
Furthermore, choosing Diplomacy leads to the subsequent policy Cultural Exchange, which boosts culture income.

In summary, for early game cycles, the optimal choices centre on Clear Cutting (for wood/infrastructure), Tradition (for manuscript/science velocity), and Monarchy/Epicureanism (for maximizing kitten production via happiness and leader efficiency).

item.title: Rationality vs Mysticism
item.description:
The conflict between Rationality and Mysticism is presented in Kittens Game as a choice between two philosophical Policy/ that offer distinct bonuses to your production. You may only select one of these options, and your choice impacts the resources you prioritise.

Policy Comparison

Policy Prerequisite Cost (Culture) Effect Strategic Assessment
Rationality Stoicism or Epicureanism 3000 +5% science and iron production Recommended to skip, as science is generally easy to get.
Mysticism Stoicism or Epicureanism 3000 +5% culture and faith production Recommended to pick, as culture and faith accumulation is intrinsically slow.

Both Policy/ are available after you have chosen between Stoicism and Epicureanism.
item.content:encoded:
The conflict between Rationality and Mysticism is presented in Kittens Game as a choice between two philosophical Policy/ that offer distinct bonuses to your production. You may only select one of these options, and your choice impacts the resources you prioritise.

Policy Comparison

Policy Prerequisite Cost (Culture) Effect Strategic Assessment
Rationality Stoicism or Epicureanism 3000 +5% science and iron production Recommended to skip, as science is generally easy to get.
Mysticism Stoicism or Epicureanism 3000 +5% culture and faith production Recommended to pick, as culture and faith accumulation is intrinsically slow.

Both Policy/ are available after you have chosen between Stoicism and Epicureanism.

Strategic Implications

The choice between the two Policy/ is often straightforward, based on which resources present a greater long-term bottleneck:

  1. Mysticism (Recommended Choice): It is generally recommended to choose Mysticism.

    • Culture and Faith Bottleneck: The primary reason is that Faith and Culture accumulation is notoriously slow in the game, particularly in the mid-game when these resources become necessary for advancements like Theology and Temple upgrades.
    • Maximising Production: The $+5%$ bonus provided by Mysticism is useful for accelerating the rate at which you can generate these inputs, helping to overcome the cultural hurdle.

  2. Rationality (Generally Avoided): The benefit offered by Rationality is often considered less valuable.

    • Science Accumulation: Science is generally easy to acquire through dedicated Scholar kittens and scientific buildings (like Libraries and Academies), meaning the $+5%$ science bonus is not needed as urgently as the boost to slower resources.
    • Iron Production: While iron is a critical resource, boosting its production by $+5%$ is less impactful than improving the speed of faith and culture generation, especially since iron can often be acquired efficiently through trade (e.g., trading wood to Griffins).

item.title: Workers
item.description:
The term “rank” in relation to kittens/workers in Kittens Game refers to two distinct systems: the Skill Level gained through job experience, which boosts a kitten’s productivity in that specific job, and the Leader Rank, gained through promotion, which boosts the selected leader’s overall production regardless of their job.

1. Kitten Skill Levels (Job Rank)

Kittens assigned to a job gather experience and increase their skill level in that task. This skill level provides a multiplicative bonus to productivity in their specific job.
item.content:encoded:
The term “rank” in relation to kittens/workers in Kittens Game refers to two distinct systems: the Skill Level gained through job experience, which boosts a kitten’s productivity in that specific job, and the Leader Rank, gained through promotion, which boosts the selected leader’s overall production regardless of their job.

1. Kitten Skill Levels (Job Rank)

Kittens assigned to a job gather experience and increase their skill level in that task. This skill level provides a multiplicative bonus to productivity in their specific job.

The seven progressive skill levels and their associated bonuses are:

Skill Level Experience Needed Bonus to Productivity
Dabbling 0 0%
Novice 100 1%
Adequate 500 3%
Competent 1200 4%
Skilled 2500 8%
Proficient 5000 13%
Master 9000 18.75%

These bonuses can be further enhanced by the Workshop upgrades Logistics (increasing the skill bonus by 15%) and Augmentations (increasing the skill bonus by 100%).

2. Leader Rank (Promotion)

The Leader Rank is a separate ranking system unlocked by the Civil Service science. A kitten gains a rank when promoted, which requires spending gold and experience. The bonus from the Leader’s rank applies to that kitten’s production regardless of their job.

Leader Rank (n) Experience Cost Gold Cost Production Bonus (to Leader)
0 0 0 0%
1 500 25 43%
4 2680 100 257%
6 8207 150 400%
8 25133 200 543%

A promoted leader can be unassigned and reassigned to whatever job needs the most assistance.

Policy Interaction:

  • If the Monarchy policy is researched, the leader’s trait is twice as powerful.
  • If the Autocracy policy is researched, the leader’s production bonus (based on rank) is doubled (x2).
  • If the Republic policy is researched, all non-leader kittens get a bonus to their jobs equal to $1%$ of the leader’s bonus.

item.title: Aqueduct
item.description:
The Aqueduct is an early-to-mid-game food production building in Kittens Game, unlocked through the technological progression.

Here is a detailed breakdown of the Aqueduct based on the provided sources:

1. Construction and Unlocks

  • Technology Prerequisite: The Aqueduct is unlocked by researching Engineering. Engineering itself is unlocked by Construction.
  • Cost: The base cost to construct an Aqueduct is 75 Minerals, and it has a price ratio of 1.12.
  • Visibility: Like most buildings, the Aqueduct will stay hidden in the Bonfire tab until you have at least 30% of the necessary resources to build the first one.

2. Purpose and Effects

The Aqueduct’s primary function is to boost Catnip production by applying a percentile bonus:
item.content:encoded:
The Aqueduct is an early-to-mid-game food production building in Kittens Game, unlocked through the technological progression.

Here is a detailed breakdown of the Aqueduct based on the provided sources:

1. Construction and Unlocks

  • Technology Prerequisite: The Aqueduct is unlocked by researching Engineering. Engineering itself is unlocked by Construction.
  • Cost: The base cost to construct an Aqueduct is 75 Minerals, and it has a price ratio of 1.12.
  • Visibility: Like most buildings, the Aqueduct will stay hidden in the Bonfire tab until you have at least 30% of the necessary resources to build the first one.

2. Purpose and Effects

The Aqueduct’s primary function is to boost Catnip production by applying a percentile bonus:

  • Catnip Production: It provides a +3% bonus to Catnip production.
  • Strategy Recommendation: Players are advised to research Engineering and build lots of Aqueducts, as they increase Catnip production by a percentile and should be “far cheaper for a while” compared to constantly buying more Catnip Fields.

3. Upgrades and Progression

The Aqueduct is categorized as an Upgraded Building, meaning it can be converted into a more advanced structure:

  • Upgrade Path: The Aqueduct can be upgraded to a Hydro Plant.
  • Strategic Conversion Advice: The decision to upgrade is based on resource needs: “When you need Energy more than you need catnip”.
    • Demolishing Aqueducts carelessly by upgrading them can quickly lead to a starvation situation.
    • The guide notes that upgrading Aqueducts to Hydro Plants is a riskier conversion than upgrading Pastures to Solar Farms.
    • Hydro Plants also cost a fair amount of Titanium, so players should wait until they have good Titanium production before switching.

4. General Economic Context

The Aqueduct is part of the early game routine focused on establishing a strong economic foundation, known as the Basic Resource Rotation (BRR). After capping catnip fields and focusing on wood, the routine advises focusing on minerals and then mineral-only buildings, which includes Aqueducts.

item.title: Barn
item.description:
The Barn is a crucial early-to-mid-game storage building in Kittens Game, designed to increase resource storage limits, particularly for Catnip, which helps in managing seasonal challenges.

Here is a detailed breakdown of the Barn:

1. Construction and Unlocks

  • Technology Prerequisite: The Barn building is unlocked by researching Agriculture.
  • Cost: The base cost to build one Barn is 50 Wood.
  • Price Ratio: The Barn has a price ratio of 1.75.

2. Core Function and Storage Capacity

Barns primarily serve to increase the maximum storage capacity for fundamental resources. Increasing storage maximums (caps) is cited as the second most important thing in the game, preventing progress walls when resources exceed storage limits.
item.content:encoded:
The Barn is a crucial early-to-mid-game storage building in Kittens Game, designed to increase resource storage limits, particularly for Catnip, which helps in managing seasonal challenges.

Here is a detailed breakdown of the Barn:

1. Construction and Unlocks

  • Technology Prerequisite: The Barn building is unlocked by researching Agriculture.
  • Cost: The base cost to build one Barn is 50 Wood.
  • Price Ratio: The Barn has a price ratio of 1.75.

2. Core Function and Storage Capacity

Barns primarily serve to increase the maximum storage capacity for fundamental resources. Increasing storage maximums (caps) is cited as the second most important thing in the game, preventing progress walls when resources exceed storage limits.

A single Barn provides the following storage increases:

Resource Maximum Storage Increase per Barn
Catnip +5000
Wood +200
Minerals +250
Iron +50
Coal +60
Gold +10
Titanium +2

3. Strategic Importance

  • Winter Survival: The major increase in Catnip storage provided by Barns makes surviving Winters (when Catnip production nosedives by up to -75% or -90% in a Cold Winter) significantly easier, helping to prevent kittens from starving.
  • Early Game Priority: Unlocking Agriculture and then purchasing Barns is essential to quickly establish a strong economic foundation. They are classified as general storage buildings that should be built “as needed”.
  • Resource Rotation: In the Basic Resource Rotation (BRR), after capping Catnip fields, players are advised to focus on “wood only buildings,” which includes Barns.

4. Upgrades and Storage Synergy

Barns benefit from several workshop upgrades, many of which apply across multiple storage structures (Barns, Warehouses, and Harbors):

  • Direct Capacity Increases:
    • Expanded Barns: Increases max storage for Wood, Minerals, and Iron by 75%.
    • Reinforced Barns: Increases max storage for Wood, Minerals, and Iron by 80%.
    • Titanium Barns and Alloy Barns: Each increase max storage for Wood, Minerals, and Iron by 100%.
    • Concrete Barns: Increases max storage for Wood, Minerals, and Iron by 75%.
  • General Storage Upgrades: Barns also benefit from upgrades that apply broadly to common resource storage across multiple buildings, such as Reinforced Warehouses, Titanium Warehouses, Alloy Warehouses, and Concrete Warehouses.
  • Concrete Pillars: This upgrade increases the maximum storage for Wood, Minerals, and Iron from Barns and Warehouses by 5%. It also applies a 5% bonus to max Coal, Gold, and Titanium storage from Barns and other facilities.
  • Silos Synergy: Although Warehouses are the only building that can directly store Catnip via the Silos upgrade, once Silos is researched, all storage upgrades with “barns” in their name apply 25% of their effect to maximum Catnip storage as well.

item.title: Calciner
item.description:
The Calciner is an industrial building in Kittens Game that plays a key role in mid-to-late game resource refinement, specifically concerning Iron and Titanium production.

Here is a comprehensive breakdown of the Calciner’s purpose, costs, effects, and strategic importance, drawing on the sources:

1. Construction and Unlocks

  • Prerequisite Technology: The Calciner building is unlocked by researching the Chemistry technology. Chemistry is a late-Physics technology.
  • Cost: The base cost to construct a Calciner is 100 Steel, 15 Titanium, 1 Blueprint, and 500 Oil.
  • Energy: It consumes 1 Energy per tick to operate.

2. Purpose and Effects

The Calciner’s primary function is advanced refinement, specifically converting minerals and oil into Iron and Titanium:
item.content:encoded:
The Calciner is an industrial building in Kittens Game that plays a key role in mid-to-late game resource refinement, specifically concerning Iron and Titanium production.

Here is a comprehensive breakdown of the Calciner’s purpose, costs, effects, and strategic importance, drawing on the sources:

1. Construction and Unlocks

  • Prerequisite Technology: The Calciner building is unlocked by researching the Chemistry technology. Chemistry is a late-Physics technology.
  • Cost: The base cost to construct a Calciner is 100 Steel, 15 Titanium, 1 Blueprint, and 500 Oil.
  • Energy: It consumes 1 Energy per tick to operate.

2. Purpose and Effects

The Calciner’s primary function is advanced refinement, specifically converting minerals and oil into Iron and Titanium:

  • Input Consumption:
    • It consumes 1.5 Minerals per tick.
    • It consumes 0.024 Oil per tick.
  • Output Production (Conversion Production):
    • It produces 0.15 Iron per tick.
    • It produces 0.0005 Titanium per tick.

Calciners are one of the core buildings whose production counts as “Conversion production”.

3. Upgrades and Enhancements

The efficiency of Calciners can be significantly boosted through Workshop upgrades, usually unlocked by Metallurgy and Nanotechnology:

Upgrade Name Effect Prerequisite
Oxidation Increases Iron production by +95% and Titanium production by +285%. Metallurgy.
Rotary Kiln Increases Iron production by +75% and Titanium production by +225%. Robotics.
Fluidized Reactors Increases Iron production by +100% and Titanium production by +300%. Nanotechnology.
Steel Plants Converts 10% of the Calciner’s Iron output into Steel (100:1 ratio), decreasing the final Iron output by 10%. Robotics.
Automated Plants Boosts the Steel production from Steel Plants by 25% of the general craft ratio. Steel Plants.
Nuclear Plants Boosts the Steel production from Steel Plants by an additional 2% per active Reactor. Automated Plants.
Policy Bonus The Autocracy policy provides a bonus of 0.4% per leader rank per uncapped population building to all conversion production, which includes Calciners.
Policy Bonus The Griffin Relations: Metallurgists policy increases the Calciner’s steel production bonus by +15%. Griffin Embassy Level 20, Diplomacy metaphysics.

4. Strategic Role and Recommendations

Calciners are a type of building that boosts general production but costs hard-to-acquire blueprints.

  • Resource Focus: They are one of the main ways to produce Iron and Titanium.
  • Mid-Game Investment: In the Pre Titanium era notes, it is advised that players should consider purchasing production-boosting buildings that cost blueprints, such as Calciners, Steamworks, Magnetos, and Reactors, as this “will help a lot in creating the base resources”.
  • Black Sky Challenge: In the Black Sky Challenge, where astronomical events (a source of Starcharts/Blueprints) do not occur, the initial cost of Calciners is altered to make them possible to obtain without relying on Starcharts.
  • Pollution: Calciners are among the buildings that produce pollution.

item.title: Factory
item.description:
The Factory is a mid-to-late-game industrial building in Kittens Game, primarily focused on boosting crafting efficiency and playing a role in advanced resource production, pollution management, and policy prerequisites.

Here is a comprehensive breakdown of the Factory:

1. Unlocking and Cost

  • Prerequisite Technology: The Factory is unlocked by researching Mechanization, which costs 115K Science and 45 Blueprints, and follows the Industrialization branch.
  • Resource Cost: Factories are expensive, requiring three processed, mid-game resources:
    • Titanium: 2000 units
    • Plate: 2500 units
    • Concrete: 15 units
  • Price Ratio: The Factory has a price ratio of 1.15.
  • Policy Reduction: The Communism policy makes factories 30% cheaper.

2. Effects and Function

The Factory’s primary effect is boosting crafting efficiency and consuming energy:
item.content:encoded:
The Factory is a mid-to-late-game industrial building in Kittens Game, primarily focused on boosting crafting efficiency and playing a role in advanced resource production, pollution management, and policy prerequisites.

Here is a comprehensive breakdown of the Factory:

1. Unlocking and Cost

  • Prerequisite Technology: The Factory is unlocked by researching Mechanization, which costs 115K Science and 45 Blueprints, and follows the Industrialization branch.
  • Resource Cost: Factories are expensive, requiring three processed, mid-game resources:
    • Titanium: 2000 units
    • Plate: 2500 units
    • Concrete: 15 units
  • Price Ratio: The Factory has a price ratio of 1.15.
  • Policy Reduction: The Communism policy makes factories 30% cheaper.

2. Effects and Function

The Factory’s primary effect is boosting crafting efficiency and consuming energy:

  • Crafting Bonus: Each Factory provides a +5% Crafting bonus. This bonus is equivalent to the effect provided by a kitten with the Artisan trait when they are selected as the leader.
  • Energy Consumption: Each Factory consumes -2 Energy.
  • Pollution: Factories are listed among the structures that produce pollution. However, pollution produced by factories can be reduced to zero by the Carbon Sequestration upgrade.

3. Upgrades and Policy Interactions

Factories are central to several mid-to-late-game scaling mechanics:

  • Policy Prerequisite: Factories are required to unlock high-tier Government Policy/ such as Liberalism, Communism, and Fascism.
    • If you choose the Full Industrialization policy (which follows Strip Mining or Clear Cutting), the crafting bonus from Factories is further improved by 5% (e.g., from +5% to +5.25%, or from +6% to +6.3% depending on upgrades). This policy is recommended from the second run onward, as players will be building many Factories.
  • Crafting Boost Upgrades:
    • The Factory Logistics Workshop upgrade increases the craft bonus of Factories by an additional +1%.
  • Space Manufacturing: The Space Manufacturing upgrade enables Factories to improve Space Elevators and Orbital Arrays by 3.75% per factory (4.5% with Factory Logistics). This bonus is crucial because most production bonuses (like Paragon and Magnetos) do not apply to space structures, making Factories one of the few ways to increase space building production efficiency.
  • Oil and Refinement: The Factory Processing upgrade, unlocked by Oil Processing Science, causes every Factory to increase oil refinement effectiveness by 5%. Factories also help oil production once the Hydraulic Fracturers are employed (unlocked by the Dune Mission).
  • Pollution Mitigation: The Carbon Sequestration upgrade allows Factories to capture pollution from the atmosphere instead of creating it by consuming 4Wt of energy per Factory, reducing pollution by 2 points per tick.

4. Strategic Role

Factories are built to enhance the creation of complex resources needed for endgame technologies, especially in subsequent runs.

  • Endgame Crafting: Factories are maximized (along with Workshops) to increase the crafting ratio, which helps reduce the number of crafts needed to produce high-tier materials like Eludium.
  • Unobtainium Production: Factories are instrumental in maximizing Unobtainium production in the late game through the Space Manufacturing upgrade. They contribute to the space production bonus via the number of Factories and the Factory Logistics upgrade.
  • Blueprint Generation: Factories contribute indirectly to the essential task of generating Blueprints by boosting the crafting process (Furs $\to$ Parchment $\to$ Manuscript $\to$ Compendium $\to$ Blueprint).
  • Building Priority: Factories are one of the key production-boosting structures that “should be built provided you have the resources to use on them” in the mid-to-late game.

item.title: Harbour
item.description:
The Harbour is a crucial mid-game storage building in Kittens Game, essential for expanding resource limits, especially as your civilization begins advanced production and trading operations.

Here is a detailed overview of the Harbour:

The Harbour is unlocked after reaching the Navigation stage of your technology tree, and it requires crafted materials to build:

  • Prerequisite Technology: Navigation.
  • Resource Cost: Building a Harbour costs a combination of processed materials:
    • Scaffold: 5 units
    • Slab: 50 units
    • Plate: 75 units. Plate is listed as a craftable resource required for early and mid-game buildings, especially Harbours.
  • Price Ratio: The Harbour has a price ratio of 1.15.

Primary Function: Resource Storage

Harbours are categorized as general storage buildings designed to increase the maximum capacity of numerous common and uncommon resources:

The Harbour is a crucial mid-game storage building in Kittens Game, essential for expanding resource limits, especially as your civilization begins advanced production and trading operations.

Here is a detailed overview of the Harbour:

Unlocking and Cost

The Harbour is unlocked after reaching the Navigation stage of your technology tree, and it requires crafted materials to build:

  • Prerequisite Technology: Navigation.
  • Resource Cost: Building a Harbour costs a combination of processed materials:
    • Scaffold: 5 units
    • Slab: 50 units
    • Plate: 75 units. Plate is listed as a craftable resource required for early and mid-game buildings, especially Harbours.
  • Price Ratio: The Harbour has a price ratio of 1.15.

Primary Function: Resource Storage

Harbours are categorized as general storage buildings designed to increase the maximum capacity of numerous common and uncommon resources:

Resource Storage Increase per Harbour
Catnip +2,500
Wood +700
Minerals +950
Iron +150
Coal +100
Gold +25
Titanium +50

Scaling and Upgrades

The effectiveness of Harbours can be enhanced through various Workshop and technology upgrades:

  • Trade Ship Capacity Bonus (Expanded Cargo): The Expanded Cargo upgrade, unlocked by Navigation, grants a bonus of +1% to Harbour capacity per Trade Ship. This bonus is subject to diminishing returns past 168.75% and is capped at 225%.
  • Reactor Capacity Boost (Reactor Vessel): The Reactor Vessel upgrade increases the Expanded Cargo limit by +5% per Reactor.
  • Coal Storage (Barges): The Barges upgrade increases the maximum Coal storage provided by Harbours by 50%.
  • General Storage Upgrades: Harbours also benefit from global storage upgrades initially designed for Barns and Warehouses, such as Expanded Barns, Reinforced Barns, Titanium Barns, Alloy Barns, and Concrete Barns, which increase the storage capacity for wood, minerals, and iron.

Strategic Role

Harbours are vital for maintaining economic momentum in the mid-game:

  • Resource Management: They address the strategic need to increase resource storage limits (or “caps”). If progress is stalled because resource storage limits are too low, building storage buildings like Harbours is necessary.
  • Progression Path: The early policy choice Clear Cutting is recommended because the resulting wood production boost is crucial for constructing Harbours, Observatories, and Trade Ships.
  • Titanium Buff: Harbours are among the structures that provide an early boost to Titanium storage capacity, which is necessary before more advanced storage options become available.

item.title: Magneto
item.description:
The Magneto is a crucial industrial building in Kittens Game, marking an advancement in your civilization’s energy and production capabilities.

Here is a comprehensive breakdown of the Magneto’s features, strategic role, and related concepts:

Unlocking and Cost

  • Technology Requirement: The Magneto is unlocked by researching Electricity. Electricity requires 75,000 Science and 85 Compendiums.
  • Resource Cost: Building a Magneto is expensive, requiring advanced materials:
    • Alloy: 10 units
    • Gear: 5 units
    • Blueprint: 1 unit
  • Price Ratio: The Magneto has a price ratio of 1.25.

Effects and Function

The Magneto serves two primary functions: generating energy and boosting global production.
item.content:encoded:
The Magneto is a crucial industrial building in Kittens Game, marking an advancement in your civilization’s energy and production capabilities.

Here is a comprehensive breakdown of the Magneto’s features, strategic role, and related concepts:

Unlocking and Cost

  • Technology Requirement: The Magneto is unlocked by researching Electricity. Electricity requires 75,000 Science and 85 Compendiums.
  • Resource Cost: Building a Magneto is expensive, requiring advanced materials:
    • Alloy: 10 units
    • Gear: 5 units
    • Blueprint: 1 unit
  • Price Ratio: The Magneto has a price ratio of 1.25.

Effects and Function

The Magneto serves two primary functions: generating energy and boosting global production.

  1. Global Production Boost: Magnetos provide a +2% Global Production bonus.
    • This makes them highly desirable, as global modifiers are generally prioritized over specific resource upgrades for efficient scaling.
    • In the strategic advice of the mid-game, Magnetos are among the general production-boosting items that “should be built provided you have the resources to use on them”.
  2. Energy Production: Each Magneto provides +5 Energy.
  3. Consumption: Magnetos consume -0.05 Oil per Tick.

Strategic Role and Integration

Magnetos are vital in the mid-to-late game for powering energy-intensive structures, often working in tandem with other industrial buildings.

  • Energy Generation Focus: Magnetos, along with Steamworks and Reactors, are listed as structures that increase production for resources. They provide necessary energy to ensure that other advanced buildings operate at full efficiency.
  • Relationship with Steamworks: Steamworks are industrial buildings that consume Coal and provide +1 Energy as well as a Magneto Boost of +15%. This suggests that Steamworks enhance the production effects of Magnetos.
    • In the late game, the effectiveness of Magnetos is listed as one of the primary production boosts, alongside Reactor bonuses and the Solar Revolution bonus.
    • The Griffin Relations: Machinists policy further improves this synergy, increasing the Steamwork’s Magneto boost bonus by +0.5%.
  • Energy/Pollution Policy Interaction: The Lizard Relations: Ecologists policy can interact with Magnetos. Depending on how many Hydro Plants are active, some of your Magnetos will continue to boost resource production even if they are turned off.
  • Endgame Context: Once Magnetos come into play, the influence of population growth on global production becomes “very minor”.

In essence, the Magneto is a powerful scaling tool that uses high-tier crafting resources (Alloy, Gear, Blueprint) to provide clean energy and a straight global production multiplier, reinforcing the strategy of focusing on overall efficiency rather than singular resource production gains.

The Steamworks building primarily benefits the Magneto structure, as well as several other production-related processes through its upgrades and functionality.

Here is a breakdown of the buildings that benefit from Steamworks:

4. Magneto (Boosted Production)

The Magneto building receives a direct, inherent boost from the Steamworks.

  • Magneto Boost: Each Steamworks provides a +15% Magneto Boost. This increases the Magneto’s effect of providing a +2% Global Production bonus.
  • Policy Enhancement: This Magneto boost provided by the Steamworks can be further improved by the Griffin Relations: Machinists policy, which increases the Steamwork’s Magneto boost bonus by +0.5%.

item.title: Mansion

The Mansion becomes available after reaching the mid-game architectural stage of development.

  • Prerequisite Technology: Mansions are unlocked by researching Architecture. Architecture costs 42,000 Science and 10 Compendiums, and is unlocked after Navigation.
  • Resource Cost: Constructing a Mansion requires advanced, processed materials:
    • Slab: 185 units
    • Steel: 75 units
    • Titanium: 25 units
  • Price Ratio: The Mansion has a price ratio of 1.15.

Effects and Function

As a population building, the Mansion contributes to increasing your workforce capacity.
item.content:encoded:
The Mansion is a high-tier housing structure in Kittens Game, succeeding the Hut and Log House, and is essential for maximizing your kitten population in the later stages of the game.

Here is a detailed breakdown of the Mansion:

Unlocking and Cost

The Mansion becomes available after reaching the mid-game architectural stage of development.

  • Prerequisite Technology: Mansions are unlocked by researching Architecture. Architecture costs 42,000 Science and 10 Compendiums, and is unlocked after Navigation.
  • Resource Cost: Constructing a Mansion requires advanced, processed materials:
    • Slab: 185 units
    • Steel: 75 units
    • Titanium: 25 units
  • Price Ratio: The Mansion has a price ratio of 1.15.

Effects and Function

As a population building, the Mansion contributes to increasing your workforce capacity.

  • Maximum Kittens: Each Mansion increases the maximum number of Kittens by +1.
  • Maximum Catpower: Each Mansion increases the maximum Catpower storage by +50.

Strategic Role

The ability to build Mansions signifies entry into the mid-game where titanium and processed goods are necessary, and they are critical for population-based prestige farming.

  • Population Expansion: Mansions provide housing for more kittens, which is necessary since population acts as a “THE global modifier” in the early game and remains a factor later on.
  • Late-Game Housing Priority: In rapid paragon grinding runs, particularly after multiple resets, players are advised to focus on building Space Stations, Mansions, Log Houses, and Huts to accommodate incoming kittens as fast as they arrive. They are considered key components for maximizing population alongside Huts and Log Houses.
  • Policy Interaction: Mansions are included in the calculation for the Autocracy government policy. The Autocracy leader’s conversion production bonus on Cath is based on the number of uncapped population buildings (Huts, Log Houses, Mansions) for which the player has enough storage space to build more.

item.title: Oil Well
item.description:
The Oil Well is a significant resource-producing building in Kittens Game, marking a progression into the era of advanced fuel and energy infrastructure.

Here is a comprehensive breakdown of the Oil Well based on the sources:

1. Construction and Unlocks

  • Prerequisite Technology: The Oil Well building is unlocked by researching the Chemistry technology.
  • Cost: The base cost to construct an Oil Well is 50 Steel, 25 Gears, and 25 Scaffold.
  • Energy Consumption: Once the Pumpjack upgrade is applied, the Oil Well consumes 1 Energy per tick to operate.

2. Purpose and Production

The Oil Well’s primary function is to introduce and produce Oil, which is crucial for subsequent advanced crafting and energy production.
item.content:encoded:
The Oil Well is a significant resource-producing building in Kittens Game, marking a progression into the era of advanced fuel and energy infrastructure.

Here is a comprehensive breakdown of the Oil Well based on the sources:

1. Construction and Unlocks

  • Prerequisite Technology: The Oil Well building is unlocked by researching the Chemistry technology.
  • Cost: The base cost to construct an Oil Well is 50 Steel, 25 Gears, and 25 Scaffold.
  • Energy Consumption: Once the Pumpjack upgrade is applied, the Oil Well consumes 1 Energy per tick to operate.

2. Purpose and Production

The Oil Well’s primary function is to introduce and produce Oil, which is crucial for subsequent advanced crafting and energy production.

  • Output: The Oil Well produces +0.02 Oil per Tick.
  • Storage: Each Oil Well provides +1500 Max Oil capacity.

Oil is classified as a Common Resource, produced by Oil Wells or refined from catnip by upgraded Bio Labs. Oil is vital for constructing Calciners and is later processed into Kerosene, a rocket fuel.

3. Upgrades and Strategic Importance

Oil Wells are critical, as Oil quickly becomes a bottleneck resource during the transition to space exploration.

The output of Oil Wells can be boosted by several Workshop upgrades:

Upgrade Name Effect Prerequisite
Pumpjack Improves effectiveness by +45% (additive with other effects). Also adds automation and causes the Oil Well to consume 1 Energy. Mechanization.
Oil Refinery Improves effectiveness by +35%. Combustion.
Oil Distillation Output is improved by +75%. Rocketry.

The need for Oil Wells is frequently emphasized:

  • Early Space Era: In the pre-Metaphysics, “early Space” phase, Oil is slow to produce, making it necessary to build Oil Wells quickly and let them “fill up” their production/storage.
  • Grinding: Grinding out the necessary Steel for Oil Wells is recommended over relying on Tankers for storage cap increases.
  • Coal Management: When grinding coal for Oil Wells, players are advised to turn off Steamworks or anything else consuming coal to maximize the available coal.
  • Overbuilding: Players should build more Oil Wells than they initially need to help increase the oil production rate.

4. Policy Connection

The Full Industrialization policy, which becomes available after researching Industrialization and choosing either Strip Mining or Clear Cutting, boosts the production of Iron, Coal, and Titanium. Although it doesn’t directly boost the Oil Well, it is generally preferred over Sustainability in runs where many factories (which consume Oil indirectly via Kerosene crafting) are built.

item.title: Smelter
item.description:
The Smelter is a foundational industrial building in Kittens Game, crucial for transitioning from basic resource gathering into metal production and industrial expansion. It is primarily used to refine raw minerals and wood into Iron and, eventually, other critical resources.

1. Unlocking and Base Function

  • Prerequisite: The Smelter building is unlocked once you research the Metal Working technology. Metal Working costs 900 Science.
  • Cost: The base cost to build one Smelter is 200 Minerals, with a price ratio of 1.15.
  • Base Conversion: The Smelter converts Wood and Minerals into Iron.
    • It consumes 0.05 Wood per Tick and 0.1 Minerals per Tick.
    • It produces 0.02 Iron per Tick.

2. Strategic Importance

Smelters are vital in the early-to-mid game because they provide the necessary resources to construct key infrastructure and unlock economic options:
item.content:encoded:
The Smelter is a foundational industrial building in Kittens Game, crucial for transitioning from basic resource gathering into metal production and industrial expansion. It is primarily used to refine raw minerals and wood into Iron and, eventually, other critical resources.

1. Unlocking and Base Function

  • Prerequisite: The Smelter building is unlocked once you research the Metal Working technology. Metal Working costs 900 Science.
  • Cost: The base cost to build one Smelter is 200 Minerals, with a price ratio of 1.15.
  • Base Conversion: The Smelter converts Wood and Minerals into Iron.
    • It consumes 0.05 Wood per Tick and 0.1 Minerals per Tick.
    • It produces 0.02 Iron per Tick.

2. Strategic Importance

Smelters are vital in the early-to-mid game because they provide the necessary resources to construct key infrastructure and unlock economic options:

  • Iron for Construction: Iron produced by Smelters is necessary for building:
    • Lumber Mills, which significantly boost Wood output.
    • Observatories, required for Starchart generation.
  • Gold Production for Trade: You must begin creating Gold before you can trade with other civilizations. Smelters enable Gold production once the Gold Ore upgrade is researched in the Workshop.
  • Conversion Production: Smelters are categorized as buildings that contribute to “Conversion production”. Policy/ like Autocracy can boost the output of conversion production based on leader ranks and uncapped housing buildings.

3. Key Upgrades (Expanding Output)

Through Workshop upgrades, the Smelter’s function can be greatly enhanced to produce resources beyond just Iron:

Upgrade Name Resource Unlocked Effect/Purpose Technology Prerequisite
Gold Ore Gold Allows Smelters to produce 0.001 Gold/tick. (In Iron Will mode, Hunting also produces gold after this is researched.) Currency
Coal Furnace Coal Smelters produce 0.005 Coal/tick while operating. Steel
Electrolytic Smelting Increased Iron & Coal Makes Smelters “twice as effective,” producing +95% more Iron and Coal. Metallurgy
Nuclear Smelters Titanium Allows Smelters to produce a small amount of Titanium (0.0015 per tick). Nuclear Fission

4. Context and Drawbacks

Smelters are considered “Industry” buildings, and they are a source of Pollution. Along with other industrial buildings like Mines, Steamworks, Calciners, and Oil Wells, they contribute to the high level of CO2 in the atmosphere that negatively affects kitten happiness and resource production.

In the Iron Will challenge, where kittens are unavailable, players on a long run are advised that Smelters operate at a loss until they reach a “smelt-positive point” where they have enough Magnetos and Steamworks (and potentially Solar Revolution bonus) to make Gold production positive. For early runs generally, Smelters are initially recommended as a way to convert Minerals into Iron.

item.title: Steamworks
item.description:
The Steamworks is an essential industrial building in Kittens Game that introduces early automation, supplements energy production, and is crucial for overcoming the manuscript bottleneck in the mid-game.

Unlocks, Cost, and Base Effects

The Steamworks building is unlocked by researching the Machinery technology, which costs 15,000 Science.

  • Cost: The base cost to construct a Steamworks is 65 Steel, 20 Gear, and 1 Blueprint.
  • Price Ratio: The building has a high price ratio of 1.25.
  • Base Effects:
    • Energy: Provides +1 Energy.
    • Coal: Reduces Coal consumption by 80%.
    • Production Boost: Provides a Magneto Boost of +15%.
  • Drawback: Like other industrial buildings (Mines, Smelters, etc.), the Steamworks produces Pollution.

Strategic Purpose: Automation and Manuscript Production

The primary strategic role of the Steamworks is to introduce automation and overcome resource bottlenecks:
item.content:encoded:
The Steamworks is an essential industrial building in Kittens Game that introduces early automation, supplements energy production, and is crucial for overcoming the manuscript bottleneck in the mid-game.

Unlocks, Cost, and Base Effects

The Steamworks building is unlocked by researching the Machinery technology, which costs 15,000 Science.

  • Cost: The base cost to construct a Steamworks is 65 Steel, 20 Gear, and 1 Blueprint.
  • Price Ratio: The building has a high price ratio of 1.25.
  • Base Effects:
    • Energy: Provides +1 Energy.
    • Coal: Reduces Coal consumption by 80%.
    • Production Boost: Provides a Magneto Boost of +15%.
  • Drawback: Like other industrial buildings (Mines, Smelters, etc.), the Steamworks produces Pollution.

Strategic Purpose: Automation and Manuscript Production

The primary strategic role of the Steamworks is to introduce automation and overcome resource bottlenecks:

  1. Manuscript Automation: Steamworks consume Coal to create a variety of handy items. Critically, once the Printing Press upgrade is researched, Steamworks automatically print Manuscripts at a base rate of 0.0025 manuscripts/sec. Manuscript production can be further boosted by the Offset Press and Photolithography upgrades, which each multiply production by a factor of 4. This automation is necessary for overcoming the steep requirements of the later Theology and Astronomy sciences.

  2. Resource Conversion: The Workshop Automation upgrade allows Steamworks to automatically convert a percentage of wood into beams and minerals into slabs once per year when those resources are nearly capped (at 98% of capacity). The Advanced Automation upgrade makes this process activate twice per year, and Pneumatic Press adds the conversion of iron to plates.

  3. Industrial Foundation: Steamworks are listed among the supplemental production-boosting buildings (alongside Magnetos, Reactors, Calciners, and Quarrys) that cost blueprints and help create base resources.

Upgrades and Efficiency

Several upgrades directly affect the Steamworks’ efficiency and resource consumption:

  • Coal Efficiency: The High Pressure Engine and Fuel Injector upgrades each reduce the Coal consumption of Steamworks by 20%.
  • Magneto Synergy: The Magneto Boost is further improved by the Griffin Relations: Machinists policy, which increases the Steamworks’ Magneto boost bonus by +0.5%.

Contextual Notes

  • Prerequisite Grinding: The Steamworks presents a hurdle because it requires Blueprints and Gears (which require Steel). In the IW 40K run, the Sharks and Griffins trading loop is cited as a key method for collecting the necessary steel, gears, and blueprints for Steamworks.
  • Coal Management: Since Steamworks consume coal, players are advised to turn off Steamworks when grinding coal for other priorities, such as building Oil Wells.
  • Challenges:
    • The Steamworks is listed as a necessary building to complete the Energy Challenge.
    • In the Pacifism Challenge, the cost of the Steamworks increases by 1.5, rounded down to the nearest integer, and the blueprint cost linearly increases by 5.

4. Magneto (Boosted Production)

The Magneto building receives a direct, inherent boost from the Steamworks.

  • Magneto Boost: Each Steamworks provides a +15% Magneto Boost. This increases the Magneto’s effect of providing a +2% Global Production bonus.
  • Policy Enhancement: This Magneto boost provided by the Steamworks can be further improved by the Griffin Relations: Machinists policy, which increases the Steamwork’s Magneto boost bonus by +0.5%.

5. Manuscripts (Automated Production)

The Steamworks facility can be upgraded to automate the production of the advanced resource Manuscripts.

  • Printing Press: The Printing Press upgrade allows Steamworks to produce Manuscript per Tick +0.0005 (or 0.0025 manuscripts/sec). This requires the Steamworks building (unlocked by Machinery).
  • Further Upgrades: This automated production rate can be substantially increased by subsequent Workshop upgrades:
    • Offset Press increases manuscript production by a factor of 4 (to 0.01 manuscripts/sec).
    • Photolithography also increases manuscript production by a factor of 4 (to 0.04 manuscripts/sec).

3. Crafted Resources (Automation)

The core functionality of the Workshop benefits from Steamworks through automated material conversion:

  • Workshop Automation: Steamworks unlock the Workshop Automation upgrade, which causes the Steamworks to convert resources into craftable materials when those resources reach their cap.
    • Once per year, Steamworks convert wood (to beams) and minerals (to slabs) at $98%$ of the resource’s cap.
    • The Advanced Automation upgrade allows this conversion to activate twice per year.
  • Pneumatic Press: This upgrade further expands the automation to include iron being converted to plates.

Strategic Considerations

It is noted that Steamworks consume coal. In the mid-game, experts advise against keeping Steamworks active unless you plan to be idle for long periods, as running them can severely restrict your coal production.

item.title: Star Charts
item.description:
The Starchart is a critical mid-to-late-game special resource necessary for advancing space exploration, unlocking advanced trade methods, and progressing the technological tree.

Here is a detailed breakdown of its acquisition, production, and importance:

1. Acquisition and Production

Starcharts are unlocked after researching Astronomy. They are initially acquired through rare events, with later production managed through dedicated buildings and kitten jobs.

Method Mechanism/Source Details
Astronomical Events Observing rare events after building a Library. The base chance for an event is 0.25% every day. Each Observatory built increases this chance by an additive 0.2% per day. The event must be manually clicked, or it may automatically succeed with a 1% chance per Observatory.
Automation SETI Workshop Upgrade (unlocked by Electronics). This upgrade causes all astronomical events to succeed automatically and silently, instantly granting associated science and starcharts.
Buildings Observatories, Satellites, Research Vessels, and Space Beacons. Research Vessels produce 0.05 starcharts/sec, and Space Beacons produce 0.125 starcharts/sec. Satellites produce 0.005 starcharts/sec.
Kitten Jobs Scholar profession. The Astrophysicists Workshop upgrade allows Scholar kittens to produce +0.0005 starcharts/sec.
Trade Leviathans. Leviathans trade 250 Starchart (with a 50% chance) in exchange for 5000 Unobtainium.
Cycles Numerology and Numeromancy Metaphysics. Certain cycles (Kairo, Cath, Piscine) boost the production of starcharts from space structures. The Kairo Cycle provides a large boost, increasing starchart income by 5x and increasing space beacon starchart production by +400%.

2. Strategic Role and Progression Bottleneck

Starcharts are often considered a major roadblock in the progression towards the space phase of the game.
