Here is a detailed breakdown of its acquisition, production, and importance:

1. Acquisition and Production

Starcharts are unlocked after researching Astronomy. They are initially acquired through rare events, with later production managed through dedicated buildings and kitten jobs.

Method Mechanism/Source Details
Astronomical Events Observing rare events after building a Library. The base chance for an event is 0.25% every day. Each Observatory built increases this chance by an additive 0.2% per day. The event must be manually clicked, or it may automatically succeed with a 1% chance per Observatory.
Automation SETI Workshop Upgrade (unlocked by Electronics). This upgrade causes all astronomical events to succeed automatically and silently, instantly granting associated science and starcharts.
Buildings Observatories, Satellites, Research Vessels, and Space Beacons. Research Vessels produce 0.05 starcharts/sec, and Space Beacons produce 0.125 starcharts/sec. Satellites produce 0.005 starcharts/sec.
Kitten Jobs Scholar profession. The Astrophysicists Workshop upgrade allows Scholar kittens to produce +0.0005 starcharts/sec.
Trade Leviathans. Leviathans trade 250 Starchart (with a 50% chance) in exchange for 5000 Unobtainium.
Cycles Numerology and Numeromancy Metaphysics. Certain cycles (Kairo, Cath, Piscine) boost the production of starcharts from space structures. The Kairo Cycle provides a large boost, increasing starchart income by 5x and increasing space beacon starchart production by +400%.

2. Strategic Role and Progression Bottleneck

Starcharts are often considered a major roadblock in the progression towards the space phase of the game.

Key Uses:

  • Trade Ships: Starcharts are required for crafting Trade Ships, which are crucial for finding and trading with the Zebras to acquire Titanium. Crafting a Trade Ship costs 25 Starchart (this cost can be reduced by the Satellite Navigation upgrade).
  • Space Missions: They are required for all missions in the Space tab, which is unlocked by Rocketry. The costs escalate significantly: the initial Orbital Launch costs 250 Starchart, and the subsequent Moon Mission costs 500 Starchart. Later missions require thousands, such as the Kairo Mission (5000 Starchart) and Rorschach Mission (15,000 Starchart).
  • Advanced Structures: They are necessary for high-tier structures like the Space Beacon (25,000 Starchart) and the Orbital Array (2000 Starchart).
  • Workshop Upgrades: The Geodesy Workshop upgrade, which enables Geologists to find gold, requires 500 Starchart.

Mitigation Strategy:

  • To overcome the starchart bottleneck and obtain the necessary titanium, it is crucial to focus on Observatories immediately after unlocking Astronomy.
  • Metaphysics upgrades like Chronomancy and Astromancy are recommended because starchart production tends to lag, and these upgrades help increase the chance of astronomical events, accelerating the building of a large trade fleet.
  • In the late game, the most efficient method for starchart production is through Research Vessels, although acquiring the first vessel is costly (requiring 2000 total Starcharts for mission and building).

3. Challenge Mode Interactions

The production and necessity of Starcharts change dramatically when certain challenges are active:

  • Black Sky Challenge: This challenge specifically disables astronomical events. Furthermore, Research Vessels no longer produce starcharts in this challenge. However, the initial cost of the Orbital Launch mission is altered, and the starchart requirement is removed.
  • Iron Will Mode: In this challenging mode, astronomical events observed after building Libraries are the only initial source of Science. If the Iron Will mode is combined with the Black Sky Challenge, astrological events are fully disabled, removing one of the main sources of science.

Starcharts are one of the resources that may conditionally carry over on a reset if you have Chronospheres. Specifically, starcharts are included in the list of non-crafted resources preserved by Chronospheres. For a quick paragon farming run, players may stock up to 390k starcharts to carry over 5,850 starcharts (assuming one Chronosphere).

item.title: Titanium
item.description:
Titanium is a vital common resource in Kittens Game, marking the entry into the mid-to-late game “Titanium era,” where complex construction and space exploration become possible.

It is particularly difficult to acquire in large volumes early on, necessitating a pivot to advanced trade and refined production methods.

1. Acquisition and Trade

Titanium is initially acquired primarily through trade, though advanced structures provide domestic production later.

Trading with Zebras

The most important early source is through trading with Zebras, who are initially a Hostile civilisation (-30% attitude).
item.content:encoded:
Titanium is a vital common resource in Kittens Game, marking the entry into the mid-to-late game “Titanium era,” where complex construction and space exploration become possible.

It is particularly difficult to acquire in large volumes early on, necessitating a pivot to advanced trade and refined production methods.

1. Acquisition and Trade

Titanium is initially acquired primarily through trade, though advanced structures provide domestic production later.

Trading with Zebras

The most important early source is through trading with Zebras, who are initially a Hostile civilisation (-30% attitude).

  • Trade Mechanism: Zebras sell Titanium in exchange for Slab (a craftable resource made from Minerals).
  • Scaling: The amount of titanium sold by Zebras is not affected by typical trading bonuses like those from Tradeposts. Instead, the amount of titanium they give is calculated as (0.03 * Trade Ships) + 1.5.
  • Prerequisite: To unlock Zebras for trade, you must first build at least one Trade Ship.
  • Policy Boost: The policy Zebra Relations: Appeasement improves relations with Zebras (as 15 extra Tradeposts) and grants a +15 tradeposts worth of trade ratio titanium sold (multiplicative).
  • Strategic Focus: The strategic goal in the mid-game is to build Observatories to generate Starcharts, which allow you to craft more Trade Ships, thereby accelerating the rate of titanium flow.

Domestic Production (Conversion)

Titanium can be produced domestically through industrial structures that convert other resources:

  • Calciners: Titanium is refined from oil and minerals by Calciners. A single Calciner produces +0.0005 Titanium per Tick. This production can be significantly boosted by upgrades like Oxidation (+285%) and Fluidized Reactors (+300%).
  • Smelters: After researching Nuclear Fission, the Nuclear Smelter upgrade allows Smelters to produce Titanium at a rate of 0.0015 per tick.
  • Policy Boost: The Communism policy provides a straight +25% production boost to iron, coal, and titanium.

2. Strategic Uses and Cost

Titanium is a heavily demanded resource for high-level buildings, workshop upgrades, and space travel.

Key Building Costs

Titanium is required for constructing advanced infrastructure and housing:

Building Titanium Cost Prerequisite/Context
Reactor 3500 Required for Nuclear Fission
Factory 2000 Unlocked by Mechanization
Hydro Plant 2500 Upgrade from Aqueduct; transition should wait until Titanium production is good
Accelerator 7500 Unlocked by Particle Physics
Mansion 25 High-tier housing
Cryostation 7500 (in cost of Cryostation) Advanced storage facility

Upgrades and Progression

Titanium is needed to progress through the housing and crafting technology tree:

  • Housing Upgrades: The core progression upgrade Concrete Huts requires 3000 Titanium, and the later Unobtainium Huts requires 15,000 Titanium.
  • Workshop Upgrades: Titanium is needed for efficiency upgrades such as Titanium Saw and Titanium Axe, and advanced industrial upgrades like Factory Logistics.
  • Space Missions: Titanium is a required resource for several space missions, including the Moon Mission (5000 Titanium) and Dune Mission (7000 Titanium).
  • Uranium Acquisition: Dragons buy Titanium (250 units) and sell Uranium.

3. Storage and Capacity

Titanium has a default initial storage capacity of 2 units. This limit must be increased via storage buildings:

  • Harbours increase storage by +50 Titanium.
  • Moon Bases increase storage by +1250 Titanium.
  • Cryostations increase storage by +7500 Titanium.
  • Accelerators with the Energy Rifts upgrade provide a substantial storage boost, including +750 Titanium.
  • Sunforges also improve storage capacity for base metals, including titanium, by +1% each.

In the mid-game, Titanium storage may become capped quickly due to high rates of trade, requiring players to continuously build more storage structures and trade with Dragons to convert excess Titanium into Uranium.

item.title: Uranium
item.description:
Uranium is a critical, late-game resource primarily used for nuclear power, advanced material refinement, and storage enhancement in Kittens Game.

Here is a comprehensive breakdown of its acquisition, storage, and uses:

Acquisition and Production

Uranium is an uncommon resource that can be acquired through three main methods, with one being an advanced crafting method and the others relying on trade and late-game buildings:

  1. Trade (Primary Source): Uranium can be bought from the Dragons in exchange for Titanium [1, 2]. Dragons will sell 1 Uranium with a 95% chance of success. The required technology to unlock the Dragons is Nuclear Fission [3, 4].
  2. Refinement: Uranium can be refined from Titanium using the Accelerator building.
    • One Accelerator produces $0.0025$ Uranium per tick (or $0.0125$ per second) but consumes $0.015$ Titanium per tick [5, 6].
    • In comparison, a Lunar Outpost consumes Uranium 140 times faster than a single Accelerator produces it, highlighting the importance of multiple accelerators or trade [6, 7].
  3. Quarry Upgrade: After researching Orbital Geodesy (unlocked by Satellites technology), Quarries will produce a small amount of Uranium at a rate of $0.0005$ per tick [5, 8]. This rate is boosted by the Enriched Uranium workshop upgrade (+25%) [5, 9].
  4. Space Production: Uranium is produced by Planet Crackers [1, 10]. Production from Planet Crackers is affected by the Dune cycle (-10% effect without Numerology, +10% effect with Numerology) [11].

Uses and Upgrades

Uranium is essential for progressing into the space and atomic eras of the game:
item.content:encoded:
Uranium is a critical, late-game resource primarily used for nuclear power, advanced material refinement, and storage enhancement in Kittens Game.

Here is a comprehensive breakdown of its acquisition, storage, and uses:

Acquisition and Production

Uranium is an uncommon resource that can be acquired through three main methods, with one being an advanced crafting method and the others relying on trade and late-game buildings:

  1. Trade (Primary Source): Uranium can be bought from the Dragons in exchange for Titanium [1, 2]. Dragons will sell 1 Uranium with a 95% chance of success. The required technology to unlock the Dragons is Nuclear Fission [3, 4].
  2. Refinement: Uranium can be refined from Titanium using the Accelerator building.
    • One Accelerator produces $0.0025$ Uranium per tick (or $0.0125$ per second) but consumes $0.015$ Titanium per tick [5, 6].
    • In comparison, a Lunar Outpost consumes Uranium 140 times faster than a single Accelerator produces it, highlighting the importance of multiple accelerators or trade [6, 7].
  3. Quarry Upgrade: After researching Orbital Geodesy (unlocked by Satellites technology), Quarries will produce a small amount of Uranium at a rate of $0.0005$ per tick [5, 8]. This rate is boosted by the Enriched Uranium workshop upgrade (+25%) [5, 9].
  4. Space Production: Uranium is produced by Planet Crackers [1, 10]. Production from Planet Crackers is affected by the Dune cycle (-10% effect without Numerology, +10% effect with Numerology) [11].

Uses and Upgrades

Uranium is essential for progressing into the space and atomic eras of the game:

  • Refining Unobtainium: Uranium is refined into Unobtainium by a Lunar Outpost [1, 6]. This is a critical step for unlocking Metaphysics [6, 12].
  • Fueling Reactors: Uranium is consumed by the Reactor building at a rate of $0.001$ per tick to generate energy [13]. The Enriched Uranium upgrade reduces this consumption by 25% [9, 13].
  • Refining Thorium: Uranium is used to craft Thorium at a rate of 250 Uranium per unit of Thorium [14]. This is unlocked by the Thorium science [15].
  • Advanced Buildings: Uranium is a cost component for several advanced buildings, including the Accelerator (25 Uranium) [5] and the Reactor (25 Blueprints, 50 Concrete, 5,000 Plate, and 3,500 Titanium) [13].
  • Workshop Upgrades: Uranium is required for several high-tier upgrades, such as:
    • Energy Rifts (from Accelerators) [16].
    • Stasis Chambers [16].
    • Void Energy [16].
    • Nuclear Plants [8].
    • Augmentations [9].

Storage Capacity

The default maximum storage capacity for Uranium is 250 [17].

  • This capacity is mainly increased by building Reactors, as each Reactor increases the maximum Uranium storage by +250 [13].
  • The Accelerator building is also a key component for storage upgrades, as Accelerators, with the Energy Rifts upgrade, provide substantial storage capacity for common resources, including Uranium [16].

Uranium represents a bottleneck resource in the mid-to-late game [18]. Its acquisition and refinement pathway is critical because Unobtainium, the resource it creates, is necessary to unlock the powerful and permanent upgrades found in the Metaphysics system [6, 19].

What Produces Uranium

Uranium, a critical resource in the later stages of the game, is primarily acquired through three methods: trading with the Dragons, production via upgraded Quarries, and refinement using Accelerators.

Here is a breakdown of what produces or provides Uranium:

1. Production via Buildings and Upgrades

Uranium can be produced directly using advanced buildings and upgrades:

  • Quarry (with Orbital Geodesy): Quarries will provide a small amount of uranium once the Orbital Geodesy upgrade is purchased [1, 2]. Quarries produce uranium at a rate of 0.0005 per tick.
    • Orbital Geodesy requires Satellites technology and costs 150,000 Science, 1,000 Alloy, and 35,000 Oil.
  • Accelerator: This building refines titanium into uranium. Accelerators produce 0.0025 uranium per tick (or 0.0125 per second) [3, 4].
    • The Accelerator building is unlocked by researching the Particle Physics science [3, 5]. It costs 7,500 Titanium, 125 Concrete, and 25 Uranium.
  • Planet Cracker: Uranium is produced by the Planet Cracker structure [1, 6]. This structure’s output is affected by the Dune cycle, which can increase its uranium output by +10% [7].
  • Reactor (Consumption Reduction): While Reactors consume Uranium [8], the Enriched Uranium upgrade reduces this consumption by 25% and also provides a +25% uranium production bonus that applies only to Quarries [9].

2. Acquisition via Trade

The most straightforward way to initially acquire Uranium is through trade:

  • Dragons: Uranium can be bought from the Dragons civilization, in exchange for Titanium.
    • Dragons sell 1 Uranium and the trade has a 95% chance of success (reaching 100% chance with 6 Embassy levels) [10, 11].
    • Dragons are unlocked after researching Nuclear Fission [12].

3. Production Boosts

Uranium production can be boosted by:

  • Cycles (Dune): The Dune cycle doubles Uranium income when the Numerology metaphysics upgrade is researched [7].
  • Enriched Uranium: This Workshop upgrade increases Uranium production by +25% (but only applies to Quarries) [9].
  • Planet Busters: This upgrade doubles the output of the Planet Cracker structure [13].

Uranium is an important resource, particularly in the later stages of the game, as it is needed to refine Unobtainium via a Lunar Outpost [1, 4].

item.title: Workshop
item.description:
The Workshop is a fundamental game interface tab that becomes available fairly early in the game and serves two crucial, interconnected functions: purchasing Upgrades and Crafting resources.

1. Unlocks and Access

  • Technology Prerequisite: The Workshop building itself is unlocked by researching the Mining technology.
  • Construction: The Workshop building costs 100 Wood and 400 Minerals.
  • Base Effect: Each Workshop built provides a base +6% bonus to Crafting efficiency.
  • Timing: Players receive the option to create Workshops shortly after unlocking Lumber Mills, Mines, and Amphitheatres.

2. Primary Functions of the Workshop Tab

The Workshop tab contains three main sections:
item.content:encoded:
The Workshop is a fundamental game interface tab that becomes available fairly early in the game and serves two crucial, interconnected functions: purchasing Upgrades and Crafting resources.

1. Unlocks and Access

  • Technology Prerequisite: The Workshop building itself is unlocked by researching the Mining technology.
  • Construction: The Workshop building costs 100 Wood and 400 Minerals.
  • Base Effect: Each Workshop built provides a base +6% bonus to Crafting efficiency.
  • Timing: Players receive the option to create Workshops shortly after unlocking Lumber Mills, Mines, and Amphitheatres.

2. Primary Functions of the Workshop Tab

The Workshop tab contains three main sections:

A. Upgrades

This section allows players to purchase upgrades that are essential for improving overall village productivity, resource efficiency, and kitten functionality.

  • Purpose: Upgrades generally improve the efficiency of buildings or workers, which is highly beneficial in the long run.
  • Examples: Upgrades unlocked here include Reinforced Saw (Lumber Mill efficiency), Gold Ore (Smelters produce gold), Composite Bow (Hunter catpower boost), and Caravanserai (Trade relations boost).

B. Crafting

This section allows for the creation of composite materials necessary for advanced buildings and subsequent technological progression.

  • Purpose: Crafted items are generally composite parts for buildings, and advanced structures require a fair amount of crafting to complete.
  • Craftable Resources: The Workshop is used to convert basic resources into crucial craftable resources like Beam, Slab, Plate, Steel, and later, Manuscript, Compendium, and Blueprint.
  • Exchange: The Workshop also allows you to exchange Catnip directly for basic resources.
  • Automation: The Engineer job, enabled by Mechanization technology, allows kittens to automate crafting within the Workshop.

C. Zebra Upgrades

This section houses upgrades that become available once the Zebra Workshop building is constructed.

3. Strategic Importance of the Workshop

  • Resource Management: The Workshop allows for quick/mass purchases of any items you have crafted at least once.
  • Bottleneck Breaking: Upgrades unlocked via the Workshop are vital for efficiency. For example, some useful early upgrades require Iron, and expert advice recommends pushing to get a Workshop early to acquire these initial economic boosts.
  • Blueprint Conversion: The Workshop is where advanced science resources are created, such as Blueprints (crafted from Compendiums), which are required for late-game technology and structures like Steamworks.
  • Crafting Ratio: The crafting bonus provided by the Workshop can be further enhanced by other buildings, such as the Factory, which provides an additional crafting bonus. The Full Industrialization policy also slightly improves the crafting bonus each factory provides.

The Workshop is the central hub for optimizing and processing resources, moving your civilization past the initial gathering phase and into complex industrialization.

item.title: Time Crystals
item.description:
Time Crystals (TC) are a crucial, uncommon resource that marks the transition into the late-game phase, often referred to as Phase 2 or the Unicorn/Time Crystal Era. They are primarily used for time manipulation, unlocking advanced physics and void technologies, and are the precursor to Relics.

Acquisition and Generation

Time Crystals cannot be produced by standard buildings or jobs; they must be acquired through specific late-game conversions and trade:

  1. Sacrificing Alicorns: You receive 1 Time Crystal by sacrificing 25 Alicorns [3, 4]. This conversion ratio is improved by Unicorn Utopia (+5%) and Sunspire (+10%) .
  2. Trading with Leviathans: Leviathans sell Time Crystals (minimum amount 0.25) with a 98% chance of success . They require 5,000 Unobtainium in exchange [6]. The amount received per trade is increased by the Leviathan’s energy level (which is maintained by feeding them Necrocorns) and by the number of Tradeposts you have .
  3. Shatter Engine: In the late game, Time Crystals can become self-sustaining through the Type 2 Relic Engine (Shatter Engine). This involves purchasing Resource Retrieval upgrades (unlocked by Paradox Theory) high enough that shattering a Time Crystal yields enough Unobtainium and Alicorns to Civilisations/sacrifice for more Time Crystals [9-11].

Primary Uses

Time Crystals are essential for advanced technological and religious progression, especially concerning time mechanics and void resources:
item.content:encoded:
Time Crystals (TC) are a crucial, uncommon resource that marks the transition into the late-game phase, often referred to as Phase 2 or the Unicorn/Time Crystal Era. They are primarily used for time manipulation, unlocking advanced physics and void technologies, and are the precursor to Relics.

Acquisition and Generation

Time Crystals cannot be produced by standard buildings or jobs; they must be acquired through specific late-game conversions and trade:

  1. Sacrificing Alicorns: You receive 1 Time Crystal by sacrificing 25 Alicorns [3, 4]. This conversion ratio is improved by Unicorn Utopia (+5%) and Sunspire (+10%) .
  2. Trading with Leviathans: Leviathans sell Time Crystals (minimum amount 0.25) with a 98% chance of success . They require 5,000 Unobtainium in exchange [6]. The amount received per trade is increased by the Leviathan’s energy level (which is maintained by feeding them Necrocorns) and by the number of Tradeposts you have .
  3. Shatter Engine: In the late game, Time Crystals can become self-sustaining through the Type 2 Relic Engine (Shatter Engine). This involves purchasing Resource Retrieval upgrades (unlocked by Paradox Theory) high enough that shattering a Time Crystal yields enough Unobtainium and Alicorns to Civilisations/sacrifice for more Time Crystals [9-11].

Primary Uses

Time Crystals are essential for advanced technological and religious progression, especially concerning time mechanics and void resources:

  • Refining into Relics: 25 Time Crystals can be refined into 1 Relic . Relics are necessary for buying Cryptotheology buildings like the Black Obelisk and Black Nexus .
  • Time and Void Science: TCs are prerequisites for key late-game technologies:
    • Chronophysics: Costs 5 Time Crystals.
    • Tachyon Theory: Costs 25 Time Crystals and 1 Relic.
    • Void Space: Costs 30 Time Crystals and 100 Void.
    • Paradox Theory: Costs 40 Time Crystals and 250 Void.
  • Time Manipulation and Antimatter: Time Crystals are integral to the Chronoforge system (unlocked by Tachyon Theory).
    • They are combusted in the Chrono Furnace to advance the year. Shattering TCs is done to skip time, triggering Antimatter gain from Sunlifters faster.
    • Shattering TCs is also required to reach the goal of the 1000 Years Challenge.
  • Advanced Structures and Upgrades: TCs are components for various high-tier structures and workshop upgrades:
    • Chronosphere: Costs 1 Time Crystal, among other resources, and is a prerequisite for generating Void and Temporal Flux [14, 21].
    • Flux Condensator: Requires 5 Time Crystals and is crucial for preserving a fraction of crafted resources across resets via Chronospheres.
    • Stasis Chambers (1 TC) and Void Energy (2 TCs) are upgrades for Accelerators.
  • Zebra Crafting: Time Crystals are also needed to craft Bloodstone (5K TCs and 10K Relics), which is used to craft T-Mythril.

Strategic Significance

Time Crystals play a unique role in game persistence and efficiency:

  • Reset Retention: The Metaphysics upgrade Anachronomancy (Cost: 125 Paragon) ensures that Time Crystals and the Chronophysics technology are saved across resets. This capability is critical for accelerating future runs. quick paragon farming runs
  • Engine Goal: Due to their importance in resets and late-game systems (Relics/Void), players aim to build up a large stockpile (20-30K TCs) to acquire upgrades like Resource Retrieval immediately after a reset, eliminating the slow initial grind for them.
  • Challenging Use: The 1000 Years Challenge is unlocked by shattering a Time Crystal and requires constant shattering (and associated TC costs) to advance the game’s calendar to Year 1000.

Time Crystals act as the key to temporal mechanics in Kittens Game. If Unobtainium is the material that unlocks space, Time Crystals are the resource that unlocks control over the flow of time itself, allowing kittens to either speed up their civilization or carry advantages across dimensional resets.

item.title: Relic
item.description:
Relics are an uncommon resource used exclusively in the late and end phases of Kittens Game. They are central to unlocking the highest tiers of religious upgrades and advancing the time manipulation and antimatter systems.

The phase of the game focused on acquiring relics is often referred to as the Mid Game.

Here is a detailed breakdown of how Relics are acquired and what they are used for:

Acquisition

Relics are not produced by buildings or jobs but must be acquired through late-game conversion, trade, or specialized structures:
item.content:encoded:
Relics are an uncommon resource used exclusively in the late and end phases of Kittens Game. They are central to unlocking the highest tiers of religious upgrades and advancing the time manipulation and antimatter systems.

The phase of the game focused on acquiring relics is often referred to as the Mid Game.

Here is a detailed breakdown of how Relics are acquired and what they are used for:

Acquisition

Relics are not produced by buildings or jobs but must be acquired through late-game conversion, trade, or specialized structures:

  1. Refining Time Crystals (Crafting): You can refine 25 Time Crystals to receive 1 Relic. This action requires having at least 25 Time Crystals.
  2. Trade (Leviathans): Relics can be bought from the Leviathans. Leviathans buy 5,000 Unobtainium and sell 1 Relic with a 5% chance of success. Leviathans are unlocked after building a Black Pyramid.
  3. Relic Station (Production): The Relic Station building (unlocked by the Cryptotheology science and purchased with 5,000 Antimatter and 100 Eludium) generates $0.01$ relic per day. Relic production from the Relic Station scales based on Antimatter storage, meaning production is reduced proportionally if maximum Antimatter storage is less than 5,000.
  4. Black Nexus Boost: The production from Space Beacons upgraded with Relic Station is improved by the Black Nexus Cryptotheology upgrade, which produces $0.01* (1 + (Black Pyramid * Black Nexus/10))$ relics per day.

Primary Uses and Upgrades

Relics are the required resource for purchasing most buildings and upgrades within the Cryptotheology system, which unlocks advanced mechanics and bonuses:

  • Technology Advancement: Relics are necessary for key high-tier sciences:
    • Tachyon Theory: Costs 1 Relic and 750K Science .
    • Cryptotheology: Costs 5 Relics and 650K Science.
    • Antimatter: Costs 1 Relic and 500K Science.
    • Terraformation: Costs 5 Relics and 750K Science.
    • Quantum Cryptography: Costs 1024 Relics and 1.25M Science.
  • Cryptotheology Buildings: Relics are spent to purchase permanent prestige buildings:
    • Black Obelisk: Costs 100 Relics.
    • Black Nexus: Costs 5,000 Relics.
    • Blazar: Costs 50,000 Relics and is required to reach Transcendence Tier 15.
    • Event Horizon: Costs 25,000 Relics and increases global resource storage ratio by 10%.
    • Holy Genocide: Costs 100,000 Relics and unlocks the Post Apocalypse challenge.
  • Chronoforge: Relics are a cost component for the Chronoforge upgrade (5 Relics), which is necessary for time manipulation features and the Shatter Engine.
  • Pacts: Pacts are purchased for 100 Relics each.

Strategic Role (Relic Engines)

Obtaining Relics is the primary focus of the mid-game. Players develop specialized strategies, or “engines,” to increase relic flow:

  1. Type 0 Engine (Leviathan Trade): Relies on trading 5,000 Unobtainium to Leviathans for relics. This can be optimized by using the Chronoforge to skip non-Redmoon cycles (which boost Unobtainium production) .
  2. Type 1 Engine (Relic Stations): Involves mass-producing Space Beacons and the Relic Station upgrade, enhancing production with Black Nexus and AI Cores.
  3. Type 2 Engine (Shatter Engine): Requires investing vast amounts of Time Crystals into Resource Retrieval to reach a point where shattering a single Time Crystal yields enough Unobtainium to immediately trade with Leviathans for multiple new Time Crystals, allowing for rapid Time Crystal refinement into Relics.

Relics are the final currency gate before the ultimate goal of maximizing Antimatter and Void resources to prepare for the End Game push for Infinity.

item.title: Autocracy
item.description:
Autocracy is a policy available in the Government category within the Kittens Game policy system. It is a Tier 2 Government policy, following the choice of either Liberty or Tradition.

Here is a detailed breakdown of the Autocracy policy:

Overview and Cost

  • Cost: Autocracy costs 1500 Culture.
  • Prerequisites: Requires researching Writing and having previously chosen either Liberty or Tradition.
  • Locks: Choosing Autocracy locks out both the Monarchy and Republic Policy/.
  • Description: It is considered the “Best for societies with highly promoted kittens”.

Effects of Autocracy

The Autocracy policy provides two distinct benefits focused on leveraging a highly promoted leader and conversion production:
item.content:encoded:
Autocracy is a policy available in the Government category within the Kittens Game policy system. It is a Tier 2 Government policy, following the choice of either Liberty or Tradition.

Here is a detailed breakdown of the Autocracy policy:

Overview and Cost

  • Cost: Autocracy costs 1500 Culture.
  • Prerequisites: Requires researching Writing and having previously chosen either Liberty or Tradition.
  • Locks: Choosing Autocracy locks out both the Monarchy and Republic Policy/.
  • Description: It is considered the “Best for societies with highly promoted kittens”.

Effects of Autocracy

The Autocracy policy provides two distinct benefits focused on leveraging a highly promoted leader and conversion production:

  1. Leader Production Bonus: The leader’s production bonus is multiplied by 2 (x2).
  2. Conversion Production Bonus: The leader increases conversion production based on the number of uncapped housing buildings. This bonus amounts to 0.4% per leader rank per uncapped population building applied to all conversion production during the Cath cycle.

Conversion production specifically includes resources produced by Smelters, Calciners, and Accelerators.

Uncapped population buildings refers to housing structures (Huts, Log Houses, Mansions) for which you have sufficient storage capacity to build more, but have chosen not to.

Strategic Context and Policy Path

Autocracy is part of a crucial path that dictates subsequent Government policy options:

  • Policy Path: Autocracy allows access to Socialism (which currently has no effect) and subsequently Communism or Fascism. This progression requires building a Factory.
  • Endgame Strategy (Iron Will): For self-imposed restriction runs, such as the Iron Will 40K run, one suggested policy path is Tradition $\to$ Autocracy $\to$ Communism. This specific path is chosen because Communism provides better Time Crystal results.
  • General Assessment: While the doubling of the leader’s effect is considered amazing for Monarchy (which follows Tradition) due to multiplying the leader’s trait bonus, Autocracy’s base doubling of the leader’s production bonus and its conversion production boost are generally considered minor when compared to Monarchy’s flexibility and scaling potential through traits. Autocracy and Republic grant “tiny bonuses that are dwarfed by pretty much everything else”.

If you were seeking maximum immediate leverage from your leader, Monarchy is generally recommended. However, Autocracy offers a specific advantage for players focused on highly promoted kittens and boosting resource conversion structures like Smelters, Calciners, and Accelerators, particularly during the Cath cycle.

item.title: Clear Cutting
item.description:
The policy Clear Cutting is a foundational option in the Environment policy group, unlocked once your civilization has researched Engineering.

This policy is generally recommended by experienced players due to the large production boost it provides to a critical early/mid-game resource: wood.

Here is a detailed breakdown of the Clear Cutting policy:

Policy Details and Effects

Clear Cutting is described as an effort to totally destroy the forest to improve wood production.
item.content:encoded:
The policy Clear Cutting is a foundational option in the Environment policy group, unlocked once your civilization has researched Engineering.

This policy is generally recommended by experienced players due to the large production boost it provides to a critical early/mid-game resource: wood.

Here is a detailed breakdown of the Clear Cutting policy:

Policy Details and Effects

Clear Cutting is described as an effort to totally destroy the forest to improve wood production.

  • Cost: The policy requires 2000 Science.
  • Primary Effect (Standard Game): It grants a substantial +30% wood production bonus.
  • Drawbacks: This focus on aggressive resource extraction comes at the cost of environmental health and happiness:
    • -2% happiness.
    • +5% pollution.
  • Iron Will Effect: In the challenging Iron Will mode, Clear Cutting provides a +10% bonus to catnip refinement, which is similar to the effect of one un-upgraded Lumber Mill.

Strategic Importance

Clear Cutting is considered a crucial early policy because wood is necessary for major construction goals in the mid-game, validating the policy’s drawbacks.

  • Mid-Game Progression: The increased wood production is “a huge help” for gathering the resources necessary to build subsequent critical structures like observatories, harbours, and ships.
  • Comparison to Alternatives: Experts advise choosing Clear Cutting over its initial rivals in the Environment tree:
    • Strip Mining: This policy boosts mineral production, but minerals are generally easier to acquire than wood during this phase.
    • Environmentalism: This policy is considered “pretty weak” and doesn’t offer much practical benefit, especially compared to the production boost from Clear Cutting.
  • Mitigation and Upgrades: The negative happiness penalty associated with Clear Cutting (and Strip Mining) can be removed later by adopting the Sustainability policy. Additionally, choosing Clear Cutting keeps the path open for the later policy Full Industrialization, which boosts factory effectiveness, crucial for deep mid-game scaling.

In essence, Clear Cutting is a policy choice that prioritizes aggressive short-term resource growth (wood) over early happiness and pollution control, leveraging that wood to quickly build the structures needed for navigating the next phase of the game.

item.title: Communism
item.description:
The policy Communism is an advanced Government policy choice in Kittens Game, aimed at accelerating industrial output at the expense of environmental stability.

Here is a detailed breakdown of the policy:

Policy Mechanics

  • Cost: Communism costs 15,000 Culture.
  • Description: It is described as supporting “Industrialization at all costs”.
  • Prerequisites: You must have researched the initial government policy path and built a Factory. Communism is available if you previously chose Autocracy or Republic.
  • Locks: Choosing Communism prevents you from selecting Liberalism or Fascism.

Effects and Drawbacks

Communism provides powerful industrial bonuses but carries a severe risk related to food production:
item.content:encoded:
The policy Communism is an advanced Government policy choice in Kittens Game, aimed at accelerating industrial output at the expense of environmental stability.

Here is a detailed breakdown of the policy:

Policy Mechanics

  • Cost: Communism costs 15,000 Culture.
  • Description: It is described as supporting “Industrialization at all costs”.
  • Prerequisites: You must have researched the initial government policy path and built a Factory. Communism is available if you previously chose Autocracy or Republic.
  • Locks: Choosing Communism prevents you from selecting Liberalism or Fascism.

Effects and Drawbacks

Communism provides powerful industrial bonuses but carries a severe risk related to food production:

Type Effect Details
Production Boost +25% iron, coal, and titanium production This provides a significant boost to key industrial and late-game resources.
Cost Reduction Factories are 30% cheaper This makes scaling industrial capacity less expensive.
Major Drawback Catnip field production becomes -100% in cold winters This severely impacts food security during the harshest season.

Strategic Context

In the mid-to-late game, the choice between Liberalism, Fascism, and Communism depends on the player’s immediate needs:

  • Industry Boost: If zebra hostility has been negated already, players are advised to pick Communism to boost your industry.
  • Time Crystal Production: In extreme long-term runs, such as the Iron Will 40K challenge, experts suggest aiming for the policy path Tradition $\to$ Autocracy $\to$ Communism, specifically noting that Communism will give you better time crystal results compared to Liberalism.
  • Alternatives: If the player is struggling with zebra hostility (which inhibits acquiring necessary titanium), Liberalism might be preferred. In a first run, Fascism might be chosen temporarily, as it makes log cabins 50% cheaper and helps the player reach the target of 130+ kittens before the first reset.

item.title: Conservation
item.description:
Conservation is a mid-to-late-game policy available in Kittens Game, focusing on environmental preservation.

Here is a breakdown of the Conservation policy, its effects, prerequisites, and strategic evaluation:

Policy Details and Effects

  • Cost: Conservation costs 10,000 Culture.
  • Description: This policy represents actively protecting the environment, building upon earlier environmental efforts.
  • Effects: Conservation provides bonuses primarily related to happiness and pollution control:
    • +5% happiness.
    • -5% pollution.

Prerequisites

Conservation is located deep within the Environment policy tree and requires specific research and an initial policy choice:
item.content:encoded:
Conservation is a mid-to-late-game policy available in Kittens Game, focusing on environmental preservation.

Here is a breakdown of the Conservation policy, its effects, prerequisites, and strategic evaluation:

Policy Details and Effects

  • Cost: Conservation costs 10,000 Culture.
  • Description: This policy represents actively protecting the environment, building upon earlier environmental efforts.
  • Effects: Conservation provides bonuses primarily related to happiness and pollution control:
    • +5% happiness.
    • -5% pollution.

Prerequisites

Conservation is located deep within the Environment policy tree and requires specific research and an initial policy choice:

  1. Technology: It requires Ecology to be researched.
  2. Parent Policy: It is unlocked by choosing the Environmentalism policy earlier in the game.
  3. Locks: Conservation locks the subsequent choice of Open Woodlands.

Strategic Context and Evaluation

Policy/ in the Environment category often present a choice between immediate resource maximization (like wood or minerals) and environmental moderation (like pollution control).

  • Weak Utility: Conservation is generally considered “pretty weak and doesn’t do much for you”. While it offers increased happiness and reduced pollution, it lacks the raw resource boost offered by its alternatives.
  • Alternative Choice: Conservation is frequently compared unfavorably to Open Woodlands, which follows the same Environmentalism path. Open Woodlands provides a substantial production boost of +12.5% wood and mineral production (but adds +5% pollution). Expert advice usually recommends Open Woodlands because production bonuses are crucial for progression.
  • Pollution Management: The small reduction in pollution from Conservation may not be sufficient to negate the pollution generated by industrial buildings like Mines, Smelters, and Factories, which negatively impacts catnip production, happiness, and kitten arrival speed. Players are generally advised that some pollution will occur regardless of the environmental Policy/ chosen.

item.title: Environmentalism
item.description:
The term Environmentalism refers to a specific policy available to your kitten society, categorized under the Environment section of the policy system. This policy category is unlocked after researching Engineering.

Here is a detailed breakdown of the Environmentalism policy:

Effects and Cost

  • Cost: Environmentalism costs 2000 Culture.
  • Description: The policy is focused on preserving the natural beauty of your village.
  • Effects: Environmentalism provides a slight boost to kitten happiness and a small reduction in pollution:
    • +3% happiness.
    • -5% pollution.

Policy Context and Strategy

Environmentalism is one of three initial options within the Environment policy group, and selecting it dictates the future path of subsequent environmental Policy/.
item.content:encoded:
The term Environmentalism refers to a specific policy available to your kitten society, categorized under the Environment section of the policy system. This policy category is unlocked after researching Engineering.

Here is a detailed breakdown of the Environmentalism policy:

Effects and Cost

  • Cost: Environmentalism costs 2000 Culture.
  • Description: The policy is focused on preserving the natural beauty of your village.
  • Effects: Environmentalism provides a slight boost to kitten happiness and a small reduction in pollution:
    • +3% happiness.
    • -5% pollution.

Policy Context and Strategy

Environmentalism is one of three initial options within the Environment policy group, and selecting it dictates the future path of subsequent environmental Policy/.

  1. Policy Group: Environmentalism is available alongside Strip Mining (which increases mineral production and pollution) and Clear Cutting (which increases wood production and pollution).
  2. Prerequisite: Engineering.
  3. Subsequent Policy/: Choosing Environmentalism unlocks the Conservation and Open Woodlands Policy/ later in the game.

Strategic Evaluation

Guidance from experts in the sources suggests that Environmentalism is generally the least favourable choice among the initial environmental Policy/:

  • Weak Effect: Environmentalism is considered “pretty weak and doesn’t do much for you”. The reduction in pollution is generally slight.
  • Recommended Alternative: Clear Cutting is usually recommended instead, as the substantial boost to wood production is crucial for constructing observatories, harbours, and trade ships later in the game.
  • Pollution Mitigation: While pollution is a concern (negatively affecting catnip production, happiness, and kitten arrival speed), the effect of Environmentalism is often insufficient to fully mitigate it. Most players must accept that some pollution will happen.

Later Policy/ that stem from Environmentalism, like Conservation, can increase happiness further (+5% happiness, -5% pollution), while Open Woodlands offers production bonuses (+12.5% wood and mineral production, +5% pollution).

In summary, Environmentalism is an early-game policy focused on minor happiness and pollution control, but its immediate resource gain is generally inferior to the resource-boosting options like Clear Cutting or Strip Mining.

item.title: Frugality
item.description:
The term “Frugality” refers to a specific policy available to your kittens’ civilization within Kittens Game.

Here is a comprehensive breakdown of the Frugality policy:

Overview and Prerequisite

  • Cost: Frugality costs 3500 Culture.
  • Prerequisite: The Frugality policy is unlocked only after first choosing Stoicism. Stoicism, in turn, is a policy in the Philosophy category, which requires researching Philosophy.
  • Context: Frugality is an option that appears as part of the philosophical policy tree, contrasted with Rationing.

Effects of Frugality

The Frugality policy focuses on optimizing output from economic buildings by reducing perceived corruption.
item.content:encoded:
The term “Frugality” refers to a specific policy available to your kittens’ civilization within Kittens Game.

Here is a comprehensive breakdown of the Frugality policy:

Overview and Prerequisite

  • Cost: Frugality costs 3500 Culture.
  • Prerequisite: The Frugality policy is unlocked only after first choosing Stoicism. Stoicism, in turn, is a policy in the Philosophy category, which requires researching Philosophy.
  • Context: Frugality is an option that appears as part of the philosophical policy tree, contrasted with Rationing.

Effects of Frugality

The Frugality policy focuses on optimizing output from economic buildings by reducing perceived corruption.

  • Effect: Stoic philosophers placed in charge of the mints make them more effective by reducing corruption. Consequently, Mints produce 10% more resources.

Strategic Considerations

Frugality is typically considered as an alternative choice when dealing with luxury resource consumption and happiness management:

  • Policy Path: Frugality follows the Stoicism path, which is centered on enduring hardship and reducing luxury consumption.
  • Alternative: Frugality is paired against the Rationing policy. Rationing, also following Stoicism, makes hunting more effective (+0.1 Hunting bonus) and reduces the catnip consumption increase per happiness by 10%.
  • Expert Opinion: Strategic advice suggests that Frugality might be chosen if consumption mitigation (provided by Stoicism or Rationing) is still insufficient, or if the increased output from Mints is desired, though one source notes, “…maybe the increased output from mints with Frugality… but probably not…”.

In essence, Frugality is a philosophical policy intended to boost the output of specialized financial/luxury-resource structures (Mints) after prioritizing austerity (Stoicism).

item.title: Tradition
item.description:
Tradition is an early-game policy available in the Government category of the policy system, which helps accelerate the production and effectiveness of cultural resources, especially manuscripts.

Here is a detailed breakdown of the Tradition policy:

Overview and Effects

  • Cost: Tradition costs 150 Culture.
  • Description: It is considered a policy “good for small culture oriented societies”.
  • Prerequisite: It is unlocked after researching Writing.
  • Locks: Selecting Tradition locks out the Liberty policy.
  • Effects: Tradition provides two key benefits focused on manuscripts:
    1. Cost Reduction: It reduces the manuscript cost by $-100$ culture and $-5$ parchment.
    2. Capacity Boost: It grants a doubled manuscript maximum culture effect.

Strategic Context

Tradition is highly relevant in the early-to-mid game as players struggle to overcome the manuscript grind, which is necessary for advancing the science tree (leading toward Theology and Astronomy).
