Here is a detailed breakdown of the Tradition policy:

Overview and Effects

  • Cost: Tradition costs 150 Culture.
  • Description: It is considered a policy “good for small culture oriented societies”.
  • Prerequisite: It is unlocked after researching Writing.
  • Locks: Selecting Tradition locks out the Liberty policy.
  • Effects: Tradition provides two key benefits focused on manuscripts:
    1. Cost Reduction: It reduces the manuscript cost by $-100$ culture and $-5$ parchment.
    2. Capacity Boost: It grants a doubled manuscript maximum culture effect.

Strategic Context

Tradition is highly relevant in the early-to-mid game as players struggle to overcome the manuscript grind, which is necessary for advancing the science tree (leading toward Theology and Astronomy).

  • Preference over Liberty: Strategic advice generally recommends choosing Tradition all the way over its alternative, Liberty. This is because the core objective at this stage is to produce lots of manuscripts cheaply to unlock essential science, and Tradition directly supports this goal. The Liberty policy is sometimes deemed a “noob trap”.
  • Scientific Velocity: By accelerating cultural resource generation, Tradition directly expedites the scientific path towards advanced technologies like Theology and Astronomy.
  • First Run Nuance: Although Tradition is generally preferred, experts note that in very early runs, a player might consider choosing Liberty to help offset the large production hit caused by unhappiness. However, once a player has accumulated sufficient Karma from resets (which increases overall happiness), it is advisable to switch to the Tradition policy.
  • Subsequent Policy Path: Choosing Tradition allows progression toward Autocracy or Monarchy. The path of Tradition $\to$ Autocracy $\to$ Communism is recommended in late-game Iron Will runs for achieving better time crystal results.

item.title: Gold
item.description:
Gold is a strategic metal in Kittens Game primarily used for international trade, religious advancement, and leadership development. It is categorized as a common resource that can be produced through industrial refinement or specialized worker roles.

Production and Acquisition

Gold acquisition shifts from manual hunting in specialized modes to automated industrial production as your village advances:

  • Smelting: Once the Gold Ore workshop upgrade is researched, Smelters begin producing $0.001$ gold per tick ($0.005$ per second) as a byproduct of smelting iron.
  • Geologists: After researching Geodesy, kittens assigned as Geologists can find gold at a rate of $0.0008$ per tick. This rate can be further enhanced by the Mining Drill and Unobtainium Drill upgrades.
  • Hunting (Iron Will): In Iron Will mode, where there are no kittens, hunting has a 25% chance to yield gold once Gold Ore is researched.
  • Trade: While most civilizations require gold from the player to trade, gold can be obtained through specific loops, such as trading with the Nagas for minerals to feed smelters.

Strategic Uses

Gold is a critical bottleneck for mid-game progression due to its diverse applications:
item.content:encoded:
Gold is a strategic metal in Kittens Game primarily used for international trade, religious advancement, and leadership development. It is categorized as a common resource that can be produced through industrial refinement or specialized worker roles.

Production and Acquisition

Gold acquisition shifts from manual hunting in specialized modes to automated industrial production as your village advances:

  • Smelting: Once the Gold Ore workshop upgrade is researched, Smelters begin producing $0.001$ gold per tick ($0.005$ per second) as a byproduct of smelting iron.
  • Geologists: After researching Geodesy, kittens assigned as Geologists can find gold at a rate of $0.0008$ per tick. This rate can be further enhanced by the Mining Drill and Unobtainium Drill upgrades.
  • Hunting (Iron Will): In Iron Will mode, where there are no kittens, hunting has a 25% chance to yield gold once Gold Ore is researched.
  • Trade: While most civilizations require gold from the player to trade, gold can be obtained through specific loops, such as trading with the Nagas for minerals to feed smelters.

Strategic Uses

Gold is a critical bottleneck for mid-game progression due to its diverse applications:

  • Trade: Each trade transaction with civilizations like the Lizards, Sharks, or Zebras typically costs 1 unit of gold.
  • Religion: Gold is a required component for building Temples and purchasing many Order of the Sun upgrades, such as Solar Revolution, Golden Spire, and Sun Altar.
  • Village Infrastructure: It is necessary for constructing Tradeposts (which improve trade and happiness) and Mints (which automate the gathering of furs and ivory).
  • Leadership: Promoting a kitten to a higher rank requires both experience and gold. Higher-ranked leaders provide significant production bonuses, especially if the Monarchy or Republic policies are enacted.

Strategic Gold Cap Benchmarks

Expanding gold storage is critical for scientific and religious progression:

  • Solar Revolution: Requires a gold cap of 500.
  • Apocrypha: Requires a gold cap of 5,000.
  • Transcendence: Requires a gold cap of 7,500.
  • Leadership Promotions: Higher ranks for your kitten leaders require significant gold amounts, ranging from 25 to 200+ gold.

Policies and Efficiency

Several government and foreign policies directly impact your gold economy:

  • Liberalism: This policy is highly valued as it reduces all gold costs by 20% and improves trade relations.
  • Zebra Relations (Appeasement): While this policy improves titanium trade, it imposes a -5% penalty to gold income.
  • Monarchy: This policy doubles the power of your leader’s trait but consumes 10% of your gold production as upkeep for the royal court.

The initial storage limit for Gold is 10 units. This capacity can be increased through the construction of specific storage buildings, as well as production buildings that feature storage benefits, such as the Mint [1, 2].

Here are the ways to increase your maximum Gold storage:

1. Dedicated Buildings and Upgrades

Several buildings directly contribute to your maximum Gold capacity:

  • Mint: The Mint building increases your Max Gold by +100. Mints are unlocked by researching Architecture and are constructed using 5,000 Minerals, 200 Plate, and 500 Gold. Building more Mints is suggested as a method to increase your Gold storage limit.
  • Barn: The Barn, unlocked by Agriculture, provides a base increase of +10 Max Gold [1, 5].
  • Warehouse: The Warehouse, unlocked by Construction, provides a base increase of +5 Max Gold.
  • Harbour: The Harbour, unlocked by Navigation, provides a base increase of +25 Max Gold.
  • Sky Palace: The Sky Palace, a religious building, improves gold storage by +1%.

2. Storage Upgrades

Various Workshop upgrades applied to storage buildings will further increase the Gold capacity of Mints, Warehouses, and Harbours:

  • Reinforced Warehouses: Increases the maximum limit for several resources, including Gold, from Warehouses, Barns, Harbors, and Mints by +25% [7]. This upgrade is unlocked by Steel [7, 8].
  • Titanium Warehouses: Increases Gold capacity from the specified storage buildings by +50% [4, 7].
  • Alloy Warehouses: Increases Gold capacity from the specified storage buildings by +45% [7].
  • Concrete Pillars: Increases Gold capacity from the specified storage buildings by +5% [7].
  • Concrete Warehouses: Increases Gold capacity from the specified storage buildings by +35% [7].
  • Storage Bunkers: Increases Gold capacity from the specified storage buildings by +20%. This upgrade is unlocked by Exogeology [7, 9].

3. Advanced Mechanisms

Late-game advanced production and prestige mechanics also influence Gold capacity:

  • Paragon: High levels of Paragon (gained by resetting with more than 70 kittens) improve resource caps, and this effect on storage never diminishes [10, 11].
  • Accelerator Upgrades: Advanced Accelerator Workshop upgrades, associated with pocket dimensions, also increase the maximum capacity of Gold:
    • Energy Rifts (Requires Dimensional Physics) [12].
    • Stasis Chambers (Requires Chronophysics) increases max Gold from Accelerators by +95% [12].
    • Void Energy (Requires Stasis Chambers) increases max Gold from Accelerators by +75% [12].
    • Dark Energy (Requires Void Energy) increases max Gold from Accelerators by +250% [12].
    • Tachyon Accelerators (Requires Tachyon Theory) increases max Gold from Accelerators by +500% [12].
  • Event Horizon: This Cryptotheology upgrade, available at Transcendence-Tier 7, increases the global resource storage ratio by +10% [13].

Strategic Importance

Increasing Gold storage is necessary because Gold is used extensively:

  • Trading: Gold is required for trading with civilizations [14], and the Isolationism policy reduces the Gold cost per trade by 1 [15].
  • Building: Gold is needed to construct high-tier buildings like Temples [16, 17], Tradeposts [2, 18], and Mints.
  • Upgrades: Gold is a component cost for several religious upgrades, such as Golden Spire, Sun Altar, Stained Glass, Solar Revolution, Basilica, Templars, Apocrypha, and Transcendence [19-22].

In the “Titanium era,” Gold becomes a major bottleneck for trade and building Temples, emphasizing the need to maximize its accumulation and storage [23, 24].

item.title: Plate
item.description:
Plate is a core mid-game resource in Kittens Game that is produced entirely through crafting using Iron as the primary input.

Here is a detailed breakdown of plate production, the required input, and mechanisms for acquisition:

1. Primary Production: Crafting

Plate (specifically Metal Plate) is categorized as a craftable resource.

  • Input Cost: One Metal Plate is crafted in the Workshop by consuming 125 Iron.
  • Purpose: Plate is required for advanced construction in the early and mid-game, particularly for buildings like Harbours.

2. Supporting Iron Production (The Prerequisite)

Since Plate production is capped by your Iron supply, effective production requires robust Iron generation, which is achieved through refining and trade:
item.content:encoded:
Plate is a core mid-game resource in Kittens Game that is produced entirely through crafting using Iron as the primary input.

Here is a detailed breakdown of plate production, the required input, and mechanisms for acquisition:

1. Primary Production: Crafting

Plate (specifically Metal Plate) is categorized as a craftable resource.

  • Input Cost: One Metal Plate is crafted in the Workshop by consuming 125 Iron.
  • Purpose: Plate is required for advanced construction in the early and mid-game, particularly for buildings like Harbours.

2. Supporting Iron Production (The Prerequisite)

Since Plate production is capped by your Iron supply, effective production requires robust Iron generation, which is achieved through refining and trade:

  • Smelters: Iron is refined from wood and minerals using Smelters. Smelters unlock after researching Metal Working.
  • Calciners: Iron can also be refined using Calciners from oil and minerals.
  • Upgrades: Several Workshop upgrades boost Iron production from these buildings:
    • Electrolytic Smelting increases Smelter output of iron (and coal) by +95%.
    • Fluidized Reactors boost Calciner output by +100% more iron.
    • Oxidation increases Calciner iron production by +95%.
    • The Rotary Kiln also provides a +75% increase to Calciner iron output.
  • Policy/: The Communism policy grants a +25% increase to iron production. The Rationality policy grants a +5% iron production bonus.
  • Trade: Iron can be acquired directly by trading with other races. For example, Griffins sell Iron for Wood, and Zebras sell Iron for Slab.

3. Automated Conversion and Trade Acquisition

  • Automation: The Pneumatic Press Workshop upgrade, unlocked via Physics, allows Workshop Automation to automatically convert iron to plates when iron resources are near their capacity limit.
  • Trade Acquisition: Plate can be acquired through trade with Zebras. Zebras sell Plate (2 units per trade, with a 65% chance) in exchange for 50 Slab. Building Embassies increases the chance of receiving plates from Zebras, reaching 100% chance at Embassy level 54.

4. Uses of Plate

Plate is crucial for further expanding infrastructure and developing advanced resources:

  • Storage: Plate is needed to build a Harbour (75 Plate), a storage building essential for increasing capacity for Catnip, Wood, Minerals, and Iron, among others.
  • Culture/Gold: Plate is required for Temples (15 Plate) and Mints (200 Plate). Mints increase gold storage and produce rare resources.
  • High-Tier Structures: Significant amounts of Plate are needed for Reactors (5000 Plate) and Factories (2500 Plate).
  • Late-Game Crafting: Plate is an input for crafting Megaliths (5 Plate).

Plate serves as an early example of vertical production integration in the game, where continuous management of raw resources (Wood, Minerals) is required to ensure a steady supply of an intermediary resource (Iron) which is then crafted into Plate for infrastructure expansion.

item.title: Culture
item.description:
Culture is a special expendable resource in Kittens Game. It is essential for technological progression, particularly during the transition from the early to mid-game phases.

Culture is critical because it is required to craft Manuscripts, which are necessary prerequisites for several key technologies, including Theology and Astronomy.

Production of Culture

Culture is primarily generated by specialized cultural and religious buildings:

  • Amphitheatres: These are unlocked after researching Writing. They generate +0.005 Culture per Tick. Amphitheatres can be upgraded to Broadcast Towers, which significantly increase culture per tick based on your energy surplus.
  • Temples: Unlocked by Philosophy, Temples generate +0.1 Culture per Tick.
  • Chapels: Unlocked by Acoustics, Chapels generate +0.05 Culture per Tick.

Culture production can be further boosted through religious upgrades, Policy/, and game cycles:
item.content:encoded:
Culture is a special expendable resource in Kittens Game. It is essential for technological progression, particularly during the transition from the early to mid-game phases.

Culture is critical because it is required to craft Manuscripts, which are necessary prerequisites for several key technologies, including Theology and Astronomy.

Production of Culture

Culture is primarily generated by specialized cultural and religious buildings:

  • Amphitheatres: These are unlocked after researching Writing. They generate +0.005 Culture per Tick. Amphitheatres can be upgraded to Broadcast Towers, which significantly increase culture per tick based on your energy surplus.
  • Temples: Unlocked by Philosophy, Temples generate +0.1 Culture per Tick.
  • Chapels: Unlocked by Acoustics, Chapels generate +0.05 Culture per Tick.

Culture production can be further boosted through religious upgrades, Policy/, and game cycles:

  • Stained Glass: This upgrade (which costs 500 Faith and 250 Gold, and requires 750 Worship) enhances Temple functionality by increasing their culture output by +0.05 Culture per Tick. This bonus increases by an additional +0.05 for each subsequent level purchased using Transcendence.
  • Basilica: This upgrade, available after accumulating 10,000 Worship, increases Temple culture per tick by +0.2.
  • Mysticism Policy: This policy provides a +5% culture and faith production bonus.
  • Cultural Exchange Policy: This policy grants a +5% culture income bonus.
  • Yarn Cycle: If Numeromancy is researched, holding a festival during the Yarn cycle grants a Culture income x2 bonus.

Like other special resources, Culture production benefits from Paragon and Religion production boosts.

Usage and Progression

Culture is used exclusively in the Workshop tab to craft Manuscripts.

  1. Crafting Manuscripts: To craft one Manuscript, you typically require 25 Parchment and 400 Culture. This cost can be reduced if you adopt the Tradition Policy, which reduces the cost to 20 Parchment and 300 Culture.
  2. Unlocking Advanced Tech: Manuscripts are vital for unlocking mid-game sciences:
    • Theology requires 20,000 Science and 35 Manuscripts.
    • Astronomy requires 28,000 Science and 65 Manuscripts.

The sources highlight that reaching the Theology science is gated by the steep requirement of needing to create Manuscripts using Parchment and Culture, a resource that accumulates slowly at first.

Storage Capacity

Culture is a capped resource, with an initial storage capacity of 100. Expanding this limit is necessary for accumulating enough culture to craft expensive manuscripts.

Maximum Culture capacity is increased by buildings and upgrades:

  • Library: +10 max culture.
  • Academy: +25 max culture.
  • Amphitheatre: +50 max culture.
  • Chapel: +200 max culture.
  • Data Center (Library upgrade): +250 max culture.
  • Basilica (Temple upgrade): +125 max culture to Temples, increasing by +50 per additional level via Transcendence.
  • Ziggurat: +8% max culture.
  • Broadcast Tower (Amphitheatre upgrade): Max Culture + (300 multiplied by the Energy Surplus Ratio).
  • Unicorn Graveyard (Religious building): Increases maximum culture by +1% per Ziggurat.
  • Codex Logos (Metaphysics upgrade): Increases the Manuscript craft multiplier, which grants a minor bonus to maximum culture (with diminishing returns).

Accumulating enough Culture capacity is also necessary to interact with certain trade partners, as the Nagas are unlocked when you reach a 1500 Culture cap.

To progress through the initial difficulty of Culture accumulation, many players focus on building Amphitheatres and Temples and maximize their ability to hunt for Furs (which are refined into Parchment) to ensure they can sustain Manuscript production.

How to increase Culture

1. Primary Production Buildings

The production of Culture is generated by specific structures, which are unlocked as you progress through the Science tree:

Building Prerequisite Technology Culture Per Tick Max Culture Increase
Amphitheatre Writing [5] +0.005 [6] +50 [6]
Chapel Acoustics [7] +0.05 [6] +200 [6]
Temple Philosophy (which unlocks Theology) [4] +0.1 [6] N/A (increases Faith cap instead) [6]

2. Upgraded Production and Efficiency

Culture generation can be significantly boosted by upgrading buildings and purchasing religious and Workshop upgrades:

  • Broadcast Tower (Amphitheatre Upgrade): This is an upgrade available after researching Electronics [8]. A single Broadcast Tower can increase production as much as two hundred times compared to an Amphitheatre [9].
    • It produces Culture per Tick based on the Energy Surplus Ratio [10].
    • The Satellite Radio upgrade further boosts the Broadcast Tower’s culture per tick and max culture by +0.5% per active Satellite [11].
  • Temple Upgrades:
    • Stained Glass (Religion Upgrade): Temples produce an additional +0.05 culture per tick (+0.05 per additional level via Transcendence) [12].
    • Basilica (Religion Upgrade): Temples produce an additional +0.2 culture per tick (+0.05 per additional level via Transcendence) [13].
  • Cycles: If you have researched Numeromancy [14], running a Festival during the Yarn cycle will multiply Culture income by x2 [15].

3. Culture Storage (Max Culture)

The initial default storage capacity for Culture is 100 [16]. This limit can be increased through several means:

Source Max Culture Increase Prerequisite
Amphitheatre +50 [6] Writing [5]
Library +10 [17] N/A
Academy +25 [17] Mathematics [18]
Chapel +200 [6] Acoustics [7]
Ziggurat +8% Max Culture [19] Construction [18]
Manuscripts Provides a minor bonus (subject to diminishing returns) [2]. N/A
Data Center (Library Upgrade) +250 [10]. Electronics [8]
Broadcast Tower (Amphitheatre Upgrade) +($300*$ Energy Surplus Ratio) [10]. Electronics [8]
Basilica (Temple Upgrade) Temples gain +125 max culture (+50 per additional level via Transcendence) [13]. Worship 10K [13]
Policy: City On A Hill +5% culture cap [20]. Isolationism [20]
Data Center/Bio Lab Synergy: Uplink increases the max culture of Data Centers by +1% per Bio Lab [21]. Satellites [21]

4. Production Boosting Policy/

Culture production is also influenced by selecting certain Policy/:

  • Mysticism: Provides a +5% culture and faith production bonus [22].
  • Cultural Exchange: Provides a +5% culture income bonus [23].

5. Culture Consumption (Manuscripts)

Culture is required to craft Manuscripts [1, 2]. Each Manuscript typically requires 400 Culture and 25 Parchment [2].

  • The Tradition policy, available after researching Writing, is recommended for culture-oriented societies as it reduces the Manuscript cost by 100 culture and 5 parchment, and doubles the manuscript’s effect on maximum culture [2, 24, 25].

A key progression bottleneck in the mid-game involves creating Manuscripts, and since Culture accumulates slowly at first [3], you must focus on building Amphitheatres and Temples to increase generation rates [26, 27]. The resource is further affected by Paragon and Religion production boosts [28].

To visualize the early focus on culture production, consider it like building a sustainable theater industry: You start with a few small Amphitheatres (local playhouses), eventually upgrade to Chapels and Temples (larger venues with dedicated staff), and ultimately deploy Broadcast Towers (mass media/streaming services) to dramatically amplify output and r

item.title: Amphitheatre
item.description:
The Amphitheatre is an important early-to-mid-game building in Kittens Game, crucial for managing kitten happiness and initiating Culture production, which is vital for later scientific and religious progression.

Here is a comprehensive breakdown of the Amphitheatre:

Unlocking and Cost

  • Prerequisite Technology: The Amphitheatre is unlocked after researching Writing. Writing costs 3600 Science and is unlocked by Engineering.
  • Resource Cost: Constructing an Amphitheatre requires a mix of common and crafted resources:
    • Wood: 200 units
    • Minerals: 1200 units
    • Parchment: 3 units (Parchment is a craftable resource made from Furs)
  • Price Ratio: The Amphitheatre has a price ratio of 1.15.

Effects and Function

The Amphitheatre serves two critical functions for societal development: culture production and unhappiness mitigation.
item.content:encoded:
The Amphitheatre is an important early-to-mid-game building in Kittens Game, crucial for managing kitten happiness and initiating Culture production, which is vital for later scientific and religious progression.

Here is a comprehensive breakdown of the Amphitheatre:

Unlocking and Cost

  • Prerequisite Technology: The Amphitheatre is unlocked after researching Writing. Writing costs 3600 Science and is unlocked by Engineering.
  • Resource Cost: Constructing an Amphitheatre requires a mix of common and crafted resources:
    • Wood: 200 units
    • Minerals: 1200 units
    • Parchment: 3 units (Parchment is a craftable resource made from Furs)
  • Price Ratio: The Amphitheatre has a price ratio of 1.15.

Effects and Function

The Amphitheatre serves two critical functions for societal development: culture production and unhappiness mitigation.

  • Culture Production: Each Amphitheatre produces +0.005 Culture per Tick. Culture is a special resource necessary to convert Parchment into Manuscripts in the Workshop.
  • Culture Storage: Each Amphitheatre increases the maximum Culture storage capacity by +50.
  • Happiness/Unhappiness: Amphitheatres reduce population penalties to happiness, providing -4.8% Unhappiness mitigation.

Strategic Importance

The decision to build Amphitheatres is a major early-game strategic step, as it addresses a key bottleneck in the technology tree:

  • Culture Grind: Amphitheatres are one of the earliest buildings to generate Culture. Culture is required to craft Manuscripts, which are necessary to research Theology and subsequent high-tier sciences like Astronomy. This resource requirement creates a significant hurdle, forcing players to focus on culture generation.
  • Managing Population Happiness: As your kitten population grows (by building Huts and Log Houses, which you should keep maxed out), they become unhappy. Since Happiness dictates the overall efficiency of your Kittens in their work, Amphitheatres are extremely important in the early game to reduce unhappiness and maintain high production levels.
    • It is advised to build Amphitheatres until they stop noticeably improving Happiness, which can be monitored via the ‘population penalty’ percentage on the top bar of the game.
  • Preparation for Temples: Amphitheatres help make obtaining Temples easier, as Temples are another structure that generates Culture.
  • Building Priority: When happiness starts becoming a serious problem, players should consider pushing for the Writing science to unlock Amphitheatres. You may need to temporarily employ all kittens as Hunters to stockpile the Parchment required to craft them.

Upgrades and Progression

  • Upgrade Path: The Amphitheatre can be upgraded to a Broadcast Tower. This upgrade is unlocked by researching Electronics.
  • Broadcast Tower Conversion: The Broadcast Tower upgrade offers a significant boost to culture production and unhappiness reduction, with a single tower potentially replacing an entire stock of Amphitheatres for happiness purposes. A single tower increases the culture cap as much as six Amphitheatres, and increases culture production as much as “two hundred”. There is generally little reason to delay this upgrade once the metal is available to build a tower.
  • Alternative Culture Buildings: Culture can also be generated by Temples and Chapels.

item.title: AI Core
item.description:
The AI Core is a crucial Mega Structure building associated with late-game progression, particularly concerning energy consumption and the introduction of the advanced science mechanic known as Gigaflops.

Here is a comprehensive breakdown of the AI Core:

1. Construction and Core Function

The AI Core is a building that is unlocked during the late game, after significant technological investment.

  • Technology Prerequisite: The AI Core is unlocked by researching the Artificial Intelligence technology.
  • Cost: The base cost to construct an AI Core is 125 Antimatter and 500,000 Science.
  • Energy Consumption: AI Cores consume energy, and their consumption increases with the number of Cores built. The formula is -(2 + 1.5 * AI Core) Energy per tick.
  • Output: The primary output of the AI Core is +0.02 Gigaflops per Tick.

2. Strategic Role and Mechanics

The AI Core is central to the very late-game progression involving high-level technology and the risk of the “AI Apocalypse”.
item.content:encoded:
The AI Core is a crucial Mega Structure building associated with late-game progression, particularly concerning energy consumption and the introduction of the advanced science mechanic known as Gigaflops.

Here is a comprehensive breakdown of the AI Core:

1. Construction and Core Function

The AI Core is a building that is unlocked during the late game, after significant technological investment.

  • Technology Prerequisite: The AI Core is unlocked by researching the Artificial Intelligence technology.
  • Cost: The base cost to construct an AI Core is 125 Antimatter and 500,000 Science.
  • Energy Consumption: AI Cores consume energy, and their consumption increases with the number of Cores built. The formula is -(2 + 1.5 * AI Core) Energy per tick.
  • Output: The primary output of the AI Core is +0.02 Gigaflops per Tick.

2. Strategic Role and Mechanics

The AI Core is central to the very late-game progression involving high-level technology and the risk of the “AI Apocalypse”.

  • Gigaflops Generation: AI Cores are the sole source of Gigaflops. Gigaflops contribute to the hashrate level, which increases the relic production of Space Beacons that have been upgraded with Relic Stations.
  • AI Apocalypse Risk: Accumulating Gigaflops can potentially lead to the AI Apocalypse. If the AI level reaches 15, you start losing resources.
  • Synergy with Entanglement Stations: AI Cores are typically built alongside Entanglement Stations (unlocked by Quantum Cryptography), which produce Hashes. The combination of AI Cores and Entanglement Stations creates hashes, which increase the hashrate level.
  • Ratio Management: When building AI Cores and Entanglement Stations, players must monitor the Gigaflops accumulation to avoid the AI Apocalypse. The ratio is suggested to be roughly 5 AI Cores to 1 Entanglement Station to prevent excessive Gigaflops accumulation, especially since Gigaflops are always lost on reset.

3. Upgrades and Policy Synergies

The effectiveness of AI Cores can be enhanced through specific Workshop upgrades and Government Policy/:

  • Machine Learning: This Workshop upgrade makes Data Center effectiveness increase by +10% per AI Core. The effect is based on the number of AI Cores built, not the AI level.
  • AI Bases: This Workshop upgrade increases Moon Base storage by +10% per AI Core. The effect is also based on the number of AI Cores.
  • Transkittenism Policy: This late-game government policy makes AI Cores twice as effective. The AI Cores produce twice as many Gigaflops, and the policy ensures that the AI apocalypse will not occur. Furthermore, AI Bases and the Machine Learning upgrades are strengthened.
  • Anarchy Challenge Goal: Interestingly, the AI Core is specified as the building that must be built to complete the Anarchy challenge.

item.title: Ivory Temple
item.description:
The Ivory Temple is a specialized building available in Kittens Game, particularly associated with the zebra race and the conversion of advanced hunting resources.

Here is a detailed breakdown of the Ivory Temple:

Building Details and Cost

  • Resource Cost: The Ivory Temple requires 1 T-Mythril and 100 Ivory.
  • Price Ratio: It has a price ratio of 1.15.
  • Prerequisite: The Ivory Temple is listed as a building unlocked via Zebra Upgrades, meaning you need to build the Zebra Workshop and Zebra Forge first, which are unlocked by Archery and cost Bloodstone.

Primary Function and Effects

The main function of the Ivory Temple is to convert large amounts of the rare resource Ivory into Minerals.
item.content:encoded:
The Ivory Temple is a specialized building available in Kittens Game, particularly associated with the zebra race and the conversion of advanced hunting resources.

Here is a detailed breakdown of the Ivory Temple:

Building Details and Cost

  • Resource Cost: The Ivory Temple requires 1 T-Mythril and 100 Ivory.
  • Price Ratio: It has a price ratio of 1.15.
  • Prerequisite: The Ivory Temple is listed as a building unlocked via Zebra Upgrades, meaning you need to build the Zebra Workshop and Zebra Forge first, which are unlocked by Archery and cost Bloodstone.

Primary Function and Effects

The main function of the Ivory Temple is to convert large amounts of the rare resource Ivory into Minerals.

  • Conversion: It converts ivory to minerals.
  • Resource Rates: It consumes 100 Ivory per tick and produces 1 Mineral per tick.
  • Catpower: It also increases maximum Catpower storage by +10.

Upgrades and Automation

The functionality of the Ivory Temple can be significantly boosted through late-game religious upgrades, specifically those related to the “Whispers” religion path (though not explicitly detailed in the provided sources, the automation is listed under its effects):

  • Whispers Unlock: The “Whispers” religion unlocks automation for the Ivory Temple.
  • Automation Effect: When automation is enabled, the Temple doubles ivory consumption and minerals production.
  • Drawbacks (Automation): The automation process comes with small associated costs: -2 Titanium per tick and -0.00002 Alicorns per tick.
  • Bonus Production (Automation): Automation also yields a slight production of another resource: +0.00005 T-Mythril per tick.

Context in the Game

The Ivory Temple provides a mechanism to monetize the rare resource Ivory, which is typically acquired through Hunting. Hunting is unlocked by Archery, costs 100 Catpower per hunt, and has a chance to yield Ivory, Furs, and Unicorns. Ivory itself is classified as a rare resource that gives +10% happiness but is gradually consumed.

The Ivory Temple offers a way to convert this consumable rare resource into a common resource (Minerals) at a high volume, which is particularly useful in scenarios where mineral supply is a bottleneck, or when accumulating high levels of Ivory from consistent hunting or Mint production.

Here is a comprehensive breakdown of the Mint, including its prerequisites, costs, effects, and strategic usage:

  • Resource Cost: Building a Mint is expensive, requiring significant amounts of processed materials:
    • Minerals: 5000 units
    • Plate: 200 units
    • Gold: 500 units
  • Price Ratio: The Mint has a price ratio of 1.15.

Effects and Function

The Mint has several specialized effects, making it a critical structure for resource stability and progression:
item.content:encoded:
The Mint is a crucial mid-to-late-game building in Kittens Game, primarily focused on increasing gold storage and generating rare resources, specifically Furs and Ivory.

Here is a comprehensive breakdown of the Mint, including its prerequisites, costs, effects, and strategic usage:

Unlocking and Cost

  • Prerequisite Technology: The Mint is unlocked after researching Architecture. Architecture costs 42,000 Science and 10 Compendiums, and is unlocked after Navigation.
  • Resource Cost: Building a Mint is expensive, requiring significant amounts of processed materials:
    • Minerals: 5000 units
    • Plate: 200 units
    • Gold: 500 units
  • Price Ratio: The Mint has a price ratio of 1.15.

Effects and Function

The Mint has several specialized effects, making it a critical structure for resource stability and progression:

  1. Rare Resource Generation: The Mint generates valuable rare resources, consuming Catpower and Gold:

    • Furs per Tick: +0.00875% of Max Catpower
    • Ivory per Tick: +0.0021% of Max Catpower
    • Furs and Ivory are rare resources that provide +10% happiness each but are gradually consumed over time.

  2. Resource Consumption: The Mint operates by consuming resources:

    • Catpower per Tick: -0.75
    • Gold per Tick: -0.005

  3. Gold Storage: Each Mint increases your maximum storage capacity for Gold by +100.

    • This storage limit is essential because Gold is needed for trading, building Temples, and acquiring Tradeposts. Max Gold storage can be further increased by Workshop upgrades such as Reinforced Warehouses, Titanium Warehouses, Alloy Warehouses, Concrete Pillars, Concrete Warehouses, and Storage Bunkers.

Strategic Role

Mints play a key role in the mid-to-late game, especially for automation and prestige farming:

  • Ivory and Fur Stockpiling: Mints allow you to generate Furs and Ivory passively based on your maximum Catpower, reducing the reliance on manually clicking “Send Hunters”. This is especially useful for maintaining high happiness and is very useful to run when you are idling to stockpile Furs.
  • Catpower Scaling: Since Mint production scales with maximum Catpower capacity, continued investment in structures that boost Catpower (like Temples and Templars) and cheap housing is mandated to maintain maximum output.
  • Blueprint Generation: In the hyper-speed “quick chrono-reset” endgame phase, the focus shifts to Mints for blueprint generation. Mints generate Furs, which can be crafted into Parchment, and subsequently into Manuscripts, Compendiums, and finally Blueprints. This method is preferred over hunting/crafting because Mints do not spend catpower, allowing it to grow for later use.
  • Gold Acquisition: Mints are production-boosting buildings that increase gold storage capacity. Gold is a necessary input for building Temples (for Faith/Culture) and Tradeposts (for trade effectiveness).
  • Policy Interaction: The Frugality policy (part of the Stoicism philosophy tree) directly impacts Mints by making them 10% more effective at producing resources.
  • Usage Advice: Experts advise running Mints when you are idling to stockpile Furs, but to turn them off when you are active to manage resource consumption. Furthermore, Mints, like Steamworks, are generally structures you should only use when away from your computer in the mid-game, as they can limit coal production.

Detail Requirement/Value Source
Technology Prerequisite Philosophy

Primary Outputs +0.1 Culture per Tick; Unlocks the Order of the Sun religion tab
Storage Increase +100 Max Faith

Strategic Purpose and Progression

The Temple is highly significant because it helps overcome a major early bottleneck and initiates the Faith system:
item.content:encoded:
The Temple is a critical mid-game building in Kittens Game, serving as a foundational structure for both your society’s culture and its religious system.

It is unlocked after researching the Philosophy technology.

Construction and Base Effects

The Temple is a key building in the Culture category.

Detail Requirement/Value Source
Technology Prerequisite Philosophy
Base Cost 25 Slab, 15 Plate, 50 Gold, 10 Manuscript
Primary Outputs +0.1 Culture per Tick; Unlocks the Order of the Sun religion tab
Storage Increase +100 Max Faith

Strategic Purpose and Progression

The Temple is highly significant because it helps overcome a major early bottleneck and initiates the Faith system:

  1. Culture Generation: Temples are a source of Culture, alongside Amphitheatres and Chapels. Culture is required to craft Manuscripts, which are necessary for researching advanced technologies like Theology and Astronomy. Amphitheatres are the earliest buildings to generate culture, which helps make “getting temples easier”.
  2. Faith Production: Temples are essential for generating Faith. Once the subsequent technology, Theology, is researched, Temples each begin generating 0.0015 Faith per tick. Faith is an expendable resource used exclusively via the Religion tab to purchase upgrades.
  3. Gold Sink and Priority: After learning Philosophy and once happiness is stable, players are strongly advised to focus on Temples and to “spend all your gold on temples”. As a general rule, if a Temple can be built soon, it “should be built before anything else”.

Upgrades and Synergies

Temples benefit directly from several upgrades, primarily found within the Order of the Sun religion tab, which is unlocked by the Temple itself. These religious upgrades use Faith to enhance the Temple’s non-religious utility, often contributing to Science, Culture, and Happiness:

  • Faith and Worship: Upgrades like Golden Spire (+50% max faith) and Sun Altar (+50 max faith) increase the capacity for faith storage within Temples.
  • Science and Culture:
    • Scholasticism grants Temples a bonus of +500 Max Science.
    • Stained Glass provides an additional +0.1 Culture per tick.
    • Basilica provides +0.2 Culture per tick and +125 Max Culture from Temples.
  • Happiness: Sun Altar increases the overall Happiness bonus by +0.5%.
  • Catpower: Templars increases the maximum catpower by +75 per Temple.

The total accumulation of Culture from Temples and Amphitheatres is necessary to eventually unlock the Trade with Nagas, which requires 1500 Culture Cap. Furthermore, the eventual goal for many players is the Solar Revolution upgrade, which relies on generating high amounts of Worship (converted from Faith via Temples and Chapels).

1. Construction and Unlocks

  • Technology Prerequisite: The Tradepost building is unlocked by researching the Currency technology. Currency costs 2,200 Science.
  • Cost: The base cost to construct a Tradepost is 500 Wood, 200 Minerals, and 10 Gold.
  • Price Ratio: The Tradepost has a price ratio of 1.15.

2. Purpose and Effects

The Tradepost provides benefits related to trade and resource consumption:
item.content:encoded:
The Tradepost is an early-game cultural building in Kittens Game that facilitates international commerce and manages the demand for luxury resources.

Here is a breakdown of the Tradepost’s purpose, costs, and strategic value, drawing on the sources provided:

1. Construction and Unlocks

  • Technology Prerequisite: The Tradepost building is unlocked by researching the Currency technology. Currency costs 2,200 Science.
  • Cost: The base cost to construct a Tradepost is 500 Wood, 200 Minerals, and 10 Gold.
  • Price Ratio: The Tradepost has a price ratio of 1.15.

2. Purpose and Effects

The Tradepost provides benefits related to trade and resource consumption:

  • Trade Bonus: It increases your effectiveness in trade by +1.5%.
  • Luxury Demand Reduction: It reduces the consumption rate of luxury resources (Furs, Ivory, Spice) by -4%.
  • Gold Consumption: The guide suggests building Tradeposts to use up excess gold.

3. Key Upgrades and Synergies

The Tradepost is essential for unlocking an important upgrade that manages race relations:

  • Caravanserai Upgrade: Researching Navigation technology allows you to purchase the Caravanserai upgrade.
    • This upgrade costs 25,000 Science, 10,000 Ivory, and 250 Gold.
    • It gives Tradeposts a minor effect on race standing. Specifically, each Tradepost decreases the hostile event probability by 0.35% and increases the friendly event probability by 0.175%.
    • For example, 85 Tradeposts can negate the chance that the hostile Zebras will give you nothing during a trade (or 58 if you have the Diplomacy Metaphysics upgrade).

4. Strategic Role and Context

Tradeposts are important during the mid-game transition, particularly when dealing with hostile races and managing luxury resources:

  • Trade Ratio Boost: The Pacifism Challenge reward involves the trade ratio, where the reward either gives a ratio boost times the number of Tradeposts you have, or a flat boost to the number of Tradeposts, whichever is smaller. The ratio boost begins at 10.65% of your Tradeposts and increases linearly per completion.
  • Trading with Leviathans: The amount of Time Crystals received per trade with the Leviathans is affected by the number of Tradeposts built.
  • Luxury Management: Experts generally favor the Epicureanism philosophy policy over Stoicism, noting that by the time Epicureanism is available, players should have plenty of Tradeposts to slow down luxury consumption.

5. Trade Unlocking Context

The ability to trade with other races, which Tradeposts enhance, is unlocked when a member of the Lizards arrives at your Village, usually after 20 years of game play. You must first research the Gold Ore upgrade (unlocked by Currency) to produce Gold in your Smelters before you can trade with anyone.

item.title: Broadcast Tower

The Broadcast Tower is a powerful upgraded structure derived from the Amphitheatre, serving primarily to drastically improve your civilization’s Happiness and Culture mechanics.
