The Broadcast Tower is an upgrade path (indicated by ∨) from the Amphitheatre.

  • Prerequisite: The building upgrade is enabled once the Electronics technology is researched.
  • Cost: Constructing a Broadcast Tower requires 1,250 Iron and 75 Titanium.
  • Upgrade Advice: There is very little reason to delay this upgrade once the necessary metal is acquired.

Primary Effects

The Broadcast Tower’s effects far surpass those of its prerequisite, the Amphitheatre:
item.content:encoded:
The Broadcast Tower is a powerful upgraded structure derived from the Amphitheatre, serving primarily to drastically improve your civilization’s Happiness and Culture mechanics.

Acquisition and Cost

The Broadcast Tower is an upgrade path (indicated by ∨) from the Amphitheatre.

  • Prerequisite: The building upgrade is enabled once the Electronics technology is researched.
  • Cost: Constructing a Broadcast Tower requires 1,250 Iron and 75 Titanium.
  • Upgrade Advice: There is very little reason to delay this upgrade once the necessary metal is acquired.

Primary Effects

The Broadcast Tower’s effects far surpass those of its prerequisite, the Amphitheatre:

  1. Happiness Management: The Broadcast Tower substantially reduces Unhappiness by -75%. Crucially, for managing population morale, a single broadcast tower can replace your entire stock of amphitheaters.
  2. Culture Generation and Cap: The tower provides massive bonuses to culture output and storage, with both effects tied to your Energy Surplus Ratio.
    • It grants Culture per Tick equal to 1 times the Energy Surplus Ratio.
    • It increases the Max Culture limit by 300 times the Energy Surplus Ratio.
    • For comparison to the Amphitheatre, a single Broadcast Tower increases the culture cap by as much as six amphitheaters, and increases production by as much as two hundred amphitheaters.

Upgrades

Broadcast Towers can be further improved with the Satellite Radio upgrade. This upgrade increases the tower’s Culture per Tick and Max Culture by 0.5% per active Satellite.

item.title: Catnip Field
item.description:
The Catnip Field is the most foundational building in Kittens Game, enabling the automatic accumulation of food necessary for the survival and expansion of your civilization.

Here is a breakdown of the Catnip Field:

Core Function and Cost

The Catnip Field is the initial food production building, crucial for transitioning the game from manual clicking to passive resource gain:

  • Acquisition: You begin by manually gathering Catnip until you accumulate 10 pieces.
  • Base Cost: The first Catnip Field costs 10 Catnip.
  • Price Ratio: The price ratio for purchasing additional fields is 1.12.
  • Effect: Each Catnip Field produces +0.125 Catnip per Tick.

Strategic Importance

Building Catnip Fields is the first step in establishing a stable food supply, which is critical because every kitten consumes Catnip:
item.content:encoded:
The Catnip Field is the most foundational building in Kittens Game, enabling the automatic accumulation of food necessary for the survival and expansion of your civilization.

Here is a breakdown of the Catnip Field:

Core Function and Cost

The Catnip Field is the initial food production building, crucial for transitioning the game from manual clicking to passive resource gain:

  • Acquisition: You begin by manually gathering Catnip until you accumulate 10 pieces.
  • Base Cost: The first Catnip Field costs 10 Catnip.
  • Price Ratio: The price ratio for purchasing additional fields is 1.12.
  • Effect: Each Catnip Field produces +0.125 Catnip per Tick.

Strategic Importance

Building Catnip Fields is the first step in establishing a stable food supply, which is critical because every kitten consumes Catnip:

  • Initial Progression: Purchasing fields allows Catnip to accumulate on its own without requiring further manual clicking. Buying multiple fields early (up to 19 or 20) is advised to speed up progress.
  • Basic Resource Rotation (BRR): The earliest routine for building a strong economic foundation involves taking all kittens and making them farmers, and then capping (or close to capping) everything that ONLY costs catnip, which includes Catnip Fields.
  • Diminishing Returns: Eventually, the fields become too expensive and do not produce enough to be truly useful. At this stage, players are advised to research Engineering and build Aqueducts instead, which increase Catnip production by a percentile.
  • Storage: The default maximum storage capacity for Catnip is 5000.

Seasonal and Environmental Effects

Catnip Fields are highly susceptible to the game’s weather system, especially during the harsh Winter season:

  • Seasonal Fluctuations: Production values change radically throughout the year.
    • In Spring, production receives a hefty bonus (average +50%).
    • In Winter, production sharply nosedives (average -75%).
    • A Cold Winter can reduce Catnip production by -90%.
  • Contrast with Farmers: Unlike the Catnip accumulated by the Farmer job (which produces +1 Catnip per tick), the production from Catnip Fields is subject to the effects of Winter. Juggling Catnip production is crucial for survival, particularly in Winter.

Challenge and Policy Interactions

Catnip Fields are affected by specific late-game Policy/ and challenges:

  • Communism Policy: This policy causes Catnip Field production to become -100% in cold winters.
  • Winter Has Come Challenge: When this challenge (which imposes endless winter) is active, Catnip production from fields will not benefit from the paragon production bonus. The increasing reward for completing this challenge increases the effect of Spring on Catnip Fields by 5% per run.
  • Post Apocalypse Challenge: In this high-pollution scenario, Catnip Fields may cost unobtainium at high pollution levels or with high numbers of broken cryochambers.

In the early game, managing Catnip production from these fields is like stocking a simple pantry: you have to gather enough food during the bounty of spring and summer to ensure you have reserves large enough to survive the consumption during winter’s famine.

item.title: Hut
item.description:
The Hut is the foundational housing building in the early stages of Kittens Game, enabling population growth and expanding your basic resources.

Here is a comprehensive overview of the Hut, its purpose, cost, and strategic role:

1. Function and Effect

Huts are essential for early progression as they directly increase the capacity for your workforce.

  • Population: Each Hut increases the maximum number of Kittens your village can support by +2.
  • Catpower Storage: Each Hut increases your maximum Catpower capacity by +75. Catpower is generated by Hunters and is used for trade and acquiring rare resources like Furs and Ivory.

2. Acquisition and Cost

Huts are one of the first structures a player builds after establishing basic resource production.
item.content:encoded:
The Hut is the foundational housing building in the early stages of Kittens Game, enabling population growth and expanding your basic resources.

Here is a comprehensive overview of the Hut, its purpose, cost, and strategic role:

1. Function and Effect

Huts are essential for early progression as they directly increase the capacity for your workforce.

  • Population: Each Hut increases the maximum number of Kittens your village can support by +2.
  • Catpower Storage: Each Hut increases your maximum Catpower capacity by +75. Catpower is generated by Hunters and is used for trade and acquiring rare resources like Furs and Ivory.

2. Acquisition and Cost

Huts are one of the first structures a player builds after establishing basic resource production.

  • Resource Cost: Constructing a Hut requires 5 Wood.
  • Price Ratio: Huts have a price ratio of 2.5.
  • Unlocking Kittens: Purchasing the first Hut unlocks Kittens and the Village tab, allowing you to assign jobs like Woodcutter.
  • Initial Build Order: A player must first accumulate 10 Catnip to build Catnip Fields, then refine 100 Catnip into 1 Wood (doing this five times) before they can purchase the first Hut.

3. Strategic Importance (Early Game)

Huts are a critical component for early resource scaling:

  • Global Modifier: In the early game, population is THE global modifier for production. Therefore, experts strongly recommend keeping Huts (and subsequent Log Houses) maxed out whenever possible to maximize population.
  • Catnip Management: Because each Kitten consumes Catnip (4.25 units per second), players should not buy too many Huts until they have a balanced Catnip supply, especially considering the severe production decrease during Winter (-75%).
  • Housing Progression: Huts are the initial form of housing and are superseded by Log Houses (unlocked by Construction) and later Mansions (unlocked by Architecture).

4. Upgrades and Price Reduction

The cost efficiency of Huts can be permanently improved through various Workshop upgrades, which reduce their price ratio:

Upgrade Price Ratio Reduction Prerequisite
Ironwood Huts -50% Reinforced Warehouses
Concrete Huts -30% Concrete Pillars
Unobtainium Huts -25% Exogeology
Eludium Huts -10% Advanced Exogeology/Exometallurgy

These price ratio reductions, along with other Metaphysics bonuses like Paragon, are essential for allowing players to continue maxing out Huts as their wood reserves and costs escalate.

item.title: Hydro Plant
item.description:
The Hydro Plant is an advanced energy-generating structure in Kittens Game that is designed to replace the earlier catnip-boosting Aqueduct building.

Here is a detailed breakdown of the Hydro Plant, its costs, effects, and strategic considerations:

Acquisition and Cost

  • Prerequisite Technology: The Hydro Plant is unlocked by researching Robotics. Robotics requires 140K Science and 80 Blueprints.
  • Resource Cost: Building a Hydro Plant is resource-intensive, requiring advanced materials: 100 Concrete and 2500 Titanium. It has a price ratio of 1.15.
  • Upgrade Path: The Hydro Plant is classified as an upgraded building that supersedes the Aqueduct.

Effects and Upgrades

  • Energy Production: Each Hydro Plant provides +5 Energy.
  • Upgrades: The Hydro Plant Turbines upgrade enhances its effectiveness, increasing Hydro Plant energy production by +15% (raising output from 5Wt to 5.75Wt). This upgrade costs 250k Science and 125 Unobtainium.
  • Policy Interaction: The Lizard Relations: Ecologists policy is affected by the number of active Hydro Plants, allowing some Magnetos to still boost resource production even when turned off.

Strategic Considerations for Conversion

Upgrading Aqueducts to Hydro Plants represents a crucial transition from basic resource augmentation to industrial power generation. This decision carries significant risk:
item.content:encoded:
The Hydro Plant is an advanced energy-generating structure in Kittens Game that is designed to replace the earlier catnip-boosting Aqueduct building.

Here is a detailed breakdown of the Hydro Plant, its costs, effects, and strategic considerations:

Acquisition and Cost

  • Prerequisite Technology: The Hydro Plant is unlocked by researching Robotics. Robotics requires 140K Science and 80 Blueprints.
  • Resource Cost: Building a Hydro Plant is resource-intensive, requiring advanced materials: 100 Concrete and 2500 Titanium. It has a price ratio of 1.15.
  • Upgrade Path: The Hydro Plant is classified as an upgraded building that supersedes the Aqueduct.

Effects and Upgrades

  • Energy Production: Each Hydro Plant provides +5 Energy.
  • Upgrades: The Hydro Plant Turbines upgrade enhances its effectiveness, increasing Hydro Plant energy production by +15% (raising output from 5Wt to 5.75Wt). This upgrade costs 250k Science and 125 Unobtainium.
  • Policy Interaction: The Lizard Relations: Ecologists policy is affected by the number of active Hydro Plants, allowing some Magnetos to still boost resource production even when turned off.

Strategic Considerations for Conversion

Upgrading Aqueducts to Hydro Plants represents a crucial transition from basic resource augmentation to industrial power generation. This decision carries significant risk:

  1. Risk of Starvation: Aqueducts provide a direct percentage boost to catnip production. Demolishing Aqueducts carelessly can “very quickly put you in a starvation situation”.
  2. Resource Bottleneck: You should wait until you have good titanium production before beginning this transition, as Hydro Plants cost a fair amount of titanium.
  3. Optimal Timing: The upgrade should be performed when you need Energy more than you need catnip. The strategic goal is to repurpose land previously devoted to marginal catnip bonuses for energy generation, which powers structures that offer stronger global scaling. Pastures are considered much safer to upgrade (to Solar Farms) than Aqueducts, as Pastures’ food demand reduction is subject to strict diminishing returns.

Late Game Importance

Hydro Plants, along with Sunlifters and Reactors, are a main focus for power generation in the late game. They are also counted among the list of energy production buildings required to complete the Energy Challenge.

item.title: Library
item.description:
The Library is a foundational early-game building in Kittens Game that is essential for unlocking scientific progression and accessing the core mechanics of the game.

Here is a detailed breakdown of the Library:

1. Unlocking and Cost

  • Prerequisite: The Library is unlocked once you have accumulated 25 Wood.
  • Resource Cost: Building a Library requires 25 Wood.
  • Price Ratio: The Library has a price ratio of 1.15.

2. Primary Effects

The Library is critical because it unlocks the mechanism for generating and storing Science.
item.content:encoded:
The Library is a foundational early-game building in Kittens Game that is essential for unlocking scientific progression and accessing the core mechanics of the game.

Here is a detailed breakdown of the Library:

1. Unlocking and Cost

  • Prerequisite: The Library is unlocked once you have accumulated 25 Wood.
  • Resource Cost: Building a Library requires 25 Wood.
  • Price Ratio: The Library has a price ratio of 1.15.

2. Primary Effects

The Library is critical because it unlocks the mechanism for generating and storing Science.

  • Science Production: Each Library provides a +10% Science boost.
  • Science Storage: Each Library increases the maximum Science storage capacity by +250. The initial capacity for Science is 250 units.
  • Culture Storage: Each Library also provides +10 to maximum Culture capacity.
  • Kitten Job: Creating a Library unlocks the Scholar job, which allows you to employ Kittens in harvesting Science. Scholars produce 0.035 Science per tick.
  • Astronomical Events: After building your first Library, there is a 0.25% chance every day that an astronomical event will occur, which, when observed, earns Science.

3. Strategic Role in Early Progression

In the early game, purchasing Libraries is a critical step in achieving scientific velocity.

  • Science Rush: Experts recommend that players prioritize converting accumulated wood into Libraries before Barns.
  • Accelerated Tech: Libraries are essential because they immediately increase science storage, enabling the rapid accumulation necessary to cross crucial technological thresholds in a shorter time span. Having more Libraries increases the science gained from observing astronomical events.
  • Iron Will Mode: In Iron Will mode (playing without kittens/housing), the Library is crucial as astronomical events observed after building Libraries become the only initial source of Science. Players in this mode are advised to concentrate on building nothing but Libraries until they have researched Calendar, Agriculture, and Archery.

4. Upgrades and Progression

The Library is an early building that can be upgraded later in the game:

  • Upgrade Path: The Library upgrades to a Data Center. This upgrade is unlocked by researching Electronics.
  • Data Center Conversion: Data Centers are generally superior to Libraries, providing +750 max Science and +250 max Culture. However, if you are planning to upgrade, be aware that astronomical events cease to occur if you have zero Libraries and zero Data Centers. Additionally, switching to Data Centers will decrease your bonus for crafting blueprints since you will have fewer total buildings compared to Libraries.
  • Science Cap Boosts: Libraries’ maximum science bonus increases by 2% per Observatory if you have researched upgrades like Titanium Reflectors, Unobtainium Reflectors, or Eludium Reflectors.

Libraries are classified as structures that increase maximum storage, and experts emphasize that increasing resource storage limits (or “caps”) is the second most important thing in the game, right after production.

item.title: Log House
item.description:
Build a house (each has a space for 1 kitten)

The Log House is an important early-to-mid-game population building in Kittens Game, serving as an upgrade to the basic Hut and contributing to population growth and resource capacity.

Here is a detailed breakdown of the Log House:

Unlocking and Cost

  • Prerequisite Technology: Log Houses are unlocked after researching Construction. Construction costs 1300 Science and is unlocked after Animal Husbandry.
  • Resource Cost: Constructing a Log House requires both Wood and Minerals:
    • Wood: 200 units
    • Minerals: 250 units
    • Price Ratio: Log Houses have a price ratio of 1.15.
  • Acquisition Timing: Players can start building Log Houses once they have Minerals.

Effects

Log Houses primarily increase the maximum number of kittens your village can support and boost your Catpower limit.
item.content:encoded:
Build a house (each has a space for 1 kitten)

The Log House is an important early-to-mid-game population building in Kittens Game, serving as an upgrade to the basic Hut and contributing to population growth and resource capacity.

Here is a detailed breakdown of the Log House:

Unlocking and Cost

  • Prerequisite Technology: Log Houses are unlocked after researching Construction. Construction costs 1300 Science and is unlocked after Animal Husbandry.
  • Resource Cost: Constructing a Log House requires both Wood and Minerals:
    • Wood: 200 units
    • Minerals: 250 units
    • Price Ratio: Log Houses have a price ratio of 1.15.
  • Acquisition Timing: Players can start building Log Houses once they have Minerals.

Effects

Log Houses primarily increase the maximum number of kittens your village can support and boost your Catpower limit.

  • Maximum Kittens: Each Log House increases the maximum number of kittens by +1.
  • Maximum Catpower: Each Log House increases the maximum Catpower storage by +50.
  • Strategic Role: Log Houses are key to increasing your kitten population. Since kittens are the primary unit of production, experts recommend keeping Huts and Log Houses maxed out whenever possible in the early game to maximize population.

Comparison and Progression

Log Houses are the second tier of housing, following Huts, and preceding Mansions:

  • Huts increase maximum kittens by +2 and maximum Catpower by +75. Log Houses are often built alongside Pastures to manage the increased kitten burden on Catnip supplies.
  • Log Houses can be seen as an intermediate population step before unlocking Mansions (requiring Slab, Steel, and Titanium, and unlocked by Architecture).
  • Population Strategy: Log Houses, along with Huts, are a focus point in the early game for maximizing global production since population acts as “THE global modifier” in early phases.

Policy Influence

The Fascism policy, unlocked later in the game (Phase 3), specifically benefits Log Houses:

  • Fascism Policy Effect: If you select Fascism (which requires building a Factory and having chosen Autocracy or Monarchy), Log Houses cost half as much (50% cheaper). Fascism also eliminates population penalties to happiness. This policy might be chosen on a first run to help reach 130+ kittens before the first reset, aided by the reduced Log House cost.

Endgame Context (Paragon Grinding)

In later cycles, particularly when prioritizing maximum paragon gain in short runs, Log Houses are still essential housing components alongside Huts, Mansions, and Space Stations. Guidance for late-game paragon grinding often advises building the first few Log Houses quickly to allow kittens to trickle in during the first couple of minutes, before transitioning to more advanced housing options.

item.title: Lumber Mill
item.description:
The Lumber Mill is a crucial early-to-mid-game building in Kittens Game, primarily focused on significantly increasing your Wood output and efficiency.

Here is a comprehensive overview of the Lumber Mill, drawing on the provided sources:

1. Construction and Unlocks

  • Prerequisite: The Lumber Mill building is unlocked by researching the Construction technology.
  • Cost: The base cost to construct a Lumber Mill is 100 Wood, 50 Iron, and 250 Minerals.
  • Context: The walkthrough notes that Wood accumulates “reeeaallyyyy slowlyyyy” until you invest in Lumber Mills. To construct them, you must first research Metal Working to gain access to Smelters, which produce the necessary Iron.

2. Purpose and Effects

The Lumber Mill serves two primary functions:
item.content:encoded:
The Lumber Mill is a crucial early-to-mid-game building in Kittens Game, primarily focused on significantly increasing your Wood output and efficiency.

Here is a comprehensive overview of the Lumber Mill, drawing on the provided sources:

1. Construction and Unlocks

  • Prerequisite: The Lumber Mill building is unlocked by researching the Construction technology.
  • Cost: The base cost to construct a Lumber Mill is 100 Wood, 50 Iron, and 250 Minerals.
  • Context: The walkthrough notes that Wood accumulates “reeeaallyyyy slowlyyyy” until you invest in Lumber Mills. To construct them, you must first research Metal Working to gain access to Smelters, which produce the necessary Iron.

2. Purpose and Effects

The Lumber Mill serves two primary functions:

  1. Wood Production Boost: It increases your Wood production by +10%.
  2. Catnip Refinement Efficiency: It increases the Catnip Refinement rate by +10%.

3. Upgrades and Enhancements

The efficiency of Lumber Mills can be improved through several Workshop upgrades, which stack multiplicatively with the base production:

Upgrade Name Cost Prerequisite Tech Effect
Reinforced Saw Science, Iron (2,500/1,000) Construction Each Lumber Mill gives an additional +20% to the production ratio.
Steel Saw Science, Steel (52K/750) Physics Each Lumber Mill gives an additional +20% to the production ratio.
Titanium Saw Science, Titanium (70K/500) Steel Saw Each Lumber Mill gives an additional +15% to the production ratio.
Alloy Saw Science, Alloy (85K/75) Titanium Saw Each Lumber Mill gives an additional +15% to the production ratio.

4. Strategic Role

Lumber Mills are strategically important for several reasons in the early and mid-game:

  • Early Iron Management: In the early game, before later technologies are available, Lumber Mills are recommended as a way to use up excess Iron.
  • Wood Bottleneck Solution: They are necessary to increase Wood output to a sustainable rate, which supports the construction of other early buildings like Barns, Huts, and Libraries.
  • Iron Will Mode: In the Iron Will challenge, where you cannot build housing, the Lumber Mill’s Catnip Refinement bonus is particularly important as the Clear Cutting policy provides a similar bonus.

The priority placed on building Lumber Mills is highlighted by the advice to hold off on building steel until the Coal upgrades are secured, noting that players are going to need the Iron for Lumber Mills and Observatories.

item.title: Mine
item.description:
The Mine is a foundational resource-gathering building in Kittens Game, crucial for establishing mineral production and unlocking the Miner profession.

Here is a detailed breakdown of the Mine:

1. Unlocking and Cost

  • Prerequisite Technology: The Mine is unlocked after researching Mining. Mining costs 500 Science and is unlocked after Agriculture.
  • Cost: The Mine building requires 100 Wood to construct, and it has a price ratio of 1.15.

2. Primary Effects and Function

The Mine is the key structure for accessing and increasing your Minerals supply:
item.content:encoded:
The Mine is a foundational resource-gathering building in Kittens Game, crucial for establishing mineral production and unlocking the Miner profession.

Here is a detailed breakdown of the Mine:

1. Unlocking and Cost

  • Prerequisite Technology: The Mine is unlocked after researching Mining. Mining costs 500 Science and is unlocked after Agriculture.
  • Cost: The Mine building requires 100 Wood to construct, and it has a price ratio of 1.15.

2. Primary Effects and Function

The Mine is the key structure for accessing and increasing your Minerals supply:

  • Mineral Production Bonus: Each Mine built provides a +20% Minerals bonus.
  • Unlocks Job: Building a Mine unlocks the Miner job, allowing you to employ Kittens to accumulate resources. Kittens assigned as Miners produce 0.05 Minerals per Tick.
  • Meteors: Researching Mining also enables Meteors, which automatically grant a small boost to Minerals when they fall near your village. In the challenging Iron Will mode (playing without kittens/housing), Meteors are the only initial source of Minerals, and building more Mines increases the amount of minerals gained from these events.
  • Pollution: Mines are listed among the structures that produce pollution, which negatively impacts catnip production, happiness, and kitten arrival speed.

3. Upgrades and Strategic Role

While essential in the early game, the effectiveness of Mines is often compared to superior global multipliers later on.

  • Coal Production Upgrade: The Mine building can be upgraded through the Deep Mining Workshop upgrade, which is unlocked by researching Steel. Deep Mining allows Mines to produce Coal at a rate of 0.003 coal per Tick (or 0.015 per second).
  • Strategic Priority: Minerals quickly become increasingly important for advanced buildings. Building Mines is a component of the Basic Resource Rotation (BRR) recommended in the early game to ensure a strong economic foundation by focusing on basic resource buildings.
  • Scaling: Although necessary for initial progression, experts suggest that structures like Mines are generally considered “pretty lame” and inefficient beyond the early game when compared to global production boosts like happiness or Magnetos.

item.title: Observatory
item.description:
The Observatory is a key mid-game science building in Kittens Game, primarily designed to boost science accumulation, increase science capacity, and, most importantly, enable and enhance the discovery of Starcharts.

Here is a detailed breakdown of the Observatory:

1. Construction and Unlocks

  • Prerequisite Technology: The Observatory is unlocked by researching Astronomy. Astronomy requires 28,000 Science and 65 Manuscripts.
  • Cost: The base cost to construct an Observatory is 50 Scaffold, 35 Slab, 750 Iron, and 1,000 Science.
  • Price Ratio: The price ratio of the Observatory is 1.1.

2. Purpose and Effects

The Observatory provides several critical functions related to science and celestial mechanics:
item.content:encoded:
The Observatory is a key mid-game science building in Kittens Game, primarily designed to boost science accumulation, increase science capacity, and, most importantly, enable and enhance the discovery of Starcharts.

Here is a detailed breakdown of the Observatory:

1. Construction and Unlocks

  • Prerequisite Technology: The Observatory is unlocked by researching Astronomy. Astronomy requires 28,000 Science and 65 Manuscripts.
  • Cost: The base cost to construct an Observatory is 50 Scaffold, 35 Slab, 750 Iron, and 1,000 Science.
  • Price Ratio: The price ratio of the Observatory is 1.1.

2. Purpose and Effects

The Observatory provides several critical functions related to science and celestial mechanics:

  • Science and Capacity: It provides a +25% bonus to Science production and increases the Max Science cap by +1000.
  • Astronomical Events: It is essential for managing Starchart acquisition:
    • It increases the Astronomical Event Chance by +0.2% (additive).
    • It increases the Automatic Event Observation Chance by +1%.
    • Every Observatory built increases the daily chance of an astronomical event occurring (base chance is 0.25%).

3. Strategic Importance (The Titanium Era)

The Observatory is a high-priority building during the mid-game (referred to as the “Titanium era”) because it is the primary bottleneck-breaker for unlocking trade with Zebras and acquiring titanium.

  • Starchart Production: Observatories are necessary for producing Starcharts. Starcharts are required to craft Trade Ships, which are needed to discover Zebras.
  • Iron Priority: In the Titanium era, players are advised that all Iron should be going towards Observatories.
  • Automation: The increase in Automatic Event Observation Chance is crucial because it reduces the player’s need to manually click the “Observe” button whenever an astronomical event occurs. The game suggests paying attention and clicking every meteor until you have 25 Starcharts, after which the Observatory’s automatic observation chance helps significantly.
  • Alternative Science Generation: In the early stages of the Iron Will challenge, where housing cannot be built and kitten jobs are unavailable, the science gained from astronomical events (which are boosted by Observatories) is the only initial source of Science.

4. Upgrades and Synergies

Observatories benefit from and contribute to other systems via upgrades:

  • Science Storage Boosts: Observatories contribute directly to the effectiveness of your Library and later Data Center buildings through specialized Reflectors:
    • Titanium Reflectors, Unobtainium Reflectors, and Eludium Reflectors each increase the Libraries’ (and Data Centers’) max science bonus by an additional 2% per Observatory.
    • The Astrolabe upgrade boosts the Observatory’s science storage capacity by 50%.
  • Event Chance Metaphysics: The Metaphysics upgrade Astromancy doubles the Observatory’s effectiveness regarding event chance and auto-event observation chance (though not the science bonus itself).
  • Satellite Synergy: The Militarize Space policy increases the Observatory’s maximum science bonus from Satellites by 10%. Additionally, the Uplink and Starlink upgrades, which boost Data Centers and Bio Labs, respectively, are unlocked by Satellites, further highlighting the interconnected nature of late-game science buildings.

item.title: Pasture
item.description:
A Pasture is an early-game food production building in Kittens Game that helps reduce your civilization’s Catnip consumption rate.

Here is a breakdown of the Pasture:

Functionality and Benefits

  • Primary Effect: The Pasture decreases the amount of Catnip required by each Kitten, specifically reducing Catnip Demand by 0.5%. This reduction helps kittens survive, especially during Winter when Catnip production nosedives.
  • Cost: A Pasture costs 100 Catnip and 10 Wood to construct, and its price ratio increases by 1.15 for each subsequent purchase.
  • Prerequisite: Pastures are unlocked after you research the Animal Husbandry technology. Animal Husbandry itself is unlocked after researching Archery.

Relation to Catnip Survival

In the early game, surviving Winter can be challenging because Catnip Field production decreases by 75% in Winter (and 90% in a Cold Winter).
item.content:encoded:
A Pasture is an early-game food production building in Kittens Game that helps reduce your civilization’s Catnip consumption rate.

Here is a breakdown of the Pasture:

Functionality and Benefits

  • Primary Effect: The Pasture decreases the amount of Catnip required by each Kitten, specifically reducing Catnip Demand by 0.5%. This reduction helps kittens survive, especially during Winter when Catnip production nosedives.
  • Cost: A Pasture costs 100 Catnip and 10 Wood to construct, and its price ratio increases by 1.15 for each subsequent purchase.
  • Prerequisite: Pastures are unlocked after you research the Animal Husbandry technology. Animal Husbandry itself is unlocked after researching Archery.

Relation to Catnip Survival

In the early game, surviving Winter can be challenging because Catnip Field production decreases by 75% in Winter (and 90% in a Cold Winter).

  • While Farmers (unlocked by Agriculture) are essential because their Catnip accumulation is not subject to the effects of Winter, Pastures provide a vital complementary benefit by lowering the overall Catnip needed by your growing population.
  • Acquiring Pastures, along with increasing your Catnip Fields and constructing Barns (which boost Catnip storage capacity), is crucial for maintaining a healthy and productive population during resource-scarce seasons.

Upgrades and Achievements

  • Upgrade Path: The Pasture (indicated by the ∧ symbol) can be upgraded to a Solar Farm after researching the Ecology technology. This upgrade is generally performed when you need Energy more than you need Catnip, but it means you lose the Pasture’s food bonus.
  • Achievements: Building 45 Pastures is associated with an achievement, although Pastures are considered “useless” in the specific context of the Iron Will challenge.

Unicorn Pastures (Related Building)

The Unicorn Pasture is a separate, related building that also reduces Catnip Demand.

  • Acquisition: You must first find two Unicorns (which have a 5% chance of being gathered during a Hunt) to create a Unicorn Pasture.
  • Effect: A Unicorn Pasture costs 2 Unicorns and has a price ratio of 1.75. Its primary effect is reducing Catnip Demand by 0.15% and automatically generating more Unicorns.
  • Long-Term Benefit: Unicorn Pastures are handy in the long run because they further reduce the amount of Catnip consumed by each Kitten.

item.title: Warehouse
item.description:
The Warehouse is an essential resource storage building in Kittens Game, unlocked in the mid-early game, which helps address the fundamental bottleneck of resource caps.

Here is a detailed summary of the Warehouse, based on the sources:

1. Construction and Unlocks

  • Technology Prerequisite: The Warehouse building is unlocked by researching the Construction technology. Construction costs 1,300 Science.
  • Cost: The base cost to construct a Warehouse is 1.5 Beam and 2 Slab. These materials are crafted resources, requiring Wood and Minerals.
  • Upgrade Path: The Warehouse is an upgradeable building, designed to eventually be replaced by the Spaceport.

2. Purpose and Storage Effects

Warehouses increase the storage capacity for common and processed resources:
item.content:encoded:
The Warehouse is an essential resource storage building in Kittens Game, unlocked in the mid-early game, which helps address the fundamental bottleneck of resource caps.

Here is a detailed summary of the Warehouse, based on the sources:

1. Construction and Unlocks

  • Technology Prerequisite: The Warehouse building is unlocked by researching the Construction technology. Construction costs 1,300 Science.
  • Cost: The base cost to construct a Warehouse is 1.5 Beam and 2 Slab. These materials are crafted resources, requiring Wood and Minerals.
  • Upgrade Path: The Warehouse is an upgradeable building, designed to eventually be replaced by the Spaceport.

2. Purpose and Storage Effects

Warehouses increase the storage capacity for common and processed resources:

Resource Maximum Storage Increase per Warehouse
Wood +150
Minerals +200
Iron +25
Coal +30
Gold +5
Titanium +10

A key upgrade, Silos, also allows Warehouses to store Catnip, adding +750 Max Catnip per Warehouse.

3. Strategic Importance and Progression

The Warehouse is strategically vital for alleviating resource storage limits, which the sources note is the second most important thing in the game, as hitting storage limits greatly slows progress.

  • Mid-Game Building: Warehouses, along with Barns and Harbors, are categorized as general storage buildings that should be built “as needed”.
  • Filling Gaps: When grinding for specific resources in the mid-game, if other production buildings (Mines, Smelters, Log Houses, Workshops) are capped, players are advised to build Warehouses.
  • Early Game Strategy: While Barns are unlocked earlier (via Agriculture), Warehouses are the next step in storage capacity after Barns are introduced.

4. Key Upgrades

Warehouses benefit from numerous Workshop upgrades that increase their storage capacity, often stacking additively with other storage buildings like Barns and Harbors:

Upgrade Name Effect on Storage Capacity Technology/Prerequisite
Reinforced Warehouses Max storage for common resources (Wood, Minerals, Coal, Iron, Gold, Titanium) is increased by 25%. Steel
Titanium Warehouses Max storage for common resources is increased by 50%. Silos
Alloy Warehouses Max storage for common resources is increased by 45%. Chemistry
Concrete Warehouses Max storage for common resources is increased by 35%. Concrete Pillars
Storage Bunkers Max storage for common resources is increased by 20%. Exogeology
Concrete Pillars Increases Max storage for Wood, Minerals, Iron, Coal, Gold, and Titanium by 5%. Mechanization

Warehouses can also benefit from upgrades that apply to all storage facilities (Barns, Warehouses, Harbors, and Mints), such as those relating to Reinforced Barns, Titanium Barns, and Alloy Barns, which increase Wood, Minerals, and Iron storage capacity.

item.title: Geology
item.description:
Geology is a crucial mid-game technology that opens up advanced mineral extraction, job specialization, and boosts industrial resource production, particularly Coal and Gold.

Here is a detailed breakdown of the Geology technology:

Technology Details and Cost

  • Prerequisite: Geology is unlocked by researching Navigation.
  • Cost: Researching Geology requires 65,000 Science and 65 Compendium.
  • Unlocks: Geology unlocks the Geologist job, the Quarry building, and the Geodesy upgrade. It also unlocks the Biology technology.

Key Unlocks and Effects

Geology introduces new ways to gather important base resources, accelerating industrial capacity:
item.content:encoded:
Geology is a crucial mid-game technology that opens up advanced mineral extraction, job specialization, and boosts industrial resource production, particularly Coal and Gold.

Here is a detailed breakdown of the Geology technology:

Technology Details and Cost

  • Prerequisite: Geology is unlocked by researching Navigation.
  • Cost: Researching Geology requires 65,000 Science and 65 Compendium.
  • Unlocks: Geology unlocks the Geologist job, the Quarry building, and the Geodesy upgrade. It also unlocks the Biology technology.

Key Unlocks and Effects

Geology introduces new ways to gather important base resources, accelerating industrial capacity:

Unlock Type Production/Effect Details Source
Geologist Job Coal per Tick +0.015 This kitten job is enabled by Geology.
Quarry Building Minerals +35%, Coal per Tick +0.015 This building is unlocked by Geology.
Geodesy Upgrade Geologists gain +0.0075 coal/tick and +0.0008 gold/tick This workshop upgrade makes Geologists more effective and allows them to find gold.
Mineralogy Department Upgrade Not detailed, but listed as a Zebra Upgrade associated with Geology This is an upgrade for the Academy building.

The Quarry building requires 50 Scaffold, 125 Steel, and 1,000 Slab to construct.

Strategic Importance

Geology and its associated upgrades are highly valuable for boosting key industrial inputs, especially Gold, which becomes a bottleneck resource during the Titanium era:

  • Coal and Gold Production: Strategically, Geology improves both coal and gold production.
  • Gold Generation (Geodesy): The Geodesy upgrade is considered a major milestone. While the upgrade itself is costly (90,000 Science, 250 Titanium, 500 Starchart), acquiring it GREATLY increases gold production. Gold is essential for trading (including the vital trade for Titanium with Zebras) and for funding Temple construction.
  • Resource Bottleneck: In the Titanium era, once you have enough Observatories to get Starcharts at a healthy rate, players are advised to focus on researching Geology and pushing for Geodesy.

In essence, researching Geology provides the necessary specialization (Geologists and Quarries) to rapidly scale the production of fundamental inputs (Minerals and Coal) and provides a pathway (Geodesy) to alleviate the mid-game bottleneck associated with Gold, ensuring smoother trade and cultural progression.

item.title: Happiness
item.description:
Happiness is a critical game mechanic that directly influences the productivity and overall efficiency of your Kittens in their work. The higher the level of happiness, the better the results of their labour.

However, happiness can become a hindrance, as it is considered a production killer until you have enough Amphitheaters. As the population grows, Kittens become unhappy, and this affects overall production.

Sources and Effects of Happiness

Positive Sources (Boosts)

  1. Rare Resources: Rare resources (Furs, Ivory, and Spice) provide a happiness bonus. Hunting accumulates Furs and Ivory, which serves the purpose of increasing Happiness. Each rare resource, when consumed, gives +10% to happiness. Mints, which generate rare resources, also help boost happiness and therefore production. The Epicureanism policy can increase the happiness gained from rare resources to 11% each, and the Extravagance policy increases happiness from consumable luxury resources by 5.
  2. Karma: Karma, which is gained upon resetting the game (if you have more than 35 kittens), increases happiness, making your kittens happier and thus more productive.
  3. Buildings and Upgrades:
    • Amphitheatres are crucial for the early game as they help reduce unhappiness caused by rising population.
    • The religious upgrade Sun Altar (unlocked via the Order of the Sun) provides +0.5% happiness from Temples, with additional levels available through Transcendence.
    • Sacrificing unicorns for a unicorn tear grants a happiness/production bonus.
    • A single Broadcast Tower can replace your entire stock of Amphitheaters for happiness purposes.
  4. Policy/ and Policy Effects:
    • The Liberty policy increases the production effect of happiness by 10% and grants free housing for one kitten.
    • The Environmentalism policy provides a +3% happiness effect.
    • The Conservation policy increases happiness by +5%.
    • The Fascism policy eliminates population penalties to happiness.

Negative Sources (Penalties)

  1. Population Growth: As population rises, kittens become unhappy.
  2. Pollution: A high level of pollution in the atmosphere negatively affects your kittens and reduces your happiness.
  3. Policy/: Certain Policy/ increase happiness penalties, such as Strip Mining and Clear Cutting, which both incur a -2% happiness penalty. The Sustainability policy can be used later to remove this happiness penalty.
  4. Challenges:Running the Atheism challenge decreases happiness by 0.5 for each run completed after the first.

Management

To maintain a healthy, productive population, it is crucial to keep your Happiness nice and high. Players are advised to build Amphitheatres until they stop noticeably improving Happiness, as monitored by the ‘population penalty’ percentage on the top bar of the game. Trade Depots decrease the consumption rate of rare resources (luxuries).

item.title: Sun Altar
item.description:
The Sun Altar is a crucial religious upgrade available in Kittens Game, found under the Order of the Sun within the Religion tab.

Here is a breakdown of its effects, costs, and requirements:

Function and Effects

The Sun Altar provides dual benefits by enhancing both resource capacity (Faith) and kitten morale (Happiness):

  1. Faith Storage Increase: The upgrade increases Temple maximum faith storage by +50.
    • This bonus stacks, as each additional level of Sun Altar purchased using Transcendence increases this storage bonus by an additional +50.
  2. Happiness Contribution: The Sun Altar contributes to your civilization’s overall Happiness by increasing the happiness provided by Temples by +0.5%.
    • This happiness bonus also scales with Transcendence, increasing by an additional +0.1% for each additional level purchased.

The sources also mention that the Sun Altar contributes to overall Happiness, highlighting that Religious upgrades do affect things outside the Religion tab.

Function and Effects

The sources also mention that the Sun Altar contributes to overall Happiness, highlighting that Religious upgrades do affect things outside the Religion tab.

Requirements and Cost

To purchase the Sun Altar, you must have progressed sufficiently within the religious system:

  • Prerequisite: The upgrade requires you to have accumulated 750 Worship. Worship is the resource gained by converting Faith via the “Praise the sun!” action.
  • Cost: The Sun Altar costs 500 Faith and 250 Gold.

Context within Religious Progression

The Sun Altar is one of several upgrades available once you accumulate Worship, following earlier upgrades like Scholasticism (300 Worship) and Golden Spire (500 Worship). These upgrades are essential for expanding the role and efficiency of Temples, which are unlocked after researching Theology. Increasing faith storage is particularly important for later-game progression, as reaching high faith caps (100K Faith limit) is necessary to unlock Apocrypha and the related Epiphany mechanics.

item.title: Stoicism vs Epicurianism
item.description:
The Policy/ of Stoicism and Epicureanism represent two distinct philosophical approaches available to your kittens’ civilization, primarily impacting the management of luxury resources and Happiness. These choices, unlocked after researching Philosophy, determine subsequent policy options in the Philosophy category.

Here is a comparison of the two Policy/ based on the source material:

Stoicism

The Stoicism policy focuses on endurance and restraint regarding consumption.

  • Description: The stoics teach that your civilization ought to endure hardship without complaint.
  • Effect: Stoicism halves the consumption of luxury resources. Luxury resources include Furs, Ivory, and Spice.
  • Other Impact: It also introduces a -25% reduction in Brewery consumption.
  • Subsequent Policy/: Stoicism leads to Frugality and Rationing Policy/.
    • Frugality improves Mints’ resource production by 10%.
    • Rationing makes hunting more effective (+0.1 Hunting bonus) and reduces the catnip consumption increase per happiness by 10%.

Epicureanism

Epicureanism emphasizes pleasure as the highest good, leveraging luxury resources for increased satisfaction and production bonuses.

The Policy/ of Stoicism and Epicureanism represent two distinct philosophical approaches available to your kittens’ civilization, primarily impacting the management of luxury resources and Happiness. These choices, unlocked after researching Philosophy, determine subsequent policy options in the Philosophy category.

Here is a comparison of the two Policy/ based on the source material:

Stoicism

The Stoicism policy focuses on endurance and restraint regarding consumption.

  • Description: The stoics teach that your civilization ought to endure hardship without complaint.
  • Effect: Stoicism halves the consumption of luxury resources. Luxury resources include Furs, Ivory, and Spice.
  • Other Impact: It also introduces a -25% reduction in Brewery consumption.
  • Subsequent Policy/: Stoicism leads to Frugality and Rationing Policy/.
    • Frugality improves Mints’ resource production by 10%.
    • Rationing makes hunting more effective (+0.1 Hunting bonus) and reduces the catnip consumption increase per happiness by 10%.

Epicureanism

Epicureanism emphasizes pleasure as the highest good, leveraging luxury resources for increased satisfaction and production bonuses.

  • Description: Epicureans believe that pleasure is the highest good.
  • Effect: Luxury resources provide slightly more happiness, increasing the bonus from 10% to 11% each.
  • Subsequent Policy/: Epicureanism leads to Carnivale and Extravagance Policy/.
    • Extravagance triples luxury consumption (200% increase) but dramatically boosts happiness derived from consumable resources to 5 (instead of 11%).
    • Carnivale boosts kitten arrival speed during festivals (30% increase) but also increases luxury consumption during them (30% increase).

Strategic Considerations

Guidance from experts in the sources suggests that the preferred choice often depends on the state of your resource production:

  • Epicureanism (Epi) is generally preferred because the extra happiness provides an overall production boost. Happiness dictates the overall efficiency of your Kittens in their work; the happier they are, the better the results of their labor.
  • By the time this policy is unlocked, players should ideally have established robust Hunting operations and sufficient Tradeposts to slow down the consumption of luxury items, reducing the need for the consumption mitigation offered by Stoicism.
  • Stoicism (and its associated Policy/) is considered if you are struggling to keep up with luxury resource demands. If consumption is outpacing a fully upgraded hunting team and tradepost effects, Stoicism, or its subsequent Policy/ like Rationing, may be necessary to control costs and maintain happiness levels.

In short, Epicureanism favours maximising output via happiness, while Stoicism favours optimising input via consumption reduction.

item.title: Machinery vs Steel
item.description:
The choice between researching Machinery versus Steel in Kittens Game involves prioritizing different aspects of technological advancement and economic development during the mid-game phase, after researching Writing.

Machinery and Steel are considered “specialist Techs that won’t help you much right now” when Philosophy is the immediate priority to continue down the path of new science Techs like Theology. However, both are important for long-term growth.

Here is a comparison of the two technologies based on the sources:
item.content:encoded:
The choice between researching Machinery versus Steel in Kittens Game involves prioritizing different aspects of technological advancement and economic development during the mid-game phase, after researching Writing.

Machinery and Steel are considered “specialist Techs that won’t help you much right now” when Philosophy is the immediate priority to continue down the path of new science Techs like Theology. However, both are important for long-term growth.

Here is a comparison of the two technologies based on the sources:

Steel Technology

  • Cost and Prerequisite: Steel costs 12,000 Science and is unlocked by Writing.
  • Effect/Unlocks:
    • It enables the resource Steel, which is crafted from 100 Iron and 100 Coal.
    • It unlocks several key Workshop Upgrades, including:
      • Steel Axe (50% more effective Woodcutters).
      • Reinforced Warehouses (25% more storage for various resources).
      • Coal Furnace (Smelters produce 0.005 coal/tick while burning wood).
      • Deep Mining (Mines produce 0.003 coal/tick).
      • High Pressure Engine (reduces Steamworks coal consumption by 20%).
      • Steel Armour (Hunting bonus +0.5).
  • Strategic Importance: A general strategy suggests starting with Steel to get some useful upgrades that make your economy stronger. Acquiring Steel allows you to craft Steel, a composite part needed for Gears and complex machinery. You will need Steel later for construction, such as building Lumber Mills (which require Iron, and are needed to increase Wood output).

Machinery Technology

  • Cost and Prerequisite: Machinery costs 15,000 Science and is unlocked by Writing.
  • Effect/Unlocks:
    • It unlocks the Steamworks building.
    • It unlocks Workshop Upgrades, including:
      • Printing Press (Steamworks automatically prints manuscripts).
      • Workshop Automation (Steamworks converts small quantities of wood/minerals to beams/slabs annually if resource is near cap).
      • Crossbow (25% boost to catpower production from Hunters).
  • Strategic Importance: Machinery is valuable because it unlocks Steamworks. Steamworks consumes Coal to produce various handy items, including Manuscripts via the Printing Press upgrade. Acquiring Machinery allows for a way to automatically make manuscripts, and provides a hunting upgrade.

Strategic Takeaways

  1. Prioritization: It is suggested to research Steel first to boost economic efficiency via storage and production upgrades, then Machinery for automation and manuscript generation, before finally tackling Philosophy for Temples and Theology.
  2. Manufacturing: Steel is a necessary material for creating Gears. Gears, along with Steel and a Blueprint, are required to build a Steamworks, which is unlocked by Machinery.
  3. Manuscripts: While Philosophy leads to Theology (which requires Manuscripts), Steamworks (unlocked by Machinery) can automate manuscript production via the Printing Press upgrade.

In essence, Steel provides necessary structural components and early resource bonuses, while Machinery unlocks advanced automation and specialized buildings (Steamworks).

item.title: Trading
item.description:
The decision of when is a good time to trade in Kittens Game depends heavily on your current stage of progression, what specific resource you need, and which civilization you are trading with.

Here is a comprehensive breakdown of trading timelines and strategic considerations:

Early Game Trading (After Year 20)

You can begin trading early, as the Trade tab unlocks after 20 years of gameplay when a Lizard arrives, offering to trade Wood for Minerals. This can be decreased to Year 5 if you have more than 0 Karma, and even to Year 1 with the Diplomacy Metaphysics upgrade.
item.content:encoded:
The decision of when is a good time to trade in Kittens Game depends heavily on your current stage of progression, what specific resource you need, and which civilization you are trading with.

Here is a comprehensive breakdown of trading timelines and strategic considerations:

Early Game Trading (After Year 20)

You can begin trading early, as the Trade tab unlocks after 20 years of gameplay when a Lizard arrives, offering to trade Wood for Minerals. This can be decreased to Year 5 if you have more than 0 Karma, and even to Year 1 with the Diplomacy Metaphysics upgrade.

Trading is immediately useful for:

  • Acquiring needed starting resources: For example, Lizards sell Wood for Minerals.
  • Hunting for Blueprints: Any successful trade has a 10% chance of including one Blueprint as an extra resource. This is fixed and cannot be increased by other trade bonuses. Because Blueprints have an incredibly steep production cost, players are advised to keep Trading until they “luck out and get a Blueprints for free”.
  • Acquiring Spice: Spice (a luxury resource) has a 35% chance of being included in a successful trade.

You must first create Gold before you can trade with anyone, which is accomplished by developing the Gold Ore upgrade in the Workshop.

Mid-to-Late Game Trading (Titanium and Blueprint Acquisition)

Trading becomes central during the mid-game, particularly in the Titanium era (after researching Astronomy and Navigation).

  • Trading for Titanium and Iron (Zebras):

    • Once you learn Navigation and build Trade Ships (which require Starcharts), you can Send Explorers to discover additional civilizations, including the hostile Zebras.
    • Zebras trade Slabs for Titanium and Iron.
    • The focus becomes trading with Zebras non-stop to acquire Titanium and Iron.
    • This is especially important in the Concrete era, where Blueprint requirements for sciences start becoming a bottleneck. Trading allows you to stockpile blueprints while also acquiring titanium and steel.

  • Trading for Minerals/Automation (Nagas and Griffins):

    • Nagas are discovered once you achieve 1500 Culture Cap. They sell Minerals for Ivory. This trade can be used in a loop: trading Ivory for Minerals, then putting Minerals back into Smelters to produce Gold, which is needed for trade costs and other buildings.
    • The sources also suggest a trading loop involving Sharks and Griffins to collect Wood, Steel, Gears, and Blueprints for Steamworks.

Seasonal Considerations (Optimizing Trade Timing)

Trade rates are affected by seasons, making it optimal to trade certain resources during specific times of the year:

Race/Resource Season for Optimal Trade Modifier Strategic Note
Lizards (Wood) Summer +35% (Also good in Autumn: +15%, and Winter: +5%) Wood is generally useful for construction.
Sharks (Catnip) Winter +45% (Also good in Spring: +20%, and Autumn: +15%) Good for supplementing food supply, especially during harsh winters.
Griffins (Iron) Autumn +35% Useful for supporting Smelters and Steel production.
Nagas (Minerals) Spring +25% Useful for early building materials and supporting Smelters. The guide suggests trading with Nagas only in Spring.
Zebras (Iron) Summer +15% Zebras generally buy Slabs, making them an import source for Iron and Titanium.
Zebras (Plate) Winter +25% (Also good in Spring/Autumn: +5%) Plate is important for advanced storage (Harbours).
Spiders (Coal) Autumn +15% Useful for powering industrial buildings.

End-Game Trading (Blueprints and Final Push)

In the end-game, trading remains the fastest way to acquire large amounts of Blueprints and facilitates rapid resets:

  • Fastest Reset Method: Trading becomes the fastest reset possible once you have a massive Catpower stockpile. You can trade, acquire necessary Blueprints (which are needed for Chronospheres), and reset rapidly.
  • Leviathans (Relics and Time Crystals): Once you acquire a Black Pyramid, Leviathans appear and trade Unobtainium for advanced resources like Time Crystals, Relics, and Sorrow. This trade has no seasonal adjustment.

In summary, you should start trading as soon as you meet the prerequisites (Gold and Currency technology), prioritize it in the Titanium era to secure Blueprints and Titanium from Zebras, and time your trades with Nagas, Griffins, and Sharks according to the seasons to maximize resource returns.

Trading often acts as a supply chain bridge, like using a freight train to move large quantities of bulk goods needed for heavy industry, rather than trying to hand-carry every component.

How Tradeposts Affect the TradeRatio

Tradeposts affect the {TradeRatio} through three distinct mechanisms:

A. Direct Building Effect (Base Trade Ratio) Each built Tradepost (tradepost.val) adds to the global building effect tradeRatio.

Bonus per Tradepost: +0.015 (or +1.5%) Formula contribution: {Base Tradeposts Bonus} = 0.015 * {Number of Tradeposts}$$

B. Synergy with Policies (Phantom Tradeposts)

The diplomatic policy bonus (calculateTradeBonusFromPolicies) treats certain policy effects as “phantom tradeposts” that are multiplied by the base tradepost efficiency 0.015.

Formula:{Policy Bonus} = 0.015 * {PhantomTradeposts}

Phantom Tradepost Sources (for non-zebra races like Leviathans):

  • Liberalism: +10 Phantom Tradeposts
  • Outer Space Treaty: +10 Phantom Tradeposts
  • Zebra Relations Bellicosity: +5 Phantom Tradeposts
  • Max Contribution: Up to +0.375 (+37.5%) to {TradeRatio} from policies.

Note: The number of physically built Tradeposts does not scale this policy bonus; it only utilizes the base tradepost multiplier coefficient of 0.015.

C. Pacifism Challenge Completion Synergy

If the Pacifism challenge has been completed one or more times, it unlocks a permanent trade ratio bonus when the challenge is inactive:

{Pacifism Bonus} = 0.015 * \min\Big({TradepostLimit}, {Number of Tradeposts} * {TradepostRatioLimit}\Big)

Where:

{TradeKnowledge}: Typically 1.0 per completion of the Pacifism challenge.

{TradepostLimit}: (7 + 3 * {TradeKnowledge}) * (0.99 + 0.01 * {TradeKnowledge})

{TradepostRatioLimit}$: A diminishing returns factor capped at 0.25.

This means completed Pacifism runs directly scale the efficiency of your built Tradeposts, allowing your physical Tradepost count to provide an extra multiplicative boost to the {TradeRatio}.

item.title: Antimatter
item.description:
Antimatter is a high-tier late-game resource in Kittens Game that serves as the primary currency for the Relic Era and advanced space engineering. It is a non-crafted resource, meaning a portion of it can be preserved across resets if you possess Chronospheres.

Acquisition and Production

Antimatter is primarily generated through orbital infrastructure in the Helios system:

  • Unlocking: It requires the Superconductors technology (225k Science, 175 Blueprints) to access the Antimatter science node, which costs 500k Science and 1 Relic.
  • Sunlifters: These are the primary source of production. Each Sunlifter produces 1 antimatter per year.
  • The Energy Prerequisite: Antimatter production only occurs if your colony has a positive energy surplus. If energy is negative, Sunlifters will not generate antimatter.
  • Temporal Acceleration: Because standard production is tied to the game year (which lasts roughly 13 minutes and 20 seconds), players often use the Chronoforge to combust/shatter Time Crystals. Each shatter advances the calendar to the next year, triggering an immediate antimatter deposit.

Storage and Capacity Milestones

The default storage capacity for antimatter is 100 units. Expanding this cap is mandatory for high-level progression:
item.content:encoded:
Antimatter is a high-tier late-game resource in Kittens Game that serves as the primary currency for the Relic Era and advanced space engineering. It is a non-crafted resource, meaning a portion of it can be preserved across resets if you possess Chronospheres.

Acquisition and Production

Antimatter is primarily generated through orbital infrastructure in the Helios system:

  • Unlocking: It requires the Superconductors technology (225k Science, 175 Blueprints) to access the Antimatter science node, which costs 500k Science and 1 Relic.
  • Sunlifters: These are the primary source of production. Each Sunlifter produces 1 antimatter per year.
  • The Energy Prerequisite: Antimatter production only occurs if your colony has a positive energy surplus. If energy is negative, Sunlifters will not generate antimatter.
  • Temporal Acceleration: Because standard production is tied to the game year (which lasts roughly 13 minutes and 20 seconds), players often use the Chronoforge to combust/shatter Time Crystals. Each shatter advances the calendar to the next year, triggering an immediate antimatter deposit.

Storage and Capacity Milestones

The default storage capacity for antimatter is 100 units. Expanding this cap is mandatory for high-level progression:

  • Containment Chambers: Constructed in the Kairo system, these provide +100 max antimatter each, but consume a heavy 50 Watts of energy.
  • Heatsinks: These increase the storage effectiveness of Containment Chambers by +2% per building.
  • The 5,000 Cap Goal: A major strategic milestone is reaching a 5,000 unit capacity, which is the cost of a Relic Station. To achieve this, a typical configuration requires approximately 34 Heatsinks and 29 Containment Chambers, supported by significant Paragon levels. If your maximum antimatter is below 5,000, your relic production efficiency is reduced proportionally.

Primary Uses

Antimatter is essential for transitioning into the endgame “Relic Engine” and optimizing space travel:

  • Relic Era Infrastructure: It is the core requirement for Relic Stations (5,000 AM) and Space Beacons (50 AM), which automate the generation of Relics.
  • Quantum Computing: Entanglement Stations, which generate hashes for cryptographical attacks on the elders, cost 5,250 AM.
  • AI and Automation: It is required to build AI Cores (125 AM) and purchase the Machine Learning upgrade (125 AM).
  • Space Upgrades: Advanced space missions and structures depend on it, including Terraforming Stations (25 AM), Tectonics (500 AM), and Antimatter Drives (125 AM).
  • Reactor Enhancements: It is used to upgrade standard infrastructure, such as Advanced AM Reactors (1,750 AM) and Void Reactors (2,500 AM).

Strategic Considerations

During the late game, players often engage in a “Seed Run”—a very long game session focused specifically on maximizing energy and containment to build a massive antimatter and void stockpile. Once the cap is high enough, you can perform Positive Resets with 70+ Chronospheres to exponentially grow your antimatter reserves across subsequent runs. To maximize production during these loops, players often turn off Thorium Reactors except when actively time-skipping to ensure the energy surplus remains positive for antimatter generation.

item.title: Alicorn
item.description:
Alicorns are a unique, late-game resource in Kittens Game, categorized as a Unique Resource. They are crucial for progressing into the Time Crystal era of the game.

Here is a detailed overview of their mechanics, acquisition, and uses:

1. Resource Type and Persistence

Alicorns are classified as a Luxury Resource, which means they are always lost upon reset (along with Furs, Ivory, and Unicorns) [1, 2].

2. Acquisition and Production

Alicorns are not produced by standard jobs or early buildings; they are acquired through late-game religious structures and rare events:
item.content:encoded:
Alicorns are a unique, late-game resource in Kittens Game, categorized as a Unique Resource. They are crucial for progressing into the Time Crystal era of the game.

Here is a detailed overview of their mechanics, acquisition, and uses:

1. Resource Type and Persistence

Alicorns are classified as a Luxury Resource, which means they are always lost upon reset (along with Furs, Ivory, and Unicorns) [1, 2].

2. Acquisition and Production

Alicorns are not produced by standard jobs or early buildings; they are acquired through late-game religious structures and rare events:

  • Sky Palaces: This religious building, which requires Tears, Ivory, and Megalith to construct, is the main way to gain Alicorns [3].
    • Building a Sky Palace enables a random event that grants one Alicorn, and each palace increases the frequency of this event by $0.01%$ per game-day [3].
    • Sky Palaces also passively produce $0.00002$ alicorns per tick ($0.08$ per year) [3].
  • Unicorn Utopia: This subsequent unicorn religious upgrade improves alicorn summon chance by $0.015%$ per game-day and increases passive production to $0.000025$ alicorns per tick [4].
  • Pacifism Challenge Reward: Completing the Pacifism challenge provides an increasing reward, including a $+10%$ Alicorn chance per completion (up to $120%$) and a $10%$ increase to Alicorn per tick production (with no diminishing returns) [5].

3. Primary Uses and Conversion

Alicorns are primarily consumed to generate Time Crystals (TC), a valuable prestige resource:

  • Sacrifice for Time Crystals: You can Sacrifice 25 Alicorns to receive 1 Time Crystal [6].
    • The conversion ratio is improved by the religious upgrades Unicorn Utopia (+5%) and Sunspire (+10%) [4, 6].
    • The act is described as “Banish the alicorns to the Bloodmoon” [6].
  • Resource Retrieval Strategy: In the end game, acquiring enough levels of the Resource Retrieval upgrade means shattering a Time Crystal will yield enough unobtainium and alicorns to allow the player to Civilisations/sacrifice immediately for new Time Crystals, sustaining the flow of this resource [7].

4. Consumption and Corruption

Alicorns are consumed or corrupted in three ways:

  • Necrocorn Corruption: The religious building Marker starts a process that slowly changes alicorns into Necrocorns [1, 8].
  • Unicorn Necropolis: The Unicorn Necropolis building, an advanced religious structure, requires 100 Alicorn (along with Necrocorn, Megalith, and Void) [9].
  • Ivory Temple Consumption: The Ivory Temple, a building related to Zebras, consumes $0.00002$ alicorns per tick while converting Ivory to Minerals [10].

In terms of strategy, it is advised to conserve your alicorn supply until the “last moment” to maximize the Time Crystal conversion ratio, particularly during a final run before a reset [11].

item.title: Cat Power
item.description:
Based on the sources, Catpower (a special resource generated by the Hunter profession [1, 2]) is reduced primarily through its consumption by game mechanics, including hunting, trade, and certain buildings.

Here are the specific actions and costs that reduce your Catpower:

1. Consumption for Hunting

The primary and initial use of Catpower is for hunting:

  • Each time you initiate a hunt (after researching Archery), it costs 100 Catpower [2, 3].
  • Hunting allows you the chance to gather rare resources like Furs and Ivory [3, 4].

2. Consumption for Trade and Exploration

Catpower is necessary for diplomatic actions and trade:
item.content:encoded:
Based on the sources, Catpower (a special resource generated by the Hunter profession [1, 2]) is reduced primarily through its consumption by game mechanics, including hunting, trade, and certain buildings.

Here are the specific actions and costs that reduce your Catpower:

1. Consumption for Hunting

The primary and initial use of Catpower is for hunting:

  • Each time you initiate a hunt (after researching Archery), it costs 100 Catpower [2, 3].
  • Hunting allows you the chance to gather rare resources like Furs and Ivory [3, 4].

2. Consumption for Trade and Exploration

Catpower is necessary for diplomatic actions and trade:

  • Exploring: Sending explorers to find new races costs 1,000 Catpower [5, 6].
    • If no trading partner is found during the exploration attempt, 950 Catpower is refunded (in the web version of the game) [5, 6].
  • Trading: Diplomacy is a Policy option that, if chosen, makes trades cheaper in terms of Catpower, reducing the cost by 5 Catpower per trade [7]. (The standard cost per trade is not explicitly stated in Catpower units, but the diplomacy policy affects it [7]).

3. Consumption by Buildings

One building consumes Catpower passively while active:

  • Mint: The Mint building, unlocked by researching Architecture [8], consumes Catpower at a rate of $0.75$ per tick [9].

4. Challenge Restriction

In addition to consumption, the maximum available Catpower can be reduced by challenges:

  • Atheism Challenge (Increasing Challenge): For each completion of the Atheism challenge after the first run, the maximum Catpower will decrease by 125 [10].

Summary of Catpower Management

Catpower is a vital early-game resource for obtaining luxury items (furs, ivory, unicorns) [4, 11, 12] and for finding new trade partners [5]. High Catpower limits are necessary for purchasing certain religion upgrades like Templars, which increase Max Catpower by 75 per Temple [13]. Therefore, actions that consume Catpower should be balanced by its production through Hunters (+$0.06$ per tick).

item.title: Coal
item.description:
Coal is a Common Resource in Kittens Game that is essential for progressing into the industrial phase of the game.

Here is a comprehensive overview of how Coal is produced, its strategic importance, and its consumption:

Acquisition and Production

Coal production is unlocked after researching the Steel technology. Once unlocked, Coal can be generated in several ways:

  1. Mines (Deep Mining Upgrade): The Deep Mining upgrade, unlocked by Steel, allows Mines to produce Coal.

    • Mines produce Coal at a rate of 0.003 Coal per tick (0.015 per second).
    • This upgrade requires 5,000 Science, 1,200 Iron, and 50 Beam.

  2. Smelters (Coal Furnace Upgrade): The Coal Furnace upgrade, also unlocked by Steel, enables Smelters to produce Coal.

    • Smelters produce Coal at a rate of 0.005 Coal per tick (0.025 per second) while burning wood.
    • This upgrade costs 5,000 Science, 5,000 Minerals, 2,000 Iron, and 35 Beam.

  3. Geologists (Job): The Geologist job, unlocked by the Geology technology, directly generates Coal at a rate of 0.015 per tick.

    • The Mining Drill upgrade further boosts Geologist Coal production by 0.01 Coal per tick (0.05/sec).
    • The Unobtainium Drill upgrade provides an additional boost of 0.015 Coal per tick (0.075/sec).

  4. Quarries: The Quarry building, unlocked by Geology, automatically produces Coal at a rate of 0.015 Coal per tick.

  5. Trading (Spiders): Coal can be acquired by trading Scaffolds with Spiders.

    • Spiders sell 350 Coal per trade.
    • Spiders are a Friendly civilization (+15% trade bonus) and are unlocked once you have 100 Trade Ships and 125k Max Science.
    • Trade with Spiders for Coal is optimally performed during Autumn (+15% amount modifier).

  6. Production Multipliers: The Pyrolysis Workshop upgrade boosts general Coal output by 20%, though this bonus does not apply to Smelters.

    • This upgrade requires 5,000 Science, 1,200 Iron, and 50 Beam.
