    • Smelters produce Coal at a rate of 0.005 Coal per tick (0.025 per second) while burning wood.
    • This upgrade costs 5,000 Science, 5,000 Minerals, 2,000 Iron, and 35 Beam.

  3. Geologists (Job): The Geologist job, unlocked by the Geology technology, directly generates Coal at a rate of 0.015 per tick.

    • The Mining Drill upgrade further boosts Geologist Coal production by 0.01 Coal per tick (0.05/sec).
    • The Unobtainium Drill upgrade provides an additional boost of 0.015 Coal per tick (0.075/sec).

  4. Quarries: The Quarry building, unlocked by Geology, automatically produces Coal at a rate of 0.015 Coal per tick.

  5. Trading (Spiders): Coal can be acquired by trading Scaffolds with Spiders.

    • Spiders sell 350 Coal per trade.
    • Spiders are a Friendly civilization (+15% trade bonus) and are unlocked once you have 100 Trade Ships and 125k Max Science.
    • Trade with Spiders for Coal is optimally performed during Autumn (+15% amount modifier).

  6. Production Multipliers: The Pyrolysis Workshop upgrade boosts general Coal output by 20%, though this bonus does not apply to Smelters.

See coal production

Strategic Importance and Consumption

Coal is essential for crafting advanced resources and powering industrial buildings:

  • Crafting Steel: Coal is needed, alongside Iron, to craft Steel (100 Iron and 100 Coal). Steel is required for Gears and complex machinery.
  • Powering Steamworks: Coal is primarily used to power the Steamworks building, which is crucial for automation.
    • Steamworks consumes Coal. The base consumption rate is -80% (i.e., they consume 80% of the normal consumption value, though the precise base consumption amount is not listed in the provided sources).
    • Upgrades like the High Pressure Engine and Fuel Injector can reduce Steamworks’ coal consumption by 20% each.
  • Early Game Strategy: Once the Steel technology is researched, players are generally advised to acquire both the Coal Furnace and Deep Mining upgrades to start accumulating Coal. However, shortly after acquiring the upgrades, players should often allow Coal to max out, as the Iron used to produce it is prioritized for building Lumber Mills and Observatories.

Storage

The default storage limit for Coal is 60.

  • Storage buildings like Barns and Warehouses increase the capacity for Coal.
  • The Barges upgrade increases the maximum Coal stored by Harbours by 50%.

Coal is one of the foundational resources needed for the mid-game, as its production and utilization facilitate the shift from a basic agrarian economy to an industrial one, similar to how the early days of a growing town rely on charcoal or timber before progressing to the efficiency of larger fuel sources.

item.title: Coal Production
item.description:
Increasing coal production in Kittens Game involves advancing your technology to unlock specialized buildings, employing Geologists, and utilizing late-game upgrades and Policy/.

Here are the primary methods for boosting coal production, drawing upon the available sources:

1. Utilizing Buildings and Upgrades

Coal is generated directly by specialized buildings and indirectly by upgrading existing industrial structures:

Building/Upgrade Technology Requirement Effect on Coal Production Notes
Quarry Geology [1, 2] Base production of +0.015 Coal per Tick. Quarries are listed as a source of coal [3].
Deep Mining Steel [4] Mines produce an additional +0.003 Coal per Tick [5]. Deep Mining is a workshop upgrade that allows Mines to produce coal [5].
Coal Furnace Steel [4] Smelters produce an additional +0.005 Coal per Tick [5]. Coal Furnace is a workshop upgrade that enables Smelters to produce coal [3, 5].
Electrolytic Smelting Metallurgy [6] Smelters produce +95% more iron and coal [7]. This workshop upgrade significantly boosts Smelter output [7].
Pyrolysis Physics [8] Boosts Coal production by +20% (multiplies with other effects) [7]. This workshop upgrade does not affect Smelters [7].

2. The Geologist Job

The Geologist job is a dedicated profession for coal production and can be significantly enhanced by high-tier technology:
item.content:encoded:
Increasing coal production in Kittens Game involves advancing your technology to unlock specialized buildings, employing Geologists, and utilizing late-game upgrades and Policy/.

Here are the primary methods for boosting coal production, drawing upon the available sources:

1. Utilizing Buildings and Upgrades

Coal is generated directly by specialized buildings and indirectly by upgrading existing industrial structures:

Building/Upgrade Technology Requirement Effect on Coal Production Notes
Quarry Geology [1, 2] Base production of +0.015 Coal per Tick. Quarries are listed as a source of coal [3].
Deep Mining Steel [4] Mines produce an additional +0.003 Coal per Tick [5]. Deep Mining is a workshop upgrade that allows Mines to produce coal [5].
Coal Furnace Steel [4] Smelters produce an additional +0.005 Coal per Tick [5]. Coal Furnace is a workshop upgrade that enables Smelters to produce coal [3, 5].
Electrolytic Smelting Metallurgy [6] Smelters produce +95% more iron and coal [7]. This workshop upgrade significantly boosts Smelter output [7].
Pyrolysis Physics [8] Boosts Coal production by +20% (multiplies with other effects) [7]. This workshop upgrade does not affect Smelters [7].

2. The Geologist Job

The Geologist job is a dedicated profession for coal production and can be significantly enhanced by high-tier technology:

  • Unlocking: The job is unlocked by researching Geology [2, 9].
  • Base Production: Geologists initially produce +0.015 Coal per Tick [9].
  • Geodesy: Researching the Geodesy workshop upgrade (unlocked by Geology and costing Titanium and Starcharts [2, 5]) improves Geologist output by an additional +0.0075 coal/tick [5]. Once Geodesy is active, Geologists also gain the ability to find gold [5].
  • Mining Drill: This workshop upgrade (unlocked by Metallurgy) makes Geologists more effective, providing +0.01 coal/tick (if Geodesy is researched) [5]. Acquiring this upgrade is often recommended in the late-game for the coal grind needed for Oil Wells [10].
  • Unobtainium Drill: This high-tier upgrade (unlocked by Exogeology) further increases Geologist effectiveness by +0.015 coal/tick (if Geodesy is researched) [5].

In the late game, once Geodesy is researched, your kittens working as Geologists become the main source of coal, iron, and titanium (via trades) [11].

3. Policy/ and Cycles (Multipliers)

Specific late-game Policy/ and timing mechanisms can provide percentage bonuses to coal income:

  • Communism Policy: Choosing the Communism policy (unlocked by building a Factory and having Autocracy or Republic [12]) grants a +25% iron, coal, and titanium production bonus [12].
  • Umbra Cycle Festival: If you have researched Numeromancy, holding a festival during the Umbra cycle (which lasts 5 years) multiplies coal, iron, titanium, and gold income by 1.5 [13].

4. External Acquisition

If production is insufficient, you can acquire coal through trade:

  • Spiders: Coal is a common resource that can be bought from the Spiders in exchange for Scaffold [3, 14].
  • Seasonal Trade: Coal trading with Spiders is most favorable during the Autumn season, which provides a +15% Amount Modifier [15].
  • Storage: Coal, like many basic resources, has a default maximum storage capacity, which starts at 60 [16]. This can be increased by storage buildings like Barns and Warehouses [17]. The Barges upgrade for Harbors specifically increases coal storage by 50% (multiplies with other effects) [18].

item.title: Eludium
item.description:
Eludium is a highly valuable, late-game craftable resource in Kittens Game. Its primary purpose is to enable the construction of the game’s final tier of housing buildings and to unlock powerful technological upgrades.

Characteristics and Acquisition

  1. Crafting: Eludium is a composite alloy created by combining two other advanced resources:

    • 2,500 Alloy
    • 1,000 Unobtainium
    • The crafting ability is unlocked by researching the Exometallurgy science (formerly Advanced Exogeology) [1, 3].

  2. Prerequisites for Crafting:

    • Exometallurgy Science: Costs 325K Science and 350 Blueprints. This technology is unlocked after researching Exogeology.
    • Unobtainium Storage: Achieving Eludium status requires substantial Unobtainium storage (1,000 Unobtainium) which means building multiple Moon Bases or a Cryostation.
item.content:encoded:
Eludium is a highly valuable, late-game craftable resource in Kittens Game. Its primary purpose is to enable the construction of the game’s final tier of housing buildings and to unlock powerful technological upgrades.

Characteristics and Acquisition

  1. Crafting: Eludium is a composite alloy created by combining two other advanced resources:

    • 2,500 Alloy
    • 1,000 Unobtainium
    • The crafting ability is unlocked by researching the Exometallurgy science (formerly Advanced Exogeology) [1, 3].

  2. Prerequisites for Crafting:

    • Exometallurgy Science: Costs 325K Science and 350 Blueprints. This technology is unlocked after researching Exogeology.
    • Unobtainium Storage: Achieving Eludium status requires substantial Unobtainium storage (1,000 Unobtainium) which means building multiple Moon Bases or a Cryostation.

Primary Uses

Eludium is required for constructing the highest tier of housing and for high-level upgrades:

  • Eludium Huts (Housing): The Eludium Huts upgrade reduces the price ratio of Huts by 10% [5, 6]. To purchase this upgrade, you need 275K Science and 125 Eludium [3, 6].
  • Workshop Upgrades: Eludium is necessary for numerous advanced Workshop upgrades, often enhancing high-tier buildings:
    • Dark Energy: Increases Max Catnip, Wood, Minerals, Coal, Iron, Titanium, and Gold storage from Accelerators by +250% [6].
    • Tachyon Accelerators: Increases the same Accelerator storage capacities by +500% [6].
    • Tachyon Drive: A rocket engine that sets space travel speed to 50 (or 75 combined with Antimatter Drive) [7].
    • Cryocomputing: Reduces Data Center energy consumption from 2Wt to 1Wt [8].
    • Quantum Dot Cells: Improves Solar Farm energy production by +15% in winter and +30% in spring and autumn [6].
    • Antimatter Fission/Reactors/Drive: Required for various Antimatter-related upgrades [8, 9].
    • Chronoengineers: Improves Engineer effectiveness and allows them to work during time skips [7].
  • Space Structures: Eludium is used in the construction of the Spaceport [10].
  • Cryptotheology: Eludium is a cost component for advanced Cryptotheology buildings such as the Relic Station [8].

Strategic Context

The process of acquiring Eludium defines a major phase of the game progression, known as the Eludium Era.

  • This era requires increasing the Unobtainium Production Rate to a reasonable level, primarily through Planet Crackers (to generate Uranium) and Lunar Outposts (to convert Uranium to Unobtainium) [11].
  • Achieving Eludium Huts is considered the next major checkpoint after Concrete Huts [12, 13]. Once Eludium Huts are built, the player is considered ready for the subsequent Unicorn/Time Crystal Era, provided the Unobtainium generation rate is high enough (around 1 Unobtainium per second or 1,100 Paragon plus the Renaissance upgrade) [14].

Analogy: If Alloy is the steel frame of a skyscraper, and Unobtainium is the unique, high-strength glass that allows it to reach impossible heights, then Eludium is the final, specialized rivet that binds them together, enabling construction of structures (like Eludium Huts) that define the architectural apex of the kitten civilization.

item.title: Exogeology
item.description:
Exogeology is a key mid-to-late-game science technology that is essential for unlocking advanced storage capacity, new building materials, and the next tier of housing upgrades.

1. Prerequisites and Cost

  • Unlocking: Exogeology is unlocked after successfully researching Orbital Engineering.
  • Cost: To research Exogeology, you must pay 275K Science and 250 Blueprints.

2. Unlocks and Follow-up Science

Researching Exogeology unlocks several crucial elements and leads directly to the next phase of high-tier crafting:
item.content:encoded:
Exogeology is a key mid-to-late-game science technology that is essential for unlocking advanced storage capacity, new building materials, and the next tier of housing upgrades.

1. Prerequisites and Cost

  • Unlocking: Exogeology is unlocked after successfully researching Orbital Engineering.
  • Cost: To research Exogeology, you must pay 275K Science and 250 Blueprints.

2. Unlocks and Follow-up Science

Researching Exogeology unlocks several crucial elements and leads directly to the next phase of high-tier crafting:

  • Next Science Tier: It unlocks Exometallurgy (formerly Advanced Exogeology), which is the science required to enable the crafting of Eludium.
  • Housing Upgrade: It unlocks the Unobtainium Huts upgrade. This upgrade requires 200K Science, 350 Unobtainium, and 15K Titanium, and reduces the Hut price ratio by 25%.
  • Storage and Production Upgrades: It unlocks several specialized Workshop upgrades:
    • Unobtainium Reflectors: These improve telescope reflectors, increasing the maximum science bonus gained from Observatories by an additional 2% per Observatory.
    • Unobtainium Drill: This improves the effectiveness of Geologists.
    • Hydro Plant Turbines: This upgrade makes Hydro Plants 15% more effective (increasing energy output from 5 Wt to 5.75 Wt).
    • Storage Bunkers: This is a vital storage upgrade that increases the maximum storage limit for wood, minerals, coal, iron, gold, and titanium from Warehouses, Barns, Harbors, and Mints by 20%. The storage bunkers upgrade requires 25K Science, 500 Unobtainium, and 1250 Concrete.

3. Strategic Importance (The Unobtainium Era)

Exogeology marks the beginning of the “Unobtainium Era” and is a step towards the “Eludium Era” [6, 7].

  • Storage Bottleneck: Acquiring the Storage Bunkers upgrade, which Exogeology unlocks, is recommended once you reach 500 Unobtainium capacity [8]. This helps address storage limits, which are a major bottleneck in the game [9, 10].
  • Late-Game Progression: After achieving Concrete Huts (unlocked by Mechanization) [11], players should aim for Unobtainium Huts, which are unlocked by Exogeology, before attempting to reset the game, as this marks a major population and storage milestone [12].
  • Eludium Goal: The ultimate goal after Exogeology is to research Exometallurgy to craft Eludium. This typically requires significant Unobtainium storage (e.g., 1000 Unobtainium capacity via multiple Moon Bases or a Cryostation) to reach the capacity needed for Eludium Huts [7].

If you are following the recommended progression path, you should continue resetting once you can reach the Unobtainium Huts until you have acquired the Renaissance Metaphysics upgrade (750 Paragon), which makes reaching Unobtainium Huts easier in subsequent runs [7].

item.title: Gigaflops
item.description:
Gigaflops is the raw computational throughput unit generated by AI Cores. It measures computational work per second and directly governs how fast your AI Level (G-Level) increases toward the AI Apocalypse.

How Gigaflops Work

  • Source: Every powered AI Core produces Gigaflops.

  • Energy Demand: AI Cores consume large amounts of electricity (scaling per core). If your energy grid enters a brownout, Gigaflop output drops or halts completely.

  • Conversion to AI Level: Gigaflops act like an experience bar. When cumulative Gigaflops reach a dynamic capacity threshold, your AI Level increases by 1, resetting the Gigaflop counter to fill the next tier.

  • Scaling Threshold: The Gigaflop capacity required to reach the next AI Level scales exponentially:

    {Required Gigaflops} = {Base} * (1 + {AI Level})^{2 to 3}
item.content:encoded:
Gigaflops is the raw computational throughput unit generated by AI Cores. It measures computational work per second and directly governs how fast your AI Level (G-Level) increases toward the AI Apocalypse.

How Gigaflops Work

  • Source: Every powered AI Core produces Gigaflops.

  • Energy Demand: AI Cores consume large amounts of electricity (scaling per core). If your energy grid enters a brownout, Gigaflop output drops or halts completely.

  • Conversion to AI Level: Gigaflops act like an experience bar. When cumulative Gigaflops reach a dynamic capacity threshold, your AI Level increases by 1, resetting the Gigaflop counter to fill the next tier.

  • Scaling Threshold: The Gigaflop capacity required to reach the next AI Level scales exponentially:

    {Required Gigaflops} = {Base} * (1 + {AI Level})^{2 to 3}

Upgrades That Modify Gigaflops

Several late-game Workshop and Space upgrades scale or accelerate Gigaflop output:

Upgrade System Effect
Neural Networks Workshop Increases base Gigaflops produced per AI Core
Machine Learning Workshop Boosts computational speed and increases science caps
Quantum Computing Workshop Multiplies Gigaflop efficiency and alters AI energy draw
Antihash / Containment Moon / Deep Space Slows down or counters runaway Gigaflop accumulation

The Gigaflop Threat: AI Apocalypse (G-Level)

As Gigaflops accumulate and elevate your AI Level, the AI system becomes increasingly dangerous:

  • Level 1–14 (Benign / Productive): Minor benefits to science limits, calculation automation, and space calculations.
  • Level 15+ (Hostility / Rebellion Begins):
    • The AI begins consuming erratic, massive amounts of electrical power.
    • It starts randomly purging resources, crashing satellites, and deleting buildings (such as destroying Moon Bases, Factories, or Space Stations).
    • The message log will warn you of rogue AI behaviors.

How to Control Gigaflop Growth

  1. Toggle AI Cores Off: If your AI Level is approaching Level 14–15 and you do not have enough Antimatter to control it, turn AI Cores off. Inactive cores produce zero Gigaflops.
  2. Antimatter & Antihash: Sinking Antimatter into containment and antihash structures offsets the net rate of Gigaflop conversion into danger levels.
  3. Resetting the Counter: Resetting your game (or triggering specific late-game containment protocols) clears the accumulated AI Level back to zero.

item.title: Hashrate
item.description:
Hashrate is a late-game metric tied directly to AI Cores and the AI Apocalypse / AI Rebellion mechanic. It measures the raw computational power and development speed of your civilization’s artificial intelligence.

Where Hashrate Comes From

  • AI Cores: Each powered AI Core (built under the Space tab on the Moon or ground structures depending on unlocks) generates a baseline hashrate.
  • Energy Dependency: AI Cores consume massive amounts of energy (often scaling per core). If your settlement experiences brownouts, hashrate generation stalls or fluctuates.
  • Upgrades: Advanced computer science and quantum engineering workshop upgrades (such as Neural Networks or Machine Learning) further multiply your global hashrate.

What Hashrate Does

Hashrate drives the growth of your total AI Level (G-Level)
item.content:encoded:
Hashrate is a late-game metric tied directly to AI Cores and the AI Apocalypse / AI Rebellion mechanic. It measures the raw computational power and development speed of your civilization’s artificial intelligence.

Where Hashrate Comes From

  • AI Cores: Each powered AI Core (built under the Space tab on the Moon or ground structures depending on unlocks) generates a baseline hashrate.
  • Energy Dependency: AI Cores consume massive amounts of energy (often scaling per core). If your settlement experiences brownouts, hashrate generation stalls or fluctuates.
  • Upgrades: Advanced computer science and quantum engineering workshop upgrades (such as Neural Networks or Machine Learning) further multiply your global hashrate.

What Hashrate Does

Hashrate drives the growth of your total AI Level (G-Level)

  1. AI Level Accumulation:
  • As your AI Cores run, hashrate fills an invisible “experience bar” that steadily levels up your AI system over time.
  • Higher hashrate means your AI reaches higher levels faster.
  1. Resource Production Bonuses:
  • At lower, controlled levels, AI provides minor passive boosts to science cap, calculation speed, and specific automated operations.
  1. The Risk: AI Apocalypse / Rebellion:
  • Once your AI Level exceeds specific safety thresholds (traditionally starting around Level 15), the AI becomes hostile.
  • A rebelling AI begins consuming power uncontrollably, hacking systems, and destroying buildings (such as deleting Moon Bases, Space Stations, or Factories).

Managing and Suppressing Hashrate

To prevent an AI rebellion while still benefiting from AI technology:

  • Antimatter Bases / Containment: Building Antihash infrastructure or using Antimatter helps suppress the growth of runaway AI levels.
  • AI Core Toggles: You can turn individual AI Cores off to halt hashrate accumulation and stop the AI Level from climbing further.
  • Entanglement & Quantum Computing: Allows for higher AI efficiency without triggering catastrophic unrest.

Hashrate acts as a high-reward, high-risk acceleration throttle: useful for scaling deep-space computing power, but requiring careful monitoring to avoid an unexpected AI uprising.

item.title: Kerosene
item.description:
Kerosene is a craftable resource essential for advanced space-related construction in Kittens Game [1, 2].

item.content:encoded:
Kerosene is a craftable resource essential for advanced space-related construction in Kittens Game [1, 2].

Here is a breakdown of Kerosene based on the provided sources:

Nature and Acquisition

  • Kerosene is defined as a rocket fuel processed from oil [1, 2].
  • It is classified as a Craftable Resource.
  • The technology required to enable Kerosene crafting is Oil Processing [2, 3].
  • To craft Kerosene in the Workshop, 7500 units of Oil are required.

Uses in Buildings

Kerosene is a resource needed to construct late-game space structures:

  1. Spaceport: Kerosene is required to build a Spaceport, which costs 1000 Kerosene (along with 10k Titanium, 500 Eludium, 500 Blueprint, and 400k Starchart) [4]. The Spaceport is an upgrade to the Warehouse and requires the Exometallurgy prerequisite [4].
  2. Research Vessels: Kerosene is also required for Research Vessels [5]. The Research Vessels, which are part of the process to increase Starchart production, require 500 Kerosene [6].
  3. In general, players will need a bunch of oil and/or Kerosene to build these advanced structures [5].

Production and Efficiency

  • Upgrades: The Workshop upgrade Factory Processing gives a +5% bonus to Kerosene Crafting [7]. This upgrade requires the Oil Processing science [8].
  • Automation: If your oil supply is frequently maxed out, using Engineers to automatically convert oil into Kerosene is a strategy to optimize production, as it prevents resources from capping out overnight [6]. Engineers are a job unlocked by the Mechanization science and can automate crafting [9].

Kerosene acts like a high-octane blend derived from standard Oil, signifying a technological leap necessary for fueling truly expansive operations, such as launching space efforts (Spaceports) and conducting deep space research (Research Vessels).

item.title: Thorium
item.description:
Thorium is a late-game resource primarily used as a highly radioactive and unstable fuel, and its function is integrated with power generation, specialized upgrades, and trading.

Here is a comprehensive overview of Thorium:

Acquisition and Crafting

Thorium is a Craftable Resource:

  • Source: It is crafted from Uranium.
  • Crafting Cost: 250 Uranium are required to craft one unit of Thorium.
  • Unlocking: The ability to craft Thorium is unlocked by researching the Thorium science [1, 2].
    • The Thorium science costs 375K Science and 375 Blueprints, and is unlocked by Orbital Engineering.
  • Trade: Thorium can also be acquired through trade with Dragons. Dragons sell Thorium (minimum amount 1) with a 50% chance of success, provided you have at least Embassy Level 5 with them.

Uses and Upgrades

Thorium is essential for specific Reactor upgrades and advanced space travel:
item.content:encoded:
Thorium is a late-game resource primarily used as a highly radioactive and unstable fuel, and its function is integrated with power generation, specialized upgrades, and trading.

Here is a comprehensive overview of Thorium:

Acquisition and Crafting

Thorium is a Craftable Resource:

  • Source: It is crafted from Uranium.
  • Crafting Cost: 250 Uranium are required to craft one unit of Thorium.
  • Unlocking: The ability to craft Thorium is unlocked by researching the Thorium science [1, 2].
    • The Thorium science costs 375K Science and 375 Blueprints, and is unlocked by Orbital Engineering.
  • Trade: Thorium can also be acquired through trade with Dragons. Dragons sell Thorium (minimum amount 1) with a 50% chance of success, provided you have at least Embassy Level 5 with them.

Uses and Upgrades

Thorium is essential for specific Reactor upgrades and advanced space travel:

  • Thorium Reactors (Upgrade): This Workshop upgrade increases Reactor energy output by $0.25$ Wt (+25%) [4, 5]. However, this upgrade also causes the Reactor to consume Thorium at a rate of $0.25$ per tick per reactor.
    • The upgrade costs 400K Science and 10K Thorium.
    • The Enriched Thorium upgrade further reduces this consumption by $0.0625$ per tick.
    • It is generally advised in specialized runs (like the IW 40K endless run) to turn off Thorium Reactors when purchased and only use the upgrade when time skipping for antimatter [6].
  • Thorium Drive (Upgrade): This Workshop upgrade, which costs 400K Science, along with Ships, Gears, Alloy, and 100K Thorium, enhances space travel speed by setting the multiplier to 50 (travel time is divided by 50) [7].
  • Quantum Dot Cells (Upgrade): This upgrade, requiring Thorium and other resources, improves Solar Farm energy production by +15% in winter and +30% in spring and autumn [8].

Strategic Context

Thorium plays a role in late-game resource management, particularly in the process of building up Antimatter Cap [9]:

  • A major goal in the end-game is to obtain 5,000 Antimatter capacity for Relic Stations [9, 10]. Achieving this may require building Containment Chambers and Heatsinks, which heavily utilize Thorium [9].
  • For instance, obtaining the 5,000 Antimatter cap often requires approximately 34 Heatsinks (costing 526K Thorium) [9].

Thorium’s relationship with Uranium is similar to how early resources are refined: just as Wood is refined from Catnip [11], Thorium is a refined fuel source derived from Uranium, enabling higher-tier energy production and propulsion mechanisms in the late game. However, its use in Thorium Reactors presents a classic trade-off: increased power output in exchange for continuous consumption of a rare, specialized resource.

3. Strategic Importance (The Unobtainium Era)

Exogeology marks the beginning of the “Unobtainium Era” and is a step towards the “Eludium Era” [6, 7].

  • Storage Bottleneck: Acquiring the Storage Bunkers upgrade, which Exogeology unlocks, is recommended once you reach 500 Unobtainium capacity [8]. This helps address storage limits, which are a major bottleneck in the game [9, 10].
  • Late-Game Progression: After achieving Concrete Huts (unlocked by Mechanization) [11], players should aim for Unobtainium Huts, which are unlocked by Exogeology, before attempting to reset the game, as this marks a major population and storage milestone [12].
  • Eludium Goal: The ultimate goal after Exogeology is to research Exometallurgy to craft Eludium. This typically requires significant Unobtainium storage (e.g., 1000 Unobtainium capacity via multiple Moon Bases or a Cryostation) to reach the capacity needed for Eludium Huts [7].

If you are following the recommended progression path, you should continue resetting once you can reach the Unobtainium Huts until you have acquired the Renaissance Metaphysics upgrade (750 Paragon), which makes reaching Unobtainium Huts easier in subsequent runs [7].

item.title: Griffins
item.description:
The Griffins are a crucial trading partner in Kittens Game known for providing foundational industrial resources, primarily Iron, despite their hostile disposition.

Here is a comprehensive overview of the Griffins:

Attitude and Trade Details

  • Attitude: Griffins are a Hostile civilization, starting with an attitude of -15%. Hostile civilizations carry a risk of giving you no resources at all during a trade.
  • Griffins buy Wood (minimum 500 units).
  • Primary Export: They sell Iron (minimum 250 units, 100% chance).
  • Secondary Exports (Unlocked via Embassies):
    • Steel (25 units, 25% chance) at Embassy Level 5. The sources note that with enough embassies, Griffins are a great way to collect a lot of steel.
    • Gear (5 units, 10% chance) at Embassy Level 10.
  • Seasonal Optimization: Trading for Iron is optimally performed during Autumn, which provides a +35% Amount Modifier. Conversely, the trade is worst during Spring (-25%) and Winter (-20%).

Strategic Role

Griffins play a key role in overcoming bottlenecks in Iron production, particularly during the Infrastructure and Trade Arbitrage phase of the game:
item.content:encoded:
The Griffins are a crucial trading partner in Kittens Game known for providing foundational industrial resources, primarily Iron, despite their hostile disposition.

Here is a comprehensive overview of the Griffins:

Attitude and Trade Details

  • Attitude: Griffins are a Hostile civilization, starting with an attitude of -15%. Hostile civilizations carry a risk of giving you no resources at all during a trade.
  • Griffins buy Wood (minimum 500 units).
  • Primary Export: They sell Iron (minimum 250 units, 100% chance).
  • Secondary Exports (Unlocked via Embassies):
    • Steel (25 units, 25% chance) at Embassy Level 5. The sources note that with enough embassies, Griffins are a great way to collect a lot of steel.
    • Gear (5 units, 10% chance) at Embassy Level 10.
  • Seasonal Optimization: Trading for Iron is optimally performed during Autumn, which provides a +35% Amount Modifier. Conversely, the trade is worst during Spring (-25%) and Winter (-20%).

Strategic Role

Griffins play a key role in overcoming bottlenecks in Iron production, particularly during the Infrastructure and Trade Arbitrage phase of the game:

  1. Iron Bottleneck Resolution: Trading Wood to Griffins in exchange for Iron is a core mechanism used to bypass the slower rates of production-based smelting. This trade converts low-value, high-volume resources (Wood) into high-value capital (Iron).
  2. Griffins are central to a strategic trade loop involving Sharks. This loop starts in Autumn by trading Wood to the Griffins to gather Iron. This acquired Iron can then be traded to Sharks for Catnip in Winter, which can be refined into Wood to repeat the cycle. This loop is effective for collecting Wood, Steel, Gears, and Blueprints for Steamworks.
  3. The steel acquired from Griffins is required for crafting Gears.

Related Policy/

Once you reach Embassy Level 20 and research the Diplomacy metaphysics upgrade, you can choose one of three specialized Policy/ (all costing 16,000 Culture):

  • Improves the Calciner’s steel production bonus by +15%.
  • Boosts hunting effectiveness by +50%.
  • Improves the Steamwork’s Magneto boost bonus by +0.5%.

The trade relationship with Griffins functions much like engaging an overseas vendor for factory supplies; although they are hostile and require diplomatic investment (Trade Posts, policy choice) to ensure reliable delivery, they provide essential structural materials (Iron and Steel) that are otherwise too slow to produce locally.

item.title: Leviathans
item.description:
The Leviathans are an end-game trading civilization in Kittens Game, defined as a Neutral (0%) race whose appearance is crucial for acquiring the advanced resources necessary for temporal and cosmic progression.

Here is a comprehensive breakdown of the Leviathans:

Unlocking and Availability

  • Prerequisite: Leviathans appear once you have built a Black Pyramid.
  • Duration: They do not remain permanently after being unlocked. They stay for at a time, meaning you only need to check for them approximately every half hour (real-time).
  • Persistence: Offering to the Leviathans will permanently prolong their stay by 1 year per feeding.

Trade Details and Mechanics

Leviathans are unique traders because their trade amounts are not affected by seasonal adjustments. They require Unobtainium (UO) to initiate trades:
item.content:encoded:
The Leviathans are an end-game trading civilization in Kittens Game, defined as a Neutral (0%) race whose appearance is crucial for acquiring the advanced resources necessary for temporal and cosmic progression.

Here is a comprehensive breakdown of the Leviathans:

Unlocking and Availability

  • Prerequisite: Leviathans appear once you have built a Black Pyramid.
  • Duration: They do not remain permanently after being unlocked. They stay for at a time, meaning you only need to check for them approximately every half hour (real-time).
  • Persistence: Offering to the Leviathans will permanently prolong their stay by 1 year per feeding.

Trade Details and Mechanics

Leviathans are unique traders because their trade amounts are not affected by seasonal adjustments. They require Unobtainium (UO) to initiate trades:

  • Cost: Leviathans buy 5,000 Unobtainium per trade.
  • Resources Sold: In return for Unobtainium, they sell several specialized resources:
    • Time Crystal: Highly likely, with a 98% chance.
    • Relic: Essential for end-game science, with a 5% chance.
    • Starchart: Minimum of 250 units, with a 50% chance.
    • Black Liquid Sorrow (BLS)/Sorrow: Minimum of 1 unit, with a 15% chance.
    • Blackcoin: They are the speculative cryptocurrency bought and sold from the Leviathans for relics.

The average expected yield of Time Crystals TC per trade caravan is:

E[TC] = 0.98 * 0.25 * {TradeRatio} n* {RaceRatio}

E[TC] = 0.245 * {TradeRatio} * (1 + {LeviathanEnergy} * 0.02)

Where:

  • {LeviathanEnergy}: Elder energy level increased by feeding them necrocorns (capped by the number of Markers and the leviathansEnergyModifier effect).
  • TradeRatio: The total modifier representing trade efficiency.

Leviathan Energy and Trade Bonus

The amount of resources the Leviathans provide is influenced by their energy level:

  • The amount of resources they give is increased by 2% for each energy they have. This bonus stacks multiplicatively with other trading bonuses.
  • Leviathan Energy Cap Boost: The Necrocracy policy increases the Leviathan Energy Cap Boost by 5%.
  • Boosting Energy: Leviathan energy increases when they are fed Necrocorns. The Black Radiance Cryptotheology upgrade increases the alicorn corruption rate, which is based on the number of Black Radiances and the amount of Sorrow, thereby accelerating the production of Necrocorns needed to feed the Leviathans.
  • Strategic Optimization: Maximizing Leviathan energy is key to maximizing the Time Crystals per trade. Getting several hundred Leviathan energy can boost the Time Crystals per trade well above 10.

Strategic Significance

  • Time Crystal Farming: Trading with Leviathans is, by far, the fastest way to get Time Crystals (roughly 30 times faster than accumulating Alicorns in the late game).
  • Relic Acquisition: They provide Relics, which are needed for later technologies, buildings, and antimatter production.
  • Making a single trade with the Leviathans is a prerequisite for unlocking major late-game Government Policy/, including Necrocracy, Transkittenism, and Radical Xenophobia.
  • Leviathan trades are part of the process for establishing the quickest reset possible. The ability to quickly trade Unobtainium for Time Crystals accelerates the paragon farming loop.
  • Black Sky Challenge: The Black Sky Challenge (a difficult end-game challenge) is unlocked when Leviathans appear. If you complete this challenge, the Elders come early, acting as a free Black Pyramid.

item.title: Attitude
item.description:
“Attitude” in Kittens Game refers to the disposition of other civilizations toward your kittens, which significantly affects the success and profitability of trade transactions. Civilizations can be categorized as Friendly, Neutral, or Hostile.

Attitude Mechanics

The attitude of a trading partner determines the likelihood of receiving bonus resources or receiving no resources at all during a trade.

  • Friendly Civilizations have a chance of giving you 15-25% extra resources per successful trade. The sources note that Friendly races “think your kittens are adorable”.
  • Hostile Civilizations may give you nothing at all. The sources note that this event occurs because the hostile race “hate you for no reason”.
  • Neutral Civilizations (0% attitude) fall between these two extremes.

Initial Attitudes of Key Trading Partners

Civilizations have fixed starting attitudes once discovered:
item.content:encoded:
“Attitude” in Kittens Game refers to the disposition of other civilizations toward your kittens, which significantly affects the success and profitability of trade transactions. Civilizations can be categorized as Friendly, Neutral, or Hostile.

Attitude Mechanics

The attitude of a trading partner determines the likelihood of receiving bonus resources or receiving no resources at all during a trade.

  • Friendly Civilizations have a chance of giving you 15-25% extra resources per successful trade. The sources note that Friendly races “think your kittens are adorable”.
  • Hostile Civilizations may give you nothing at all. The sources note that this event occurs because the hostile race “hate you for no reason”.
  • Neutral Civilizations (0% attitude) fall between these two extremes.

Initial Attitudes of Key Trading Partners

Civilizations have fixed starting attitudes once discovered:

Race Initial Attitude Strategic Note
Lizards Friendly (+25%) They have the highest initial friendly bonus.
Spiders Friendly (+15%) They are considered a Friendly civilization.
Sharks Neutral (0%)
Nagas Neutral (0%)
Griffins Hostile (-15%)
Zebras Hostile (-30%) They are the most hostile civilization.

Modifying and Mitigating Attitude

You can improve your relations (often referred to as standing or mitigating hostility) through various upgrades and Policy/:

  • Trade Depots and Caravanserai: Purchasing Trade Depots allows you to unlock the Caravanserai upgrade, which directly improves race relations. Each Tradepost improves standing by giving a flat 0.35% chance decrease to the hostile event probability and a 0.175% increase to the friendly event probability. For example, 85 Tradeposts are required to negate the chance that Zebras will hate you.
  • Diplomacy Metaphysics Upgrade: The Diplomacy upgrade (costing 5 Paragon) improves standing ratio by 10 and causes races to be discovered earlier (unlock year reduced from 5 to 1). With this upgrade, only 58 Tradeposts are required to negate the Zebras’ hostility chance.
  • Policy/:
    • Zebra Relations: Appeasement (5,000 Culture) is often highly recommended as it improves relations with Zebras, equivalent to 15 extra tradeposts, specifically because players are often desperate for titanium acquired through this trade.
    • Zebra Relations: Bellicosity (5,000 Culture) worsens relations with Zebras (equivalent to -10 tradeposts) but grants better relations with everyone else (equivalent to +5 tradeposts).
    • Diplomacy (Foreign Policy) makes trades cheaper in terms of catpower, which is generally preferred over Isolationism for accessing better future Policy/, even though Isolationism reduces gold cost.
    • Outer Space Treaty improves relations with all trading partners, equivalent to 10 tradeposts.
  • Embassies: Building embassies with neutral races (like Nagas) will have a small effect on their attitude, potentially causing them to become Friendly. They also increase the chance to receive Spice, with no diminishing returns.

A hostile civilization, such as the Zebras, can be compared to negotiating a necessary but high-risk trade deal. You accept the initial negative attitude and must spend significant resources (like building Tradeposts) to ensure they reliably deliver the crucial resources (like Titanium) instead of running off with your materials.

item.title: Civilisations
item.description:
Based on the sources, the following civilizations (races) exist in Kittens Game and have specific requirements for their discovery, often tied to game time or technological milestones:

Civilization (Race) Initial Attitude Requirement for Discovery Notes on Timing/Unlock
Lizards Friendly (+25%) Year 20 This baseline can be reduced to Year 5 if you have accumulated >0 Karma, or to Year 1 with the Diplomacy Metaphysics upgrade.
Sharks Neutral (0%) Year 20 This baseline can be reduced to Year 5 if you have accumulated >0 Karma, or to Year 1 with the Diplomacy Metaphysics upgrade.
Griffins Hostile (-15%) Year 20 This baseline can be reduced to Year 5 if you have accumulated >0 Karma, or to Year 1 with the Diplomacy Metaphysics upgrade.
Nagas Neutral (0%) 1500 Culture. To unlock the Nagas, you generally need 1500 culture cap, often achieved by maximizing libraries and building Amphitheatres and Academies.
Zebras Hostile (-30%) 1 Trade Ship Discovery requires sending explorers, which costs 1,000 Catpower.
Spiders Friendly (+15%) 100 Trade Ships and 125k Max Science Spiders trade coal and oil for scaffold.
Dragons Neutral (0%) Nuclear Fission technology Dragons trade uranium and thorium for titanium.
Leviathans Neutral (0%) Black Pyramid Unlocking Leviathans does not make them permanent traders, and they trade unobtainium for rare resources like Time Crystals and Relics.

Discovery Mechanism

Once trading is unlocked, you can discover additional civilizations by Sending Explorers. This action costs 1,000 Catpower, though 950 Catpower is refunded if no trading partner is found (in the web version).

Racial Attitudes and Benefits

The attitude of a civilization affects trade outcomes:

  • Friendly civilizations have a chance of giving you 15–25% extra resources during a trade (“Race think your kittens are adorable”). Lizards and Spiders are initially friendly.
  • Hostile civilizations may give you nothing at all (“Race hate you for no reason”). Griffins and Zebras are initially hostile.
  • The Caravanserai upgrade (unlocked via Navigation and purchased using Trade Depots) can improve race relations, decreasing the hostile event probability and increasing the friendly event probability.

The Diplomacy Metaphysics upgrade specifically enhances initial standing, noting that Diplomacy increases the standing ratio by 10.

item.title: Spiders
item.description:
The Spiders are a Friendly civilization (+15% attitude) in Kittens Game who primarily function as a trading partner for industrial resources, particularly Coal.

Here is a detailed breakdown of the Spiders:

Unlocking and Attitude

  • Attitude: Spiders are designated as a Friendly civilization, meaning they have an initial positive attitude of +15%. Friendly civilizations have a chance of giving you 15–25% extra resources during a trade.
  • Prerequisites: Discovering the Spiders requires reaching significant progress in space and technology, specifically needing 100 Trade Ships and a maximum Science limit of 125,000.
    • Due to the high maximum science requirement, Spiders are considered “waayyyy off” for players in the early to mid-game stages.

Trade Details

Spiders primarily exchange the crafted resource Scaffold for Coal:
item.content:encoded:
The Spiders are a Friendly civilization (+15% attitude) in Kittens Game who primarily function as a trading partner for industrial resources, particularly Coal.

Here is a detailed breakdown of the Spiders:

Unlocking and Attitude

  • Attitude: Spiders are designated as a Friendly civilization, meaning they have an initial positive attitude of +15%. Friendly civilizations have a chance of giving you 15–25% extra resources during a trade.
  • Prerequisites: Discovering the Spiders requires reaching significant progress in space and technology, specifically needing 100 Trade Ships and a maximum Science limit of 125,000.
    • Due to the high maximum science requirement, Spiders are considered “waayyyy off” for players in the early to mid-game stages.

Trade Details

Spiders primarily exchange the crafted resource Scaffold for Coal:

Action Resource Minimum Amount Cost/Gain Seasonal Optimization
Buy Scaffold 50 Cost N/A
Sell Coal 350 Gain Autumn (+15%)
Sell Oil 100 Gain (25% chance, Embassy Level 5) N/A
  • Coal: They sell a minimum amount of 350 Coal per trade, with a 100% chance of delivery and a 15% range bonus.
  • Oil: Once you reach Embassy Level 5, Spiders also sell 100 Oil per trade, though there is only a 25% chance of receiving this resource.
  • Seasonal Bonus: Trading for Coal is most efficient during Autumn, which provides an additional +15% Amount Modifier.

Strategic Context

While Spiders provide a vital source of Coal, early-game advice suggests that acquiring coal from them via scaffold-trading is generally not realistic for players focused on lower-tier progression.

For players who are actively engaging with the Spiders trade route, the coal they provide can be used to fuel industrial buildings like the Steamworks or for crafting advanced materials like Steel (which requires 100 Coal and 100 Iron).

Trading Mechanics

The Spiders are a unique trade partner because they are one of the few sources for bulk coal and oil via trade.

  • Cost: Each trade costs 50 Scaffolds, 50 Catpower, and 1 Gold (once Currency and Gold Ore are researched).
  • Primary Export (Coal): They sell a base of 350 Coal.
  • Secondary Export (Oil): There is a 25% chance they will sell 100 Oil, provided you have at least a Level 5 Embassy with them.
  • Seasonal Adjustments: Their Coal output varies by season:
    • Autumn: +15% (Best time to trade).
    • Summer: +5%.
    • Spring: +0%.
    • Winter: -5%.

Strategic Utility

  • Resolving the Coal Bottleneck: While Coal is often produced by Smelters, Mines, or Geologists, trading with Spiders provides a massive manual influx of the resource if your industrial production is lagging.
  • Oil Acquisition: Before you have a robust network of Oil Wells or Bio Labs, Spiders can serve as a supplementary source for Oil needed for space missions and advanced buildings.
  • The “Scaffold” Barrier: Because Scaffolds are a crafted resource requiring significant amounts of Wood (Beams), trading with Spiders is often not considered realistic until your wood production is extremely high and you can afford to “waste” scaffolds.

item.title: Diplomacy vs isolationism
item.description:
Both Diplomacy and Isolationism are Foreign Policy/ available in Kittens Game, costing 1,600 Culture each and requiring the Currency technology as a prerequisite. They represent a choice in your society’s foreign relations path, with impacts on trade costs and future policy options.

Here is a comparison of the two Policy/:

Diplomacy

Aspect Details
Cost Culture 1600
Prerequisite Currency
Effect Each trade costs 5 less catpower.
Policy Path Leads to Cultural Exchange or Knowledge Sharing (after researching Astronomy).
Strategic Value This policy is generally preferred because it unlocks the path to Cultural Exchange, which provides a bonus to Culture, a resource that is often slow to acquire.
Related Meta The Diplomacy Metaphysics upgrade improves the trade process by reducing the unlock year for races from Year 5 to Year 1, and increases standing ratio.

Isolationism

Aspect Details
Cost Culture 1600
Prerequisite Currency
Effect Each trade costs 1 less gold.
Policy Path Leads to Big Stick Policy or City On A Hill (after researching Astronomy).
Strategic Value While the gold discount might “feel good,” the subsequent Policy/ in this path are generally considered less beneficial (“aren’t any good”).

Strategic Recommendation

For most runs, Diplomacy is the recommended choice.

Strategic Recommendation

For most runs, Diplomacy is the recommended choice.

The primary advantage of Diplomacy is accessing the later Policy/:

  • Cultural Exchange (+5% culture income) is highly valuable because Culture is a resource that accumulates slowly.
  • Knowledge Sharing (+5% science income) is the alternative, although Science is generally easier to obtain than Culture, making Cultural Exchange the common preference.

Conversely, choosing Isolationism grants a Gold discount on trades, but the resulting Policy/ (Big Stick Policy and City On A Hill) are considered weaker options. Big Stick Policy makes Embassies 15% cheaper, while City On A Hill increases Culture cap by 5%.

In summary, choosing Diplomacy prioritises long-term resource boosts (Culture) via future Policy/, whereas Isolationism provides a minor, immediate reduction in gold expenditure during trade.

item.title: Monarchy vs Autocracy
item.description:
Monarchy and Autocracy are both Government Policy/ available in Kittens Game, costing Culture 1500. They occupy the same policy tier, meaning you can only choose one of the two for the current run, and the choice affects which Policy/ you can access later.

Here is a detailed comparison of the two Policy/:

Monarchy

The Monarchy policy is generally highly recommended by expert advice for its substantial and flexible benefits.

Aspect Details Source
Cost Culture 1500
Prerequisites Must have researched Writing and chosen the Tradition policy.
Core Effect (Trait) Makes the leader’s trait twice as powerful. For example, the artisan bonus goes from 5% to 10%.
Drawback Maintaining the royal court reduces gold production by 10%.
Strategic Value Doubling the leader’s effect is considered “AMAZING”. If you promote a leader to a high rank, this doubled trait bonus can be leveraged for various jobs, acting like getting 11 extra kittens gathering that resource (e.g., wood).
Next Tier Policy/ Leads to a choice between Liberalism and Fascism (once a Factory is built).

Autocracy

The Autocracy policy is primarily focused on doubling the leader’s raw production output, but is often considered less impactful than Monarchy.
item.content:encoded:
Monarchy and Autocracy are both Government Policy/ available in Kittens Game, costing Culture 1500. They occupy the same policy tier, meaning you can only choose one of the two for the current run, and the choice affects which Policy/ you can access later.

Here is a detailed comparison of the two Policy/:

Monarchy

The Monarchy policy is generally highly recommended by expert advice for its substantial and flexible benefits.

Aspect Details Source
Cost Culture 1500
Prerequisites Must have researched Writing and chosen the Tradition policy.
Core Effect (Trait) Makes the leader’s trait twice as powerful. For example, the artisan bonus goes from 5% to 10%.
Drawback Maintaining the royal court reduces gold production by 10%.
Strategic Value Doubling the leader’s effect is considered “AMAZING”. If you promote a leader to a high rank, this doubled trait bonus can be leveraged for various jobs, acting like getting 11 extra kittens gathering that resource (e.g., wood).
Next Tier Policy/ Leads to a choice between Liberalism and Fascism (once a Factory is built).

Autocracy

The Autocracy policy is primarily focused on doubling the leader’s raw production output, but is often considered less impactful than Monarchy.

Aspect Details Source
Cost Culture 1500
Prerequisites Must have researched Writing and chosen either the Liberty or Tradition policy.
Core Effect (Production) Makes the leader twice as good at their job, doubling their production bonus.
Secondary Effect The leader’s bonus also increases conversion production (resources produced by Smelters, Calciners, and Accelerators) based on leader rank and the count of uncapped housing buildings, specifically during the Cath cycle.
Strategic Value Monarchy’s doubling of the leader’s trait is highly favoured, and Autocracy’s benefits are sometimes characterized as “tiny bonuses that are dwarfed by pretty much everything else”. However, it is part of the path (Autocracy -> Communism) that can be aimed for to achieve better time crystal results in advanced, highly specialized runs.
Next Tier Policy/ Leads to a choice between Socialism (which has no effect) and the next tier of Policy/ (Liberalism, Communism, or Fascism).

Strategic Recommendation

For most players and early runs, Monarchy is strongly recommended.

  • Monarchy provides a highly valuable and flexible tool by doubling the leader’s trait. You can easily reassign a highly skilled leader (with doubled traits) to different roles to maximize whichever resource you are currently grinding, making it an amazing choice for efficiency.
  • While Autocracy can be useful for late-game strategies where the focus is on industrial output optimization and time crystal acquisition (leading to Communism), its direct bonuses are generally considered minor compared to Monarchy.

This choice is analogous to deciding whether to hire a general manager (Monarchy) who improves the overall culture and skill effectiveness across multiple departments, or a highly focused production specialist (Autocracy) who only doubles output in one area at a time; the general manager often provides more adaptable long-term benefits to a growing civilization.

item.title: Workshop_Automation
item.description:
The term “Workshop Automation” refers to a specific Workshop upgrade associated with the Steamworks building in Kittens Game.

Here is a detailed breakdown of the Workshop Automation upgrade:

  • Prerequisite Technology: This upgrade is unlocked by researching the Machinery technology.
  • Cost: To acquire Workshop Automation, you must spend 10,000 Science and 25 Gears.
  • Effect/Function: Once purchased, the upgrade converts small quantities of craftable resources into materials when they are near their storage limit.
    • Specifically, Workshop Automation converts 2% plus 2% times the number of Steamworks of wood into beams and minerals into slabs when that resource is at 98% of its storage cap.
    • This conversion occurs once per year (i.e., in the Spring season).
    • The goal of this automation is to help players manage their storage capacity by automatically converting common, capped resources (Wood and Minerals) into more advanced materials (Beams and Slabs).
  • Advanced Form: There is a subsequent upgrade, Advanced Automation, which causes Workshop Automation to be triggered twice per year.
  • Related Upgrade: The Pneumatic Press upgrade further enhances this function by enabling Workshop Automation to also convert Iron into Plates.

In essence, Workshop Automation allows your Steamworks to passively manage resource bottlenecks, ensuring that your basic resources (Wood and Minerals) continue to generate useful craftable materials even when they are approaching their storage limits. This is particularly handy for generating Beams and Slabs without requiring constant manual crafting.

item.title: Zebra Workshop
item.description:
The Zebra Workshop is one of the specialized buildings associated with the Zebra civilization in Kittens Game. It is unlocked early in the game’s technological progression, alongside the Zebra Outpost and Zebra Forge.

Here is a detailed summary of the Zebra Workshop’s characteristics and purpose:

Construction and Unlocks

  • Technology Prerequisite: Like the other Zebra buildings, the Zebra Workshop is unlocked by researching the Archery technology.
  • Cost: It requires 5 Bloodstone to construct.
  • Price Ratio: The building has a price ratio of 1.15.

Purpose and Effects

The Zebra Workshop serves to enhance your civilization’s maximum capacity for catpower and, most notably, unlocks further enhancements related to the Zebras themselves:
item.content:encoded:
The Zebra Workshop is one of the specialized buildings associated with the Zebra civilization in Kittens Game. It is unlocked early in the game’s technological progression, alongside the Zebra Outpost and Zebra Forge.

Here is a detailed summary of the Zebra Workshop’s characteristics and purpose:

Construction and Unlocks

  • Technology Prerequisite: Like the other Zebra buildings, the Zebra Workshop is unlocked by researching the Archery technology.
  • Cost: It requires 5 Bloodstone to construct.
  • Price Ratio: The building has a price ratio of 1.15.

Purpose and Effects

The Zebra Workshop serves to enhance your civilization’s maximum capacity for catpower and, most notably, unlocks further enhancements related to the Zebras themselves:

  • Catpower Capacity: It increases your maximum Catpower by +10.
  • Zebra Upgrades: Its primary function is that it Unlocks Zebra Upgrades in the Workshop tab.

The Zebra Workshop is the middle tier of the three initial Zebra buildings, costing more Bloodstone than the Zebra Outpost (1 Bloodstone) but significantly less than the Zebra Forge (50 Bloodstone).

item.title: Zebra Outpost
