The Zebra Outpost is the foundational building associated with the Zebra civilization in Kittens Game. It is one of three specialized Zebra buildings, all unlocked early in the game’s technological progression.

Here are the details regarding the Zebra Outpost:

1. Construction and Unlocks

  • Technology Prerequisite: The Zebra Outpost is unlocked by researching the Archery technology.
  • Cost: It requires 1 Bloodstone to construct.
  • Price Ratio: The building has a price ratio of 1.35.

2. Effects and Purpose

The Zebra Outpost provides two main benefits:
item.content:encoded:
The Zebra Outpost is the foundational building associated with the Zebra civilization in Kittens Game. It is one of three specialized Zebra buildings, all unlocked early in the game’s technological progression.

Here are the details regarding the Zebra Outpost:

1. Construction and Unlocks

  • Technology Prerequisite: The Zebra Outpost is unlocked by researching the Archery technology.
  • Cost: It requires 1 Bloodstone to construct.
  • Price Ratio: The building has a price ratio of 1.35.

2. Effects and Purpose

The Zebra Outpost provides two main benefits:

  • Hunting Bonus: It grants a +5% bonus to Hunting.
  • Catpower Capacity: It increases your maximum Catpower by +5.

The hunting bonus is significant, as the ability to hunt is unlocked by the same technology (Archery), allowing you to accumulate rare resources like Furs and Ivory, which are used for happiness and crafting.

3. Strategic Context (Iron Will Mode)

The Zebra Outpost is particularly relevant in the Iron Will challenge:

  • Zebra Limit: In the Iron Will challenge, where players cannot build housing and thus cannot assign kitten jobs, Zebras act as hunters to replace the missing kitten population.
  • Acquisition: If a player, while in Iron Will mode, researches Archery and their Zebra limit is less than 10, their Zebra limit increases by 1. The maximum number of Zebras obtained this way is 10 (or possibly 11, depending on other limits).
  • Production Cap: The Dark Revolution policy increases the Zebra base catpower production cap by +1 (or +0.1 in non-Iron Will mode).
  • Resetting for Zebras: The Iron Will procedure involves resetting the game after achieving Archery multiple times to accumulate a higher Zebra limit before embarking on a longer run. This is done to gain sufficient Catpower generation for hunting, which is essential for acquiring early resources.

Progression of Zebra Buildings

The Zebra Outpost is the first of three Zebra buildings, followed by the Zebra Workshop and the Zebra Forge, all unlocked by Archery:

  • Zebra Outpost: 1 Bloodstone.
  • Zebra Workshop: 5 Bloodstone; this unlocks additional Zebra Upgrades.
  • Zebra Forge: 50 Bloodstone; this unlocks the crafting of Bloodstone and T-Mythril.

item.title: Zebra Forge
item.description:
The Zebra Forge is a specialized building associated with the Zebra civilization in Kittens Game. Its primary purpose is to unlock advanced crafting of resources specific to the Zebras and their materials.

Here is a breakdown of the Zebra Forge’s characteristics, cost, and function:

1. Construction and Unlocks

  • Location: The Zebra Forge is listed under the “Zebras” category of buildings.
  • Cost: It requires 50 Bloodstone to construct.
  • Prerequisite: The building is unlocked by researching the Archery technology.
  • Secondary Effect: Building the Zebra Forge provides a permanent increase to your maximum Catpower by +50.

2. Primary Function: Advanced Crafting

The most critical function of the Zebra Forge is enabling the crafting of two specialized resources:
item.content:encoded:
The Zebra Forge is a specialized building associated with the Zebra civilization in Kittens Game. Its primary purpose is to unlock advanced crafting of resources specific to the Zebras and their materials.

Here is a breakdown of the Zebra Forge’s characteristics, cost, and function:

1. Construction and Unlocks

  • Location: The Zebra Forge is listed under the “Zebras” category of buildings.
  • Cost: It requires 50 Bloodstone to construct.
  • Prerequisite: The building is unlocked by researching the Archery technology.
  • Secondary Effect: Building the Zebra Forge provides a permanent increase to your maximum Catpower by +50.

2. Primary Function: Advanced Crafting

The most critical function of the Zebra Forge is enabling the crafting of two specialized resources:

  1. Bloodstone: The Forge unlocks the ability to craft Bloodstone itself. Bloodstone is a unique resource required for Zebra buildings (like the Forge itself and the Zebra Outpost/Workshop) and is crafted from Time Crystal (5k) and Relic (10k).
  2. T-Mythril: The Forge also unlocks the crafting of T-Mythril (Titanium-Mythril). T-Mythril is crafted from 5 Bloodstone, 1,000 Ivory, and 500 Titanium.

3. Strategic Context

The Zebra Forge (along with the Zebra Outpost and Zebra Workshop) is part of a progression path aimed at leveraging the Zebra civilization:

  • Bloodstone Acquisition: In the standard game, Bloodstone is a rare resource that has a 0.05% chance of being acquired through Hunting if you have at least 10 Zebras in Iron Will mode. Unlocking the Forge and the ability to craft Bloodstone allows for a reliable production method, though the required materials (Time Crystals and Relics) indicate this is a very late-game industrial capability.
  • T-Mythril Use: T-Mythril, unlocked by the Forge, is required to construct the Ivory Temple.

Progression of Zebra Buildings

The Zebra buildings typically follow a cost hierarchy based on Bloodstone:

  1. Zebra Outpost: 1 Bloodstone.
  2. Zebra Workshop: 5 Bloodstone; unlocks Zebra Upgrades.
  3. Zebra Forge: 50 Bloodstone; unlocks advanced crafting.

item.title: Bio Lab
item.description:
The Bio Lab is an advanced mid-to-late-game science building in Kittens Game, primarily designed to significantly boost science capacity and production, and to introduce the ability to refine Catnip into Oil.

Unlocking and Construction

The Bio Lab building is unlocked after significant investment in the Science tree:

  • Technology Prerequisite: The Bio Lab is unlocked by researching Biology. Biology is unlocked by Geology.
  • Base Cost: Construction requires a combination of processed materials and science: 100 Slab, 25 Alloy, and 1,500 Science.
  • Price Ratio: The building has a price ratio of 1.1.

Core Effects

The Bio Lab provides major boosts to your research capabilities:
item.content:encoded:
The Bio Lab is an advanced mid-to-late-game science building in Kittens Game, primarily designed to significantly boost science capacity and production, and to introduce the ability to refine Catnip into Oil.

Unlocking and Construction

The Bio Lab building is unlocked after significant investment in the Science tree:

  • Technology Prerequisite: The Bio Lab is unlocked by researching Biology. Biology is unlocked by Geology.
  • Base Cost: Construction requires a combination of processed materials and science: 100 Slab, 25 Alloy, and 1,500 Science.
  • Price Ratio: The building has a price ratio of 1.1.

Core Effects

The Bio Lab provides major boosts to your research capabilities:

  • Science Production: Provides a +35% bonus to Science production.
  • Science Capacity: Increases your Max Science cap by +1,500.
  • Catnip Refinement: Provides a +10% Catnip refinement bonus.

Strategic Context

The Bio Lab is strategically important but carries a heavy upfront cost:

  • Science Scaling: Bio Labs are listed as buildings that increase science cap, helping players reach high science limits needed for advanced technology.
  • Late-Game Utility: To reach the 125K science limit required for Concrete Huts, players are advised to consider researching Biology to unlock Bio Labs, as they increase science and help “reduce the need to build so many observatories/temples (which start getting very costly)”.
  • Expense: However, Bio Labs are noted to be “really expensive on your first couple runs,” and new players may want to “feel free to skip it first time around”. In later runs, they may still be skipped if high Paragon levels already provide a sufficient storage boost.
  • Pollution: Bio Labs are one of the many industrial buildings that produce Pollution.

Key Upgrades and Synergies

The Bio Lab’s function shifts significantly through specific upgrades, allowing it to become an oil production facility and synergizing with other science structures:

A. Oil Conversion Upgrades

The following upgrades allow the Bio Lab to convert food resources into Oil, requiring energy:

  1. Biofuel Processing (Unlocked by Biochemistry): This upgrade causes Bio Labs to consume 5 Catnip per second (or 1 Catnip per tick) and consume 1 Energy per tick. In return, it produces 0.10 Oil per second (or 0.02 Oil per tick). Additionally, it grants a +35% Science bonus.
  2. GM Catnip (Unlocked by Genetics): This upgrade improves the Bio Lab’s oil yield by +60% (multiplicative with other effects), although it does not affect the amount of Catnip consumed.
  3. Shark Relations: Botanists Policy: This foreign policy reduces the Bio Lab’s energy consumption by 75%.

B. Science and Data Center Synergy

Bio Labs interact closely with the late-game Data Center building, which is an upgrade to the Library:

  1. Uplink (Unlocked by Satellites): This upgrade creates a reciprocal bonus: Data Centers gain a +1% bonus to Max Science, Max Culture, and Compendium Cap per Bio Lab, and Bio Labs gain a +1% Max Science bonus per Data Center.
  2. Starlink (Unlocked by Orbital Engineering): Further increases the Max Science bonus of Bio Labs by +1% per Data Center.
  3. CAD System (Unlocked by Electronics): Bio Labs are one of the specific scientific buildings (along with Libraries/Data Centers, Academies, and Observatories) that improve the effectiveness of Blueprint crafting via the CAD System workshop upgrade. Bio Labs contribute this bonus even when they are turned off.

The Bio Lab thus facilitates the transition into the oil and advanced science era, often being built primarily for its energy-efficient method of converting excess catnip into valuable oil resources.

item.title: Woodcutter
item.description:
Produces +0.09 wood per second

Quote: “Must. Not. Scratch.”

Woodcutters are one of the very first specialised jobs you can assign to your kittens, and they serve as the foundation of your early-game economy by continuously harvesting Wood.

Base Production and Acquisition

  • Base Output: A kitten actively assigned as a Woodcutter natively generates +0.0018 wood per tick.
  • Unlock Requirement: To employ Woodcutters, you must first gather Catnip, refine it into Wood, and use that Wood to construct your first Hut. Once kittens begin arriving in your Small Village tab, you can assign them to the Woodcutter job.

Upgrades and Boosts (The Axe Chain)

You can drastically improve the effectiveness of your Woodcutters through a dedicated series of Workshop technologies known as the “axe chain”. These upgrades provide massive percentage-based boosts to their output:
item.content:encoded:
Produces +0.09 wood per second

Quote: “Must. Not. Scratch.”

Woodcutters are one of the very first specialised jobs you can assign to your kittens, and they serve as the foundation of your early-game economy by continuously harvesting Wood.

Base Production and Acquisition

  • Base Output: A kitten actively assigned as a Woodcutter natively generates +0.0018 wood per tick.
  • Unlock Requirement: To employ Woodcutters, you must first gather Catnip, refine it into Wood, and use that Wood to construct your first Hut. Once kittens begin arriving in your Small Village tab, you can assign them to the Woodcutter job.

Upgrades and Boosts (The Axe Chain)

You can drastically improve the effectiveness of your Woodcutters through a dedicated series of Workshop technologies known as the “axe chain”. These upgrades provide massive percentage-based boosts to their output:

  • Mineral Axe +70% effectiveness.
  • Iron Axe: +50% effectiveness.
  • Steel Axe: +50% effectiveness.
  • Titanium Axe: +50% effectiveness.
  • Alloy Axe: +50% effectiveness.
  • Unobtainium Axe: The final upgrade in the Woodcutter tool chain.

Strategic Management

  • The Early Game Grind: Before you unlock advanced buildings, wood will accumulate very slowly. It is highly recommended to heavily focus your workforce on wood production until you can afford Lumber Mills.
  • Multiplicative Synergy: The percentage bonuses granted by the workshop axe upgrades stack multiplicatively with the bonuses provided by your Lumber Mills. This means combining both upgrade paths will exponentially skyrocket your Woodcutters’ yields.
  • Workforce Ratios: When balancing your early-to-mid game economy, a standard community strategy is to employ half as many Miners as you have Woodcutters. Because wood is constantly required to build the structures that boost mineral output, this 2:1 ratio generally maintains a stable and parallel growth of both resources.
  • Leader Synergy: If you are desperately bottlenecked by wood, you can assign a Woodcutter as your village Leader and promote them with gold. A highly ranked leader provides such a massive percentage boost to their specific job that it can be the equivalent of adding up to 11 extra kittens to your woodcutting workforce.

item.title: Titanium_Barns
item.description:
Titanium Barns is a powerful storage upgrade available in the Workshop tab of Kittens Game, specifically designed to increase your capacity for common resources.

Function and Effects

The primary effect of the Titanium Barns upgrade is to significantly increase the storage capacity provided by your fundamental storage structures:

  • Storage Increase: Titanium Barns causes storage facilities to store twice as many resources.
  • Specific Resources Affected: This upgrade increases the maximum storage for wood, minerals, and iron provided by Barns, Warehouses, and Harbors by 100%.

This capacity increase is vital, as reaching resource storage limits (“caps”) is a major bottleneck that greatly slows progress in the game.
item.content:encoded:
Titanium Barns is a powerful storage upgrade available in the Workshop tab of Kittens Game, specifically designed to increase your capacity for common resources.

Function and Effects

The primary effect of the Titanium Barns upgrade is to significantly increase the storage capacity provided by your fundamental storage structures:

  • Storage Increase: Titanium Barns causes storage facilities to store twice as many resources.
  • Specific Resources Affected: This upgrade increases the maximum storage for wood, minerals, and iron provided by Barns, Warehouses, and Harbors by 100%.

This capacity increase is vital, as reaching resource storage limits (“caps”) is a major bottleneck that greatly slows progress in the game.

Cost and Prerequisites

To purchase Titanium Barns, you must have previously acquired the necessary predecessor upgrade and accumulated substantial resources:

  • Prerequisite: The upgrade requires you to have already purchased Reinforced Barns.
  • Cost:
    • Science: 60,000.
    • Titanium: 25.
    • Steel: 200.
    • Scaffold: 250.

Context in Storage Progression

Titanium Barns is one of several upgrades available for the basic Barn structure, which is initially unlocked after researching Agriculture. It belongs to a line of barn-related upgrades intended to manage increasing resource needs, following upgrades like Expanded Barn and Reinforced Barns.

It is important to note that if you research Exogeology, you unlock Unobtainium Huts and the Storage Bunkers upgrade, the latter of which provides an additional +20% storage increase for a variety of resources (wood, minerals, iron, etc.).

Upgrade Effect on Max Storage (Wood, Minerals, Iron) Prerequisite
Reinforced Barns +80% increase -
Titanium Barns +100% increase Reinforced Barns
Alloy Barns +100% increase Chemistry (Science), Titanium Saw (Upgrade)
Concrete Barns +75% increase Concrete Pillars (Upgrade)

item.title: Steel
item.description:
Steel in Kittens Game functions as both a crucial mid-game technology required for industrial expansion and as a valuable crafted resource necessary for advanced construction and automation.

1. Technology Overview and Cost

The Steel technology is unlocked in the Science tab once you have researched Writing.

  • Cost: It requires 12,000 Science.
  • Context: Steel is one of three key technologies (alongside Philosophy and Machinery) that become available after researching Writing.
  • Unlocks: Researching Steel unlocks the ability to craft steel, and also grants access to several specialized Workshop Upgrades.

2. Steel as a Resource and its Production

Steel is a craftable resource.
item.content:encoded:
Steel in Kittens Game functions as both a crucial mid-game technology required for industrial expansion and as a valuable crafted resource necessary for advanced construction and automation.

1. Technology Overview and Cost

The Steel technology is unlocked in the Science tab once you have researched Writing.

  • Cost: It requires 12,000 Science.
  • Context: Steel is one of three key technologies (alongside Philosophy and Machinery) that become available after researching Writing.
  • Unlocks: Researching Steel unlocks the ability to craft steel, and also grants access to several specialized Workshop Upgrades.

2. Steel as a Resource and its Production

Steel is a craftable resource.

  • Crafting Recipe: Steel is created in the Workshop by combining 100 Iron and 100 Coal.
  • Resource Role: It is a durable metal required for the construction of gears and complex machinery.
  • Acquisition via Trade: Steel can also be acquired through trade, as the Griffins sell Steel (25 units per trade). In the Iron Will 40K endless run guide, the Sharks and Griffins trading loop is cited as a great way to start collecting steel.

3. Key Upgrades Unlocked by Steel

Researching the Steel technology immediately enables several important upgrades in the Workshop:

  • Resource Production:
    • Steel Axe: Permanently increases Woodcutter output by 50%.
    • Coal Furnace: Allows Smelters to produce Coal (0.005 coal/tick) while operating.
    • Deep Mining: Allows Mines to produce Coal (0.003 coal/tick).
    • High Pressure Engine: Reduces the Coal consumption of Steamworks by 20%.
  • Storage and Hunting:
    • Reinforced Warehouses: Increases the storage space for common resources (wood, minerals, coal, iron, gold, and titanium) from Warehouses, Barns, Harbors, and Mints by 25%.
    • Steel Armour: Provides a permanent +0.5 Hunting bonus to increase resource yields from hunting.

4. Strategic Importance and Use

Steel is a required component for many major buildings and subsequent technological advancements:

  • Buildings Requiring Steel:
    • Steamworks: The crucial automation building (requires 65 Steel).
    • Mansion: A later housing upgrade.
    • Quarry: A resource building (requires 125 Steel).
    • Calciner: An industry building.
    • Data Center: An upgraded Science building (requires 100 Steel).
  • Crafting Requirements: Steel is needed to craft Gears and is a component in making Alloy.
  • Conflicting Advice:
    • The “Monstrous Advice” column recommends prioritizing Steel first among the three post-Writing technologies, specifically to gain the useful upgrades that strengthen your economy, before moving to Machinery and Philosophy.
    • Conversely, the walkthrough advises considering Steel a “specialist Tech” and suggests prioritizing Philosophy because it is cheaper and maintains forward progression.
  • Resource Management: In early runs, after acquiring the initial Workshop upgrades unlocked by Steel, players are often advised to ignore coal and let it max out, dedicating their iron production to building Lumber Mills and Observatories, as Steel quickly becomes a bottleneck for future construction.

Steel acts as the foundation for the next stage of industrial complexity, marking the point where your civilization transitions from basic resource gathering to automated production and advanced crafting. This reliance on Steel leads directly into the Machinery era, as Steel is required for the construction of the Steamworks.

item.title: Kerosene Resource
item.description:
Kerosene is a high-tier craftable resource in Kittens Game that serves as the essential rocket fuel for late-game space exploration. It is produced by refining oil and is required to fund most space missions and construct advanced orbital infrastructure.

Acquisition and Cost

  • Unlocking: You must research the Oil Processing technology (215k Science, 150 Blueprints), which is available only after completing Rocketry.
  • Crafting Cost: Each unit of kerosene costs 7,500 oil.
  • Refinement Bonuses:
    • Factory Processing: This workshop upgrade (available via Oil Processing) increases the effectiveness of kerosene refinement by 5% per Factory.
    • Chemist Trait: Assigning a kitten with the Chemist trait as your Leader provides a +0.075 craft ratio bonus to kerosene production.

Primary Uses in Space

Kerosene is mandatory for nearly all activities beyond the initial orbital launch:
item.content:encoded:
Kerosene is a high-tier craftable resource in Kittens Game that serves as the essential rocket fuel for late-game space exploration. It is produced by refining oil and is required to fund most space missions and construct advanced orbital infrastructure.

Acquisition and Cost

  • Unlocking: You must research the Oil Processing technology (215k Science, 150 Blueprints), which is available only after completing Rocketry.
  • Crafting Cost: Each unit of kerosene costs 7,500 oil.
  • Refinement Bonuses:
    • Factory Processing: This workshop upgrade (available via Oil Processing) increases the effectiveness of kerosene refinement by 5% per Factory.
    • Chemist Trait: Assigning a kitten with the Chemist trait as your Leader provides a +0.075 craft ratio bonus to kerosene production.

Primary Uses in Space

Kerosene is mandatory for nearly all activities beyond the initial orbital launch:

  • Space Missions: It is required for missions to Dune (75 kerosene), Piscine (250), Helios (1,250), T-minus (750), Kairo (7,500), and beyond.
  • Orbital Structures: Large quantities are needed for high-tier buildings, most notably Space Beacons (7,500), Heatsinks (5,000), Terraforming Stations (5,000), and Sunlifters (2,500).
  • Infrastructure Upgrades: It is a required material for upgrading Warehouses into Spaceports (1,000 kerosene).

Strategic Management and Automation

Because oil production is often slow but kerosene requirements are massive, managing the oil-to-kerosene pipeline is a common late-game bottleneck.

  • Engineer Automation: Once you have Engineers, you can assign them to automatically craft kerosene. This is highly recommended to prevent oil from hitting its storage cap and halting production while you are away from the game.
  • Storage Requirements: To reach the 7,500 oil threshold for a single craft, you will likely need to build numerous Oil Wells or Tankers.

Preservation and Resets

As a crafted resource, kerosene is normally lost when you reset the game. However, it can be preserved across runs if you possess:

  1. Chronospheres: Each active sphere preserves a portion of your resources.
  2. Flux Condensator: This specific workshop upgrade (unlocked via Chronophysics) is required for Chronospheres to carry over crafted resources like kerosene.

The amount of kerosene saved is determined by the number of Chronospheres and the square root of your total kerosene at the time of reset. This preservation is essential for “Positive Resets,” allowing you to bypass the early-game oil grind and return to space immediately in a new run.

item.title: Academy
item.description:
The Academy is a significant early-to-mid-game science building in Kittens Game, unlocked through the core Science technology path.

Unlocks and Cost

The Academy building is unlocked once you research the Mathematics technology.

  • Technology Prerequisite: Mathematics, which costs 1,000 Science.
  • Base Cost: The construction requires 50 Wood, 70 Minerals, and 100 Science.
  • Price Ratio: The Academy has a price ratio of 1.15.

Primary Effects

The Academy provides multiple benefits, focusing on science, culture capacity, and kitten efficiency:
item.content:encoded:
The Academy is a significant early-to-mid-game science building in Kittens Game, unlocked through the core Science technology path.

Unlocks and Cost

The Academy building is unlocked once you research the Mathematics technology.

  • Technology Prerequisite: Mathematics, which costs 1,000 Science.
  • Base Cost: The construction requires 50 Wood, 70 Minerals, and 100 Science.
  • Price Ratio: The Academy has a price ratio of 1.15.

Primary Effects

The Academy provides multiple benefits, focusing on science, culture capacity, and kitten efficiency:

  • Science Production: It increases Science production by +20%. The sources note that Academies grant a [decent bonus]({< “decent bonus” >}) to the accumulation of Science.
  • Science Capacity: It increases your maximum Science capacity by +500.
  • Culture Capacity: It increases your maximum Culture capacity by +25.
  • Kitten Experience: It provides a +5% bonus to Kitten Experience (Exp).

Strategic Role

Academies play an important role in the game progression, particularly in scaling up science and culture caps:

  • Science Growth: Researching Mathematics to unlock Academies is described as “especially useful” for improving the accumulation of Science.
  • Culture Cap: Academies are listed as buildings that increase culture cap, along with Libraries. They contribute to the total culture cap needed to unlock trade with the Nagas (1,500 culture cap).
  • Science Limit: Academies are listed as structures that contribute to increasing maximum storage for Science, which is the third most important thing in the game, behind production and resource caps.

Upgrades

The Academy has a dedicated upgrade that enhances its functionality:

  • Mineralogy Department: This upgrade provides a +1% bonus to production from meteors.

Academies are one of the core buildings (along with Libraries, Observatories, and Bio Labs) whose effectiveness can be boosted by the CAD System workshop upgrade, which improves blueprint crafting ratio.

item.title: Accelerator
item.description:
The Accelerator is a specialized, late-game building in Kittens Game, unlocked through advanced technology. Its primary function is resource conversion, specifically processing Titanium into Uranium, and greatly increasing resource storage capacity through upgrades.

Here is a detailed breakdown of the Accelerator:

1. Construction and Core Function

The Accelerator building is a vital component of the late-game resource chain, particularly in the run-up to unlocking Metaphysics.

  • Technology Prerequisite: The Accelerator is unlocked by researching Particle Physics. Particle Physics requires 185,000 Science and 135 Blueprints.
  • Base Cost: 7,500 Titanium, 125 Concrete, and 25 Uranium.
  • Conversion Production: The Accelerator is designed to convert Titanium into Uranium, consuming energy in the process.
    • Consumption: -0.015 Titanium per Tick.
    • Production: +0.0025 Uranium per Tick.
    • Energy: It consumes -2 Energy per tick to operate.

The Accelerator is one of the buildings whose output is considered “Conversion production” and can be boosted by Policy/ like Autocracy.
item.content:encoded:
The Accelerator is a specialized, late-game building in Kittens Game, unlocked through advanced technology. Its primary function is resource conversion, specifically processing Titanium into Uranium, and greatly increasing resource storage capacity through upgrades.

Here is a detailed breakdown of the Accelerator:

1. Construction and Core Function

The Accelerator building is a vital component of the late-game resource chain, particularly in the run-up to unlocking Metaphysics.

  • Technology Prerequisite: The Accelerator is unlocked by researching Particle Physics. Particle Physics requires 185,000 Science and 135 Blueprints.
  • Base Cost: 7,500 Titanium, 125 Concrete, and 25 Uranium.
  • Conversion Production: The Accelerator is designed to convert Titanium into Uranium, consuming energy in the process.
    • Consumption: -0.015 Titanium per Tick.
    • Production: +0.0025 Uranium per Tick.
    • Energy: It consumes -2 Energy per tick to operate.

The Accelerator is one of the buildings whose output is considered “Conversion production” and can be boosted by Policy/ like Autocracy.

2. Strategic Role and Bottleneck Mitigation

Accelerators help address the significant bottleneck of obtaining Uranium, which is required for Reactors and later converted into Unobtainium by the Lunar Outpost.

  • Uranium Source: It is one of the ways Uranium can be produced, alongside trading with Dragons and production from Quarries after the Orbital Geodesy upgrade.
  • Efficiency Concerns: The initial conversion rate is slow; one Accelerator creates Uranium at a rate 140 times slower than a Lunar Outpost consumes it. This means if the Accelerator is the sole source of Uranium, the Lunar Outpost will run 140 times slower. Players are advised to create multiple Accelerators to speed things up, or rely on trading with Dragons for Uranium.
  • Dark Future Mitigation: Accelerators can be purchased to “ward off” the rising Time Crystal cost caused by the “dark future” mechanic, although players are advised not to worry about this too much as the effect is minimal.

3. Key Upgrades (Energy Rifts)

The most notable feature of the Accelerator is its ability to unlock substantial storage upgrades through the “Energy Rifts” technology, significantly boosting resource capacity.

Upgrade Name Technology Prerequisite Effect (Storage Boost per Accelerator)
Energy Rifts Dimensional Physics Unlocks substantial storage capacity for Catnip, Wood, Minerals, Iron, Coal, Gold, and Titanium.
Stasis Chambers Chronophysics Increases the storage gain from Energy Rifts by +95%.
Void Energy Stasis Chambers Increases the storage gain from Energy Rifts by +75%.
Dark Energy Void Energy Increases the storage gain from Energy Rifts by +250%.
Tachyon Accelerators Tachyon Theory Increases the storage gain from Energy Rifts by +500%.

Furthermore, the LHC upgrade (unlocked by Dimensional Physics) provides a bonus of +2500 Max Science per Accelerator.

In the late game, using the Energy Rift upgrade is key to increasing storage capacity for unobtainium.

4. Challenge Context

  • Energy Challenge: The Accelerator is not listed among the necessary buildings required to complete the Energy Challenge, which focuses on energy production buildings (Steamworks, Magneto, Solar Farms, Hydro Plant, Reactor, Satellite, Sunlifter, Tectonic, HR Harvester).
  • Paragon Grind: In the Paragon grinding phase, after the 40K mark, the advice is to buy a few Time Impedances and Accelerators to slow down the rising Time Crystal cost due to “dark future”.

item.title: Advanced Exogeology
item.description:
Advanced Exogeology, now primarily referred to as Exometallurgy, is an essential late-game science technology that serves as the gateway to the Eludium Era. It represents a significant shift in production scaling, focusing on the refinement of space-based resources and the drastic expansion of population and scientific limits.

Costs and Prerequisites

  • Science Cost: 325,000.
  • Blueprint Cost: 350 Blueprints.
  • Prerequisite: Researching Exogeology is mandatory before this technology becomes available.

Unlocking Eludium

The primary function of this technology is enabling the crafting of Eludium in the Workshop. Eludium is an extremely rare and expensive composite resource required for deep-space missions and advanced storage structures.
item.content:encoded:
Advanced Exogeology, now primarily referred to as Exometallurgy, is an essential late-game science technology that serves as the gateway to the Eludium Era. It represents a significant shift in production scaling, focusing on the refinement of space-based resources and the drastic expansion of population and scientific limits.

Costs and Prerequisites

  • Science Cost: 325,000.
  • Blueprint Cost: 350 Blueprints.
  • Prerequisite: Researching Exogeology is mandatory before this technology becomes available.

Unlocking Eludium

The primary function of this technology is enabling the crafting of Eludium in the Workshop. Eludium is an extremely rare and expensive composite resource required for deep-space missions and advanced storage structures.

  • Crafting Recipe: 1,000 Unobtainium and 2,500 Alloy.

Enabled Workshop Upgrades

Researching Advanced Exogeology/Exometallurgy provides access to four high-impact Workshop upgrades that optimize the late-game economy:

  • Microwarp Reactors:
    • Cost: 150k Science and 50 Eludium.
    • Effect: Increases the Unobtainium production of Lunar Outposts by 75%. This is considered a vital upgrade for scaling UO production to meet endgame demands.
  • Eludium Huts:
    • Cost: 275k Science and 125 Eludium.
    • Effect: Reduces the Hut price ratio by 10%. This reduction allows for significantly higher kitten populations, which is critical for maximizing Paragon gains upon resetting.
  • Planet Busters:
    • Cost: 275k Science and 250 Eludium.
    • Effect: Doubles the effectiveness of Planet Crackers (Hissmeowra), making them twice as efficient at producing Uranium.
  • Eludium Reflectors:
    • Cost: 250k Science and 15 Eludium.
    • Effect: Improves the maximum science bonus provided by Observatories to Libraries and Data Centers by an additional 2% each.

Strategic Utility

Advanced Exogeology is the threshold where Unobtainium transitions from a rare mission requirement to a primary industrial input. The technology and its associated upgrades are designed to overcome the production bottlenecks of the space era. Specifically, Microwarp Reactors are a priority for any run lasting longer than five minutes, as they provide a massive boost to UO velocity. While Eludium Huts are expensive, they are essential for players pushing toward the highest possible population caps (such as 500+ kittens) to maximize the return on investment for each reset.

item.title: AI Bases
item.description:
AI Bases is a high-tier Workshop upgrade in Kittens Game that leverages your AI infrastructure to significantly expand space-based storage capacity.

Costs and Prerequisites

To access this upgrade, you must have researched the Artificial Intelligence science technology and established at least one AI Core. Once unlocked, it can be purchased in the Workshop for:

  • Science: 750,000
  • Antimatter: 7,500

Core Effect: Moon Base Scaling

The primary function of AI Bases is to create a multiplicative storage bonus based on your mega-structure population:
item.content:encoded:
AI Bases is a high-tier Workshop upgrade in Kittens Game that leverages your AI infrastructure to significantly expand space-based storage capacity.

Costs and Prerequisites

To access this upgrade, you must have researched the Artificial Intelligence science technology and established at least one AI Core. Once unlocked, it can be purchased in the Workshop for:

  • Science: 750,000
  • Antimatter: 7,500

Core Effect: Moon Base Scaling

The primary function of AI Bases is to create a multiplicative storage bonus based on your mega-structure population:

  • Effect: Every AI Core you have built increases the effectiveness of your Moon Bases by +10%.
  • Independence from AI Level: Crucially, this bonus is derived strictly from the number of AI Cores owned. It is not affected by your current AI Level, Gigaflops count, or the threat of an AI Apocalypse.

Strategic Synergies

  • Transkittenism Policy: If the Transkittenism policy is active (requiring a Leviathan trade), the bonus provided by AI Bases is further enhanced. Advanced guides indicate that under this policy, the bonus effectively increases to 11% per AI Core.
  • Unobtainium Capacity: AI Bases are a critical component of the deep late-game “Chrono-Engine.” Because Moon Bases are one of only two structures that provide Unobtainium storage (the other being Cryostations), scaling them with AI Cores is essential for reaching the 8.14 billion Unobtainium cap required to build 100 Chronospheres for “positive resets”.
  • Antimatter Management: Since the upgrade itself costs 7,500 Antimatter and requires AI Cores (which consume significant energy), players typically prioritize this after they have stabilized their Sunlifter production and Containment Chamber storage.

By combining a large number of AI Cores with the AI Bases upgrade, your Moon Bases—which initially provide only 150 Unobtainium storage each—can scale to support the massive resource requirements of the endgame.

item.title: Alloy Armour
item.description:
Alloy Armour is a mid-to-late game Workshop upgrade that further improves the efficiency of your Hunters, serving as the fourth tier of weapon technology.

Core Effects

  • Hunting Bonus: It provides a +0.5 increase to your civilization’s hunting bonus.
  • Yield Increase: This bonus translates to roughly a 40–50% increase in the base amount of Furs and Ivory obtained per hunt.
  • Additive Stacking: Like previous armor upgrades, this bonus is additive. For example, if you already have Bolas (+1), Hunting Armour (+2), and Steel Armour (+0.5), adding Alloy Armour brings your total hunting bonus to 4.0.

Requirements and Costs

  • Prerequisite: You must research the Chemistry technology to unlock this upgrade.
  • Science Cost: 50,000 Science.
  • Resource Cost: 25 Alloy.

Strategic Context

  • Diminishing Returns: Compared to Hunting Armour (which gives +2.0) or Bolas (which gives +1.0), the +0.5 bonus from Alloy Armour is relatively small. However, by this stage of the game, increasing your Ivory income is crucial for trading with the Nagas (to get Minerals) and for the Unicorn religion (Minting ivory/sacrificing).
  • Progression: It acts as a stepping stone toward the final hunter upgrade, Nanosuits (unlocked via Nanotechnology), which provides another +0.5 bonus.

item.title: Amphitheater
item.description:
The Amphitheatre is a vital early-game building designed to manage population morale and introduce the critical resource, Culture.

Here is a detailed explanation of the Amphitheatre:

Purpose and Effects

The primary function of the Amphitheatre is to combat the negative effects of population growth on your civilization’s efficiency.

  • Unhappiness Reduction: As your kitten population rises, they become unhappy, which acts as a “production killer” that reduces overall efficiency. The Amphitheatre directly addresses this by reducing Unhappiness by -4.8%.
  • Culture Generation: Amphitheatres are the earliest buildings available for generating the resource Culture. They provide +0.005 Culture per Tick and increase the Max Culture limit by +50. Culture is necessary for crafting Manuscripts, which are required for subsequent advanced technologies like Theology.

Acquisition and Cost

The Amphitheatre building is unlocked once you research the Writing technology.
item.content:encoded:
The Amphitheatre is a vital early-game building designed to manage population morale and introduce the critical resource, Culture.

Here is a detailed explanation of the Amphitheatre:

Purpose and Effects

The primary function of the Amphitheatre is to combat the negative effects of population growth on your civilization’s efficiency.

  • Unhappiness Reduction: As your kitten population rises, they become unhappy, which acts as a “production killer” that reduces overall efficiency. The Amphitheatre directly addresses this by reducing Unhappiness by -4.8%.
  • Culture Generation: Amphitheatres are the earliest buildings available for generating the resource Culture. They provide +0.005 Culture per Tick and increase the Max Culture limit by +50. Culture is necessary for crafting Manuscripts, which are required for subsequent advanced technologies like Theology.

Acquisition and Cost

The Amphitheatre building is unlocked once you research the Writing technology.

To construct a single Amphitheatre, the costs are:

  • 200 Wood
  • 1,200 Minerals
  • 3 Parchment
  • The price ratio for successive purchases increases by 1.15.

Strategic Importance

Amphitheatres are considered extremely important in the early game.

  • Players are advised to build Amphitheatres until they stop noticeably improving Happiness, a metric monitored by the ‘population penalty’ percentage shown on the top bar of the game.
  • Accumulating Amphitheatres helps facilitate the path to Temples, as they are essential for generating the Culture needed for Manuscripts. Furthermore, maximizing Amphitheatres and Temples is recommended when preparing to grind out manuscripts for advanced sciences.
  • Karma, gained upon resetting the game, increases overall happiness, which in turn helps offset the need for Amphitheatres as much as they are needed in earlier runs.

Upgrade Path

The Amphitheatre is a building that can be later upgraded to a Broadcast Tower. This upgrade is highly beneficial:

  • For Happiness purposes, a single Broadcast Tower is potent enough to replace your entire stock of Amphitheatres.
  • For Culture purposes, a single tower can increase the maximum culture capacity as much as six Amphitheatres and increase production as much as two hundred Amphitheatres. Consequently, there is little reason to delay this upgrade once the metal resources are available.

item.title: Antimatter Bases
item.description:
Antimatter Bases is a late-game Workshop upgrade that significantly improves the energy efficiency of your space infrastructure by optimizing Moon Bases.

Costs and Prerequisites

To unlock this upgrade, you must first research the Antimatter science technology. Once researched, the upgrade is available in the Workshop for the following resources:

  • Antimatter: 250
  • Eludium: 15

Core Effect

The primary function of Antimatter Bases is to reduce the high energy cost of maintaining bases on Redmoon:
item.content:encoded:
Antimatter Bases is a late-game Workshop upgrade that significantly improves the energy efficiency of your space infrastructure by optimizing Moon Bases.

Costs and Prerequisites

To unlock this upgrade, you must first research the Antimatter science technology. Once researched, the upgrade is available in the Workshop for the following resources:

  • Antimatter: 250
  • Eludium: 15

Core Effect

The primary function of Antimatter Bases is to reduce the high energy cost of maintaining bases on Redmoon:

  • 50% Energy Reduction: It halves the energy consumption of every Moon Base.
  • Impact: A standard Moon Base consumes 10 Watts (Wt) of energy; with this upgrade, the drain is reduced to 5 Wt per building.

Strategic Importance

  • Energy Management: As you progress into the late game, energy becomes a major bottleneck for advanced structures like Containment Chambers and AI Cores. Reducing the drain from your primary storage buildings (Moon Bases) is critical for maintaining a positive energy balance.
  • Antimatter Production Synergy: Maintaining a positive energy surplus is the mandatory requirement for Sunlifters to generate antimatter at the change of each year. By lowering Moon Base power consumption, Antimatter Bases helps ensure your civilization continues to produce the very resource needed for further endgame expansion.
  • Scaling Storage: Moon Bases provide essential storage for Unobtainium, Titanium, and Oil. Reducing their power cost allows you to build more bases, which in turn increases your resource caps for even more advanced space missions and technologies.

item.title: Antimatter Drive
item.description:
The Antimatter Drive is a high-tier late-game Workshop upgrade that functions as an advanced rocket engine to significantly increase the speed of space exploration.

Costs and Prerequisites

To access this upgrade, you must first research the Antimatter science technology, which requires 500,000 Science and 1 Relic. Once unlocked, the Antimatter Drive can be purchased in the Workshop for the following resources:

  • Science: 450,000
  • Antimatter: 125

Core Effects on Space Travel

The primary function of the Antimatter Drive is to drastically reduce the real-time duration of space missions:
item.content:encoded:
The Antimatter Drive is a high-tier late-game Workshop upgrade that functions as an advanced rocket engine to significantly increase the speed of space exploration.

Costs and Prerequisites

To access this upgrade, you must first research the Antimatter science technology, which requires 500,000 Science and 1 Relic. Once unlocked, the Antimatter Drive can be purchased in the Workshop for the following resources:

  • Science: 450,000
  • Antimatter: 125

Core Effects on Space Travel

The primary function of the Antimatter Drive is to drastically reduce the real-time duration of space missions:

  • Travel Time Reduction: Researching this upgrade divides all listed space travel times by 25.
  • Thorium Drive Synergy: If the Thorium Drive has also been researched, their combined efficiency divides all space travel times by 75.

Strategic Importance

This upgrade is essential for reaching the most distant reaches of the Helios system and beyond, where base travel times are otherwise prohibitive. For instance, without any drive upgrades, a mission to Umbra takes over 4 hours of real-time, and a mission to Centaurus takes over 66 hours. By applying the Antimatter Drive (especially in tandem with the Thorium Drive), these times are reduced to manageable levels, allowing you to establish endgame infrastructure like HR Harvesters and Tectonic stations much faster.

Additionally, while these drives provide a permanent passive speed increase, players can further reduce travel times for missions already in progress by combusting Time Crystals in the Time tab.

item.title: Antimatter Fission
item.description:
Antimatter Fission is a late-game Workshop upgrade that enhances the industrial efficiency of your workforce, specifically targeting the production of Eludium.

Costs and Prerequisites

To unlock this upgrade, you must first research the Antimatter science technology (which requires 500,000 Science and 1 Relic). Once the science is discovered, the upgrade becomes available in the Workshop for the following resources:

  • Science: 525,000
  • Antimatter: 175
  • Thorium: 7,500

Core Effect

The primary function of Antimatter Fission is to improve the productivity of Engineers—the kittens that provide automated crafting:
item.content:encoded:
Antimatter Fission is a late-game Workshop upgrade that enhances the industrial efficiency of your workforce, specifically targeting the production of Eludium.

Costs and Prerequisites

To unlock this upgrade, you must first research the Antimatter science technology (which requires 500,000 Science and 1 Relic). Once the science is discovered, the upgrade becomes available in the Workshop for the following resources:

  • Science: 525,000
  • Antimatter: 175
  • Thorium: 7,500

Core Effect

The primary function of Antimatter Fission is to improve the productivity of Engineers—the kittens that provide automated crafting:

  • Effect: It makes Engineers 25% more effective when they are assigned to craft Eludium.

Strategic Utility

Researching Antimatter Fission is a vital step for players entering the Eludium Era and the Unicorn/Time Crystal Era for several reasons:

  • Unobtainium Conservation: Eludium is extremely expensive, requiring 1,000 Unobtainium per craft. Increasing the efficiency of your Engineers allows you to generate more of this rare resource for the same Unobtainium cost, which is critical since Unobtainium is a major late-game bottleneck.
  • Scaling Infrastructure: High yields of Eludium are necessary to afford Eludium Huts (which significantly reduce the price ratio of housing) and advanced space structures like Sunlifters and Cryostations.
  • Automated Management: By improving Engineer effectiveness, players can rely more on passive, automated crafting to reach the high storage caps and material counts required for Phase 3 (“Endgame”) progression.

item.title: Antimatter Reactors
item.description:
Antimatter Reactors is a late-game Workshop upgrade that significantly expands your science storage capacity by enhancing your space-based research infrastructure.

Costs and Prerequisites

  • Technology Unlock: You must first research the Antimatter science technology.
  • Resource Cost: The upgrade requires 750 Antimatter and 35 Eludium.

Core Effects

The primary function of this upgrade is to boost the effectiveness of your primary endgame science structures:

  • Science Storage Boost: It increases the maximum science storage provided by Research Vessels and Space Beacons by 95%.
  • Efficiency: The upgrade is described as making these structures “95% more effective” overall.

Endgame Progression

Antimatter Reactors is the first in a chain of three upgrades focused on scaling your science cap through space structures:
item.content:encoded:
Antimatter Reactors is a late-game Workshop upgrade that significantly expands your science storage capacity by enhancing your space-based research infrastructure.

Costs and Prerequisites

  • Technology Unlock: You must first research the Antimatter science technology.
  • Resource Cost: The upgrade requires 750 Antimatter and 35 Eludium.

Core Effects

The primary function of this upgrade is to boost the effectiveness of your primary endgame science structures:

  • Science Storage Boost: It increases the maximum science storage provided by Research Vessels and Space Beacons by 95%.
  • Efficiency: The upgrade is described as making these structures “95% more effective” overall.

Endgame Progression

Antimatter Reactors is the first in a chain of three upgrades focused on scaling your science cap through space structures:

  1. Antimatter Reactors: +95% Max Science.
  2. Advanced AM Reactors: Increases the total science bonus to 150% (requires 70 Eludium and 1,750 Antimatter).
  3. Void Reactors: Increases the total science bonus by 400% (requires 250 Void and 2,500 Antimatter).

This progression is vital for reaching the high science caps necessary for “Endgame” (Phase 3) technologies like Quantum Cryptography (1.25M Science) or Blackchain (5M Science). While early-game science relies on Libraries and Academies, the bonuses from Antimatter Reactors allow Research Vessels (base +10k science) and Space Beacons (base +25k science) to become your dominant sources of science capacity.

item.title: Archery
item.description:
Archery is a fundamental early-game scientific technology that serves as the gateway to the hunt system, rare resource acquisition, and the specialised Iron Will progression path. It costs 300 Science and is unlocked after researching Agriculture.

Core Unlocks and Mechanics

Researching Archery introduces several critical components to the colony’s development:

  • The Hunter Job: This technology enables you to assign kittens as Hunters, who produce 0.06 catpower per tick.
  • The Hunt System: Once you have accumulated 100 catpower, you can send your kittens on a hunt. This is the primary method for obtaining rare resources like Furs and Ivory, and it offers a 5% chance to find Unicorns.
  • Technological Branching: Archery is the mandatory prerequisite for Animal Husbandry, which leads to housing improvements and the “Unicorn Tree”.
  • Zebra Buildings: For advanced players, Archery unlocks Zebra-specific structures including the Zebra Outpost, Zebra Workshop, and Zebra Forge.

Workshop Enhancements

The effectiveness of the systems unlocked by Archery can be drastically improved through specific Workshop upgrades:
item.content:encoded:
Archery is a fundamental early-game scientific technology that serves as the gateway to the hunt system, rare resource acquisition, and the specialised Iron Will progression path. It costs 300 Science and is unlocked after researching Agriculture.

Core Unlocks and Mechanics

Researching Archery introduces several critical components to the colony’s development:

  • The Hunter Job: This technology enables you to assign kittens as Hunters, who produce 0.06 catpower per tick.
  • The Hunt System: Once you have accumulated 100 catpower, you can send your kittens on a hunt. This is the primary method for obtaining rare resources like Furs and Ivory, and it offers a 5% chance to find Unicorns.
  • Technological Branching: Archery is the mandatory prerequisite for Animal Husbandry, which leads to housing improvements and the “Unicorn Tree”.
  • Zebra Buildings: For advanced players, Archery unlocks Zebra-specific structures including the Zebra Outpost, Zebra Workshop, and Zebra Forge.

Workshop Enhancements

The effectiveness of the systems unlocked by Archery can be drastically improved through specific Workshop upgrades:

  • Catpower Production: You can boost the rate at which Hunters generate catpower using the Composite Bow (+50%), Crossbow (+25%), and Railgun (+25%).
  • Hunting Bonuses: To increase the yield of Furs and Ivory per hunt, you can research various tiers of gear, starting with Bolas (+1.0) and Hunting Armour (+2.0), followed by smaller increments from Steel Armour, Alloy Armour, and Nanosuits. These bonuses are additive.

Strategic Utility

In the early game, there is often a choice between researching Archery or Mining. Most strategic guides recommend prioritising Mining first, as hunting starts very weak and the colony initially lacks the spare kittens to compensate for the rapid consumption of Furs and Ivory. However, hunting is essential long-term because Furs and Ivory provide a +10% happiness boost, which improves the overall production efficiency of all kittens.

Iron Will and Zebra Accumulation

Archery is the strategic pivot point for the specialised “Iron Will” (IW) mode, where the player progresses without any kitten housing:

  • Zebra Discovery: In IW mode, Zebras serve as the primary source of catpower (acting as passive Hunters) and begin to appear only after Archery is researched.
  • The Reset Loop: A common strategy involves researching Archery and then immediately resetting the game. Doing this while in Iron Will increases your maximum Zebra limit for the next run.
  • Prestige Setup: Players often perform 6 to 10 of these short “Archery resets” to accumulate 50–60 Zebras. This provides a permanent, efficient catpower source that bypasses the need to feed kittens, significantly accelerating mid-game economic stability.

item.title: Artificial Intelligence
item.description:
Artificial Intelligence is an advanced late-game science that serves as the gateway to quantum computing and high-tier automation. It is researched in the Science tab for 250,000 Science and 150 Blueprints.

The AI Core and Gigaflops

Researching this technology unlocks the AI Core building, a megastructure that produces Gigaflops.

  • Production: Each AI Core generates +0.02 Gigaflops per tick.
  • Energy Consumption: AI Cores are power-intensive, consuming energy according to the formula: $2 + (1.5* number of AI Cores)$.
  • Risks (The AI Apocalypse): Gigaflops represent raw processing power that increases your “AI Level.” If your AI Level reaches 15, an AI Apocalypse occurs, causing you to start losing resources. Resetting the game is the only way to end an active AI Apocalypse and clear accumulated Gigaflops.

Workshop Upgrades and Synergies

Despite the risks, Artificial Intelligence provides critical upgrades that scale ground and space infrastructure:

Artificial Intelligence is an advanced late-game science that serves as the gateway to quantum computing and high-tier automation. It is researched in the Science tab for 250,000 Science and 150 Blueprints.

The AI Core and Gigaflops

Researching this technology unlocks the AI Core building, a megastructure that produces Gigaflops.

  • Production: Each AI Core generates +0.02 Gigaflops per tick.
  • Energy Consumption: AI Cores are power-intensive, consuming energy according to the formula: $2 + (1.5* number of AI Cores)$.
  • Risks (The AI Apocalypse): Gigaflops represent raw processing power that increases your “AI Level.” If your AI Level reaches 15, an AI Apocalypse occurs, causing you to start losing resources. Resetting the game is the only way to end an active AI Apocalypse and clear accumulated Gigaflops.

Workshop Upgrades and Synergies

Despite the risks, Artificial Intelligence provides critical upgrades that scale ground and space infrastructure:

  • Machine Learning: Increases the effectiveness of Data Centers by +10% for every AI Core you own.
  • AI Bases: Enhances Moon Base storage capacity by +10% per AI Core.
  • Neural Network: A powerful efficiency upgrade that doubles the effectiveness of all Engineers.
  • AI Engineers: Significantly improves the “know-how” of Engineers, allowing them to craft more resources per tick.

Strategic Management

To benefit from AI Cores without triggering an apocalypse, players must balance them with Entanglement Stations (unlocked via Quantum Cryptography).

  • Hash Production: Entanglement Stations consume 0.1 Gigaflops per tick to produce Hashes, which are used to reverse-engineer relics.
  • The Safe Ratio: It is generally recommended to maintain a ratio of roughly 5 AI Cores to 1 Entanglement Station to ensure Gigaflops are consumed as fast as they are produced, keeping the AI Level stable.
  • Transkittenism Policy: This policy allows your society to “merge with the AI.” It doubles Gigaflop production, prevents the AI Apocalypse from occurring, and strengthens both AI Bases and Machine Learning.

item.title: Astrophysicists
item.description:
Astrophysicists is a late-mid-game Workshop upgrade that allows your Scholar kittens to produce starcharts passively. This is a critical milestone for transitioning from manual observation of astronomical events to automated starchart production for deep-space exploration.

Costs and Prerequisites

To unlock and purchase this upgrade, you must meet the following requirements:

  • Technology: You must first research the Orbital Engineering science technology.
  • Science Cost: 250,000.
  • Resource Cost: 350 Unobtainium.

Core Effect

The primary function of the Astrophysicists upgrade is to augment the Scholar job:
item.content:encoded:
Astrophysicists is a late-mid-game Workshop upgrade that allows your Scholar kittens to produce starcharts passively. This is a critical milestone for transitioning from manual observation of astronomical events to automated starchart production for deep-space exploration.

Costs and Prerequisites

To unlock and purchase this upgrade, you must meet the following requirements:

  • Technology: You must first research the Orbital Engineering science technology.
  • Science Cost: 250,000.
  • Resource Cost: 350 Unobtainium.

Core Effect

The primary function of the Astrophysicists upgrade is to augment the Scholar job:

  • Starchart Generation: Every kitten assigned to the Scholar job will generate +0.0005 starcharts per second.
  • Continued Science Output: Scholars continue to produce their base science (+0.035 per tick) while simultaneously generating starcharts.

Strategic Utility

  • Automating Space Missions: Early in the game, starcharts are primarily obtained by manually clicking on astronomical events in the log. Astrophysicists provides a reliable, passive income of starcharts, which are mandatory for launching rockets and establishing space missions to planets like Redmoon, Dune, and Piscine.
  • Scaling Starchart Production: While individual Scholars provide a small amount, a large population of Scholars (boosted by upgrades like Neural Network) can significantly accelerate starchart accumulation.
  • Complementary Structures: This upgrade works alongside other starchart-generating structures such as Satellites (+0.005/sec), Research Vessels (+0.05/sec), and Space Beacons (+0.125/sec) to meet the high starchart demands of late-game missions.

item.title: Atheism Challenge
item.description:
The Atheism Challenge is a significant milestone within the “Special Modes” of Kittens Game, designed to bridge the gap between standard play and the advanced Relic Era. It is unlocked through the Adjustment Bureau metaphysics upgrade.

The Atheism Challenge Overview

The primary restriction of this mode is the complete removal of the Order of the Sun, which means players receive no faith-based production bonus (Solar Revolution) throughout the run.

  • Goal: Successfully reset the game while owning at least one Cryochamber.
  • Infrastructure Requirements: To reach the goal, you must research Chronophysics, Tachyon Theory, and Void Space. A single cryochamber costs 100 Void, 2 Time Crystals, and 1 Karma.
  • Preparation: It is highly recommended to enter the challenge with a minimum of 63 Time Crystals and 1 Relic to ensure you can afford the necessary late-game research and structures without the help of a faith bonus.

Atheism in the Context of Special Modes

Challenges in Kittens Game are “Special Modes” that impose specific constraints in exchange for permanent, stacking rewards.
item.content:encoded:
The Atheism Challenge is a significant milestone within the “Special Modes” of Kittens Game, designed to bridge the gap between standard play and the advanced Relic Era. It is unlocked through the Adjustment Bureau metaphysics upgrade.

The Atheism Challenge Overview

The primary restriction of this mode is the complete removal of the Order of the Sun, which means players receive no faith-based production bonus (Solar Revolution) throughout the run.

  • Goal: Successfully reset the game while owning at least one Cryochamber.
  • Infrastructure Requirements: To reach the goal, you must research Chronophysics, Tachyon Theory, and Void Space. A single cryochamber costs 100 Void, 2 Time Crystals, and 1 Karma.
  • Preparation: It is highly recommended to enter the challenge with a minimum of 63 Time Crystals and 1 Relic to ensure you can afford the necessary late-game research and structures without the help of a faith bonus.

Atheism in the Context of Special Modes

Challenges in Kittens Game are “Special Modes” that impose specific constraints in exchange for permanent, stacking rewards.

  • Negative Synergies: Combining Atheism with other challenges often creates severe bottlenecks. For example, running Atheism and Unicorn Tears simultaneously makes generating unicorn resources nearly impossible, as the faith bonus is one of the few multipliers affecting them.
  • Resource Management: In most challenges, including Atheism, Chronospheres do not bring resources into the run. Instead, those resources are placed in reserves and can only be reclaimed after the challenge is completed.
  • Iron Will Interaction: While Iron Will (the kittenless mode) is technically a “Special Mode,” it does not require the Adjustment Bureau to unlock. Attempting Atheism within an Iron Will run is exceptionally difficult due to the lack of worker-based production and faith multipliers.

Strategic Rewards

The rewards for completing Atheism focus on removing the standard caps on faith-based production, making it essential for late-game optimisation:

Reward Type Effect
Base Reward The Solar Revolution cap increases by 100 percentage points per Transcendence tier. This is equivalent to owning 20 Black Obelisks.
Increasing Reward Each subsequent completion increases Solar Revolution effectiveness by 10% (capped at 400%). This effect is multiplicative with Black Obelisks.

Completion of the challenge also allows for the construction of more cryochambers in future runs, provided you have the support of enough Chronospheres. This is vital for carrying over a larger population of skilled kittens into new timelines.

item.title: Augmentations
item.description:
Augmentations is a late-game Workshop upgrade that significantly boosts the productivity of your entire workforce by enhancing the effectiveness of kitten job skills.

Costs and Prerequisites

To unlock this upgrade, you must first research the Nanotechnology science technology. Once researched, the upgrade becomes available in the Workshop for the following resources:

  • Science: 150,000
  • Titanium: 5,000
  • Uranium: 50

Core Effect: Skill Enhancement

The primary function of Augmentations is to make kitten job skills 100% more effective.

Core Effect: Skill Enhancement

The primary function of Augmentations is to make kitten job skills 100% more effective.

  • Broad Impact: Because it targets the skill system itself, this upgrade provides a productivity increase for all jobs, including Woodcutters, Farmers, Scholars, Hunters, Miners, [Priests] ( /job/priest/), and Geologists.
  • Mechanical Scaling: The bonus from Augmentations multiplies with the base skill bonus a kitten has earned through experience (such as the +18.75% bonus from a Master-level kitten).
  • Additive Stacking: This 100% boost is additive with the Logistics workshop upgrade, which provides a separate 15% increase to skill effectiveness. When both are researched, your kittens’ total skill-based production bonuses are increased by 115%.

Strategic Utility

Augmentations is a vital milestone for late-game industrial scaling. As your kittens reach higher mastery levels (like Master or Proficient), the multiplicative nature of this upgrade allows you to reach significantly higher production yields for the same population. This is especially useful for overcoming mid-to-late game bottlenecks in wood, minerals, and science, as it improves the output of every specialized worker simultaneously.

item.title: Automated_Plants
item.description:
Automated Plants is a mid-to-late-game Workshop upgrade that enhances the passive steel production capabilities of your Calciners.

Costs and Prerequisites

To purchase this upgrade, you must have researched the Robotics science technology.

  • Science Cost: 200,000
  • Resource Cost: 750 Alloy
  • Prerequisite Upgrade: You must first purchase Steel Plants in the Workshop.

Core Effect

The primary function of Automated Plants is to scale the effectiveness of the Steel Plants upgrade using your village’s industrial efficiency:

  • Craft Ratio Bonus: It applies 25% of your general craft ratio as a bonus to the steel produced by Calciners.
  • Resource Efficiency: This bonus increases the steel yield without increasing the consumption of iron or coal.

Mechanical Context

To understand the value of Automated Plants, it is helpful to look at the progression of Calciner steel upgrades:
item.content:encoded:
Automated Plants is a mid-to-late-game Workshop upgrade that enhances the passive steel production capabilities of your Calciners.

Costs and Prerequisites

To purchase this upgrade, you must have researched the Robotics science technology.

  • Science Cost: 200,000
  • Resource Cost: 750 Alloy
  • Prerequisite Upgrade: You must first purchase Steel Plants in the Workshop.

Core Effect

The primary function of Automated Plants is to scale the effectiveness of the Steel Plants upgrade using your village’s industrial efficiency:

  • Craft Ratio Bonus: It applies 25% of your general craft ratio as a bonus to the steel produced by Calciners.
  • Resource Efficiency: This bonus increases the steel yield without increasing the consumption of iron or coal.

Mechanical Context

To understand the value of Automated Plants, it is helpful to look at the progression of Calciner steel upgrades:

  1. Steel Plants: This initial upgrade allows Calciners to automatically convert 10% of their iron output into steel (at a 100:1 ratio).
  2. Automated Plants: Leverages your Workshop and Factory bonuses to boost that output.
  3. Nuclear Plants: A subsequent upgrade (unlocked via Nuclear Fission) that further boosts this production by 2% per active Reactor.

Strategic Utility

Automated Plants is essential for transitioning away from manual steel crafting. While the “Theology hurdle” often requires manual clicking to get enough steel for Steamworks and early storage, this upgrade allows your industrial grid to produce significant quantities of steel passively. Because it scales with your craft ratio, it becomes increasingly powerful as you cap your Workshops (+6% each) and Factories (+5% each).

item.title: Barges
item.description:
Barges is a mid-game workshop upgrade that significantly expands your colony’s energy and industrial capacity by increasing the maximum coal storage from Harbours by 50%.

Costs and Unlocking

To access the Barges upgrade, you must first research the Industrialisation technology. Once unlocked, the upgrade requires the following resources to purchase:

  • 100,000 Science
  • 1,500 Titanium
  • 30 Blueprints

Mechanical Effects

The primary function of Barges is to enhance the utility of Harbours, which are high-capacity storage buildings unlocked by Navigation.
item.content:encoded:
Barges is a mid-game workshop upgrade that significantly expands your colony’s energy and industrial capacity by increasing the maximum coal storage from Harbours by 50%.

Costs and Unlocking

To access the Barges upgrade, you must first research the Industrialisation technology. Once unlocked, the upgrade requires the following resources to purchase:

  • 100,000 Science
  • 1,500 Titanium
  • 30 Blueprints

Mechanical Effects

The primary function of Barges is to enhance the utility of Harbours, which are high-capacity storage buildings unlocked by Navigation.

  • Storage Scaling: While a base Harbour provides +100 max coal, the Barges upgrade applies a 50% increase to this specific contribution.
  • Multiplicative Interaction: The bonus from Barges is unique because it multiplies with other effects affecting Harbour storage, rather than just being added to the base value. This synergy makes it increasingly valuable as you construct more Harbours and acquire other storage multipliers.

Strategic Utility

Expanding coal storage is a critical step in transitioning to heavy industry:

  • Steel Production: Coal is a mandatory component for crafting Steel (100 coal and 100 iron), which is used for advanced components like Gears and Alloy.
  • Steamworks Management: Coal is the primary fuel for Steamworks, which provide a boost to Magnetos and can automate the production of manuscripts. However, Steamworks consume a large amount of coal, making high storage caps necessary to prevent production slumps.
  • Overcoming terrestrial limits: As terrestrial buildings like Barns and Warehouses reach their cost-prohibitive levels, Harbours (enhanced by Barges and Expanded Cargo) become the most efficient way to scale storage for the resources needed to reach the Space Era.

item.title: Big Stick Policy
item.description:
In Kittens Game, the Big Stick Policy is a mid-game Foreign policy that makes building Embassies cheaper. It is part of the isolationist branch of the policy tree and is designed to help players reach higher embassy levels with other civilisations more efficiently.

Mechanics and Costs

  • Effect: Reduces the cost of all Embassies by 15%.
  • Cost: 4,000 Culture.
  • Prerequisites: You must have researched Astronomy and enacted the Isolationism policy.
  • Mutual Exclusivity: Choosing this policy permanently locks out the City On A Hill policy for the remainder of the run.

Strategic Utility

While often regarded as a niche choice, the Big Stick Policy has specific applications depending on your current goals:
item.content:encoded:
In Kittens Game, the Big Stick Policy is a mid-game Foreign policy that makes building Embassies cheaper. It is part of the isolationist branch of the policy tree and is designed to help players reach higher embassy levels with other civilisations more efficiently.

Mechanics and Costs

  • Effect: Reduces the cost of all Embassies by 15%.
  • Cost: 4,000 Culture.
  • Prerequisites: You must have researched Astronomy and enacted the Isolationism policy.
  • Mutual Exclusivity: Choosing this policy permanently locks out the City On A Hill policy for the remainder of the run.

Strategic Utility

While often regarded as a niche choice, the Big Stick Policy has specific applications depending on your current goals:

  • Naga Trade Synergies: This policy is often preferred over its counterparts when players are focused on Naga exchanges. Because Nagas provide minerals in exchange for ivory, reaching the embassy thresholds required to unlock rare Naga resources (like slabs or blueprints) is easier with cheaper building costs.
  • Comparative Value: Strategic advice suggests that while both Big Stick Policy and City On A Hill are relatively weak compared to late-game options, Big Stick Policy is generally considered to have more practical usefulness because it provides a tangible resource discount.
  • Discovery Path: It sits opposite the Diplomacy -> Cultural Exchange path. If you choose the Isolationism route, you are prioritising lower trade gold costs and cheaper embassies over the catpower discounts and culture boosts found in the Diplomacy route.

Context in the Policy Tree

The Big Stick Policy represents a “speak softly but carry a big stick” philosophy, focusing on using your military or economic weight to organise your relationships with the other races of Cath. In the long term, most players eventually transition toward policies like Outer Space Treaty or more advanced government forms as they move into the space and eludium eras.

item.title: Biofuel Processing
item.description:
Biofuel Processing is a mid-game Workshop upgrade that transforms your Bio Labs into automated oil production facilities, providing a vital passive source of fuel at the cost of catnip and energy.

Costs and Prerequisites

To unlock this upgrade, you must first research the Biochemistry science technology. Once discovered, the upgrade can be purchased in the Workshop for:

  • Science: 150,000
  • Titanium: 1,250

Core Effects on Bio Labs

Researching Biofuel Processing significantly changes the resource profile of every active Bio Lab:
item.content:encoded:
Biofuel Processing is a mid-game Workshop upgrade that transforms your Bio Labs into automated oil production facilities, providing a vital passive source of fuel at the cost of catnip and energy.

Costs and Prerequisites

To unlock this upgrade, you must first research the Biochemistry science technology. Once discovered, the upgrade can be purchased in the Workshop for:

  • Science: 150,000
  • Titanium: 1,250

Core Effects on Bio Labs

Researching Biofuel Processing significantly changes the resource profile of every active Bio Lab:

  • Automated Oil Production: Each Bio Lab will produce 0.10 oil per second (+0.02 per tick).
  • Catnip Consumption: This production consumes 5 catnip per second (-1 per tick).
  • Energy Drain: Active Bio Labs will consume 1 Watt (Wt) of energy each.
  • Science Storage: The upgrade also provides a +35% bonus to the maximum science storage of the Bio Lab.

Strategic Utility

  • Passive Oil Generation: This upgrade is essential for maintaining a steady oil income without relying solely on Oil Wells. It is particularly effective if you have a massive surplus of catnip and can afford the food cost.
  • Synergy with GM Catnip: The oil yield from Bio Labs can be further enhanced by the GM Catnip upgrade (unlocked via Genetics), which increases their oil production by 60% without increasing the catnip cost.
  • Late-Game Automation: In the late game, players often use Engineers to auto-convert this oil into Kerosene, ensuring that oil production never halts due to reaching storage caps.
  • Pollution Note: Bio Labs are listed as buildings that contribute to pollution, and Biofuel Processing increases their industrial activity.

item.title: Black Core
item.description:
A Black Core is a late-game Cryptotheology building that increases your maximum limit of Black Liquid Sorrow (BLS) by +1%. This expansion of the sorrow cap is essential for scaling your religious infrastructure as you approach the endgame.

Costs and Requirements

  • Initial Cost: 10,000 Relics.
  • Price Ratio: 1.15.
  • Prerequisite: You must reach Transcendence Tier 5 to unlock it.

Strategic Utility

The Black Core is a fundamental piece of the “Relic Engine” because it allows for the continued construction of Black Pyramids:
item.content:encoded:
A Black Core is a late-game Cryptotheology building that increases your maximum limit of Black Liquid Sorrow (BLS) by +1%. This expansion of the sorrow cap is essential for scaling your religious infrastructure as you approach the endgame.

Costs and Requirements

  • Initial Cost: 10,000 Relics.
  • Price Ratio: 1.15.
  • Prerequisite: You must reach Transcendence Tier 5 to unlock it.

Strategic Utility

The Black Core is a fundamental piece of the “Relic Engine” because it allows for the continued construction of Black Pyramids:

  • Bypassing the Sorrow Cap: The base storage cap for Black Liquid Sorrow (BLS) is 16. Since each Black Pyramid requires 5 units of sorrow to build, you are naturally restricted in how many pyramids you can own.
  • Scaling Pyramids: By building Black Cores, you increase the BLS limit, allowing you to accumulate the sorrow necessary to purchase more pyramids.
  • Synergy with Relic Production: Increasing your pyramid count is critical for the Black Nexus. The Black Nexus improves relic production from space beacons and Time Crystal refinement by a factor determined by your total number of Black Pyramids.

Operational Context

The Black Core belongs to Phase 3 (Late/Endgame) of development. It is a permanent investment that carries over through resets, provided you research the “Cryptotheology” technology in each new run to view the buildings you have purchased.

At this stage, players typically focus on “chasing infinity” by using these cores to maximise the efficiency of their Time Crystal and Relic engines.

item.title: Black Library
item.description:
The Black Library is an advanced Cryptotheology building used to scale your science storage cap by enhancing the effectiveness of your existing religious and scientific upgrades. It is a permanent structure that carries over through resets, allowing for exponential growth in science capacity across multiple runs.

Requirements and Costs

Because it is part of the endgame “Phase 3” progression, the requirements for the Black Library are steep:

  • Cost: 30,000 Relics.
  • Price Ratio: 1.15.
  • Prerequisite: You must have attained Transcendence Tier 9.
  • Technology: You must research the Cryptotheology technology each run to view or purchase these buildings.

Primary Effect: Codex Scaling

The Black Library focuses on improving the Codex Leviathanianus, a metaphysics upgrade that increases your compendia science limit based on your Transcendence tier.
item.content:encoded:
