It is a permanent structure that carries over through resets, allowing for exponential growth in science capacity across multiple runs.

Requirements and Costs

Because it is part of the endgame “Phase 3” progression, the requirements for the Black Library are steep:

  • Cost: 30,000 Relics.
  • Price Ratio: 1.15.
  • Prerequisite: You must have attained Transcendence Tier 9.
  • Technology: You must research the Cryptotheology technology each run to view or purchase these buildings.

Primary Effect: Codex Scaling

The Black Library focuses on improving the Codex Leviathanianus, a metaphysics upgrade that increases your compendia science limit based on your Transcendence tier.

  • Scaling Bonus: Each Black Library improves the Codex Leviathanianus scaling by +2%.
  • Science Storage: This allows Compendiums to continue providing +10 science storage even after you have reached the standard science cap provided by buildings.

Synergies and Advanced Scaling

The Black Library is highly integrated with other late-game religious and industrial systems:

Synergy Component Effect on Black Library
Unicorn Graveyard Directly improves the bonus provided by the Black Library.
Pact of Purity Increases the Black Library ratio by +0.05% for every Black Pyramid you own.
Transcendence As your Transcendence tier increases, the base effectiveness of the Codex it scales also rises.

Strategic Context

In the larger context of a “Relic Engine” run, the Black Library is essential for bypassing the science caps required for the most expensive endgame technologies, such as Exophysics (25M Science) or advanced space structures. By stacking Black Libraries and Unicorn Graveyards, you ensure that your stockpile of Compendiums provides a massive, stable foundation for your scientific research.

item.title: Black Nexus
item.description:
A Black Nexus is a high-tier Cryptotheology building found in the Religion tab that serves as a cornerstone for scaling your late-game relic production. It is designed to make the conversion of Time Crystals into Relics more efficient and to boost the passive generation of relics from space-based structures.

Core Mechanics and Costs

  • Cost: 5,000 Relics.
  • Price Ratio: 1.15.
  • Prerequisite: You must have attained Transcendence Tier 3 to unlock it.
  • Synergy: Its effectiveness is directly tied to the number of Black Pyramids you have constructed.

Primary Effects

The Black Nexus enhances two specific methods of obtaining relics:
item.content:encoded:
A Black Nexus is a high-tier Cryptotheology building found in the Religion tab that serves as a cornerstone for scaling your late-game relic production. It is designed to make the conversion of Time Crystals into Relics more efficient and to boost the passive generation of relics from space-based structures.

Core Mechanics and Costs

  • Cost: 5,000 Relics.
  • Price Ratio: 1.15.
  • Prerequisite: You must have attained Transcendence Tier 3 to unlock it.
  • Synergy: Its effectiveness is directly tied to the number of Black Pyramids you have constructed.

Primary Effects

The Black Nexus enhances two specific methods of obtaining relics:

  1. Time Crystal Refinement: Standard refinement converts 25 Time Crystals into 1 Relic. With a Black Nexus, the yield increases according to the formula: 1 + (Black Nexus × Black Pyramid) relics per 25 crystals.
  2. Relic Station Production: It significantly boosts the output of Relic Stations (upgraded Space Beacons). Each Black Nexus improves this production by 10% per Black Pyramid.

Strategic Utility: The “Type 1 Relic Engine”

In the mid-to-late game, the Black Nexus is a vital part of what players call the “Type 1 Relic Engine”.

  • Scaling Passive Income: Once you have at least 5,000 maximum Antimatter, Relic Stations produce 0.01 relics per day. By stacking Black Nexuses and Black Pyramids, you can increase this passive daily income to a point where you no longer rely solely on manual trading with Leviathans for your relic supply.
  • Synergy with Black Sky: Completing the Black Sky challenge provides an “invisible” Black Pyramid, which permanently improves the scaling of your Black Nexus buildings in all future runs.
  • Late-Game Goal: Experienced players recommend buying several levels of Black Nexus alongside Black Core (to increase the sorrow limit for more pyramids) to maximise the efficiency of your time-skipping and relic-farming operations.

Comparison Table: Relic Scaling

Feature Standard Effect With Black Nexus
TC to Relic Ratio 25:1 25 : (1 + Nexus × Pyramid)
Beacon Production 0.01 Relics/day +10% boost per Pyramid level
Unlock Level Theology Tech Transcendence Tier 3

item.title: Black Obelisk
item.description:
A Black Obelisk is a permanent endgame building found in the Cryptotheology section of the Religion tab. Its primary function is to increase the Solar Revolution production bonus cap, allowing your kitten civilisation to benefit from higher levels of faith-based productivity.

Cost & Scaling

  • Tab: Religion –> Cryptotheology
  • Unlock Requirement: Requires building at least one Black Pyramid (via Ziggurats) to access the Cryptotheology panel.
  • Cost: Scales exponentially with each purchased rank:
  • Relics: approx 500 times 1.15^N
  • Void: approx 5 times 1.15^N
  • Reset Behavior: Permanent. Like all Cryptotheology upgrades, Black Obelisks persist across all future resets.

Core Statistics

  • Prerequisite: You must have attained at least Transcendence Tier 1.
  • Fidelity: Like all Cryptotheology buildings, Black Obelisks carry over through resets; however, you must research the “Cryptotheology” technology in each new run to view or purchase them.

The Solar Revolution Cap

The standard Solar Revolution bonus is typically capped at 1000%, with diminishing returns beginning at 750%. Black Obelisks are the primary method for raising this ceiling:
item.content:encoded:
A Black Obelisk is a permanent endgame building found in the Cryptotheology section of the Religion tab. Its primary function is to increase the Solar Revolution production bonus cap, allowing your kitten civilisation to benefit from higher levels of faith-based productivity.

Cost & Scaling

  • Tab: Religion –> Cryptotheology
  • Unlock Requirement: Requires building at least one Black Pyramid (via Ziggurats) to access the Cryptotheology panel.
  • Cost: Scales exponentially with each purchased rank:
  • Relics: approx 500 times 1.15^N
  • Void: approx 5 times 1.15^N
  • Reset Behavior: Permanent. Like all Cryptotheology upgrades, Black Obelisks persist across all future resets.

Core Statistics

  • Prerequisite: You must have attained at least Transcendence Tier 1.
  • Fidelity: Like all Cryptotheology buildings, Black Obelisks carry over through resets; however, you must research the “Cryptotheology” technology in each new run to view or purchase them.

The Solar Revolution Cap

The standard Solar Revolution bonus is typically capped at 1000%, with diminishing returns beginning at 750%. Black Obelisks are the primary method for raising this ceiling:

  • Scaling Formula: Every obelisk improves the cap by +5% per Transcendence Tier.
  • Multiplicative Synergies: This effect is multiplicative with the rewards gained from completing the Atheism Challenge.

Strategic Context

In the late game (Phase 3), the Black Obelisk is often compared to the Atheism Challenge reward. Completing the Atheism Challenge provides a base reward that increases the Solar Revolution cap by 100 percentage points per Transcendence Tier, which the sources note is the equivalent of owning 20 Black Obelisks.

For players focusing on a “Relic Engine” run, stacking these obelisks alongside high Transcendence Tiers is essential for maximizing global production modifiers.

What It Does

  • Raises the Solar Revolution Diminishing Returns Limit:

    • Base Solar Revolution provides a massive global percentage boost to all production, but it normally begins hitting diminishing returns around a theoretical maximum (base cap around $1,000%$).
    • Each Black Obelisk increases the soft/hard cap ceiling of your Solar Revolution bonus by $+5%$.
    • The formula scales additively per rank:

    {Solar Revolution Cap Multiplier} = 1 + (0.05 times Black Obelisks)

  • Synergy with Void Resonators & Time Shattering:

    • When shattering Time Crystals, Void Resonators project your Solar Revolution bonus across skipped years.
    • Without Black Obelisks, your massive accumulated faith hits a hard plateau. Black Obelisks allow that bonus to keep climbing into thousands of percent of global production.

Strategic Priority

Upgrade Primary Focus Synergy with Black Obelisk
Black Nexus Boosts Relic/TC trade yields Fuels the Relics needed to buy Obelisks
Event Horizon Multiplies storage caps Lets you store more Unobtainium per shatter
Black Obelisk Scales faith production ceiling Multiplies the output of all ground resources

item.title: Black Radiance
item.description:
Black Radiance is an advanced Cryptotheology building that accelerates the rate at which Alicorns are corrupted into Necrocorns. It is a permanent structure that carries over through resets, provided you research the Cryptotheology technology in each new run.

Cost and Requirements

  • Cost: 37.5K Relics.
  • Price Ratio: 1.15.
  • Prerequisite: Transcendence Tier 12.

Core Effects

The primary function of Black Radiance is to speed up the corruption countdown initiated by Markers.

  • Corruption Bonus: The approximate bonus to corruption speed is 3.464% multiplied by the square root of (number of Black Radiances $\times$ points of Black Liquid Sorrow).
  • Synergy: Because the bonus depends on your current Black Liquid Sorrow (BLS), its effectiveness increases as you accumulate more sorrow or build Black Cores to raise your sorrow limit.

Strategic Utility

In the late-game “Relic Engine” phase, Black Radiance is used to optimize the generation of Necrocorns:

  • Trade Efficiency: Higher Leviathan energy results in more Time Crystals and Relics per trade, making Black Radiance a vital component for accelerating the growth of your endgame resources.

item.title: Blazar
item.description:
A Blazar is a high-tier Cryptotheology building that serves as a cornerstone for the late-game “time crystal engine”. It is a permanent structure that carries over through resets, though you must research the Cryptotheology technology in each new run to access its benefits.

Requirements and Cost

Because it is a pinnacle endgame structure, the barriers to entry are significant:

  • Cost: 50,000 Relics.
  • Price Ratio: 1.15.
  • Prerequisite: Transcendence Tier 15. Reaching this tier requires a massive accumulation of Epiphany (roughly 3.04 million percent).

Core Effects and Multipliers

Each level of Blazar provides stacking bonuses to several critical late-game mechanics:
item.content:encoded:
A Blazar is a high-tier Cryptotheology building that serves as a cornerstone for the late-game “time crystal engine”. It is a permanent structure that carries over through resets, though you must research the Cryptotheology technology in each new run to access its benefits.

Requirements and Cost

Because it is a pinnacle endgame structure, the barriers to entry are significant:

  • Cost: 50,000 Relics.
  • Price Ratio: 1.15.
  • Prerequisite: Transcendence Tier 15. Reaching this tier requires a massive accumulation of Epiphany (roughly 3.04 million percent).

Core Effects and Multipliers

Each level of Blazar provides stacking bonuses to several critical late-game mechanics:

  • Resource Retrieval: Improves effectiveness by 2%. This is vital for “shatter engines,” as it increases the resources gained when you skip years using Time Crystals.
  • Time Manipulation: Improves Chronomancy by 2.5%.
  • Unicorn Generation: Improves Unicornmancy by 2.5%.
  • Dark Future Mitigation: Improves Time Impedance by 10%. This helps suppress the temporal penalties encountered once your calendar year exceeds 40,000.

Strategic Utility

The Blazar is primarily used to transition into the “Type 2 Relic Engine” and beyond.

  • Shatter Engine Efficiency: By boosting Resource Retrieval, Blazars allow you to reach a “break-even” point where shattering a Time Crystal provides enough Unobtainium or Alicorns to immediately regain that crystal through trading or sacrifice.
  • Relic Scaling: In the late game, relics are often generated by refining Time Crystals. Blazars, along with Black Nexuses, make this process far more productive, eventually allowing for the “positive resets” necessary to reach the theoretical limits of the game.
  • Infinite Loop Resets: For players aiming to achieve “Infinity”, Blazars are used to grow the Unobtainium stockpile exponentially across short runs, enabling the construction of up to 100 Chronospheres for massive resource carry-over.

While reaching Transcendence Tier 15 is a daunting task, the Blazar is the primary tool used to overcome the late-game bottlenecks of Time Crystals and Relics.

item.title: Bolas
item.description:
Bolas is an early-game Workshop upgrade that serves as a throwing weapon to improve the results of your hunts. You can unlock this upgrade after researching the Mining science technology. It costs 1,000 Science, 250 Minerals, and 50 Wood to purchase.

The primary effect of Bolas is to provide a flat +1.0 hunting bonus. This bonus makes your hunters twice as effective, resulting in an 80% to 100% increase in the amount of fur and ivory collected per hunt. Specifically, the expected fur yield increases from 39.50 to 71.50, and the expected ivory yield increases from 10.78 to 20.24.
item.content:encoded:
Bolas is an early-game Workshop upgrade that serves as a throwing weapon to improve the results of your hunts. You can unlock this upgrade after researching the Mining science technology. It costs 1,000 Science, 250 Minerals, and 50 Wood to purchase.

The primary effect of Bolas is to provide a flat +1.0 hunting bonus. This bonus makes your hunters twice as effective, resulting in an 80% to 100% increase in the amount of fur and ivory collected per hunt. Specifically, the expected fur yield increases from 39.50 to 71.50, and the expected ivory yield increases from 10.78 to 20.24.

These bonuses are additive with other hunting upgrades. For example, if you have researched both Bolas (+1.0) and Hunting Armour (+2.0), your total hunting bonus will be 3.0. This increased bonus expands the range of random integers the game uses to calculate your total resources per hunt.

In Iron Will mode, Bolas also helps with gold acquisition. Once Gold Ore is researched in this mode, each hunt has a 25% chance of yielding gold, and the amount produced is partially determined by your current hunting bonus .

item.title: Brewery
item.description:
The Brewery is an industrial building in Kittens Game that specializes in boosting the effects of festivals, often considered a non-essential but beneficial structure for players advancing into the mid-game and later religious/cultural phases.

Unlocking and Construction

The Brewery is part of a non-mandatory branch of the Technology tree.

  • Technology Prerequisite: The Brewery is unlocked by researching Drama and Poetry.
  • Cost: Building a Brewery requires a combination of common and luxury resources: 1000 Wood, 750 Culture, 5 Spice, and 375 Parchment.
  • Initial Advice: The technology that unlocks the Brewery, Drama and Poetry, is noted to be “waaaay too expensive to be useful” on a player’s first couple of runs, and players are advised to feel free to skip it initially.

Function and Consumption

The Brewery provides passive benefits related to festivals, and consumes two resources:

Unlocking and Construction

The Brewery is part of a non-mandatory branch of the Technology tree.

  • Technology Prerequisite: The Brewery is unlocked by researching Drama and Poetry.
  • Cost: Building a Brewery requires a combination of common and luxury resources: 1000 Wood, 750 Culture, 5 Spice, and 375 Parchment.
  • Initial Advice: The technology that unlocks the Brewery, Drama and Poetry, is noted to be “waaaay too expensive to be useful” on a player’s first couple of runs, and players are advised to feel free to skip it initially.

Function and Consumption

The Brewery provides passive benefits related to festivals, and consumes two resources:

Resource Effect/Consumption Source
Festival Happiness +1%
Festival Cycle Bonus +1%
Festival Kitten Speed +0.1%
Catnip Consumption -1 per Tick
Spice Consumption -0.1 per Tick

Strategic Context and Synergies

  1. Festival Enhancement: The Brewery’s effect on the “Festival Cycle Bonus” is important in the late game. If the Numeromancy Metaphysics upgrade is researched, the cycle-based bonuses granted by holding a festival are boosted, and Breweries further enhance these effects.
  2. Policy Interaction:
    • The Stoicism philosophy policy, which aims to reduce the consumption of luxury resources, provides a reduction of -25% to brewery consumption.
    • The foreign policy Shark Relations: Botanists grants a 1% Brewery catpower bonus.
  3. Resource Management: Breweries consume Spice, a luxury resource that gradually degrades over time and is sometimes received when trading with other races.

item.title: CAD System
item.description:
The CAD System is a mid-game Workshop upgrade that enhances your ability to craft blueprints by leveraging your existing scientific infrastructure. It effectively scales your crafting efficiency based on how many research buildings you have constructed.

Requirements and Prerequisites

To unlock and purchase the CAD System, you must meet the following criteria:

  • Science Cost: 125,000.
  • Titanium Cost: 750.
  • Technological Prerequisite: You must have researched Electronics.

Mechanics and Effects

The CAD System provides a +1% bonus to your blueprint craft ratio for every eligible scientific building in your village. This is particularly useful because blueprints are a major late-game bottleneck and normally require a high volume of science (25,000 per craft) to produce manually.
item.content:encoded:
The CAD System is a mid-game Workshop upgrade that enhances your ability to craft blueprints by leveraging your existing scientific infrastructure. It effectively scales your crafting efficiency based on how many research buildings you have constructed.

Requirements and Prerequisites

To unlock and purchase the CAD System, you must meet the following criteria:

  • Science Cost: 125,000.
  • Titanium Cost: 750.
  • Technological Prerequisite: You must have researched Electronics.

Mechanics and Effects

The CAD System provides a +1% bonus to your blueprint craft ratio for every eligible scientific building in your village. This is particularly useful because blueprints are a major late-game bottleneck and normally require a high volume of science (25,000 per craft) to produce manually.

Eligible Buildings

The bonus is calculated based on the total number of the following structures:

  • Libraries (or Data Centres).
  • Academies.
  • Observatories.
  • Bio Labs.

Note: Bio Labs contribute to this crafting bonus even if they are currently turned off or unpowered.

Strategic Utility

In the mid-to-late game, your scientific infrastructure typically grows quite large to accommodate the escalating science caps required for advanced technologies. The CAD System turns this necessary expansion into a tool for industrial scaling, making the transition into the “Space Era”—which requires hundreds of blueprints for structures like Steamworks and Magnetos—significantly more efficient.

item.title: Caravanserai
item.description:
Caravanserai is a critical mid-game Workshop upgrade that enhances your trade efficiency by improving relations with other civilizations.

Costs and Prerequisites

  • Science Cost: 25,000.
  • Resource Cost: 10,000 Ivory and 250 Gold.
  • Prerequisite Technology: You must first research Navigation.

Core Effects and Mechanics

The primary function of Caravanserai is to allow your Tradeposts to influence race standing:

  • Standing Bonus: Once researched, every Tradepost you build provides a flat +0.35% bonus to trade relations.
  • Hostility Mitigation: This bonus manifests as a 0.35% decrease in the probability of a “hostile event” (where a race gives you no resources) and a 0.175% increase in “friendly events” (yielding 15–25% extra resources).
  • Synergy with Diplomacy: If you have the Diplomacy metaphysics upgrade, the effectiveness of your Tradeposts in improving standing is further increased.

Strategic Importance

The main purpose of Caravanserai is to manage hostile races, specifically the Zebras, who are your primary source of Titanium.

Strategic Importance

The main purpose of Caravanserai is to manage hostile races, specifically the Zebras, who are your primary source of Titanium.

  • Negating Hostility: Without this upgrade, Zebras have a high chance to simply send your kittens packing with no resources.
  • Efficiency Benchmarks: With Caravanserai active, building 85 Tradeposts will completely negate the Zebra’s hostility, ensuring every trade is successful. If you also have the Diplomacy upgrade, this benchmark is reduced to only 58 Tradeposts.
  • Mid-Game Progression: Strategic guides recommend acquiring Caravanserai as soon as you begin the “Titanium buildup” phase to avoid wasting precious gold and catpower on failed trades.

item.title: Carbon Sequestration
item.description:
Carbon Sequestration is a late-game Workshop upgrade that allows your civilization to actively mitigate the negative effects of pollution. To unlock this upgrade, you must first research the Ecology science technology.

Costs and Prerequisites

  • Science Cost: 75,000.
  • Resource Costs: 1,250 Titanium, 125 Gears, 4,000 Steel, and 1,000 Alloy.
  • Prerequisite Technology: Ecology (which itself requires Combustion and 55 Blueprints).

Core Effects and Mechanics

The upgrade transforms your Factories from industrial polluters into tools for environmental recovery:
item.content:encoded:
Carbon Sequestration is a late-game Workshop upgrade that allows your civilization to actively mitigate the negative effects of pollution. To unlock this upgrade, you must first research the Ecology science technology.

Costs and Prerequisites

  • Science Cost: 75,000.
  • Resource Costs: 1,250 Titanium, 125 Gears, 4,000 Steel, and 1,000 Alloy.
  • Prerequisite Technology: Ecology (which itself requires Combustion and 55 Blueprints).

Core Effects and Mechanics

The upgrade transforms your Factories from industrial polluters into tools for environmental recovery:

  • Factory Pollution Reduction: It immediately reduces the pollution produced by all Factories to zero.
  • Active Carbon Capture: It enables a toggle for Factories to capture pollution from the atmosphere. When this mode is activated, each Factory consumes 4 Watts of energy (double its standard requirement) and reduces the global pollution level by 2 points per tick.
  • Enhanced UI and Management: The upgrade provides more detailed information via the pollution indicator in the Science tab and adds +/- buttons to all polluting buildings. This allows you to manually enable or disable specific structures to balance resource production against environmental health.

Strategic Utility

Managing pollution is critical because high levels of atmospheric CO2 negatively impact several areas of your village:

  • Production Penalties: High pollution reduces catnip production, which can lead to kitten starvation.
  • Civilian Penalties: It decreases kitten happiness and slows down the arrival speed of new kittens.
  • Religious Penalties: Eventually, extreme pollution can reduce the Solar Revolution bonus for certain resources.

While some pollution is considered inevitable, Carbon Sequestration is one of the few active methods to keep levels below the ~1,000 ppm threshold, where negative effects are generally negligible.

item.title: Celestial Mechanics
item.description:
Celestial Mechanics is an early-game Workshop upgrade that improves the rewards gained from observing the heavens.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Prerequisite: You must first research the Mathematics science technology.
  • Resource Cost: 250 Science.

Core Effects

The primary function of Celestial Mechanics is to increase the yield of Science (and Minerals from meteors) provided by random celestial occurrences.

  • Standard Bonus: In a normal run, it provides a 20% bonus to the science generated by astronomical events.
  • Iron Will Bonus: In Iron Will mode, where these events are a primary source of early science, the bonus is significantly increased to 60%.
  • Mathematical Impact: The game calculates science from astronomical events using the formula: (25 + Celestial Bonus) * (1 + Science Bonus) Science. Researching this upgrade sets the “Celestial Bonus” value to 5 (or 15 in Iron Will mode).

Strategic Importance

In the early game, particularly before you have a large population of Scholars, manual observation of astronomical events is a vital way to accumulate science. Celestial Mechanics makes each click more valuable, accelerating your path through the mid-game technology tree. For players in Iron Will mode, this upgrade is considered essential because astronomical events and meteors are the only initial ways to gain science and minerals.

item.title: Centaurus System Mission
item.description:
The Centaurus System Mission is a high-tier late-game space project that allows your kittens to travel to a warm, faraway star system. It represents one of the final stages of stellar exploration before reaching the theoretical “end of the universe”.

Mission Logistics and Costs

  • Unlock Prerequisite: You must first successfully complete the Rorschach Mission to unlock Centaurus.
  • Resource Requirements: The launch requires 100k Starcharts, 40k Titanium, 400k Science, 50k Kerosene, and 50k Thorium.
  • Travel Time: The base travel time is 120,000 game-days, which is approximately 2 days, 18 hours, and 40 minutes in real-time. This can be reduced by a factor of 75 (bringing it down to roughly 53 minutes) if you have researched both Thorium and Antimatter Drives.

Unlocked Infrastructure

Successfully reaching the Centaurus System provides access to powerful energy-generating structures:
item.content:encoded:
The Centaurus System Mission is a high-tier late-game space project that allows your kittens to travel to a warm, faraway star system. It represents one of the final stages of stellar exploration before reaching the theoretical “end of the universe”.

Mission Logistics and Costs

  • Unlock Prerequisite: You must first successfully complete the Rorschach Mission to unlock Centaurus.
  • Resource Requirements: The launch requires 100k Starcharts, 40k Titanium, 400k Science, 50k Kerosene, and 50k Thorium.
  • Travel Time: The base travel time is 120,000 game-days, which is approximately 2 days, 18 hours, and 40 minutes in real-time. This can be reduced by a factor of 75 (bringing it down to roughly 53 minutes) if you have researched both Thorium and Antimatter Drives.

Unlocked Infrastructure

Successfully reaching the Centaurus System provides access to powerful energy-generating structures:

  • Tectonic: A massive industrial project that rips open the planet near the Centaurus star to collect magma energy. It costs 600k Science, 500 Antimatter, and 75k Thorium to build and provides a base +25 Energy Production. It requires the Terraformation technology.
  • Molten Core: An advanced upgrade that costs 25M Science and 5M Uranium. Each level of Molten Core improves the effectiveness of Tectonic structures by 5%. It requires the Exophysics technology.

Strategic Progression

  • Challenge Unlocks: Completing the Centaurus Mission is the mandatory prerequisite to unlock the Energy Challenge. This challenge doubles energy consumption but rewards players with a permanent reduction in production penalties caused by negative energy.
  • Furthest Ring: Reaching the Centaurus System is the final requirement before you can launch the mission to the Furthest Ring, described as the end of the universe.
  • Endgame Utility: Because this mission and its associated buildings require massive amounts of Thorium, Antimatter, and Science, it is typically undertaken only after the player has established a robust “Shatter Engine” and significant science storage through structures like Space Beacons.

item.title: Charon Mission
item.description:
The Charon Mission is a significant late-game space project that takes your kittens to a small, incredibly dense dwarf planet on the far edge of the Helios system. Known colloquially as “The Gates of Death” due to its hostile and barren environment, it represents one of the final frontiers of planetary exploration before reaching the Centaurus system.

Mission Requirements and Unlocks

  • Prerequisite: You must successfully complete the Umbra Mission before the Charon Mission becomes available.
  • Launch Costs: This project requires a massive stockpile of advanced resources: 75,000 Starcharts, 750,000 Science, 35,000 Kerosene, and 35,000 Thorium.
  • Unlocks: Successfully landing on the planet unlocks the Charon Planet tab and the ability to construct the Entanglement Station.

Entanglement Stations

Once Charon is reached, you can build Entanglement Stations, which are essential for advanced quantum computing and hashrate generation.
item.content:encoded:
The Charon Mission is a significant late-game space project that takes your kittens to a small, incredibly dense dwarf planet on the far edge of the Helios system. Known colloquially as “The Gates of Death” due to its hostile and barren environment, it represents one of the final frontiers of planetary exploration before reaching the Centaurus system.

Mission Requirements and Unlocks

  • Prerequisite: You must successfully complete the Umbra Mission before the Charon Mission becomes available.
  • Launch Costs: This project requires a massive stockpile of advanced resources: 75,000 Starcharts, 750,000 Science, 35,000 Kerosene, and 35,000 Thorium.
  • Unlocks: Successfully landing on the planet unlocks the Charon Planet tab and the ability to construct the Entanglement Station.

Entanglement Stations

Once Charon is reached, you can build Entanglement Stations, which are essential for advanced quantum computing and hashrate generation.

  • Cost: Each station costs 1,250 Relics, 5,250 Antimatter, and 5,000 Eludium.
  • Function: These stations consume 25 Wt of energy and 0.1 gigaflops per tick (produced by AI Cores) to generate 0.1 hashes per tick.
  • Strategic Utility: Hashes are used to increase your hashrate level, which provides a +25% bonus to relic production from Space Beacons for every level achieved. This is a core component of the “Antimatter Phase” of the endgame, where players aim to automate and scale relic generation.

The Charon Cycle

“Charon” is also the first of the ten five-year celestial cycles, represented by the glyph ⍙. If you have researched Numerology and Numeromancy, the cycle introduces the following global modifiers:

  • Production Penalties: During this cycle, Lunar Outpost unobtainium output is reduced by 10%.
  • Operational Costs: Gigaflop consumption for Entanglement Stations is increased by +100% (doubled).
  • Festival Bonus: Holding a festival during the Charon cycle provides a 1.5x income multiplier for catnip, wood, and minerals.

Strategic Considerations

The Charon Mission is often viewed as a major resource gate because of its Thorium and Starchart requirements. By this stage, players generally rely on a robust “Shatter Engine” to skip through non-productive years and harvest enough antimatter to afford the Entanglement Stations. Additionally, because Entanglement Stations consume gigaflops, players must carefully balance the number of AI Cores and stations to prevent an AI Apocalypse, ensuring that gigaflop production stays ahead of consumption without allowing the AI level to reach critical thresholds.

item.title: Chrono Engineers
item.description:
Chronoengineers is a high-tier late-game Workshop upgrade that enhances the capabilities of your Engineer kittens, specifically allowing them to function during temporal manipulations.

Costs and Prerequisites

To access this upgrade, you must first research the Tachyon Theory science technology. Once unlocked, it can be purchased in the Workshop for the following resources:

  • Science: 500,000
  • Time Crystals: 5
  • Eludium: 100

Core Effects and Functionality

The upgrade provides two primary benefits to your automated workforce:
item.content:encoded:
Chronoengineers is a high-tier late-game Workshop upgrade that enhances the capabilities of your Engineer kittens, specifically allowing them to function during temporal manipulations.

Costs and Prerequisites

To access this upgrade, you must first research the Tachyon Theory science technology. Once unlocked, it can be purchased in the Workshop for the following resources:

  • Science: 500,000
  • Time Crystals: 5
  • Eludium: 100

Core Effects and Functionality

The upgrade provides two primary benefits to your automated workforce:

  1. Improved Engineer Know-how: It provides a flat +2 know-how bonus to all five classes of Engineers. While other upgrades like AI Engineers or Space Engineers provide higher specific class bonuses, Chronoengineers ensure a baseline efficiency boost across the entire job spectrum.
  2. Work During Time Skips: This is the upgrade’s most unique feature. It enables Engineers to continue their automated crafting tasks even when you are combusting Time Crystals to skip years.

Synergy with Resource Retrieval

When a time skip occurs, the amount of crafting performed by Chronoengineers is dictated by your Resource Retrieval level.

  • Automated Conversion: Just as Resource Retrieval allows you to collect a percentage of your annual production during a skip, Chronoengineers allow your Engineers to “catch up” on their work for that skipped period.
  • Material Consumption: It is important to note that this automated crafting consumes the required materials just like standard crafting; it does not produce resources “for free” during the skip.

This upgrade is essential for maintaining a stable industrial output during the late-game “shatter engine” phase, ensuring that your refined resource stocks (like Steel, Plate, or Alloy) continue to grow alongside your raw materials as you skip through the centuries.

item.title: Chronophysics
item.description:
Chronophysics is a pivotal mid-to-late game technology that marks the transition from simple space exploration to the manipulation of time itself. It is the primary gateway to carrying resources over through resets and unlocking the advanced “Void” and “Relic” phases of the game.

Requirements and Costs

Chronophysics is often the first technology players encounter that requires Time Crystals rather than standard resources.

  • Prerequisite: You must first research Particle Physics.
  • Science Cost: 250,000.
  • Special Cost: 5 Time Crystals.

Strategic Note: For your first run, obtaining these 5 Time Crystals usually requires trading 5,000 Unobtainium with the Leviathans or sacrificing 25 Alicorns at the Ziggurat.
item.content:encoded:
Chronophysics is a pivotal mid-to-late game technology that marks the transition from simple space exploration to the manipulation of time itself. It is the primary gateway to carrying resources over through resets and unlocking the advanced “Void” and “Relic” phases of the game.

Requirements and Costs

Chronophysics is often the first technology players encounter that requires Time Crystals rather than standard resources.

  • Prerequisite: You must first research Particle Physics.
  • Science Cost: 250,000.
  • Special Cost: 5 Time Crystals.

Strategic Note: For your first run, obtaining these 5 Time Crystals usually requires trading 5,000 Unobtainium with the Leviathans or sacrificing 25 Alicorns at the Ziggurat.

Key Unlocks

Researching Chronophysics unlocks three critical components for endgame progression:

Unlock Function
Chronosphere A mega-structure that allows you to carry over resources to a new reset. Each sphere preserves 1.5% of your non-crafted resources.
Flux Condensator A Workshop upgrade that allows Chronospheres to also preserve crafted resources (like Blueprints, Eludium, and Steel).
Stasis Chambers An upgrade that nearly doubles the storage capacity of your Accelerators.
Tachyon Theory The subsequent technology required to unlock the Chronoforge, Void Space, and the Atheism Challenge.

Synergy with Anachronomancy

One of the most powerful interactions in the game involves the Anachronomancy metaphysics upgrade.

  • Permanent Unlock: If you own Anachronomancy, Chronophysics is saved across resets.
  • Immediate Access: This means you start every future run with Chronophysics already researched. Combined with carried-over Time Crystals and Unobtainium, this allows you to build Chronospheres immediately at the start of a new run, drastically accelerating your recovery speed.

Strategic Context

You previously asked about resets and Iron Will. Chronophysics is the technology that makes resetting highly profitable rather than a complete restart. By building Chronospheres (unlocked here) and the Flux Condensator, you can carry over millions of blueprints and science resources, effectively bypassing the early-game “grind” entirely.

item.title: Chronosphere
item.description:
The Chronosphere is a crucial, high-tier Mega Structure in Kittens Game, unlocked late in the game’s progression. It is central to managing resources across multiple runs and is key to accessing the very late-game phases of Time and Void mechanics.

Here is a comprehensive breakdown of the Chronosphere:

1. Unlocks and Construction

The Chronosphere is unlocked by researching Chronophysics and requires extremely rare resources to build:

  • Technology Prerequisite: Chronophysics. Chronophysics itself requires 250,000 Science and 5 Time Crystal.
  • Base Cost: 2,500 Unobtainium, 1 Time Crystal, 100 Blueprint, and 250,000 Science.
  • Price Ratio: 1.25.

2. Core Functions and Effects

The Chronosphere has several critical, interrelated functions that affect resource management and game mechanics:
item.content:encoded:
The Chronosphere is a crucial, high-tier Mega Structure in Kittens Game, unlocked late in the game’s progression. It is central to managing resources across multiple runs and is key to accessing the very late-game phases of Time and Void mechanics.

Here is a comprehensive breakdown of the Chronosphere:

1. Unlocks and Construction

The Chronosphere is unlocked by researching Chronophysics and requires extremely rare resources to build:

  • Technology Prerequisite: Chronophysics. Chronophysics itself requires 250,000 Science and 5 Time Crystal.
  • Base Cost: 2,500 Unobtainium, 1 Time Crystal, 100 Blueprint, and 250,000 Science.
  • Price Ratio: 1.25.

2. Core Functions and Effects

The Chronosphere has several critical, interrelated functions that affect resource management and game mechanics:

  • Resource Preservation on Reset: Its main purpose is to preserve a percentage of your non-crafted, non-luxury resources upon resetting the game. Each Chronosphere preserves 1.5% of these resources (Catnip, Wood, Minerals, Oil, Uranium, etc.).
    • If the total preservation percentage exceeds 100%, you receive multiple units of those resources upon reset.
  • Void Generation: Chronospheres are necessary for generating Void. Void is a unique resource that is generated randomly every year change if you have Chronospheres.
  • Energy Consumption: It consumes -20 Energy per tick to operate.
  • Temporal Flux Generation (Upgrade): While the base function generates Temporal Flux at a rate of 5 units per minute when the game is not active, the Chronosurge upgrade causes each Chronosphere to generate 1 flux per year.
  • Temporal Paradox: It has an associated risk: “Occasional Temporal Paradox”.

3. Strategic Importance and Progression

The Chronosphere is strategically vital for transitioning into high-paragon, high-speed runs and the late-game resource cycles:

  • Accelerating Future Runs (The Seed): By building multiple Chronospheres, players can carry over essential late-game resources (like unobtanium, antimatter, and blueprints). This drastically speeds up subsequent runs, allowing players to immediately purchase most high-tier technologies and upgrades after a reset.
  • The Chrono-Reset Loop: The concept of the “quick” chrono-reset involves building Chronospheres out of the resource profit generated from the reset itself, leading to faster paragon farming.
  • Void Acquisition: The Void resource generated by Chronospheres is needed to unlock high-tier Metaphysics upgrades (like Void Space and Paradox Theory) and to purchase upgrades like Cryochambers and Void Rifts.
  • Unobtainium Capacity Goal: A late-game goal is to build enough Chronospheres to reach an extreme Unobtainium capacity (e.g., 8.14 billion UO capacity to build 100 Chronospheres).

4. Key Upgrades (Flux Condensator)

The utility of the Chronosphere is greatly enhanced by the Flux Condensator upgrade:

  • Flux Condensator: This upgrade costs 250 Alloy, 5,000 Unobtainium, and 5 Time Crystals.
    • It causes Chronospheres to affect craftable resources (like Beam, Slab, Steel, Blueprint, and Megalith).
    • The amount preserved is calculated with diminishing returns: $1.5 ({# of Chronospheres}) \sqrt{{resource amount}}$** of each craftable resource is carried over on reset.

5. Challenge Interaction

  • Challenges and Reserves: When resetting with most challenges active, Chronospheres will not bring over any resources. Instead, resources are placed in reserves and can be reclaimed after the challenge is complete.
  • Iron Will: Iron Will mode is entered by resetting with zero Chronospheres.

item.title: City On A Hill
item.description:
City On A Hill is a mid-game Foreign policy in Kittens Game that provides a small +5% increase to your maximum culture cap. It represents an isolationist approach where your village seeks to be a “shining example” to the rest of the world.

Quick Stats

Attribute Details
Cost 4,000 Culture
Primary Effect +5% Culture Cap
Prerequisites Astronomy (Tech) and Isolationism (Policy)
Mutually Exclusive Big Stick Policy

Strategic Utility

While a larger culture cap can be helpful for researching advanced technologies like Theology, this policy is generally considered a suboptimal choice for several reasons:
item.content:encoded:
City On A Hill is a mid-game Foreign policy in Kittens Game that provides a small +5% increase to your maximum culture cap. It represents an isolationist approach where your village seeks to be a “shining example” to the rest of the world.

Quick Stats

Attribute Details
Cost 4,000 Culture
Primary Effect +5% Culture Cap
Prerequisites Astronomy (Tech) and Isolationism (Policy)
Mutually Exclusive Big Stick Policy

Strategic Utility

While a larger culture cap can be helpful for researching advanced technologies like Theology, this policy is generally considered a suboptimal choice for several reasons:

  • Weak Bonus: Compared to other global multipliers, a 5% increase to the culture cap is relatively minor and often described as “kinda sucking” in strategic guides.
  • The Big Stick Alternative: By choosing City On A Hill, you permanently lock yourself out of the Big Stick Policy for the remainder of the run. Big Stick Policy provides a 15% discount on Embassies, which is widely viewed as more practically useful for progressing trade relations with other civilisations.
  • Isolationist Drawbacks: Because this policy requires the Isolationism prerequisite, you are already trading away the benefits of the Diplomacy policy branch, which offers better trade efficiency and faster discovery of other races.

Strategic Recommendation

Most experienced players advise skipping City On A Hill in favour of the Big Stick Policy if you have committed to the Isolationism branch. If your goal is to increase culture throughput or cap, investment in Amphitheatres, Temples, and Academies typically provides more substantial results without the opportunity cost of a policy slot.

item.title: Concrete Warehouses
item.description:
Concrete Warehouses is a mid-game Workshop upgrade that further expands your storage infrastructure during the “Concrete Era.” It serves as a vital companion to Concrete Barns, helping you reach the resource caps necessary for advanced housing and space technologies.

Core Effects

  • Storage Boost: It increases the storage capacity of Warehouses, Barns, Harbors, and Mints by +35%.
  • Resources Affects: This multiplier applies to your maximum Wood, Minerals, Coal, Iron, Gold, and Titanium.
  • Catnip Synergy: If you have the Silos upgrade, Concrete Warehouses also increases the Catnip capacity of your storage buildings (contributing 25% of its total effect, or roughly +8.75%).

Costs and Requirements

  • Science Cost: 100,000 Science.
  • Resource Cost: 35 Concrete and 1,250 Titanium.
  • Prerequisite: You must have researched Mechanization and purchased the Concrete Pillars upgrade first.

Strategic Utility

  • The Concrete Suite: This upgrade is part of the critical trio of concrete upgrades (Pillars, Barns, Warehouses). While Concrete Barns offers a higher percentage boost (+75%), Concrete Warehouses is essential because it scales your Harbors, which become your primary source of storage in the mid-to-late game.
  • Pre-Reset Push: Players often purchase this alongside Concrete Huts to maximize their storage limits, allowing them to build a few extra Log Houses or Mansions to squeeze out more kittens (and thus more Paragon) before resetting.
  • Gold and Titanium: Unlike early barn upgrades, Concrete Warehouses boosts Gold and Titanium storage (via Harbors and Warehouses), which is critical for affording the 125,000 Science cap required for technologies like Electronics and Robotics.

item.title: Cosmological Libertarianism
item.description:
Cosmological Libertarianism is an endgame government policy that increases your global unobtainium production by 15%. It represents a shift towards privatising space resources to accelerate the expansion of your kitten civilisation beyond the home planet.

Policy Overview

  • Cost: 150,000 Culture.
  • Prerequisite: Your civilisation must have reached Dune.
  • Primary Effect: A global +15% multiplier to all unobtainium production.
  • Mutual Exclusivity: Enacting this policy permanently locks out Technocracy and Order of the Stars for the remainder of the run.

Strategic Comparison

In the late game, players must choose one of three mutually exclusive policies. Cosmological Libertarianism is widely considered the superior choice for general progression.
item.content:encoded:
Cosmological Libertarianism is an endgame government policy that increases your global unobtainium production by 15%. It represents a shift towards privatising space resources to accelerate the expansion of your kitten civilisation beyond the home planet.

Policy Overview

  • Cost: 150,000 Culture.
  • Prerequisite: Your civilisation must have reached Dune.
  • Primary Effect: A global +15% multiplier to all unobtainium production.
  • Mutual Exclusivity: Enacting this policy permanently locks out Technocracy and Order of the Stars for the remainder of the run.

Strategic Comparison

In the late game, players must choose one of three mutually exclusive policies. Cosmological Libertarianism is widely considered the superior choice for general progression.

Policy Effect Strategic Value
Cosmological Libertarianism +15% Unobtainium production High. Unobtainium is the primary bottleneck for advanced space missions and Chronospheres.
Order of the Stars +20% Faith production Situational. Only recommended if your sole goal is grinding religion bonuses or Transcendence tiers.
Technocracy +20% Science cap Low. Science storage is generally easy to manage via buildings like Data Centres and Bio Labs.

The Unobtainium Bottleneck

Unobtainium is essential for crafting Eludium and building Chronospheres, which are required for self-sustaining “positive resets”. Because unobtainium production is significantly slower than most other base resources, the 15% boost from Cosmological Libertarianism provides a massive advantage in scaling your civilisation’s temporal and space-faring capabilities.

Mathematical Impact

The bonus from this policy is applied multiplicatively in the unobtainium production formula, stacking with other modifiers such as:

  • Space Elevators and Orbital Arrays.
  • Microwarp Reactors.
  • Redmoon Cycle effects (if Numerology is researched).

item.title: Cultural Exchange
item.description:
Cultural Exchange is a mid-game Foreign policy that provides a permanent +5% boost to your culture income. It represents the strategic choice to send your poets and actors to foreign lands to increase your civilisation’s cultural throughput.

Requirements and Costs

To enact this policy, you must meet the following criteria:

  • Cost: 4,000 Culture.
  • Science Prerequisite: You must have researched Astronomy.
  • Policy Prerequisite: You must have already enacted the Diplomacy policy.
  • Mutual Exclusivity: Choosing Cultural Exchange permanently locks out the Knowledge Sharing policy for the remainder of your current run.

Strategic Comparison

In Kittens Game, players must choose between boosting culture or science via this policy pair:

Cultural Exchange is a mid-game Foreign policy that provides a permanent +5% boost to your culture income. It represents the strategic choice to send your poets and actors to foreign lands to increase your civilisation’s cultural throughput.

Requirements and Costs

To enact this policy, you must meet the following criteria:

  • Cost: 4,000 Culture.
  • Science Prerequisite: You must have researched Astronomy.
  • Policy Prerequisite: You must have already enacted the Diplomacy policy.
  • Mutual Exclusivity: Choosing Cultural Exchange permanently locks out the Knowledge Sharing policy for the remainder of your current run.

Strategic Comparison

In Kittens Game, players must choose between boosting culture or science via this policy pair:

Policy Primary Bonus Strategic Context
Cultural Exchange +5% Culture income Preferred because culture is often a bottleneck in the mid-game.
Knowledge Sharing +5% Science income Generally skipped because science is considered “easy” to generate through other buildings.

Why Choose Cultural Exchange?

Most experienced players follow the Diplomacy $\to$ Cultural Exchange path rather than the Isolationism path. This is because culture is a “slow” resource compared to science, making any percentage boost highly valuable for:

  • Scaling Manuscripts: Mid-game technological progress is often gated by the volume of manuscripts you can craft, which require significant amounts of culture.
  • Policy Branching: This policy is the logical conclusion of the Diplomacy branch, which focuses on building better relationships with other races to lower trade costs.
  • Late-Game Efficiency: In very long runs, such as the 40k Endless Run, maintaining a steady stream of culture is vital for religious and industrial growth.

item.title: Dark Energy
item.description:
Dark Energy is a specific Workshop upgrade in the late game that dramatically improves the utility of your Accelerators. It is part of the “Energy Rifts” upgrade chain, which transforms Accelerators from simple uranium producers into massive storage silos.

Core Effects

  • Storage Boost: It increases the resource storage provided by Accelerators by an additional +250%.
  • Affected Resources: This bonus applies to the storage caps for Catnip, Wood, Minerals, Coal, Iron, Titanium, and Gold.
  • Cumulative Stacking: This bonus is additive with other Accelerator upgrades. For example, if you have Stasis Chambers (+95%), Void Energy (+75%), and Dark Energy (+250%), your total storage bonus for Accelerators becomes +420%.

Requirements and Costs

Dark Energy is an advanced upgrade that requires you to have entered the Time Crystal era.

Requirements and Costs

Dark Energy is an advanced upgrade that requires you to have entered the Time Crystal era.

  • Prerequisite: You must have researched the Void Energy upgrade first.
  • Science Cost: 350,000 Science.
  • Resource Cost: 75 Eludium and 3 Time Crystals.

Strategic Utility

  • Breaking Storage Bottlenecks: By the time you reach the Eludium era, storage caps (particularly for Titanium and Unobtainium) become the primary hurdle for purchasing advanced buildings like Chronospheres and Moon Bases. Dark Energy provides a massive spike in capacity without requiring you to build new structures.
  • Progression Chain: It is a stepping stone to the final Accelerator upgrade, Tachyon Accelerators (which provides a further +500% storage), unlocked later via Tachyon Theory.
  • Reset Preparation: Increasing your storage caps is vital for Chronosphere resets. The more resources you can store, the more you can carry over to your next run.

Note: Do not confuse “Dark Energy” with “Dark Future,” which is a game state that triggers after year 40,000 and affects game mechanics like Time Impedance.

item.title: Dark Nova
item.description:
Dark Nova is a permanent endgame Cryptotheology building that increases your civilisation’s global energy production by +2% per level. Like all Cryptotheology structures, it carries over through resets, although you must re-research the “Cryptotheology” technology in each new run to view or purchase additional units.

Costs and Requirements

Building a Dark Nova represents a significant investment in late-game resources and spiritual progression.

  • Relic Cost: 75,000 Relics.
  • Void Cost: 7,500 Void.
  • Price Ratio: 1.15.
  • Prerequisite: You must have attained Transcendence Tier 20 to unlock this building. Reaching Tier 20 requires an accumulation of approximately 451.14M% Epiphany.

Strategic Utility

Dark Nova is situated in the final phase of the game (Phase 3/Endgame), where energy management becomes a primary bottleneck for scientific and industrial expansion.

Like all Cryptotheology structures, it carries over through resets, although you must re-research the “Cryptotheology” technology in each new run to view or purchase additional units.

Costs and Requirements

Building a Dark Nova represents a significant investment in late-game resources and spiritual progression.

  • Relic Cost: 75,000 Relics.
  • Void Cost: 7,500 Void.
  • Price Ratio: 1.15.
  • Prerequisite: You must have attained Transcendence Tier 20 to unlock this building. Reaching Tier 20 requires an accumulation of approximately 451.14M% Epiphany.

Strategic Utility

Dark Nova is situated in the final phase of the game (Phase 3/Endgame), where energy management becomes a primary bottleneck for scientific and industrial expansion.

  • Endgame Power Demands: As you progress toward the “positive reset” loop, you must power high-consumption buildings like AI Cores (which consume increasing energy per unit), Containment Chambers (50 Watts each), and Entanglement Stations (25 Watts each). The +2% global production bonus helps sustain these power-hungry systems.
  • Scaling for Infinity: Advanced players utilize the energy boost to support massive arrays of Sunlifters and Hydro Plants while attempting to reach the 8.14 billion Unobtainium capacity required for 100 Chronospheres.
  • Synergy with Void Rifts: The global energy production bonus stacks with other modifiers, helping to maintain a positive energy surplus during Time Skips, which is necessary for Antimatter generation and the automated “shatter engine”.

Building Tier Context

In the progression of Cryptotheology, Dark Nova is one of the final buildings unlocked, coming after other critical structures like Blazars (Tier 15) but before Mausoleums (Tier 23) and Holy Genocide (Tier 25). It is a foundational component for players seeking to “chase infinity” by overcapping resources through thousands of years of skipped time.

item.title: Diplomacy
item.description:
In Kittens Game, Diplomacy refers to both a foundational Metaphysics upgrade and a mid-game Foreign policy. Both systems focus on improving your relations with other civilisations to make trading more efficient and accessible.

1. Diplomacy (Foreign Policy)

This policy is one of the first major choices you make regarding your international relations.

  • Cost: 1,600 Culture.
  • Prerequisites: Researching Currency.
  • Primary Effect: Reduces the cost of every trade by 5 catpower.
  • Mutual Exclusivity: Selecting Diplomacy permanently locks you out of the Isolationism policy for the current run.

Strategic Advice: Experienced players generally recommend Diplomacy over Isolationism. While Isolationism offers a gold discount, Diplomacy is considered superior because it leads to the Cultural Exchange policy, which provides a +5% boost to culture income—addressing one of the game’s most persistent mid-game bottlenecks.

1. Diplomacy (Foreign Policy)

This policy is one of the first major choices you make regarding your international relations.

  • Cost: 1,600 Culture.
  • Prerequisites: Researching Currency.
  • Primary Effect: Reduces the cost of every trade by 5 catpower.
  • Mutual Exclusivity: Selecting Diplomacy permanently locks you out of the Isolationism policy for the current run.

Strategic Advice: Experienced players generally recommend Diplomacy over Isolationism. While Isolationism offers a gold discount, Diplomacy is considered superior because it leads to the Cultural Exchange policy, which provides a +5% boost to culture income—addressing one of the game’s most persistent mid-game bottlenecks.

2. Diplomacy (Metaphysics Upgrade)

This is a permanent upgrade purchased with Paragon that persists across game resets.

  • Cost: 5 Paragon.
  • Core Effects:
    • Earlier Discovery: Races can be discovered as early as Year 1 (instead of Year 5).
    • Better Standing: Increases your standing ratio with other races by 10, making them more likely to be friendly.
  • The Diplomacy Tree: Purchasing this unlocks several follow-up upgrades, including:
    • Zebra Diplomacy (35 Paragon): Allows a percentage of your Zebras to stay when ending an Iron Will run.
    • Navigation Diplomacy (300 Paragon): Allows races to be discovered as soon as you have Ships.

3. Advanced Race Relations

Once you have the Diplomacy metaphysics upgrade and reach an Embassy level of 20 with specific races, you unlock specialized diplomatic policies:

Policy Name Effect
Lizard Relations: Diplomats Increases standing ratio by 0.1% per Embassy with neutral races.
Shark Relations: Merchants Increases trade ratio by 3%, scaling up to 30% based on total trades completed.
Griffin Relations: Scouts Increases hunting effectiveness by 50%.
Naga Relations: Architects Increases blueprint trade chance by 0.25% per embassy (up to 10%).

item.title: Drama and Poetry
item.description:
Drama and Poetry is a mid-game technology that moves your civilisation from basic resource management into cultural and temporal optimization. It is primarily known for unlocking the Festival mechanic and the Brewery building.

Costs and Prerequisites

Because of its high requirement for a specific crafted resource, it is often seen as a significant hurdle for new players.

  • Science Cost: 90,000.
  • Resource Cost: 5,000 Parchment.
  • Prerequisite: Researching Acoustics.

Unlocked Mechanics

  • Festivals: Once researched, you can spend resources to hold a festival that lasts for one game year (400 days, or 800 real-time seconds).
    • Kitten Growth: Festivals are the primary way to double the arrival speed of kittens (from ~0.16 to 0.32 kittens per second), which is essential for reaching the population thresholds needed for Paragon.
    • Numeromancy Synergies: If the Numeromancy Metaphysics upgrade is researched, holding a festival grants massive global production multipliers based on the current Cycle (e.g., x2 Unobtainium in Redmoon, x2 Science in Piscine, or x2 Catpower in Cath).
  • Brewery: A building that enhances the effectiveness of your festivals.
    • Cost: 1,000 Wood, 750 Culture, 5 Spice, and 375 Parchment.
    • Effects: Provides a +1% bonus to Festival Happiness and the Festival Cycle Bonus, while increasing Festival Kitten Speed by +0.1%.
    • Upkeep: Each active Brewery consumes -1 Catnip and -0.1 Spice per tick.

Strategic Utility

  • Early Game Skip: Experienced players recommend skipping this tech on your first few runs because the 5,000 Parchment cost is considered “waaaay too expensive” to be useful when your economy is still weak.
  • Mid-to-Late Game Priority: It becomes vital when you start pursuing Unobtainium farming or rapid Paragon grinding. In short runs (approx. 30 minutes), players often stack multiple festivals to ensure kittens fill housing as fast as it is built.
  • Parchment Grinding: To prepare for this tech, it is recommended to stockpile at least 7,500 Parchment so you can afford the research and immediately hold several festivals to see the benefit.

item.title: Dune Mission
item.description:
The Dune Mission is a mid-to-late game space project that involves launching a rocket to explore Dune, described as a large, lifeless planet covered by sand and volcanic rock. It serves as a critical bridge for industrial scaling, particularly in stabilizing the uranium and oil supplies required for advanced space exploration.

Mission Requirements and Logistics

To access the Dune mission, you must have first successfully completed the Moon mission. The specific resource costs for the launch include:
item.content:encoded:
The Dune Mission is a mid-to-late game space project that involves launching a rocket to explore Dune, described as a large, lifeless planet covered by sand and volcanic rock. It serves as a critical bridge for industrial scaling, particularly in stabilizing the uranium and oil supplies required for advanced space exploration.

Mission Requirements and Logistics

To access the Dune mission, you must have first successfully completed the Moon mission. The specific resource costs for the launch include:

  • Starcharts: 1,000.
  • Titanium: 7,000.
  • Science: 175,000.
  • Kerosene: 75.

The base travel time for the mission is 356 game-days, which equates to approximately 11 minutes and 52 seconds in real-time. This duration can be reduced significantly by researching drive upgrades such as the Antimatter Drive or Thorium Drive.

Unlocked Infrastructure and Resources

Successfully exploring Dune unlocks the Helios mission and provides access to several vital space structures:

  • Planet Cracker: A massive mining vessel that produces 1.5 uranium per second and increases uranium storage by 1,750. This is a primary source of uranium needed to power Lunar Outposts for unobtainium production.
  • Hydraulic Fracturer: Produces oil at a rate of 2.5 per second. While helpful for oil management, these structures are notably more effective once you have researched Space Manufacturing.
  • Spice Refinery: Refines the planet’s sand into Spice at 0.125 per second. Spice is a rare luxury resource that provides a +10% happiness boost but is gradually consumed over time.

Technological and Policy Unlocks

Reaching Dune is a prerequisite for advanced societal and scientific developments. It allows the research of Cosmological Technocracy and unlocks the ability to enact high-tier Policy/:

  • Technocracy: Increases the science cap by 20%.
  • Cosmological Libertarianism: Increases unobtainium production by 15%.
  • Order of the Stars: Increases faith production by 20% but restricts leaders to the priest job.

The Dune Cycle and Synergy

Dune is also one of the ten celestial cycles (represented by the glyph ⍫). If you have researched Numerology, the Dune cycle provides specific modifiers to your space production:

  • Planet Cracker uranium output: +10%.
  • Hydraulic Fracturer oil output: +50%.
  • HR Harvester energy production: -25% penalty.
  • Festival Effect: If Numeromancy is researched, holding a festival during the Dune cycle provides a 2x multiplier to uranium income.

Strategic Utility

The mission marks the transition into the Eludium Era. Because Planet Crackers provide a more stable and faster uranium supply than terrestrial Accelerators or trading with Dragons, the Dune mission is essential for players looking to mass-produce unobtainium and eventually eludium. Additionally, the spice produced here provides a reliable way to maintain kitten happiness as populations grow larger.

item.title: Ecology
item.description:
Ecology is a mid-to-late game technology that focuses on energy transition and environmental management. It is a critical component of Phase 3 of the game, known as the Prestige and Energy Transition Epoch.

Costs and Prerequisites

  • Science Cost: 125,000 Science.
  • Resource Cost: 55 Blueprints.
  • Prerequisite: You must first research the Combustion technology to unlock Ecology.

Core Effects and Building Upgrades

  • Solar Farms: Researching Ecology allows you to upgrade your Pastures into Solar Farms.
    • Energy Production: Solar Farms provide a base of +2 Energy (+1.5 in Winter, +2.67 in Summer).
    • Trade-off: Upgrading to Solar Farms removes the catnip demand reduction bonus provided by the original Pasture. This transition is generally considered safe in later runs because the food demand reduction from Pastures suffers from strict diminishing returns, making energy production more valuable.
  • Carbon Sequestration: This technology is a prerequisite for the Carbon Sequestration workshop upgrade, which allows Factories to capture pollution rather than produce it.

Pollution Management and UI

Ecology significantly enhances your ability to monitor and manage Pollution:

Core Effects and Building Upgrades

This transition is generally considered safe in later runs because the food demand reduction from Pastures suffers from strict diminishing returns, making energy production more valuable.
  • Carbon Sequestration: This technology is a prerequisite for the Carbon Sequestration workshop upgrade, which allows Factories to capture pollution rather than produce it.

Pollution Management and UI

Ecology significantly enhances your ability to monitor and manage Pollution:

  • Detailed Information: It adds more detailed statistics to the pollution indicator in the Science tab.
  • Building Controls: It adds +/- buttons to buildings that produce pollution, allowing you to manually toggle them to manage your environmental impact.

Policy Integration

Ecology is a mandatory prerequisite for several late-game Environmental policies:

  • Conservation: Provides +5% happiness and a -5% reduction in pollution.
  • Open Woodlands: Increases wood and mineral production by +12.5% but increases pollution by +5%. In Iron Will mode, this policy instead provides a 4.16% bonus to both catnip refinement and minerals from meteors.

item.title: Electronics
item.description:
Electronics is a crucial mid-game science technology that introduces significant building upgrades, sets up your transition into the Space phase, and unlocks powerful automation tools.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Prerequisite: You must first research the Mechanization technology.
  • Cost: 135,000 Science and 70 Blueprints.

Core Unlocks: Building Upgrades

Researching Electronics directly enables you to upgrade two of your standard terrestrial buildings into more powerful variants:

  • Libraries into Data Centers: Data Centers provide a larger boost to your Science (+10%), Max Science (+750), Max Culture (+250), and Compendium Cap (+1000) at the cost of 2 Watts of energy.
  • Amphitheatres into Broadcast Towers: Broadcast Towers drastically reduce unhappiness (-75%) and generate Culture based on your energy surplus.

Unlocked Technology and Sciences

Electronics acts as the gateway to the space age and advanced automation, unlocking the following science technologies:
item.content:encoded:

Acquisition and Costs

  • Prerequisite: You must first research the Mechanization technology.
  • Cost: 135,000 Science and 70 Blueprints.

Core Unlocks: Building Upgrades

  • Libraries into Data Centers: Data Centers provide a larger boost to your Science (+10%), Max Science (+750), Max Culture (+250), and Compendium Cap (+1000) at the cost of 2 Watts of energy.
  • Amphitheatres into Broadcast Towers: Broadcast Towers drastically reduce unhappiness (-75%) and generate Culture based on your energy surplus.

Unlocked Technology and Sciences

Electronics acts as the gateway to the space age and advanced automation, unlocking the following science technologies:

  • Robotics
  • Nuclear Fission
  • Rocketry (which enables the Space tab and space missions)

Unlocked Workshop Upgrades

Electronics grants access to a massive suite of Workshop upgrades:

  • SETI: One of the most highly recommended upgrades to rush. For 125K Science and 250 Titanium, SETI makes all astronomical events automatic and silent, completely removing the need to manually click meteors to gather Science and Starcharts.
  • Refrigeration: Expands your maximum catnip limit by +75%.
  • CAD System: Science buildings improve your blueprint crafting ratio.
  • Factory Logistics: Increases the craft bonus of your Factories.
  • Factory Optimization: Improves your Engineer kittens’ effectiveness.
  • Telecommunication: Allows kittens to learn job skills from each other.from: pierre

item.title: Eludium
item.description:
Eludium is an extremely rare and expensive high-tier crafted resource in Kittens Game, described as a composite of Unobtainium and Alloy.

Acquisition and Production

  • Unlocking: Eludium is unlocked through the Exometallurgy science (formerly known as Advanced Exogeology).
  • Crafting Recipe: Crafting one unit of eludium requires 1,000 Unobtainium and 2,500 Alloy.
  • Production Multipliers: The yield is significantly boosted by your overall Workshop craft ratio. Furthermore, kittens with the Chemist trait provide a specific crafting bonus (+0.075) for eludium, and the Antimatter Fission workshop upgrade makes Engineers 25% more effective at producing it.

Strategic Infrastructure and Buildings

Eludium is a critical component for late-game population scaling and advanced industrial structures:
item.content:encoded:
Eludium is an extremely rare and expensive high-tier crafted resource in Kittens Game, described as a composite of Unobtainium and Alloy.

Acquisition and Production

  • Unlocking: Eludium is unlocked through the Exometallurgy science (formerly known as Advanced Exogeology).
  • Crafting Recipe: Crafting one unit of eludium requires 1,000 Unobtainium and 2,500 Alloy.
  • Production Multipliers: The yield is significantly boosted by your overall Workshop craft ratio. Furthermore, kittens with the Chemist trait provide a specific crafting bonus (+0.075) for eludium, and the Antimatter Fission workshop upgrade makes Engineers 25% more effective at producing it.

Strategic Infrastructure and Buildings

Eludium is a critical component for late-game population scaling and advanced industrial structures:

  • Eludium Huts: This bonfire upgrade reduces the price ratio of Huts by 10%, allowing for much higher populations. While powerful, some strategic guides note that the 125 eludium cost may only provide a marginal (~1%) increase in paragon-per-hour efficiency in very short runs.
  • Cryostation: These supermassive storage facilities cost 25 eludium and are essential for reaching the high resource caps required for the deep endgame.
  • Spaceport: Eludium is required to build Spaceports, which enhance the capacity of other space structures like Moon Bases and Cryostations.
  • Sunlifter: Each Sunlifter costs 225 eludium and is the primary structure used to generate Antimatter.
  • Entanglement Station: These late-game structures require 5,000 eludium each and are used for quantum computing and reverse-engineering relics.

Workshop and Advanced Upgrades

Many high-tier upgrades are gated by eludium costs:

  • Eludium Reflectors: This upgrade increases your maximum Science capacity by +2% for every Observatory you own.
  • Microwarp Reactors: Costing 50 eludium, this is a vital upgrade that increases the Unobtainium production of Lunar Outposts by 75%.
  • Scientific Utility: It is required for several advanced workshop techs including Cryocomputing (Data Center efficiency), Machine Learning, Antimatter Reactors, and Chronoengineers.

Preservation and Reset Strategy

  • Preservation: Eludium is a crafted resource and can be carried over through game resets if you have Chronospheres and the Flux Condensator upgrade.
  • Diminishing Returns: The amount preserved follows a square root formula: $1.5* {number of Chronospheres}* sqrt(current eludium amount)$.
  • Efficiency Tipping Point: A common strategy for rapid resets is to stockpile 1,111 eludium before resetting with one Chronosphere. This ensures you start the next run with the 50 eludium needed to immediately purchase Microwarp Reactors and accelerate your Unobtainium production.

item.title: Energy_Rifts
item.description:
An Energy Rift is a vital mid-to-late-game Workshop upgrade that transforms the Accelerator building from a simple industrial refiner into a massive storage facility. While Accelerators initially only consume energy to refine titanium into uranium, this upgrade allows them to “create rifts to pocket dimensions,” granting them significant storage capacity across several resources.

Unlocking and Costs

To access Energy Rifts, you must follow a specific scientific path:

  • Prerequisite Technology: You must research Dimensional Physics (which itself requires Particle Physics).
  • Upgrade Cost: Purchasing the upgrade in the Workshop requires 200k Science, 7,500 Titanium, and 250 Uranium.

Storage Effects

Once the upgrade is active, every Accelerator built provides a substantial boost to your maximum storage caps. The specific bonuses per Accelerator include:
item.content:encoded:
An Energy Rift is a vital mid-to-late-game Workshop upgrade that transforms the Accelerator building from a simple industrial refiner into a massive storage facility. While Accelerators initially only consume energy to refine titanium into uranium, this upgrade allows them to “create rifts to pocket dimensions,” granting them significant storage capacity across several resources.

Unlocking and Costs

To access Energy Rifts, you must follow a specific scientific path:

  • Prerequisite Technology: You must research Dimensional Physics (which itself requires Particle Physics).
  • Upgrade Cost: Purchasing the upgrade in the Workshop requires 200k Science, 7,500 Titanium, and 250 Uranium.

Storage Effects

Once the upgrade is active, every Accelerator built provides a substantial boost to your maximum storage caps. The specific bonuses per Accelerator include:

  • Catnip: +30,000
  • Wood: +20,000
  • Minerals: +25,000
  • Iron: +7,500
  • Coal: +2,500
  • Gold: +250
  • Titanium: +750

Scaling and Synergies

The storage provided by Energy Rifts is the foundation for further endgame scaling through several sequential Workshop upgrades:

  • Stasis Chambers: Makes Energy Rifts twice as effective (+95% bonus).
  • Void Energy: Provides an additional +75% bonus to the storage ratio.
  • Dark Energy: Increases effectiveness by 2.5 times (+250% bonus).
  • Tachyon Accelerators: Increases effectiveness by 5 times (+500% bonus).

Strategic Utility

In the late game, Energy Rifts are considered a primary solution for the titanium storage bottleneck. While standard storage buildings like Harbours and Warehouses eventually hit diminishing returns or become too expensive, the additive +750 titanium storage per Accelerator (further multiplied by upgrades like Stasis Chambers) allows players to reach the high titanium caps necessary for advanced space missions and eludium crafting.

However, players must manage the energy cost of these rifts; while the storage is passive, the Accelerator building itself consumes 2 Watts of energy and is an “active” consumer of titanium for uranium production.

item.title: Epicurianism
item.description:
Epicureanism is a mid-game Philosophy policy in Kittens Game that focuses on maximising kitten morale by increasing the happiness bonus provided by rare luxury resources.

Core Mechanics

  • Cost: 2,500 Culture.
  • Prerequisite: Researching the Philosophy technology.
  • Primary Effect: Rare luxury resources (such as Furs, Ivory, and Spice) provide 11% happiness each, rather than the base 10%.
  • Mutual Exclusivity: Choosing Epicureanism permanently locks out the Stoicism policy for the remainder of the run.

Strategic Utility: Epicureanism vs. Stoicism

In the Kittens Game community, Epicureanism is generally preferred over Stoicism for several reasons:

  • Primary Effect: Rare luxury resources (such as Furs, Ivory, and Spice) provide 11% happiness each, rather than the base 10%.
  • Mutual Exclusivity: Choosing Epicureanism permanently locks out the Stoicism policy for the remainder of the run.

Strategic Utility: Epicureanism vs. Stoicism

In the Kittens Game community, Epicureanism is generally preferred over Stoicism for several reasons:

  • Production Scaling: Higher happiness directly translates to a global production bonus for all kitten jobs. By increasing the value of each luxury, you can significantly boost your village’s overall output.
  • Luxury Availability: By the time you can afford this policy, your hunting team and Tradeposts should be established enough to maintain a steady supply of luxuries.
  • Consumption Management: While Stoicism reduces luxury consumption by 50%, most players find that having enough Tradeposts provides sufficient diminishing returns on consumption to make the extra happiness from Epicureanism worth the cost.

Policy Branching

Enacting Epicureanism is the gateway to the “pleasure-focused” branch of the philosophy tree, eventually allowing you to choose between:

  • Extravagance: Increases happiness from consumable luxuries to 5, but triples their consumption rate.
  • Carnivale: Boosts kitten arrival speed and festival growth.

Comparison Table

Feature Epicureanism Stoicism
Philosophy “Pleasure is the highest good.” “Endure hardship without complaint.”
Main Bonus +11% happiness per luxury. -50% consumption of luxuries.
Secondary Effect Unlocks Extravagance/Carnivale. Unlocks Rationing/Frugality.
Expert Verdict Often the standard choice for the “happy%” bonus. Situational; used if luxuries are scarce.

item.title: Extravagance
item.description:
Extravagance is a mid-game Philosophy policy that prioritises kitten morale by significantly increasing the happiness provided by luxury goods, at the cost of consuming those resources much faster.

Core Mechanics

  • Cost: 3,500 Culture.
  • Prerequisites: You must have previously enacted the Epicureanism policy.
  • Mutual Exclusivity: Selecting Extravagance permanently locks you out of the Carnivale policy for the remainder of your current run.

Primary Effects

The policy represents a society “doubling down” on its epicurean ideals, leading to the following mechanical changes:
