Extravagance is a mid-game Philosophy policy that prioritises kitten morale by significantly increasing the happiness provided by luxury goods, at the cost of consuming those resources much faster.

Core Mechanics

  • Cost: 3,500 Culture.
  • Prerequisites: You must have previously enacted the Epicureanism policy.
  • Mutual Exclusivity: Selecting Extravagance permanently locks you out of the Carnivale policy for the remainder of your current run.

Primary Effects

The policy represents a society “doubling down” on its epicurean ideals, leading to the following mechanical changes:

  • Enhanced Happiness: Consumable luxury resources (such as Furs, Ivory, and Spice) provide 5 happiness each.
  • Increased Depletion: Consumable luxury resources are used up three times as quickly (indicated as 200% additional consumption).

Strategic Advice

  • Extravagance vs. Carnivale: Players often prefer Extravagance when they want to maximise their “happy%” bonus to global production. Strategic guides suggest that if your hunting and trading infrastructure is strong enough to maintain a steady supply of luxuries, the faster consumption rate is a worthwhile trade-off for the morale boost.
  • Mitigation: To handle the rapid drain of resources, it is recommended to have a robust number of Tradeposts, which help slow down the consumption of rare resources through diminishing returns.
  • First Run Utility: On initial runs, some players find Carnivale (which focuses on kitten arrival speed during festivals) less useful than the raw production boost provided by the higher happiness of Extravagance.

item.title: Full Industrialization
item.description:
Full Industrialisation is an advanced environment policy that boosts the effectiveness of your factories’ crafting bonuses. It represents the choice to prioritise industrial throughput over environmental preservation.

Core Stats and Requirements

  • Cost: 10,000 Culture.
  • Prerequisites: You must have researched the Industrialisation technology and already enacted either the Strip Mining or Clear Cutting policy.
  • Mutual Exclusivity: Enacting this policy permanently locks out the Sustainability policy for the current run.

Primary Effects

The policy focuses on squeezing more production out of your industrial infrastructure at a cost to the climate:
item.content:encoded:
Full Industrialisation is an advanced environment policy that boosts the effectiveness of your factories’ crafting bonuses. It represents the choice to prioritise industrial throughput over environmental preservation.

Core Stats and Requirements

  • Cost: 10,000 Culture.
  • Prerequisites: You must have researched the Industrialisation technology and already enacted either the Strip Mining or Clear Cutting policy.
  • Mutual Exclusivity: Enacting this policy permanently locks out the Sustainability policy for the current run.

Primary Effects

The policy focuses on squeezing more production out of your industrial infrastructure at a cost to the climate:

  • Enhanced Factories: Increases the power of your factories by 5%. This means a factory providing a base 5% crafting bonus will instead provide 5.25%, or a factory boosted by Logistics to 6% will provide 6.3%.
  • Pollution Penalty: Increases your global pollution levels by +5%. High pollution can eventually lead to reduced catnip production, lower happiness, and slower kitten arrival speeds.

Strategic Advice

  • Run Timing: Most experienced players recommend choosing Sustainability on your first run to avoid happiness penalties. From your second run onwards, when you are building a larger number of factories, Full Industrialisation becomes the “obvious pick” for its crafting benefits.
  • Resource Staging: It is best to wait until you have at least 2,000 Science to spare and a solid cultural foundation before pushing for this policy.
  • Industrial Synergy: This policy is a key component for scaling your industry into the late game, as it stacks with other factory upgrades like Factory Logistics (+20% crafting) and Factory Processing.

Endgame Utility: The Space Loop

In the late game, Full Industrialisation becomes critical for space expansion. Once you research Space Manufacturing, your factories begin to provide a bonus to space structures like Space Elevators and Orbital Arrays.

Because Full Industrialisation increases the base power of these factories, it directly accelerates your unobtainium production in space. This makes it a foundational policy for players aiming to build a self-sustaining positive chrono-reset engine using Chronospheres.

item.title: Furthest Ring
item.description:
The Furthest Ring is the final space mission currently available in the sources, famously described as “the end of the universe”. It represents the ultimate frontier of exploration for your kitten civilisation, situated far beyond the Centaurus System.

Mission Costs and Prerequisites

Launching a rocket to the Furthest Ring requires an astronomical amount of high-tier resources, far exceeding any previous mission:

  • Starcharts: 500,000
  • Science: 1.25 Million
  • Kerosene: 75,000
  • Thorium: 75,000

To even see this mission in the Ground Control tab, you must first successfully complete the Centaurus System mission.
item.content:encoded:
The Furthest Ring is the final space mission currently available in the sources, famously described as “the end of the universe”. It represents the ultimate frontier of exploration for your kitten civilisation, situated far beyond the Centaurus System.

Mission Costs and Prerequisites

Launching a rocket to the Furthest Ring requires an astronomical amount of high-tier resources, far exceeding any previous mission:

  • Starcharts: 500,000
  • Science: 1.25 Million
  • Kerosene: 75,000
  • Thorium: 75,000

To even see this mission in the Ground Control tab, you must first successfully complete the Centaurus System mission.

The Travel Time Challenge

The most defining characteristic of the Furthest Ring is its extreme distance. The base travel time is 725,200,000 game-days. Even with the most advanced propulsion technologies researched, the journey is incredibly long:

  • Drive Reductions: By researching both Thorium Drives and Antimatter Drives, travel times are divided by 75.
  • Real-Time Duration: Even with these upgrades, the trip takes approximately 223 days, 19 hours, and 51 minutes of real-world time (representing over 24,000 in-game years).
  • Acceleration: To progress this mission within a reasonable timeframe, you would typically need to rely on combusting Time Crystals to skip through years rapidly.

Functionality and Content

Despite its name and the massive investment required, the Furthest Ring serves more as a symbolic endgame milestone than a functional colony site in the current version of the sources:

  • No Structures: As of version 1.4.6.2.b, there are no structures that can be built in the Furthest Ring.
  • Interface: Later updates (v1.4.8.5) introduced a text-based interface for players who reach the destination, though its specific unlocks remain listed as “TBD” (To Be Determined).
  • Offline Interaction: When the game is in offline mode, the sources note that the interface will simply state that the “Furthest ring is empty”.

Because of the extreme time and resource requirements, reaching the Furthest Ring is considered a long-term goal for the most advanced, late-game “Phase 4” civilisations that have already established a self-sustaining positive chrono-reset engine.

item.title: Golden Spire
item.description:
Golden Spire is a religious upgrade within the Order of the Sun that significantly expands your colony’s capacity to store faith by enhancing the effectiveness of your Temples.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Unlocking: The upgrade becomes available in the Religion tab once you have accumulated at least 500 Worship (formerly known as “praised faith”).
  • Cost: The initial purchase requires 350 Faith and 150 Gold.
  • Price Scaling: It follows a price ratio of 2.5, meaning that if you unlock the ability to buy multiple levels, each subsequent tier will be significantly more expensive.

Effects and Multipliers

  • Base Bonus: Upon the first purchase, Golden Spire provides a +50% bonus to the maximum faith provided by your Temples.
  • Application: Crucially, this 50% multiplier is applied after other effects, making it a powerful “final” multiplier for your faith cap.
  • Transcendence Synergy: Once you have unlocked Transcendence, Golden Spire becomes a tiered upgrade. Each additional level purchased increases the Temple storage bonus by an additional +10%.

Strategic Importance

As your religious progression moves toward the prestige transition, the Golden Spire is essential for overcoming storage bottlenecks. Late-game milestones require increasingly large faith caps; for example, unlocking Transcendence itself requires a 125k faith cap. By boosting the storage potential of every Temple you own, the Golden Spire allows you to reach these high thresholds without needing to build an excessive number of physical structures.

Furthermore, having a larger faith cap facilitates deeper “Praising the Sun” sessions, which in turn helps you reach the worship totals required to maintain a high Solar Revolution production bonus or to generate the Epiphany needed for high Transcendence tiers.

item.title: Helios Mission
item.description:
The Helios Mission is a significant mid-to-late game space project that involves launching a rocket to the G2V spectral type star at the centre of the Cath solar system. Completing this mission is a prerequisite for moving further into the star system, specifically unlocking the Yarn Mission.

Mission Requirements and Logistics

To launch the Helios mission, you must have first successfully completed the Dune Mission. The specific resource requirements are:

  • Starcharts: 3,000
  • Titanium: 15,000
  • Science: 250,000
  • Kerosene: 1,250

The travel time for the mission is 1,200 game-days, which equates to approximately 40 minutes in real-time. This duration can be reduced significantly by researching drive upgrades such as the Antimatter Drive or Thorium Drive.
item.content:encoded:
The Helios Mission is a significant mid-to-late game space project that involves launching a rocket to the G2V spectral type star at the centre of the Cath solar system. Completing this mission is a prerequisite for moving further into the star system, specifically unlocking the Yarn Mission.

Mission Requirements and Logistics

To launch the Helios mission, you must have first successfully completed the Dune Mission. The specific resource requirements are:

  • Starcharts: 3,000
  • Titanium: 15,000
  • Science: 250,000
  • Kerosene: 1,250

The travel time for the mission is 1,200 game-days, which equates to approximately 40 minutes in real-time. This duration can be reduced significantly by researching drive upgrades such as the Antimatter Drive or Thorium Drive.

Unlocked Structures and Infrastructure

The primary importance of the Helios mission is the gateway it provides to advanced energy and antimatter production. Successfully completing the mission unlocks four critical space structures:

  • Sunlifter: The primary source of antimatter, producing 1 unit per year while also generating 30 Watts of energy.
  • Containment Chamber: Provides base storage for up to 100 units of antimatter, though it consumes 50 Watts of energy.
  • Heatsink: Increases the antimatter storage capacity of Containment Chambers by +2%.
  • Sunforge: Enhances the storage capacity of base metals (iron, titanium, gold, uranium, and unobtainium) by 1% per building.

The Helios Cycle

If you have researched Numerology, the “Helios” cycle (one of ten 5-year cycles in the game) provides specific benefits to your infrastructure. During this cycle:

  • Sunlifter energy output is increased by 50%.
  • Cryostation storage is reduced by 10%.
  • If Numeromancy is also researched, holding a festival during the Helios cycle provides double Faith income and a 1.25x multiplier to Unicorn income.

Strategic Utility

The Helios mission marks the transition into the Relic Era. To obtain the 5,000 antimatter capacity required for Relic Stations, players must typically invest heavily in Helios-based structures, specifically building enough Heatsinks (often up to 34 or 37) and Containment Chambers to reach the necessary cap. Furthermore, building a Sunlifter is a mandatory goal for completing the Energy Challenge.

item.title: Holy Genocide
item.description:
Holy Genocide is the final building in the Cryptotheology section of the Religion tab. It represents the absolute pinnacle of the endgame, requiring an immense investment of resources and spiritual progression to unlock.

Requirements and Costs

Building a Holy Genocide is significantly more expensive than any other religious structure and is gated by the highest Transcendence Tier in the game.

  • Relic Cost: 100,000 Relics.
  • Void Cost: 25,000 Void.
  • Price Ratio: 1.15.
  • Prerequisite: Transcendence Tier 25 (requiring approximately 66.96G% Epiphany).

Primary Effects

The building alters the fundamental math of your kitten population and production to favor high-efficiency resets.
item.content:encoded:
Holy Genocide is the final building in the Cryptotheology section of the Religion tab. It represents the absolute pinnacle of the endgame, requiring an immense investment of resources and spiritual progression to unlock.

Requirements and Costs

Building a Holy Genocide is significantly more expensive than any other religious structure and is gated by the highest Transcendence Tier in the game.

  • Relic Cost: 100,000 Relics.
  • Void Cost: 25,000 Void.
  • Price Ratio: 1.15.
  • Prerequisite: Transcendence Tier 25 (requiring approximately 66.96G% Epiphany).

Primary Effects

The building alters the fundamental math of your kitten population and production to favor high-efficiency resets.

  • Population Penalty: It reduces your maximum kitten capacity by 1% per level (with diminishing returns starting at 75%).
  • Prestige Boost: It provides a +2% bonus to Karma and Paragon gained per kitten upon resetting.
  • Production Compensation: To offset the lower population, it grants +2% kitten production per housing building.
  • Zebra Synergy: For players in Iron Will mode, the building provides the 2% production boost to Zebras without the accompanying decrease in maximum population.

Unlocking the Post Apocalypse Challenge

The most significant utility of Holy Genocide is that it serves as the unlock requirement for the Post Apocalypse challenge.

  • The Challenge: You enter a timeline with 10M ppm of pollution where kittens arrive 10 times slower and natural pollution dissipation is disabled.
  • The Goal: You must clear all pollution within the broken timeline.
  • The Rewards: Successful completion increases the number of cryochambers that can be operational in future runs and unlocks special policies. Each subsequent completion adds +1 to the cryochamber support cap.

Strategic Context

Holy Genocide is considered a “Phase 3” or Endgame structure. Because the building and your Transcendence Tier carry over through resets, it is used by advanced players to “chase infinity” by overcapping resources and maximizing the efficiency of Paragon farming. By the time you can afford this building, you are likely using a Type 2 Relic Engine or a Shatter Engine to generate the necessary thousands of relics and void units required for construction.

item.title: Hydroponics
item.description:
Hydroponics is an advanced, late-game space structure located on the Yarn planet in the Space tab. It serves as a powerful tool for scaling your food economy to support massive populations without the risk of starvation.

Requirements and Costs

Unlocking and building Hydroponics represents a significant technological investment:

  • Technology: You must first research Terraformation (750k Science, 5 Relics) to unlock the Hydroponics technology, which itself costs 1M Science and 25 Relics.
  • Mission: You must complete the Yarn Mission (7,500 Starcharts, 35k Titanium, 350k Science, 12k Kerosene) to access the planet.
  • Building Cost: Each Hydroponics unit costs 1 Unobtainium and 500 Kerosene.

Core Effects

Hydroponics provides three distinct types of bonuses that help manage late-game resource bottlenecks:
item.content:encoded:
Hydroponics is an advanced, late-game space structure located on the Yarn planet in the Space tab. It serves as a powerful tool for scaling your food economy to support massive populations without the risk of starvation.

Requirements and Costs

Unlocking and building Hydroponics represents a significant technological investment:

  • Technology: You must first research Terraformation (750k Science, 5 Relics) to unlock the Hydroponics technology, which itself costs 1M Science and 25 Relics.
  • Mission: You must complete the Yarn Mission (7,500 Starcharts, 35k Titanium, 350k Science, 12k Kerosene) to access the planet.
  • Building Cost: Each Hydroponics unit costs 1 Unobtainium and 500 Kerosene.

Core Effects

Hydroponics provides three distinct types of bonuses that help manage late-game resource bottlenecks:

  • Catnip Production: Each unit increases global catnip production by +2.5%.
  • Catnip Storage: Each unit provides a +10% bonus to your maximum catnip storage capacity. This bonus is additive with the Refrigeration upgrade (+75%). For example, having 50 Hydroponics alongside Refrigeration results in a +575% total storage bonus.
  • Terraforming Synergy: Every unit provides a +1.0% bonus to the kitten capacity of Terraforming Stations (which normally house +1 kitten each).

Cycle Multipliers (Numerology)

If you have researched the Numerology metaphysics upgrade, the effectiveness of Hydroponics is dramatically altered by the current Cycle:

  • Yarn Cycle: Production effectiveness is increased by +100% (doubled).
  • Piscine Cycle: Production effectiveness is decreased by -50%.

Strategic Utility

Hydroponics is primarily used to mitigate the “happiness liability” of a mature civilization. In the late game, high happiness (often over 400%) can cause kittens to consume more than triple their base catnip requirement. Because Hydroponics scales both production and storage multiplicatively with other bonuses, it allows you to maintain a high-happiness, high-productivity workforce without needing to dedicate a large portion of your population to Farmer jobs.

item.title: Industrialization
item.description:
Industrialisation is a mid-game technology that marks a major shift from basic resource gathering to advanced manufacturing and efficiency,. It is unlocked by researching Electricity and requires 100,000 Science and 25 Blueprints to purchase,.

Technological Unlocks

Researching Industrialisation is a prerequisite for several critical advancement paths:

  • Technologies: It unlocks Mechanization (which enables Factories and Engineers), Metallurgy (which improves metal production), and Combustion (which enables Oil Refineries and higher oil throughput),.
  • Workshop Upgrades: Three specific efficiency upgrades become available:
    • Barges: Increases the maximum coal storage from Harbours by 50%, which is vital for maintaining steel production and Steamworks,.
    • Advanced Automation: Increases the frequency of Workshop Automation from once per year to twice per year, helping to prevent resource caps from halting production,.
    • Logistics: Increases the effectiveness of kitten skills by 15%, providing a global multiplicative boost to productivity across all jobs.

The “Full Industrialization” Policy

Once Industrialisation is researched and the player has established at least one Factory, the Full Industrialization policy can be enacted,.

Technological Unlocks

    • Logistics: Increases the effectiveness of kitten skills by 15%, providing a global multiplicative boost to productivity across all jobs.

The “Full Industrialization” Policy

Once Industrialisation is researched and the player has established at least one Factory, the Full Industrialization policy can be enacted,.

  • Requirements: Costs 10,000 Culture and requires the player to have already chosen either Strip Mining or Clear Cutting as an environmental policy,.
  • Effects: It increases the effectiveness of Factories, making their crafting bonus 5% more powerful.
  • Drawbacks: It adds +5% to pollution levels,.
  • Strategy: Strategic advice generally suggests that Full Industrialization is the “obvious pick” from the second game run onwards, as the crafting boost outweighs the pollution penalty in most scenarios.

Strategic Progression

Industrialisation serves as a mandatory gate for reaching the Concrete era and eventually Space,. The tech path typically follows Physics → Electricity → Industrialisation → Mechanization.

This phase is critical because it allows the player to overcome bottlenecks in Titanium and Blueprints through more efficient trading and crafting systems,. Enacting Policy/ like Full Industrialization, when combined with Communism, can significantly boost the industry’s throughput for Iron, Coal, and Titanium, which are the primary requirements for mid-to-late-game infrastructure,. Furthermore, the science cap required for following technologies, such as Mechanization (115k Science) and Electronics (135k Science), necessitates the expanded storage and production capabilities that Industrialisation-related upgrades provide,,.

item.title: Isolationism
item.description:
In Kittens Game, Isolationism is a Foreign policy that focuses on economic protectionism by reducing the amount of gold required for each trade mission.

Core Mechanics

  • Cost: 1,600 Culture.
  • Prerequisite: You must have researched the Currency technology.
  • Primary Effect: Each trade mission costs 1 less gold.
  • Mutual Exclusivity: Enacting Isolationism permanently locks you out of the Diplomacy policy for the remainder of that run.

The Isolationism Policy Branch

Choosing Isolationism unlocks a specific path of follow-up policies available after you research Astronomy:
item.content:encoded:
In Kittens Game, Isolationism is a Foreign policy that focuses on economic protectionism by reducing the amount of gold required for each trade mission.

Core Mechanics

  • Cost: 1,600 Culture.
  • Prerequisite: You must have researched the Currency technology.
  • Primary Effect: Each trade mission costs 1 less gold.
  • Mutual Exclusivity: Enacting Isolationism permanently locks you out of the Diplomacy policy for the remainder of that run.

The Isolationism Policy Branch

Choosing Isolationism unlocks a specific path of follow-up policies available after you research Astronomy:

Policy Cost Effect Mutual Exclusivity
Big Stick Policy 4,000 Culture Embassies are 15% cheaper to build. Locks City On A Hill.
City On A Hill 4,000 Culture Increases the Culture cap by 5%. Locks Big Stick Policy.

Strategic Utility

The choice between Isolationism and Diplomacy is often a significant decision for early-to-mid-game trade management.

  • Gold Management: Isolationism is primarily useful if gold is your main bottleneck for trading. Some players find it preferable for facilitating high-volume exchanges with the Nagas, which are critical for mineral supplies.
  • Comparison to Diplomacy: While the gold discount “might feel good,” many experienced players consider the Isolationism branch to be weaker than the Diplomacy branch. Diplomacy reduces the catpower cost of trades (by 5) and leads to Cultural Exchange (+5% culture income), which addresses a much more persistent bottleneck in the mid-game.
  • Policy Efficiency: The follow-up policies in this branch are often described as suboptimal. Big Stick Policy and City On A Hill are noted for being relatively “weak” compared to the bonuses offered by the Diplomacy-based alternatives.

Advanced Synergies

In an Iron Will run (playing without kittens), Isolationism can be part of a strategy to reach the space era by prioritising cheaper embassies and specific trade loops to overcome the lack of a workforce.

item.title: Ivory Citadel
item.description:
An Ivory Citadel is a mid-to-high-tier religious building found in the Ziggurat section of the Religion tab. It is a critical component of the “Unicorn Era”, serving as an upgrade to the Ivory Tower and a stepping stone toward advanced structures like Sky Palaces and Sunspires.

Cost and Requirements

  • Initial Cost: 50 Unicorn Tears and 50,000 Ivory.
  • Price Ratio: 1.15 (meaning each subsequent citadel costs 15% more).
  • Prerequisite: You must have constructed at least one Ivory Tower.

Core Effects

The Ivory Citadel provides two primary benefits to your civilisation:
item.content:encoded:
An Ivory Citadel is a mid-to-high-tier religious building found in the Ziggurat section of the Religion tab. It is a critical component of the “Unicorn Era”, serving as an upgrade to the Ivory Tower and a stepping stone toward advanced structures like Sky Palaces and Sunspires.

Cost and Requirements

  • Initial Cost: 50 Unicorn Tears and 50,000 Ivory.
  • Price Ratio: 1.15 (meaning each subsequent citadel costs 15% more).
  • Prerequisite: You must have constructed at least one Ivory Tower.

Core Effects

The Ivory Citadel provides two primary benefits to your civilisation:

  • Unicorn Production: It increases your base unicorn generation by +25% per tick.
  • Ivory Meteors: It unlocks a random event called an Ivory Meteor. Each citadel provides a 0.05% chance per game-day to summon a meteor that grants a lump sum of ivory upon impact.

Strategic Analysis

Managing your Ivory Citadels is essential for transitioning from basic resource gathering to the advanced time-manipulation phase of the game.

  • The “25 Citadel” Rule: Experienced players recommend optimising for ivory early in the religious grind. A common strategy is to build approximately 25 Ivory Citadels before focusing heavily on Unicorn Utopias or Sunspires. This provides a stable enough ivory income (via meteors) to fund more expensive endgame structures.
  • AFK Resource Generation: Because Ivory Meteors provide a passive source of ivory, Citadels are highly valued for “AFK” playstyles where you may be away from the computer for long periods.
  • Synergy with Mints: While Mints also produce ivory, their output does not scale with paragon or religious buildings. Ivory Citadels, by contrast, accelerate the unicorn-to-tear pipeline, which is necessary to eventually unlock Time Crystals and Relics through Leviathan trading.

item.title: Ivory Tower
item.description:
An Ivory Tower is a religious structure found in the Ziggurat section of the Religion tab. It serves as a mid-tier building in the unicorn-to-time-crystal pipeline, primarily used to accelerate unicorn production and unlock rare celestial events.

Core Statistics and Costs

  • Cost: 25 Unicorn Tears and 25,000 Ivory.
  • Price Ratio: 1.15.
  • Prerequisite: You must have constructed at least one Unicorn Tomb.

Primary Effects

  • Unicorn Generation: Each tower provides a +10% bonus to your unicorns produced per tick.
  • Unicorn Rifts: This is the most significant feature of the building. It unlocks a random event called a Unicorn Rift, which provides a large lump sum of unicorns instantly.

Unicorn Rift Mechanics

The Ivory Tower is the only way to trigger rifts, which become more frequent and powerful as your civilisation grows:
item.content:encoded:
An Ivory Tower is a religious structure found in the Ziggurat section of the Religion tab. It serves as a mid-tier building in the unicorn-to-time-crystal pipeline, primarily used to accelerate unicorn production and unlock rare celestial events.

Core Statistics and Costs

  • Cost: 25 Unicorn Tears and 25,000 Ivory.
  • Price Ratio: 1.15.
  • Prerequisite: You must have constructed at least one Unicorn Tomb.

Primary Effects

  • Unicorn Generation: Each tower provides a +10% bonus to your unicorns produced per tick.
  • Unicorn Rifts: This is the most significant feature of the building. It unlocks a random event called a Unicorn Rift, which provides a large lump sum of unicorns instantly.

Unicorn Rift Mechanics

The Ivory Tower is the only way to trigger rifts, which become more frequent and powerful as your civilisation grows:

  • Frequency: Each tower adds a 0.05% chance per game-day for a rift to occur. For example, building 20 towers ensures a 1% chance every day.
  • Yield Scaling: While the base rift reward is 500 unicorns, it is boosted by 10% of your total unicorn ziggurat production bonus.

Strategic Progression

In the broader “Unicorn Era” strategy, the Ivory Tower is the second step in a long chain of increasingly expensive buildings:

  1. Unicorn Tomb (+5% unicorns).
  2. Ivory Tower (+10% unicorns + Rifts).
  3. Ivory Citadel (+25% unicorns + Ivory Meteors).
  4. Sky Palace (+50% unicorns + Alicorn generation).

To maximize your returns, it is often recommended to use a unicorn calculator to decide when to stop building towers and start saving for Ivory Citadels, which provide a much larger production boost and allow you to farm ivory through meteors.

item.title: Kairo Mission
item.description:
The Kairo Mission is a late-game space project that involves travelling to a dwarf planet located at the far end of the Cath solar system. Completing this mission is a crucial step for advancing your colony’s scientific capacity and transitioning into the relic-production phase of the game.

Mission Logistics and Costs

To launch a rocket to Kairo, you must have successfully completed the T-minus mission. The resource requirements for the launch are substantial:
item.content:encoded:
The Kairo Mission is a late-game space project that involves travelling to a dwarf planet located at the far end of the Cath solar system. Completing this mission is a crucial step for advancing your colony’s scientific capacity and transitioning into the relic-production phase of the game.

Mission Logistics and Costs

To launch a rocket to Kairo, you must have successfully completed the T-minus mission. The resource requirements for the launch are substantial:

  • Starcharts: 5,000
  • Titanium: 20,000
  • Science: 300,000
  • Kerosene: 7,500

The mission has a travel time of 5,000 game-days, which is approximately 2 hours, 46 minutes, and 40 seconds in real-time. This duration can be significantly reduced by researching drive upgrades like the Thorium or Antimatter Drives.

Unlocks and Infrastructure

Successfully exploring Kairo provides access to the following:

  • The Rorschach Mission: Unlocks the next stage of deep-space exploration.
  • Space Beacons: This is the primary infrastructure unlocked by the mission. Each Space Beacon costs 25,000 Starcharts, 50 Antimatter, 25,000 Alloy, and 7,500 Kerosene.
    • Science Boost: Every Space Beacon provides a massive +25,000 bonus to maximum science storage.
    • Starchart Production: They generate 0.125 starcharts per second.
    • Relic Production: Once upgraded with a Relic Station, Space Beacons become a primary source of passive relics, yielding 0.01 relics per day (scaled by your current antimatter storage).

The Kairo Cycle

Kairo is also the name of one of the ten five-year cycles that govern the Cath solar system. If you have researched Numerology and Numeromancy, the Kairo cycle and associated festivals provide unique modifiers:

  • Space Modifiers: During this cycle, the Space Beacon’s starchart production is boosted by +400%, though it imposes a -25% to -50% penalty on the science bonuses of Space Stations and Satellites, as well as the Space Elevator’s production bonus.
  • Festival Effect: Holding a festival during the Kairo cycle provides a massive 5x multiplier to starchart income.

Strategic Utility

In the late game, the Kairo mission is essential for overcoming the science storage ceiling. While early-game buildings like Libraries and Academies provide modest caps, the +25,000 boost from each Space Beacon is necessary to afford the multi-million science costs of endgame technologies. Additionally, Space Beacons are the foundation of the “Type 1 Relic Engine,” where they are used alongside Relic Stations and Black Nexuses to automate relic generation.

item.title: LHC
item.description:
The LHC (Large Hadron Collider) is a high-tier Workshop upgrade for the Accelerator building, designed to significantly expand your colony’s scientific capacity.

Unlocking and Requirements

  • Technological Path: The LHC is unlocked by researching Dimensional Physics, which itself requires Particle Physics.
  • Building Prerequisite: To benefit from this upgrade, you must have constructed Accelerators, which are energy-intensive buildings used to refine titanium into uranium.

Primary Effects and Scaling

Once purchased, the LHC provides a substantial boost to your maximum science storage:
item.content:encoded:
The LHC (Large Hadron Collider) is a high-tier Workshop upgrade for the Accelerator building, designed to significantly expand your colony’s scientific capacity.

Unlocking and Requirements

  • Technological Path: The LHC is unlocked by researching Dimensional Physics, which itself requires Particle Physics.
  • Building Prerequisite: To benefit from this upgrade, you must have constructed Accelerators, which are energy-intensive buildings used to refine titanium into uranium.

Primary Effects and Scaling

Once purchased, the LHC provides a substantial boost to your maximum science storage:

  • Science Storage Bonus: Every Accelerator in your village provides a flat +2500 bonus to maximum science.
  • Scientific Progression: This upgrade is a critical component of the late-game science infrastructure. It allows Accelerators to contribute to your total science cap alongside other major structures like Data Centres (+750 science), Bio Labs (+1500 science), and Space Beacons (+25,000 science).

Strategic Utility

The LHC is essential for breaking through the “science ceiling” required for the most advanced technologies in the game. While early-game storage relies on Libraries and Academies, the escalating costs of late-game research—such as Quantum Cryptography (1.25M science) and Exophysics (25M science)—necessitate the massive science storage bonuses provided by LHC-upgraded Accelerators.

When combined with Energy Rifts (another Accelerator upgrade that expands general resource storage), the LHC transforms the Accelerator from a simple industrial refiner into one of the most versatile and powerful storage facilities available to your kittens.

item.title: Liberalism
item.description:
Liberalism is a mid-to-late game Government policy in Kittens Game that represents a “peaceful and open society”. It is primarily designed to enhance economic efficiency through trade and cost reduction.

Core Mechanics

  • Cost: 15,000 Culture.
  • Primary Effects:
    • Enhanced Trade Relations: Provides a bonus to all trade partners equivalent to having 10 extra Tradeposts.
    • Gold Discount: Reduces all gold costs throughout the game by 20%.
  • Prerequisites: You must have built at least one Factory and previously enacted either the Monarchy or Republic policy.
  • Mutual Exclusivity: Choosing Liberalism permanently locks you out of Communism and Fascism for the remainder of your current run.

Strategic Utility

Liberalism is generally selected to resolve specific diplomatic or resource bottlenecks:

Liberalism is a mid-to-late game Government policy in Kittens Game that represents a “peaceful and open society”. It is primarily designed to enhance economic efficiency through trade and cost reduction.

Core Mechanics

  • Cost: 15,000 Culture.
  • Primary Effects:
    • Enhanced Trade Relations: Provides a bonus to all trade partners equivalent to having 10 extra Tradeposts.
    • Gold Discount: Reduces all gold costs throughout the game by 20%.
  • Prerequisites: You must have built at least one Factory and previously enacted either the Monarchy or Republic policy.
  • Mutual Exclusivity: Choosing Liberalism permanently locks you out of Communism and Fascism for the remainder of your current run.

Strategic Utility

Liberalism is generally selected to resolve specific diplomatic or resource bottlenecks:

  • Mitigating Zebra Hostility: It is highly recommended if you are struggling with Zebra hostility, as the relationship bonus makes trades more reliable and productive.
  • Boosting Catpower and Ivory: Strategic guides suggest Liberalism is excellent for long runs because it allows for more Templar upgrades. These upgrades increase your maximum catpower cap, which in turn assists with ivory generation and large-scale trading.
  • Gold Scarcity: The 20% discount on all gold costs is a significant advantage if gold production is your primary bottleneck for building expansion or promoting leaders.

The Ideological Path

Liberalism is the final stage of the “Liberty” branch of the policy tree: Liberty $\to$ Republic $\to$ Liberalism.

In contrast, if you have already negated Zebra hostility through other means (such as having a high number of Tradeposts or the Caravanserai upgrade), many players prefer Communism for its +25% boost to iron, coal, and titanium production.

item.title: Liberty
item.description:
Liberty is an early-game Government policy designed for societies that prioritise kitten morale and population growth. It is one of the first major ideological choices you will make after researching Writing.

Costs and Prerequisites

  • Culture Cost: 150.
  • Science Prerequisite: You must have researched Writing.
  • Mutual Exclusivity: Enacting Liberty permanently locks the Tradition policy for the duration of your current run.

Core Effects

Liberty provides two immediate mechanical benefits to your village:

  • Happiness Scaling: It increases the production bonus derived from happiness by 10%. This makes every point of happiness more effective at boosting your resource output.
  • Free Housing: It grants one free housing slot, allowing you to host an additional kitten without building further Huts or Log Houses.

Strategic Utility: Liberty vs. Tradition

The choice between Liberty and Tradition is a common point of debate among players, as they cater to different stages of game progression:

Costs and Prerequisites

  • Culture Cost: 150.
  • Science Prerequisite: You must have researched Writing.
  • Mutual Exclusivity: Enacting Liberty permanently locks the Tradition policy for the duration of your current run.

Core Effects

Liberty provides two immediate mechanical benefits to your village:

  • Happiness Scaling: It increases the production bonus derived from happiness by 10%. This makes every point of happiness more effective at boosting your resource output.
  • Free Housing: It grants one free housing slot, allowing you to host an additional kitten without building further Huts or Log Houses.

Strategic Utility: Liberty vs. Tradition

The choice between Liberty and Tradition is a common point of debate among players, as they cater to different stages of game progression:

Feature Liberty Tradition
Primary Goal Happiness & Production. Culture & Science.
Main Benefit +10% happiness production effect. Reduced Manuscript costs.
Secondary Benefit +1 free housing slot. Doubled Manuscript max culture effect.
Best For… Early runs with low Karma where happiness is a struggle. Mid-to-late runs where culture is the primary bottleneck.

The “Noob Trap” Debate

While Liberty is often recommended for first-time players to offset the production penalties caused by unhappy kittens, some veteran guides label it a “noob trap”. This is because culture and manuscripts become massive bottlenecks very quickly; Tradition helps bypass these hurdles more effectively than the small happiness boost from Liberty.

Progression Path

Choosing Liberty sets you on a specific “Liberal” branch of government policies:

  1. Republic (1,500 Culture): Follows Liberty and provides a global job bonus to all kittens based on your leader’s rank.
  2. Socialism (7,500 Culture): A follow-up to Republic that is noted in the records as having no actual effect on gameplay.
  3. Liberalism (15,000 Culture): A powerful late-game choice that improves trade relations and reduces all gold costs by 20%.

item.title: Manuscript
item.description:
Manuscripts are a vital mid-game craftable resource that serves as a sum of modern knowledge for your kittens, acting as a primary gate for advanced scientific research and cultural expansion.

Crafting and Acquisition

  • Unlocked By: You gain the ability to craft manuscripts after researching the Writing technology.
  • Standard Cost: Each manuscript costs 25 Parchment and 400 Culture.
  • Policy Efficiency: By enacting the Tradition policy, the cost is reduced to 20 Parchment and 300 Culture, and the manuscript’s effect on maximum culture is doubled.
  • Trading: Manuscripts can be obtained through trade with the Sharks (15% chance) once you have an Embassy level of at least 10.

Automation and Scaling

The “Theology hurdle”—the period where you must grind manuscripts manually—is a notorious progression bottleneck. To overcome this, players typically rely on the Steamworks building for automated production:
item.content:encoded:
Manuscripts are a vital mid-game craftable resource that serves as a sum of modern knowledge for your kittens, acting as a primary gate for advanced scientific research and cultural expansion.

Crafting and Acquisition

  • Unlocked By: You gain the ability to craft manuscripts after researching the Writing technology.
  • Standard Cost: Each manuscript costs 25 Parchment and 400 Culture.
  • Policy Efficiency: By enacting the Tradition policy, the cost is reduced to 20 Parchment and 300 Culture, and the manuscript’s effect on maximum culture is doubled.
  • Trading: Manuscripts can be obtained through trade with the Sharks (15% chance) once you have an Embassy level of at least 10.

Automation and Scaling

The “Theology hurdle”—the period where you must grind manuscripts manually—is a notorious progression bottleneck. To overcome this, players typically rely on the Steamworks building for automated production:

  • Printing Press: This workshop upgrade allows Steamworks to automatically print 0.0025 manuscripts per second.
  • Offset Press: Increases Steamworks production to 0.01 per second.
  • Photolithography: Further boosts production to 0.04 per second.

Primary Uses

Manuscripts are mandatory for transitioning into the religious and celestial eras of the game:

  • Technology Requirements: They are required to research Theology (35), Astronomy (65), and Navigation (100).
  • Building Construction: Each Temple requires 10 manuscripts to build.
  • Resource Conversion: They are the base material for crafting Compendiums, requiring 50 manuscripts each.
  • Culture Boost: Owning manuscripts provides a minor bonus to your maximum culture cap, though this effect suffers from diminishing returns.

Strategic Advice

  • Grinding Tactic: Before automation is available, the most efficient way to acquire manuscripts is to assign all kittens to the Hunter job to mass-produce parchment, then wait for culture to max out before using the “craft all” manuscript button.
  • Metaphysics Synergy: The Codex Vox upgrade adds a +25% bonus to your craft ratio for manuscripts and provides a 1.05x multiplier to all manuscript crafting.
  • Religious Pivot: If you enact the Lizard Relations: [Priests] ( /job/priest/) policy, manuscripts will grant maximum faith instead of a portion of the maximum culture they usually provide.

item.title: Megalith
item.description:
Megaliths are a mid-to-late game craftable resource used primarily for the construction of megastructures and the advancement of the unicorn religion.

Acquisition and Crafting

  • Workshop Crafting: Once the prerequisite technologies are met, a single megalith can be crafted using 50 Slabs, 25 Beams, and 5 Plates.
  • Trading with Nagas: Megaliths can also be obtained through trade with the Nagas. This requires 500 Ivory per trade and has a 10% chance of yielding a megalith, provided the player has reached an Embassy level of 15.

Primary Use: Ziggurats

The most critical application of megaliths is building Ziggurats, which cost 50 Megaliths, 50 Scaffolds, and 1 Blueprint each.
item.content:encoded:
Megaliths are a mid-to-late game craftable resource used primarily for the construction of megastructures and the advancement of the unicorn religion.

Acquisition and Crafting

  • Workshop Crafting: Once the prerequisite technologies are met, a single megalith can be crafted using 50 Slabs, 25 Beams, and 5 Plates.
  • Trading with Nagas: Megaliths can also be obtained through trade with the Nagas. This requires 500 Ivory per trade and has a 10% chance of yielding a megalith, provided the player has reached an Embassy level of 15.

Primary Use: Ziggurats

The most critical application of megaliths is building Ziggurats, which cost 50 Megaliths, 50 Scaffolds, and 1 Blueprint each.

  • Unlocks: Ziggurats are the gateway to the unicorn religion system, enabling the sacrifice of unicorns to obtain Unicorn Tears.
  • Culture Boost: Each Ziggurat provides a +8% increase to maximum culture.
  • Visibility: While unlocked by the Construction technology, the Ziggurat will not appear in the Bonfire tab until the player possesses approximately 5 Megaliths, 5 Scaffolds, and 1 Blueprint.

Endgame and Religious Structures

In the late game, megaliths are a mandatory component for advanced structures within the Cryptotheology and unicorn trees:

  • Sky Palace: 5 Megaliths.
  • Marker: 750 Megaliths.
  • Unicorn Graveyard: 1,000 Megaliths.
  • Unicorn Necropolis: 2,500 Megaliths.
  • Black Pyramid: 2,500 Megaliths.

Strategic Considerations

Strategic guides recommend building a significant number of Ziggurats (ideally 25–30) before heavily investing in unicorn sacrifices, as the number of tears received per sacrifice is directly determined by the total number of Ziggurats owned.

Persistence and Resets

As a crafted resource, megaliths are normally lost upon resetting the game. To carry them over into a new run, a player must have at least one Chronosphere and the Flux Condensator Workshop upgrade. The amount preserved follows a square root formula based on the total quantity held before the reset.

item.title: Metal_Plate
item.description:
Metal Plates (often simply referred to as Plates) are a foundational mid-game craftable resource refined from iron, primarily used for expanding storage and established industrial infrastructure.

Crafting and Acquisition

  • Workshop Crafting: A single Metal Plate costs 125 Iron. Because the default iron storage limit is only 50, you must first expand your capacity using Barns or other storage buildings before you can craft them.
  • Trading with Zebras: Once you have discovered the Zebras, they provide a reliable alternative source for plates. There is a 65% base chance to receive 2 plates per successful trade. This probability can be increased to 100% by reaching Embassy level 54.
  • Automation: Researching the Pneumatic Press workshop upgrade allows Steamworks to automatically convert a portion of your iron into plates twice per year whenever your iron is near its storage limit.
  • Kitten Traits: Assigning a kitten with the Metallurgist trait as your Leader provides a +0.1 bonus to the craft ratio for plates.

Primary Uses

Metal plates are mandatory for progressing into the “Titanium Era” and establishing advanced energy systems:
item.content:encoded:
Metal Plates (often simply referred to as Plates) are a foundational mid-game craftable resource refined from iron, primarily used for expanding storage and established industrial infrastructure.

Crafting and Acquisition

  • Workshop Crafting: A single Metal Plate costs 125 Iron. Because the default iron storage limit is only 50, you must first expand your capacity using Barns or other storage buildings before you can craft them.
  • Trading with Zebras: Once you have discovered the Zebras, they provide a reliable alternative source for plates. There is a 65% base chance to receive 2 plates per successful trade. This probability can be increased to 100% by reaching Embassy level 54.
  • Automation: Researching the Pneumatic Press workshop upgrade allows Steamworks to automatically convert a portion of your iron into plates twice per year whenever your iron is near its storage limit.
  • Kitten Traits: Assigning a kitten with the Metallurgist trait as your Leader provides a +0.1 bonus to the craft ratio for plates.

Primary Uses

Metal plates are mandatory for progressing into the “Titanium Era” and establishing advanced energy systems:

  • Trade Ships: Building your first fleet requires 150 plates (along with scaffolds and starcharts). These ships are essential for discovering Zebras and beginning titanium acquisition.
  • Storage Buildings: They are a core component for Harbours (75 plates) and Mints (200 plates).
  • Industrial Structures: High-tier buildings require massive quantities, including Factories (2,500 plates) and Reactors (5,000 plates).
  • Religious Infrastructure: Each Temple requires 15 plates.
  • Workshop Upgrades: Several critical upgrades depend on plates, such as Reinforced Warehouses (50 plates) and Alloy Barns (750 plates).

Strategic Utility

In the early-to-mid game, plates are often a bottleneck for expanding storage. Strategic guides suggest that if your Coal production is too slow to craft Steel, you should instead focus your iron on crafting plates to build more Harbours. This increases your global storage caps, allowing you to eventually afford the more expensive upgrades and buildings.

Persistence and Resets

As a crafted resource, Metal Plates are normally lost upon resetting the game. To preserve a portion of your stockpile for the next run, you must possess at least one Chronosphere and the Flux Condensator workshop upgrade. The amount carried over is determined by the number of active Chronospheres and the square root of your total plate count at the time of reset.

item.title: Militarize_Space
item.description:
Militarize Space is a late-game Foreign policy that focuses on aggressive scientific research to expand your knowledge limits. It specifically enhances the synergy between your orbital infrastructure and ground-based research buildings.

Core Effects and Requirements

  • Cost: 10,000 Culture.
  • Prerequisite: You must have successfully launched at least one Satellite.
  • Scientific Bonus: It makes the Satellite science bonus to Observatories 10% more powerful.
  • Mutual Exclusivity: Choosing this policy permanently locks you out of the Outer Space Treaty for the remainder of your current run.

Strategic Analysis: Militarize Space vs. Outer Space Treaty

Deciding between these two policies depends on whether your current bottleneck is Science storage or Trade efficiency.

Strategic Analysis: Militarize Space vs. Outer Space Treaty

Deciding between these two policies depends on whether your current bottleneck is Science storage or Trade efficiency.

Policy Primary Benefit Best Used When…
Militarize Space Increases maximum Science storage via Satellites. All your space structures and ground buildings are consistently hitting their science caps.
Outer Space Treaty Improves trade relations with all races (equivalent to 10 Tradeposts). You need to maximize trade yields (especially for Titanium or Unobtainium).

Expert Recommendation

In most standard playstyles, Outer Space Treaty is considered the superior choice because trade remains a vital part of resource acquisition even in the late game. Science storage can often be expanded through other means—such as building more Data Centers, Bio Labs, or Research Vessels—without sacrificing a policy slot.

However, if you are deep into the space era and find that your science limit is preventing you from researching the next multi-million science technology (like Exophysics or Quantum Cryptography), Militarize Space can provide that final necessary push.

item.title: Monarchy
item.description:
Monarchy is a mid-game Government policy that significantly amplifies the utility of your civilisation’s leader. It is generally considered the most effective choice in its tier because it doubles the effectiveness of the leader’s unique trait, providing a flexible bonus that you can swap as your needs change.

Core Mechanics

  • Cost: 1,500 Culture.
  • Prerequisites: You must have researched Writing and enacted the Tradition policy.
  • Mutual Exclusivity: Choosing Monarchy permanently locks out the Autocracy and Republic policies for the remainder of that run.
  • The Gold Penalty: Maintaining the royal court imposes a -10% penalty to your overall gold production.

Trait Doubling Effects

The primary draw of Monarchy is its interaction with kitten traits. When a kitten is assigned as the leader, their trait becomes twice as powerful. Common synergies include:
item.content:encoded:
Monarchy is a mid-game Government policy that significantly amplifies the utility of your civilisation’s leader. It is generally considered the most effective choice in its tier because it doubles the effectiveness of the leader’s unique trait, providing a flexible bonus that you can swap as your needs change.

Core Mechanics

  • Cost: 1,500 Culture.
  • Prerequisites: You must have researched Writing and enacted the Tradition policy.
  • Mutual Exclusivity: Choosing Monarchy permanently locks out the Autocracy and Republic policies for the remainder of that run.
  • The Gold Penalty: Maintaining the royal court imposes a -10% penalty to your overall gold production.

Trait Doubling Effects

The primary draw of Monarchy is its interaction with kitten traits. When a kitten is assigned as the leader, their trait becomes twice as powerful. Common synergies include:

  • Artisan Leader: Boosts crafting efficiency. Under Monarchy, the bonus increases from 5% to 10%.
  • Scientist Leader: Reduces the science cost of technologies and workshop upgrades. Under Monarchy, the discount is doubled.
  • Philosopher Leader: Reduces the faith and gold costs for the Order of the Sun.

Strategic Comparison: Monarchy vs. Republic

As discussed previously with other policies, choosing between the government branches depends on your current population and goals.

Feature Monarchy Republic
Prerequisite Tradition (Culture-focused) Liberty (Happiness-focused)
Primary Effect Doubles the leader’s specific trait Small production boost to all kittens
Penalty -10% Gold production None
Expert Verdict Often called “Amazing” due to its high flexibility. Bonuses are often considered too small compared to Monarchy.

Advanced Synergy: The “11 Kitten” Bonus

The strength of Monarchy scales with your leader’s rank. You can use gold and experience to promote your leader up to five times. A high-ranking Artisan leader under a Monarchy is so efficient that it provides a crafting boost equivalent to having 11 extra kittens assigned to that resource.

Because you can swap leaders at any time without a penalty, Monarchy allows you to adapt to your current bottleneck—switching to a Scientist when researching expensive tech like Theology, or an Artisan when mass-producing Manuscripts or Compendiums.

item.title: Moon Mission
item.description:
The Moon Mission is a pivotal space project in Kittens Game that involves launching a rocket to Redmoon, a satellite of the planet Cath. It represents the first major step into space exploration beyond orbital deployment and is the primary gateway to the Unobtainium Era.

Mission Requirements and Logistics

  • Prerequisites: You must first research Rocketry and successfully complete the Orbital Launch mission.
  • Resource Costs: The launch requires 500 Starcharts, 5000 Titanium, 125k Science, and 45k Oil.
  • Travel Time: The journey to Redmoon takes 30 game-days, which is approximately 1 minute in real-time. This can be further reduced by drive upgrades like the Antimatter or Thorium Drives.

Unlocks and Infrastructure

Successfully completing the Moon Mission is essential for unlocking the infrastructure required to produce and store advanced materials:
item.content:encoded:
The Moon Mission is a pivotal space project in Kittens Game that involves launching a rocket to Redmoon, a satellite of the planet Cath. It represents the first major step into space exploration beyond orbital deployment and is the primary gateway to the Unobtainium Era.

Mission Requirements and Logistics

  • Prerequisites: You must first research Rocketry and successfully complete the Orbital Launch mission.
  • Resource Costs: The launch requires 500 Starcharts, 5000 Titanium, 125k Science, and 45k Oil.
  • Travel Time: The journey to Redmoon takes 30 game-days, which is approximately 1 minute in real-time. This can be further reduced by drive upgrades like the Antimatter or Thorium Drives.

Unlocks and Infrastructure

Successfully completing the Moon Mission is essential for unlocking the infrastructure required to produce and store advanced materials:

  • Lunar Outpost: A nuclear-powered mining facility that is the primary source of Unobtainium. It consumes 1.75 uranium per second to produce 0.035 unobtainium per second.
  • Moon Base: A vital storage building that provides a base capacity of +150 Unobtainium, along with significant boosts to other resources such as Catnip (+45k), Wood (+25k), and Titanium (+1250).
  • Subsequent Missions: Completing the Moon Mission is a prerequisite for launching missions to Dune and Piscine.

Strategic Importance

  • The Unobtainium Bottleneck: Progressing past the mid-game is heavily gated by Unobtainium, which is required for Metaphysics upgrades and the high-tier Eludium alloy.
  • Oil Management: A major hurdle for this mission is oil storage. While the mission itself costs 45k oil, building the first Moon Base (which is necessary to store enough unobtainium for Unobtainium Huts) requires 70k oil. Players often need to build numerous Oil Wells or tankers to reach these caps.
  • Resource Scaling: The effectiveness of Moon Bases can be significantly boosted by the AI Bases upgrade, which adds a 10% storage bonus per AI Core.
  • Challenges: In the Black Sky Challenge, the starchart requirement for the preceding Orbital Launch is removed, but science and oil costs are significantly increased, making the path to the Moon Mission more difficult.

Economic Utility

Beyond unobtainium, the Catnip storage provided by Moon Bases (45k) is critical for surviving the harsh food penalties of Winter in the late game, especially during challenges like “Winter Has Come” where the seasonal cycle is permanently frozen in winter.

item.title: Mysticism
item.description:
Mysticism is a mid-game Philosophy policy that provides a global bonus to your Culture and Faith production. It represents a societal shift towards acknowledging forces beyond feline comprehension, prioritising spiritual and artistic growth over pure logic.

Key Statistics

  • Cost: 3,000 Culture.
  • Primary Effects: +5% Culture production and +5% Faith production.
  • Prerequisites: Researching the Philosophy technology and enacting either the Stoicism or Epicureanism policy.
  • Mutually Exclusive: Choosing Mysticism permanently locks you out of the Rationality policy for the remainder of the run.

Strategic Utility

In the Kittens Game community, Mysticism is almost universally recommended over its counterpart, Rationality.
item.content:encoded:
Mysticism is a mid-game Philosophy policy that provides a global bonus to your Culture and Faith production. It represents a societal shift towards acknowledging forces beyond feline comprehension, prioritising spiritual and artistic growth over pure logic.

Key Statistics

  • Cost: 3,000 Culture.
  • Primary Effects: +5% Culture production and +5% Faith production.
  • Prerequisites: Researching the Philosophy technology and enacting either the Stoicism or Epicureanism policy.
  • Mutually Exclusive: Choosing Mysticism permanently locks you out of the Rationality policy for the remainder of the run.

Strategic Utility

In the Kittens Game community, Mysticism is almost universally recommended over its counterpart, Rationality.

  • The Resource Bottleneck: Faith and culture are considered “slow” resources that are often difficult to accumulate in large quantities during the mid-game.
  • Science Overabundance: The alternative policy, Rationality, provides a bonus to science and iron. However, science is generally viewed as “easy” to acquire through buildings like Libraries, Academies, and Observatories, making a percentage bonus less impactful.
  • Religious Engine: The +5% Faith bonus is particularly valuable for accelerating your progress through the Order of the Sun upgrades, helping you reach the Solar Revolution production cap more efficiently.

Strategic Recommendation

Most experienced players follow the Stoicism -> Mysticism path. While a 5% increase might seem minor, the fact that it targets two of the most persistent mid-game bottlenecks makes it the “meta” choice for standard runs.

item.title: Nanotechnology
item.description:
Nanotechnology is a high-level science in the late-mid game that serves as a vital gateway to endgame industrial efficiency and space exploration. It is unlocked after researching Nuclear Fission and requires 200,000 Science and 150 Blueprints to research.

Unlocked Workshop Upgrades

Researching Nanotechnology provides access to several powerful upgrades that drastically scale your production and efficiency:

  • Augmentations: This is one of the most significant upgrades for population efficiency, as it increases the production bonus from kitten skills by 100%. This stacks with other multipliers to make your specialized workforce far more productive.
  • Nanosuits: This upgrade provides a flat +0.5 hunting bonus, increasing the yield of rare resources like Furs and Ivory from hunts. Notably, the Manager kitten trait provides a bonus equivalent to this upgrade.
  • Photovoltaic Cells: This significantly boosts your renewable energy infrastructure by making Solar Farms 50% more effective at producing energy.
  • Fluidized Reactors: This dramatically improves the output of your Calciners, causing them to produce +100% more Iron and +300% more Titanium.

Role in Scientific Progression

Nanotechnology is a mandatory prerequisite for the following advanced technologies:

  • Augmentations: This is one of the most significant upgrades for population efficiency, as it increases the production bonus from kitten skills by 100%. This stacks with other multipliers to make your specialized workforce far more productive.
  • Nanosuits: This upgrade provides a flat +0.5 hunting bonus, increasing the yield of rare resources like Furs and Ivory from hunts. Notably, the Manager kitten trait provides a bonus equivalent to this upgrade.
  • Photovoltaic Cells: This significantly boosts your renewable energy infrastructure by making Solar Farms 50% more effective at producing energy.
  • Fluidized Reactors: This dramatically improves the output of your Calciners, causing them to produce +100% more Iron and +300% more Titanium.

Role in Scientific Progression

Nanotechnology is a mandatory prerequisite for the following advanced technologies:

  • Superconductors: The next step in the physics tree, which eventually leads to Antimatter.
  • Particle Physics: This unlocks Accelerators, which are essential for generating Uranium and expanding resource storage.

Space and Industrial Utility

In addition to workshop upgrades, Nanotechnology is a required component for the Space Elevator (when combined with Orbital Engineering). The Space Elevator is crucial for the space race as it reduces the oil requirements for space missions and structures by up to 75% through diminishing returns.

item.title: Necrocracy
item.description:
Necrocracy is an endgame Government policy that provides a global production bonus based on your accumulated Black Liquid Sorrow (BLS) and increases the energy capacity of Leviathans. It represents a society that has offered itself to the “Elders” (Leviathans), trading kittenhood for dark industrial efficiency.

Core Statistics and Requirements

Attribute Details
Culture Cost 1,500,000
Prerequisite Must have made at least one trade with the Leviathans
Primary Effect Global production bonus: 0.1% for every 1% of Black Liquid Sorrow (BLS)
Secondary Effect Leviathan Energy Cap Boost: +5%
Mutual Exclusivity Locks out Transkittenism and Radical Xenophobia

Strategic Utility

Necrocracy is considered a niche but powerful choice for players in the deep Late Game or End Game phases.

Necrocracy is an endgame Government policy that provides a global production bonus based on your accumulated Black Liquid Sorrow (BLS) and increases the energy capacity of Leviathans. It represents a society that has offered itself to the “Elders” (Leviathans), trading kittenhood for dark industrial efficiency.

Core Statistics and Requirements

Attribute Details
Culture Cost 1,500,000
Prerequisite Must have made at least one trade with the Leviathans
Primary Effect Global production bonus: 0.1% for every 1% of Black Liquid Sorrow (BLS)
Secondary Effect Leviathan Energy Cap Boost: +5%
Mutual Exclusivity Locks out Transkittenism and Radical Xenophobia

Strategic Utility

Necrocracy is considered a niche but powerful choice for players in the deep Late Game or End Game phases.

  • Production Scaling: The primary draw is the production bonus tied to BLS. In the late game, players accumulate BLS through Unicorn Tears or trading, and buildings like Black Cores can increase the BLS limit.
  • Leviathan Energy: The 5% boost to the Leviathan Energy Cap allows these elders to stay longer and provide better trade ratios when fed necrocorns.
  • The “Paragon” Threshold: Strategic advice suggests that Necrocracy’s production bonus requires a significant amount of Paragon to effectively outcompete the utility of alternative policies.

Comparison with Alternatives

Because this policy is mutually exclusive with two other high-tier options, your choice depends on your current bottleneck:

  • Vs. Transkittenism: Transkittenism is generally preferred by many players because it prevents the AI Apocalypse and doubles Gigaflop production, which is essential for scaling Moon Base storage.
  • Vs. Radical Xenophobia: Radical Xenophobia focuses on Mausoleums and Pacts. Necrocracy is usually seen as more generally useful for raw production compared to the “steep debt” associated with Pact-based play.

Strategic Recommendation

Most expert advice suggests holding off on enacting any of these three policies as long as possible. If your primary goal is to maximise raw output and you have a massive stockpile of Black Liquid Sorrow, Necrocracy is the superior choice for production. However, if you are struggling with energy or science caps, Transkittenism is often the more practical route.

item.title: Oil Processing
item.description:
Oil processing in Kittens Game is a multi-stage industrial system that involves extracting raw oil, refining it for greater efficiency, and eventually converting it into high-tier fuels like Kerosene.

Primary Production and Automation

Oil is initially produced by Oil Wells (unlocked via Chemistry), which provide a base of +0.02 oil per tick. As you progress, you can unlock two primary methods for scaling this output:

  • Mechanical Extraction: The Pumpjack workshop upgrade improves Oil Well effectiveness by 45% and introduces automation (costing 1 Watt per well), while the Oil Refinery upgrade provides a separate +35% boost.
  • Biological Refinement: After researching Biochemistry, the Biofuel Processing upgrade allows Bio Labs to automatically convert 5 catnip/sec into 0.10 oil/sec at the cost of 1 Watt of energy. This biological output can be further increased by 60% with the GM Catnip genetics upgrade.

Refinement Multipliers

Once you have established a steady flow of raw oil, you can use specialized technologies and structures to improve its refinement:
item.content:encoded:
Oil processing in Kittens Game is a multi-stage industrial system that involves extracting raw oil, refining it for greater efficiency, and eventually converting it into high-tier fuels like Kerosene.

Primary Production and Automation

Oil is initially produced by Oil Wells (unlocked via Chemistry), which provide a base of +0.02 oil per tick. As you progress, you can unlock two primary methods for scaling this output:

  • Mechanical Extraction: The Pumpjack workshop upgrade improves Oil Well effectiveness by 45% and introduces automation (costing 1 Watt per well), while the Oil Refinery upgrade provides a separate +35% boost.
  • Biological Refinement: After researching Biochemistry, the Biofuel Processing upgrade allows Bio Labs to automatically convert 5 catnip/sec into 0.10 oil/sec at the cost of 1 Watt of energy. This biological output can be further increased by 60% with the GM Catnip genetics upgrade.

Refinement Multipliers

Once you have established a steady flow of raw oil, you can use specialized technologies and structures to improve its refinement:

  • Oil Distillation: Researching Rocketry unlocks this upgrade, which provides a massive 75% boost to the output of your Oil Wells.
  • Factory Processing: This workshop upgrade (unlocked by the Oil Processing technology) causes every Factory to increase your oil refinement effectiveness by 5%. This bonus is particularly powerful because it stacks multiplicatively with regular craft bonuses.
  • Space Manufacturing: Factories also apply a “Space Production Bonus” to structures like Hydraulic Fracturers (on Dune), which produce 2.5 oil/sec.

Processed Output: Kerosene

The ultimate goal of oil processing is the creation of Kerosene, a specialized fuel required for nearly all space-faring missions and structures.

  • Crafting: Kerosene is crafted from oil once the Oil Processing technology is researched.
  • Efficiency: The Factory Processing workshop upgrade also provides a +5% bonus specifically to Kerosene crafting.
  • Automation: In the late game, Engineers can be assigned to automatically craft Kerosene, ensuring your oil production does not stall when it hits the storage cap.

Strategic Consumption and Storage

Managing processed oil is a delicate balance, as it is a major input for other systems:

  • Industrial Use: Calciners consume oil (-0.024/tick) to produce Iron and Titanium.
  • Energy Production: Magnetos consume oil (-0.05/tick) to provide a global production boost.
  • Storage Barriers: Oil has a default storage cap of 1,500. This limit is expanded by Oil Wells (+1500), Tankers (+500), and large-scale structures like Moon Bases (+3500) and Cryostations (+7500). High oil storage is mandatory for the Moon Mission (45K Oil) and building Lunar Outposts (55K Oil).

item.title: Open Woodlands
item.description:
Open Woodlands is a mid-to-late game Environment policy that boosts raw resource output at the cost of increased pollution. It is part of the Environmentalism branch of the policy tree and becomes available once you have established a stable cultural and scientific foundation.

Core Mechanics

  • Cost: 10,000 Culture.
  • Primary Effect: Provides a +12.5% boost to both Wood and Mineral production.
  • Drawback: Increases Pollution by +5%.
  • Prerequisites: You must have researched the Ecology technology and previously enacted the Environmentalism policy.
  • Mutual Exclusivity: Choosing Open Woodlands permanently locks out the Conservation policy for the remainder of the run.

Strategic Comparison

In most playthroughs, Open Woodlands is considered the superior choice compared to its alternative, Conservation.

Strategic Comparison

In most playthroughs, Open Woodlands is considered the superior choice compared to its alternative, Conservation.

  • Production vs. Morale: While Conservation provides a small happiness boost and reduces pollution, the production bonuses from Open Woodlands are generally viewed as more impactful for scaling a growing village.
  • Resource Scaling: The 12.5% boost to wood and minerals provides essential throughput for mid-game building projects, making it a “must-have” for players focused on rapid economic expansion.

Iron Will Specifics

For players engaged in an Iron Will run (playing without kittens), Open Woodlands provides specialized utility:

  • Catnip Refinement: Grants a 4.16% bonus to catnip-to-wood refinement.
  • Meteor Rewards: Provides a 4.16% bonus to minerals gathered from meteor events.

Environmental Impact

Like many industrial-leaning policies, the +5% pollution penalty can eventually lead to reduced catnip production and lower kitten happiness if not managed. However, by the time you can afford the 10,000 culture cost, your infrastructure is typically robust enough to absorb this penalty in exchange for higher material yields.

item.title: Orbital Launch
item.description:
The Orbital Launch mission serves as the critical gateway in the sources, transitioning the colony from terrestrial development to the Space era. It is the first project available in the “Ground Control” section of the Space tab once the Rocketry technology has been researched. For a standard game run, the launch requires a stockpile of 250 Starcharts, 5,000 Catpower, 100,000 Science, and 15,000 Oil.

Requirements and Challenge Variations

The resource demands for this mission change significantly depending on the active game mode:
item.content:encoded:
The Orbital Launch mission serves as the critical gateway in the sources, transitioning the colony from terrestrial development to the Space era. It is the first project available in the “Ground Control” section of the Space tab once the Rocketry technology has been researched. For a standard game run, the launch requires a stockpile of 250 Starcharts, 5,000 Catpower, 100,000 Science, and 15,000 Oil.

Requirements and Challenge Variations

The resource demands for this mission change significantly depending on the active game mode:

  • Standard Costs: As noted, the primary hurdles are the science and oil caps.
  • Black Sky Challenge: In this mode, the Starchart requirement is removed entirely (0). However, to compensate, the mission requires 1.1 million Science, 55,000 Catpower, and 165,000 Oil, representing an 11-fold increase for non-starchart resources.

Unlocks and Infrastructure

Successfully completing the Orbital Launch provides access to the foundational structures and locations of the star system:

  • Missions and Locations: It unlocks the Moon Mission and makes the planet Cath accessible.
  • Satellite Deployment: Players can begin deploying Satellites, which consume energy to provide a passive income of Starcharts (0.005/sec) and increase the science storage capacity of Observatories by 5%.
  • Space Elevator: This structure is essential for long-term expansion as it provides a 1% bonus to all space structures and reduces the oil requirements for future space missions and buildings by 5% (up to a 75% discount with diminishing returns).
  • Space Stations: These provide a 50% science bonus and housing for +2 kittens.

Strategic Considerations

  • The Oil Bottleneck: Strategic guides highlight that Oil management is the dominant constraint at this stage. While the launch itself costs 15,000 Oil, the next mission requires 45,000, and the first Moon Base requires 70,000, necessitating a rapid increase in Oil Wells and storage.
  • Resource Pivot: This milestone marks the end of “Phase 1” and “Phase 2” of the game; once space is unlocked, common terrestrial resources begin to matter less as the economy shifts toward Uranium, Unobtainium, and Antimatter.
  • Iron Will Mode: In this specialized mode, achieving an Orbital Launch is a prerequisite for obtaining the Space Oddity gold star achievement. Players in this mode often find the Catpower and Gold requirements for space missions particularly challenging due to the lack of a kitten workforce.

item.title: Order Of The Stars
item.description:
Order of the Stars is a late-game Government policy that focuses on accelerating religious progression by increasing Faith production. It represents a shift where [Priests] ( /job/priest/) take control of the government after the horrors of deep space are discovered.

Core Mechanics and Costs

  • Cost: 150,000 Culture.
  • Primary Effect: Provides a +20% bonus to Faith production.
  • Leadership Restriction: Once enacted, only kittens with the Priest job are allowed to be assigned as the village leader.
  • Prerequisites: You must have reached Dune and currently have a kitten assigned to the Priest job.
  • Mutual Exclusivity: This policy is mutually exclusive with Technocracy (+20% science cap) and Cosmological Libertarianism (+15% unobtainium production).

Strategic Utility

Choosing Order of the Stars is a highly specific strategic decision depending on your current run goals:
