Core Mechanics and Costs

  • Cost: 150,000 Culture.
  • Primary Effect: Provides a +20% bonus to Faith production.
  • Leadership Restriction: Once enacted, only kittens with the Priest job are allowed to be assigned as the village leader.
  • Prerequisites: You must have reached Dune and currently have a kitten assigned to the Priest job.
  • Mutual Exclusivity: This policy is mutually exclusive with Technocracy (+20% science cap) and Cosmological Libertarianism (+15% unobtainium production).

Strategic Utility

Choosing Order of the Stars is a highly specific strategic decision depending on your current run goals:

  • The Religion Grind: This policy is the ideal choice for runs where your primary objective is to work on religious bonuses and grind Transcendence tiers. Because faith production is naturally slow, the +20% boost is significant for reaching high tiers like TT15, which is a major gateway for late-game time crystal production.
  • Leadership Flexibility: Although the policy restricts leaders to [Priests] ( /job/priest/), it is noted in endgame guides that the policy remains effective even if you choose to have no leader assigned at all.
  • Comparison with Alternatives:
    • Most players prefer Cosmological Libertarianism because the need for Unobtainium is often more pressing than Faith in the late game.
    • Technocracy is generally avoided because science storage can be easily increased through other buildings and upgrades, making it less valuable than a production boost.

When to Enact

You should consider Order of the Stars if you have already optimized your Unobtainium production and are now hitting a bottleneck with your Apocrypha bonus or trying to break through higher Transcendence levels to fuel your Time Crystal engine.

item.title: Outer_Space_Treaty
item.description:
The Outer Space Treaty is a high-tier Foreign policy in Kittens Game that improves global trade relations by declaring space a domain for all races. It is primarily used to boost the effectiveness of trade with all civilisations once you have reached the space era.

Requirements and Costs

To enact this policy, your civilisation must meet the following criteria:

  • Cost: 10,000 Culture.
  • Prerequisite: You must have launched at least one Satellite.
  • Mutual Exclusivity: Choosing this policy permanently locks out the Militarize Space policy for the remainder of your current run.

Core Effects

  • Global Trade Bonus: It provides a permanent boost to relations with all trading partners, equivalent to having 10 extra Tradeposts.
  • Pacifism Challenge Goal: Researching this policy and subsequently resetting the game is the primary objective and win condition for the Pacifism Challenge.

Strategic Comparison

When choosing between the available space policies, the Outer Space Treaty is widely considered the superior choice for most playstyles.

When choosing between the available space policies, the Outer Space Treaty is widely considered the superior choice for most playstyles.

Policy Primary Benefit Strategic Context
Outer Space Treaty Better trade relations (+10 Tradeposts). Generally useful most of the time to resolve resource bottlenecks through trade.
Militarize Space Boosts the science bonus that Satellites provide to Observatories. Only recommended if your space structures are consistently hitting their science storage caps.

Role in the Endgame

In the late game, the Outer Space Treaty serves as a vital component for players focusing on system arbitrage and trade efficiency. Because trade is one of the most effective ways to acquire restricted resources like Titanium and Iron without relying on slower production buildings, the relationship bonus provided by the treaty helps ensure consistent, high-yield exchanges with all discovered races.

item.title: Paragon
item.description:
Paragon is a unique, persistent resource in Kittens Game that is fundamental to the game’s prestige system, allowing players to purchase permanent upgrades that make subsequent runs easier.

Acquisition and Persistence

Paragon is primarily acquired by reaching a certain population level before resetting the game:

  • You gain Paragon upon reset if you have more than 70 kittens [3, 4].
  • The reward is one point per kitten over 70.
  • Paragon is also gained at a passive rate of +1 for every 1,000 years that pass in the game.
  • Paragon, along with burned paragon, carries over after every game reset.

Primary Purpose: The Metaphysics System

Paragon is the currency used to purchase permanent enhancements in the Metaphysics tab. The Metaphysics system itself must be researched again each run, but the purchased upgrades persist.
item.content:encoded:
Paragon is a unique, persistent resource in Kittens Game that is fundamental to the game’s prestige system, allowing players to purchase permanent upgrades that make subsequent runs easier.

Acquisition and Persistence

Paragon is primarily acquired by reaching a certain population level before resetting the game:

  • You gain Paragon upon reset if you have more than 70 kittens [3, 4].
  • The reward is one point per kitten over 70.
  • Paragon is also gained at a passive rate of +1 for every 1,000 years that pass in the game.
  • Paragon, along with burned paragon, carries over after every game reset.

Primary Purpose: The Metaphysics System

Paragon is the currency used to purchase permanent enhancements in the Metaphysics tab. The Metaphysics system itself must be researched again each run, but the purchased upgrades persist.

The central function of Metaphysics upgrades is to reduce the cost growth of buildings, often referred to as price ratio reduction, allowing players to buy “lots more stuff” [6-8]. This reduction only applies to buildings in the Bonfire tab.

Key Metaphysics upgrades and their Paragon costs include:

Upgrade Category Upgrade Name Paragon Cost Purpose/Effect
Price Ratio Reduction Enlightenment 5 Reduces all price ratios by 1%.
Golden Ratio 50 [9] Reduces price ratios by approximately 1.618% [9].
Divine Proportion 100 [10] Reduces price ratios by approximately 1.777% [10].
Vitruvian Feline 250 [10] Reduces price ratios by 2% [10].
Renaissance 750 [10] Reduces price ratios by 2.25% [10].
QoL/Progression Diplomacy 5 [10] Races are discovered earlier and with better standing [10].
Anachronomancy 125 [11] Saves Time Crystals and Chronophysics technology across resets [11].
Megalomania 10 [9] Unlocks late-game Unicorn mechanics (Markers and Black Pyramids) [9].
Adjustment Bureau 5 [12] Unlocks Challenges [12, 13].

Effects on Production and Storage

Paragon provides substantial, permanent boosts to your civilization:

  • Production Boost: Paragon generally increases production rates [2, 14]. However, the production benefit experiences diminishing returns. Once a player reaches about 150 Paragon, the effectiveness starts to decrease. For example, 150 Paragon provides a 150% production increase, but 400 Paragon only increases it to 190%.
  • Storage Boost: Paragon increases resource storage capacity, and this effect never diminishes [15]. High levels of Paragon are crucial for bypassing major storage bottlenecks [15]. Specifically, Paragon boosts Moon Bases and Cryostations storage by 0.1% per Paragon [16].
  • Space Production: It is noted that Paragon has no effect on the production of space structures [17].

The Production Bonus Threshold

The global production bonus increases linearly for your first 150 Paragon (1 point = +1% production) After this point, each additional point of Paragon provides progressively less production value:

  • 150 Paragon: +150% productivity bonus
  • 200 Paragon: +175% productivity bonus
  • 400 Paragon: +190% productivity bonus

Plateau: Once you reach approximately 300 normal Paragon, additional points provide negligible increases to your production rates.

The Exception: Storage Capacity Unlike the production bonus, the effectiveness of Paragon on storage never diminishes. Each point of Paragon provides a permanent +0.1% bonus to resource storage capacity. This makes high levels of Paragon (into the thousands or millions) essential for the late-game “Chrono-resets,” where breaking through massive Unobtainium storage caps is the primary bottleneck.

Burned Paragon

Players have the option to “burn” Paragon, which is useful for specialized runs and stacking bonuses [4, 18]:

  • Effectiveness: Burned Paragon has half the effectiveness of regular Paragon, but it stacks with regular Paragon. The production gain from the first 75 burned Paragon gives a 1% production gain and is additive to the normal Paragon bonus [19].
  • Strategy: It is suggested that players aiming for maximum efficiency burn Paragon once they reach around 400 regular Paragon [19]. The boost from burned Paragon is particularly important in the Iron Will challenge mode, where the Metaphysics price ratio upgrades are still beneficial [18].

End Game Scaling

In the very late game, Paragon scaling can be improved through high-cost Metaphysics upgrades called Sefirot metas (e.g., Malkuth, Yesod, Hod, etc.) [20]. These upgrades cost between 500 Paragon (Malkuth) and 60,000 Paragon (Keter) [12, 21]. Each Sefirot meta improves Paragon effect and scaling by 5% [12, 21].

For players pursuing extreme end-game goals, specific strategies exist for rapid Paragon generation, such as the “cryo engine” method, which can yield up to 15 million Paragon per day [22].

You accumulate paragon primarily through two mechanisms: resetting your game based on your kitten population, and through the passage of time [5, 6].

Primary Methods of Accumulation

  1. Resetting with Kittens: Paragon is gained when you reset the game if you have more than 70 kittens [5-7]. You earn one paragon point for every kitten beyond the initial 70 [7].

    • Resetting the game is considered the fifth step in the basic gameplay cycle, occurring when progress becomes too slow.
    • For your first reset, it is recommended to aim for 130 or more kittens to secure at least 60 paragon [8]. Subsequent runs aim for higher kitten counts, such as 170+ for 100 paragon, or 220+ for 150 paragon [8].

  2. Time Passage: You are granted +1 paragon for every 1,000 years that pass in the game.

Advanced and End-Game Accumulation

In the later stages of the game, players utilize highly efficient methods to generate massive amounts of paragon:

  • Mass Shatterings (Time Skipping): You can gain paragon rapidly by advancing time using Time Crystals (TCs) and the Chronoforge or Time Boilers. This method yields 1 paragon for every thousand years skipped [9]. This technique is sometimes referred to as the “Shatter Engine” [9, 10].
  • The Holy Genocide Upgrade: Once you reach Transcendence-Tier 25 and purchase the Holy Genocide cryptotheology upgrade, resetting grants a +2% increase in paragon gained per kitten [11].
  • The Cryo Engine: A late-game technique involving resetting while possessing 3,000 Cryochambers is theorised to yield approximately 15 million paragon per day [12].
  • Mass Kitten Accumulation: Utilizing Festivals, especially when combined with the Terraformation mission upgrade “Tempus Fugit” (not explicitly detailed how it works with festivals in the source, but mentioned in context), to rapidly grow a large kitten population (e.g., ~60,000 kittens) can yield up to 120,000 paragon per day [9].

Once accumulated, paragon is used to purchase Metaphysics upgrades such as the price ratio reduction upgrades (e.g., Enlightenment, Golden Ratio, Divine Proportion, Vitruvian Feline, and Renaissance), which make buildings cheaper in future runs [2, 13-15].

Analogy: Accumulating paragon is like cashing in your retirement savings (your current civilization) to gain a permanent, compounding financial head start (Metaphysics bonuses and production boosts) for your next business venture (the next run). The more investment you put into your current civilization (getting more than 70 kittens), the larger the bonus you get for the next startup. In the end-game, you learn to manipulate time itself to fast-forward through years and maximize these compounded benefits.

item.title: Parchment
item.description:
Parchment is a vital mid-game craftable resource in Kittens Game that serves as the foundation for your colony’s cultural and religious expansion. It is primarily used to construct culture-generating buildings and to craft more advanced intellectual resources.

Acquisition and Crafting

  • Unlocking: You gain the ability to craft parchment after researching the Writing technology (3,600 Science).
  • Workshop Crafting: A single unit of parchment is crafted from 175 Furs in the Workshop.
  • Trading: Once you reach Embassy level 5 with the Sharks, they have a 25% chance of selling you parchment in exchange for iron. This chance can be increased by +25% if you enact the Shark Relations: Scribes policy.
  • Automation: While there is no direct early-game automation for parchment itself, maximizing your Workshops provides a multiplicative boost to the number of parchments produced per craft.

Primary Uses

Parchment is a mandatory requirement for transitioning out of the early game and establishing a “cultural engine”:
item.content:encoded:
Parchment is a vital mid-game craftable resource in Kittens Game that serves as the foundation for your colony’s cultural and religious expansion. It is primarily used to construct culture-generating buildings and to craft more advanced intellectual resources.

Acquisition and Crafting

  • Unlocking: You gain the ability to craft parchment after researching the Writing technology (3,600 Science).
  • Workshop Crafting: A single unit of parchment is crafted from 175 Furs in the Workshop.
  • Trading: Once you reach Embassy level 5 with the Sharks, they have a 25% chance of selling you parchment in exchange for iron. This chance can be increased by +25% if you enact the Shark Relations: Scribes policy.
  • Automation: While there is no direct early-game automation for parchment itself, maximizing your Workshops provides a multiplicative boost to the number of parchments produced per craft.

Primary Uses

Parchment is a mandatory requirement for transitioning out of the early game and establishing a “cultural engine”:

  • Resource Conversion: It is the primary input for crafting Manuscripts. Each manuscript requires 25 parchment (reduced to 20 with the Tradition policy).
  • Building Construction: It is a required material for several essential structures:
    • Amphitheatres: 3 Parchment (essential for reducing unhappiness and generating early culture).
    • Chapels: 250 Parchment (the primary structure for generating faith).
    • Breweries: 375 Parchment (required for holding Festivals).
  • Scientific Research: A massive stockpile of 5,000 parchment is required to research Drama and Poetry, which enables the festival system.

Strategic Management

  • Early-Game Grind: Strategic guides recommend beginning to craft parchment as often as possible once the Workshop is unlocked, as you will need vast quantities for the “Theology hurdle”.
  • The “Hunter Dump” Strategy: To efficiently accumulate parchment before automation is available, players should temporarily reassign all kittens to the Hunter job. This allows you to mass-produce the furs necessary for a bulk parchment craft session.
  • Policy Synergy: Enacting the Tradition policy is highly recommended because it reduces the parchment cost for manuscripts and doubles their cultural effectiveness, significantly speeding up mid-game scientific progress.

Special Constraints

  • Pacifism Challenge: In this challenge, hunting is disabled. You cannot obtain furs, and therefore cannot craft parchment, until you build a Mint to generate a passive supply of luxury resources.
  • Iron Will: Since you lack kittens for standard jobs in this mode, your parchment supply depends entirely on the furs gathered by Zebras acting as passive hunters.
  • Persistence: As a crafted resource, parchment is lost upon resetting the game unless you possess Chronospheres and the Flux Condensator workshop upgrade.

item.title: Philosophy
item.description:
The term Philosophy in Kittens Game refers to a critical mid-early game technology that unlocks essential progression paths, as well as a subsequent category of Policy/ that govern societal beliefs regarding luxury and endurance.

Here is a detailed breakdown of the Philosophy technology and its associated Policy/:

1. Philosophy as a Technology

Philosophy is a specialist science research that becomes available after you have researched Writing.

Detail Information Source
Cost 9,500 Science.
Prerequisite Writing.
Key Unlock (Tech) Theology.
Key Unlock (Building) Temple.
Main Effect Enables the creation of compendiums.

Compendiums

Compendiums are a crucial craftable resource unlocked by Philosophy.

The term Philosophy in Kittens Game refers to a critical mid-early game technology that unlocks essential progression paths, as well as a subsequent category of Policy/ that govern societal beliefs regarding luxury and endurance.

Here is a detailed breakdown of the Philosophy technology and its associated Policy/:

1. Philosophy as a Technology

Philosophy is a specialist science research that becomes available after you have researched Writing.

Detail Information Source
Cost 9,500 Science.
Prerequisite Writing.
Key Unlock (Tech) Theology.
Key Unlock (Building) Temple.
Main Effect Enables the creation of compendiums.

Compendiums

Compendiums are a crucial craftable resource unlocked by Philosophy.

  • Purpose: They are composite documents required for subsequent technological advancement. Every compendium created provides +10 to max science, though this bonus cannot exceed the maximum science cap derived from buildings.
  • Crafting: A compendium is crafted in the Workshop by combining 50 Manuscripts and 10,000 Science.

Strategic Importance

There is conflicting advice in the sources regarding when to prioritize the Philosophy technology:

  • Walkthrough Advice: The “Kittens Game” walkthrough suggests that among the three technologies unlocked by Writing (Philosophy, Machinery, and Steel), you should choose Philosophy to start because it is the cheapest and keeps you on the main path of advancement.
  • Expert Advice: The “Monstrous Advice” column recommends prioritizing Steel and Machinery first to strengthen your economy and automate manuscripts, and then taking Philosophy last, specifically so you will have ways to make all the manuscripts needed to build Temples.

After researching Philosophy, you will immediately face a “fair bump” because the subsequent technology, Theology, has “fairly steep requirements” involving manuscripts and culture.

2. Philosophy as a Policy Category

Philosophy is one of the four categories of Policy/ (along with Government, Foreign, and Environment) that defines your society’s path in certain areas.

The main policy choices unlocked once the Philosophy technology has been researched are Stoicism and Epicureanism.

Stoicism vs. Epicureanism

Both Policy/ cost 2,500 Culture and lock out the other choice.

Policy Description & Effect Prerequisite & Progression
Stoicism Teaches endurance without complaint. Effect: Halves the consumption of luxury resources (Fur, Ivory, and Spice are consumed 50% slower), and reduces Brewery consumption by 25%. This policy unlocks the choice between Frugality and Rationing later on.
Epicureanism Believes pleasure is the highest good. Effect: Luxury resources provide 11% happiness each (instead of the base 10%). This policy unlocks the choice between Carnivale and Extravagance later on.

Expert advice suggests preferring Epicureanism for the extra happiness boost, noting that Stoicism addresses a problem (managing luxury consumption) that should ideally be manageable by the time the policy is available through hunting and trade upgrades. Choosing either Epicureanism or Stoicism is a prerequisite for subsequent philosophical choices like Rationality or Mysticism.

item.title: Piscine Mission
item.description:
The Piscine Mission is a mid-to-late game space project involving travel to a gigantic aquatic planet characterised by an acidic body and a methane atmosphere. It is a critical milestone for expanding your colony’s scientific and astronomical infrastructure.

Requirements and Logistics

  • Prerequisites: Players must first successfully complete the Moon Mission to unlock the Piscine project.
  • Launch Costs: The mission requires 1500 Starcharts, 9000 Titanium, 200,000 Science, and 250 Kerosene.
  • Travel Time: The journey to Piscine takes 256 game-days, which is approximately 8 minutes and 32 seconds in real-time. This duration can be reduced using advanced drives like the Antimatter or Thorium Drives.

Critical Unlocks and Infrastructure

Successfully exploring Piscine is the gateway to some of the most powerful starchart-generating structures in the star system:
item.content:encoded:
The Piscine Mission is a mid-to-late game space project involving travel to a gigantic aquatic planet characterised by an acidic body and a methane atmosphere. It is a critical milestone for expanding your colony’s scientific and astronomical infrastructure.

Requirements and Logistics

  • Prerequisites: Players must first successfully complete the Moon Mission to unlock the Piscine project.
  • Launch Costs: The mission requires 1500 Starcharts, 9000 Titanium, 200,000 Science, and 250 Kerosene.
  • Travel Time: The journey to Piscine takes 256 game-days, which is approximately 8 minutes and 32 seconds in real-time. This duration can be reduced using advanced drives like the Antimatter or Thorium Drives.

Critical Unlocks and Infrastructure

Successfully exploring Piscine is the gateway to some of the most powerful starchart-generating structures in the star system:

  • Research Vessels: These mobile space stations provide a base +10,000 science storage and generate 0.05 starcharts per second. The sources identify these vessels as the most efficient method for generating starcharts, outperforming Satellites by a factor of ten.
  • Orbital Arrays: This space structure provides a 2% bonus to all space structures, though it consumes a significant 20 Watts of energy.
  • Future Exploration: Completing this mission is required to unlock the T-minus mission.

The Piscine Cycle

In the game’s ten-cycle celestial system, the Piscine cycle (identified by the glyph ⎈) introduces specific modifiers that players should manage strategically:

  • Hydroponics production suffers a -50% penalty to catnip generation.
  • Research Vessel starchart production is boosted by +50%.
  • Science Multiplier: If Numeromancy is researched, holding a festival during the Piscine cycle provides a 2x multiplier to Science income.

Strategic Utility

  • Solving the Starchart Bottleneck: The primary reason to rush the Piscine Mission is to transition from manual “astronomical event” clicking to the automated starchart production provided by Research Vessels. This is essential for building the massive trade fleets of Trade Ships required for late-game titanium and blueprint acquisitions.
  • Science Progression: With upgrades like Antimatter Reactors, the science storage of Research Vessels can be boosted by up to 400%, providing a massive foundation for multi-million science technologies.
  • Challenge Note: It is important to note that Research Vessels do not produce starcharts while in a Black Sky Challenge, as this would circumvent the core difficulty of that mode.

item.title: Radical_Xenophobia
item.description:
Radical Xenophobia is an endgame government policy in Kittens Game that prioritises the rejection of “evil aliens and evil robots” in favour of self-reliance. It costs 1,500,000 Culture to enact and is primarily focused on enhancing Mausoleums and the Pact system.

Key Statistics and Requirements

Attribute Details
Cost 1,500,000 Culture
Prerequisite At least one successful trade with the Leviathans
Mutual Exclusivity Selecting this locks out Transkittenism and Necrocracy for the current run

Core Effects and Benefits

The policy provides specific bonuses to cryptotheology and resource management:
item.content:encoded:
Radical Xenophobia is an endgame government policy in Kittens Game that prioritises the rejection of “evil aliens and evil robots” in favour of self-reliance. It costs 1,500,000 Culture to enact and is primarily focused on enhancing Mausoleums and the Pact system.

Key Statistics and Requirements

Attribute Details
Cost 1,500,000 Culture
Prerequisite At least one successful trade with the Leviathans
Mutual Exclusivity Selecting this locks out Transkittenism and Necrocracy for the current run

Core Effects and Benefits

The policy provides specific bonuses to cryptotheology and resource management:

  • Mausoleum Buff: It increases the efficacy of all Mausoleums, effectively doubling their impact.
  • Free Pacts: It immediately grants 5 free Pacts.
  • Pact Unlocking: Along with the Mausoleum upgrade, this policy is one of two ways to make Pacts available for purchase in the religion tab.

Strategic Analysis

While Radical Xenophobia offers unique bonuses, it is often viewed as a niche choice compared to its counterparts:

  • Strategic Delay: Experienced players generally recommend holding off on this tier of policy as long as possible, as the initial benefits of Pacts are considered minimal and the “necrocorn debt” required to maintain them can be steep.
  • Holy Genocide Synergy: Some strategic advice suggests that Radical Xenophobia remains “worthless” until Holy Genocide (a high-tier cryptotheology building) becomes available, which unlocks the Post Apocalypse challenge.
  • Comparison: Most players opt for Transkittenism to prevent AI uprisings and boost space storage, or Necrocracy for global production bonuses tied to Black Liquid Sorrow (BLS).

Understanding Pacts

If you choose this policy, you gain access to different types of Pacts (such as the Pact of Cleansing or Pact of Destruction) which provide global resource limits or production bonuses based on your number of Black Pyramids. However, failure to pay the required necrocorn upkeep can lead to a Broken Pact, which imposes a severe 50% penalty to global storage and production.

item.title: Rationality
item.description:
Rationality is a mid-game Philosophy policy in Kittens Game that provides a modest boost to scientific and industrial production. It represents the societal view that the world can be fundamentally understood through logic and reason.

Core Effects and Costs

  • Effect: Increases both Science and Iron production by 5%.
  • Cost: 3000 Science.
  • Prerequisites: You must have researched the Philosophy technology and enacted either the Stoicism or Epicureanism policy.
  • Mutual Exclusivity: Choosing Rationality permanently locks you out of the Mysticism policy for the remainder of the run.

Strategic Comparison: Rationality vs. Mysticism

Because these policies are mutually exclusive, you must choose between boosting techs/Iron or Culture/Faith.

Core Effects and Costs

  • Effect: Increases both Science and Iron production by 5%.
  • Cost: 3000 Science.
  • Prerequisites: You must have researched the Philosophy technology and enacted either the Stoicism or Epicureanism policy.

Strategic Comparison: Rationality vs. Mysticism

Because these policies are mutually exclusive, you must choose between boosting techs/Iron or Culture/Faith.

Policy Production Bonuses Strategic Context
Rationality +5% Science, +5% Iron Focuses on technical and industrial throughput.
Mysticism +5% Culture, +5% Faith Focuses on religious and cultural scaling.

Expert Recommendation

Strategic guides generally recommend choosing Mysticism over Rationality for the following reasons:

  • Science is “Easy”: Science production and storage are relatively easy to manage through buildings like Libraries, Academies, and Observatories.
  • Culture/Faith Bottlenecks: Culture and Faith accumulate much more slowly, especially in the early-to-mid game, making percentage bonuses for these resources far more valuable.
  • Iron Scaling: While a 5% Iron boost is helpful, industrial production is often better scaled through Workshops, Smelters, and Calciners rather than a dedicated philosophy policy.

item.title: Rationing
item.description:
Rationing is a mid-game Philosophy policy in Kittens Game designed to mitigate the food-related “cost of happiness” and provide a minor boost to hunting effectiveness. It is particularly useful when your civilisation reaches high happiness levels that would otherwise cause your kittens to consume catnip at an unsustainable rate.

Policy Overview

  • Cost: 3,500 Culture.
  • Prerequisite: Stoicism policy.
  • Mutual Exclusivity: Enacting Rationing permanently locks out the Frugality policy for the remainder of the run.

Core Effects

Effect Description
Catnip Efficiency Reduces the catnip consumption increase caused by high happiness by 10%.
Hunting Bonus Provides a flat +0.1 bonus to all hunting activities.

Strategic Utility

The primary value of Rationing lies in managing the Resource/Consumption Equilibrium as your village matures.
item.content:encoded:
Rationing is a mid-game Philosophy policy in Kittens Game designed to mitigate the food-related “cost of happiness” and provide a minor boost to hunting effectiveness. It is particularly useful when your civilisation reaches high happiness levels that would otherwise cause your kittens to consume catnip at an unsustainable rate.

Policy Overview

  • Cost: 3,500 Culture.
  • Prerequisite: Stoicism policy.
  • Mutual Exclusivity: Enacting Rationing permanently locks out the Frugality policy for the remainder of the run.

Core Effects

Effect Description
Catnip Efficiency Reduces the catnip consumption increase caused by high happiness by 10%.
Hunting Bonus Provides a flat +0.1 bonus to all hunting activities.

Strategic Utility

The primary value of Rationing lies in managing the Resource/Consumption Equilibrium as your village matures.

  • Mitigating the Happiness Liability: While high happiness is essential for scaling production, it also causes kittens to eat significantly more catnip. For example, at 420% happiness, kittens consume 320% more catnip than their base rate. Rationing acts as a safety valve, ensuring that a sudden spike in morale does not lead to a catastrophic food shortage or mass starvation during Winter.
  • Hunting Support: The +0.1 hunting bonus is a helpful, albeit minor, addition to your passive or active hunting teams, increasing the yield of Furs and Ivory used for crafting parchment and manuscripts.
  • Choosing Between Branches: Because this policy is locked behind Stoicism, you have already committed to a path of restraint over the Epicureanism branch. Within the Stoicism branch, you must choose between Rationing (food and hunting) or Frugality (which boosts Mint production by 10%).

In some strategic guides, Rationing is viewed as a situational choice; if you have a robust hunting team and sufficient Tradeposts to manage luxury consumption, the benefits of Rationing or Frugality may feel minor compared to high-tier industrial or scientific policies.

item.title: Reactor
item.description:
The Reactor is a late-mid-game industrial structure in Kittens Game that is crucial for generating significant amounts of energy and enabling progression into the space and unobtainium era.

Here is a comprehensive breakdown of the Reactor:

1. Unlocking and Construction

The Reactor building is unlocked by researching Nuclear Fission technology.

  • Technology Prerequisite: Nuclear Fission.
  • Base Cost: 3,500 Titanium, 5,000 Plate, 50 Concrete, and 25 Blueprint.
  • Price Ratio: 1.15.

2. Purpose and Effects

The Reactor is primarily used for large-scale power generation and resource management of highly processed materials:
item.content:encoded:
The Reactor is a late-mid-game industrial structure in Kittens Game that is crucial for generating significant amounts of energy and enabling progression into the space and unobtainium era.

Here is a comprehensive breakdown of the Reactor:

1. Unlocking and Construction

The Reactor building is unlocked by researching Nuclear Fission technology.

  • Technology Prerequisite: Nuclear Fission.
  • Base Cost: 3,500 Titanium, 5,000 Plate, 50 Concrete, and 25 Blueprint.
  • Price Ratio: 1.15.

2. Purpose and Effects

The Reactor is primarily used for large-scale power generation and resource management of highly processed materials:

  • Energy Generation: Produces a substantial +10 Energy per tick.
  • Production Boost: Provides a +5% Global Production bonus.
  • Uranium Management: It consumes -0.001 Uranium per Tick and increases your Max Uranium storage by +250.
  • Strategic Role: Reactors are categorized as supplemental production-boosting buildings that cost hard-to-acquire blueprints. They are necessary to increase Uranium storage, which is required for obtaining Unobtainium. The Reactor is also listed as one of the required energy production buildings to complete the Energy Challenge.

3. Key Upgrades and Synergies

Reactors benefit from several dedicated Workshop upgrades, enhancing their power output and leveraging them to boost other systems:

Upgrade/Policy Effect Source
Cold Fusion Increases Reactor energy output by +2.5 (+25%).
Thorium Reactors Increases Reactor energy output by +0.25 (+25%) but introduces a consumption of -0.25 Thorium/tick per reactor.
Enriched Uranium Reduces the Reactor’s uranium consumption by 25%.
Reactor Vessel Allows upgraded trade ships to increase Harbor capacity by +5% per active Reactor beyond the base capacity limit.
Nuclear Plants Increases the steel produced by Steel Plants (a Calciner upgrade) by an additional 2% per active Reactor.

The IW 40K Endless Run Guide specifically advises that Reactors provide a lot of power, but due to their blueprint cost, players should consider turning off Thorium Reactors unless they are time skipping for antimatter.

The Reactor building is a prerequisite for buying the Lunar Outpost, which is necessary for converting Uranium into Unobtainium.

item.title: Refine_Catnip
item.description:
Refining catnip is the primary method for producing wood during the early stages of the game before kittens can be assigned as woodcutters. The “Refine catnip” button appears in the Left UI once the colony has accumulated at least 100 catnip.

Conversion and Efficiency

  • Base Rate: Initially, the conversion rate is 100 catnip for 1 wood.
  • Cost Reduction: Researching Catnip Enrichment in the Workshop reduces the cost to 50 catnip per unit of wood.
  • Effectiveness Bonuses: While this process does not benefit from standard crafting bonuses, its output can be increased through specific structures and Policy/.
    • Bio Labs: Each lab increases catnip refinement effectiveness by 10%.
    • Shark Relations (Botanists): This foreign policy provides a +25% wood crafting bonus.

Iron Will Strategies

In Iron Will mode, where kitten housing is forbidden, refining catnip is the essential source of wood for early infrastructure like Libraries. Several mode-specific bonuses help scale this production:
item.content:encoded:
Refining catnip is the primary method for producing wood during the early stages of the game before kittens can be assigned as woodcutters. The “Refine catnip” button appears in the Left UI once the colony has accumulated at least 100 catnip.

Conversion and Efficiency

  • Base Rate: Initially, the conversion rate is 100 catnip for 1 wood.
  • Cost Reduction: Researching Catnip Enrichment in the Workshop reduces the cost to 50 catnip per unit of wood.
  • Effectiveness Bonuses: While this process does not benefit from standard crafting bonuses, its output can be increased through specific structures and Policy/.
    • Bio Labs: Each lab increases catnip refinement effectiveness by 10%.
    • Shark Relations (Botanists): This foreign policy provides a +25% wood crafting bonus.

Iron Will Strategies

In Iron Will mode, where kitten housing is forbidden, refining catnip is the essential source of wood for early infrastructure like Libraries. Several mode-specific bonuses help scale this production:

  • Lumber Mills: In Iron Will, these buildings provide a +10% bonus to catnip refinement rather than boosting woodcutter output.
  • Clear Cutting Policy: This environmental policy provides a +10% refinement bonus, functioning similarly to an un-upgraded Lumber Mill.
  • Open Woodlands Policy: This provides a smaller +4.16% bonus to refinement.

Strategic Utility

  • Early Game: Players are encouraged to refine catnip five times to reach the 5 wood required to build their first Hut, which unlocks the village system.
  • Production Balancing: Because Catnip Fields suffer a -75% production penalty during Winter, players must ensure their food supply is stable before aggressively refining their stores into wood.
  • Trade Loops: In some mid-game strategies, players trade Iron to the Sharks for massive amounts of catnip, which is then refined into wood to be traded to Griffins for more Iron.

item.title: Reinforced_Barns
item.description:
The Reinforced Barns upgrade is a critical early-to-mid-game investment in the Workshop tab, designed to alleviate constraints on your resource capacity.

Function and Effects

The primary function of Reinforced Barns is to expand the maximum storage limits of core resources provided by your general storage buildings.

  • Storage Increase: The upgrade provides 80% more storage space for the affected resources.
  • Buildings and Resources Affected: This 80% bonus is applied to the maximum storage capacity for wood, minerals, and iron provided by Barns, Warehouses, and Harbors.

This increase is vital because resource storage limits are a major bottleneck that can slow progress significantly.
item.content:encoded:
The Reinforced Barns upgrade is a critical early-to-mid-game investment in the Workshop tab, designed to alleviate constraints on your resource capacity.

Function and Effects

The primary function of Reinforced Barns is to expand the maximum storage limits of core resources provided by your general storage buildings.

  • Storage Increase: The upgrade provides 80% more storage space for the affected resources.
  • Buildings and Resources Affected: This 80% bonus is applied to the maximum storage capacity for wood, minerals, and iron provided by Barns, Warehouses, and Harbors.

This increase is vital because resource storage limits are a major bottleneck that can slow progress significantly.

Cost and Progression

Reinforced Barns is an upgrade that improves upon the base storage capacity established by the Barn, which is unlocked after researching Agriculture.

  • Cost: The upgrade costs 800 Science, 25 Beam, 10 Slab, and 100 Iron.

It is part of a progression of storage capacity upgrades for Barns, and is a prerequisite for more advanced upgrades:

Upgrade Effect on Max Storage (Wood, Minerals, Iron) Predecessor
Expanded Barns +75% increase N/A
Reinforced Barns +80% increase N/A (listed as having no prerequisite in the table)
Titanium Barns +100% increase (twice as many resources) Requires Reinforced Barns

Additionally, once the Silos upgrade is purchased, all storage upgrades containing “barns” in their name, including Reinforced Barns, apply 25% of their effect to maximum Catnip storage as well.

item.title: Republic
item.description:
Republic is a mid-game Government policy that provides a global production bonus to your entire kitten population based on the rank of your current leader.

Core Mechanics

To enact the Republic policy, your civilisation must meet the following requirements:

  • Cost: 1500 Culture.
  • Prerequisites: You must have researched Writing and already enacted the Liberty policy.
  • Mutual Exclusivity: Choosing Republic permanently locks you out of Monarchy and Autocracy for the remainder of the run.

The Republic Bonus

While other government forms focus on the leader’s individual traits, Republic allows the leader’s experience to benefit every worker.
item.content:encoded:
Republic is a mid-game Government policy that provides a global production bonus to your entire kitten population based on the rank of your current leader.

Core Mechanics

To enact the Republic policy, your civilisation must meet the following requirements:

  • Cost: 1500 Culture.
  • Prerequisites: You must have researched Writing and already enacted the Liberty policy.
  • Mutual Exclusivity: Choosing Republic permanently locks you out of Monarchy and Autocracy for the remainder of the run.

The Republic Bonus

While other government forms focus on the leader’s individual traits, Republic allows the leader’s experience to benefit every worker.

  • Global Effect: All non-leader kittens receive a job bonus equal to 1% of the leader’s own rank bonus.
  • Mathematical Formula: The specific percentage bonus is calculated as (leader rank + 1) / 70.
  • Multiplicative Scaling: This bonus stacks multiplicatively with other production modifiers, such as happiness or workshop upgrades.

Strategic Comparison

In the Kittens Game community, Republic is often compared to its alternative, Monarchy:

Feature Republic Monarchy
Best For Large societies (high kitten count). Flexible utility and specific resource grinding.
Primary Effect Small production boost to all kittens. Doubles the leader’s specific trait (e.g., Artisan or Scientist).
Prerequisite Liberty. Tradition.
Community View Often considered to provide “tiny bonuses” compared to Monarchy. Generally preferred because doubling a leader’s trait is highly effective.

Progression and Synergy

Enacting Republic is a key step in the Liberty branch of the policy tree. It typically leads toward:

  • Liberalism: A peaceful society that improves trade relations and reduces gold costs.
  • Catpower Scaling: Choosing the Liberty-Republic-Liberalism path is strategically useful for players aiming to maximise Templar upgrades, which increase the catpower cap to aid in ivory generation and trading.

Note: To make the most of Republic, you must actively promote your leader using gold and experience, as the bonus scales directly with their rank.

item.title: Robotics
item.description:
Robotics is a pivotal late-mid-game science in Kittens Game, marking a critical transition in the “Prestige and Energy Transition Epoch”. It focuses on industrial automation, significant energy infrastructure shifts, and reducing the biological burden of your kitten workforce.

Costs and Prerequisites

  • Science Cost: 140,000.
  • Resource Cost: 80 Blueprints.
  • Prerequisite: You must have researched Electronics.

The Hydro Plant Pivot

Researching Robotics allows you to upgrade your Aqueducts into Hydro Plants.

  • Effect: Each Hydro Plant provides +5 Energy (which can be increased to 5.75Wt with the Hydro Plant Turbines upgrade).
  • Strategic Risk: This is described as a “high-risk” infrastructure pivot. While Hydro Plants are vital for powering your growing industrial base, upgrading them causes you to lose the +3% catnip production bonus provided by Aqueducts.
  • Recommendation: Do not upgrade until your titanium production is robust and you are certain your catnip production (boosted by Paragon and Karma) can sustain the population without the Aqueduct bonus.

Unlocked Workshop Upgrades

Robotics provides access to several upgrades that drastically improve industrial output and kitten efficiency:
item.content:encoded:
Robotics is a pivotal late-mid-game science in Kittens Game, marking a critical transition in the “Prestige and Energy Transition Epoch”. It focuses on industrial automation, significant energy infrastructure shifts, and reducing the biological burden of your kitten workforce.

Costs and Prerequisites

  • Science Cost: 140,000.
  • Resource Cost: 80 Blueprints.
  • Prerequisite: You must have researched Electronics.

The Hydro Plant Pivot

Researching Robotics allows you to upgrade your Aqueducts into Hydro Plants.

  • Effect: Each Hydro Plant provides +5 Energy (which can be increased to 5.75Wt with the Hydro Plant Turbines upgrade).
  • Strategic Risk: This is described as a “high-risk” infrastructure pivot. While Hydro Plants are vital for powering your growing industrial base, upgrading them causes you to lose the +3% catnip production bonus provided by Aqueducts.
  • Recommendation: Do not upgrade until your titanium production is robust and you are certain your catnip production (boosted by Paragon and Karma) can sustain the population without the Aqueduct bonus.

Unlocked Workshop Upgrades

Robotics provides access to several upgrades that drastically improve industrial output and kitten efficiency:

  • Robotic Assistance: Reduces the catnip consumption of working kittens by 25%. This is essential for managing the “happiness liability,” where high happiness levels normally cause massive spikes in food demand.
  • Steel Plants: This causes Calciners to automatically convert 10% of their iron output into Steel (at a 100:1 ratio).
  • Rotary Kiln: Dramatically enhances Calciner efficiency, making them 75% more effective at producing Iron and 3 times as effective at producing Titanium.
  • Factory Robotics: Improves Engineer effectiveness by increasing the “know-how” of Class 1, 2, and 3 Engineers.

Resource and Progression Unlocks

  • Tankers: Robotics enables the crafting of Tankers in the Workshop. Each Tanker increases your maximum Oil capacity by 500. While useful for reaching the high oil caps required for space missions, some strategies suggest prioritizing steel-grinding for Oil Wells instead, as Tankers can be expensive in the early-space era.
  • Artificial Intelligence: Robotics is the mandatory prerequisite for the Artificial Intelligence science, which leads to AI Cores and the Gigaflop era.

Strategic Significance

Robotics represents the point where your civilization begins to “replace” marginal agricultural bonuses with high-density energy generation and automated manufacturing. By reducing food demand and automating steel and titanium production, Robotics allows you to focus on the massive resource requirements of the Space era and the transition toward Antimatter.

item.title: Rocketry
item.description:
Rocketry is a high-level late-game technology that acts as the primary gateway to the Space era. It transitions your civilization from ground-based industrialisation to interstellar exploration and resource acquisition.

Costs and Prerequisites

  • Science Cost: 175,000.
  • Resource Cost: 125 Blueprints.
  • Prerequisite: You must first research Electronics.

Immediate Unlocks

Researching Rocketry provides several critical features and further technological paths:

  • Space Tab: This new tab becomes available, allowing you to build rockets and launch missions.
  • Technologies: It unlocks the Satellites and Oil Processing sciences.
  • Workshop Upgrade: You gain access to Oil Distillation, which costs 175k Science and 5,000 Titanium, improving Oil Well output by 75%.
  • Missions: It allows you to undertake the first space mission, Orbital Launch (Cost: 250 Starcharts, 5,000 Catpower, 100k Science, and 15k Oil).

Strategic Importance

Rocketry is the mandatory starting point for the “Space Race.” Its primary strategic functions include:
item.content:encoded:
Rocketry is a high-level late-game technology that acts as the primary gateway to the Space era. It transitions your civilization from ground-based industrialisation to interstellar exploration and resource acquisition.

Costs and Prerequisites

  • Science Cost: 175,000.
  • Resource Cost: 125 Blueprints.
  • Prerequisite: You must first research Electronics.

Immediate Unlocks

Researching Rocketry provides several critical features and further technological paths:

  • Space Tab: This new tab becomes available, allowing you to build rockets and launch missions.
  • Technologies: It unlocks the Satellites and Oil Processing sciences.
  • Workshop Upgrade: You gain access to Oil Distillation, which costs 175k Science and 5,000 Titanium, improving Oil Well output by 75%.
  • Missions: It allows you to undertake the first space mission, Orbital Launch (Cost: 250 Starcharts, 5,000 Catpower, 100k Science, and 15k Oil).

Strategic Importance

Rocketry is the mandatory starting point for the “Space Race.” Its primary strategic functions include:

  • The Path to Unobtainium: Completing the missions unlocked by Rocketry leads to the Moon Mission, which is the only way to build Lunar Outposts and begin generating Unobtainium.
  • Oil Economy Scaling: The Oil Distillation upgrade is vital for meeting the massive oil demands of subsequent space missions, such as the Moon Mission (45k Oil) and Moon Bases (70k Oil).
  • Starchart Automation: By unlocking the Satellites technology, it allows you to begin automating the production of Starcharts, which are required in large quantities for all further space exploration.

Special Challenge Effects

In the Black Sky challenge, where astronomical events do not occur, the initial costs for missions and buildings unlocked by Rocketry are significantly altered. For example, the Orbital Launch mission removes the starchart requirement entirely but increases the Science, Catpower, and Oil costs by 11x.

item.title: Rorschach Mission
item.description:
Rorschach is a late-game celestial body in the Helios star system, specifically described as the biggest comet near Helios.

The Rorschach Mission

To explore Rorschach, you must first successfully complete the Kairo Mission. The mission represents a significant investment in late-game resources:

  • Starcharts: 15,000
  • Titanium: 80,000
  • Science: 500,000
  • Kerosene: 25,000.

While travel times for space missions can be significantly reduced by researching Thorium Drives (divided by 50) or Antimatter Drives (divided by 25), the base travel time for Rorschach is not explicitly listed alongside the other missions in the provided technical logs.

Rorschach is a late-game celestial body in the Helios star system, specifically described as the biggest comet near Helios.

The Rorschach Mission

To explore Rorschach, you must first successfully complete the Kairo Mission. The mission represents a significant investment in late-game resources:

  • Starcharts: 15,000
  • Titanium: 80,000
  • Science: 500,000
  • Kerosene: 25,000.

While travel times for space missions can be significantly reduced by researching Thorium Drives (divided by 50) or Antimatter Drives (divided by 25), the base travel time for Rorschach is not explicitly listed alongside the other missions in the provided technical logs.

Strategic Impact and Unlocks

The primary function of the Rorschach mission is to serve as a gateway to the furthest reaches of the star system:

  • Expanded Vision: Upon completion, the sources note that while Rorschach is “impenetrable,” its discovery allows your kittens to “see farther”.
  • Centaurus Mission: Successfully exploring Rorschach is the mandatory prerequisite to unlock the Centaurus Mission, which leads to a warm, faraway star system.

Context in Late-Game Progression

In the broader “Phase 4” of game progression, Rorschach is part of the deep-space exploration arc that follows the stabilization of the Unobtainium and Antimatter economies. Because the mission requires a substantial 80,000 Titanium, players often need to have reached the “Titanium Era” high-storage milestones—such as building numerous Moon Bases, Cryostations, or Accelerators with the Energy Rift upgrade—to satisfy the mission’s resource caps.

item.title: Scaffold
item.description:
Scaffolds are a vital mid-game craftable resource used primarily for industrial construction, storage expansion, and the development of the colony’s naval fleet. They are produced in the Workshop at a base cost of 50 Beams per craft.

Core Utility: Naval and Trade Expansion

The most significant strategic milestone involving scaffolds is the transition into the Titanium Era.

  • Trade Ships: Crafting a set of trade ships requires 100 scaffolds each.
  • Discovery: Possessing at least one trade ship is the prerequisite for exploring and discovering the Zebras, the primary source of titanium through trade.
  • Harbours: Scaffolds are required to build Harbours (5 scaffolds each), which provide a massive boost to the storage capacity of multiple resources.

Industrial and Scientific Infrastructure

Scaffolds serve as a foundational material for several critical bonfire structures and religious buildings:
item.content:encoded:
Scaffolds are a vital mid-game craftable resource used primarily for industrial construction, storage expansion, and the development of the colony’s naval fleet. They are produced in the Workshop at a base cost of 50 Beams per craft.

Core Utility: Naval and Trade Expansion

The most significant strategic milestone involving scaffolds is the transition into the Titanium Era.

  • Trade Ships: Crafting a set of trade ships requires 100 scaffolds each.
  • Discovery: Possessing at least one trade ship is the prerequisite for exploring and discovering the Zebras, the primary source of titanium through trade.
  • Harbours: Scaffolds are required to build Harbours (5 scaffolds each), which provide a massive boost to the storage capacity of multiple resources.

Industrial and Scientific Infrastructure

Scaffolds serve as a foundational material for several critical bonfire structures and religious buildings:

  • Observatories: Each observatory requires 50 scaffolds. These are essential for increasing the science cap and automating the collection of Starcharts.
  • Production Buildings: They are a required component for Oil Wells (25 scaffolds) and Quarries (50 scaffolds), both of which are necessary for stabilizing energy and mineral supplies.
  • Unicorn Religion: Building Ziggurats requires 50 scaffolds each. This is the gateway structure for sacrificing unicorns to obtain Unicorn Tears.

Trade and High-Tier Upgrades

  • Trading with Spiders: Scaffolds are the primary trade currency for the Spiders. They will buy 50 scaffolds in exchange for a large amount of Coal and Oil.
  • Advanced Workshop Upgrades: Later in the game, scaffolds are required for expensive upgrades such as Titanium Warehouses (500) and Logistics (1,000).

Persistence and Resets

As a crafted resource, scaffolds are normally lost upon resetting the game. To preserve a portion of your stockpile across runs, you must possess at least one Chronosphere and the Flux Condensator workshop upgrade. The amount carried over is calculated based on the number of chronospheres and the square root of the total quantity held at the time of reset.

item.title: Scholasticism
item.description:
Scholasticism is a religious upgrade available within the Kittens Game, found under the Order of the Sun in the Religion tab.

This upgrade is crucial because, like other religious upgrades, it affects functionality outside of the Religion system.

Prerequisites and Cost

To purchase Scholasticism, you must meet the following requirements:

  • Prerequisite: You must have accumulated 300 Worship. Worship is converted from Faith by using the “Praise the sun!” action.
  • Cost: The upgrade costs 250 Faith.

Effects and Function

The primary function of Scholasticism is to integrate your religious structures into your scientific development:
item.content:encoded:
Scholasticism is a religious upgrade available within the Kittens Game, found under the Order of the Sun in the Religion tab.

This upgrade is crucial because, like other religious upgrades, it affects functionality outside of the Religion system.

To purchase Scholasticism, you must meet the following requirements:

  • Prerequisite: You must have accumulated 300 Worship. Worship is converted from Faith by using the “Praise the sun!” action.
  • Cost: The upgrade costs 250 Faith.

Effects and Function

The primary function of Scholasticism is to integrate your religious structures into your scientific development:

  • Science Contribution: Scholasticism allows Temples to contribute to Science.
  • Maximum Science Bonus: Specifically, it grants Temples an effect of +500 maximum science. This helps prevent the Science resource cap from becoming a bottleneck when researching advanced technologies.
  • Scaling: The maximum science bonus provided by Temples is further increased by +100 for each additional level of Scholasticism purchased using Transcendence.

The ability to increase your maximum science cap is highly beneficial, as achieving high science limits (like the 125K needed for Concrete Huts) often requires numerous Science buildings such as Libraries, Academies, and Observatories. Scholasticism provides a direct boost to this vital resource capacity through existing Temple infrastructure.

item.title: Sky Palace
item.description:
The Sky Palace is a specialized religious building that is part of the advanced Unicorn progression line.

Here is a detailed breakdown of its function, effects, and prerequisites:

Function and Effects

The Sky Palace provides multiple bonuses related to the generation of rare luxury resources and general storage:

  • Unicorn Generation: It improves unicorn generation by 50%.
  • Gold Storage: It improves gold storage by +1%.
  • Alicorn Production: It produces $0.00002$ alicorns per tick (or $0.0001$ per second, $0.08$ per year).
  • Alicorn Event: It enables a random event that grants one alicorn.
    • Each Sky Palace built increases the frequency of this event by $0.01%$ per game-day (or $1%$ per day per 100 palaces).
  • Ivory Meteors: It increases ivory gained from Ivory Meteors by $5%$.

Acquisition and Prerequisites

The Sky Palace is unlocked and constructed in the Religion tab, following a specific upgrade path:

Here is a detailed breakdown of its function, effects, and prerequisites:

Function and Effects

  • Unicorn Generation: It improves unicorn generation by 50%.
  • Gold Storage: It improves gold storage by +1%.
  • Alicorn Production: It produces $0.00002$ alicorns per tick (or $0.0001$ per second, $0.08$ per year).

  • Ivory Meteors: It increases ivory gained from Ivory Meteors by $5%$.

Acquisition and Prerequisites

The Sky Palace is unlocked and constructed in the Religion tab, following a specific upgrade path:

  • Prerequisites: You must complete 1 Ivory Citadel to unlock the Sky Palace.
    • The Ivory Citadel requires completing an Ivory Tower, which in turn requires completing a Unicorn Tomb [1, 2].
  • Cost: The Sky Palace requires the following resources to build:
    • 500 Tears
    • 125,000 Ivory
    • 5 Megalith
  • Ratio: It has a price ratio of $1.15$.

Place in the Unicorn Progression

The Sky Palace is an intermediate step in maximizing unicorn-related production, leading to even more powerful buildings:

  • Once you complete 1 Sky Palace, you unlock the Unicorn Utopia, which further improves unicorn generation by $250%$ and increases the Time Crystal Refine ratio by $5%$ [3].
  • The Sky Palace, along with other advanced Unicorn buildings like the Ivory Tower and Ivory Citadel, helps generate ivory and alicorns, which are critical for late-game progression [1, 2]. Unicorns, alicorns, and tears are all considered luxury resources, contributing a bonus to happiness [4].

item.title: Solar Chant
item.description:
Solar Chant is an essential religious upgrade available in the Kittens Game under the Order of the Sun. It specifically targets and enhances your civilization’s ability to generate the special resource, Faith.

Here is a detailed explanation of Solar Chant, its prerequisites, and its strategic function:

Function and Effect

The primary purpose of Solar Chant is to increase your production of Faith.

  • Base Effect: Solar Chant improves your base faith generation rate by 10%.
  • Scaling: As you progress into the mid-to-late game, you can purchase additional levels of Solar Chant using Transcendence. Each additional level purchased increases this bonus by an additional +10%.

Cost and Prerequisites

Solar Chant is one of the early-game religious upgrades you should aim for to boost your Faith economy.

Here is a detailed explanation of Solar Chant, its prerequisites, and its strategic function:

Function and Effect

The primary purpose of Solar Chant is to increase your production of Faith.

  • Base Effect: Solar Chant improves your base faith generation rate by 10%.
  • Scaling: As you progress into the mid-to-late game, you can purchase additional levels of Solar Chant using Transcendence. Each additional level purchased increases this bonus by an additional +10%.

Cost and Prerequisites

Solar Chant is one of the early-game religious upgrades you should aim for to boost your Faith economy.

  • Prerequisite: The upgrade only becomes available for purchase once you have accumulated 150 Worship.
  • Cost: The initial cost of the upgrade is 100 Faith.

Strategic Importance

Purchasing multiple levels of Solar Chant is a critical late-game strategy, especially as Faith production is generally affected by production boosts like Paragon but remains inherently slow.

By boosting your Faith income via multiple levels of Solar Chant (achieved through Transcendence), you can more effectively engage in the “Praise the sun!” mechanic, which converts accumulated Faith into Worship.

This strategy is vital because maximizing faith generation allows you to quickly restore your Solar Revolution bonus (a global production boost derived from Worship) after you have “reset” your faith pool using the Adore the galaxy option (unlocked via Apocrypha). In the late game, many kittens are typically assigned as [Priests] ( /job/priest/) to maximize Faith generation, making the boost provided by Solar Chant highly impactful.

item.title: Solar Farm
item.description:
The Solar Farm is an advanced building in Kittens Game that serves as an environmentally friendly source of energy. It is categorized as an Upgraded Building that replaces an existing food production structure.

Here is a comprehensive breakdown of the Solar Farm:

1. Unlocks and Construction

  • Prerequisite Technology: The Solar Farm is unlocked by researching Ecology.
  • Cost: The base cost for construction is 250 Titanium, with a price ratio of 1.15.
  • Upgrade Path: The Solar Farm is an upgrade of the Pasture building, meaning that existing Pastures can be converted to Solar Farms. This choice, however, results in the loss of the Pasture’s catnip food bonus.

2. Purpose and Effects

The primary purpose of the Solar Farm is energy generation, with its output fluctuating based on the game’s seasons:
item.content:encoded:
The Solar Farm is an advanced building in Kittens Game that serves as an environmentally friendly source of energy. It is categorized as an Upgraded Building that replaces an existing food production structure.

Here is a comprehensive breakdown of the Solar Farm:

1. Unlocks and Construction

  • Prerequisite Technology: The Solar Farm is unlocked by researching Ecology.
  • Cost: The base cost for construction is 250 Titanium, with a price ratio of 1.15.
  • Upgrade Path: The Solar Farm is an upgrade of the Pasture building, meaning that existing Pastures can be converted to Solar Farms. This choice, however, results in the loss of the Pasture’s catnip food bonus.

2. Purpose and Effects

The primary purpose of the Solar Farm is energy generation, with its output fluctuating based on the game’s seasons:

  • Base Energy Output: It provides +2 Energy.
  • Seasonal Fluctuations:
    • In Summer, the Solar Farm produces +2.67 Energy.
    • In Winter, the production drops to +1.5 Energy.
    • The Quantum Dot Cells upgrade also adds a +30% production bonus in Spring and Autumn.

3. Upgrades and Enhancements

The energy output of Solar Farms can be significantly boosted through several workshop upgrades:

Upgrade Name Technology Prerequisite Effect Source
Photovoltaic Cells Nanotechnology Increases Solar Farm energy production by +50%.
Thin Film Cells Satellites Increases Solar Farm energy production by +15% in Winter.
Quantum Dot Cells Thorium Increases Solar Farm energy production by +15% in Winter (additive with Thin Film Cells) and +30% in Spring and Autumn.

4. Strategic Context

The decision to build or upgrade to Solar Farms is a strategic choice regarding resource priority:

  • Energy vs. Food: You should only upgrade from a Pasture to a Solar Farm “When you need Energy more than you need catnip”. The upgrade is considered “much safer” than upgrading Aqueducts to Hydro Plants, because the demand reduction provided by Pastures inherently has strict diminishing returns.
  • Challenges: The Solar Farm is a required building for the Energy Challenge, which necessitates building at least one of every energy production building. Furthermore, the Winter Has Come challenge grants an increasing reward that boosts the effect of Summer on Solar Farms by 5% per run (capped at 200%).
  • Pollution Mitigation: Solar Farms are considered an environmentally friendly energy source, which can help mitigate the negative effects of pollution.

item.title: Solar Revolution
item.description:
Solar Revolution is a high-impact religious upgrade within the Order of the Sun that provides a permanent global production bonus to nearly all resources in the game. To unlock this multiplier, you must first research Theology, accumulate at least 1,000 Worship, and spend 750 Faith and 500 Gold.

Mechanism and Scaling

  • Calculation: The bonus is calculated based on your total accumulated worship using the formula: $(sqrt(1+8 * worship / 1000)-1)/2$.
  • Initial Impact: While it may only provide a modest boost of 4–5% shortly after it is unlocked, it eventually becomes a primary driver of colony growth.
  • Production Speed: At higher levels, it can increase production rates to 50x normal speeds, making expensive buildings and housing far more affordable.
  • Science Boost: In addition to physical resources, overall science production is directly enhanced by the Solar Revolution multiplier.

Caps and Diminishing Returns

The production bonus is subject to diminishing returns starting at 750% and is initially hard-capped at 1,000%. However, this cap can be extended through advanced late-game mechanics:
item.content:encoded:
Solar Revolution is a high-impact religious upgrade within the Order of the Sun that provides a permanent global production bonus to nearly all resources in the game. To unlock this multiplier, you must first research Theology, accumulate at least 1,000 Worship, and spend 750 Faith and 500 Gold.

Mechanism and Scaling

  • Calculation: The bonus is calculated based on your total accumulated worship using the formula: $(sqrt(1+8 * worship / 1000)-1)/2$.
  • Initial Impact: While it may only provide a modest boost of 4–5% shortly after it is unlocked, it eventually becomes a primary driver of colony growth.
  • Production Speed: At higher levels, it can increase production rates to 50x normal speeds, making expensive buildings and housing far more affordable.
  • Science Boost: In addition to physical resources, overall science production is directly enhanced by the Solar Revolution multiplier.

Caps and Diminishing Returns

The production bonus is subject to diminishing returns starting at 750% and is initially hard-capped at 1,000%. However, this cap can be extended through advanced late-game mechanics:

  • Black Obelisks: These cryptotheology buildings improve the Solar Revolution bonus cap by +5% per transcendence tier.
  • Atheism Challenge: While this challenge disables the Solar Revolution bonus entirely during the run, completing it provides a permanent reward where the cap increases by 100 percentage points for every Transcendence tier you possess.
  • Effectiveness Reward: Successive completions of the Atheism challenge also increase the effectiveness of the bonus by 10% per run, multiplicative with Black Obelisks.

Strategic Utility and Management

  • Unicorn Era: Solar Revolution is essential for late-game progression because it is one of the only multipliers that affects unicorn production.
  • Managing Sacrifices: Because the bonus is so powerful, it is generally considered suboptimal to sacrifice faith for Apocrypha or Transcendence mid-run if it will significantly lower your current production bonus. Strategic advice suggests only sacrificing once you can quickly rebuild the bonus to the 750–1,000% range.
  • Apocrypha Synergy: A high Apocrypha (epiphany) bonus is vital because it allows you to praise the sun more effectively, enabling you to regain your maximum Solar Revolution multiplier in seconds after a reset.
  • Environmental Factors: You should be aware that high levels of pollution can harm resource production by negatively affecting your Solar Revolution bonus.
  • Iron Will: In specialized Iron Will runs, Solar Revolution is a critical tool for overcoming the lack of kitten-based labor; players are encouraged to build a high Apocrypha bonus in previous runs to facilitate rapid growth in this mode.

Where to See Its Value

You can check your active Solar Revolution bonus in two places in the game interface:

  1. On the Religion Tab (Direct Value)
  • Open the Religion tab.
  • Look directly beneath the Order of the Sun section header (near the “Praise the Sun!” button).
  • You will see a readout displaying: +XXX.XX% bonus
  1. Resource Hover Tooltips (Applied Breakdown)
  • In the left-hand resource pane, hover your cursor over the +per sec production rate of any standard resource (such as Catnip, Minerals, or Iron).
  • A breakdown tooltip will appear detailing all active modifiers. Look for the Solar Revolution line item, which shows the exact percentage boost it contributes to that specific resource’s net output.

item.title: Solarchant
item.description:
Solar Chant is a fundamental religious upgrade found within the Order of the Sun section of the Religion tab. It serves as a primary driver for scaling your colony’s religious economy by directly increasing the rate at which Faith is generated.

Cost and Requirements

  • Initial Cost: 100 Faith.
  • Prerequisite: You must have accumulated at least 150 Worship (formerly known as “praised faith”) to unlock the option to purchase it.
  • Price Ratio: It has a price ratio of 2.5, meaning that if you unlock the ability to purchase multiple levels, each subsequent tier will cost 2.5 times more than the last.

Core Effects and Stacking

  • Base Bonus: Upon the first purchase, Solar Chant provides a permanent 10% boost to your overall faith generation rate.
  • Transcendence Scaling: Once you unlock the Transcendence upgrade (which requires 125,000 Worship, 7,500 Faith, and 7,500 Gold), Solar Chant becomes a tiered upgrade.
  • Incremental Growth: For every additional level of Solar Chant purchased using Transcendence, the faith production bonus increases by an additional +10%.

Strategic Utility

  • Late-Game “Priest Strategy”: As players enter the late game and find themselves waiting for slow-moving resources like Unobtainium or Eludium, a common strategy is to reassign the majority of the kitten workforce to the Priest job. Solar Chant is critical here, as multiple levels of the upgrade significantly amplify the output of these [Priests] ( /job/priest/).
  • Faith Reset Loops: High levels of Solar Chant facilitate a positive feedback loop. By dramatically increasing faith production, players can more rapidly rebuild their Solar Revolution production bonus (which caps at 1000%) after performing a faith reset or “Adoring the Galaxy”.
  • Transcendence Progression: Accelerating faith production via Solar Chant is essential for reaching the extremely high epiphany requirements of later Transcendence Tiers, such as Tier 15, which requires approximately 3.04 million percent epiphany.
