item.title: Space Expansionism
item.description:
Space expansionism in Kittens Game refers to the phase where your civilisation leaves its home planet, Cath, to colonise the solar system. This era is officially unlocked by researching the Rocketry technology, which enables the Space tab and allows you to build rockets for interstellar missions.

Initial Unlocking and Missions

To begin your expansion, you must first navigate the “Titanium Era” to secure the necessary materials and storage caps. The first milestone is Orbital Launch, which requires a significant investment in Starcharts, Catpower, Science, and Oil.
item.content:encoded:
Space expansionism in Kittens Game refers to the phase where your civilisation leaves its home planet, Cath, to colonise the solar system. This era is officially unlocked by researching the Rocketry technology, which enables the Space tab and allows you to build rockets for interstellar missions.

Initial Unlocking and Missions

To begin your expansion, you must first navigate the “Titanium Era” to secure the necessary materials and storage caps. The first milestone is Orbital Launch, which requires a significant investment in Starcharts, Catpower, Science, and Oil.

Key initial missions include:

  • Orbital Launch: Unlocks the ability to deploy Satellites and build Space Elevators.
  • Moon Mission: The most critical early goal, as it provides access to Unobtainium through Lunar Outposts and significantly expanded storage via Moon Bases.
  • Dune Mission: Provides a source of Uranium (via Planet Crackers) and high-pressure Oil (via Hydraulic Fracturers).
  • Piscine Mission: Unlocks Research Vessels, which are essential for generating large quantities of Starcharts in the mid-to-late game.

Critical Resources for Space

Successful space expansion relies on several specific resources that become the primary bottlenecks of the late game:

  • Starcharts: Found by observing astronomical events or produced by Satellites and Research Vessels; these are the “currency” of space travel.
  • Unobtainium (UO): A rare resource refined from Uranium at Lunar Outposts. It is the gateway to Time Crystals, Eludium, and the endgame storage loops.
  • Oil and Kerosene: Oil is used for initial launches, while advanced missions require Kerosene, a fuel processed from oil.
  • Antimatter: Produced by Sunlifters (Helios), it is used for high-tier upgrades and increasing resource caps.

Strategic Optimization

Space expansion is not just about exploring; it is a mechanism for scaling your civilisation’s resource caps geometrically.

  • Space Manufacturing: This is a vital workshop upgrade that allows your Factories to improve the production of space buildings. Without this, space structures often provide marginal returns.
  • Global Multipliers: Buildings like the Space Elevator (reduces oil costs) and Orbital Array (provides a 2% bonus to all space structures) are essential for making expansion efficient.
  • Storage Caps: Late-game progression is gated by the 8.14 billion Unobtainium storage requirement needed for 100 Chronospheres. This is achieved through massive investment in Moon Bases, Cryostations, and AI Bases.

Planetary Destinations and Utilities

Destination Key Structure Primary Benefit
Redmoon Lunar Outpost Primary source of Unobtainium.
Dune Planet Cracker High-volume Uranium production.
Piscine Research Vessel Massive Science and Starchart generation.
Helios Sunlifter Primary source of Antimatter.
T-Minus Cryostation Massive storage for base metals and Unobtainium.
Kairo Space Beacon Late-game Relic and Science production.

item.title: Space Manufacturing
item.description:
Space Manufacturing is a critical late-game Workshop upgrade that serves as the primary multiplier for space-based resource production. It fundamentally shifts the economy by allowing terrestrial Factories to enhance the effectiveness of orbital infrastructure.

Unlocking and Costs

To access Space Manufacturing, you must first research the Superconductors technology. Once unlocked, the upgrade can be purchased in the Workshop for:

  • Science: 250,000
  • Titanium: 125,000

Reaching the 125,000 Titanium cap is often a significant hurdle for players. The sources recommend increasing storage capacity through Paragon, Cryostations, Moon Bases, and Accelerators (with the Energy Rift upgrade) to satisfy this requirement.
item.content:encoded:
Space Manufacturing is a critical late-game Workshop upgrade that serves as the primary multiplier for space-based resource production. It fundamentally shifts the economy by allowing terrestrial Factories to enhance the effectiveness of orbital infrastructure.

Unlocking and Costs

To access Space Manufacturing, you must first research the Superconductors technology. Once unlocked, the upgrade can be purchased in the Workshop for:

  • Science: 250,000
  • Titanium: 125,000

Reaching the 125,000 Titanium cap is often a significant hurdle for players. The sources recommend increasing storage capacity through Paragon, Cryostations, Moon Bases, and Accelerators (with the Energy Rift upgrade) to satisfy this requirement.

Core Mechanics and Scaling

The primary function of Space Manufacturing is to provide a “Space Bonus” based on your number of Factories.

  • Base Effect: Each Factory provides a bonus to space production equal to 75% of the factory craft ratio.
  • Specific Modifiers: It specifically increases the production bonus provided by Space Elevators and Orbital Arrays by 3.75% per factory.
  • Synergy: If you have researched Factory Logistics, this bonus is further improved to 4.5% per factory.
  • Exclusions: It is important to note that this bonus does not apply to Planet Crackers.

Strategic Importance

The acquisition of Space Manufacturing is considered a turning point in the “Titanium Era” and beyond for several reasons:

  • Validating Space Infrastructure: Before this upgrade, Space Elevators are generally considered not worth their high construction cost; however, Space Manufacturing makes them highly useful for scaling production.
  • Unobtainium Production: By boosting the effectiveness of Space Elevators and Orbital Arrays, Space Manufacturing significantly accelerates the production of Unobtainium from Lunar Outposts.
  • Late-Game Efficiency: The “Space Production Bonus” derived from this upgrade is a core component in calculating the return on investment for late-game structures. For example, in short runs, it helps determine the exact point at which building additional Space Elevators becomes profitable.
  • Industrial Integration: It represents a deeper integration of the village’s industrial base with its space program, utilizing the Full Industrialization policy to further refine the effectiveness of Factories.

item.title: Space Navigation
item.description:
Navigation is a mid-game technology that acts as the essential bridge between terrestrial development and space exploration. It primarily enables the construction of Trade Ships and Harbours, allowing your kittens to expand their storage limits and find new civilisations to trade for rare resources.

Technological Requirements

To unlock Navigation, your civilisation must first research Astronomy.

  • Science Cost: 35,000.
  • Resource Cost: 100 Manuscripts.
  • Unlocks: Physics, Geology, and Architecture technologies.

The Starchart Economy

The “fuel” for space navigation is the Starchart. These are rare resources used to build trade ships and launch space missions.
item.content:encoded:
Navigation is a mid-game technology that acts as the essential bridge between terrestrial development and space exploration. It primarily enables the construction of Trade Ships and Harbours, allowing your kittens to expand their storage limits and find new civilisations to trade for rare resources.

Technological Requirements

To unlock Navigation, your civilisation must first research Astronomy.

  • Science Cost: 35,000.
  • Resource Cost: 100 Manuscripts.
  • Unlocks: Physics, Geology, and Architecture technologies.

The Starchart Economy

The “fuel” for space navigation is the Starchart. These are rare resources used to build trade ships and launch space missions.

  • Generation: Starcharts are primarily found by observing astronomical events (0.25% base chance per day). Once you reach the space era, they are produced passively by Satellites (0.005/sec), Research Vessels (0.05/sec), and Space Beacons (0.125/sec).
  • Optimization: Building Observatories is the most effective way to manage the starchart bottleneck. Each Observatory adds a 0.2% chance to see an event and a 1% chance for the event to succeed automatically without you clicking the “Observe” button.
  • Kitten Jobs: Researching the Astrophysicists upgrade allows your Scholar kittens to generate 0.0005 starcharts per second.

Space Missions and Logistics

Once Rocketry is researched, the Space tab opens, allowing you to use your starcharts for navigation beyond Cath.

Mission Starchart Cost Key Unlocks
Orbital Launch 250 Space Elevator, Moon Mission, Satellites
Moon Mission 500 Lunar Outpost, Moon Base, Dune Mission
Dune Mission 1,000 Planet Crackers, Hydraulic Fracturers
Piscine Mission 1,500 Research Vessels

Note: In the Black Sky challenge, the starchart requirement for the Orbital Launch is removed, but other resource costs increase by 11x.

Key Navigation Upgrades

  • Satellite Navigation: Each active satellite reduces the starchart cost of crafting Trade Ships by 1.25%, capping at a 75% discount once you have 45 satellites.
  • Antimatter & Thorium Drives: These upgrades significantly reduce mission travel times. An Antimatter Drive divides travel time by 25, a Thorium Drive by 50, and both together by 75.
  • Caravanserai: This Workshop upgrade allows your Tradeposts to improve your standing with hostile races like the Zebras, making trade navigation safer.

item.title: Spaceport
item.description:
The Spaceport is a high-tier late-game structure that serves as a direct upgrade to the Warehouse. It transitions your storage infrastructure from ground-based facilities into energy-consuming logistics hubs that significantly expand your capacity in space.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Prerequisite: You must first research the Exometallurgy technology (formerly known as Advanced Exogeology).
  • Upgrade Path: It is an upgraded version of the Warehouse; however, if energy is lost, it can “downgrade” or revert back to its Warehouse state.
  • Construction Costs:
    • Titanium: 10,000
    • Eludium: 500
    • Kerosene: 1,000
    • Blueprints: 500
    • Starcharts: 400,000

Core Effects and Energy Consumption

The Spaceport provides multiplicative storage bonuses to critical space structures rather than providing flat storage itself.

    • Cryostations
  • Energy Consumption: Unlike the standard Warehouse, which requires no power, each Spaceport consumes 5 Watts of energy.
  • Scaling Drain: The energy consumption of Spaceports begins to increase further once you have constructed more than 10 of them.

Strategic Considerations

The shift from Warehouses to Spaceports is a major infrastructure pivot. While the storage bonuses are essential for reaching the massive resource caps required for the deep endgame, the -5W drain per building (and higher beyond the 10th) can quickly overwhelm a mid-game energy grid. Players are generally advised to ensure their power production (from Sunlifters, Reactors, or Tectonics) is robust before committing to a mass upgrade of their Warehouse network.

item.title: Spice
item.description:
Spice is primarily used as a rare luxury resource and a building component for advanced structures in Kittens Game [1-3].

Uses and Effects

  1. Happiness Bonus (Luxury Resource) Spice is categorized as a rare luxury resource. Every rare resource, including spice, provides a +10% bonus to happiness.
  2. Building Material Spice is a resource required for constructing late-game religious buildings:
    • The Brewery requires 5 Spice, along with Wood, Culture, and Parchment.
    • The Marker, a strange structure made of unknown metal, costs 50,000 Spice.
    • The Black Pyramid, a dark relic of unspeakable horrors that unlocks trade with Leviathans, costs 150,000 Spice.

Characteristics and Management

  • Consumption and Degradation: Spice is a resource that gradually degrades over time [3, 5].
    • Tradeposts help decrease the consumption rate of spice, though with diminishing returns.
    • The Stoicism policy can be chosen to halve the consumption of luxury resources, which includes Spice, and also reduces Brewery consumption by 25% [6].
    • Once a Brewery is built, it consumes 0.1 Spice per tick.

Acquisition

Spice is acquired during successful trade transactions [3, 5].

  • There is a 35% chance of one Spice being included in the trade, with a minimum amount of 25, which can be increased by your trade ratio value [7].
  • The chance of receiving spice increases by 1 percentage point per embassy built, and this increase has no diminishing returns [7, 8].

item.title: Stasis Chambers
item.description:
Stasis Chambers are a high-tier Workshop upgrade that significantly enhances the storage capacity of your Accelerators. It is a key component in scaling resource caps during the late game, particularly for deep runs where standard storage buildings reach their limits.

Technological Unlock and Cost

  • Prerequisite: You must first research Chronophysics.
  • Science Cost: 235,000.
  • Resource Cost: 200 Alloy, 2,000 Uranium, and 1 Time Crystal.

Core Effect: Energy Rift Enhancement

The primary function of Stasis Chambers is to augment the Energy Rifts upgrade, which allows Accelerators to store basic materials in pocket dimensions.
item.content:encoded:
Stasis Chambers are a high-tier Workshop upgrade that significantly enhances the storage capacity of your Accelerators. It is a key component in scaling resource caps during the late game, particularly for deep runs where standard storage buildings reach their limits.

Technological Unlock and Cost

  • Prerequisite: You must first research Chronophysics.
  • Science Cost: 235,000.
  • Resource Cost: 200 Alloy, 2,000 Uranium, and 1 Time Crystal.

Core Effect: Energy Rift Enhancement

The primary function of Stasis Chambers is to augment the Energy Rifts upgrade, which allows Accelerators to store basic materials in pocket dimensions.

  • Storage Bonus: Each Stasis Chamber increases the maximum storage for catnip, wood, minerals, coal, iron, titanium, and gold provided by Accelerators by +95%.
  • Additive Nature: This bonus stacks additively with other Accelerator storage upgrades, such as Void Energy (+75%), Dark Energy (+250%), and Tachyon Accelerators (+500%).

Strategic Utility

  • Deep Runs: Because this upgrade costs a Time Crystal, it is generally recommended only when you are performing a “Deep Run”. Using rare Time Crystals on Workshop upgrades that do not carry over across resets can be considered a waste in shorter runs unless you can easily replenish them.
  • Storage Bottlenecks: This upgrade is vital for bypassing major mid-to-late game bottlenecks, such as the titanium and gold caps required to afford advanced space structures or expensive religious upgrades.
  • Non-Permanence: Unlike metaphysics upgrades, Stasis Chambers are lost upon resetting the game. You will need to repurchase the upgrade in every subsequent run to regain its storage benefits.

By effectively doubling the effectiveness of Energy Rifts, Stasis Chambers represent the first major step in transforming your industrial base from production-only into a critical component of your global storage network.

item.title: Steel Armour
item.description:
Steel Armour is a mid-game Workshop upgrade that enhances the effectiveness of the hunting system. It is researched in the Workshop tab and is unlocked once you have discovered the Steel science technology.

Costs and Prerequisites

  • Science Cost: 10,000.
  • Resource Cost: 50 Steel.
  • Prerequisite: Researching the Steel technology is mandatory before this upgrade appears.

Effects on Hunting

The primary function of Steel Armour is to increase the hunting bonus for your kittens (or Zebras in Iron Will mode).
item.content:encoded:
Steel Armour is a mid-game Workshop upgrade that enhances the effectiveness of the hunting system. It is researched in the Workshop tab and is unlocked once you have discovered the Steel science technology.

Costs and Prerequisites

  • Science Cost: 10,000.
  • Resource Cost: 50 Steel.
  • Prerequisite: Researching the Steel technology is mandatory before this upgrade appears.

Effects on Hunting

The primary function of Steel Armour is to increase the hunting bonus for your kittens (or Zebras in Iron Will mode).

  • Hunting Bonus: It provides a flat +0.5 bonus to hunting effectiveness.
  • Additive Stacking: This bonus is additive with other hunting upgrades. For example, if you have already researched Bolas (+1.0) and Hunting Armour (+2.0), adding Steel Armour brings your total hunting bonus to 3.5.
  • Yield Increase: This upgrade increases the basic fur and ivory hunting amounts by approximately 40–50%.
  • Expected Results: With Bolas, Hunting Armour, and Steel Armour active, the expected yield per hunt is approximately 153.25 fur and 47.94 ivory.

Technical Mechanics

Because Steel Armour provides a non-integral bonus (+0.5), it causes the probability distribution for hunting resources to become non-uniform. When calculating the amount of furs or gold acquired, the game generates a random integer range; a non-integral hunting bonus allows for the possibility of generating the next highest integer in the range, though with half the probability of the other integers.

Strategic Utility

Steel Armour is essential for scaling your cultural engine in the mid-game. Higher fur yields allow for more rapid crafting of Parchment, which is the foundational material for Manuscripts and Compendiums. Additionally, increased ivory yields are critical for trading with the Nagas to resolve mineral bottlenecks.

item.title: Steel Axe
item.description:
The Steel Axe is a mid-game Workshop upgrade that significantly increases your civilization’s wood production efficiency. It is unlocked after researching the Steel science technology.

Cost and Requirements

  • Science Cost: 20,000.
  • Resource Cost: 75 Steel.
  • Prerequisite: Researching the Steel technology is mandatory for this upgrade to appear in the Workshop.

Core Effects

The Steel Axe is described as being “very sharp and durable” and provides a flat +50% bonus to Woodcutter output (woodRatio). This upgrade is part of a linear progression chain for Woodcutters, following the Mineral Axe (+70%) and Iron Axe (+50%) and preceding the Titanium Axe.

Cost and Requirements

Core Effects

The Steel Axe is described as being “very sharp and durable” and provides a flat +50% bonus to Woodcutter output (woodRatio). This upgrade is part of a linear progression chain for Woodcutters, following the Mineral Axe (+70%) and Iron Axe (+50%) and preceding the Titanium Axe.

Strategic Utility

The axe chain of workshop upgrades is particularly powerful because its bonuses are multiplicative with the production boost from Lumber Mills. Because wood production often becomes a major bottleneck for constructing advanced buildings like Observatories and Harbours in the mid-game, acquiring the Steel Axe is essential for maintaining infrastructure scaling once you have established a steady supply of steel.

item.title: Stoicism
item.description:
Stoicism is a mid-game Philosophy policy that focuses on resource preservation by significantly reducing the consumption rate of luxury goods. It is primarily used to maintain high kitten happiness and trade liquidity when rare resource production is low.

Core Mechanics

  • Cost: 2,500 Culture.
  • Prerequisites: You must have researched the Philosophy technology.
  • Mutual Exclusivity: Enacting Stoicism permanently locks you out of the Epicureanism policy for the remainder of the run.

Primary Effects

The policy encourages restraint within your feline society, leading to the following benefits:
item.content:encoded:
Stoicism is a mid-game Philosophy policy that focuses on resource preservation by significantly reducing the consumption rate of luxury goods. It is primarily used to maintain high kitten happiness and trade liquidity when rare resource production is low.

Core Mechanics

  • Cost: 2,500 Culture.
  • Prerequisites: You must have researched the Philosophy technology.
  • Mutual Exclusivity: Enacting Stoicism permanently locks you out of the Epicureanism policy for the remainder of the run.

Primary Effects

The policy encourages restraint within your feline society, leading to the following benefits:

  • Luxury Preservation: Reduces the consumption of Furs, Ivory, and Spice by 50%.
  • Brewery Efficiency: Reduces brewery consumption by 25%.

The Stoicism Policy Branch

Choosing Stoicism unlocks a specific path of follow-up policies focused on efficiency and restraint:

  • Frugality: Increases Mint production by 10% by reducing corruption.
  • Rationing: Reduces the catnip consumption penalty from high happiness by 10% and provides a +0.1 Hunting bonus.

Strategic Advice

  • Stoicism vs. Epicureanism: This is a common choice for players. While Epicureanism increases the happiness bonus provided by rare resources (from 10% to 11%), Stoicism ensures your limited stock of those resources lasts twice as long.
  • Early Game Utility: Some guides suggest that Stoicism is less necessary if you have a robust hunting team and many Tradeposts, as these already slow down luxury consumption.
  • Iron Will Context: In specialized modes where resources like Ivory are harder to come by and essential for trade (such as trading with the Nagas), Stoicism can be a vital tool for maintaining your progress.

item.title: Stone_Slab
item.description:
A Stone Slab (often simply called a Slab) is a foundational mid-game craftable resource refined from minerals. Each slab is produced in the Workshop at a base cost of 250 Minerals.

Acquisition and Automation

Beyond manual crafting, slabs can be acquired through several channels:

  • Trading with Nagas: The Nagas have a 75% base chance to sell 5 slabs per trade in exchange for ivory.
  • Currency for Zebras: Slabs serve as the primary trade currency for the Zebras, who buy 50 slabs per successful trade to provide iron, metal plates, and titanium.
  • Steamworks Automation: Researching Workshop Automation allows Steamworks to automatically convert minerals into slabs once per year whenever minerals reach 98% of their storage cap. This frequency increases to twice per year with Advanced Automation.

Construction and Crafting Uses

Slabs are a mandatory material for a vast array of essential infrastructure and higher-tier resources:
item.content:encoded:
A Stone Slab (often simply called a Slab) is a foundational mid-game craftable resource refined from minerals. Each slab is produced in the Workshop at a base cost of 250 Minerals.

Acquisition and Automation

Beyond manual crafting, slabs can be acquired through several channels:

  • Trading with Nagas: The Nagas have a 75% base chance to sell 5 slabs per trade in exchange for ivory.
  • Currency for Zebras: Slabs serve as the primary trade currency for the Zebras, who buy 50 slabs per successful trade to provide iron, metal plates, and titanium.
  • Steamworks Automation: Researching Workshop Automation allows Steamworks to automatically convert minerals into slabs once per year whenever minerals reach 98% of their storage cap. This frequency increases to twice per year with Advanced Automation.

Construction and Crafting Uses

Slabs are a mandatory material for a vast array of essential infrastructure and higher-tier resources:

  • Storage Buildings: Warehouses (2 slabs) and Harbours (50).
  • Scientific Facilities: Observatories (35), Bio Labs (100), and Data Centres (upgraded from Libraries).
  • Industrial and Religious Buildings: Quarries (1000), Temples (25), and Mansions (185).
  • Resource Conversion: Slabs are required to craft Megaliths (50 slabs) and Concrete (2500 slabs).

Strategic Enhancements

Players can optimize slab production through specific Policy/ and technology paths:

  • Masons Policy: Enacting the Naga Relations: Masons policy provides a +2.5% Quarry slab crafting bonus.
  • Titanium Era: Slabs are considered a high priority during the transition to space, as they are the gating resource required to discovery Zebras and begin mass-acquiring titanium.
  • Iron Will Mode: In this specialized mode, the ability to craft slabs is unlocked once you have established 5 Naga Embassies.

Persistence and Resets

As a crafted resource, stone slabs are lost upon resetting the game by default. To carry them over into a new run, a player must possess at least one Chronosphere and the Flux Condensator Workshop upgrade. The amount preserved follows a formula based on the number of active chronospheres and the square root of the total quantity held before the reset.

item.title: Strip Mining
item.description:
Strip Mining is an environmental policy that increases your global mineral production by 30%. While it provides a significant boost to raw material output, it introduces negative side effects to your colony’s morale and environment.

Core Stats and Requirements

  • Cost: 2000 Science.
  • Prerequisite: Researching the Engineering technology.
  • Mutual Exclusivity: Enacting Strip Mining permanently locks out the Clear Cutting and Environmentalism policies for the remainder of the run.
  • Iron Will Bonus: In this specialized mode, it grants a +10% bonus to minerals gathered from meteors.

Trade-offs and Penalties

Implementing this policy comes with two primary drawbacks:
item.content:encoded:
Strip Mining is an environmental policy that increases your global mineral production by 30%. While it provides a significant boost to raw material output, it introduces negative side effects to your colony’s morale and environment.

Core Stats and Requirements

  • Cost: 2000 Science.
  • Prerequisite: Researching the Engineering technology.
  • Mutual Exclusivity: Enacting Strip Mining permanently locks out the Clear Cutting and Environmentalism policies for the remainder of the run.
  • Iron Will Bonus: In this specialized mode, it grants a +10% bonus to minerals gathered from meteors.

Trade-offs and Penalties

Implementing this policy comes with two primary drawbacks:

  • Happiness Penalty: It imposes a -2% penalty to kitten happiness.
  • Pollution: It increases pollution by +5%. High levels of pollution can eventually lead to reduced catnip production, lower happiness, and slower kitten arrival speeds.

Strategic Advice

  • Early-Game Choice: Most veteran players recommend choosing Clear Cutting over Strip Mining in early runs. This is because minerals are generally easier to accumulate than wood at that stage, and the wood boost from Clear Cutting is vital for reaching the Navigation era.
  • Mid-to-Late Game Role: Despite being less popular early on, Strip Mining (or Clear Cutting) is a mandatory stepping stone to unlock powerful industrial policies like Full Industrialization or Sustainability once you research Industrialization.
  • Unobtainium Production: In the late game, the Full Industrialization policy—which requires having purchased Strip Mining or Clear Cutting—is considered essential for maximizing the output of factories and space structures.

Advanced Synergies

  • Sustainability: Once you reach the industrial era, you can enact the Sustainability policy to remove the -2% happiness penalty and mitigate the pollution caused by Strip Mining.
  • Full Industrialization: Alternatively, you can lean into the industrial path, making your factories 5% more powerful at the cost of even more pollution.

item.title: Sunspire
item.description:
A Sunspire is a high-tier endgame religious building found in the Ziggurat section of the Religion tab. It represents one of the final stages in the unicorn-to-time-crystal pipeline, offering massive bonuses to unicorn generation and alicorn summoning.

Statistics and Requirements

To construct a Sunspire, you must first have at least one Unicorn Utopia.

  • Cost: 25,000 Unicorn Tears, 750,000 Ivory, and 1,000 Gold.
  • Price Ratio: 1.15.
  • Production Bonus: It provides a massive +500% bonus to unicorn generation.

Core Effects

The Sunspire is critical for the late-game “Unicorn Era”, as it automates and enhances the production of rare celestial resources:
item.content:encoded:
A Sunspire is a high-tier endgame religious building found in the Ziggurat section of the Religion tab. It represents one of the final stages in the unicorn-to-time-crystal pipeline, offering massive bonuses to unicorn generation and alicorn summoning.

Statistics and Requirements

To construct a Sunspire, you must first have at least one Unicorn Utopia.

  • Cost: 25,000 Unicorn Tears, 750,000 Ivory, and 1,000 Gold.
  • Price Ratio: 1.15.
  • Production Bonus: It provides a massive +500% bonus to unicorn generation.

Core Effects

The Sunspire is critical for the late-game “Unicorn Era”, as it automates and enhances the production of rare celestial resources:

  • Alicorn Generation: It provides a passive 0.00005 alicorns per tick (0.2 per year) and increases the random alicorn summon chance by 0.03% per game-day.
  • Time Crystal Efficiency: It improves the Time Crystal (TC) refine ratio by 10%, meaning you receive more Time Crystals when sacrificing alicorns.
  • Ivory Harvesting: It increases the ivory gained from Ivory Meteors (a random event summoned by Ivory Citadels) by 50%.

Strategic Utility

In the progression toward a self-sustaining “Positive Reset” engine, Sunspires are used to overcome the massive resource requirements of the late game.

  • Build Order: Strategic guides recommend first building a solid foundation of roughly 25 Ivory Citadels before prioritising higher-tier structures like Unicorn Utopias and Sunspires.
  • Synergy: The effectiveness of a Sunspire is heavily reliant on your Solar Revolution bonus. By the time you are constructing these, you should aim to have your faith production near the 1000% cap to maximise unicorn growth.
  • Relic Engine: Sunspires are a foundational component of the “Type 0 Relic Engine”, where increased unicorn and alicorn production allows for more frequent sacrifices to generate the Time Crystals and Relics needed for Cryptotheology.

item.title: Superconductors
item.description:
Superconductors is an advanced late-mid-game technology that acts as a vital transition point between industrial expansion and deep-space exploration. It focuses on enhancing energy efficiency and bridging the gap to high-tier temporal and antimatter mechanics.

Costs and Prerequisites

  • Science Cost: 225,000.
  • Resource Cost: 175 Blueprints.
  • Prerequisite: Researching Nanotechnology is required before this science becomes available.

Unlocked Technology

  • Antimatter: Superconductors is the mandatory prerequisite for the Antimatter technology, which begins Phase 4 of the game (Chrono-Optimization and Geometric Growth).

Unlocked Workshop Upgrades

Researching this technology provides access to three highly impactful upgrades that drastically improve your energy balance and production:
item.content:encoded:
Superconductors is an advanced late-mid-game technology that acts as a vital transition point between industrial expansion and deep-space exploration. It focuses on enhancing energy efficiency and bridging the gap to high-tier temporal and antimatter mechanics.

Costs and Prerequisites

  • Science Cost: 225,000.
  • Resource Cost: 175 Blueprints.
  • Prerequisite: Researching Nanotechnology is required before this science becomes available.

Unlocked Technology

  • Antimatter: Superconductors is the mandatory prerequisite for the Antimatter technology, which begins Phase 4 of the game (Chrono-Optimization and Geometric Growth).

Unlocked Workshop Upgrades

Researching this technology provides access to three highly impactful upgrades that drastically improve your energy balance and production:

  • Space Manufacturing:
    • Effect: This allows your village’s Factories to provide a production bonus to space-based structures based on 75% of your factory craft ratio.
    • Impact: It specifically increases the Space Bonus from Space Elevators and Orbital Arrays by 3.75% per factory (this increases to 4.5% if you also have the Factory Logistics upgrade). This is essential for scaling Unobtainium production to the levels required for the deep endgame.
  • Cold Fusion:
    • Effect: Increases the energy output of Reactors by 25%.
    • Impact: This provides a flat boost of +2.5 Watts per active Reactor, significantly easing energy bottlenecks.
  • Cryocomputing:
    • Effect: Reduces the energy consumption of Data Centers by 50%.
    • Impact: Each Data Center’s power drain is reduced from 2 Watts to 1 Watt, allowing you to maintain massive science storage without overwhelming your power grid.

Strategic Importance

Superconductors is often considered the threshold for the “Positive Reset” loop. By unlocking Space Manufacturing, players can finally farm enough Unobtainium to build the high number of Chronospheres needed to carry over more resources than they spent during a run. Additionally, the combined effects of Cold Fusion and Cryocomputing allow for a much larger industrial and scientific infrastructure to be powered simultaneously, which is critical for supporting energy-intensive late-game buildings like AI Cores and Entanglement Stations.

item.title: Sustainability
item.description:
In Kittens Game, Sustainability is an environmental policy that focuses on mitigating the negative effects of industrialisation by removing happiness penalties and slightly reducing pollution.

Core Mechanics

  • Cost: 10,000 Culture.
  • Primary Effect: It removes the -2% happiness penalty associated with the Strip Mining or Clear Cutting policies.
  • Secondary Effect: It provides a -5% reduction to overall pollution levels.
  • Prerequisites: You must have researched Industrialization and enacted either the Strip Mining or Clear Cutting policy.

Sustainability vs. Full Industrialization

Sustainability is part of a mutually exclusive pair; once you choose it, you are locked out of Full Industrialization for the remainder of that run.
item.content:encoded:
In Kittens Game, Sustainability is an environmental policy that focuses on mitigating the negative effects of industrialisation by removing happiness penalties and slightly reducing pollution.

Core Mechanics

  • Cost: 10,000 Culture.
  • Primary Effect: It removes the -2% happiness penalty associated with the Strip Mining or Clear Cutting policies.
  • Secondary Effect: It provides a -5% reduction to overall pollution levels.
  • Prerequisites: You must have researched Industrialization and enacted either the Strip Mining or Clear Cutting policy.

Sustainability vs. Full Industrialization

Sustainability is part of a mutually exclusive pair; once you choose it, you are locked out of Full Industrialization for the remainder of that run.

Feature Sustainability Full Industrialization
Main Benefit Removes happiness penalties from mining/logging. Improves Factory crafting bonus by 5%.
Pollution Reduces pollution by 5%. Increases pollution by 5%.
Kitten Morale Better for keeping kittens happy. Focuses on raw industrial output.

Strategic Utility

  • Early Game (First Run): Sustainability is often recommended for your first run. At this stage, you typically only have a single factory to unlock the policy, so the crafting bonus from Full Industrialization is negligible compared to the benefit of maintaining kitten happiness.
  • Mid-to-Late Game: From your second run onwards, most players switch to Full Industrialization. Once you begin building a large number of factories, the multiplicative crafting bonus becomes far more valuable than the small happiness and pollution benefits offered by Sustainability.
  • Pollution Management: While Sustainability helps reduce pollution, it is noted that some pollution is inevitable as your civilisation grows. High pollution can harm catnip production, happiness, and kitten arrival speed. Sustainability is one of the few ways to actively mitigate these atmospheric effects.

item.title: T Minus Mission
item.description:
The T-minus mission is a significant mid-to-late-game space project in Kittens Game that involves travelling to Terminus, described as a supermassive ice giant located at the far end of the Helios solar system. This mission serves as a critical bridge between the mid-game industry and the advanced resource management required for late-game space exploration.

Mission Logistics and Costs

To launch a mission to Terminus, you must first successfully complete the Piscine mission. The resource requirements for the launch are as follows:
item.content:encoded:
The T-minus mission is a significant mid-to-late-game space project in Kittens Game that involves travelling to Terminus, described as a supermassive ice giant located at the far end of the Helios solar system. This mission serves as a critical bridge between the mid-game industry and the advanced resource management required for late-game space exploration.

Mission Logistics and Costs

To launch a mission to Terminus, you must first successfully complete the Piscine mission. The resource requirements for the launch are as follows:

  • Starcharts: 2,500
  • Titanium: 12,000
  • Science: 225,000
  • Kerosene: 750

The base travel time for the mission is 2,500 game-days, which is approximately 1 hour, 23 minutes, and 20 seconds in real-time. As with other missions, this duration can be divided by 25 with an Antimatter Drive, 50 with a Thorium Drive, or 75 if both are researched.

Critical Unlocks: Cryostations

Successfully completing the T-minus mission unlocks the Kairo mission and the T-Minus planet, but its most strategically vital unlock is the Cryostation. Cryostations are massive storage facilities that provide essential boosts to your global caps:

  • Storage Gains: Each station increases the maximum capacity for Wood and Minerals (+200K), Iron (+50K), Titanium (+7,500), Uranium (+5,000), Oil (+7,500), Unobtainium (+750), and Coal (+25K).
  • Titanium Bottleneck: Cryostations are identified as one of the most effective ways to increase titanium storage, which is necessary to reach the 125K cap required for the Space Manufacturing upgrade.
  • Unobtainium Progression: Because they provide 750 unobtainium storage each, they are also a primary method for reaching the 1,000-unit threshold required for the Eludium Era.

The T-minus Cycle

“T-minus” is also one of the ten five-year cycles within the Helios system, represented by the glyph ⍝. If you have researched Numerology or Numeromancy, this cycle introduces specific global modifiers:

  • Production and Storage: During this cycle, Sunlifter energy output is reduced by 50%, but Cryostation storage capacity is increased by 20%.
  • Festival Effect: Holding a festival during the T-minus cycle provides an Oil income x2 multiplier.

Strategic Utility

In the broader progression of the game, the T-minus mission is a gateway to “Phase 4,” where the player begins to focus on chrono-optimization and geometric growth. By providing a massive leap in storage capacity through Cryostations, it allows kittens to store the high-tier materials (like Eludium and Unobtainium) needed to build Chronospheres and prepare for self-sustaining resets.

item.title: Tachyon Accelerators
item.description:
Tachyon Accelerators is a powerful late-game Workshop upgrade that provides a massive boost to your resource storage capacity by enhancing the effectiveness of your Accelerators.

Prerequisites and Costs

To unlock this upgrade, you must first research the Tachyon Theory science technology, which itself requires Chronophysics.

  • Upgrade Cost: 500,000 Science, 125 Eludium, and 10 Time Crystals.

Core Effect: Energy Rift Enhancement

The primary function of Tachyon Accelerators is to augment the Energy Rifts upgrade, which allows Accelerators to store basic materials in pocket dimensions.
item.content:encoded:

Prerequisites and Costs

To unlock this upgrade, you must first research the Tachyon Theory science technology, which itself requires Chronophysics.

  • Upgrade Cost: 500,000 Science, 125 Eludium, and 10 Time Crystals.

Core Effect: Energy Rift Enhancement

The primary function of Tachyon Accelerators is to augment the Energy Rifts upgrade, which allows Accelerators to store basic materials in pocket dimensions.

  • Storage Multiplier: It makes Energy Rifts 5 times as effective, providing a flat +500% bonus to the maximum storage of catnip, wood, minerals, coal, iron, titanium, and gold provided by Accelerators.
  • Additive Stacking: This bonus stacks additively with other Accelerator storage upgrades, such as Stasis Chambers (+95%), Void Energy (+75%), and Dark Energy (+250%). When all upgrades are combined, the total storage bonus for Accelerators reaches +920%.

Strategic Utility

Tachyon Accelerators are a cornerstone of late-game resource scaling. By the time you reach Tachyon Theory, basic storage buildings like Barns and Warehouses often hit their limits. This upgrade allows your industrial infrastructure to double as high-capacity storage, which is essential for:

  • Bypassing Bottlenecks: Reaching the massive titanium and gold caps required for advanced space structures and expensive religious upgrades.
  • Endgame Resets: Increasing your resource caps to maximize the amount of materials you can carry over when resetting with Chronospheres.
  • Science Scaling: Helping you reach the high science caps required for endgame research like Void Space (800k) or Paradox Theory (1M) by allowing you to store more resources used in crafting Compendiums.

item.title: Tachyon Theory
item.description:
Tachyon Theory is a high-level science technology that marks a major turning point in the late game, transitioning your civilization from standard industrialization into the era of time manipulation and void exploration. It is a mandatory step for unlocking the most advanced endgame mechanics.

Costs and Prerequisites

Researching Tachyon Theory is expensive and requires resources that can only be obtained through advanced trading or religious sacrifices.

  • Science Cost: 750,000.
  • Resource Cost: 25 Time Crystals and 1 Relic.
  • Prerequisite: You must first research Chronophysics.

Unlocked Technology and Upgrades

Researching this technology unlocks the Void Space science and provides access to three powerful Workshop upgrades:
