Costs and Prerequisites

Researching Tachyon Theory is expensive and requires resources that can only be obtained through advanced trading or religious sacrifices.

  • Science Cost: 750,000.
  • Resource Cost: 25 Time Crystals and 1 Relic.
  • Prerequisite: You must first research Chronophysics.

Unlocked Technology and Upgrades

Researching this technology unlocks the Void Space science and provides access to three powerful Workshop upgrades:

  • Chronoforge: Unlocks the “Chronoforge” section in the Time tab. This allows you to combust (shatter) Time Crystals to skip ahead to the next spring, advancing the calendar year instantly. This is the foundation of the late-game “Shatter Engine,” used to rapidly generate antimatter and resources.
  • Tachyon Accelerators: A massive storage upgrade for Accelerators, increasing the capacity they provide for catnip, wood, minerals, iron, coal, gold, and titanium by 500%.
  • Chronoengineers: An efficiency upgrade that allows Engineers to continue performing crafts during a time skip (provided you have Resource Retrieval levels).

Strategic Importance

Tachyon Theory is primarily used as a gateway to the Endgame Reset Loop. By unlocking the Chronoforge, it allows you to manipulate time to stay within beneficial cycles, such as the Redmoon cycle, which provides a massive boost to Unobtainium production.

Furthermore, it is a required prerequisite for Void Space, which is necessary to attempt the Atheism Challenge and to begin collecting Void, a resource essential for reaching the game’s theoretical limits.

item.title: Technocracy
item.description:
Technocracy is a high-tier Government policy that provides a 20% increase to your maximum science storage capacity. While this sounds substantial, it is generally considered the least effective option in its tier because there are many other ways to expand science storage that do not require sacrificing a policy slot.

Key Statistics

  • Cost: 150,000 Culture.
  • Requirement: You must have reached Dune to unlock it.
  • Mutual Exclusivity: Enacting Technocracy permanently locks you out of Cosmological Libertarianism and Order of the Stars for the remainder of the run.

Strategic Analysis: Why it is often Skipped

In the late game, science storage is rarely the primary bottleneck. Players have access to numerous structures and items that expand this cap, making the 20% boost from Technocracy redundant:
item.content:encoded:
Technocracy is a high-tier Government policy that provides a 20% increase to your maximum science storage capacity. While this sounds substantial, it is generally considered the least effective option in its tier because there are many other ways to expand science storage that do not require sacrificing a policy slot.

Key Statistics

  • Cost: 150,000 Culture.
  • Requirement: You must have reached Dune to unlock it.
  • Mutual Exclusivity: Enacting Technocracy permanently locks you out of Cosmological Libertarianism and Order of the Stars for the remainder of the run.

Strategic Analysis: Why it is often Skipped

In the late game, science storage is rarely the primary bottleneck. Players have access to numerous structures and items that expand this cap, making the 20% boost from Technocracy redundant:

  • Science Buildings: Libraries (and their upgrade, Data Centers), Academies, Observatories, and Bio Labs all provide flat and percentage-based science cap increases.
  • Compendiums: Every Compendium you craft increases your science storage by 10 units.
  • Late-Game Structures: Research Vessels and Space Beacons provide massive science cap boosts (+10k and +25k respectively).

Superior Alternatives

Because you can only choose one policy at this tier, the community generally recommends the other two options depending on your current goals:

  • Cosmological Libertarianism: Provides +15% Unobtainium production. Unobtainium is a much harder bottleneck to clear than science storage, making this the “meta” choice for most players.
  • Order of the Stars: Provides +20% Faith production. This is ideal for long runs focused on grinding Transcendence tiers and religious bonuses.

When to Consider Technocracy

Technocracy is only truly useful if you are attempting to reach a specific, massive science threshold for an endgame technology (like Blackchain or Exophysics) and have already maxed out all other science storage options without reaching the required amount.

item.title: Telecommunication
item.description:
Telecommunication is a late-mid-game Workshop upgrade that drastically accelerates the rate at which your workforce gains professional experience. It represents a shift towards a more connected society where kittens can share knowledge and master their trades more efficiently.

Costs and Prerequisites

To unlock this upgrade, you must first research the Electronics science technology. Once researched, the upgrade becomes available in the Workshop for the following resources:

  • Science: 150,000
  • Titanium: 5,000
  • Uranium: 50

Core Effect: Rapid Skill Acquisition

The primary function of Telecommunication is to modify the speed at which kittens gain job skills.
item.content:encoded:
Telecommunication is a late-mid-game Workshop upgrade that drastically accelerates the rate at which your workforce gains professional experience. It represents a shift towards a more connected society where kittens can share knowledge and master their trades more efficiently.

Costs and Prerequisites

To unlock this upgrade, you must first research the Electronics science technology. Once researched, the upgrade becomes available in the Workshop for the following resources:

  • Science: 150,000
  • Titanium: 5,000
  • Uranium: 50

Core Effect: Rapid Skill Acquisition

The primary function of Telecommunication is to modify the speed at which kittens gain job skills.

  • Mechanism: It sets the base learning rate percentage for job skills equal to your current number of kittens, provided you have a population of at least 100 kittens.
  • Impact: By scaling learning speed directly with population, your kittens will reach high proficiency levels—such as Proficient (+13%) or Master (+18.75%)—significantly faster than through standard manual work alone.

Strategic Utility

Telecommunication is highly valuable for maintaining high production efficiency across multiple runs. Because job skills provide multiplicative productivity bonuses that stack with happiness and other global multipliers, having a fully “Mastered” workforce is essential for maximizing resource yields. This upgrade is particularly useful in the late game when you are frequently assigning new kittens to specialized roles or moving them between professions to address specific resource bottlenecks.

item.title: Templars
item.description:
Templars is a high-tier religious upgrade available under the Order of the Sun in the Religion tab. It specifically enhances the utility of Temples by increasing the colony’s maximum Catpower capacity.

Acquisition and Costs

To unlock the Templars upgrade, you must first research Theology and accumulate a significant amount of religious capital.

  • Prerequisites: You must have at least 75,000 Worship accumulated through “Praising the Sun”.
  • Cost: The initial upgrade costs 3,500 Faith and 3,000 Gold.
  • Price Ratio: Like most religious upgrades, it has a price ratio of 2.5, meaning subsequent levels (if unlocked via Transcendence) become significantly more expensive.

Effects and Scaling

The primary function of Templars is to turn your Temples into storage facilities for Catpower.
item.content:encoded:
Templars is a high-tier religious upgrade available under the Order of the Sun in the Religion tab. It specifically enhances the utility of Temples by increasing the colony’s maximum Catpower capacity.

Acquisition and Costs

To unlock the Templars upgrade, you must first research Theology and accumulate a significant amount of religious capital.

  • Prerequisites: You must have at least 75,000 Worship accumulated through “Praising the Sun”.
  • Cost: The initial upgrade costs 3,500 Faith and 3,000 Gold.
  • Price Ratio: Like most religious upgrades, it has a price ratio of 2.5, meaning subsequent levels (if unlocked via Transcendence) become significantly more expensive.

Effects and Scaling

The primary function of Templars is to turn your Temples into storage facilities for Catpower.

  • Base Effect: Each Temple provides +75 max catpower.
  • Transcendence Scaling: If you have purchased Transcendence, you can buy additional levels of the Templars upgrade. Each additional level increases the bonus by a further +25 max catpower per Temple.

Strategic Utility

While it may seem like a minor bonus early on, Templars is a critical component for late-game industrial and trade optimization:

  • Blueprint Farming: In the endgame, players often rely on Mints to generate the massive quantities of blueprints needed for high-tier structures. Because Mints scale their output based on your maximum Catpower capacity, the boost provided by Templars directly increases your blueprint production speed.
  • Policy Synergies: The Liberalism policy is specifically noted for allowing players to acquire more levels of the Templars upgrade more easily, which in turn assists with ivory generation and international trade.
  • Resource Management: By significantly raising the Catpower cap, Templars allows you to store enough energy to fund massive space missions, such as Orbital Launches (which require 5,000 Catpower) or Rorschach Missions (which require 80,000 Catpower), without being limited by standard housing caps.

item.title: Terraformation
item.description:
Terraformation is a high-level endgame science technology in Kittens Game that serves as a vital gateway to scaling your population and energy production through deep-space engineering.

Costs and Prerequisites

  • Science Cost: 750,000.
  • Resource Cost: 5 Relics.
  • Prerequisite: You must first research Antimatter.

Unlocked Technologies and Structures

Researching Terraformation is required to unlock several critical endgame components:

  • Hydroponics (Technology): Unlocks the Hydroponics structure, which is mandatory for massive late-game food scaling.
  • Terraforming Station (Building): Located on the planet Yarn in the Space tab.
  • Tectonic (Building): Located in the Centaurus System in the Space tab.

The Terraforming Station (Yarn)

This structure represents the process of melting Yarn’s ice and oxygenating its atmosphere to support life.
item.content:encoded:
Terraformation is a high-level endgame science technology in Kittens Game that serves as a vital gateway to scaling your population and energy production through deep-space engineering.

Costs and Prerequisites

  • Science Cost: 750,000.
  • Resource Cost: 5 Relics.
  • Prerequisite: You must first research Antimatter.

Unlocked Technologies and Structures

Researching Terraformation is required to unlock several critical endgame components:

  • Hydroponics (Technology): Unlocks the Hydroponics structure, which is mandatory for massive late-game food scaling.
  • Terraforming Station (Building): Located on the planet Yarn in the Space tab.
  • Tectonic (Building): Located in the Centaurus System in the Space tab.

The Terraforming Station (Yarn)

This structure represents the process of melting Yarn’s ice and oxygenating its atmosphere to support life.

  • Cost: 25 Antimatter, 5,000 Uranium, and 5,000 Kerosene.
  • Effect: Each station increases your maximum kitten population by +1.
  • Synergy: Every unit of Hydroponics you own provides a +1.0% bonus to the kitten capacity of your Terraforming Stations, allowing them to eventually house more than one kitten each.

Tectonic (Centaurus System)

This structure involves ripping open the planet near the star Centaurus to harvest magma energy.

  • Cost: 600,000 Science, 500 Antimatter, and 75,000 Thorium.
  • Effect: Each Tectonic provides +25 Energy.
  • Upgrades: Every level of Molten Core (requires Exophysics) improves Tectonic energy production by an additional 5%.
  • Challenge Goal: Building at least one Tectonic is a requirement for completing the Energy Challenge.

Strategic Utility

Terraformation is a cornerstone of the Endgame Paragon phase. By “Terraforming Yarn,” players can build a vast amount of housing (potentially support up to 60,000 kittens), which is essential for generating massive amounts of Paragon per reset. Additionally, Tectonic structures provide the high-density energy required to power late-game facilities like AI Cores and Entanglement Stations without relying solely on ground-based reactors.

item.title: Theology
item.description:
Theology is a pivotal science technology in Kittens Game that marks a significant transition point in the civilization’s progression, particularly by introducing the Religion system.

Prerequisites and Cost

Theology is unlocked in the Science tab after researching Philosophy. Reaching this science is noted as a “fair bump” because it has steep requirements that force the player to establish production systems for specialized resources.

The cost to research Theology is:

  • Science: 20,000
  • Manuscripts: 35

This Manuscripts requirement involves grinding out resources, as Manuscripts must be crafted from Parchment (derived from Furs, acquired through Hunting) and Culture (generated by buildings like Amphitheatres and Temples). Overcoming this hurdle will likely take a long time.
item.content:encoded:
Theology is a pivotal science technology in Kittens Game that marks a significant transition point in the civilization’s progression, particularly by introducing the Religion system.

Prerequisites and Cost

Theology is unlocked in the Science tab after researching Philosophy. Reaching this science is noted as a “fair bump” because it has steep requirements that force the player to establish production systems for specialized resources.

The cost to research Theology is:

  • Science: 20,000
  • Manuscripts: 35

This Manuscripts requirement involves grinding out resources, as Manuscripts must be crafted from Parchment (derived from Furs, acquired through Hunting) and Culture (generated by buildings like Amphitheatres and Temples). Overcoming this hurdle will likely take a long time.

Effects and Unlocks

Upon successful research, Theology provides several immediate unlocks crucial for advancing the civilization:

  1. New Resource and Production: Theology unlocks the generation of Faith, a new expendable resource used primarily in the Religion tab.

    • It enables the Priest profession. Kittens assigned as [Priests] ( /job/priest/) initially produce 0.0015 faith per tick.
    • It enables Temples to generate Faith, specifically at a rate of 0.0015 faith per tick per Temple.

  2. New Systems:

    • It unlocks the Religion tab.
    • It unlocks the ability to build Temples (which were already unlocked by Philosophy, but Theology makes them functional for Faith).
    • It unlocks the Order of the Sun, the religious upgrade system.

Importance in Progression

Theology is crucial because it gates access to the next stages of technological and religious development:

  • Religious Upgrades: It allows the player to start investing Faith in religious upgrades by using the “Praise the sun!” option to gain Worship. Religious upgrades, such as Scholasticism (which lets Temples boost Science maximum capacity by +500) and Sun Altar (which contributes to Happiness), affect areas outside of the Religion system.
  • Scientific Path: Theology unlocks the pathway to the next major sciences, Astronomy and Cryptotheology.
  • Manuscript Reliance: Once Theology is researched, future sciences, such as Astronomy (requiring 65 Manuscripts), will also require Manuscripts, making efficient Culture and Parchment production essential for continued technological growth.

item.title: Thin Film Cells
item.description:
Thin Film Cells is a specialized Workshop upgrade designed to enhance the reliability of your energy grid during the winter season by improving the efficiency of Solar Farms.

Costs and Prerequisites

To unlock and purchase this upgrade, you must meet the following criteria:

  • Technology: You must first research the Satellites science technology.
  • Science Cost: 125,000.
  • Resource Cost: 200 Unobtainium and 1,000 Uranium.

Core Effect

The primary function of Thin Film Cells is to mitigate the seasonal drop in solar energy production:
item.content:encoded:
Thin Film Cells is a specialized Workshop upgrade designed to enhance the reliability of your energy grid during the winter season by improving the efficiency of Solar Farms.

Costs and Prerequisites

To unlock and purchase this upgrade, you must meet the following criteria:

  • Technology: You must first research the Satellites science technology.
  • Science Cost: 125,000.
  • Resource Cost: 200 Unobtainium and 1,000 Uranium.

Core Effect

The primary function of Thin Film Cells is to mitigate the seasonal drop in solar energy production:

  • Winter Boost: It provides a +15% bonus to Solar Farm energy production during Winter.
  • Context: Without upgrades, Solar Farm output drops to its lowest level (+1.5 Watts) in Winter compared to Summer (+2.67 Watts). This upgrade helps stabilize your power levels when environmental conditions are least favourable.

Synergy and Stacking

Thin Film Cells is part of a progression of solar upgrades:

  • Quantum Dot Cells: This later upgrade (unlocked via Thorium) provides an additional +15% energy boost in winter that stacks additively with Thin Film Cells, for a total winter bonus of +30%.
  • Photovoltaic Cells: While Thin Film Cells targets winter specifically, Photovoltaic Cells (unlocked via Nanotechnology) provides a flat +50% bonus to Solar Farm production that multiplies with these seasonal effects.

Strategic Utility

This upgrade is particularly useful in the late-mid game as you transition your infrastructure from Pastures to Solar Farms. Because energy-consuming structures like Calciners, Factories, and Satellites do not reduce their power demand in winter, having Thin Film Cells is vital for preventing a “negative energy” state that would penalize your global production.

item.title: Thorium
item.description:
Thorium is a high-tier, highly radioactive craftable resource in Kittens Game that serves as a critical fuel for late-game energy production and deep-space exploration. It is primarily used to power advanced reactors and fund missions to the furthest reaches of the star system.

Acquisition and Production

  • Research Requirements: To unlock Thorium, you must research the Thorium science node, which costs 375,000 Science and 375 Blueprints. This technology becomes available after researching Orbital Engineering.
  • Workshop Crafting: Once researched, Thorium can be crafted in the Workshop at a base cost of 250 Uranium per unit.
  • Trading: You can also acquire Thorium by trading with Dragons. They have a 50% chance to sell Thorium in exchange for titanium, provided you have reached Embassy level 5.
  • Crafting Bonuses: Assigning a kitten with the Chemist trait as your Leader provides a +0.075 bonus to the craft ratio for Thorium.

Energy and Infrastructure Upgrades

Thorium is central to scaling your energy grid and scientific capacity through several key Workshop upgrades:
item.content:encoded:
Thorium is a high-tier, highly radioactive craftable resource in Kittens Game that serves as a critical fuel for late-game energy production and deep-space exploration. It is primarily used to power advanced reactors and fund missions to the furthest reaches of the star system.

Acquisition and Production

  • Research Requirements: To unlock Thorium, you must research the Thorium science node, which costs 375,000 Science and 375 Blueprints. This technology becomes available after researching Orbital Engineering.
  • Workshop Crafting: Once researched, Thorium can be crafted in the Workshop at a base cost of 250 Uranium per unit.
  • Trading: You can also acquire Thorium by trading with Dragons. They have a 50% chance to sell Thorium in exchange for titanium, provided you have reached Embassy level 5.
  • Crafting Bonuses: Assigning a kitten with the Chemist trait as your Leader provides a +0.075 bonus to the craft ratio for Thorium.

Energy and Infrastructure Upgrades

Thorium is central to scaling your energy grid and scientific capacity through several key Workshop upgrades:

  • Thorium Reactors: This upgrade increases the energy output of your Reactors by 25%, but introduces a consumption rate of 0.05 Thorium per tick (0.25 per second) per active reactor.
  • Enriched Thorium: This vital efficiency upgrade reduces the Thorium consumption of your reactors by 0.0625 per tick, helping to stabilise your stockpiles.
  • Quantum Dot Cells: Costs 175k Science, 200 Eludium, and 1000 Thorium. It improves Solar Farm energy production by 15% in winter and 30% in spring and autumn.
  • Thorium Drive: A high-tier engine that divides space travel time by 50 (or 75 if combined with an Antimatter Drive).

Space Missions and Structures

As you progress into the late-game “Umbra” and “Centaurus” eras, Thorium becomes a mandatory requirement for exploration:

  • Missions: Significant quantities are required for missions to Umbra (15,000), Charon (35,000), Centaurus (50,000), and the Furthest Ring (75,000).
  • Heatsinks: Essential for increasing antimatter storage, each Heatsink costs 12,500 Thorium.
  • Tectonics: These space structures, which generate 25 Watts of energy, cost 75,000 Thorium each.

Strategic Utility

  • The Antimatter Seed: In long “seed runs” aimed at reaching a 5,000 antimatter capacity, Thorium is often a major bottleneck. Reaching the milestone of 34 Heatsinks requires over 526,000 Thorium.
  • Energy Management: Strategic guides recommend turning off Thorium Reactors during most of the run to conserve fuel, only activating them when time skipping or when a massive energy surplus is required for antimatter generation.
  • Preservation: As a crafted resource, Thorium is normally lost upon resetting. To carry it over into a new run, you must possess Chronospheres and the Flux Condensator Workshop upgrade. The amount preserved is determined by the square root of your total Thorium at the time of reset.

item.title: Thorium
item.description:
Thorium is a late-game craftable resource and fuel type in Kittens Game, described as a highly radioactive and unstable material. It is essential for deep-space exploration and enhancing the efficiency of your industrial energy grid.

Technological Unlock and Costs

  • Technology: You must research the Thorium science technology, which becomes available after Orbital Engineering.
  • Research Cost: 375,000 Science and 375 Blueprints.
  • Unlocked Upgrades: Researching this technology enables the thorium resource and unlocks the Thorium Reactors, Thorium Drive, and Quantum Dot Cells workshop upgrades.

Acquisition and Production

There are two primary ways to obtain Thorium once the technology is researched:
item.content:encoded:
Thorium is a late-game craftable resource and fuel type in Kittens Game, described as a highly radioactive and unstable material. It is essential for deep-space exploration and enhancing the efficiency of your industrial energy grid.

Technological Unlock and Costs

  • Technology: You must research the Thorium science technology, which becomes available after Orbital Engineering.
  • Research Cost: 375,000 Science and 375 Blueprints.
  • Unlocked Upgrades: Researching this technology enables the thorium resource and unlocks the Thorium Reactors, Thorium Drive, and Quantum Dot Cells workshop upgrades.

Acquisition and Production

There are two primary ways to obtain Thorium once the technology is researched:

  • Workshop Crafting: You can craft thorium from Uranium.
    • Recipe: 250 Uranium yields 1 Thorium.
    • Efficiency: Kittens with the Chemist trait provide a specific crafting bonus (+0.075) to thorium yield.
  • Trading: Once you have reached a Level 5 Embassy with the Dragons, you can trade with them for thorium.
    • Exchange: They buy 250 Titanium and have a 50% chance to sell 1 unit of Thorium (with a 25% range).

Key Workshop Upgrades

Thorium is a required input for several high-tier upgrades that optimize your village and space travel:

  • Thorium Reactors:
    • Effect: Increases the energy output of your Reactors by 25% (+2.5 Watts).
    • Upkeep: While active, each Reactor consumes -0.05 thorium per tick.
    • Strategy: Players are advised to turn off this upgrade after purchasing and only activate it when time-skipping to generate antimatter, as the thorium drain can quickly deplete stockpiles.
  • Enriched Thorium: Costs 500,000 Thorium; it reduces Reactor thorium consumption by 25%.
  • Thorium Drive: Costs 100,000 Thorium; it significantly increases space travel speed, dividing travel times by 50.
  • Quantum Dot Cells: Costs 1,000 Thorium; it improves Solar Farm efficiency throughout the year, particularly providing a 30% boost in spring and autumn.

Space Missions and Infrastructure

Thorium is a major mission-gate resource for reaching the farthest points of the Helios system:

  • Umbra Mission: 15,000 Thorium.
  • Charon Mission: 35,000 Thorium.
  • Centaurus System Mission: 50,000 Thorium.
  • Furthest Ring Mission: 75,000 Thorium.
  • Tectonic (Centaurus structure): Requires 75,000 Thorium to build.

Endgame Strategic Utility

In the late-game “Iron Will” 40k runs, thorium becomes a critical bottleneck for reaching high antimatter caps. To reach a 5,000 Antimatter capacity for relic stations, players often need around 34 Heatsinks, which carries a total cost of approximately 526,000 Thorium. Because of these massive costs, managing your uranium-to-thorium crafting chain is vital for entering the Relic and Antimatter eras.

item.title: Thorium Drive
item.description:
Thorium Drive is a late-game Workshop upgrade that functions as a high-performance rocket engine, significantly accelerating the speed of space exploration.

Unlock and Construction Costs

  • Prerequisite Technology: You must first research the Thorium science technology (375,000 Science and 375 Blueprints), which becomes available after Orbital Engineering.
  • Upgrade Costs: To purchase the Thorium Drive in the Workshop, you need:
    • 400,000 Science.
    • 10,000 Ships.
    • 40,000 Gears.
    • 2,000 Alloy.
    • 100,000 Thorium.

Core Effects on Space Travel

The primary function of the Thorium Drive is to drastically reduce the duration of space missions by increasing travel speed.
item.content:encoded:
Thorium Drive is a late-game Workshop upgrade that functions as a high-performance rocket engine, significantly accelerating the speed of space exploration.

Unlock and Construction Costs

  • Prerequisite Technology: You must first research the Thorium science technology (375,000 Science and 375 Blueprints), which becomes available after Orbital Engineering.
  • Upgrade Costs: To purchase the Thorium Drive in the Workshop, you need:
    • 400,000 Science.
    • 10,000 Ships.
    • 40,000 Gears.
    • 2,000 Alloy.
    • 100,000 Thorium.

Core Effects on Space Travel

The primary function of the Thorium Drive is to drastically reduce the duration of space missions by increasing travel speed.

  • Travel Time Reduction: Researching this upgrade divides all listed space travel times by 50.
  • Antimatter Drive Synergy: If the Antimatter Drive (unlocked via the Antimatter technology) is also researched, the combined effect divides travel times by 75.
  • Strategic Utility: This speed boost is essential for reaching the most distant points of the Helios system and beyond, where base travel times are otherwise prohibitive. For example, without upgrades, the mission to Centaurus takes over 66 hours of real-time, and Umbra takes over 4 hours.

Additional Speed Modifiers

While the Thorium Drive provides a permanent passive speed increase, players can also combust Time Crystals to instantly reduce the travel time of missions currently in progress. The drive upgrades are particularly vital in the late game to reduce the “dead time” between launching missions and being able to construct new space-based infrastructure.

item.title: Thorium Reactors
item.description:
Thorium Reactors is a high-tier late-game Workshop upgrade that enhances the power output of your standard Reactor buildings. It represents a shift towards more advanced nuclear fuels to meet the escalating energy demands of space exploration and artificial intelligence.

Costs and Prerequisites

  • Science Cost: 400,000.
  • Resource Cost: 10,000 Thorium.
  • Prerequisite Technology: You must first research the Thorium science technology, which is unlocked after Orbital Engineering.

Core Effects and Mechanics

The upgrade allows your existing Reactors to utilise Thorium as a secondary, more potent fuel source:
item.content:encoded:
Thorium Reactors is a high-tier late-game Workshop upgrade that enhances the power output of your standard Reactor buildings. It represents a shift towards more advanced nuclear fuels to meet the escalating energy demands of space exploration and artificial intelligence.

Costs and Prerequisites

  • Science Cost: 400,000.
  • Resource Cost: 10,000 Thorium.
  • Prerequisite Technology: You must first research the Thorium science technology, which is unlocked after Orbital Engineering.

Core Effects and Mechanics

The upgrade allows your existing Reactors to utilise Thorium as a secondary, more potent fuel source:

  • Energy Boost: It provides a +25% increase to the energy production of every Reactor. Given that a base Reactor produces 10 Watts, this upgrade typically adds +2.5 Watts per building.
  • Fuel Consumption: This boost comes at the cost of Thorium consumption, which is depleted at a rate of 0.05 to 0.25 units per tick depending on your current level of automation and research.
  • Toggleable Functionality: Like many advanced industrial buildings, the Thorium consumption (and its associated energy bonus) can be toggled on or off to manage resource levels.

Strategic Importance

  • Supporting the Endgame Grid: Thorium Reactors are essential for powering energy-heavy structures such as AI Cores, Entanglement Stations, and Terraforming Stations.
  • Antimatter Generation: A common strategy is to only activate Thorium Reactors during time skips to ensure a positive energy state. This is vital because Sunlifters only produce antimatter if your energy production is positive when the year changes.
  • Efficiency Upgrades: Once Thorium Reactors are active, you should prioritise the Enriched Thorium upgrade. This reduces the fuel consumption of your reactors by 25%, allowing your Thorium stockpiles to last significantly longer.

In specialised challenge runs like Iron Will, where kittens are unavailable, the energy boost from Thorium Reactors is often a mandatory requirement for reaching the high power thresholds needed for deep-space missions.

item.title: Titanium Axe
item.description:
The Titanium Axe is a mid-to-late-game Workshop upgrade that provides a significant boost to your wood production infrastructure.

Costs and Prerequisites

  • Science Cost: 38,000.
  • Resource Cost: 10 Titanium.
  • Prerequisite: You must first research the Navigation science technology.

Core Effects

The Titanium Axe is described as being “indestructible” and provides a flat +50% bonus to Woodcutter output (woodRatio). It is part of a linear progression of woodcutting tools, following the Steel Axe and preceding the Alloy Axe.
item.content:encoded:
The Titanium Axe is a mid-to-late-game Workshop upgrade that provides a significant boost to your wood production infrastructure.

Costs and Prerequisites

  • Science Cost: 38,000.
  • Resource Cost: 10 Titanium.
  • Prerequisite: You must first research the Navigation science technology.

Core Effects

The Titanium Axe is described as being “indestructible” and provides a flat +50% bonus to Woodcutter output (woodRatio). It is part of a linear progression of woodcutting tools, following the Steel Axe and preceding the Alloy Axe.

Strategic Utility

  • Multiplicative Scaling: A critical strategic detail of the axe upgrade chain is that its bonuses are multiplicative with the production boost provided by Lumber Mills. This makes the upgrade far more impactful than simple additive bonuses, allowing wood production to scale effectively as construction costs for advanced buildings like Harbours and Observatories rise.
  • Transition into the Titanium Era: Because this upgrade requires Titanium, it serves as one of the first practical uses for the resource after you begin trading with the Zebras.
  • Resolving Wood Bottlenecks: Wood is often a major bottleneck in the mid-game for building Ships and Scaffolds; acquiring the Titanium Axe is essential for maintaining the velocity of your expansion during the “Titanium buildup” phase.

item.title: Transcendence
item.description:
Transcendence is a permanent religious progression system in the sources that allows players to stack tiered upgrades and boosts the efficiency of “Adoring the stars”. It is unlocked in the religion tab for 7,500 Faith and 7,500 Gold once you have reached a prerequisite of 125,000 Worship.

Mechanics of Transcending

Once the initial upgrade is purchased, a permanent “Transcend” button appears. This allows you to spend Epiphany—a hidden resource converted from Worship when you “Adore the Galaxy”—to increase your Transcendence Tier.
item.content:encoded:
Transcendence is a permanent religious progression system in the sources that allows players to stack tiered upgrades and boosts the efficiency of “Adoring the stars”. It is unlocked in the religion tab for 7,500 Faith and 7,500 Gold once you have reached a prerequisite of 125,000 Worship.

Mechanics of Transcending

Once the initial upgrade is purchased, a permanent “Transcend” button appears. This allows you to spend Epiphany—a hidden resource converted from Worship when you “Adore the Galaxy”—to increase your Transcendence Tier.

  • Carry Over: Transcendence tiers are among the few things that permanently carry over through game resets.
  • Tier Thresholds: The cost in Epiphany increases exponentially; for example, Tier 1 requires ~1.97% Epiphany, while Tier 15 requires ~3.04M%.

Key Benefits of Increasing Tiers

  • Epiphany Multiplier: Each Transcendence Tier increases the amount of Epiphany you receive when you “Adore the Galaxy”. The conversion multiplier is (TT+1)^2 (e.g., at Tier 10, your conversion is 121x stronger).
  • Cryptotheology Unlocks: Specific tiers are required to purchase advanced endgame buildings using Relics:
    • Tier 1: Black Obelisk (increases Solar Revolution cap).
    • Tier 7: Event Horizon (increases global resource storage).
    • Tier 15: Blazar (massively boosts Time Crystal and Relic production).
    • Tier 25: Holy Genocide (unlocks the Post-Apocalypse challenge).
  • Multi-Level Upgrades: Researching the Transcendence upgrade allows you to purchase religious abilities like Solar Chant, Scholasticism, and Golden Spire multiple times, with each level further boosting faith production and storage.
  • Atheism Challenge: In the Atheism challenge, your Solar Revolution cap is increased by +100% per Transcendence Tier.

Progression and Costs

Increasing your Transcendence Tier requires a set amount of Epiphany. The cost escalates exponentially, with Tier 1 requiring only ~1.97% Epiphany bonus, while Tier 15 requires over 3.04 million%.

Transcendence Tier Minimum Epiphany Bonus Needed Milestones & Unlocks
Tier 1 ~1.97% Black Obelisk
Tier 3 ~17.38% Black Nexus
Tier 12 ~8.26M% Black Radiance
Tier 15 ~3.04M% Blazar (Endgame Goal)
Tier 20 ~451.14M% Dark Nova
Tier 25 ~66.96G% Holy Genocide/Post-Apocalypse

Strategic Progression: BMF and TAP

The sources provide two specific methods for managing Transcendence to avoid losing progress or production bonuses:

  1. The BMF Reset Protocol: To maximize prestige gains before a game reset, players should follow the Backup, Metas, Faith (BMF) order. Within the Faith step, you must Transcend before you Adore the stars. Because higher Transcendence tiers increase the conversion multiplier for Adoration, this order ensures you receive the maximum possible Epiphany for your next run.
  2. The Mid-Run TAP Method: If you wish to Transcend without resetting the entire game, the sources suggest the TAP (Transcend, Adore, Praise) procedure. A rule of thumb is to have at least 1.5 times the Epiphany threshold listed for the next tier before doing this, otherwise, you may severely decrease your praising bonus and harm your current production.

Endgame Benefits and Unlocks

Reaching higher Transcendence tiers is essential for late-game and “Phase 3” progression:

  • Cryptotheology: Tiers are required to unlock specific endgame buildings. For instance, Black Obelisks require Tier 1, while Blazars—which are vital for time crystal and relic production—require Tier 15.
  • Atheism Challenge: Completing this challenge grants a permanent reward where the Solar Revolution cap increases by 100 percentage points for every Transcendence tier you possess.
  • Tiered Upgrades: Each tier allows you to purchase additional levels of religious upgrades like Solar Chant (+10% faith generation), Scholasticism (+ science), and Sun Altar (+ happiness/faith storage).
  • Unicorn Tears Challenge: In this mode, Unicorn Tombs increase your maximum faith specifically based on your Transcendence Tier.

Pro-Tip: Strategists recommend waiting until you have 1.5x to 2x the required Epiphany bonus for the next tier before Transcending mid-run to avoid a significant temporary drop in your Solar Revolution production bonus.

item.title: Transkittenism
item.description:
Transkittenism is an endgame Government policy that allows your civilisation to merge with Artificial Intelligence, effectively neutralising the threat of a machine uprising while significantly boosting your technological infrastructure.

It is generally considered the “best” choice among its tier for long-term runs, especially those focused on space storage and AI-driven production.

Costs and Prerequisites

  • Culture Cost: 1,500,000.
  • Discovery Prerequisite: You must have successfully completed at least one trade with the Leviathans.
  • Availability: It is mutually exclusive with the Necrocracy and Radical Xenophobia policies. Once one is chosen, the others are locked for the remainder of the run.
  • Critical Restriction: You cannot purchase Transkittenism if the AI Apocalypse has already begun.

Core Effects

The primary benefit of Transkittenism is the total prevention of the AI Apocalypse, but it provides several specific mechanical buffs:

Transkittenism is an endgame Government policy that allows your civilisation to merge with Artificial Intelligence, effectively neutralising the threat of a machine uprising while significantly boosting your technological infrastructure.

It is generally considered the “best” choice among its tier for long-term runs, especially those focused on space storage and AI-driven production.

Costs and Prerequisites

  • Culture Cost: 1,500,000.
  • Discovery Prerequisite: You must have successfully completed at least one trade with the Leviathans.
  • Availability: It is mutually exclusive with the Necrocracy and Radical Xenophobia policies. Once one is chosen, the others are locked for the remainder of the run.
  • Critical Restriction: You cannot purchase Transkittenism if the AI Apocalypse has already begun.

Core Effects

The primary benefit of Transkittenism is the total prevention of the AI Apocalypse, but it provides several specific mechanical buffs:

  • Gigaflop Doubling: AI Cores produce twice as many gigaflops.
  • Apocalypse Immunity: The “AI level” no longer carries a downside, and the apocalypse will not occur regardless of your hashrate or gigaflop accumulation.
  • Workshop Buffs: The Machine Learning workshop upgrade becomes stronger.
  • Storage Synergy: AI Bases are strengthened. Specifically, each AI Core will boost Moon Base storage by 11% (up from the base 10%).

Strategic Comparison

When choosing your final government path, Transkittenism competes with two other philosophies:

Policy Primary Focus Best For…
Transkittenism AI and Space Storage Long runs requiring massive unobtainium/resource caps.
Necrocracy Global Production Runs with high Black Liquid Sorrow (BLS) levels.
Radical Xenophobia Pacts and Mausoleums Increasing the efficacy of Mausoleums and gaining free Pacts.

The “Meta” Verdict

While some strategy guides describe the extra gigaflops as “pretty meh,” the policy is highly valued in the deep endgame because it allows you to build as many AI Cores as you wish without risk. This is essential for scaling Moon Base storage, which is a key component in reaching the 8.14 billion unobtainium cap required for the 100-Chronosphere “Positive Reset” loop.

item.title: Umbra Mission
item.description:
The Umbra Mission is a late-game space project focused on exploring the supermassive black hole located at the centre of the Helios system. It represents a significant step into the furthest reaches of the star system, transitioning the colony into the deepest “Phase 3” of developmental progression.

Mission Logistics and Prerequisites

To launch the Umbra mission, your kittens must have already successfully explored Yarn. The resource requirements are substantial, reflecting the mission’s late-game status:
item.content:encoded:
The Umbra Mission is a late-game space project focused on exploring the supermassive black hole located at the centre of the Helios system. It represents a significant step into the furthest reaches of the star system, transitioning the colony into the deepest “Phase 3” of developmental progression.

Mission Logistics and Prerequisites

To launch the Umbra mission, your kittens must have already successfully explored Yarn. The resource requirements are substantial, reflecting the mission’s late-game status:

  • Starcharts: 25,000
  • Science: 500,000
  • Kerosene: 25,000
  • Thorium: 15,000

Successfully completing the launch unlocks the Umbra Planet and the subsequent Charon Mission.

The Umbra Cycle and Festivals

“Umbra” is also one of the ten five-year celestial cycles (represented by the glyph ⍦). If you have researched Numerology and Numeromancy, the cycle provides the following modifiers:

  • Production Penalties: During this cycle, Planet Cracker uranium output is reduced by 10% and Hydraulic Fracturer oil output decreases by 25%.
  • Production Boosts: Energy production from HR Harvesters (located on the Umbra planet) is increased by 50%.
  • Festival Multipliers: Holding a festival during the Umbra cycle provides a 1.5x income multiplier for coal, iron, titanium, and gold.

Umbra Infrastructure: HR Harvesters

The primary structure available on the Umbra planet is the HR Harvester (Hawking Radiation Harvester). These are unique energy-producing structures with the following characteristics:

  • Cost: 25 Relics and 1,250 Antimatter.
  • Energy Generation: They generate energy based on black hole evaporation, providing a base of 1 Watt that increases over time.
  • Scaling: The output is boosted by Dark Future years (years beyond 40,000) and Void Rifts, which provide a +10% boost per rift.

Strategic Context

In the broader scope of the sources’ endgame guides, the Umbra mission is part of the “Mid-Game” transition into chasing relics and established cryptotheology. Because the mission requires 15,000 Thorium, it necessitates a stable uranium-to-thorium refinement pipeline and high science caps, which are typically supported by earlier structures like Space Beacons and Research Vessels. Furthermore, the mission marks the point where Antimatter becomes a primary construction material for planetary infrastructure.

item.title: Unicorn Graveyard
item.description:
The Unicorn Graveyard is an endgame building found within the Cryptotheology section of the Religion tab. It is primarily used to scale your maximum culture capacity based on your religious infrastructure.

Core Statistics and Costs

  • Cost: 5 Necrocorns and 1000 Megaliths.
  • Price Ratio: 1.15.
  • Prerequisites: You must have unlocked the Black Codex (a metaphysics upgrade costing 25 Paragon that requires Megalomania).

Primary Effects

  • Culture Scaling: Increases your maximum Culture by +1% for every Ziggurat you own.
  • Cryptotheology Synergy: It provides a bonus to the Black Library (another cryptotheology building), specifically improving the scaling of the Codex Leviathanianus.
  • Flavor Text: It is poetically described in-game as the “Grave of the fireflies”.

Strategic Value

  • When to build them: They are generally considered a “low-priority” late-game investment. You should typically focus on feeding your Necrocorns to the Leviathans first to max out their energy and Time Crystal production.

In the late game, Culture often becomes a significant bottleneck for technological advancement and crafting Manuscripts. Because your Ziggurat count can become quite high during the “Unicorn Era” as you hunt for Time Crystals, the Unicorn Graveyard provides a powerful way to expand your culture cap without relying solely on standard buildings like Amphitheatres or Temples. The requirement of Necrocorns means you must already have established Markers to corrupt your Alicorns, placing this building firmly in the late-game “Phase 3” of development.

  • Synergy: Because they boost your total culture storage (which includes bonuses from things like manuscripts and policies), the +1% per Ziggurat can result in a significant cumulative increase if you have a high Ziggurat count.

What it does

  • Black Library Bonus: It provides a small bonus to Black Libraries, which in turn helps increase your science storage cap.
  • Late-Game Utility: Because it scales with the number of Ziggurats you own, its effect can become quite powerful in deep runs where your Ziggurat count is high.

Strategic Context

  • When to build them: They are generally considered a “low-priority” late-game investment. You should typically focus on feeding your Necrocorns to the Leviathans first to max out their energy and Time Crystal production.

  • Research: You must have the Black Codex researched.
  • Cost: Each one costs 5 Necrocorns and 1000 Megaliths.

Summary: Think of the Unicorn Graveyard as a tool for “scaling” your culture cap rather than a primary production building. It is a refinement for players who have already optimized their main income streams and are looking to push their storage limits as far as possible before a reset.

item.title: Unicorn Necropolis
item.description:
The Unicorn Necropolis is an advanced endgame building found in the Cryptotheology section of the Religion tab. It is primarily used to accelerate the generation of Necrocorns by increasing the rate of alicorn corruption.

Core Statistics and Costs

Attribute Details
Cost 15 Necrocorns, 2500 Megaliths, 100 Alicorns, and 5 Void
Price Ratio 1.15
Prerequisite Unicorn Graveyard
Primary Effect Increases Necrocorn corruption speed by 10%

Mechanics and Synergy

The Unicorn Necropolis functions by speeding up the “corruption” process that transforms your Alicorns into Necrocorns.
item.content:encoded:
The Unicorn Necropolis is an advanced endgame building found in the Cryptotheology section of the Religion tab. It is primarily used to accelerate the generation of Necrocorns by increasing the rate of alicorn corruption.

Core Statistics and Costs

Attribute Details
Cost 15 Necrocorns, 2500 Megaliths, 100 Alicorns, and 5 Void
Price Ratio 1.15
Prerequisite Unicorn Graveyard
Primary Effect Increases Necrocorn corruption speed by 10%

Mechanics and Synergy

The Unicorn Necropolis functions by speeding up the “corruption” process that transforms your Alicorns into Necrocorns.

  • Corruption Loop: While Markers initiate the ticking corruption countdown, the Necropolis serves as a multiplier for that speed.
  • The “One Necrocorn” Rule: For these buildings to function, you must maintain a balance of at least 1 Necrocorn in your inventory.

Strategic Utility and ROI

Because the building itself costs Necrocorns—which are otherwise used to feed Leviathans to increase their energy cap—there is a specific threshold for when they become a “profitable” investment.

  • The Break-Even Point: Strategic guides suggest that the Unicorn Necropolis only becomes truly profitable at 11 units.
  • Opportunity Cost: For the first 9 or 10 buildings, the rate at which Necrocorns are generated is slower than the rate at which you would have gained benefits by simply feeding those Necrocorns directly to the Leviathans.
  • Total Investment: Reaching this profitability threshold (11 Necropolises) requires a total investment of 365 Necrocorns.

Endgame Context

The building is described as “The ocean of blood at the end of the lane”. It represents the final stage of the unicorn-to-necrocorn pipeline, allowing players to eventually automate the feeding of Leviathans at high speeds to maximize trade ratios for Time Crystals and Relics.

item.title: Unicorn Tomb
item.description:
A Unicorn Tomb is an early-tier building found in the Ziggurat section of the Religion tab that provides a 5% bonus to unicorn generation. It is the first building in a progression chain that leads to more powerful structures like Ivory Towers and Sky Palaces.

Core Statistics and Costs

  • Cost: 5 Unicorn Tears and 500 Ivory.
  • Price Ratio: 1.15.
  • Prerequisites: You must have unlocked Ivory and Unicorn Tears (typically by building a Ziggurat and sacrificing unicorns).
  • Primary Effect: Increases unicorns per tick by +5%.

Challenge Reward

The Unicorn Tomb gains a significant secondary utility through the Unicorn Tears challenge. Upon successfully completing this challenge, Unicorn Tombs provide a permanent base reward: they increase your maximum faith capacity based on your current Transcendence Tier. This makes them relevant even in the late game when the 5% unicorn production bonus becomes less impactful compared to higher-tier buildings like Sunspires.

Strategic Context

  • Early Unicorn Era: In the beginning of the unicorn-to-time-crystal pipeline, Unicorn Tombs are essential for accelerating your production rate so you can reach the 2,500 unicorns required for further sacrifices.
  • Scaling: Like other religious buildings, its cost increases with each one built. Strategic guides recommend using a unicorn calculator to determine if a Unicorn Tomb or another building, like an Ivory Tower, offers the best return on investment for your current resources.
  • Religion Integration: In later runs, once you have higher Solar Revolution bonuses, your unicorn production will scale significantly, and these tombs serve as a foundational layer for that growth.

item.title: Unobtainium Huts
item.description:
Unobtainium Huts is a major mid-to-late game Workshop upgrade that drastically reduces the cost scaling of your Huts, allowing you to massively expand your kitten population and boost Paragon gains.

1. Core Effect

  • Price Ratio Reduction: Reduces the price ratio of Huts by 0.25 (a flat -0.25 modifier to the base 2.5 price ratio).
  • Impact: Huts naturally have one of the steepest cost scalings in the game (a base ratio of 2.5). Combined with Ironwood Huts (-0.50) and Concrete Huts (-0.30), Unobtainium Huts allows you to build dozens of additional Huts before hitting wood storage limits, yielding significantly more kittens per run.

2. Cost and Prerequisites

  • Technology Prerequisite: Exogeology (unlocked via Orbital Engineering; costs 275k Science and 250 Blueprints).
  • Workshop Upgrade Cost:
    • 200k Science
    • 350 Unobtainium
    • 15k Titanium

3. Infrastructure Requirements to Reach It

Reaching Unobtainium Huts requires establishing a foothold in Space and expanding your resource caps:

Combined with Ironwood Huts (-0.50) and Concrete Huts (-0.30), Unobtainium Huts allows you to build dozens of additional Huts before hitting wood storage limits, yielding significantly more kittens per run.

2. Cost and Prerequisites

  • Technology Prerequisite: Exogeology (unlocked via Orbital Engineering; costs 275k Science and 250 Blueprints).
  • Workshop Upgrade Cost:
    • 200k Science
    • 350 Unobtainium
    • 15k Titanium

3. Infrastructure Requirements to Reach It

Reaching Unobtainium Huts requires establishing a foothold in Space and expanding your resource caps:

  • Unobtainium Storage Cap: Base Unobtainium storage is only 150. You must build at least 1 Moon Base (which requires 50 Unobtainium, 70k Oil capacity, 9,500 Titanium, and 250 Concrete) to raise your storage capacity past the 350 Unobtainium threshold needed for the upgrade.
  • Unobtainium Generation: Requires Lunar Outposts to convert Uranium into Unobtainium.
  • Uranium Supply: Because Lunar Outposts consume Uranium rapidly, relying on Orbital Geodesy (Quarries produce Uranium) or trading Titanium with Dragons is strongly recommended to keep Outposts running.
  • Starcharts & Oil: You will need roughly 2,100 Starcharts to fund the prerequisite space missions (Orbital Launch and Moon Mission) and an Oil capacity of at least 70k.

4. Strategic Role and Reset Checkpoint

  • Progression Milestone: Early game resets typically peak at Concrete Huts (around 130–150 kittens). Unobtainium Huts serves as the next primary milestone once your Paragon pool and storage multipliers are high enough to comfortably reach Space.
  • Farming Renaissance: A common strategy is to repeat runs pushing to Unobtainium Huts to max out kitten housing, stockpiling Paragon until you can purchase all the core price reduction Metaphysics upgrades through to Renaissance (750 Paragon) before committing to the heavier Eludium and Time Crystal eras.

item.title: Wooden_Beam
item.description:
A Wooden Beam (often simply called a Beam) is a foundational mid-game craftable resource in Kittens Game refined from wood. It serves as a primary support structure required for advanced construction and the development of the colony’s industrial and religious infrastructure.

Acquisition and Production

  • Workshop Crafting: A single wooden beam costs 175 Wood. Because this cost is relatively low compared to later-game items, players often mass-craft beams once their wood storage is expanded.
  • Trading with Lizards: Once you reach Embassy level 5 with the Lizards, they have a 15% chance of selling you 10 beams in exchange for 1,000 minerals.
  • Automation: Researching Workshop Automation allows Steamworks to automatically convert a portion of your wood into beams once per year whenever your wood reaches 98% of its storage cap. This frequency increases to twice per year with the Advanced Automation upgrade.

Primary Uses in Construction

Beams are a mandatory material for several critical buildings and higher-tier resources:
item.content:encoded:
A Wooden Beam (often simply called a Beam) is a foundational mid-game craftable resource in Kittens Game refined from wood. It serves as a primary support structure required for advanced construction and the development of the colony’s industrial and religious infrastructure.

Acquisition and Production

  • Workshop Crafting: A single wooden beam costs 175 Wood. Because this cost is relatively low compared to later-game items, players often mass-craft beams once their wood storage is expanded.
  • Trading with Lizards: Once you reach Embassy level 5 with the Lizards, they have a 15% chance of selling you 10 beams in exchange for 1,000 minerals.
  • Automation: Researching Workshop Automation allows Steamworks to automatically convert a portion of your wood into beams once per year whenever your wood reaches 98% of its storage cap. This frequency increases to twice per year with the Advanced Automation upgrade.

Primary Uses in Construction

Beams are a mandatory material for several critical buildings and higher-tier resources:

  • Storage Expansion: They are required to build Warehouses (1.5 beams each), which are essential for increasing the global caps for multiple resources.
  • Mega Structures: Beams are a component for crafting Megaliths (25 beams each), which are used to build Ziggurats and other religious structures.
  • Naval Infrastructure: They are the primary input for crafting Scaffolds (50 beams each), which are needed for building Trade Ships and Harbours.

Workshop Upgrades

Several essential Workshop upgrades require a stockpile of beams to improve the colony’s efficiency:

  • Reinforced Barns (25 Beams): Increases the storage space for wood, minerals, and iron by 80%.
  • Coal Furnace (2,000 Beams): Allows Smelters to produce coal while burning wood.
  • Deep Mining (1,200 Beams): Allows Mines to produce a small amount of coal.

Strategic Utility and Resets

In the early-to-mid game, beams are often the first major “crafting hurdle” players face as they transition from raw wood collection to organised manufacturing. Strategic guides suggest that once the Construction science is researched, players should prioritise building enough warehouses to raise their storage caps for iron and science.

As a crafted resource, wooden beams are normally lost upon resetting the game. To carry them over into a new run, a player must possess at least one Chronosphere and the Flux Condensator Workshop upgrade. The amount preserved follows a square root formula based on the total quantity held at the time of reset.

item.title: Writing
item.description:
Writing is a foundational mid-game science that costs 3,600 Science and requires Engineering as a prerequisite. It is widely identified as the first major “speedbump” or bottleneck in the game, marking the transition into a phase where progression relies on complex resource management rather than simple manual gathering.

Technological and Structural Unlocks

Researching Writing provides access to essential tools for cultural and industrial expansion:

  • Parchment: Writing enables the crafting of Parchment in the Workshop. Parchment is produced using Furs, which are primarily obtained through the Hunt system using Catpower.
  • Amphitheatres: This technology allows for the construction of Amphitheatres, which are the earliest buildings used to generate Culture. Crucially, they also mitigate unhappiness caused by population growth, which is vital for maintaining kitten productivity.
  • Science Progression: Writing is the mandatory prerequisite for the Philosophy, Machinery, and Steel technologies.
  • Register: This Workshop upgrade becomes available, allowing leaders to manage jobs by prioritizing kittens with higher experience.

Strategic Utility

The primary role of Writing is to establish the “Cultural Engine” required for the mid-game. Parchment is the mandatory base material for Manuscripts, which are required in large quantities to unlock critical sciences such as Theology, Astronomy, and Navigation.

  • Happiness Management: Building Amphitheatres until they stop “noticeably improving” happiness to offset the production penalties of a growing village.

item.title: Yarn Mission
item.description:
The Yarn Mission is a late-game space exploration project that involves travelling to Yarn, a Class M planet within the Helios star system. It is described as having a moderate climate, oxygen atmosphere, and seas.

Mission Logistics and Unlocks

  • Prerequisites: Players must successfully complete the Helios Mission before the Yarn Mission becomes available in the “Ground Control” section of the Space tab.
  • Launch Costs: The mission requires a significant investment of resources: 7,500 Starcharts, 35,000 Titanium, 350,000 Science, and 12,000 Kerosene.
  • Travel Time: The base travel time is 3,800 game-days, which is approximately 2 hours, 6 minutes, and 40 seconds in real-time. This duration can be reduced significantly by researching Thorium or Antimatter Drives.
  • Sequential Unlocks: Completing this mission unlocks the Yarn Planet and the subsequent mission to Umbra.

Yarn Infrastructure

Once the planet is reached, two specialized structures can be developed to scale the colony’s population and agricultural efficiency:
item.content:encoded:

  • Sequential Unlocks: Completing this mission unlocks the Yarn Planet and the subsequent mission to Umbra.

Yarn Infrastructure

Once the planet is reached, two specialized structures can be developed to scale the colony’s population and agricultural efficiency:

  • Terraforming Station: Costs 25 Antimatter, 5,000 Uranium, and 5,000 Kerosene. It provides +1 maximum kitten capacity.
  • Hydroponics: Requires the Hydroponics technology and costs 1 Unobtainium and 500 Kerosene. It increases maximum catnip by 10%, catnip production by 2.5%, and provides a 1.0% bonus to the kitten capacity of Terraforming Stations. Hydroponics also increases the overall catnip storage capacity by 10%, which stacks additively with the Refrigeration upgrade.

The Yarn Cycle

“Yarn” is also the name of one of the ten five-year cycles in the game (represented by the glyph ⍧). If Numerology has been researched, the Yarn cycle provides the following modifiers:

  • Production Bonuses: Hydroponics catnip production is increased by 100%.
  • Production Penalties: Research Vessel starchart production is reduced by 50%.
  • Festival Effect: If Numeromancy is also researched, holding a festival during the Yarn cycle provides a 2x multiplier to culture income.

Strategic Importance

In the late game, terraforming Yarn is a primary strategy for players aiming to maximize their kitten population (potentially reaching upwards of 60,000 kittens) to farm larger amounts of Paragon during long runs. This is achieved by stacking Terraforming Stations and leveraging the scaling bonuses from Hydroponics and AI Cores.

item.title: Zebra Relations: Appeasement
item.description:
Zebra Relations: Appeasement is a mid-game Foreign policy used to improve trade efficiency with the notoriously hostile Zebra race. It is specifically designed to overcome the titanium bottleneck by making Zebras more likely to trade and increasing the amount of titanium they provide, though it comes at the cost of a permanent penalty to your gold production.

Costs and Effects

  • Cost: 5,000 Culture.
  • Prerequisite: You must have met the Zebras (discovered after building your first Trade Ship).
  • Improved Standing: It provides a relationship boost equivalent to having 15 extra Tradeposts, making the Zebras significantly less hostile.
  • Titanium Bonus: It adds a multiplicative bonus to the titanium trade ratio, also equivalent to 15 Tradeposts.
  • Gold Penalty: It imposes a -5% penalty to your overall gold income.

Strategic Utility

Because Zebras are naturally hostile (-30% attitude), they frequently refuse to trade, which can stall progress during the “Titanium Era”.
item.content:encoded:
Zebra Relations: Appeasement is a mid-game Foreign policy used to improve trade efficiency with the notoriously hostile Zebra race. It is specifically designed to overcome the titanium bottleneck by making Zebras more likely to trade and increasing the amount of titanium they provide, though it comes at the cost of a permanent penalty to your gold production.

Costs and Effects

  • Cost: 5,000 Culture.
  • Prerequisite: You must have met the Zebras (discovered after building your first Trade Ship).
  • Improved Standing: It provides a relationship boost equivalent to having 15 extra Tradeposts, making the Zebras significantly less hostile.
  • Titanium Bonus: It adds a multiplicative bonus to the titanium trade ratio, also equivalent to 15 Tradeposts.
  • Gold Penalty: It imposes a -5% penalty to your overall gold income.

Strategic Utility

Because Zebras are naturally hostile (-30% attitude), they frequently refuse to trade, which can stall progress during the “Titanium Era”.

  • The Titanium Solution: Most strategy guides suggest that choosing Appeasement is “not even a question” because players are usually desperate for titanium. Until you have enough Tradeposts to negate Zebra hostility naturally—which requires 85 Tradeposts (or 58 if you have the Diplomacy metaphysics upgrade)—Appeasement is the most effective way to secure a steady supply of metal.
  • Managing the Gold Penalty: While gold is a critical resource for trading and religious upgrades, the -5% penalty is generally considered a fair trade-off for the increased titanium velocity. Once your gold production is bolstered by Smelters and the Geodesy upgrade, this penalty becomes negligible.

Comparison: Appeasement vs. Bellicosity

Enacting Appeasement permanently locks you out of the Zebra Relations: Bellicosity policy for the remainder of that run.

Policy Effect on Zebras Effect on Other Races Economic Penalty
Appeasement Improved relations (+15 Tradeposts) None -5% Gold Income
Bellicosity Worse relations (-10 Tradeposts) Better relations (+5 Tradeposts) None

Pro Tip: Expert players generally advise staying with Appeasement until your infrastructure (specifically your Tradepost count) is high enough to mitigate Zebra hostility on its own. Only once the Zebras are no longer hostile would the other policy options become viable for optimizing trades with other civilisations.

item.title: Zebra Relations: Bellicosity
item.description:
Zebra Relations: Bellicosity is a mid-game Foreign policy that prioritises relations with other civilisations by taking a harder stance against the Zebras. While it improves your standing with most trade partners, it significantly hinders your ability to acquire Titanium.

Core Effects and Costs

  • Cost: 5,000 Culture.
  • Prerequisite: You must have met the Zebras (discovered after building your first Trade Ship).
  • Zebra Penalty: Your relations with the Zebras worsen, equivalent to losing 10 Tradeposts.
  • Global Standing Bonus: Your relations with all other races improve, equivalent to adding 5 Tradeposts.
  • Titanium Reduction: It applies a multiplicative penalty to the amount of titanium Zebras sell, equivalent to -10 Tradeposts worth of trade ratio.

Comparison: Bellicosity vs. Appeasement

Choosing Bellicosity permanently locks you out of the Zebra Relations: Appeasement policy for that run.

Comparison: Bellicosity vs. Appeasement

Feature Bellicosity Appeasement
Zebra Standing -10 Tradeposts (Worse) +15 Tradeposts (Better)
Other Races +5 Tradeposts (Better) No change
Titanium Yield Multiplicative Penalty Multiplicative Bonus
Economic Cost None -5% Gold Income

Strategic Advice

In most standard runs, Bellicosity is considered a suboptimal choice because Titanium is one of the most critical mid-game bottlenecks.

  • The Titanium Bottleneck: Since Zebras are the primary source of Titanium, making them more hostile and reducing their trade yield is generally counter-productive.
  • Hostility Mitigation: Expert advice suggests that Appeasement is the only real option until you have enough Tradeposts (typically 85, or 58 with Diplomacy) to negate Zebra hostility naturally.
  • Late Game Viability: Bellicosity only becomes viable once Zebra hostility has been completely negated through infrastructure, and you wish to marginally boost trades with friendly races like the Lizards or Sharks.

item.title: Ziggurat
item.description:
The Ziggurat is a major structure in Kittens Game, classified as a Mega Structure. It is crucial for initiating the production chain of unicorn-related resources and advancing through the later religious tiers of the game.

1. Unlocks and Construction

The Ziggurat building is unlocked relatively early by researching the Construction technology. However, it requires highly processed and rare resources to build.

Detail Cost/Requirement Source
Technology Prerequisite Construction
Base Cost 50 Megalith, 50 Scaffold, and 1 Blueprint
Visibility Requirement Players usually need approximately 5 Megaliths, 5 Scaffolds, and 1 Blueprint before the building becomes visible in the Bonfire tab.
Price Ratio 1.25

2. Core Function: Unicorn Sacrifice

The Ziggurat’s most important function is enabling the conversion of Unicorns into Unicorn Tears.
item.content:encoded:
The Ziggurat is a major structure in Kittens Game, classified as a Mega Structure. It is crucial for initiating the production chain of unicorn-related resources and advancing through the later religious tiers of the game.

1. Unlocks and Construction

The Ziggurat building is unlocked relatively early by researching the Construction technology. However, it requires highly processed and rare resources to build.

Detail Cost/Requirement Source
Technology Prerequisite Construction
Base Cost 50 Megalith, 50 Scaffold, and 1 Blueprint
Visibility Requirement Players usually need approximately 5 Megaliths, 5 Scaffolds, and 1 Blueprint before the building becomes visible in the Bonfire tab.
Price Ratio 1.25

2. Core Function: Unicorn Sacrifice

The Ziggurat’s most important function is enabling the conversion of Unicorns into Unicorn Tears.

  • Sacrifice Unicorns: Once you have a Ziggurat, you unlock the ability to Sacrifice Unicorns in the Religion tab.
  • Cost and Yield: Each sacrifice costs 2500 Unicorns. In return, you receive one Unicorn Tear for every Ziggurat you have.
  • Initial Benefit: The resulting Unicorn Tear provides a happiness/production bonus.

3. Strategic Importance

The Ziggurat is the entry point to the “Unicorn/Time Crystal Era”.

  • Culture Boost: The Ziggurat provides a passive effect of Max Culture +8%.
  • Resource Pipeline: The Ziggurat establishes the beginning of a crucial late-game resource line: unicorns → tears → Black Liquid Sorrow (BLS) → alicorns → time crystals → relics.
  • Building Priority (Early Game): Expert advice suggests that if a player needs to ask if they should get Ziggurats, they “probably don’t need more than one” on their first few runs, due to the expensive nature of the entire resource line. It is advised to build one Ziggurat when possible, sacrificing unicorns for one tear for the initial bonus, as you “won’t need more than one tear until you hit the unicorn era”.
  • Building Priority (Late Game): In the Unicorn Era, players are advised to build a large number of ziggurats. For the IW 40K endless run, it is suggested to build at least 10 Ziggurats before converting unicorns, with 25–30 Ziggurats being the practical maximum due to resource costs.

4. Upgrades and Synergies

The Ziggurat interacts with other buildings and Policy/:

  • Religious Synergy (Nagas): The Naga Relations: Cultists policy (a Foreign policy) allows Ziggurats to gain 10% of the bonuses The Order of the Sun grants to temples.
  • Culture Capacity (Unicorn Graveyard): The Unicorn Graveyard building (unlocked by Megalomania/Black Codex) increases your culture maximum by +1% per Ziggurat.
  • Unicorn Rift Bonus: The amount of unicorns gained from a Unicorn Rift (a random event unlocked by Ivory Towers) is boosted, calculated as 500 * (1 + your unicorn ziggurat bonus production to unicorns/10).

item.title: Centaurus System
item.description:
Centaurus refers to a significant, late-game deep space mission destination—a warm, faraway star system—and the mission required to reach it in Kittens Game.

1. Centaurus Space Mission Details

The Centaurus Mission is a costly undertaking in the latter stages of space exploration:

  • Prerequisite: The mission is unlocked after completing the Rorschach Mission.
  • Cost: Researching and launching the Centaurus Mission requires vast amounts of late-game resources: 100,000 Starchart, 40,000 Titanium, 400,000 Science, 50,000 Kerosene, and 50,000 Thorium.
  • Travel Time: The base travel time is 120,000 game-days, which equates to 2 days, 18 hours, and 40 minutes in real-time.

2. Infrastructure and Challenge Unlock

A successful mission unlocks the Centaurus System and associated buildings:

2. Infrastructure and Challenge Unlock

A successful mission unlocks the Centaurus System and associated buildings:

  • Building Unlocked (Tectonic): The mission enables the construction of the Tectonic structure, provided the player has researched Terraformation. Tectonic is a highly expensive energy production building, costing 600,000 Science, 500 Antimatter, and 75,000 Thorium, and producing 25 Energy.
  • Tectonic Upgrade: The effectiveness of the Tectonic structure can be further improved by the Molten Core upgrade (unlocked by Exophysics), which provides a +5% boost to Tectonic Energy Production per level.
  • Challenge Requirement: Completion of the Centaurus Mission is the specific unlock requirement for the Energy challenge,. The Energy challenge imposes a doubled energy consumption rate on the player’s village,.

item.title: Liberty vs tradition
item.description:
The choice between the Liberty and Tradition Policy/ in Kittens Game represents an early decision regarding how your civilization addresses population growth, resource management, and scientific advancement. Both Policy/ become available once you have researched Writing and both cost 150 Culture.

This choice is particularly important because once one is selected, the other is locked out, and this initial decision influences the subsequent Government Policy/ you can pursue.

Here is a comparison of their purpose, effects, and strategic recommendations:
item.content:encoded:
The choice between the Liberty and Tradition Policy/ in Kittens Game represents an early decision regarding how your civilization addresses population growth, resource management, and scientific advancement. Both Policy/ become available once you have researched Writing and both cost 150 Culture.

This choice is particularly important because once one is selected, the other is locked out, and this initial decision influences the subsequent Government Policy/ you can pursue.

Here is a comparison of their purpose, effects, and strategic recommendations:

1. Tradition Policy

Purpose and Effects:

  • Manuscript Efficiency: Tradition is described as being “Good for small culture oriented societies”. Its primary effect is reducing the cost and increasing the impact of Manuscripts.
    • Cost Reduction: Manuscript cost is reduced by 100 Culture and 5 Parchment.
    • Culture Cap Boost: It doubles the manuscript max culture effect.
  • Expert Recommendation: “Monstrous Advice” strongly recommends Tradition (“all the way!”) because manuscripts are crucial for progression, and making them cheaper and more effective is highly beneficial.

Progression Path:

  • Choosing Tradition allows you to later select Monarchy or Autocracy (both costing 1500 Culture).

2. Liberty Policy

Purpose and Effects:

  • Happiness Focus: Liberty is intended for societies focused on happiness, addressing the natural unhappiness that arises from increasing population.
    • Happiness Bonus: It increases the production effect of happiness by 10%.
    • Population Bonus: It adds free housing for one kitten.
  • Contextual Use: In early runs, the Liberty policy can be obtained to offset a “big production hit due to happiness”.

Strategic Critique:

  • “Monstrous Advice” labels Liberty as a “noob trap” because it promises to solve a problem (low happiness/production) that can often be managed through other means, such as accumulating Karma from resets or building Amphitheatres.
  • The “Kittensgame starter guide,” however, suggests that in early runs, if progression is slowing due to low happiness/high population penalty, obtaining Liberty can be useful to mitigate that production hit. However, in later runs (once Karma is acquired), switching to Tradition may be preferable.

Progression Path:

  • Choosing Liberty allows you to later select Republic or Autocracy (both costing 1500 Culture).

Summary of Differences

Policy Primary Benefit Recommended Strategy Subsequent Governments
Tradition Reduces the cost of manuscripts and increases their culture effect. Highly recommended by experts for improving long-term progress and managing the manuscript bottleneck. Monarchy, Autocracy.
Liberty Increases kitten production based on Happiness and provides one free housing unit. Useful in specific early runs if happiness penalties are severely impacting production. Republic, Autocracy.

In essence, Tradition invests in the efficiency of your scientific engine (Manuscript production), while Liberty attempts to mask the symptoms of low kitten Happiness to maintain production. For most players seeking rapid progress, the permanent resource efficiency gained from Tradition is favored, as manuscripts quickly become a bottleneck required for advanced technologies like Theology and Astronomy.

item.title: Steel Saw
item.description:
The Steel Saw is a mid-game Workshop upgrade designed to scale your civilization’s wood production by improving the output of your Lumber Mills.

Costs and Requirements

  • Science Cost: 52,000.
  • Resource Cost: 750 Steel.
  • Prerequisite: You must research the Physics technology to unlock this upgrade in the Workshop.

Core Effects

  • Efficiency Boost: It provides an additional +2% wood production bonus for every Lumber Mill you have built.
  • Statistical Impact: A base Lumber Mill provides +10% wood production; the Steel Saw raises this total to 12% per mill. In practical terms, this makes building additional Lumber Mills more impactful, providing a relative wood production increase of approximately 20.69% when moving from 40 to 50 mills (compared to only 20% without the upgrade).
  • Scaling: This bonus is part of the “Saw” upgrade chain, which is essential for overcoming the “slow wood accumulation” typically experienced in the mid-game.

Upgrade Progression

The Steel Saw is the second tier in the specialized saw lineage:

Costs and Requirements

  • Science Cost: 52,000.
  • Resource Cost: 750 Steel.
  • Prerequisite: You must research the Physics technology to unlock this upgrade in the Workshop.

Core Effects

  • Statistical Impact: A base Lumber Mill provides +10% wood production; the Steel Saw raises this total to 12% per mill. In practical terms, this makes building additional Lumber Mills more impactful, providing a relative wood production increase of approximately 20.69% when moving from 40 to 50 mills (compared to only 20% without the upgrade).
  • Scaling: This bonus is part of the “Saw” upgrade chain, which is essential for overcoming the “slow wood accumulation” typically experienced in the mid-game.

Upgrade Progression

The Steel Saw is the second tier in the specialized saw lineage:

  1. Reinforced Saw: +2% bonus (Requires Construction).
  2. Steel Saw: +2% bonus (Requires Physics).
  3. Titanium Saw: +1.5% bonus (Requires Steel Saw).
  4. Alloy Saw: +1.5% bonus (Requires Titanium Saw).

Strategic Utility

At this stage of the game, wood production is often a major bottleneck for constructing Observatories, Harbours, and Trade Ships. While individual global multipliers (like Kittens or Magnetos) are generally preferred, the Saw upgrades are highly valued because they are multiplicative with the Axe chain of upgrades (Iron, Steel, Alloy, etc.), providing a necessary foundation for your industrial economy.
